sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and the components that keep their own clock
paragraphs: Not every IGCSE mark is earned in the exam hall. Practical tests, coursework portfolios, speaking tests and programming tasks are assessed on schedules set partly by the board and partly by the school, and those schedules are earlier than the written papers. A family tracking only the exam timetable discovers the English portfolio deadline the week before it falls. This is the part of the year where the most marks are won quietly and the most trouble is caused, so the boundaries need stating in plain words.

What a tutor may do with assessed work is teach it. That means explaining how marks are allocated against the published criteria, teaching the genre or the technique, working through examples that are not the student's submission, reading a draft and giving feedback the student then acts on themselves. What a tutor may never do is write, rewrite, edit to completion, or supply any part of what is submitted. Providers in this market sell completed assessed work. That is malpractice, it is the student who carries the consequence, and it is not something we will do at any price.

The practical components are the ones families assume cannot be taught over video, and the assumption is half right. Nobody can run a titration through a screen. What loses marks on a practical paper is almost never the manipulation: it is the table drawn after the readings, the missing unit in a column heading, the anomaly quietly dropped, the graph line drawn through every point. All of that is taught from the student's own recorded data, on screen, with the mark scheme open beside it.

sections.heading: Results day, and the two windows that close inside a fortnight
paragraphs: Results day is treated as an ending and is actually a short decision window. Two clocks start the moment the statement of results arrives. The first is the enquiry-about-results window, within which a centre can ask the board to review a mark; it is measured in weeks, not months, and it runs through the school rather than through the parent. The second is the entry window for the next series, because an IGCSE November retake has a final entry deadline of its own that falls well before the papers.

Both decisions need the marks, not the grades. A statement of results that shows a grade sitting one or two marks under a boundary is a different situation from one that shows a subject fifteen marks short, and the response differs: the first is a conversation with the exams officer about a review, the second is a teaching problem with a sensible number of weeks attached to it. Reading the subject-level marks on the day, before anyone has made a decision, is the most useful hour of the whole summer.

The gap between sitting a retake and learning the outcome is longer than families expect. Pearson's November 2025 International GCSE results reached students on 22 January 2026. A student retaking in November is therefore waiting into the new year, often while already enrolled on an A Level or IB Diploma course that assumed a particular grade. Planning what happens during the wait - which qualification continues, which conversation the school needs - belongs in the same week as the retake decision, not in January.

sections.heading: The three Ministry subjects already sitting in the week
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year starts in April. The federal position behind this is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. For a parent budgeting evenings, these are not optional extras; they are periods already on the timetable.

KHDA sets out how they are organised, and the detail matters for anyone planning tuition around them. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, while non-Arab students are taught Islamic Education and moral, social and cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two further rules shape what support can honestly be offered. Schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Practical consequence: tuition here supports the school's own material and the student's own stream, it does not substitute a parallel syllabus, and the stream a child sits in should be confirmed with the school before any hour is booked.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: open the file in Year 11, not after results
paragraphs: Equivalency is the step that turns an international certificate into something a UAE institution can read, and it is the step families discover last. For the British track the requirement is specific. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That last clause is where subject plans break. A student taking nine subjects of which Arabic and Islamic Education are two has seven candidates for the count, not nine, and if two of those seven are below the threshold the file is short. One UAE tutoring site currently ranking for these searches states that candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five. Neither number should be taken from a tutoring page, including this one - read it on moe.gov.ae or ask the attestation authority in your emirate, and do it in Year 11 rather than after results.

For the American track the same clarification sets out English proficiency as a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold is stated in that source, so no figure for the IB route is published here. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee any part of equivalency or attestation; the process belongs to the Ministry and the emirate's authority, and tutoring is not a requirement of it.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE hour costs in this market, and whether the date moves the number
paragraphs: Most UAE tutoring pages publish no price at all, and the ones that do quote in US dollars. The figures below are IGCSE tutor rates in AED as published by the providers named, read in October 2026, together with the rate table in Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026. They are market figures and not IB Gram's prices. They are here because a parent cannot judge a quote without a range, and because the spread in this market is wide enough - roughly AED 45 to AED 650 for one hour - that a quote tells you almost nothing on its own.

What moves a number inside that range is mostly the model: who the tutor is, whether travel is built into the rate, whether planning and marking happen between sessions, and whether the hour is one-to-one or shared. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work.

Does the date move the price? Not reliably, and a family should be sceptical of any suggestion that it does. What the date moves is the value: the same AED spent in November buys hours that arrive while content teaching can still be absorbed, and the same AED spent in April buys technique work on a narrower set of marks. Read against context, Dubai's school fees were held flat for 2026-27 under the emirate's second economic incentives package, so tuition is the education line item most families are actually deciding about.

sections.heading: A tutor who travels, and one-to-one over live video: which survives exam term
paragraphs: Parents searching for a 1-to-1 IGCSE tutor in the UAE are usually picturing someone in the room, and that is a reasonable thing to want. IB Gram delivers one-to-one IGCSE tuition online, over live video, to families anywhere in the Emirates; home visits are a service offered only in India. Rather than ask anyone to take that on trust, the comparison below is set out against the thing that actually decides it, which is what exam term does to a week.

Three differences do most of the work. The first is that a travelling hour is not an hour: it starts when the tutor arrives, and in exam term the family is paying for a drive out of a budget measured in whole hours. The second is the size of the pool. A visiting tutor is drawn from whoever is within a reasonable drive; a specialist on screen is drawn from whoever teaches that syllabus code. For Extended-tier sciences, 0606 Additional Mathematics and 0478 Computer Science, that distinction is the whole difference in the northern emirates.

The third is continuity, which matters most in the last twelve weeks. Study leave starts, families travel, Ramadan moves the evening, and a schedule that depends on a car stops when any of those happen. A schedule that depends on a video link follows the student. None of this makes a visiting tutor a bad choice for a family who wants one and can find a specialist nearby. It does mean the online version wins on the specific grounds that decide an IGCSE result.

process.title: Tell us the date before the subject
process.description: The first message we want is not a subject name. It is the series your child is entered for, the board, the tier and the syllabus code, plus the date of the next school assessment. If you do not have those, say so and we will tell you exactly who at the school has them and what to ask for.

process.title: The diagnostic session
process.description: A first one-to-one hour spent on the ten facts in the table above and on one marked script, read question by question. It ends with a written note of what the lost marks have in common. Families who stop here have still bought something useful, and some do.

process.title: The plan, counted backwards and written down
process.description: Usable weeks between today and the first paper, the content that fits in them, the components with earlier deadlines, and what is being left out on purpose. You get it in writing. Anything we cannot fit is named rather than quietly dropped, including the possibility that the tier has capped the target.

process.title: Weekly hours against the plan
process.description: One subject, one tutor, live online over video at a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot, with written work set between sessions and marked before the next one. The plan is reviewed at each mock against the marked script rather than against how the sessions felt.

process.title: The last fortnight, and the week after results
process.description: Sequencing for the hall, the student's own error log, and the correct zone timetable confirmed with the exams officer. On results day the marks are read subject by subject, and any review or retake decision is taken inside the published windows rather than after them.

whyPoints.title: Every hour is pointed at a date
whyPoints.description: Plans here start from the series, the entry deadline and the school's internal calendar, then work backwards to what fits. That is why this page counts usable weeks rather than promising coverage: a sixteen-hour block and a twenty-eight-hour block are different products and should be sold as such.

whyPoints.title: Specialists chosen by syllabus code
whyPoints.description: Matching is done on the code on the statement of entry, not on the subject name and not on who is nearest. For 0606 Additional Mathematics, 0478 Computer Science and Extended-tier sciences, that is the difference between a specialist and the closest available teacher in a thin local market.

whyPoints.title: Permitted to teach, and checkable
whyPoints.description: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask any provider, including us, to confirm it.

whyPoints.title: Coursework support that keeps the student the author
whyPoints.description: A tutor here teaches technique, explains how marks are allocated against the published criteria, and gives feedback on a draft the student then revises. Nothing submitted is written, rewritten or edited to completion by the tutor. Providers in this market sell finished assessed work; the student carries that risk, so we do not.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built for the UAE week
whyPoints.description: Sessions are set in Gulf Standard Time around commutes from Sharjah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain into Dubai schools, around shortened Ramadan days, and around travel. A Ramadan revision plan is agreed in advance as a block rather than renegotiated weekly, because that is the version that survives.

whyPoints.title: Honest about coverage
whyPoints.description: Some IGCSE subject and tier combinations have no UAE-based specialist free at the time a family wants. When that happens we say so, name what we can offer instead, including a specialist in another time zone teaching the same code, and let you decide rather than filling the slot with whoever is available.

faqs.question: It is October and our son sits the June series. What should a 1-to-1 IGCSE tutor do first?
faqs.answer: Collect facts, not topics. Before any teaching, the tutor should establish the board, the syllabus code, the tier on the entry, the series, the exam centre's Cambridge zone, which components are not written papers, and the school's own mock and coursework deadlines. Then one marked script read question by question. From October to a June series there are roughly thirty calendar weeks, of which about twenty-two are usable once breaks and mock fortnights come out. That is enough for a full syllabus pass and a paper block afterwards, which is the best position a family can be in without having started in Year 10.

faqs.question: How many weeks of real teaching are left if we start in January for a June paper?
faqs.answer: About sixteen, not twenty-one. The calendar gives roughly twenty-one weeks from January to a June series. The UAE term year then removes a spring break, a mock fortnight, Eid, and whatever study-leave arrangement your school runs before the papers. At one session a week in one subject, sixteen usable hours will rebuild two or three whole topics and fix paper technique across every component. It will not re-teach a two-year course. Check the losses against your own school calendar, because mock windows vary by a fortnight or more between Dubai, Abu Dhabi and the northern emirates.

faqs.question: Our school asked for forecast grades after the exams had already started. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the published dates show why. For the Cambridge March 2027 series the exam period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, while forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027 - inside that window. The school produces them from mock evidence and classwork, not from the live papers, which is one concrete reason a mock that awards nothing is still worth taking seriously. If you want to know what evidence your child's forecast will rest on, ask the head of year which assessments feed it, and when the last of those falls.

faqs.question: The statement of entry shows a code we do not recognise. What do we do with it?
faqs.answer: Treat it as the most important line on the page and give it to the tutor before the first lesson. A four-digit code such as 0580, 0625 or 0620 is Cambridge; codes like 4MA1, 4PH1 or 4PM1 are Pearson Edexcel. The code, not the subject name, defines how many papers are sat, what content is assessed and which mark scheme applies. Two children at neighbouring UAE schools can both be doing IGCSE Maths and sit entirely different papers. Any tutor who does not ask for the code is planning on an assumption.

faqs.question: The mock came back at a grade 5 with twelve weeks to go. Where should one weekly hour go?
faqs.answer: Into the subject where the grade matters most, driven by the marked script rather than by the subject your child likes least. Twelve weeks at one session a week is around nine usable hours after the spring break and Eid. Nine hours will cover paper technique on every component plus the two weakest topics, which is a realistic job. Expect the pattern of lost marks to narrow before the grade moves; that is the order improvement usually arrives in. If two subjects are below target at this distance, alternating fortnights works only if written work is set in the off week.

faqs.question: Is there any point booking one-to-one hours during the UAE winter break?
faqs.answer: It depends on the distance to the series. With more than twenty weeks to go, a break is better spent resting and reading than on scheduled sessions, and the hours are worth more in term time alongside school teaching. Inside twelve weeks the calculation flips: a break week is one of the few periods where a student has a clear day, and one session plus independent paper work in that week is often worth two term-time sessions squeezed around a commute. Decide it against your own series date rather than as a general policy.

faqs.question: Ramadan begins three weeks before the first paper. Do sessions stop?
faqs.answer: They move rather than stop, and the move should be agreed in advance. School days shorten, afternoons go quiet and evenings run later, so a 4pm slot held through Ramadan usually loses two or three sessions before anyone admits it. A post-Iftar slot booked as a block for the whole month holds well for Year 11 students. Where that does not suit, a shorter midday session during the shortened school week with written work set for later keeps the sequence intact. A Ramadan revision plan agreed in January survives; one improvised in March does not.

faqs.question: What changes in our plan if the school enters our daughter for March rather than June?
faqs.answer: Everything downstream of the entry. The Cambridge March 2027 exam period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due 27 November 2026, so revision has to peak in January rather than April and the autumn term carries the content load. Results come on Cambridge Direct on 13 May 2027 with certificates in late June. The practical effect for a UAE family is that the winter break sits at the centre of the revision block rather than at the start of it, and a mock in January may fall after the real paper.

faqs.question: How soon after a result arrives do we have to decide on a review or a retake?
faqs.answer: Faster than most families expect, and both decisions run through the school. The enquiry-about-results window for asking a board to review a mark is measured in weeks from the result, not months, and the centre submits it rather than the parent. Separately, the next series has a final entry deadline of its own that falls well before its papers. So results day is a working day: read the subject-level marks, not just the grades, decide whether a mark sitting under a boundary justifies a review, and tell the exams officer that week if a retake entry is wanted.

faqs.question: Who should we ask for our child's exam dates: the school, the board or the tutor?
faqs.answer: The school's exams officer, every time. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that using the correct version of the timetable for your zone is essential, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. Pearson publishes provisional timetables and then revises them. That means a date copied from any tutoring page, this one included, is a starting point for a conversation rather than a plan. Confirm the zone and the live official timetable before the final fortnight is sequenced.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the English coursework portfolio that is due on Sunday?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach it and give feedback on a draft your daughter then revises herself. That means explaining how the marks are allocated against the published criteria, teaching the genre and register the task asks for, working through examples that are not her piece, and reading what she has written and telling her what is missing. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or edit any part of what is submitted. Providers in this market sell finished assessed work. The consequence of that falls on the student, which is why it is not something we will do at any price.

faqs.question: Our daughter's practical paper is in April and the school has run few practicals. Can that be made up?
faqs.answer: Largely, yes, and over video. What loses marks on a practical or alternative-to-practical paper is rarely the manipulation of apparatus. It is the results table drawn after the readings instead of before, the unit missing from a column heading, the anomalous point quietly dropped rather than identified, the line of best fit drawn through every cross, and the planning question answered without a control variable. All of that is taught from the student's own recorded data with the mark scheme open on screen. The apparatus work itself remains the school's job and should be raised with them.

faqs.question: When should the Ministry of Education equivalency file be opened?
faqs.answer: In Year 11, while subject choices can still influence the count, rather than after results. For the British track a student needs five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. A child taking nine subjects of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education has seven candidates for the count. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority; IB Gram does not perform or guarantee any part of the process.

faqs.question: Who publishes the AED figures on this page, and are they your prices?
faqs.answer: They are market figures, each attributed to the provider or source that published it, read in October 2026. EdFlik publishes from AED 45 to 65 an hour; Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; Unitors IGCSE from AED 150; TutorChase AED 270; BartyED AED 650. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table gives AED 180 to 350 for visits and AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists. None of those are IB Gram's prices. For what a plan would cost here, the honest answer comes from a consultation once we know the series, the subject and the number of weeks.

faqs.question: We asked for one-to-one at our villa in Al Ain. What is actually delivered?
faqs.answer: One-to-one IGCSE tuition over live video, at a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot, with one student and one teacher. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. The case for the online version in Al Ain is practical rather than ideological: the specialist is chosen for the syllabus code rather than for the length of the drive, the hour begins when your child sits down instead of when a car arrives, and the schedule survives study leave, Ramadan and travel weeks. The comparison table above sets out what changes.

faqs.question: Nobody is free for our subject at the time that suits us. What happens then?
faqs.answer: You get told, with the alternatives named. Some IGCSE subject and tier combinations have no UAE-based specialist free in the slot a family wants, and 0478 Computer Science, 0606 Additional Mathematics and Extended-tier sciences are the usual cases. The options are a different time in the same week, a specialist in another time zone teaching the same syllabus code, or a wait with a date attached. What we will not do is fill the slot with whoever is available and leave you to discover in February that the code was never the one on the entry.

faqs.question: Before we commit to a block of hours, what does the first session involve and what does it cost?
faqs.answer: The first session is a trial lesson offered without charge: one hour, live online, one tutor and one student, no card details taken beforehand and nothing owed if you stop there. It is used as the diagnostic described above - the facts from the statement of entry, one marked script read question by question, and a written note of what the lost marks have in common. Families who want the written backwards plan after it can ask for one. The only condition is that it is one trial per student, so it is worth having the marked script ready.

faqs.question: How far ahead do subject options need settling if we want a top grade in Maths?
faqs.answer: Before the entry closes, which in practice means the start of Year 11 at the latest. Two decisions matter. The first is the tier: a Core entry on a tiered Cambridge subject caps the grade that can be awarded, and the tier is written on the entry the school submits months before the papers. The second is whether Additional Mathematics sits alongside the main entry, which changes the workload and the calculus a student meets. If a target grade is needed for an A Level or Diploma place, the evidence for an Extended entry has to be built in Year 10.

1-to-1-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Start from your date, not from your worry

The first hour is a trial lesson at no charge, used to read a marked script rather than to sell a package. Lessons are one-to-one, live online over video, at a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot, anywhere in the Emirates.

intro.heading: Start with the ADEK report, then choose the tutor
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi is the emirate where a parent can read, in public, what a trained inspection team thought of their child's school. ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, licenses every private school here, inspects it against a published framework and puts the report online. Most families searching for IB and IGCSE tutors in Abu Dhabi have that document sitting in an email somewhere and have never opened it past the cover page. It is the cheapest diagnostic available to you, it was written by people who sat in your child's classrooms, and it costs nothing.

The report is useful because it separates two things a school report blurs together. Attainment is where a cohort sits against a standard. Progress is how far that cohort moved while it was in the building. A school can be judged Good for attainment in the sciences and Acceptable for progress, and that combination says something precise: students arrive able and leave about as able as they arrived. If your child's subject sits in that gap, an hour a week of one-to-one work is doing a different job from an hour of general revision, and it should be bought for a different reason.

The second thing the report hands you is a list of departments the inspectors named. Reports in this emirate routinely single out specific areas, upper-secondary mathematics, Arabic as an additional language, the quality of practical science work, rather than grading the school as one undifferentiated block. If a department was named, the school already knows and so do the other parents in that year group. That is the month to ask whether your child needs subject-specific support, instead of waiting for a Year 11 mock grade to make the argument for you.

What IB Gram does with that information is deliberately narrow. We match a student to a tutor by syllabus: board, subject, level, paper and code. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send anyone to an address in this emirate. Tuition for UAE families is delivered online, and our home-visit service exists only in India. The trade-off that choice involves is set out plainly in a comparison table further down, cost, travel time and tutor pool included, so you can weigh it rather than take our word for it.

The rest of this page is written for the decision a parent is making this term. What the inspection band means in practice. What tuition costs in AED and who published each figure. How Arabic and Islamic Studies sit alongside the Diploma under ADEK rules. Where internal assessment marks are won and lost, criterion by criterion. What a tutor is allowed to touch on coursework and what would put a diploma at risk. And the exam calendar counted backwards from results day. Read the sections you need and ignore the rest.

abu-dhabi.programmesIntro: Abu Dhabi private schools run the IB continuum, the English National Curriculum into IGCSE, American diploma routes and the UAE Ministry of Education curriculum, often on neighbouring streets. These are the four programmes families on this page ask about most, with what ADEK oversight means for each.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around six transdisciplinary themes and finishes with the Grade 5 exhibition, a student-led inquiry presented to the school community. There are no external exams, which is exactly why parents find it hard to judge progress. The signals worth watching are reading fluency, written stamina in a second language and number facts held in long-term memory, because these are the three that show up as gaps in MYP Year 7 rather than in the PYP report.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run PYP alongside ADEK-mandated Arabic and Islamic Education from the early years, so a Grade 3 student may be literate in two scripts at once. Support at this stage is almost always reading, handwriting and number fluency rather than subject tutoring, and it works best in short sessions twice a week rather than one long block after a full school day.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses eight subject groups against four criteria each, marked 0-8, converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. Criterion labels differ by subject: in sciences they run from knowledge and understanding to reflecting on the impacts of science. Students who have never been taught what criterion D asks for routinely lose a band there while scoring well on A. Year 11 MYP ends in the personal project, which is the first piece of long-form independent work most students attempt.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the MYP to Diploma transition is where most tutoring requests begin, because MYP criterion marking and DP paper marking reward different habits. A student with 6s in MYP mathematics can meet a hard wall in Analysis and Approaches Higher Level in DP1. Where a school's ADEK inspection rating flagged upper-secondary attainment, that wall tends to arrive earlier and steeper.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, each marked out of 7 for 42 points, plus up to 3 core points from the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Extended Essay, for a maximum of 45. The diploma is awarded at 24 points subject to conditions on HL and SL totals, core grades and failing conditions. Internal assessment carries 20 to 30 per cent of most subject grades, so coursework decides more of the final number than families expect.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi DP cohorts are small by international standards, which cuts both ways: teachers know every student, but a single Higher Level class may run with one teacher and no second opinion on a borderline internal assessment. That is the gap a subject specialist reviewing a draft against the published criteria is genuinely useful for, and it is the most common reason Abu Dhabi families ask for online IB Diploma tuition in DP1 rather than DP2.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge syllabuses carry four-digit codes, 0580 for Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 English First Language. Pearson Edexcel uses its own, 4MA1 for Mathematics A and 4PH1 for Physics. The split that matters is tiering: Cambridge Core and Extended set different papers with different grade ceilings, and Edexcel Foundation and Higher do the same. A student entered for the wrong tier can work hard all year and still be capped.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi families often discover mid-Year 10 that their school entered a different board from the one the previous school used, which changes the papers, the formula sheet and the practical arrangement. Anyone comparing IGCSE tuition in Abu Dhabi should ask the school for the syllabus code before booking anything, because 0580 and 4MA1 are taught differently even where the mathematics is identical.

abu-dhabi.subjectsIntro: These are the IB Diploma subjects Abu Dhabi families ask for most often, with what each one actually assesses and where marks tend to leak. Levels are listed because an HL request and an SL request are different jobs, not the same job with more hours.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which is where algebraic fluency is exposed. HL adds Paper 3, two extended response questions worth 20 per cent of the grade and unlike anything in the textbook. Proof, complex numbers and the calculus options are the usual pressure points for Abu Dhabi students arriving from MYP mathematics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator use runs throughout, so marks are lost less on arithmetic and more on interpretation: stating what a regression line means in context, choosing the right statistical test, reading a scenario correctly. HL adds graph theory, complex numbers in matrices and Paper 3. Strong AI candidates write cleaner sentences than strong AA candidates.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The 2023 syllabus is organised around five themes with HL extensions threaded through each. Paper 1 splits into multiple choice and a data analysis section; Paper 2 is extended response. Uncertainty treatment, graph gradients with units and the difference between a definition and an explanation are the recurring mark-losers in examiner reports.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity organise the current course, with HL material integrated rather than bolted on. Organic mechanisms, equilibrium calculations and energetics carry the most marks per hour of study. Paper 2 rewards students who show working in a stated sequence, because method marks survive an arithmetic slip and a bare answer does not.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms decide this subject. Outline, explain, distinguish and evaluate each demand a different shape of answer, and a well-informed student who writes the wrong shape scores badly. Data-based questions on unfamiliar experiments reward practice with real graphs rather than rereading notes.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a portfolio of three commentaries on different units, each capped at 800 words, built from published news articles. Students lose marks by summarising the article instead of applying a diagram and evaluating it. HL adds the quantitative paper, where calculation marks are available and routinely dropped.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The pre-released case study for Paper 1 rewards preparation more than almost any other component in the Diploma. Tool-based answers using Ansoff, BCG or decision trees earn marks that generic business prose cannot. HL candidates sit the additional paper with extended data response and need practice reading financial statements under time pressure.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis of non-literary extracts, Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied works. The Individual Oral is internally assessed on a global issue, with both a literary and a non-literary extract. HL adds the HL essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words. Most lost marks come from summary where analysis was asked for.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic A: Language and Literature suits students schooled in Arabic; Arabic B serves acquisition learners, with SL and HL reading and writing demands that differ sharply. Abu Dhabi students taking Arabic as an ADEK requirement alongside a Diploma subject in another language need distinct support for each, not one combined session.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper 1 tests concepts and problem-solving; Paper 2 covers the chosen option. The internal assessment is a working solution with documented design and evaluation, which fails most often on the criteria for success stated at the outset rather than on the code itself. HL adds abstract data structures and resource management.

abu-dhabi.igcseSubjectsIntro: IGCSE requests from Abu Dhabi families cluster in a narrow set of subjects, almost always in Year 11 and almost always after a mock. Syllabus codes are given because the paper structure, not the subject name, decides what a tutor needs to prepare.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (0580 Cambridge, 4MA1 Edexcel)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Extended candidates sit two papers; Edexcel Higher candidates sit two of equal weight. The common failure is a student on Core or Foundation tier who needs a grade the tier cannot award. Check the tier and the grade ceiling before buying a single hour of tuition.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625 Cambridge, 4PH1 Edexcel)
igcseSubjects.description: A Cambridge Extended candidate sits Paper 2 at 30 per cent, Paper 4 at 50 per cent and either the practical test or the alternative to practical at 20 per cent. Electricity and waves produce the lowest marks in examiner reports, and both respond well to past-paper drilling.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620 Cambridge, 4CH1 Edexcel)
igcseSubjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and the qualitative analysis tables carry disproportionate marks. The alternative-to-practical paper is learnable in a way the theory papers are not, because the same apparatus diagrams, safety points and anomalous-result questions recur series after series.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610 Cambridge, 4BI1 Edexcel)
igcseSubjects.description: Definitions must be reproduced exactly: osmosis, active transport, homeostasis. Students who paraphrase lose marks they understood perfectly well. Genetics and transport in plants are the topics most often revisited in the final six weeks before a June series.

igcseSubjects.name: English Language (0500 Cambridge, 4EA1 Edexcel)
igcseSubjects.levels: First Language and Second Language routes
igcseSubjects.description: Directed writing and the summary task reward technique rather than reading volume. A student who marks three past-paper responses against the published mark scheme with a tutor usually moves faster than one who writes six unmarked essays.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (0455 and 0450)
igcseSubjects.description: Both subjects reward diagram accuracy and the use of case material. Four-mark and six-mark questions have predictable structures, and students who learn those structures stop writing long answers that earn half the available marks.

abu-dhabi.regionsTitle: Communities we work with across the emirate
abu-dhabi.regionsIntro: Abu Dhabi tutoring is a scheduling problem before it is an academic one. Where a family lives decides when the school bus arrives, which means it decides when a session can realistically start. These notes are about timing and school catchment, not scenery.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi Island: Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah, Al Mushrif
regions.note: Short school runs and walkable catchments, so students are home early and a 16:30 start works. Families here are often choosing between a British sixth form and the Diploma, and ask for Year 11 support with that decision in mind.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Buses commonly drop between 15:30 and 16:15 depending on the route, so a 17:00 start holds all year while 16:00 does not. A parent searching for an IB tutor in Khalifa City is usually comparing us against a neighbour who drives in, and the comparison table below is the honest answer.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Al Raha Gardens IB tuition requests cluster around the Diploma years and the Middle Years to Diploma transition. Villa households often run two children on different programmes, which is a timetabling job as much as a teaching one.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: IB tutors for Saadiyat Island families deal with a high proportion of mid-year arrivals from other systems, so the first sessions are usually mapping what a student already knows onto the syllabus the school is actually teaching.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Activity schedules bite here more than traffic does. Swimming, football and music often own the early evening, so a weekend morning slot is frequently the only sustainable one and holds better than a weekday block that keeps moving.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Apartment living and short commutes mean students are home quickly, but shared study space is tight. Sessions that end with a written task and a photograph of the marked work help where a child has nowhere quiet to spread out.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Al Shamkha
regions.note: Longer bus routes push realistic start times towards 17:30. Families here ask most often for mathematics and physics at IGCSE, and for help with the Arabic requirement running alongside an English-medium timetable.

regions.name: Al Reef and Masdar City
regions.note: Both sit near the airport corridor, with school runs that cross the emirate rather than staying local. That commute is the main reason families here look at online tuition first instead of hiring someone who has to drive in and out.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi Island, Al Bateen and Al Reem
schoolClusters.note: The island cluster mixes IB continuum schools with British-curriculum schools that run IGCSE into A level or the Diploma. Students from these schools arrive with tight timetables and short commutes, and most requests are single-subject rather than general revision.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi
American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Al Reef
schoolClusters.note: The mainland corridor holds the emirate's largest concentration of IB and British-curriculum enrolment, and the longest bus routes. Sessions for students in this cluster are scheduled late afternoon or early evening, and sibling bookings are common in the same household.

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat, Yas and the newer mainland communities
schoolClusters.note: Newer communities draw a high share of families who moved mid-year from another country and another curriculum. The first job with these students is usually syllabus mapping: establishing what was covered elsewhere and what the current board expects.

abu-dhabi.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every request that reaches us from the emirate. All three are one-to-one and delivered over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and a scanned past paper annotated as the session runs.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, single subject
modes.description: One subject, one tutor, the same slot each week, running from the current topic in the school's scheme of work. The first two sessions are diagnostic: a past paper under timed conditions, marked against the real mark scheme, so the plan is built on a mark breakdown rather than on how the student feels about the subject. Parents receive what was covered and what was set after each session.

Slot moves inside the same week are usually workable

modes.title: Exam-term intensive, mocks to finals
modes.description: A short, dense block for the weeks between mock results and the written papers. Usually two or three sessions a week on the two or three topics a mock script shows are costing the most marks, with everything else deliberately left alone. This is the format Abu Dhabi families book in February and March, and it works best when the mock script itself is available rather than just the grade.

modes.title: Coursework review clinics
modes.description: Scheduled sessions on an internal assessment, the Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay, timed around the school's own draft deadlines. The tutor teaches the criteria, questions the argument, marks a draft against the published descriptors and names what is missing. The tutor does not supply text, data or a topic, and we say so to the student in the first session so that nobody is confused about where the line sits.

sections.heading: What an ADEK inspection band actually says about your child's subject
paragraphs: ADEK rates private schools on a six-band scale: Outstanding, Very Good, Good, Acceptable, Weak and Very Weak. The band printed on the cover is a synthesis of many separate judgements made inside the building, attainment and progress by phase and by subject, teaching and assessment, leadership, and the quality of the school's own self-evaluation. A parent who reads only the cover band has read the least useful page in the document. The judgements by phase and by subject are the part that tells you whether upper-secondary mathematics, or practical work in science, was where the inspection team stopped and wrote something specific.

An ADEK inspection rating is also not a permanent property of a school. Bands move between cycles, and they move most in the secondary phase, because an upper-secondary cohort is small enough that one strong or one struggling department shifts the overall picture. A school holding Very Good overall can carry an Acceptable judgement in a named subject across two inspection cycles without that showing up in anything a parent receives at home. If the named subject happens to be the one your child takes at Higher Level, the headline band is not the figure that matters to your family.

What we do with a report is practical rather than editorial. If a family tells us the subject judgement and the phase, a tutor can start from the same evidence the inspectors used: marked work, past-paper performance, and the distance between a predicted grade and an actual paper mark. The table below translates each band into what a parent should do next, which is a different question from what a regulator should do next. It is deliberately blunt about when extra hours are the wrong purchase.

sections.heading: Attainment, progress and the two numbers on a school report
paragraphs: Most Abu Dhabi private schools run an external baseline assessment, commonly CAT4 or MAP, alongside their internal grading. That gives a school two numbers for every student: what the child is achieving, and what a cohort with that baseline would typically achieve. The second number is the one that tells you whether a 5 is a good 5. A student with a strong verbal baseline sitting on a 4 in English Language and Literature is a different case from a student with a weaker baseline sitting on the same 4, and the two need different work.

Schools in the emirate do not always put both numbers in front of parents in a readable form, so the question to ask at a parents' evening is specific: what does the baseline predict for this subject, what is the current working grade, and which component is the gap concentrated in. A teacher can usually answer all three in ninety seconds. Without that answer, tutoring tends to default to covering the syllabus again from the start, which is the most expensive and least effective shape it can take.

Once the gap is located, the work is narrow. If the shortfall is in Paper 1 under timed conditions but not in Paper 2, the problem is pace and recall, not understanding. If a student loses marks on evaluation criteria in every internal assessment but scores well on data handling, the problem is a style of writing that nobody has taught explicitly. Both are fixable in a handful of sessions. Neither is fixable by rereading notes, which is what an unsupervised student does by default in the week before a mock.
bullets: Ask for the baseline prediction, the current working grade and the component where the gap sits
A single weak component is a technique problem; weakness across every component is a content problem
Marked scripts are worth more to a tutor than a term's worth of grade summaries
Request the mock script itself, not just the grade; schools in the emirate release it on request

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IB Diploma
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi teach more than the international curriculum they advertise. Under Ministry of Education rules applied through ADEK, Arabic is taught to all students in private schools, as a first language for Arabic-speaking students and as an additional language for others, with the year groups set by the regulator. Islamic Education is taught to Muslim students. Abu Dhabi schools also deliver the moral, social and cultural studies strand that replaced the earlier separate moral education and social studies courses. These subjects sit on the school timetable, not on the IB transcript, unless a student takes Arabic as an IB language subject.

The practical consequence catches Diploma families out every year. A DP1 student with six IB subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and a creativity, activity and service commitment is also carrying mandated lessons that are assessed by the school and recorded on the school report. That report is the document a UAE university or an equivalency application eventually reads. A student who quietly disengages from Arabic because it does not count towards 45 points can still create a problem for themselves at the paperwork stage two years later.

Support for these subjects is a genuinely different service from Diploma subject tutoring, and we treat it that way. Arabic as an additional language for a student who arrived in the emirate in Year 9 needs a language-acquisition tutor working on script, vocabulary and the school's own assessment format, not an Arabic A literature specialist. Where a family needs both, that is two tutors and two slots. Combining them into one session to save money reliably produces a child who makes progress in neither.
bullets: Arabic A for first-language students, Arabic B for acquisition learners: different courses, different tutors
Islamic Education applies to Muslim students and is assessed by the school

sections.heading: What tutoring costs in Abu Dhabi, in AED, and who published those numbers
paragraphs: Most tutoring pages aimed at UAE parents publish no price at all, and the two or three that do quote in US dollars, a currency no family here pays in. So here are the figures the market itself has published, in AED, with the source named for each band. These are market rates, not an IB Gram price list. Our own figure depends on the subject, the level and the tutor, is quoted before a trial lesson, and is discussed with a parent rather than printed as a headline.

Three things move a rate more than anything else: the level, the format and the time of year. Higher Level Diploma subjects and the sciences cost more than Middle Years support. In-home work carries the drive inside the hourly figure, whether or not the invoice itemises it. And rates firm up between January and April, when every family in the emirate has seen a mock result at the same time. A family that starts in October pays the quiet-season rate and gets the pick of the slots; a family that starts in March pays the busy-season rate and takes what is left.

Ask three questions of any quote before agreeing to it. Whether the rate includes the five per cent VAT, which is the most common hidden extra in this market. Whether it is per hour or per session, because a sixty-minute and a ninety-minute session are often quoted identically. And what happens to a paid session cancelled at short notice. Monthly packages circulate too: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits, both from published provider pages.

sections.heading: A home tutor in the emirate against one-to-one online
paragraphs: A parent typing home tutor into Google in Abu Dhabi is asking a reasonable question, so it deserves a straight answer rather than a redirection. Hiring someone to come to a villa in Khalifa City or an apartment on Al Reem works, and plenty of families do it. What they are buying includes a drive. Crossing between the island and the mainland communities at school-run time is routinely twenty-five to forty minutes each way, and a tutor doing two sessions an evening either prices that in, limits their radius to a few neighbouring compounds, or arrives late.

That radius is the real cost, because it sets the pool. The constraint on an in-home match is rarely teaching quality; it is geography. A Chemistry Higher Level specialist who can mark a Paper 2 energetics question against the real mark scheme, or a Mathematics Analysis and Approaches tutor who has taught Paper 3, may simply not live within a sensible drive of Al Reef. The usual outcome is a near-match: a capable physics teacher covering Chemistry HL, or a general mathematics tutor covering Analysis and Approaches. That near-match is where families lose the money, not on the hourly rate.

Online removes the radius and keeps the one-to-one. It is also honest to name what it does not do. A student who needs an adult physically present to stay at a desk is better served in the room. Laboratory technique with real apparatus cannot be replicated on a screen, so practical skills are taught from marked practical work and from the alternative-to-practical paper instead. Everything else, marking a script line by line, annotating a diagram together, working through a past paper under timed conditions, transfers without loss.

sections.heading: The exam calendar, counted backwards from results day
paragraphs: No competitor page serving UAE parents names a single exam session, registration deadline or results date, which is strange, because the calendar is what decides whether tutoring arrives in time to matter. The deadlines that actually bite are not the written papers. They are candidate registration, which the school controls and which closes months before anyone revises, and the internal assessment deadlines, which are set subject by subject and arrive while a student is still being taught new content.

The Diploma runs two sessions. The May session is the one most Abu Dhabi schools enter, with results released in early July; the November session suits students who arrived mid-cycle or who are retaking, with results in the first days of January. Registration for each closes with the IB roughly six months before the papers, through the school's Diploma coordinator rather than the family. After results there is a window for an enquiry upon results, where a script can be remarked, and that window is short.

IGCSE adds its own series. The June series is the main one for Abu Dhabi schools, with results in mid-August; November is a resit route, and Pearson Edexcel also runs a January series for some subjects. Entries are made by the school, typically in January and February for June, and a late change of tier or board after that point is difficult. sections.heading: Where internal assessment marks sit, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Internal assessment carries between a fifth and a third of most Diploma subject grades, it is marked by the school and moderated by the IB, and it is the only part of the Diploma a student can work on with unlimited time. That combination makes it the highest-value hour of tutoring available in DP1, and the one families most often leave until DP2. Every component is marked against published criteria identified by letter, with a stated mark allocation per criterion. A student who has never read those descriptors is guessing at where the marks are.

The pattern of lost marks is consistent and specific. In the sciences, criterion D on evaluation is where strong students drop furthest, because evaluating a method requires naming concrete limitations and realistic improvements rather than writing that more trials would help. In the mathematics exploration, personal engagement and reflection are worth six of twenty marks between them and are routinely treated as decoration. In History, criterion B carries fifteen of twenty-five marks, so an elegant source evaluation attached to a thin investigation cannot score well.

Length limits are enforced, and overshooting them costs marks or loses the examiner's attention at the exact point an argument should land. The sciences investigation is capped at 3,000 words, the History internal assessment at 2,200, each Economics commentary at 800, the Extended Essay at 4,000 and the Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,600. The mathematics exploration has no word cap, which students treat as freedom and examiners read as padding; twelve to twenty pages is the published guidance. Checking a draft against its limit and its criteria, before the supervisor sees it, is twenty minutes well spent.

sections.heading: What a tutor may touch on coursework, and what would put a diploma at risk
paragraphs: The IB requires a supervisor to declare that submitted work is the student's own, and runs submitted coursework through text-matching software. A tutor who writes a paragraph of an Extended Essay is not improving a grade; they are creating an academic misconduct case that can cost the whole diploma rather than one subject mark. This is the single clearest boundary in the work we do, and a family is entitled to know exactly where it sits before paying for an hour of coursework support.

Legitimate review is substantial and still stays on the right side of that line. A tutor can teach what each criterion rewards, mark a draft against the published descriptors, ask the questions that expose a vague research question, point out that an uncertainty analysis is missing, show the student a published exemplar at a known mark band, and explain why a conclusion does not follow from the data presented. All of that is teaching. What a tutor cannot do is supply text, supply data, choose the topic, or hand over a structure the student then fills in.

This matters in the UAE market more than it should, because the supply side here includes sites that sell finished work. One site serving this market advertises completed internal assessments at around AED 3,750. Buying that is a malpractice trigger, and it is also detectable: a supervisor who has watched a student work for six months recognises a document the student did not write. If any provider offers to produce assessed coursework, that offer alone tells you what the rest of the service is worth.

sections.heading: The school year, Ramadan hours and when revision actually happens
paragraphs: The Abu Dhabi school year runs from late August to early July, with term dates published by the regulator, a winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break in the second half of March. Those breaks matter for tutoring because they are the only blocks of time a student has without homework, and they fall at exactly the right distance from the written papers. The spring break in particular sits a few weeks before the May Diploma session and the June IGCSE series, which makes it the most productive revision window in the calendar.

Ramadan reshapes the second half of the year. Ramadan 1448 is expected to begin in the second week of February 2027, subject to moon sighting, and the regulator announces shortened school days for the month. That overlaps directly with mock season and with the heaviest internal assessment deadlines, so a family that plans nothing will find that four weeks of revision quietly disappear. The arrangement that works is a Ramadan tutoring schedule built around a post-Iftar slot, usually later in the evening and often shorter than the usual session, agreed before the month starts rather than improvised during it.

Across the whole year, four windows do most of the work. September and October, when a weekly session can still change which topics are understood rather than which are revised. The winter break, for internal assessment drafting. February and March, for mock follow-up and paper technique. And the spring break, for timed past papers under exam conditions. Study leave and the exam period itself are for sitting papers, not for starting new work, and we would rather pause a booking than sell sessions in a week when a student should be resting.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency and attestation for an Abu Dhabi school leaver
paragraphs: A Diploma or an IGCSE and A level stack is recognised internationally, but a UAE university, a government employer or a national scholarship route will ask for an equivalency certificate from the Ministry of Education confirming the qualification against the UAE secondary certificate. No competitor page in this market mentions the process at all, which is how families end up discovering it in the week results arrive. It is administrative rather than difficult, and the only thing that makes it painful is starting late.

The order of operations matters. The school issues results and a transcript. Those documents are attested through the channels the school and the ministry direct. The equivalency application is then submitted with the attested certificate, the transcript, identity documents and proof of the years of schooling completed. The requirement that trips families is subject coverage: the ministry sets which subjects, and how many, must appear on the certificate, and that list is revised from time to time. A student who dropped a subject in DP1 for sensible timetable reasons can find it was one the ministry expects.

So the useful move is early and cheap. In Year 11, or at the start of DP1, ask the Diploma coordinator or the head of sixth form to confirm the current equivalency expectations against the subject choice in front of you, in writing. If a required subject is on the list and the student is weak in it, that is the subject to support, whatever else is going on. Tutoring cannot alter a transcript after the event, but it can keep a student in a required subject that they would otherwise have abandoned.

process.title: Tell us the school, the board and the paper
process.description: The useful first message names the school, the programme, the subject, the level and, for IGCSE, the syllabus code. If you have the ADEK inspection rating for the school or a marked mock script, send those too. Those details decide which tutor fits; a request for maths help does not.

process.title: We match on syllabus, not on postcode
process.description: We look for a tutor who has taught and marked the exact components your child sits, then check availability against your household timetable in Gulf Standard Time. Because lessons are online, the match is not limited to people who could drive to Khalifa City or Al Reef on a weekday evening.

process.title: A free trial lesson, with the parent welcome to sit in
process.description: The trial is a working session rather than a sales call. The tutor usually sets a short past-paper task, marks it live and explains where the marks went. Parents are welcome to listen. If the fit is wrong, say so and we match again rather than asking you to persevere.

process.title: Four weeks of diagnostics before any promises
process.description: The first month establishes a baseline from marked work: which components lose marks, whether the problem is content, pace or technique, and what a realistic target looks like. You get a written note after each session. No tutor on this platform predicts a grade, because nobody honestly can.

process.title: If no specialist is free, we say so
process.description: Some combinations are genuinely scarce, Higher Level Computer Science at a particular hour, Arabic A literature at a specific level, a Paper 3 specialist in the three weeks before a session. When nothing fits, we tell you that and when it might change, rather than placing a near-match and letting you find out later.

whyPoints.title: We read the ADEK report before we match
whyPoints.description: The regulator publishes subject and phase judgements for every private school in the emirate. Using them means a tutor starts with evidence about where a school's teaching is strongest and weakest, instead of starting with a parent's understandable but imprecise sense that something is wrong.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the syllabus code, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: Mathematics 0580 and 4MA1 are not the same course to teach, and Analysis and Approaches is not Applications and Interpretation with harder numbers. We match on the code, the tier and the paper, which is why we ask for details that feel excessive in a first message.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built for Gulf Standard Time
whyPoints.description: Sessions are set in local time around the school bus, activity schedules and, during Ramadan, a post-Iftar slot. Where a family travels between the emirate and abroad through the year, the same tutor keeps the slot rather than the booking lapsing and restarting with someone new.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on academic honesty
whyPoints.description: Tutors coach internal assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essays against the published criteria. They do not write them, supply data or choose topics. We state that to the student at the first session, because an unclear line is how a well-meaning family ends up in a malpractice case.

whyPoints.title: Market pricing published with its sources
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page come from named competitor pages and published rate tables, not from us. That lets a family judge any quote, including ours, against what the market actually charges. Our figure is quoted before a trial lesson and never presented as a market average.

whyPoints.title: Independent, with no school or board connection
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. We hold no formal connection with any Abu Dhabi school, with ADEK or with any awarding body, which is also why nothing on this page should be read as an official statement of a school's performance or a regulator's requirements.

faqs.question: What does an ADEK inspection rating tell me about whether my child needs a tutor?
faqs.answer: More than the overall band suggests. Read past the cover page to the judgements by phase and by subject. If attainment in upper-secondary mathematics is rated below the rest of the school, and your child takes a Higher Level mathematics course, that is a concrete reason to add support in that subject and only that subject. If the school is strong in the subject but your child is not, the problem is individual and the diagnostic question changes. Either way the report tells you where the school's teaching is reliable, which is exactly the information a parent otherwise has to guess at.

faqs.question: How much do IB and IGCSE tutors in Abu Dhabi charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in the UAE run from about AED 45 an hour for a university-student tutor online to AED 650 for a named specialist. EdFlik lists from AED 45 to 65, Unitors from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, TutorChase at AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350. Those are market figures from those providers, not our price list. Our own rate depends on subject, level and tutor, and is quoted before the free trial lesson so you can compare it against the bands above.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor or an online tutor the better choice for a Khalifa City family?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is scarce for you. If a genuine specialist in your child's subject and level lives a short drive away and has the slot you need, hiring locally is a reasonable choice. In practice the constraint is the radius: a Chemistry Higher Level specialist who has marked Paper 2 may not live near Khalifa City, so families end up with a near-match on subject. Online keeps the one-to-one teaching and drops the geography, so the match is made on the component your child actually sits. Lessons with us are online only in the UAE.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Abu Dhabi need a permit from the authorities?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and every official source we could check states that the permit itself is issued free of charge. Employed residents generally need their employer's agreement before tutoring privately, and the permit covers an individual tutoring privately rather than running a centre, which is a separate licence. We do not publish penalty amounts, because the ministry has not specified them publicly and the figures circulating online could not be verified against any official source.

faqs.question: Which Abu Dhabi schools do your tutors work with students from?
faqs.answer: Students come to us from across the emirate: the island cluster around Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, Saadiyat and Yas, and the newer mainland communities towards Al Shamkha. Because teaching is online, the relevant question is not which schools we are near but which boards and components a tutor has taught. We ask for the school name so a tutor knows the scheme of work and assessment calendar in use. We have no connection with any school named on this page, and naming one implies nothing about the school.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my daughter's Chemistry internal assessment without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can teach what each criterion rewards, review a draft against the published descriptors, point out that the evaluation section names no concrete limitation, question whether the conclusion follows from the data, and show an exemplar at a known mark band. A tutor cannot choose the research question, supply data, write or rewrite text, or hand over a structure to fill in. Your daughter's supervisor signs an authenticity declaration and the work goes through text-matching software, so the boundary protects her diploma rather than restricting the help she can have.

faqs.question: How many marks is the IB sciences internal assessment worth and what are its criteria?
faqs.answer: The scientific investigation is marked out of 24 across four criteria: A research design, B data analysis, C conclusion and D evaluation, each worth 6 marks, and it is capped at 3,000 words. It counts for 20 per cent of the final grade at both Higher and Standard Level in Biology, Chemistry and Physics. Criterion D is where able students lose most, because evaluating a method means naming specific limitations and realistic improvements rather than writing that more repeats would help. Knowing the mark split changes how a student allocates the weeks they have.

faqs.question: Does my child still have to take Arabic and Islamic Studies while doing the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Private schools in Abu Dhabi teach Arabic to all students under Ministry of Education rules applied through ADEK, as a first language for Arabic speakers and as an additional language for others, with the year groups set by the regulator. Islamic Education applies to Muslim students, and Abu Dhabi schools also deliver the moral, social and cultural studies strand. These are assessed by the school and recorded on the school report rather than on the IB transcript. Confirm the exact requirements for your child's year group with the school registrar, because the regulator revises them periodically.

faqs.question: What is Ministry of Education equivalency and when should an Abu Dhabi student apply?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is the ministry's assessment of an international qualification against the UAE secondary certificate, and UAE universities, government employers and some scholarship routes ask for it. The application needs the attested certificate and transcript, identity documents and evidence of years of schooling completed. Start earlier than the paperwork suggests: the ministry sets which subjects must appear on the certificate, and that list is revised, so confirm it with your Diploma coordinator in Year 11 or DP1 rather than after results. MoE equivalency for IB students is administrative, not difficult, unless a required subject was dropped two years earlier.

faqs.question: When do registration deadlines and results dates fall for the May and November IB sessions?
faqs.answer: Schools register May-session candidates with the IB around mid-November of the preceding year, and November-session candidates around mid-May of the same year. Written papers run late April to late May for the May session and October to mid-November for the November one. Results have landed in early July and in the first days of January respectively in recent sessions, each followed by a short window for a remark. Cambridge and Edexcel June series results arrive in mid-August. Your Diploma coordinator or exams officer confirms the exact dates for your child's cohort.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to after Iftar during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we would rather agree that before the month begins than improvise during it. The regulator announces shortened school days for Ramadan, and Ramadan 1448 is expected to start in the second week of February 2027, subject to moon sighting. That lands on top of mock season and the heaviest coursework deadlines, so families who plan nothing lose about four weeks of revision. A post-Iftar slot, often shorter than the usual session, holds better than an afternoon one. Tell us your preferred pattern in January and we will set it with the tutor.

faqs.question: My son sits IGCSEs in June and we are only starting in February. Is that too late?
faqs.answer: It is late enough to change what you should buy, not too late to be worth buying. With roughly fourteen weeks left, broad syllabus coverage is the wrong purchase. The productive version starts from the marked mock script, identifies the two or three topics costing the most marks, and spends the time on those plus paper technique: timing, command terms and showing working so method marks survive a slip. Spring break is the strongest revision window in the Abu Dhabi calendar. What nobody can honestly offer at this stage is a predicted outcome.

faqs.question: Should my child take Maths AA or Maths AI for a UAE university application?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches is the algebra and proof route and is the one expected by most engineering, physics, computer science and economics programmes, in the UAE and abroad. Applications and Interpretation is statistics and modelling led, calculator throughout, and suits business, social science, design and life science routes. The decision should be made against the written entry requirements of the specific programmes your child is considering, not against which course looks easier. Our Maths AA and AI tutors routinely see students who chose by reputation in DP1 and regretted it in DP2.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for the subject and the time we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we tell you when it might change. Some combinations are genuinely scarce: Higher Level Computer Science in a narrow evening window, Arabic A literature at a particular level, or a Paper 3 specialist in the three weeks before a session when everyone wants one. The alternative is placing a near-match and letting a family discover the gap in April, which costs them more than waiting. Where it helps, we suggest a different slot, a fortnightly pattern or a short diagnostic block with a specialist rather than a weekly commitment.

faqs.question: How do sessions fit around an Abu Dhabi school bus and the homework that follows?
faqs.answer: By being scheduled after the bus, not before homework. Khalifa City and Al Raha routes commonly drop between 15:30 and 16:15, so a 17:00 start holds across a term while a 16:00 start collapses the first time traffic is heavy. Al Shamkha and Al Reef routes push that later again. We set one fixed weekly slot, keep sessions to sixty or ninety minutes, and set a task that connects to the school's own homework rather than adding a parallel workload. Weekend mornings work well where weekday evenings are crowded with activities.

faqs.question: Do your tutors cover both Cambridge and Edexcel for IGCSE sciences?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the distinction matters more than parents expect. Cambridge 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology set an Extended candidate a multiple-choice paper at 30 per cent, a theory paper at 50 per cent and either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper at 20 per cent. Edexcel 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 structure their papers differently and assess practical skills within the written papers. Extended Essay support in Abu Dhabi and Diploma work aside, the single most useful thing you can send us for IGCSE is the syllabus code from the school.

abu-dhabi.closingHeading: Start with the report, then the paper, then the tutor
abu-dhabi.closingBody: If you do one thing after reading this page, open your school's ADEK inspection report and find the judgement for your child's subject and phase. Then ask the teacher three questions: what the baseline predicts, what the current working grade is, and which component the gap sits in. With those answers, matching a tutor takes a short conversation rather than a trial-and-error term. Send us the school, the board, the level and the syllabus code, and we will tell you plainly whether we have a specialist free for that component and that hour, or whether you would be better served waiting a few weeks for one.
