intro.heading: Ajman sits under a different regulator, and that changes what you can learn about a school
paragraphs: Four emirates run their own school regulator. Dubai has KHDA. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have ADEK. Sharjah has SPEA. Ajman has none of them. Private schools here are licensed and inspected federally, by the Ministry of Education, along with those in Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain. The practical consequence for a parent is simple and rarely stated: the published record of your child's school in Ajman is thinner, and organised differently, than the report a neighbour in Jumeirah can pull up in two clicks. Choosing academic support here starts with knowing exactly what a Ministry of Education school inspection covers and what it leaves for you to ask about yourself.

A UAE inspection, under any of the regulators, judges a school on attainment and progress in a fixed set of subjects, phase by phase: Islamic Education, Arabic as a first language, Arabic as an additional language, English, mathematics and science, split across foundation, primary, middle and secondary. It also judges teaching, assessment, curriculum, protection and safeguarding, and leadership. Each judgement is drawn from the same six-band scale, from Outstanding down to Very Weak, with Acceptable set as the minimum the country expects. That is genuinely useful information. What it is not is a verdict on how well Chemistry is taught at Higher Level to a class of nine Year 13 students, because no inspection framework in the UAE reports at that resolution.

That gap matters more in Ajman than in Dubai, because the cohorts are smaller. A Diploma year group of thirty or forty students cannot run every option block. Higher Level sets fill with four or five students or they do not run at all, and a subject that was offered when your child chose it in Year 11 can quietly become a self-study arrangement by the middle of Year 12. One teacher leaving mid-course moves the whole set. None of this shows up in a whole-school band, and none of it is a criticism of the school: it is arithmetic. It is also the single most common reason an Ajman family starts looking for a subject specialist.

IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform, not a school and not an agency with a van. Tuition for families in Ajman is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Ajman; home visits are a service we run only in India, and saying so plainly is more useful than pretending otherwise. The trade is deliberate. A family in Al Mowaihat gets a tutor who has taught Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level and marked its exploration against criterion E, instead of whoever is willing to drive out from Sharjah at seven in the evening.

The rest of this page is built in that order. First the regulator and how to read an inspection band without over-reading it. Then what tuition actually costs in this market, in AED, with the source of every figure named. Then the exam calendar counted backwards from the session your child sits, the Internal Assessment criteria by letter with their marks attached, the academic-honesty line a tutor may not cross, the Arabic and Islamic Education requirements that run alongside an international curriculum, and what Ministry of Education equivalency asks for when a school leaver applies to a UAE university. Nothing on this page is a promise about a grade. All of it is information you can check.

ajman.programmesIntro: Ajman carries a full IB continuum school alongside a large British and Indian sector, so a family here may be dealing with PYP report descriptors in one year group and Cambridge tier decisions in another. These are the four programme frames tuition is usually requested against, with what each one means for a student sitting in Ajman.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external exams. Progress is reported against learner-profile attributes and transdisciplinary units, which is why PYP reports read so differently from the marks-based reports a parent may expect. Support at this stage is mostly about securing number fluency, reading stamina and the habit of writing to a prompt, so that the move into MYP criteria is not the first time a child meets a rubric.
programmes.countryNote: In Ajman the PYP cohort is concentrated in a single continuum school, so there is no second PYP intake to move to if a year group does not suit. Primary requests here are usually for English reading age and for maths number work, and they come from parents comparing a PYP report with a cousin's CBSE marksheet and finding no common scale between them.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks every subject against four criteria, A to D, each out of 8, and converts the total to a 1-7 grade through published boundaries. MYP 5 can end in on-screen eAssessment and the IB MYP Certificate. The criteria are where marks are won and lost: a student who can do the science but cannot write a criterion D evaluation loses a quarter of the available marks without ever getting a question wrong.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to Diploma transition is the pressure point for Ajman families, because the local Diploma cohort is small and option blocks are decided early. A student aiming at Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level needs the MYP extended maths route, and that decision is often made in Year 9, two years before anyone in the family is thinking about a Diploma at all.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, scored 1-7, plus up to three core points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, for a maximum of 45 and a minimum pass of 24 with conditions attached. Higher Level is not the same course with more homework: Mathematics AA HL adds Paper 3, worth 20% of the grade and sat as an extended problem-solving paper with no equivalent at Standard Level.
programmes.countryNote: An Ajman Diploma student is often one of a handful taking a given Higher Level subject, which means less in-class differentiation and a timetable built around what the school can staff. That is where an online IB tutor in Ajman does most good: a weekly hour on the specific Higher Level content the set is thin on, run alongside school rather than repeating it.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Graded 9-1 in most subjects, with tiering decisions that cap the grade before the exam is sat. Cambridge splits many subjects into Core and Extended, so 0580 Core candidates take Papers 1 and 3 and cannot be awarded above grade 5 equivalence, while Extended candidates take Paper 2 non-calculator and Paper 4 with a calculator, each worth 50%. Edexcel International GCSE Maths A, 4MA1, tiers as Foundation and Higher instead.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman's British-curriculum schools do not all use the same board, and some mix boards by subject, so the first question for any IGCSE tutor in Ajman is which syllabus code the school entered. Cambridge IGCSE 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 cover similar mathematics but set it out in different papers with different formula provision, and revising from the wrong board's past papers wastes a term.

ajman.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma and Middle Years subjects Ajman families request most, with what each one is actually assessed on. Weightings are taken from the current subject guides; your school's coordinator will confirm which guide a cohort is working to, because the IB revises them on a rolling cycle.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Higher Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 carry 30% each and Paper 3 adds 20% as a two-question extended investigation. At Standard Level, Papers 1 and 2 are 40% each. Marks go missing in proof, calculus technique and the unstructured reasoning Paper 3 demands, which almost no school has time to practise properly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-active throughout, with statistics, modelling and, at Higher Level, graph theory and complex numbers. Higher Level also carries a Paper 3. The common failure is treating AI as the easier route and then meeting a modelling question that requires choosing the function, justifying it and criticising the fit.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Paper 1 splits into multiple choice and a data-based section for 36%, Paper 2 is 44%, and the scientific investigation is 20%. Organic mechanisms and energetics are where IB Chemistry HL students lose the most, usually because they can recall a reaction but cannot explain it with curly arrows and a named reagent.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Same assessment shape as Chemistry: Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44%, investigation at 20%. The Higher Level extension in fields, induction and quantum physics is where a thin set shows. Students who can manipulate the algebra still drop marks on the explanation command terms, where a formula earns nothing on its own.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy, with Paper 1 at 36% and Paper 2 at 44%, and a scientific investigation worth 20%. The marks are in precision of language: an answer that says a membrane is permeable where the mark scheme wants partially permeable scores zero, and that pattern repeats across the whole paper.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis of unseen non-literary texts is 35% at both levels. Higher Level adds the HL essay at 20%, written on a text studied, in 1,200 to 1,500 words. The Individual Oral is where most students under-prepare, because it is assessed on a global issue they chose themselves.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Productive writing, reading and listening papers plus an individual oral. A strong speaker can still score poorly, because the oral is marked on language, message and interactive skills against descriptors rather than on fluency. Ajman's multilingual cohorts often sit English B when English A would actually suit them better.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three 800-word commentaries form the portfolio, worth 30% at Standard Level and 20% at Higher Level, with Higher Level adding Paper 3 quantitative questions. Diagrams are the fastest marks on the paper and the most commonly wasted, because a diagram that is drawn but never referred to in the text earns almost nothing.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with a pre-released case for Paper 1 and an internal assessment worth 30% at Standard Level and 25% at Higher Level. Students lose marks by describing a tool rather than applying it to the organisation in front of them, and by leaving the evaluation command terms until the last paragraph.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Productive writing, a receptive paper covering listening and reading, and an individual oral. For students who speak Arabic at home but have been schooled in English, the written register is the obstacle rather than the vocabulary, and the fix is structured practice against the text-type conventions the paper expects.

ajman.igcseSubjectsIntro: Ajman's British-curriculum sector runs both Cambridge and Edexcel, sometimes within one school. The syllabus code is the thing to establish before any revision plan is written, because papers, tiering and formula provision differ between boards even where the content looks identical.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge IGCSE 0580 Extended now sets Paper 2 without a calculator and Paper 4 with one, 50% each, which has caught out cohorts drilled on older past papers. Edexcel 4MA1 Higher provides a different formula sheet. Tier choice caps the grade, so it is a decision worth revisiting in Year 11.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge runs multiple choice at 30%, theory at 50% and either the practical test or the alternative to practical at 20%. Electricity circuits and moments are the reliable losers. Students sitting the alternative to practical need taught exam technique, not more laboratory time, because it tests how experiments are described.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and the qualitative analysis tables are where Extended candidates separate from Core candidates. The analysis tables can be learned outright for straightforward marks, and most students never do. Edexcel's single-tier paper assumes the full content, with no Core safety net underneath it.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Long-answer questions reward recall expressed in the syllabus's own words. Genetics, transport in plants and the control of blood glucose produce the widest mark spread. Practice should be marked against the published scheme every time, because self-marking consistently flatters a student by a grade.

igcseSubjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / Edexcel 4EA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response carry most of the marks, and both are assessed on reading as much as on writing. Students with strong spoken English routinely under-score because they answer the text rather than analysing the writer's method, which is what the mark scheme pays for.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
igcseSubjects.description: Two papers, with structured data response carrying the heavier weight. Definitions earn marks outright and are often skipped. Diagram accuracy, especially shifting the right curve in the right direction, is the difference between a 6 and an 8 for most candidates in this subject.

igcseSubjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (Cambridge 0508)
igcseSubjects.description: Reading comprehension and composition in formal Arabic. Ajman students who speak dialect at home and English at school often meet Modern Standard Arabic only in this exam, which makes the register, not the content, the thing to work on across Years 10 and 11.

ajman.regionsTitle: Ajman district by district, and what each one does to a session time
ajman.regionsIntro: Ajman is compact at the coast and then suddenly is not: the emirate includes two inland exclaves that sit a long drive from the city. Where a family lives changes the earliest realistic start time and, in the exclaves, whether a local specialist exists at all.

regions.name: Al Nuaimiya
regions.note: The densest part of Ajman city and home to several of the emirate's long-established private schools. Most children here are within fifteen minutes of the school gate, so the constraint on IGCSE tuition in Al Nuaimiya is the shape of the evening rather than travel time.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Mixed apartment and villa blocks running back from the Corniche. A short school run means a 4.30pm start is realistic here, which is early by UAE standards and worth using, because a tired 8pm session is a wasted hour however good the tutor is.

regions.name: Al Jurf
regions.note: The industrial and school belt along Sheikh Ammar Road, with some of Ajman's largest Indian-curriculum intakes. Bus routes out of Al Jurf are long, so families here often find 5.30pm the first honest slot once a child has eaten.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Villa districts whose working parents commute to Dubai over Emirates Road. Sessions that need a parent in the room do not start before 7pm on a weekday, which is exactly why a fixed weekly slot booked in advance works better here than an ad hoc arrangement.

regions.name: Al Zahya and Al Tallah
regions.note: Newer development close to Emirates Road and to Ajman's IB continuum provision. This is where the emirate's PYP, MYP and Diploma families are concentrated, and where requests for Higher Level sciences and Mathematics AA cluster.

regions.name: Al Helio and Al Rawda
regions.note: Residential expansion inland from the city, with children bussed in several directions to different curricula. A household here can be running a Cambridge Year 11 and an MYP Year 8 on the same evening, which makes back-to-back online slots far easier than two visits.

regions.name: Ajman Corniche and Al Rumailah
regions.note: Older apartment stock near the waterfront. A noticeable share of these children attend schools across the Sharjah border, so their term dates and mock timetables follow SPEA-regulated schools rather than Ajman ones, and revision has to be planned against the school's calendar.

regions.name: Masfout
regions.note: Ajman's inland exclave, roughly a hundred kilometres from the city and close to the Hatta road. There is no meaningful local market for a Diploma subject specialist, so online tuition in Masfout is not a compromise here; it is the only route to a Higher Level subject teacher.

regions.name: Manama
regions.note: The emirate's second exclave, inland beyond Al Dhaid. Families here face the same arithmetic as Masfout: a two-hour round trip to reach the coastal tutoring market, against a scheduled video session that starts when the school bus gets back.

regions.name: Emirates City and Al Alia
regions.note: Tower developments beside Emirates Road with a largely commuter population. Weekend sessions are popular here, and Friday or Saturday morning slots are easier to hold through exam term than a weekday evening that competes with a parent's drive home.

schoolClusters.city: Ajman city: Al Nuaimiya, Al Rashidiya and Al Jurf
schoolClusters.note: The established sector, weighted towards Indian and British curricula with large year groups at primary and a narrowing at Year 12. Tuition requests from this cluster are dominated by IGCSE maths and sciences in Years 10 and 11.

sections.heading: Who inspects a private school in Ajman, and what the report actually contains
paragraphs: Ajman's private schools are licensed and inspected by the federal Ministry of Education. There is no emirate-level authority here the way KHDA exists for Dubai, ADEK for Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, and SPEA for Sharjah. The same federal arrangement covers Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain, which between them get almost no coverage from tutoring companies at all. If you have moved from Dubai, the first thing you will notice is that the familiar annual report with its colour-coded subject grid is not where you expect to find it.

What an inspection does contain is a judgement on attainment and progress in a defined subject set, phase by phase, plus judgements on teaching, assessment, curriculum, the protection and safeguarding of students, and leadership. Those judgements use one six-band scale across the country. A school rated Good in secondary English has been judged above the minimum expected standard for that phase in that subject. That is a real finding and worth reading.

What it does not contain is anything about the set your child actually sits in. No UAE framework reports on a named Higher Level class, on which option blocks ran this year, or on how long the person teaching Mathematics AA Paper 3 has taught that syllabus. Those are the three questions that determine whether a Diploma student needs outside support, and all three are answered by the school rather than by the regulator. Ask them in writing, ask them before the option deadline, and ask again in September when staffing is settled.

This is why the honest starting point for support in Ajman is not a league table. It is a short, specific conversation with the school about staffing and sets, followed by a decision about which single subject is worth an hour a week. A parent who does that usually spends less than one who buys three subjects of general tuition on the strength of a whole-school band.

sections.heading: Reading an inspection band from Outstanding down to Very Weak
paragraphs: The six bands are Outstanding, Very Good, Good, Acceptable, Weak and Very Weak, and Acceptable is defined as the minimum standard expected of a private school in the UAE. That definition is the part most parents miss. Acceptable does not mean adequate in the casual sense; it means the school has met the floor and nothing above it. A large number of private schools nationally sit at Good or Acceptable, which means the band on its own rarely separates two schools a family is choosing between.

Read the band as a filter, not a verdict. A Weak or Very Weak judgement is a reason to read the whole report, because the weakness is usually concentrated in particular phases or departments rather than spread evenly, and the phase your child is in may not be the affected one. The reverse also holds: an Outstanding school can have a department that lost two teachers in July, and the inspection that produced the band may predate that.

The most useful lines in any report are the ones about progress rather than attainment. Attainment tells you where a cohort arrived; progress tells you what the school added. A cohort with high attainment and acceptable progress is a cohort being carried by its intake, and a student in the middle of that distribution can drift for a full year without a single report flagging it. That is the student who most often turns out to need one hour a week on one subject.
Then stop reading and start asking. The table below is how to translate each band into a question for the school office, because the question is where the useful answer lives.

sections.heading: Why a good school judgement can still leave a Diploma subject uncovered
paragraphs: Cohort size is the mechanism. A Diploma year group of forty students choosing six subjects each generates a timetable with hard constraints: subjects are grouped into option blocks, and a block runs only if enough students pick it. In a large Dubai school, Chemistry at Higher Level, Economics at Higher Level and Visual Arts can all run in parallel. In a small Ajman cohort, two of those three will share a block, and a student who wanted both is told to choose. No inspection band captures that, because the school is not doing anything wrong.

The second mechanism is staffing depth. A school with one chemist can teach Chemistry at both levels competently until that chemist leaves in July, at which point an entire Year 13 set is taught by someone meeting the syllabus for the first time. Most schools handle this well. Some handle it by asking students to self-study a Higher Level option, which is a legitimate response to a staffing gap and a very poor arrangement for a sixteen-year-old carrying three other Higher Levels.

The third is the quiet one: assessment literacy. Diploma marks are awarded against command terms and mark schemes, not against general competence. A student can understand electromagnetic induction and still score four out of eight on it, because the question said explain and the answer gave an equation. In a set of five, with a teacher covering content at speed, nobody is marking enough practice for that pattern to be noticed, let alone fixed. It is the single most common thing an IB Diploma tutor in Ajman is actually asked to repair.

None of this argues against the school. It argues for diagnosing at the level of the subject and the paper. Ask which blocks ran. Ask who teaches the Higher Level set. Ask to see a marked past-paper script. Three answers tell you more than any band.

sections.heading: What IB and IGCSE tuition costs in Ajman and the northern emirates
paragraphs: Almost nobody in this market publishes a number. Of the competitor pages reviewed for this page, three gave no price at all, and two quoted in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. So here are the AED bands as the market actually advertises them, with the source of each figure named, and with one thing stated plainly: these are market rates, not an IB Gram price list.

The spread is wide because the tiers are genuinely different products. At the bottom, a budget online tutor is frequently a university student supervising homework. In the middle sits a qualified subject teacher who has taught the paper. At the top is someone with examiner familiarity, who can tell a student what a mark scheme pays for in a question they have not seen. A family in Ajman buying at the bottom of the range for a Higher Level subject usually ends up buying twice.

Travel is the hidden variable. An in-home rate quoted locally carries the tutor's journey inside it, and an Ajman address sits outside the dense Dubai tutor belt where that journey is short. The same hour costs more here than in Jumeirah for reasons that have nothing to do with teaching. Monthly packages advertised in the market show the same pattern: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, against roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits.

Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session land at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Use those as a planning figure for a full academic year rather than a quote. IB Gram's own arrangement is discussed on a free consultation, after a trial session, because the honest answer depends on the subject, the level and how many weeks remain before the paper.

sections.heading: One-to-one online against the in-home market, for an Ajman address
paragraphs: Home tuition is what parents in this market search for, and the question deserves a straight answer rather than a redirection. In-home tuition sold locally works like this: you pay the hourly rate plus the journey, the pool of available people is whoever will drive to your district on a weekday evening, and the earliest start is set by that person's own commute. For a family in Al Nuaimiya, that pool is workable. For a family in Masfout or Manama, it is close to empty.

IB Gram delivers tuition for UAE families as one-to-one online lessons over live video. We do not send anyone to an address in Ajman, and the in-home service we run exists only in India. The case for online here is not that it is cheaper, although it usually is once travel is stripped out. The case is the size of the pool. A Higher Level Chemistry specialist who has marked the scientific investigation does not have to live within a twenty-minute drive of Al Jurf to teach your child, and in this emirate they almost certainly do not.

There is a real trade-off, and pretending otherwise is how tutoring companies lose trust. A younger child who needs someone physically turning the page benefits from presence in a way video cannot replicate. A student who will not sit still for an hour unsupervised needs a parent in the room for the first few sessions. For Years 10 to 13, working on papers, mark schemes and coursework criteria, the screen-shared document is often the better tool, because the mark scheme, the script and the annotation are all visible to both people at once.

sections.heading: The exam calendar counted backwards from an Ajman school year
paragraphs: Not one competitor page reviewed for this set names an exam session, a registration deadline or a results date. That is a strange omission, because the calendar is the only part of this process with hard dates in it, and every useful decision about tuition is a function of how many weeks remain. The IB runs two sessions a year, May and November. Cambridge runs June and November series. Edexcel International GCSE adds a January series, which matters for schools that enter modular units.

Registration is done by the school, not by the family, through the Diploma coordinator or the exams officer. The IB's final registration point for a May session falls in the middle of the preceding November, and for a November session in the middle of the preceding May. Cambridge and Edexcel entry deadlines sit earlier than parents expect, and tier decisions, Core against Extended or Foundation against Higher, are locked at entry. A tier chosen in February caps the grade available in June, and that is the deadline most worth knowing about.

Counted backwards, a Diploma year looks like this. Twelve months out, the Extended Essay topic is agreed and Internal Assessments are being planned. Six months out, drafts exist and first marking has happened, while the final Higher Level content is still being taught. Three months out is the point at which content work should be giving way to timed papers. Six weeks out, new topics are a poor investment and paper technique is the only thing still moving a grade.

Confirm every date in the table with the school, because entry deadlines are set by the centre and results publication dates shift by a day or two between years. The shape, though, is stable, and the shape is what you plan against.

sections.heading: Internal Assessment criteria by letter, with the marks attached
paragraphs: Every page in this market says its tutors help with the Internal Assessment. Not one of the pages reviewed names a single criterion. That is the difference between marketing and teaching, because the criteria are the assessment: an exploration is not marked on how interesting it is, it is marked on five lettered criteria with a fixed mark each, and a student who has never read them is guessing at a fifth of their grade.

The Mathematics exploration, for both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, carries twenty marks: criterion A presentation, four; criterion B mathematical communication, four; criterion C personal engagement, three; criterion D reflection, three; criterion E use of mathematics, six. Criterion E is the heavyweight and the one most often lost, because it asks for mathematics commensurate with the level of the course. An IB Maths AA exploration built on content a Year 10 student could handle cannot score well on E however neatly it is written.

The sciences now assess one scientific investigation across four criteria of six marks each, twenty-four in total: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Research design is where most marks go missing, through a method that never states the range of the independent variable or how the controlled variables were held. The Theory of Knowledge essay is different again, marked as a single global impression out of ten against the prescribed title the student chose.

Read these numbers as a diagnostic tool. If a student's exploration is losing marks, the question is which letter, and the fix for each letter is different. That is a two-session conversation, not a term of general tuition.

sections.heading: Word and time limits by component, and what the limit is for
paragraphs: Limits are published, enforced and widely misread. A limit is a ceiling, not a target, and examiners stop reading at it. A Theory of Knowledge essay that runs to two thousand words is not a longer essay; it is an essay whose final four hundred words were not marked. Students who understand this write to about ninety per cent of the ceiling and spend the saved effort on structure.

The Extended Essay is four thousand words and is graded A to E alongside Theory of Knowledge, with the two together contributing up to three points to the diploma total. Those three points decide university offers more often than families expect, because an offer pitched at 36 points is lost by a student who scored 35 subject points and nothing from the core. The Extended Essay rubric most current cohorts work to awards marks across five criteria, with critical thinking carrying the largest single allocation.

Elsewhere the limits are tighter than students assume. The scientific investigation runs to three thousand words and is twenty per cent of the subject grade at both levels. Each Economics commentary is eight hundred words, three of them, worth thirty per cent at Standard Level and twenty at Higher. The Language and Literature Higher Level essay is twelve hundred to fifteen hundred words for twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade, which means a text chosen because it is short will not sustain the essay.

Check the current guide with the school's coordinator before planning around any of these, since the IB revises subject guides on a rolling cycle and a cohort two years apart can be working to different documents.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may and may not do with coursework
paragraphs: One competitor page found during research for this set sells completed Internal Assessments outright, at a published price. That is not tutoring. It is an academic-integrity breach, it is a malpractice trigger under IB rules, and the consequence lands on the student, not on the seller: a malpractice finding can cost the diploma. Any service offering to supply a finished exploration, essay or commentary should be treated as a risk to your child's qualification.

The legitimate line is clear and it is worth having in writing before a coursework session starts. A tutor teaches the criteria, explains what a mark scheme pays for, marks practice work, and gives feedback on a student's draft in the same way a school supervisor does. A tutor does not choose the topic, supply the data, draft a paragraph or restructure a submission. The student signs a declaration that the work is their own, and the supervisor records what the student did independently. Both statements have to be true.

Feedback itself is permitted and expected. The IB builds supervision into the Extended Essay through recorded reflection sessions, and schools mark Internal Assessment drafts. What is not permitted is work that is no longer the student's own after the help has been given. The practical test is whether the student could explain every choice in the document to an examiner, in their own words, without notes.
Everything in the table below applies to a tutor working through IB Gram, and it is the standard a session is run to.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies alongside an international curriculum
paragraphs: Every private school in the UAE, in Ajman as everywhere else, teaches Ministry of Education required subjects alongside its international curriculum. Arabic is compulsory for all students, as a first language for Arabic speakers and as an additional language for everyone else. Islamic Education is compulsory for Muslim students. Moral, Social and Cultural Studies, which covers UAE social studies content, runs across the school. These subjects appear in the inspection framework and in the school report, and they take up timetable the international curriculum does not get.

Families find this out at two moments. The first is when a non-Arabic-speaking child who joined in Year 6 is sitting Arabic B alongside students who have had it since FS1, and the gap is years wide rather than months. The second is at the end of school, when the equivalency file is assembled and Arabic and Islamic Education marks turn out to matter to the paperwork even for a student whose university offer is in Europe.

Tuition requests in this area are unglamorous and effective. For Arabic as an additional language, the work is vocabulary volume and the text-type conventions the exam uses. For Arabic as a first language under Cambridge 0508, the obstacle is Modern Standard Arabic register for a child who speaks dialect at home and English at school. For Islamic Education, the content is taught in Arabic in many schools, which turns a knowledge subject into a language problem for a student whose Arabic is weaker than their English.

The honest framing is that these subjects are not optional and not a distraction. They are part of a UAE school record, and leaving them to look after themselves until Year 11 produces the most avoidable grade problem on a northern-emirates transcript.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency and attestation for a school leaver in Ajman
paragraphs: Not one competitor page in the research set mentions equivalency at all, which is remarkable, because for a family planning a UAE university it is the part of the process with real consequences. A certificate of equivalency from the Ministry of Education is what converts an international qualification into something a UAE institution or employer recognises, and MoE equivalency is handled through the ministry's own channel rather than by the school.

The broad shape is this. An IB Diploma, awarded in full, is a recognised secondary qualification for equivalency purposes. A student who takes IB Courses without completing the full diploma is in a different position, and should check the requirement before Year 13 rather than after results. For the British route, the file looks at a set of IGCSE or GCSE subjects together with AS or A Level study, and the required combination has changed over the years, so a checklist from an older sibling's application is not a safe guide.

What catches families out is documentation rather than grades: transcripts the school must issue, attestation of documents, and the fact that Arabic and Islamic Education records are examined as part of a UAE school history. Students who moved between countries mid-school, which is common in Ajman, often discover a missing year of records at the worst possible moment. The school registrar holds the current checklist and the ministry's portal is the authoritative source; ask both, in Year 12 rather than in July of Year 13.

The practical point for tuition is that equivalency rewards a completed, coherent school record rather than a few strong grades. A student dropping a subject in Year 12 to protect three others should check what that does to the file before the drop, not afterwards.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the term calendar and when revision actually happens
paragraphs: Ramadan shortens the school day across the UAE, and in a year where it falls close to the May examination session it lands in the middle of final revision. Schools adjust timetables and reduce contact hours. Students fast. Energy at four in the afternoon is not what it is in January. A revision plan built in September that ignores this will be rewritten in March under pressure, which is the worst time to rewrite anything.

The practical adjustment is Ramadan session timing. Many Ajman families move lessons to after Iftar, when a student has eaten and can concentrate, which in practice means a later evening slot that holds for the month and then reverts. Others move to early morning at weekends. Both work. What does not work is keeping a 5pm weekday slot and watching three consecutive sessions achieve nothing while still being paid for.

The wider calendar matters too. The UAE school year runs across three terms with a long winter break around the turn of the year, which is where a November-session retake plan and the Extended Essay final draft both land. Summer runs long, and for a student entering Year 13 that break is the single largest block of uninterrupted Internal Assessment time available anywhere in the Diploma. Families who use four weeks of it lightly arrive in September with drafts, and those students have a materially easier year.
Plan the year around three fixed points: the winter break, Ramadan, and the study-leave date the school sets. Everything else can move.

sections.heading: When no specialist is free, and what we say instead
paragraphs: Availability is the thing tutoring companies are least honest about, so here is the position. The subjects that run short are the narrow Higher Level ones: Mathematics AA HL in the weeks before a May session, Chemistry HL coursework support in the autumn term, Economics HL Paper 3, and any Arabic first-language work at exam level. When a request lands in one of those windows, there is sometimes nobody suitable free at the hour an Ajman family needs.

What happens then is a choice presented plainly rather than a worse match quietly substituted. The options are a different time slot with the right specialist, often earlier on a weekend; a named wait with a date; or a different format, where a shorter fortnightly session on coursework criteria does more good than a weekly hour of general content review. What we do not do is put a Standard Level generalist in front of a Higher Level Paper 3 problem and let the family work it out in session four.

The second honest caveat is about what tuition can and cannot do. Six weeks before a paper, technique and paper strategy still move marks; untaught content largely does not. A student two years behind in foundational algebra cannot be fixed in a term alongside a full Diploma, and anyone who says otherwise is selling. The useful conversation in that case is about subject levels and option choices, which is a conversation with the school.
A free consultation exists for exactly this: to establish whether the thing you are asking for is the thing that will help, before anyone pays for an hour.

process.title: Tell us the paper, not just the subject
process.description: Subject, level, board and syllabus code, plus the exam session. Cambridge IGCSE 0580 Extended and Edexcel 4MA1 Higher are not the same request, and a May-session Diploma student in March needs a different plan from a Year 10 in October. The more specific the brief, the shorter the matching takes.

process.title: A consultation that diagnoses rather than sells
process.description: A short call about what the school is covering, what the last marked script looked like, and which Higher Level sets ran this year. If the answer is that the school has it covered and the problem is elsewhere, we say so. That conversation is free and is where most Ajman enquiries actually get resolved.

process.title: A trial session with the matched tutor
process.description: One session with the specialist proposed, not with a sales team. The tutor works through a real past-paper question or a section of coursework and reports back on what they found. If the match is wrong, it is wrong at that point, before a term has been booked.

process.title: A plan counted backwards from the exam date
process.description: Topic work first, timed papers next, technique last, with the handover points set by the session date and the school's study-leave calendar. Ramadan and the winter break are placed in the plan at the start rather than absorbed later. The plan is written down so you can hold it against progress.

process.title: Notes you can take to a parents' evening
process.description: A written note after each session naming what was covered, what was set, and what the marked work showed. Over a term that builds into a record of where the marks were going and whether that changed, which is more useful at a school meeting than an impression.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus, not by driving distance
whyPoints.description: The pool for an Ajman address is not the people willing to drive to Al Jurf on a Tuesday. It is every specialist who can teach the paper your child sits, wherever they teach from. For a narrow Higher Level subject, or for a family in Masfout, that is the whole difference between a specialist and whoever is nearby.

whyPoints.title: Built for an Ajman weekday
whyPoints.description: A household where a parent drives back from Dubai or Sharjah cannot hold a 5pm session. Slots run through the evening on Gulf Standard Time, weekend mornings are available, and Ramadan timing moves to after Iftar for the month and then reverts. A slot that survives the term is worth more than a cheaper one that does not.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what the inspection record shows
whyPoints.description: Private schools in Ajman are inspected federally, and no UAE framework rates a named Higher Level set. We will tell you which questions to put to the school instead of implying that a band is a verdict on your child's Chemistry teaching. Sometimes the answer is that no tuition is needed.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty written down before a coursework session
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches criteria, marks practice work and gives feedback. A tutor does not write, restructure or proofread a submission, choose a topic or touch a data set. One competitor in this market sells finished Internal Assessments. The risk of that lands on the student's diploma, which is why the line is published here.

whyPoints.title: Market prices published, our own model explained
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are the market's, each attributed to whoever advertises it, so you can judge any quote you receive including ours. IB Gram's own arrangement is set out on a free consultation after a trial session, because it depends on the subject, the level and the weeks left before the paper.

faqs.question: Who inspects private schools in Ajman, and where is the report?
faqs.answer: Ajman's private schools are licensed and inspected by the federal Ministry of Education, not by an emirate-level authority. Dubai has KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have ADEK, and Sharjah has SPEA, but Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain sit under the ministry. Inspection findings use the same national six-band scale, from Outstanding down to Very Weak, with Acceptable set as the minimum standard expected. Ask the school office directly for its most recent inspection outcome and the date of the visit, because a judgement can predate a change of staff by a full academic year.

faqs.question: What does an Acceptable judgement mean for my child's IB subjects?
faqs.answer: Acceptable has a defined meaning in the UAE framework: the minimum standard the country expects of a private school, met and not exceeded. It is not a comment on any single subject, because inspections report by phase and by a fixed subject list rather than by set. So an Acceptable school may teach your child's Higher Level Biology well and its Standard Level Economics poorly, and the band will not tell you which. Treat it as a prompt to look at departments one at a time, and specifically to ask whether the subject your child struggles in changed teacher during the course.

faqs.question: How much do IB and IGCSE tutors in Ajman cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Market rates, not ours: budget online tuition advertises from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject teacher online runs about AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 because the journey is inside the price. Specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. IB Gram's own arrangement is discussed on a free consultation after a trial session.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our home in Ajman?
faqs.answer: No. Tuition for families in the UAE is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The in-home service IB Gram runs exists only in India. We target the home-tutor search honestly because it is the phrase parents use, and the practical answer for Ajman is that an online session gives access to a specialist in the exact subject and level rather than to whoever is willing to drive to your district. The trade-off is real for younger children who need someone physically present, and we will say so rather than talk you into the wrong format.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in the UAE need a permit to teach my child?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and a private tutor permit is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. Every regulatory source consulted for this page states that the permit itself is issued free of charge, so a fee quoted to you for one is worth questioning. Reported penalties for unpermitted tutoring were not published with specific amounts, and figures circulating online could not be verified, so we do not repeat them. For tuition delivered online by a tutor based outside the UAE, the relevant question is qualification and syllabus experience rather than a local permit.

faqs.question: My child's school cannot run Chemistry at Higher Level. What now?
faqs.answer: This is common in a small cohort and it is arithmetic, not neglect: an option block runs only if enough students choose it. Ask the school three questions in writing. Which blocks actually ran this year? Is the subject being offered as a taught set or as supported self-study? Who teaches it, and for how long have they taught that syllabus? If the answer is self-study, weekly one-to-one support becomes the taught element rather than an extra, and the plan should follow the real syllabus sequence rather than revision order.

faqs.question: How do Ajman families fit sessions around a commute to Dubai or Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Most households here solve it in one of three ways. A fixed later evening slot, after 7pm, for families where a parent needs to be in the room. A slot immediately after the school bus arrives, which suits Al Nuaimiya and Al Rashidiya where the school run is short. Or weekend mornings, which hold better through exam term than any weekday evening. Online delivery is what makes the third option practical, because nobody is travelling. Book the same hour every week for a term rather than arranging each session, since an ad hoc slot is the first thing to collapse in March.

faqs.question: When does the school have to register my child for exams?
faqs.answer: Registration is done by the school, through the Diploma coordinator or the exams officer, not by you. The IB's final registration point for a May session falls around the middle of the preceding November, and for a November session around the middle of the preceding May. Cambridge and Edexcel entry deadlines sit earlier than families expect, often February for a June series. The deadline that matters most is tiering: Core against Extended, or Foundation against Higher, is fixed at entry and caps the grade available. Confirm all of it with the exams officer in writing.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Internal Assessment without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear line. A tutor may teach the criteria, explain what each mark is awarded for, mark practice work, and give feedback on a draft in the way a school supervisor does. A tutor may not choose the topic, supply or alter data, draft or restructure a paragraph, or proofread the submission. The student signs that the work is their own and the supervisor records what was done independently, so both statements must be true. The test is whether the student could explain every choice in the document to an examiner without notes.

faqs.question: What does MoE equivalency ask for from an IB Diploma student?
faqs.answer: A certificate of equivalency from the Ministry of Education is what converts an international qualification into something UAE universities and employers recognise. A full IB Diploma is a recognised secondary qualification for that purpose; taking IB Courses without the full diploma puts a student in a different position worth checking before Year 13. Most problems are documentary rather than academic: school transcripts, attestation, and a complete UAE school history including Arabic and Islamic Education records. The school registrar holds the current checklist and the ministry's portal is the authoritative source. Ask in Year 12, not after results.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education marks matter if my child does the IB?
faqs.answer: They matter more than most families assume. Arabic is compulsory in every UAE private school, as a first language for Arabic speakers and as an additional language for everyone else, and Islamic Education is compulsory for Muslim students. These subjects appear in the inspection framework and in the school record that supports an equivalency application. A child who joined in Year 6 with no Arabic is years behind classmates who started in FS1, and leaving that gap until Year 11 produces the most avoidable grade problem on a northern-emirates transcript.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change a revision plan for an Ajman student?
faqs.answer: It moves the hour, and most families should let it. School days shorten across the UAE during Ramadan, students are fasting, and a 5pm session in the last hour before Iftar achieves very little however good the tutor is. The usual adjustment is a later evening slot held for the month and then reverted, or a move to weekend mornings. Set this at the start of the year rather than in March, especially in a year when Ramadan falls close to the May session, because that is when final revision and the shortened timetable collide.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE board does my child's Ajman school actually use?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer, and ask subject by subject, because schools in the emirate run both Cambridge and Edexcel and some mix them. The syllabus code is the answer you want: Cambridge IGCSE 0580 for maths, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, against Edexcel 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1. The content overlaps but the papers do not. Cambridge 0580 Extended now sets one paper without a calculator and one with; Edexcel 4MA1 tiers differently and provides a different formula sheet. Revising from the wrong board's past papers wastes a term.

faqs.question: How long should the Maths exploration be and what is it marked out of?
faqs.answer: The Mathematics exploration is marked out of twenty across five criteria: A presentation, four marks; B mathematical communication, four; C personal engagement, three; D reflection, three; E use of mathematics, six. The guide expects a report of roughly twelve to twenty pages rather than a word count, so length is not the lever. Criterion E is, because it asks for mathematics commensurate with the level of the course, and an otherwise polished exploration built on content below that level cannot score well. Confirm the current guide with your school's coordinator, since the IB revises them on a cycle.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for the subject we need?
faqs.answer: You get told, with options, rather than given a weaker match quietly. The subjects that run short are narrow Higher Level ones: Mathematics AA HL before a May session, Chemistry HL coursework in the autumn, Economics HL Paper 3, and Arabic first-language work at exam level. The choices then are a different time slot with the right specialist, often a weekend morning; a named wait with a date attached; or a different format, where fortnightly work on coursework criteria does more good than a weekly hour of general review. A Standard Level generalist is not substituted for a Higher Level problem.

faqs.question: Does a family in Masfout need a different setup from one in Al Nuaimiya?
faqs.answer: The format is the same but the reasoning is not. Al Nuaimiya sits in Ajman city, with a short school run and some local tutoring market, so the question there is which hour of the evening works. Masfout is Ajman's inland exclave, roughly a hundred kilometres away near the Hatta road, where no realistic local market for a Diploma subject specialist exists. For a Masfout or Manama family, a scheduled video session is not second best to a visit; it is the only route to a Higher Level subject teacher without a two-hour round trip.

ajman.closingHeading: What to do this week if your child is in an Ajman Diploma or IGCSE cohort
ajman.closingBody: Three questions to the school, in writing, answer most of this: which option blocks ran this year, who teaches the set your child is in, and may we see a marked past-paper script. Then look at the AED bands above and decide what one hour a week is worth against the subject that is actually slipping. If a session makes sense after that, book a consultation and a trial: one hour with the matched specialist, on a real question, with a report back. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the plan is counted backwards from your child's exam date rather than from the start of term.

al-ain.tutorsIntro: These are the subject specialists Al Ain families ask for most: Diploma Programme sciences at Higher Level, Mathematics AA and AI, and Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE sciences. Each one teaches a named syllabus and has marked or taught the exact paper your child will sit, not a general version of the subject.

intro.heading: Start with the inspection report, not the search results
paragraphs: Al Ain is the second city of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, 130 kilometres inland from the capital and a short drive from the Omani border at Buraimi. That geography decides more about tuition here than most parents expect. The private-school set is far smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, so a Diploma Programme subject is often taught to a single class by a single teacher. If that teacher is strong, your child is fine. If the subject is one the school added recently, there is no second set and no second opinion inside the building.

Because Al Ain falls under the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, its private schools are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, not by KHDA, which covers Dubai, and not by SPEA, which covers Sharjah. This matters practically. ADEK publishes an inspection outcome for each private school it inspects, and the report behind that outcome is written standard by standard: what students achieve, how they are taught and assessed, what the curriculum offers, how they are cared for, and how the school is led. A parent who reads it properly learns which subjects a school is thin in before the mock results arrive.

That is the honest starting point for choosing tuition. An ADEK inspection rating is not a verdict on your child. It is a map of where the school's own capacity sits, and where an outside specialist adds something the school cannot. A school judged strong overall can still have a Physics department that lost two teachers in a year. A school in a lower band can have a Mathematics team that holds its grades. Averages hide subjects, and you are buying support for a subject, not for a school.

IB Gram works the way a good head of year would. You send the last school report and, if you have it, the page of the ADEK report that covers teaching in your child's subject group. We work out whether the gap is content, exam technique, coursework, or the particular habit of answering a command term loosely. Then a tutor who teaches that syllabus takes the student for live one-to-one lessons online. Nothing about that model depends on who happens to live within twenty minutes of Al Mutaredh.

Lessons are delivered online over live video, one tutor to one student, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own past papers on screen. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India. In Al Ain the online format is the better buy and not a compromise: a Chemistry HL tutor who has taught the current guide is worth more than a generalist who can be in Falaj Hazzaa at six. We would rather say that plainly than sell a drive time.

al-ain.programmesIntro: Al Ain families run four routes in practice: the IB continuum through the Primary Years and Middle Years into the Diploma, and the Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel route through IGCSE. Each one is assessed differently, and each one fails differently. Here is what we actually tutor at each stage, and what the Al Ain version of it looks like.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external exams, which is exactly why gaps go unnoticed until Year 7. Learning is organised around transdisciplinary units and reported against learner-profile attributes rather than percentages, so a child can look settled while number fluency or extended writing quietly falls behind. Tutoring at this stage is diagnostic and short: arithmetic automaticity, reading stamina, and the habit of writing a paragraph that answers the question asked. Thirty focused minutes twice a week does more here than a long session.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain, PYP children often move schools when a parent's posting shifts between the city and Abu Dhabi island or Dubai. A move mid-primary usually means a change of curriculum model as well as campus, and the PYP-to-national-curriculum jump exposes gaps in formal grammar and written arithmetic. We start with a short written baseline rather than a conversation, because a Year 5 report that says 'developing' tells a parent almost nothing measurable.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks everything against four criteria per subject on a 1-8 scale, then converts to a 1-7 grade. Students who have never been taught what criterion wording expects tend to plateau at 5 and 6 regardless of ability. Our MYP work is criterion-literal: the student marks their own piece against the published descriptors, sees where the band boundary sits, then redrafts once. eAssessment candidates in Year 11 also need timed practice, which most schools cannot fit inside a lesson.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain's MYP cohorts are small, and the MYP-to-Diploma step is where the city's limited subject choice bites. A student who wants Physics HL but sat MYP Sciences as an integrated course arrives in DP1 without the algebra load the course assumes. We bridge that in the summer term of Year 11 rather than in October of DP1, when the Internal Assessment clock has already started running.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The Diploma is scored out of 45, with up to three points from the TOK and EE combination. Most of the pressure is not the final papers; it is the overlap of five Internal Assessments, an Extended Essay and a TOK essay inside the same twelve weeks. Tutoring that ignores that calendar is tutoring for the wrong problem. An IB Diploma tutor in Al Ain should be able to say what is due in week six.
programmes.countryNote: Because few Al Ain schools run every Higher Level science, families here are the most likely in the emirate to need a subject their campus teaches to a handful of students, or does not teach at all. That is the single clearest case for an online specialist: the student gets the Chemistry HL tutor who has taught the current guide, from wherever that tutor is, rather than the nearest adult who did Chemistry at university a decade ago.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: IGCSE is code-specific, and the code changes what you revise. Cambridge IGCSE 0580 Mathematics tiers into Core and Extended, with Extended targeting the upper grades; 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology carry an alternative-to-practical or practical paper depending on the school's entry. Pearson Edexcel runs 4MA1 for Mathematics A and 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 for the sciences, with its own January series. We teach to the code on the student's statement of entry, not to a generic IGCSE.
programmes.countryNote: IGCSE tuition in Al Ain is complicated by mixed entries: it is common for one family's two children to sit Cambridge at one school and Edexcel at another, and for a single student to carry both boards across subjects. Before the first session we ask for the statement of entry and check the tier, the board and the practical arrangement. Half the wasted revision we see in this city is a student working through the wrong board's past papers.

al-ain.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma Programme subjects Al Ain families request most, with what each one is actually assessed on. Where a subject is taught to one small class in the city, an online specialist is usually the only way to get someone who has taught the current guide rather than the previous one.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Under the current guide both levels are assessed on Paper 1 at 36 per cent, Paper 2 at 44 per cent and the scientific investigation at 20 per cent. Marks go missing in the data-based section of Paper 1B and in extended reasoning about energetics and equilibrium. A Chemistry HL tutor works from the student's own marked Paper 2 rather than from a textbook chapter.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The same 36/44/20 split applies. The HL-only material in fields, induction and quantum physics tends to arrive late in DP2, which is why Al Ain students often meet it for the first time three weeks before a mock. Sessions focus on unit discipline, graph linearisation and the difference between a derivation and an explanation in a six-mark answer.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Biology rewards precision of language more than any other DP science: a correct idea in loose wording scores nothing. We drill command terms against the published markscheme, then work on the long-answer questions in Paper 2 where students lose marks for describing a process when the question asked them to explain or to compare.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: SL is Paper 1 at 40 per cent, Paper 2 at 40 per cent and the exploration at 20 per cent. HL adds Paper 3, worth 20 per cent, with two extended investigative questions that reward stamina and structure. Non-calculator fluency on Paper 1 is the usual weak point for students who learned maths on a graphical display calculator.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI is not the easy route; it is the modelling and statistics route, with heavy technology use and a different Paper 3 at Higher Level. Students who chose AI for the wrong reason struggle with the volume of interpretation writing. We also check the route against degree plans, because some engineering and physics programmes still expect Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: SL splits 40/40/20 across Paper 1, Paper 2 and the portfolio of three commentaries. HL moves to 20/30/30/20 and adds the quantitative Paper 3, which is where HL grades are won and lost. Diagram accuracy and the explicit use of the nine key concepts carry marks that students regularly leave on the table.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The business research project at HL and the written commentary at SL are coursework pieces that need a real organisation and a real question, which is harder in a smaller city. Exam marks are lost on tool-dropping: naming SWOT or Ansoff without applying it to the stimulus. We work from the published assessment criteria outwards.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: SL is Paper 1 at 35 per cent, Paper 2 at 35 per cent and the individual oral at 30 per cent. HL replaces part of that with the HL essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words and reweights the oral. The guided analysis in Paper 1 is a timed close-reading skill, and it is teachable in a way that reading more books is not.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic runs two different ways in Al Ain: as a first language and literature course, and as a second language at B or ab initio level. Both are assessed on productive skills, and both reward structured writing practice far more than vocabulary lists. This is one of the subjects a smaller school set struggles to staff at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a working solution with documented development, and students regularly build something impressive that documents poorly. We split the work: design and testing evidence first, code second. Paper questions on data structures and object-oriented design need pencil-and-paper tracing practice, not more time in an IDE.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The TOK essay answers one of six prescribed titles in 1,600 words and is marked out of 10 on a single global impression; the exhibition adds three objects and 950 words. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words, marked out of 34. Together they carry up to three Diploma points. Tutors coach structure, argument and source handling only.

al-ain.igcseSubjectsIntro: On the IGCSE side the board and the syllabus code decide the revision plan. These are the subjects Al Ain parents ask about most often, with the codes you will find on the statement of entry.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge IGCSE 0580 tiers, and a student entered for Core cannot reach the top grades however well they revise, so the tier decision matters more than any single topic. Edexcel 4MA1 is untiered at Higher and sets longer multi-step questions. Both reward method marks, which students lose by not writing the working down.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity and the equations around it account for a large share of lost marks every series. Circuit reasoning, not formula recall, is the skill. Where a school enters students for the alternative-to-practical paper, we drill apparatus description, anomalous-result spotting and table-and-graph conventions on screen using past practical papers.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry
igcseSubjects.description: Moles calculations and organic reaction pathways are the two reliable separators at grade 7 and above. We also work on qualitative analysis questions, which read as recall but are really a sequence: observation, deduction, ionic equation. Students who skip the middle step lose both marks.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology
igcseSubjects.description: The content is large and the examiner's vocabulary is narrow. Sessions pair a topic sweep with markscheme language drills on transport, homeostasis and inheritance. Genetic-cross questions are worth practising until the Punnett square layout is automatic, because presentation itself carries marks.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
igcseSubjects.description: Both subjects are marked on application to the case material, not on definitions. The common failure is a correct textbook answer that never touches the business in the extract. We teach the two-mark, four-mark and extended-response shapes separately, because they are different writing tasks.

igcseSubjects.name: English
igcseSubjects.description: First Language English and English as a Second Language are different examinations with different reading demands, and students are occasionally entered for the one that suits the school rather than the student. Directed writing and summary tasks are the most coachable components in the whole IGCSE set.

al-ain.regionsTitle: Al Ain districts we schedule around
al-ain.regionsIntro: Al Ain is low-rise and spread out, and the school run shapes the timetable more than traffic does. These are the districts families book from most, with the scheduling detail that matters when you are fixing a weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time.

regions.name: Asharej
regions.note: The district next to the United Arab Emirates University campus, so households here often include a parent or sibling on the UAEU timetable. Study-space competition at home is real; we book sessions when the room is quiet, often after 7pm, rather than straight after school.

regions.name: Al Jimi
regions.note: Dense, central and close to Al Jimi Mall, with several of the city's long-established private schools within a few minutes' drive. Pick-up is quick here, so a 4.30pm or 5pm start is realistic even in exam term, which makes Al Jimi families the easiest to give a consistent weekday slot.

regions.name: Al Mutaredh
regions.note: Villa district close to the oasis and the central hospital, with a high share of medical and university households. DP sciences and maths dominate requests from here. Evening sessions work well because parents on shift patterns prefer a fixed slot the student can keep without a lift.

regions.name: Al Muwaiji
regions.note: West of the centre, near the Al Ain Palace Museum side of town, and a longer run back from the newer campuses on the city's edge. A 5.30pm start is safer than a 4.30pm one here; we build the first session late and bring it forward once the family sees the real arrival time.

regions.name: Al Towayya
regions.note: Established residential area with a mix of British and Indian curriculum families, which means one household often runs IGCSE and CBSE timetables side by side. Siblings are better scheduled back to back on the same evening so one quiet room covers both lessons.

regions.name: Zakher
regions.note: On the southern edge towards Jebel Hafeet, with the longest school commute in the city for families whose children attend central campuses. Weekday sessions realistically start at 6pm. Many Zakher families move their heavier work to Friday or Saturday mornings instead.

regions.name: Falaj Hazzaa
regions.note: Large villa neighbourhood with a strong Emirati household share, so Arabic as a first language and Islamic Education sit alongside IB or IGCSE subjects in the same week. We coordinate so tuition does not collide with the school's own Arabic support sessions.

regions.name: Hili and Al Foah
regions.note: Northern districts out towards the Omani border crossing, where the archaeological parks are. Families here drive further for school than anyone else in Al Ain, and the online format removes the second journey entirely. Winter sunset timings change what counts as a late slot.

schoolClusters.city: Central Al Ain: Al Jimi, Al Mutaredh and Al Towayya
schoolClusters.note: The city's oldest private-school cluster, mostly British and Indian curriculum, feeding Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE entries with A-level or Diploma continuation depending on the campus. Requests from this cluster skew to IGCSE sciences in Year 11 and to DP maths in Year 12.

Al Dhafra Private Schools, Al Ain
The International School of Choueifat, Al Ain

schoolClusters.city: Outer Al Ain: Asharej, Zakher and the Abu Dhabi road side
schoolClusters.note: Newer and larger campuses on the city's edges, with the longest commutes and the broadest subject offer. This is where Higher Level science cohorts are smallest, and where a family is most likely to need a subject the campus runs for a single group.

al-ain.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every Al Ain request. All of them are live one-to-one video lessons with a shared whiteboard, and all of them are timed in Gulf Standard Time. The choice is about rhythm, not about delivery.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the term
modes.description: One or two fixed sessions a week against the school's own scheme of work, which is the format that actually changes a grade over a year. The tutor sees the marked class assessments, so the session targets the question the student got wrong last week rather than the next topic in the book. Most Al Ain families start here with a single subject and add a second only if the first is holding.

modes.title: Coursework clinics for the IA, EE and TOK essay
modes.description: Short, scheduled blocks aimed at one assessed piece, pinned to the school's internal deadline rather than the final submission date. The tutor reads the draft against the published criteria, marks it in the student's presence, and names the criterion losing the marks. The student does the rewriting. This is IA coaching, not drafting, and the boundary is explained to the student in the first session.

Content revision stops early; the last fortnight is timed papers marked against the official markscheme. During Ramadan these move to post-Iftar sessions, which for many Al Ain students is the most productive slot of the day anyway.

sections.heading: What an ADEK rating actually says about your child's subject
paragraphs: ADEK licenses and inspects the private schools of Abu Dhabi, Al Ain and Al Dhafra, and publishes an overall outcome for each school it inspects on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Those words are the part parents remember. They are also the part that tells you least, because an overall band is a weighted summary of an entire school across every phase and subject group it offers.

The useful information sits one level down. An inspection judgement is built from performance standards covering what students achieve, their personal development, teaching and assessment, the curriculum, the care and support around them, and leadership. Achievement itself is reported by phase and by subject group, which is where a parent of a DP2 Chemistry student should be reading. A school can hold a strong overall band while the judgement on attainment in secondary science sits a band lower, and that gap is the one tuition is for.

So use the band for what it is good at. It tells you the direction the school is moving and how much slack the leadership has. A school that has just moved up a band is usually investing in teaching and may fix your problem by itself within a term. A school holding a lower band for several cycles is unlikely to solve a single subject's staffing in the twelve weeks before your child's mocks, and that is a decision point rather than a complaint.

The table below is how we read each band when a family in Al Ain asks what it means for them. It is a working interpretation, not an official definition, and the current report for any named school should be checked on ADEK's own site before you act on it.
