sections.heading: The six things an inspector looked at, and which of them you can fix privately
paragraphs: An inspection report is not a review. It is a structured judgement against standards, and each standard has a different relationship to private tuition. Two of them a tutor can genuinely compensate for. Two a tutor can partly offset. Two are entirely the school's, and no amount of tuition will touch them. Knowing which is which stops families spending money on the wrong problem.

Students' achievement, meaning attainment and progress against curriculum standards, is the standard tuition addresses directly. Teaching and assessment is the second: where a report says feedback is not used well to move learning on, an outside tutor marking the student's own work to the published markscheme is a direct substitute for the missing feedback loop. Those two are the reason most Al Ain families start.

Curriculum, and the care, guidance and support standard, are partly addressable. If the report notes that the curriculum is not adapted for higher attainers, a tutor can extend a student beyond the class pace. If it notes weak transition support between MYP and DP, a bridging block in the summer term covers much of it. What a tutor cannot replace is subject choice: if the school does not run Physics HL, tuition does not create a class, although it does make a private or transferred entry survivable.

Personal and social development, and leadership and management, are the school's own. A tutor has no standing there, and any provider implying otherwise is selling something it does not have. We say this openly because it narrows the question usefully. Read the achievement and teaching judgements for your child's phase, decide whether the gap is content or technique or feedback, and buy exactly that.
bullets: Directly fixable by tuition: attainment, progress, exam technique, marked feedback
Partly offsettable: curriculum stretch, transition between programmes, coursework guidance
Not fixable from outside: subject availability, pastoral provision, school leadership
Always read the achievement judgement for your child's phase, not the overall band

sections.heading: What tuition costs in Al Ain, and who publishes those numbers
paragraphs: Published pricing in this market is scarce, and that is deliberate on most sites. Three of the larger agencies competing for UAE search traffic publish no hourly figure at all, and two of those that do quote in US dollars, a currency no family here transacts in. Two more publish a rate in their structured data that contradicts the rate on the visible page. So before anything else: the figures below are market rates other providers publish, not IB Gram's price list.

The pattern across the market is consistent once you convert everything into dirhams per hour. Budget online tuition, usually delivered by university students, starts in the AED 45 to 150 band. A qualified subject tutor working online sits roughly between AED 150 and AED 300. Visiting in-home tuition carries its travel cost inside the hourly rate and runs higher, commonly quoted between AED 180 and AED 500. Named IB and IGCSE specialists sit from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and examiner-level or heavily branded tutors are quoted at AED 500 to AED 650 and beyond.

Monthly packaging is where comparison gets slippery. Advertised bundles in the UAE include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and roughly AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are not comparable products: one buys eight contact hours, the other eight hours with travel folded in and half the frequency. Work in cost per contact hour and the picture clears up immediately.

Al Ain sits at the softer end of in-home pricing compared with Dubai, simply because the driving is easier and the rent lower, but the tutor pool is correspondingly smaller. That is the real trade-off for home tuition rates in Al Ain: you may pay less per hour than a Dubai Marina family and still have a much shorter list of people who have taught your child's actual syllabus.

sections.heading: In-home tuition in Al Ain against live online one-to-one
paragraphs: Parents searching for a home tutor in this city are asking a reasonable question, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a redirect. In-home tuition does real things that online does not. A tutor in the room can see a child's body language, put a hand near the page, and keep a distractible twelve-year-old on task without a single reminder. For younger children and for students with certain additional needs, that presence is worth paying for, and families should weigh it honestly.

What it costs is the other half of the answer. An in-home session in Al Ain pays for the tutor's road time, and because the city is spread out from Zakher in the south to Hili in the north, one visit can absorb forty minutes of driving at each end. That time is in the rate, and it also caps the tutor's availability: whoever teaches your child on Tuesday at five must be physically within reach of your district on Tuesday at five. In a city with a small specialist pool, that constraint, not the money, is what usually decides the match.

IB Gram delivers tuition for UAE families as live one-to-one lessons online, over video, with a shared whiteboard and screen sharing. Home visits are part of our India service only. We are not pretending that online is identical to a tutor in the room; we are saying that for Diploma and IGCSE students the specialist you reach matters more than the metre of distance, and that the saved travel converts into frequency and continuity. A student who keeps the same tutor through a house move, a posting to Abu Dhabi island, or a summer abroad does not lose a term to re-matching.

sections.heading: The exam calendar, counted backwards from the first paper
paragraphs: Almost no competitor page in this market names an exam session at all, which is strange, because the session date is the only fixed point in the whole year. Everything else, including how much tuition is worth buying, follows from it. The Diploma runs two sessions: May, which is what nearly all Al Ain schools enter, and November. Cambridge IGCSE runs a May or June series and an October or November series. Pearson Edexcel adds a January series for many International GCSE subjects, which is why a January entry quietly exists in this city for resitting students.

Work backwards and the year has a shape. A year out, the decisions are structural: subject and level combinations, Mathematics AA and AI route choice, and whether a Higher Level science the school cannot staff should be carried. Nine months out, Internal Assessment topics are chosen and approved, and this is where most of the damage is done, because an unworkable research question costs the student weeks they never get back. Six months out, candidate registration has closed and the statement of entry exists; check the board, the tier and the paper options on it rather than assuming.

Three months out, coursework should be finished, and the student should be sitting whole timed papers rather than revising topics. Six weeks out is the point at which new content stops being worth teaching and markscheme behaviour starts paying. In the final fortnight the only useful work is timed questions, marked, with the errors logged by type rather than by topic. Results land in early July for the May Diploma session and in early January for the November session, with Cambridge and Edexcel publishing in August and January; confirm your own dates with the school's exams officer, because entry deadlines vary by centre.

Ramadan moves the middle of this plan. School days shorten, evenings restructure around Iftar, and the productive hours for a teenager shift late. We plan around it rather than through it: lighter content weeks, then post-Iftar sessions for the heavier work.

sections.heading: Where the marks sit: the weightings families misread
paragraphs: A surprising amount of wasted revision in Al Ain comes from not knowing what each component is worth. Parents hear that a paper is hard and buy tuition for it, when the component actually losing the grade is a coursework piece marked months earlier, or a paper that carries nearly half the subject and gets a third of the practice. The weightings are published by the IB for every subject; they are not a secret, they are simply never put in front of parents.

In the current Diploma sciences, both Standard and Higher Level sit at Paper 1 for 36 per cent, Paper 2 for 44 per cent and the scientific investigation for 20 per cent. Read that again: the investigation is worth more than double a strong performance on any single long-answer question, and it is the one component the student controls completely, in their own time, with feedback allowed. A family deciding between coursework support and exam cramming should usually take the coursework first.

Mathematics splits differently by level. At Standard Level, Papers 1 and 2 take 40 per cent each with the exploration at 20 per cent. At Higher Level, Papers 1 and 2 drop to 30 per cent each and Paper 3 takes 20 per cent, which means the HL paper students practise least carries as much as the exploration they agonise over. Economics shifts even harder: Higher Level moves Paper 1 down to 20 per cent and brings in the quantitative Paper 3 at 30 per cent.

sections.heading: The Internal Assessment, criterion by criterion, with the marks attached
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market names a single assessment criterion, which is remarkable given that the Internal Assessment is where a fifth of most Diploma subject grades is decided. The criteria are published by letter with marks attached, and a student who has not read them is marking blind. The first thing we do in IA coaching is put the criteria next to the draft and have the student mark their own work. It is usually an uncomfortable twenty minutes and it saves weeks.

In the current science guides the scientific investigation is marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The pattern of loss is predictable. Research design loses marks for a vague methodology and an unjustified range of values. Data analysis loses them on uncertainty handling and unlabelled graphs. Conclusion loses them when the student restates results instead of comparing them with accepted values and published literature. Evaluation loses them on generic limitations: writing that there was human error is worth nothing.

The Mathematics exploration is out of 20, split across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics, with that last criterion worth 6 marks and depending on the mathematics being commensurate with the level studied. An exploration that uses nothing beyond the first year of the course caps itself regardless of how neat it looks. The Economics portfolio is three commentaries of 800 words each, marked out of 14, with explicit marks for diagrams, terminology, application, a named key concept and evaluation. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words out of 34, and critical thinking alone carries 12 of those marks.
Read those numbers once and the priorities invert. The student who spends a weekend formatting an essay is protecting 4 presentation marks while leaving 12 critical-thinking marks untouched.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an IA, EE or TOK essay
paragraphs: This has to be said plainly, because at least one provider selling to UAE families offers completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. That is not tutoring. Submitting work that is not your own is malpractice under the IB's academic integrity rules, the school is required to act on it, and the consequence falls on the student, not on the person who sold the document. A family paying for that is buying a risk to the whole Diploma.

The honest boundary is easy to describe. A tutor may teach the subject content the coursework rests on, explain what each criterion rewards, discuss the suitability of a research question, show the student how to mark a draft against the descriptors, point out where a paragraph describes instead of argues, and check that referencing meets the school's required style. All of that is ordinary teaching and all of it is allowed.

A tutor may not write, rewrite or redraft any part of the submitted text, supply paragraphs for the student to insert, produce or alter data, choose the research question for the student, write reflection or process-journal entries, or edit a draft line by line until the voice is no longer the student's. The last one is where well-meaning help usually crosses over, and it is also the easiest for a supervisor to spot, because the writing stops matching everything else the student has produced that year.
We tell students this in the first coursework session and we tell parents the same thing. If a provider cannot say where its own line is, that is the answer to the question.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency, UAEU and what an Al Ain leaver needs on file
paragraphs: Al Ain is a university city. The United Arab Emirates University sits in the Asharej area, and a meaningful share of local Diploma and IGCSE students apply to it or to another UAE institution rather than going abroad. That makes one piece of paperwork more important here than in most Gulf cities, and it is one that no competitor page in this market mentions: the Ministry of Education certificate of equivalency.

The principle is straightforward. A UAE university needs to know that a foreign school-leaving qualification is equivalent to the national secondary certificate, and the Ministry issues an equivalency decision on that basis. For an IB student the question is usually whether the full Diploma was awarded rather than a certificate of individual subjects, and whether the subject spread and points total meet the published threshold. For a British-curriculum student it is a count: a required number of IGCSE or GCSE passes alongside a required number of AS or A-level subjects, in a recognised combination. For students required to study Arabic and Islamic Education, those subjects form part of the file.

Where this goes wrong is almost never academic. It is a certificate issued under a previous passport name, a transcript that was never attested, a student who sat a resit at a centre the school did not record, or a family that only discovers at application time that the subject combination does not satisfy the rule. Start the MoE equivalency certificate file in DP1 or Year 11, not in July. Keep the originals, keep every statement of entry, and check the current requirements on the Ministry's own equivalency portal, because the rules are revised and this page is not the authority on them.

UAE University admissions, like other national institutions, also publish their own entry tests and English-language thresholds alongside the equivalency requirement, and those are a separate matter from the Diploma score. Deal with them as a separate deadline, because a student can hold the points and still miss the intake on a language score nobody flagged.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: Something that is almost completely absent from tutoring pages aimed at UAE families: an IB or IGCSE student in Al Ain is not only studying IB or IGCSE. ADEK requires private schools in the emirate to teach Arabic, Islamic Education for Muslim students, and UAE Social Studies or moral education, in specified amounts and for specified year groups. These sit on top of a six-subject Diploma, and the hours are real.

For Emirati families, particularly in districts such as Falaj Hazzaa and Al Muwaiji where Arabic as a first language is standard, this means the week already contains a demanding literacy load before any Diploma subject is counted. For expatriate families it often means a child studying Arabic as an additional language to a standard the school sets, with marks that appear on the school report but not on the Diploma. Parents are regularly surprised by how much of a term's grade pressure comes from this side of the timetable.

Practically, this changes how we schedule rather than what we teach. Arabic and Islamic Education support sessions a school runs are usually fixed, so tuition goes around them. We ask for the full school timetable, not just the subject in question, before fixing a slot, and we do not book a DP Chemistry session into the one evening a student already has school Arabic support. A tutor who ignores this side of the week ends up competing with it, and the student loses either way.

We also keep the honest limit visible. Where the requirement is a school-set Arabic course rather than an examined IB or IGCSE syllabus, the school's own department sets the standard and the materials, and our role is scheduling around it and supporting study skills, not second-guessing what the school assesses.

process.title: Send the report and the inspection page
process.description: Share the most recent school report, any marked assessment, and if you have it the section of the ADEK report covering teaching and achievement in your child's phase. Twenty minutes of reading replaces an hour of guessing, and it frequently changes which subject we recommend starting with.

process.title: Confirm board, level and entry
process.description: We check the statement of entry or the school's confirmation: Diploma level, or Cambridge and Edexcel codes and tiers for IGCSE, plus the practical arrangement for sciences. This is the step that prevents a term of revision from the wrong board's past papers, which is commoner in Al Ain than anyone admits.

process.title: One diagnostic session on a real paper
process.description: The first session is a marked past paper or a marked piece of coursework, not an introduction. The tutor identifies whether the gap is content, technique, coursework or timing, and tells you which. If the answer is that your child does not need weekly tuition, you will hear that too.

process.title: Fix a slot in Gulf Standard Time
process.description: We set a weekly slot around the school run, the school's own Arabic or Islamic Education support, and sibling timetables. Zakher, Hili and Al Foah families usually land on a later start. Ramadan moves sessions to post-Iftar automatically rather than cancelling them.

process.title: Written feedback the parent can read
process.description: After every second session you receive a short note: what was covered, what the student got wrong, and what changes next. Marked work is annotated on screen and saved where you can open it. No scores are promised, and a session that went badly is reported as a session that went badly.

process.title: Reset before each exam block
process.description: Ahead of mocks and of the May or November session we rebuild the plan backwards from the first paper: the date new content stops, which papers are sat timed, and which error types are being drilled. Blocks end when the exam ends rather than rolling on by default.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the syllabus, not to the district
whyPoints.description: The question is not who can reach Al Towayya by five. It is who has taught the paper your child is sitting, in the current guide, with the markscheme in front of them. Online delivery means the answer to that question is not limited to the people living within driving distance of your street.

whyPoints.title: We read the ADEK report with you
whyPoints.description: Al Ain schools are inspected by ADEK, and the report says more than the headline band. We read the achievement and teaching judgements for your child's phase with you and say which gaps tuition can realistically close and which belong to the school. That conversation is free and sometimes ends in us recommending nothing.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on coursework
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach content, explain criteria and mark drafts. They do not write, redraft or supply any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay, and they do not produce data. The student hears that boundary in the first coursework session, in the same words a supervisor would use.

whyPoints.title: Market pricing shown, not hidden
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are figures other providers publish, attributed to them, so you can see where any quote you receive sits. We do not pretend a monthly bundle and an hourly rate are the same product, and we would rather you compared cost per contact hour than per month.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that respects the Al Ain week
whyPoints.description: Sessions are booked in Gulf Standard Time, planned around the school's own Arabic and Islamic Education commitments, moved to post-Iftar slots in Ramadan, and arranged back to back for siblings sharing one quiet room. Scheduling is where most tuition quietly fails, so we treat it as part of the teaching.

whyPoints.title: Told plainly when nobody is free
whyPoints.description: Specialist availability is finite, particularly for minority languages and some Higher Level options. If no tutor who teaches your child's syllabus has a slot that works, we say so and give you an honest timeframe rather than offering a near-match and hoping. A wrong tutor costs more than a wait.

faqs.question: What does an ADEK inspection rating tell me about the tutoring my child needs?
faqs.answer: It tells you where the school's own capacity sits, which narrows what you should buy. The overall band is a weighted summary of a whole school, so read one level down: the judgements on students' achievement and on teaching and assessment for your child's phase and subject group. If feedback quality is criticised, an outside tutor marking your child's work to the published markscheme fills a real gap. If subject availability is the problem, no rating fixes that and an online specialist is the practical answer. Check the current report on ADEK's own site rather than an old summary.

faqs.question: Why is Al Ain inspected by ADEK rather than KHDA?
faqs.answer: Because Al Ain is part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, not Dubai. Private schools in Abu Dhabi, Al Ain and Al Dhafra are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge. KHDA covers Dubai only, and Sharjah's private schools answer to SPEA, while the northern emirates sit with the federal Ministry of Education. This matters when you read advice online: guidance written for Dubai families about KHDA fee rules, inspection cycles or school ratings does not transfer directly to your child's school in Al Ain.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay per hour for a tutor in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Market rates published by other UAE providers give the range. Budget online tuition runs from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, a qualified subject teacher online between about AED 150 and AED 300, and visiting in-home tuition from around AED 180 to AED 500 because travel is priced inside the hour. Named IB and IGCSE specialists are quoted from AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Those are other companies' figures, not ours. Compare any quote per contact hour, since monthly bundles package very different amounts of teaching.

faqs.question: Is a visiting home tutor in Al Ain worth the extra cost over online lessons?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on the age. For primary-age children and some students with additional needs, having an adult in the room genuinely helps with focus in a way a screen does not. For Diploma and IGCSE students the calculation usually flips, because what decides the grade is whether the tutor has taught that exact paper. In a city with a smaller specialist pool, insisting on someone who can drive to your district on a Tuesday evening shrinks the list sharply. IB Gram delivers UAE tuition as live one-to-one online lessons; home visits are part of our India service only.

faqs.question: Al Ain has fewer IB schools than Abu Dhabi island. Can my child still get a Higher Level specialist?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the clearest reason local families use online tuition. A smaller private-school set means some Higher Level sciences and the less common languages are taught to a single small group, or are not offered at all. Online lessons remove geography from the match, so a Chemistry HL tutor who has taught the current guide can work with a student in Zakher as easily as one in Abu Dhabi. If no specialist in your child's exact syllabus has a workable slot, we will tell you that and give a realistic timeframe rather than substituting a near-match.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in the UAE need a permit, and should I ask to see one?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and a permit for individual private tutors is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. Every regulatory source we checked states that the permit itself carries no fee. Employed residents generally need their employer's agreement before tutoring privately. It is reasonable to ask any individual tutor working in the UAE about their permit position and their qualifications. Rules and processes change, so check the current requirements on the ministry's own channels rather than relying on a tutoring company's summary, including this one.

faqs.question: Which exam board does my child's school in Al Ain actually use?
faqs.answer: Check the statement of entry rather than assuming, because mixed entries are common here. Cambridge subjects carry four-digit codes such as 0580 for Mathematics, 0625 for Physics and 0620 for Chemistry. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE codes look like 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4CH1. Cambridge IGCSE 0580 also tiers into Core and Extended, and the tier caps the grade available, so it matters as much as the board. One family can easily have two children on different boards, and one student can carry both across subjects. Send us the entry document and we check it before the first session.

faqs.question: How are the marks split between the papers and the Internal Assessment in Diploma sciences?
faqs.answer: Under the current guides both Standard and Higher Level sit at 36 per cent for Paper 1, 44 per cent for Paper 2 and 20 per cent for the scientific investigation. The investigation is the component a student controls completely, in their own time, with feedback permitted, and it is worth a fifth of the grade. Families frequently buy exam cramming while that 20 per cent goes unsupervised. Weightings are revised between syllabus cycles, so confirm the current split with your school's coordinator or the published subject guide before planning around it.

faqs.question: When should a Diploma student in Al Ain start the Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Roughly nine months before the first paper, which for a May session means the spring and summer of DP1. The work that matters at that stage is not writing; it is narrowing the research question until the criteria are actually reachable. A question that is too broad, or that depends on data the student cannot collect, costs weeks that cannot be recovered later. Once a workable question exists, the drafting is manageable. Students who start in the autumn of DP2 collide with the Extended Essay, the TOK essay and four other investigations in the same twelve weeks.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Internal Assessment without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear line. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what each criterion rewards, discuss whether a research question is feasible, show the student how to mark their own draft against the descriptors, point out where a paragraph describes rather than argues, and check referencing against the school's required style. A tutor may not write or redraft any passage, supply text to insert, produce or alter data, choose the question, or write reflection entries. Any provider offering to supply a finished Internal Assessment is offering malpractice, and the consequence lands on the student.

faqs.question: Does my child still have to study Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the Diploma?
faqs.answer: In the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, ADEK requires private schools to teach Arabic, Islamic Education for Muslim students, and UAE Social Studies or moral education, for specified year groups and in specified amounts. Those hours sit on top of a six-subject Diploma or a full IGCSE set, and they carry real grade pressure on the school report even when they do not appear on the Diploma. We ask for the complete school timetable before fixing a slot, so a tuition session never collides with the school's own Arabic support. Your school's registrar can confirm exactly what applies to your child's year.

faqs.question: What is the Ministry of Education equivalency certificate, and when should we start it?
faqs.answer: It is the decision that a foreign school-leaving qualification is equivalent to the UAE national secondary certificate, which a UAE university will expect from an IB or British-curriculum applicant. For a Diploma student the usual question is whether the full Diploma was awarded and whether the subject spread meets the published threshold; for an IGCSE and A-level student it is a count of passes in a recognised combination. Start the file in DP1 or Year 11. Most problems are administrative: unattested transcripts, a name change, or a resit the school never recorded. Confirm current rules on the ministry's own portal.

faqs.question: Should my child take Maths AA or AI for UAE University admissions?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a degree decision rather than a difficulty decision, because Applications and Interpretation is not the easy option; it is the modelling and statistics route with heavy technology use and a great deal of written interpretation. Engineering, physics and some computing programmes commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, while economics, business and many life-science routes accept either. Published entry requirements change between intakes, so read the current page for the specific degree at the specific university rather than relying on what an older sibling was told. We check the route against the degree plan before a student commits.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most Al Ain students that is the better slot anyway. School days shorten during Ramadan and the productive hours for a teenager shift later, so we schedule lighter content work in the afternoons and move the demanding sessions to after Iftar. Because lessons are delivered online there is no travel to fit around the timing change, which is one practical advantage of the format during the month. We agree the revised timetable before Ramadan begins rather than rescheduling week by week, and go back to term timings afterwards.

faqs.question: We live in Zakher and the school run finishes late. When can sessions realistically start?
faqs.answer: Plan for a 6pm start on weekdays rather than 4.30pm. Zakher sits on the southern edge of the city towards Jebel Hafeet, and families whose children attend central or northern campuses have the longest run in Al Ain. Many Zakher families also shift the heavier subject to Friday or Saturday morning, when there is no commute at either end and a student can work for ninety minutes properly. We set the first few sessions deliberately late, see what arrival time actually looks like, then move it earlier if the family wants.

faqs.question: How does online tutoring handle practical work and the alternative-to-practical paper?
faqs.answer: The practical examination itself is run by the school or the examination centre, and no tutor replaces laboratory time. What tuition does cover is the written assessment of practical skills, which is where most of those marks actually sit: describing apparatus and method, identifying variables and controls, spotting anomalous results, handling uncertainty, and following table and graph conventions. We work through past practical and alternative-to-practical papers on screen, annotating the student's answers against the published markscheme. For the Diploma investigation, the design and analysis work is exactly what online sessions suit.

faqs.question: What happens if the first tutor is not the right match for my child?
faqs.answer: Tell us after the first or second session and we change the tutor, not the plan. A mismatch is usually about pace or explanation style rather than competence, and it shows up quickly: a student who answers in single words, or who leaves a session without a clear next task. We would rather re-match in week two than discover in week ten that nothing moved. The diagnostic session exists partly for this reason, because it gives both the tutor and the parent something concrete to judge the fit against.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start if the first paper is six weeks away?
faqs.answer: It is late for content and useful for technique. Six weeks before a paper, teaching new topics rarely pays; marking timed papers does. A short block in that window works when it is built around whole past papers, marked to the published markscheme, with errors logged by type rather than by topic, so the student keeps meeting the same mistake until it stops. What a six-week block cannot do is close a year-wide content gap, and we will say so plainly rather than selling a package that cannot deliver. No tutor can promise a particular score.

al-ain.closingHeading: Start with the report, then choose the subject specialist
al-ain.closingBody: Send us the last school report, the ADEK inspection page for your child's phase if you have it, and the statement of entry. We will read them, tell you whether the gap is content, technique, coursework or scheduling, and match an online IB tutor in Al Ain who teaches that exact syllabus. The first session is a marked paper, not a sales call, and if the honest answer is that your child does not need weekly tuition, that is what you will hear. Lessons are live one-to-one video, booked in Gulf Standard Time, with written feedback you can read.

intro.heading: What a UAE family is actually choosing when it chooses a tutor
paragraphs: A search for the best IB home tutor in the UAE usually starts with a bad mock paper and a short list of names. The names are the easy part. What decides whether tuition works here is a set of decisions nobody in the family made: which curriculum the school is licensed to teach, which authority inspects it, which board enters the child for examinations, and which compulsory subjects sit on the timetable alongside the Diploma. Hire well and ignore those, and you have bought competent teaching aimed at the wrong target.

The UAE is unusual in how much of this sits above the school. Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education. Five bodies, seven emirates, and a family that moves house can change regulator without changing country.

That matters in a concrete way. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so what a child sits has been signed off locally as well as by the board. In Dubai, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in every private school whatever curriculum it holds a licence for, and the Ministry controls the content used in them. An IB home tutor in Dubai who treats those lessons as spare revision time is working against the school's own licence rather than with it.

The second choice is format, and the honest answer there is narrow. Rates published by UAE providers put a tutor visiting a home at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the number, against roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject teacher working online. IB Gram delivers lessons one-to-one over live video only. Home visits are a service offered in India, not here. No IB Gram tutor attends a UAE address, and nothing on this page pretends otherwise.

What the online format buys is choice. A Higher Level Chemistry teacher who has taught the current scientific investigation criteria is scarce in any single emirate and scarcer still within a twenty-minute drive of one particular villa. Online IB tutoring in the UAE removes the radius and leaves the variables that actually move a grade: the right specialist, the right level, the right number of hours, and a schedule that survives the school run, prayer times and a shortened Ramadan day. The rest of this page is about what the system has already decided for you, and what it has left open.

best-ib-home-tutor.programmesIntro: The IB runs four programmes, and UAE schools licence them in different combinations. Knowing which one a child is in decides what tuition can usefully do, because the assessment model changes completely between them. Each note below says what the UAE school system adds on top of the IB's own requirements.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations. Learning is organised through transdisciplinary units of inquiry, and reporting is based on teacher judgement against the programme's learning outcomes rather than on marks. Support at this stage is about literacy, number fluency and the habits that make a Middle Years transition survivable: reading stamina, written structure, and comfort with being asked to explain a method rather than produce an answer.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, a PYP child already carries Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies on the timetable, streamed separately for Arab and non-Arab pupils. Families often discover the Arabic stream only when the first report arrives. Getting the stream right early is cheaper than correcting it in Year 7.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP is assessed against criteria lettered A to D in each subject, scored out of 8 per criterion, with grade boundaries applied to the total. Those letters are the grammar of the whole programme, and most lost marks come from writing an answer that never addresses the criterion being tested. Optional eAssessment in Year 11 gives an externally moderated result for schools that choose it.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools run MYP to Year 9 then switch to IGCSE, which means a child can meet two assessment systems in three years. A Middle Years student heading for the Diploma in a UAE school needs the criterion habit intact; a child heading for IGCSE needs the opposite reflex, because mark schemes reward different things.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the core: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject is scored out of 7, with up to three further points from the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, to a maximum of 45. Twenty-four points is the pass threshold, subject to the IB's conditions on failing grades and core components.
programmes.countryNote: A UAE Diploma student carries the compulsory Ministry subjects on top of six IB courses, so the week is tighter than the IB's own guided-hours figures suggest. Registration for the session is made by the school, not the family, and the Diploma then needs a Ministry of Education equivalency file before it can be used for a UAE university application.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, plus a core of personal and professional skills, service learning, language development and a reflective project. It suits a student who wants Diploma-level subject rigour in two or three areas without the full six-subject load, and it is assessed through a mix of IB examinations and the career-related provider's own assessment.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is licensed by only a small number of UAE schools, so a family that wants it is usually choosing a school as much as a programme. Tuition for a CP student is normally concentrated on the Diploma courses inside it, because those carry the externally examined marks that universities read.

best-ib-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma courses UAE families most often ask about, with what each one actually assesses. The description matters more than the subject name: a tutor who knows Mathematics in general is not the same as one who knows where the Applications and Interpretation papers differ from Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency, calculus and proof, with a no-calculator paper at both levels. Higher Level adds depth across the same five topic areas and a third paper of extended problem-solving. Marks are lost in the move between a correct method and a justified conclusion, and in the exploration where modelling is left unexamined.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-assisted work, with a graphic display calculator permitted throughout. Higher Level adds matrices, graph theory and more demanding statistical inference. Students who chose this route to avoid proof are often surprised by how much interpretation of output the papers ask for in words rather than symbols.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields, waves and nuclear physics, with Higher Level extending the same chapters rather than adding separate ones. The scientific investigation and the data-based questions reward uncertainty handling, which is the single most commonly undertaught part of the course in a crowded UAE timetable.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity across organic, physical and inorganic topics, with multi-step calculation under time pressure. Higher Level work on organic mechanisms and energetics separates grades. The internal investigation asks for a research design that can actually be run, and weak designs cap the mark long before the data is analysed.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Unity and diversity, interaction and interdependence, across molecular to ecosystem scales. The volume of content tempts memorisation, but the papers reward applying a named mechanism to an unfamiliar context. Command terms do most of the damage here: outline, explain and justify ask for three different answers of three different lengths.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, assessed through extended response and a portfolio of three commentaries on published articles. Higher Level adds quantitative demands and a policy paper. Diagram accuracy is worth more than most students expect, and an unlabelled axis costs marks no amount of prose recovers.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisational structure, marketing, operations and finance, with case-study examinations and a written commentary. Tools are examined as analysis, not recall, so a student who can define a framework but cannot apply it to the case loses the top band. Financial calculation is the fastest place to recover marks before a session.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Non-literary and literary texts, assessed through guided analysis, a comparative essay, an individual oral and, at Higher Level, a separate essay on a studied work. Students who read well but write loosely sit in the middle bands; structure and a controlled line of inquiry move them up.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Receptive, productive and interactive skills across the IB's prescribed themes. For UAE families this course usually runs beside the school's own compulsory Arabic lessons, which follow Ministry content rather than the IB's. Keeping the two separate in a child's head is a real part of the work.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Systems fundamentals, computational thinking and a solution developed for a real client. Higher Level adds abstract data structures and a case study set annually. The solution component fails most often on documentation and testing evidence rather than on code, which is where a review session earns its fee.

best-ib-home-tutor.regionsTitle: Which authority sits above your child's school, emirate by emirate
best-ib-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Tuition plans in the UAE are shaped by the emirate more than by the neighbourhood, because the emirate decides who licenses, inspects and in some cases approves the assessment your child sits. Here is the practical position in each, with what it changes for a family buying private lessons.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The Knowledge and Human Development Authority oversees private education quality here and publishes the mandatory-subject requirements that apply whatever curriculum a school holds. With 227 private schools and 17 curricula in 2024-25, two children on the same street can sit entirely different papers.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and its professional-ethics rules for school staff bar paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. An IB Diploma tutor in Abu Dhabi should never be your child's own class teacher taking cash.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Al Ain sits under the same Abu Dhabi authority as the capital, but with a smaller IB cohort and fewer Higher Level sets per school. That is precisely the situation where a drive-time search returns a tutor for the subject you did not need and nobody for the one you did.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. An IB Higher Level tutor in Sharjah therefore works to a syllabus that has been cleared locally as well as by the board.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Private education here is regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which also approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Families routinely drive to Dubai or Sharjah for subject help; over live video that drive stops being part of the cost of a Tuesday evening.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Ajman's private schools fall to the federal Ministry of Education, which supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Many Ajman Diploma students commute into Sharjah or Dubai for school, so a session rarely starts before 6pm on a weekday.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised federally by the Ministry of Education. The IB cohort is small enough that a single Higher Level option can run with a handful of students, which makes a specialist outside the emirate the realistic option rather than the fallback.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the Ministry of Education, on the opposite coast from the Dubai school cluster. Nobody is driving a Physics Higher Level specialist over the mountains twice a week at a sensible price, which is the clearest case in the country for teaching live over video.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai, under the Knowledge and Human Development Authority
schoolClusters.note: Dubai holds the largest concentration of schools running the Diploma in the country, and the 2026-27 intake adds three more IB schools among seven new openings. More schools competing for the same experienced Higher Level teachers is the supply story behind most tutoring enquiries here.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, under the Department of Education and Knowledge
schoolClusters.note: The capital's Diploma schools are spread between the island, Khalifa City and Al Raha, with Al Ain further inland and thinner on Higher Level sciences. ADEK's ethics rules for school staff are the reason a tutor here should be someone with no connection to your child's school.

Sharjah is regulated by its own authority; Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge; Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry. Diploma cohorts shrink as you move north, which changes the question from which tutor to whether one exists within reach at all.

sections.heading: Best IB home tutor in the UAE: what is fixed, and what is actually yours to choose
paragraphs: Treat the search as a shortlist problem and you will compare the wrong things. Most of what determines whether a child's Diploma goes well was decided by an institution: the emirate regulator that licensed the school, the board that administers the papers, the Ministry rule that puts three extra subjects on the timetable, and the option blocks that decided which Higher Levels were even available. None of those move because a better tutor was hired.

What does move is the quality of the match inside those constraints. A family choosing between two tutors is really choosing between two levels of syllabus knowledge, two levels of honesty about availability, and two formats with very different time costs. Those are worth comparing carefully. Whether a tutor lives in Jumeirah or in Mumbai is worth almost nothing once the lesson is delivered live over video.

The table below splits the decisions. The left-hand column is the thing families most often try to influence late and at expense; the right-hand column is where the same money and attention produce a measurable result. Read it before a single enquiry goes out, because it also tells you which questions a provider should be able to answer in one sentence and which ones are not theirs to answer at all. A provider who cannot say which authority regulates your child's school, or who the entry deadline belongs to, is not going to catch the administrative mistake that costs a grade.

sections.heading: Four authorities sit above a single IB lesson in the UAE
paragraphs: A Diploma lesson in Dubai looks like a private arrangement between two people. It is not. Five separate bodies have a say in what is taught, when it is examined and who may be paid to teach it, and each of them publishes its position. A provider that cannot name them is telling you something about how closely it has read the market it sells into.

The federal position is the baseline everything else sits on: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That single sentence explains why an IB school in Ajman and a British school in Dubai both run the same three compulsory subjects, and why no international curriculum licence exempts a child from them.

Above the individual lesson sits the private tuition question. Paid private teaching in the UAE runs through the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure is quoted here. A parent may simply ask to see the permit before the first paid lesson.

sections.heading: A school sector adding places faster than it adds Higher Level teachers
paragraphs: The reason a Higher Level specialist is hard to book in a city this size is arithmetic rather than bad luck. Dubai's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum at 37% of the roll, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. The Diploma is a minority programme inside a very large market.

The sector is also growing. Six new private schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. The 2026-27 intake adds seven more, four following the UK curriculum and three the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. Three additional IB schools is good news for choice and awkward news for staffing, because experienced Higher Level teachers in the harder sciences and mathematics are the scarcest item in the system and new schools recruit from the same pool everybody else does.

Cost context has moved in the opposite direction. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. A family's tutoring budget is not being compressed by a fee rise this year, which makes the planning question how to spend it well rather than whether to spend at all. The sensible move in a tightening staff market is to book the scarce subject early and treat the easier ones as the flexible part of the plan, rather than the other way round.

sections.heading: The subjects on the timetable that a private tutor may not redesign
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are not optional extras in a Dubai private school. They are mandatory regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For a Diploma student that means three courses running beside six IB subjects and the core.

What surprises families is how prescriptive the rules are. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies for Arab students runs primarily in Arabic; non-Arabs are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two further rules constrain what any outside tutor can honestly offer. Schools must ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. A tutor who arrives with a worksheet pack of their own for these courses is not adding value; they are working outside the rule the school has to follow. Instructional time, meanwhile, is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with lesson length allowed to vary provided the weekly total is met and at least 25 minutes advised for any mandatory-subject lesson.

sections.heading: Why the search says home tutor and the lesson happens over live video
paragraphs: Parents type home tutor because that is what the market has sold for twenty years in this region, and the phrase still describes the thing being bought: private, one-to-one teaching organised around the family's week rather than the school's. What has changed is that the delivery no longer requires somebody in the car. IB Gram delivers this as live one-to-one online tuition to families in all seven emirates, and home visits are a service offered in India only.

Said plainly: no IB Gram tutor attends an address in the UAE, in any emirate, at any price. That is a product decision and it has reasons a parent can check. A visiting tutor is selected from whoever teaches the subject within a tolerable drive; an online specialist is selected from everybody who has taught that syllabus at that level. For Higher Level sciences and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, those two pools are not close in size.

The time arithmetic is the other half of it. A visiting tutor usually needs a two-hour minimum because the travel has to be worth the trip, which forces a weekday session that starts late and ends later. A 60 or 90-minute video session fits between the school bus and dinner, survives a traffic day, and can move to a post-Iftar slot during Ramadan without anybody renegotiating a driving route. The comparison below sets out what genuinely differs and what the UAE system fixes either way.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges for each arrangement
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for this kind of query publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. Below are the AED bands actually published by providers selling into this market, read in October 2026, with the source named in every row. These are market rates, not an IB Gram price list.

Read the bands as descriptions of what is inside the hour rather than as quality tiers. The low band usually buys supervised homework from someone with a good recent grade in the subject. The middle band usually buys a teacher who knows the paper structure and the mark scheme's language. The upper bands buy scarcity: a Higher Level specialist in a thin subject, or short-notice work in an exam term. Travel is the single biggest reason an in-home rate sits above an online one for the same teacher.

Monthly packages are where the arithmetic gets slippery. Figures seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, and rate trackers put weekly one-hour tutoring at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Divide any package by its teaching hours before comparing it with an hourly rate, and ask what happens to unused sessions. IB Gram quotes after a consultation and a free trial lesson rather than publishing a tariff, because the hours a child needs depend on the subject, the level and how far out you are starting.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, and the hours each one actually needs
paragraphs: The level decision does more to a tutoring budget than the choice of tutor does, and it is usually made in a rush during an option-block meeting. The IB publishes guided teaching hours of 150 for a Standard Level course and 240 for a Higher Level one. That ninety-hour gap is roughly a term and a half of classroom time, which is why a student who switches up late cannot be caught up by six weeks of private lessons, however good they are.

Points behave differently from how families expect. Every subject is scored out of 7 whether it is taken at Higher or Standard Level, with up to three further points available from the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. Moving a struggling Higher Level down to Standard does not cost points directly. What it changes is which university courses will accept the profile afterwards, which is a question for the named university's own entry page rather than for a tutor.

Where tutoring earns its place is after the level is locked. Higher Level work is topic-specific: the extra material in a Higher Level science is depth inside the same chapters rather than separate units, so general revision does very little and targeted teaching does a lot. Standard Level students more often need exam technique, command-term discipline and timing, because the content load is manageable and the marks are lost in how answers are written rather than in what the student knows.

sections.heading: What each piece of internally assessed work is allowed to be
paragraphs: Internally assessed components are where a tutoring relationship either proves itself or becomes a liability for the student. The limits are published in the subject guides and they are limits, not targets: an Extended Essay stops at 4,000 words, a Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,600 on a prescribed title. Markers stop reading at the limit, so a student who writes past it has thrown away the best part of their argument.

Those limits move between syllabus versions, and a page that publishes them as permanent facts will eventually be wrong. Treat the table below as a working reference and confirm each figure against the current subject guide through your child's coordinator, who holds the version the school is actually teaching. The marks matter as much as the word counts. The Mathematics exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria lettered A to E: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The sciences investigation is marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Students lose most of their marks in the criteria that reward thinking about the work rather than doing it.

The boundary is simple to state and the thing most essay-selling competitors ignore. A tutor may discuss a research question, teach the criterion a student keeps missing, read one draft and give written feedback the student then acts on, and teach referencing properly. A tutor may not choose the topic, supply paragraphs, process the data or edit a draft to a finished state. Your child's coordinator has to declare what outside help was used, and that declaration must be accurate. IB Gram works only on the teaching side of that line, and the most useful thing a provider can do for a worried parent is say so in writing before any money changes hands.

sections.heading: Who owns each deadline in the exam year
paragraphs: Almost every date that matters in an exam year belongs to somebody other than the parent, and the most expensive mistakes are administrative rather than academic. The pattern is easiest to see in a published Cambridge series. For the March 2027 series, the examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, but final entries are due on 27 November 2026 and forecast grades on 27 February 2027. Results reach centres through Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June.

Read that sequence backwards and the planning becomes obvious. The entry deadline sits more than two months before the first paper, which means tier and subject decisions have to be settled in the autumn term, while the mocks that justify a forecast grade have to be sat and marked before late February. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the school which zone it sits in, in writing.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November series, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Because Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, always work from the live official PDF rather than a date copied onto a tutoring page. IGCSE exam entry deadlines in the UAE are set by the board and submitted by the school as examination centre, never by the family. For the IB's own session dates we publish nothing: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so ask your child's coordinator and work from what the school confirms in writing.

sections.heading: Equivalency and attestation: what the Ministry counts, and the number nobody should invent
paragraphs: A Diploma or a set of IGCSEs is not automatically usable for a UAE university application. The Ministry of Education runs an equivalency route that converts a foreign secondary certificate into something UAE institutions recognise, and the requirements differ by curriculum. For the British track, students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3.

Two details inside that rule are routinely got wrong by pages ranking for these queries. The first is the subject count: the reported requirement is five accredited subjects, and at least one page ranking for UAE tutoring queries tells parents it is six. The second is what counts towards the five: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. On the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying.

For MoE equivalency for IB students there is a deliberate blank on this page. The reporting we have read does not state an IB points threshold, and no figure should be published without reading it on moe.gov.ae or the emirate's own attestation channel. Nor is equivalency something a tutoring company performs or influences. It is a process a family completes with the Ministry, using documents the school issues. What tuition can legitimately do is prepare a child for the standardised tests the American track asks for, and make sure the certificate arriving in June is one worth attesting.

sections.heading: When nobody is free: what honest unavailability looks like
paragraphs: No competitor page found in this market discloses a coverage limit, and several conceal non-UAE delivery behind an overseas phone number. The useful thing a provider can tell a parent is where it runs out, because a wasted trial lesson in an exam term costs more than the lesson. Our position on availability is published rather than implied, and it is the same whether you are in Dubai Marina or Dibba.

Supply is shaped by the same thing that shapes everything else here: cohort size. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the most requested single slot in the country, and the 5pm to 8pm Gulf Standard Time window is the most contested. Higher Level Chemistry and Physics thin out quickly in the northern emirates, where a school may run the option for a handful of students. Arts subjects at Higher Level are barely covered by any UAE provider, ourselves included, and saying so early is more useful than a hopeful maybe.

Where no UAE-based specialist is free, we match a Diploma teacher from our India-based teaching team, delivered over the same live video format, and we say that at the point of matching rather than after the first invoice. The syllabus, the board and the criteria do not change with the teacher's time zone; the session time sometimes does. Extended Essay supervision in the UAE remains with the school's own supervisor in every case, and what we provide around it is process coaching, not supervision.
