process.title: Tell us the school and the emirate first
process.description: Not just the subject. Which school, which emirate, which programme and which level decides the regulator, the board, the compulsory subjects and the option blocks a tutor has to work inside. Two Diploma students in different emirates can need different plans for the same subject at the same level.

process.title: A short consultation, with the dates on the table
process.description: We ask what the last three pieces of assessed work scored, which session the school has registered the child for, and what the coordinator has said about coursework deadlines. That conversation decides whether this is a two-year build or a single-term push, and roughly how many hours it needs.

process.title: Matched to a named specialist, with availability stated
process.description: You are told who the teacher is, what they have taught at that level, and whether they are based in the UAE or elsewhere. If nobody suitable is free for the time you need, we say so at this point rather than offering a near-enough match and hoping.

process.title: A free trial lesson before any payment
process.description: One lesson, with the specialist you would continue with, on a topic you choose from recent schoolwork. No payment is taken before it and no card is held. You get a written summary afterwards saying what the teacher found, which is the honest basis for deciding whether to carry on.

process.title: A weekly slot, a written record, and a review date
process.description: Lessons run live over video in Gulf Standard Time, with a short written note after each one. We set a review date about six sessions in to look at what has actually changed in the marks. Sessions move for Ramadan timings, mocks and the examination weeks themselves.

whyPoints.title: The regulator is named, not implied
whyPoints.description: This page names KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge and the federal Ministry of Education, and says what each one governs. IB Gram holds no permit, licence or recognition from any of them, and claims none. Explaining a regulator is useful; borrowing its authority is not.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure carries its source
whyPoints.description: The rate table quotes what other providers and a published rate tracker put in print, read in October 2026, with the source in the row. We publish no invented statistics, no satisfaction percentages and no self-assigned star ratings, because a figure without a source is worth nothing to a parent comparing options.

whyPoints.title: Coursework is taught, never produced
whyPoints.description: There are operations in this market selling completed internal assessments. We teach the criterion, question the research question and read one draft with written feedback. The student writes the work. That is an IB rule, and it is also the difference between help that survives a coordinator's declaration and help that ends a Diploma.

whyPoints.title: Delivery is stated before you pay, not after
whyPoints.description: Lessons are live, one-to-one and online. No IB Gram tutor attends an address in the UAE; home visits are a service offered in India. If the specialist for your subject sits outside the UAE, you are told at the point of matching, with no overseas phone number standing in for an explanation.

whyPoints.title: Dates come from the body that sets them
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page come from the boards' own published key dates and timetables. The IB's session dates are absent on purpose, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unverified date on a tutoring page is how a family misses a deadline that belongs to the school.

faqs.question: Why is this page about a home tutor when the lessons happen over live video?
faqs.answer: Because home tutor is the phrase UAE parents actually search, and it describes the service accurately: private, one-to-one teaching organised around your family's week. The delivery is the part that has changed. IB Gram teaches live, one-to-one, over video to families in all seven emirates, and home visits are a service offered in India only. No IB Gram tutor attends an address in the UAE. The trade is deliberate: you give up somebody in the room and you get the specialist who has actually taught your child's syllabus at that level, instead of whoever teaches that subject within a tolerable drive.

faqs.question: Which parts of my child's IB course are fixed before I hire anybody?
faqs.answer: More than most families expect. The curriculum the school is licensed to teach, the authority that inspects it, the compulsory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons, the exam board, the timetable zone, the option blocks that decided which Higher Levels were available, and the session the school registers for are all settled by institutions. What is left to you is genuinely significant: which specialist teaches your child, at what level, for how many hours a week, in what session length, and when the work starts relative to the entry deadline. Spend your attention there, because that is where it changes an outcome.

faqs.question: Which authority licensed my child's school, and what does it reach into?
faqs.answer: It depends on the emirate. Dubai's private schools sit with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge; both approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. So the body above your school can reach into fees and assessment methods, not just inspection, and its school listing is where you verify any school a provider names.

faqs.question: Does the federal Ministry of Education decide anything inside an IB school?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but they must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That federal baseline is why an IB school and a British school in the same street both run the same three compulsory subjects, and why no international curriculum licence exempts a child from them. For the mandatory subjects the Ministry also controls content: using different or additional material without prior permission is strictly prohibited, which is a real limit on what any outside tutor can offer in those lessons.

faqs.question: Dubai opens seven more private schools in 2026-27. Does that help us find a Higher Level teacher?
faqs.answer: Not immediately, and possibly the opposite in the short term. The seven new schools include three running the International Baccalaureate, and they create 16,846 new places. Those schools recruit experienced Higher Level teachers from the same pool every existing school draws on, and the pool grows more slowly than the seat count. Six schools opened in 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6% over the same period. More choice of school is good news. For a family trying to book a Higher Level Chemistry specialist in an exam term, it mostly means booking earlier and accepting that the right teacher may not live nearby.

faqs.question: Why is a tutor not free to invent their own Islamic Education or Social Studies material?
faqs.answer: Because the content for the mandatory UAE subjects is controlled. KHDA's guidance states that for these subjects the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the Ministry of Education, is strictly prohibited. Schools must also ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach them. So a tutor arriving with a worksheet pack of their own is not adding value in these lessons; they are working outside the rule the school itself has to follow. Legitimate support means working from the school's own material, in the language the school assesses the child in, on revision method and exam technique.

faqs.question: Our school builds its timetable from 40-minute units. How long should a tuition session be?
faqs.answer: KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. That tells you something useful about attention: a child used to 40-minute blocks does not suddenly concentrate for 120. For Diploma subject teaching we normally use 60 or 90 minutes, which gives room for a timed question plus feedback without losing the second half. A visiting tutor's two-hour minimum usually exists because the travel has to be worth the trip, not because two hours teaches better.

faqs.question: Which criteria is the IB Mathematics exploration marked against, letter by letter?
faqs.answer: The exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria lettered A to E: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with use of mathematics carrying the largest allocation. Most students arrive with the mathematics in reasonable shape and lose marks on reflection and personal engagement, because those reward writing about the decisions made rather than the calculation itself. Confirm the exact allocations against the current subject guide through your child's coordinator, since criteria wording and marks change between syllabus versions. A tutor may teach the mathematics and show how reflection is credited; selecting the topic or writing the commentary is not available at any price.

faqs.question: Does the Extended Essay really have to stop at 4,000 words?
faqs.answer: Yes, 4,000 words is a maximum rather than a target, and it is enforced by markers simply stopping at the limit. A student who writes 4,600 words has thrown away whatever argument sat in the last 600, which is usually the conclusion they worked hardest on. Confirm the current figure with the coordinator, because component requirements move between guide versions. A tutor's legitimate role is to question whether the research question is answerable in that length, teach referencing properly, and read one draft with written feedback the student then acts on. The supervisor remains the school's supervisor throughout.

faqs.question: How many taught hours separate a Higher Level subject from a Standard Level one?
faqs.answer: The IB publishes guided teaching hours of 150 for a Standard Level course and 240 for a Higher Level one. The ninety-hour difference is roughly a term and a half of classroom time, which is the single most useful number in any conversation about switching levels. It explains why moving up late in the first Diploma year rarely works, and why six weeks of private lessons cannot substitute for it. Moving down is a different matter and often sensible, because every subject is scored out of 7 regardless of level. The real cost of moving down is which university courses will accept the profile afterwards.

faqs.question: My daughter wants to move a Higher Level down to Standard Level. Who has to agree?
faqs.answer: The school does, through the Diploma coordinator, and the window is narrower than most families assume because the change has to be reflected in the registration the school submits to the IB. Ask in writing, ask early, and ask what the deadline for the change actually is rather than when the coordinator would prefer to discuss it. Before you ask, check the entry requirements of the courses your daughter is likely to apply to, since medicine, engineering and economics-type degrees commonly expect specific subjects at Higher Level. A tutor can tell you whether the current grade is recoverable; only the university can tell you whether the profile still works.

faqs.question: Can a UAE family enter a child for IGCSE as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: Entries are made by a registered examination centre, not by a family directly, so the practical question is which centre in the UAE will accept a private candidate for the subjects you want and in which series. Some schools and independent centres do; many do not, and availability varies by subject because practical and speaking components need facilities and assessors. Ask the centre about final entry deadlines, the administrative zone its timetable follows, and which components it can host before you plan any teaching. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, so this is an autumn-term conversation for a spring series, not a spring one.

faqs.question: Who owns each deadline in the exam year, the school, the board or us?
faqs.answer: Almost none of them belong to the family. In Cambridge's published March 2027 series, final entries fall on 27 November 2026 and are submitted by the school as examination centre; forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027 from the subject teacher; the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027 and is set by Cambridge, by zone; results reach centres on 13 May and certificates in late June. The family owns only the preparation and the decisions that feed those dates: level choices before entries close, and mocks sat early enough for a forecast grade to rest on evidence.

faqs.question: Is the equivalency file something a tutoring provider should be handling for us?
faqs.answer: No. Ministry of Education equivalency is a process a family completes with the Ministry and the emirate's attestation channel, using documents the school issues. Any provider offering to perform or secure it is overstating its role. What the reporting does establish for the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE at no less than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. For the IB there is no points figure we can cite, so verify it on moe.gov.ae rather than trusting any tutoring page.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects run short of teachers across the UAE, and what then?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Chemistry and Physics are the usual pressure points, badly so in the northern emirates where a school might run the option for a handful of students. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is not scarce so much as congested, with everybody wanting the same 5pm to 8pm Gulf Standard Time window. Higher Level arts subjects are barely covered by providers in this market, ourselves included. Where no UAE-based specialist is free we match a Diploma teacher from our India-based team over the same live video format, and we say so at matching. Where we cannot cover a subject properly, we decline on the first call.

faqs.question: If our tutor teaches from outside the UAE, whose rules apply?
faqs.answer: The IB's academic-honesty rules and your school's own policies apply regardless of where the teacher sits, and those are the rules that can actually affect your child's Diploma. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, governs individuals providing paid private tuition in the UAE; it is granted free of charge for two years and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Ask any UAE-resident tutor to show theirs. The service page on mohre.gov.ae is the official route and lists no fee.

faqs.question: How long is the Theory of Knowledge essay, and what else does the course require?
faqs.answer: The Theory of Knowledge essay is written on a prescribed title set by the IB and runs to a maximum of 1,600 words, alongside an exhibition component in which a student explains how objects connect to a prompt. It is externally marked. Theory of Knowledge is also one half of the combination that can add up to three points to a Diploma total, with the Extended Essay, so it is worth more attention than its timetable allocation suggests. A tutor can teach the knowledge framework and question the strength of an argument. Choosing the line of argument, or drafting the essay, is not legitimate help.

faqs.question: Does my child's UAE school even offer the November IB session?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and it is worth establishing before anybody plans around a retake. UAE schools overwhelmingly sit the May session, which fits the local academic year, and whether a November option exists for your child depends on what the school registers for rather than on what the IB offers globally. Ask the coordinator in writing which session the registration names and what the school's position is on a November retake. We publish no IB session or results dates on this page: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so any date here would be unverified, and a wrong date is how a family misses something that belongs to the school.

best-ib-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the school, the emirate and the session
best-ib-home-tutor.closingBody: If you are weighing up the best IB home tutor in the UAE, the three facts that shape every sensible answer are which school your child attends, which emirate regulates it, and which session the school has registered for. Send those with the subject and level and we can tell you in one conversation whether a specialist is free for the time you need, whether the plan is a two-year build or a single-term push, and roughly how many hours it takes. The first lesson is free and happens before any payment. Lessons are live, one-to-one and online, and if we cannot cover your child's subject properly we will say so on that first call.

best-ib-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Diploma and MYP subjects at the levels UAE families ask for most, with Higher Level maths and sciences first. Each profile states the subjects and levels taught, so you can see whether the person you are quoted for is the person who will actually teach the subject.

intro.heading: Price, not reputation, is what parents are really comparing
paragraphs: A search for the best IB online tutor in the UAE almost never comes from a parent who wants a league table. It comes from a parent who has three quotes in a WhatsApp thread - AED 120, AED 260 and AED 450 for the same Higher Level subject - and no way to tell which number is justified. Nobody publishes an IB tutor ranking for this country, and any page that claims to hold one has written it themselves. What can be published is the market: who charges what, on what evidence, and what the difference actually buys.

Here is the range as it stood in October 2026. Budget online tuition advertises from AED 45-65 at EdFlik and from AED 33-52 at Tutopiya. A qualified subject tutor working online sits roughly AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level work runs AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase quoting AED 270. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650 for a named premium tutor. Those are other companies' prices, read from their own pages, and they are the honest starting point for any conversation about value.

Four things move a rate inside that range, and only four are worth paying for: the level being taught, the scarcity of the subject at that level, the amount of marking and written feedback included, and the hour of the evening you want. Everything else - a logo, a claimed ranking, a star rating a company awarded itself - is priced and sold but not delivered. One UAE provider publishes an average rating in its page code that does not match the figure a reader sees on the page; that is the kind of detail worth checking before the rate is.

Value also depends on when the money is spent. A Diploma family that buys twelve hours in September of DP1 to fix algebraic fluency usually spends less, in total, than the family that buys thirty hours in March of DP2 to recover the same marks under deadline pressure. Hours bought late are hours spent on triage: past papers rather than understanding. The cheapest tutoring in this market is the tutoring that starts early enough to be ordinary.

One structural point about delivery. Lessons for UAE families are taught one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. The reason is supply rather than cost: the IB accounted for 7 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25, across 227 private schools, and a Higher Level Chemistry or Maths Analysis and Approaches specialist is a small subset of a small subset. A screen widens the pool from whoever sits within a twenty-minute drive to whoever actually teaches that syllabus at that level.

What follows is the arithmetic rather than the pitch: rate bands by what is being taught, the premium claims that survive a check, what to measure in a free trial lesson, the two decisions that quietly determine two years of spending, and the one service that no amount of money should buy.

best-ib-online-tutor.programmesIntro: IB Gram covers three IB programmes for UAE families, plus the Career-related Programme where a school runs it. The cost profile differs in each: primary work is short and diagnostic, Middle Years work is about habits, and the Diploma is where the hours and the money concentrate.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The Primary Years Programme is inquiry-led and has no external examinations, so tutoring here is diagnostic rather than remedial. Most UAE families who book primary support are chasing one of two things: an English reading level that has slipped behind the class, or number fluency that will matter in three years rather than three weeks. Sessions are short - thirty to forty-five minutes holds attention better than a full hour - and the useful output is a written note of what to practise between lessons.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, Arabic runs from the first years of primary in every private school whatever the licensed curriculum, which is why a primary parent's first tutoring question here is often about Arabic rather than maths. Market rates for primary support sit at the bottom of the published range, from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget end.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The Middle Years Programme marks against criteria in most subjects, on a scale per criterion rather than a single percentage, and that is where families lose track. A report reading 5, 6, 4, 5 tells you more than a percentage does, but only if somebody reads which criterion is weak. MYP tutoring that works is criterion-targeted: one criterion at a time, with the school's own task sheet on the shared screen in front of both of them.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 4 and 5 are the cheapest years to buy help in the UAE and the most commonly skipped. The jump from MYP 5 into Diploma sciences and Maths Analysis and Approaches is the gap that generates the biggest bills in DP1, and a term of MYP 5 support at the AED 150-250 band published in this market costs a fraction of repairing it later.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Higher Level carries more teaching hours, an additional paper in several subjects, and the Internal Assessment that most students underestimate. This is where specialist rates apply: UAE providers quote AED 200-450 and above for IB Higher Level work, and the premium is paid for scarcity at that level rather than for the brand printed on the invoice.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, with a November session existing for retakes. Entries are made by the school months before the first paper, so a family that wants a level changed has to raise it before that internal deadline. Ask your child's coordinator for the written internal calendar in the first term of DP1; it costs nothing and it decides when tutoring money is worth spending.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller number of UAE schools run the Career-related Programme, which pairs Diploma courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. Tutoring demand here is narrow and sits mostly on the DP courses inside the CP, plus academic English for the reflective project. Because the cohort is small, a subject specialist for a CP combination can take longer to match than a mainstream Diploma subject at the same level.
programmes.countryNote: Check which programmes your child's school is authorised to run before assuming a CP route exists in your emirate; the regulator's school listing and the school's own authorisation page are where to look. Fees and curricula at private schools in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah are approved by the emirate authority, so programme availability is not purely a school decision.

best-ib-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Demand is not evenly spread, and neither is price. The subjects below are the ones UAE families ask for most, each with a note on where the marks actually sit - because that is what decides whether an hour of tuition is worth AED 200 or worth nothing at all.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most requested Diploma subject in this market and the most expensive to fix late. Higher Level adds Paper 3, a longer problem-solving paper, on top of Papers 1 and 2. Marks go missing in algebraic manipulation carried over from IGCSE, in calculus notation, and in the exploration, which is marked against criteria A to E out of 20.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Chosen by students heading for business, psychology and design, and often chosen late. The statistics and modelling content rewards technology fluency, so a session where the student drives the graphic display calculator beats one where the tutor demonstrates it. Check university prerequisites before switching: several engineering and physics courses expect Analysis and Approaches instead.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and the data-based paper are where Higher Level students lose ground. The internal assessment is a single scientific investigation marked out of 24, and the most common failure is a research question too broad to produce controlled data. Confirm the current criteria with your child's teacher before planning sessions around it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields, circuits and the Higher Level extension topics absorb the most tutoring time, and the arithmetic of uncertainties quietly costs marks across every paper. Online sessions handle this well, because the working happens on a shared screen where a tutor sees each line rather than only the final answer.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A memory-heavy syllabus where marks are lost to command terms rather than to content: a question that says outline and an answer that explains scores no better than one that says too little. Useful sessions here are short, frequent, and built on the student's own most recent piece of written work.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams and the evaluation command terms carry the marks, and the Higher Level paper adds quantitative work that catches students who chose the subject to avoid maths. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on published news articles, which a tutor may discuss but must not draft.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and Paper 1's unseen analysis are the two components where preparation visibly changes a grade. Sessions work best when built around texts the school has actually taught, so ask for the school's reading list before the first lesson rather than after it.

subjects.name: Arabic in the school stream
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must run Arabic for all students, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups, and the content is set by the Ministry. Support here is about reaching the school's own material rather than replacing it, since schools may not use different or additional content without prior Ministry permission.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Neither is a subject, both are graded, and together they move the final points total. Support is process coaching: question framing, source evaluation, and reading a draft against the published criteria. The Extended Essay carries a 4,000-word limit and the TOK essay a 1,600-word limit; the text inside both has to be the student's own.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study command terms and the Higher Level extension are where marks move, and students who read the stimulus material too quickly lose application marks they already had the content for. Tutoring is mostly structured practice against the school's own marked work rather than fresh content delivery.

best-ib-online-tutor.regionsTitle: What the market looks like in each emirate
best-ib-online-tutor.regionsIntro: Rates and supply are not the same across the country. The notes below are about cost and availability rather than scenery: which authority sits above your child's school, how deep the local tutor market is, and what that does to the options a family in that emirate actually has.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA oversees private education here, with 227 private schools teaching 17 curricula and 387,441 students enrolled in 2024-25, the IB taking 7 per cent of that enrolment. Deepest tutor supply in the country, so the widest spread of quotes: budget online from about AED 45, specialist Higher Level work from AED 200 upwards.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules describes a bar on school staff taking paid tutoring work with students enrolled at their own school, so the cheapest-looking option - your child's own teacher, privately - is often the one to decline.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Families here frequently drive into Dubai for tuition centres; an online slot removes the drive and the fuel from the weekly cost without changing the teaching.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory. Fewer IB campuses than the island, which shows up as longer match times for Higher Level sciences rather than as a higher hourly rate. For some subject combinations here, delivery over video is what makes a specialist available at all.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools fall under the federal Ministry of Education. Many families commute into Sharjah or Dubai for school, which pushes a realistic session start to 17:30 or later on weekdays and makes a 16:00 slot the one that quietly gets cancelled.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. Visiting-tutor quotes here carry real travel cost, which is one reason the published in-home band runs as high as AED 500 an hour.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education territory on the east coast, with the smallest IB cohort in the country. A Higher Level specialist who happens to live nearby is close to a coincidence; a video link makes the question irrelevant rather than answering it.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under the Ministry of Education. The practical constraint here is the evening window after a school run into Sharjah or Dubai, not price. Sessions booked for 19:00 survive a full term better than ones booked for 16:30.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai campuses whose families most often ask about Higher Level supply
schoolClusters.note: Diploma cohorts at these KHDA-inspected campuses are large enough that a Higher Level subject usually runs, but small enough that one subject can rest on one teacher. sections.heading: Nobody ranks IB tutors in this country, so compare prices and evidence instead
paragraphs: An online IB hour in the UAE is advertised between roughly AED 45 and AED 650, reading October 2026 prices off providers' own pages. There is no published ranking of IB tutors in this country, and no regulator issues one. What a parent can compare is price against evidence, and the evidence is narrower than the marketing around it suggests.

Three of the six pages ranking best for these searches publish no price at all. Two quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family transacts in. One asks how much tutoring costs in its own FAQ and then declines to answer the question. That is the market a parent is comparing inside, and it is why a quote usually arrives without a reason attached to it.

So start from what the rate is made of. The level being taught is the biggest single factor: Higher Level costs more because fewer people can teach it, not because the hour is longer. Scarcity at that level is second - Higher Level Chemistry, Physics and Maths Analysis and Approaches are harder to staff than Standard Level humanities. Third is included work: marking, written feedback and a note of what to practise take a tutor time outside the lesson, and a rate that includes them is not comparable with one that does not. Fourth is the slot, because a 17:00 Gulf Standard Time weekday hour is the one every family wants.

What should not move the price: a self-awarded star rating, a claimed position in a ranking nobody publishes, or a familiar logo. One provider in this market publishes an average rating in its page code that differs from the number printed on the page itself. Ask instead what the tutor has taught, at which level, for which board, and how recently they taught it.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges for an online IB hour, sorted by what is being taught
paragraphs: Online one-to-one IB tuition in the UAE is advertised from about AED 45 an hour at the budget end, and at AED 200-450 and above for Higher Level specialist work, with one provider publishing AED 650 for a named premium tutor. Those figures are other companies' published prices, read in October 2026. IB Gram's own position is a free first lesson and then a quote for the specific subject, level and slot.

The useful way to read the table below is by component rather than by provider. A Standard Level humanities hour and a Higher Level Maths Analysis and Approaches hour are not the same product, and the market prices them differently even where a single company advertises one rate for both. Where a provider quotes one number for everything, that number is set by their cheapest tutor's cost and their most expensive tutor's margin.

Monthly packages are the other way this is sold here. An online package of eight sessions has been advertised at AED 799 a month; in-home packages of four two-hour visits at AED 1,599-1,799. Bestimate's 2026 rate work puts a weekly one-hour habit at AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Set that beside a Dubai school fee: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees in the emirate would not rise for 2026-27 under the second economic incentives package, so for one year at least the tutoring line is the part of an education budget that can still move.

Two cautions about reading any of these numbers. First, ask whether VAT sits inside the quoted figure, and ask for a tax registration number if one is claimed; this page takes no position on the VAT treatment of tuition fees, which is a question for the Federal Tax Authority. Second, treat a rate quoted without a session length as incomplete, because AED 300 for ninety minutes and AED 300 for sixty minutes are different prices wearing the same number.

sections.heading: Three claims that carry a premium, and which of them a parent can check
paragraphs: Four claims add money to an IB tutoring quote in this market: examiner status, a famous university on the tutor's degree, experience at your child's own school, and a regulator's name used as though it were an endorsement. Only two of the four can be checked by a parent before paying, and one of them should end the conversation.

Examiner status is the most common premium and the hardest to verify. Awarding bodies do not publish examiner lists, and status changes session by session. Marking experience is genuinely useful, because somebody who has applied a mark scheme at volume reads a question differently - but it carries no access to grade boundaries, unreleased papers or anybody's marks, and a provider implying otherwise is describing something that does not exist. Ask when the person last marked, for which board and which component, then accept that the answer is unverifiable and weigh it accordingly.

A degree from a well-known university is verifiable and weakly predictive. It tells you the person can do the subject; it says nothing about whether they can teach a sixteen-year-old the difference between outline and explain. Experience of your child's specific school is more useful than either, because internal deadlines and coursework calendars differ by campus. If the person is currently employed at that school, though, think carefully: press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules describes Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff being barred from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct in the same spirit.

The fourth claim is the one to walk away from. No individual tutor holds approval from KHDA. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with premises, through an initial-approval process with a six-month completion window and an annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. A page applying a regulator's name to individual tutors is either confused or counting on a parent not knowing the difference. IB Gram holds no regulator or awarding-body accreditation and claims none; what it can show you is which subjects and levels each tutor teaches.

sections.heading: The free trial lesson is the only measurement you get before you pay
paragraphs: A trial lesson is a diagnostic, not a sales call, and it is the one hour where the parent holds all the leverage. Sixty minutes is enough to see whether a tutor can find the actual problem, and the actual problem is usually not the topic the student named when asked.

Send one real artefact before it starts: the last piece of marked work, with the teacher's comments still on it. Not a syllabus, not a report card - a marked paper. A tutor who reads it beforehand and opens by asking about question 6 is doing the job. A tutor who opens by describing their own qualifications is selling, and you can hear the difference from the next room.

What to listen for is who is talking. In a good online hour the student talks for more than half of it, and the shared screen shows the student's working rather than the tutor's notes. The hour should close with two or three specific things to practise, written down, and a sentence about what the next session will do. If the summary is that they revised functions, there is nothing to measure against next week and no way to tell a good tenth hour from a wasted one.

Then check the conditions attached to the word free, before booking rather than after. Trial length, whether a card is required, whether the trial tutor is the tutor who continues, and what happens if you stop there. With IB Gram the first lesson is free, those conditions are stated before you book, and stopping afterwards costs nothing. Note the honest limit of a trial, too: it tests teaching and diagnosis. It cannot tell you whether that person will still have 17:00 on Tuesdays free in March, which is a scheduling question worth asking in the same conversation.

sections.heading: Maths AA or AI: one choice that decides two years of tutoring spend
paragraphs: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are not easy and hard versions of one subject. They are different subjects with different content, and the choice a student makes in the spring of Year 11 sets how many tutoring hours the next two years will absorb and what those hours will be spent on.

Analysis and Approaches is algebra-heavy and proof-facing, and at Higher Level it carries Paper 3, a longer problem-solving paper that rewards students who can work on unfamiliar ground. Applications and Interpretation is modelling, statistics and technology-facing, and the graphic display calculator is central rather than incidental to it. A student who enjoyed IGCSE algebra and found statistics a chore is usually in the wrong course if they pick Applications, and the reverse is just as true and just as expensive.

University prerequisites are the part families discover late. Engineering, physics, mathematics and several economics courses commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, while many business, psychology, design and life-science routes accept either. The published entry requirements of the specific universities on your child's list are the only authority worth using here, and reading them costs nothing. Check them before the choice closes, not after the first DP1 report arrives.

The spending difference is real and measurable. Switching from Applications to Analysis at Higher Level after the first term of DP1 means covering algebraic and calculus content the class has already moved past, which in this market is usually bought as a block of ten to twenty hours on top of weekly lessons. Making the choice correctly costs one conversation with the school's maths coordinator, in Year 11, before the option forms go in.

sections.heading: The move into DP1 is where the bill concentrates
paragraphs: Most of what UAE families spend on Diploma tutoring is spent repairing a transition. A student arrives in DP1 from MYP 5, from IGCSE, from CBSE Class 10 or from an American Grade 10, and the gap between what the previous system assessed and what the Diploma assumes is where the first bad report comes from.

The gaps are predictable enough to plan for. IGCSE Extended maths leaves a student fluent in procedures but light on proof and on functions notation, which Analysis and Approaches assumes from the first week. MYP 5 sciences assess criteria rather than content coverage, so a student can hold a strong MYP grade and still meet Diploma content they have never seen. CBSE Class 10 is content-rich and examination-focused, and the shift is towards extended writing and independent investigation. An American Grade 10 transcript often conceals which maths track the student was actually on, which matters directly for the AA or AI decision.

Dubai's school market makes this more common than it sounds. The emirate recorded 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools and 17 curricula in 2024-25, with the IB at 7 per cent of enrolment, and seven more private schools arrive for 2026-27 - four UK curriculum and three IB - adding 16,846 places after six opened during 2025-26. Families move between curricula inside one city, and a Diploma intake absorbs students from all of them in the same September.

The cheap version of this repair is a summer or first-term block aimed at the specific gap, priced at the market's mid band. The expensive version is a year of weekly lessons that never names the gap and spends every hour on this week's homework instead, which is the single most common way tutoring money disappears in this market.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor against live online, priced for a UAE family
paragraphs: Families who search for a home tutor are asking a sensible question, so here is the honest answer. The UAE market for a tutor in the room is advertised at roughly AED 180-500 an hour, Bestimate putting the band at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200-500. Monthly in-home packages of four two-hour visits have been advertised at AED 1,599-1,799. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address: tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service offered only in India.

The cost difference is not mainly the rate - it is the travel inside the rate. A visiting tutor crossing Dubai at 17:00 is paid for one hour and gives up two, which is why minimum session lengths of two hours are common here and why evening slots are scarce. For a family in Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain the travel line is larger again, and the number of IB Higher Level specialists willing to make that trip twice a week is close to none.

The argument for a screen is supply rather than saving. A family in Al Reem or Al Zahia choosing online is choosing from the people who teach their child's syllabus at their child's level, rather than from the people who live within a twenty-minute drive of the villa. Higher Level Chemistry, Physics and Analysis and Approaches are exactly where that distinction stops being theoretical and starts deciding whether a specialist exists for you at all.

What is lost is real and worth naming. A tutor in the room can read a page over a shoulder and can read a teenager's body language better. Shared-screen working closes most of the first gap, because the student's working appears line by line rather than arriving as a finished answer. The second gap is a reason to hold the same tutor and the same slot for the term rather than rotating between people.

sections.heading: The one thing more money must never buy
paragraphs: The clearest line in this market is also the cheapest to cross by accident. Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay, the TOK essay and the Personal Project are assessed as the student's own work. A tutor may teach, question, model with different examples, read a draft and give feedback against the published criteria. A tutor may not supply the text, the data or the analysis, at any rate, in any format, however the help is described on an invoice.

This is not a cautious reading of the rules. One provider ranking for these searches advertises finished Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. A student who submits that work faces an academic-misconduct process and a diploma can be withheld. The money is not the real risk in that transaction; the two years are.

In practice the boundary is easy to hold if the artefacts stay in the student's hands. The student's file, the student's data, the student's words, in every session. Feedback is phrased as questions and criteria references rather than as replacement sentences. Supervisors ask students to account for the help they received, and a session note a coordinator could read without concern is the simple test of whether the help was the right kind.

Published limits are part of the same discipline, because a tutor who knows them stops a student wasting weeks. The Extended Essay carries a 4,000-word limit. The TOK essay carries a 1,600-word limit and is marked out of 10 against published criteria. The Maths exploration is marked against criteria A to E out of 20. The science investigation is marked out of 24. Confirm each against the current subject guide with your child's coordinator; guides change, and a tutor quoting the previous cycle's structure is a reason to ask when they last taught the course.

sections.heading: Who the UAE permits to teach privately, and why the cheapest quote is sometimes the unpermitted one
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page - Issuance of a New Work Permit, Private Tutor Licensing - lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Because the permit costs nothing, a tutor without one is not saving you money; they are saving themselves two days of paperwork. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount appears here, and a page that quotes one has invented it. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students - which is why a confident quote from a nineteen-year-old undergraduate can be entirely lawful and sometimes good value.

A permit for an individual and a licence for a business are separate objects, and conflating them is the most common misrepresentation in this market. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute: initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and states no UAE premises, because it operates over live video rather than from a building.

There is one offer worth declining on principle. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules describes Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff as barred from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct runs the same way. The arrangement that looks cheapest and most convenient - your child's own subject teacher, paid privately - is the one that can put a teacher's position and a family's school relationship at risk. Verify the current rules against ADEK's own policy document before relying on any press summary, this one included.

sections.heading: Two UAE costs that never appear on a tutoring quote
paragraphs: Two obligations sit outside the IB and outside every tutoring price list, and both cost UAE families time, and sometimes money, late in the programme. The first is the mandatory ministry subjects. The second is Ministry of Education equivalency.

Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies; combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with KHDA advising that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education need the appropriate KHDA approval to teach them. Support here has a hard boundary: using different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is prohibited, so a tutor works with the school's own material or not at all.

Equivalency is the paperwork that turns a school-leaving certificate into something a UAE university or employer recognises. On the British track the Ministry requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited A-Level at no less than E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes six subjects; the sourced number is five. On the American track, English proficiency is shown by a 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with at least 450 in SAT Math.

For the IB Diploma this page publishes no points threshold, because none has been read on the Ministry's own site. Anyone quoting one should be asked where it came from. Open the file in the final year rather than after results, check the requirements on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate, and treat tutoring as unrelated to the process: no amount of tuition is required for equivalency, and no provider performs it on your behalf.

That is enough to say whether a specialist is free. It is also enough to give you a rate for your case rather than a range off a price page.

process.title: Send one piece of marked work
process.description: The last marked paper or assignment, with the teacher's comments still on it. This is the single most useful thing a parent can send, and it does more than a report card: it shows where marks actually went, which is what a first session should be built on rather than a general chat about confidence.

process.description: The trial is one hour with the tutor who would continue. Use the table above: who talks, what is on the shared screen, and whether the hour ends with specific things to practise. Stopping afterwards costs nothing, and no card is needed to book it in the first place.

process.description: Weekly slot, a costed block, or coursework coaching. Agree the hours, the goal and the slot in writing, and agree what will be reviewed after four sessions. Four sessions is a fair point at which to judge a match; one is not, and twelve is an expensive way to find out.

process.description: Where no specialist covers the subject, level and slot, we say so and give an honest wait rather than matching a generalist at a specialist rate. A waiting list with a date on it beats a mismatch you end up paying for twice, once in fees and once in redone work.

The market range for an online hour runs AED 45 to AED 650 and pretending otherwise helps nobody. Our own number comes after the free lesson, for your subject, level and slot.

whyPoints.description: Matching is by subject and level, not by postcode. A Higher Level Physics request produces a Higher Level Physics teacher or an honest wait, because an hour with somebody teaching outside their level is the most expensive hour available in this market.

whyPoints.description: Feedback on the student's own drafts against the published criteria, with session notes that would survive being shown to the school. The alternative is openly sold in this market, and it risks a diploma rather than only a fee.

It claims no accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, holds no UAE premises, and names schools only as context. What we will show you is what each tutor teaches, and at which level.

whyPoints.description: Slots are set on Gulf Standard Time around the school run and the commute, with sessions moving to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan and pausing rather than cancelling across exam weeks and the heaviest coursework fortnights.

whyPoints.title: Something written after every session
whyPoints.description: Each lesson ends with two or three specific things to practise, written down. It is how a parent paying AED 200 or more an hour can tell whether the hour worked, without sitting in the room or taking anybody's word for it.

faqs.question: Is an AED 400 online hour better value than an AED 200 one for the same subject?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, and the question is answerable. At AED 200 you are usually buying teaching time only. At AED 400 you should be buying a scarcer level - Higher Level maths or sciences - plus marking and written feedback between lessons. Ask what the higher rate includes that the lower one does not, in writing. If the answer is seniority or a claimed ranking, the premium is for marketing. If it is Paper 3 work, marked past papers from your child's own board and a note of what to practise, the difference is a product difference. Market bands for specialist Higher Level work in the UAE run AED 200-450 and above, so both quotes can be legitimate.

faqs.question: How do I compare three tutoring quotes that all sound equally confident?
faqs.answer: Put them in the same units first. Ask each for the rate per 60 minutes, whether marking and feedback sit inside it, whether VAT is included, the minimum commitment, and who actually teaches - the person quoting, or somebody assigned later. Then ask all three the same subject question: which component of this subject do students at my child's school find hardest, and why. A specialist answers with papers and criteria; a salesperson answers with adjectives. Finally ask what happens if the match fails after two lessons. The provider whose answers are specific and whose conditions are written down is the one to trial, whatever the rate.

faqs.question: Does examiner experience justify the premium some UAE providers charge for it?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth less than it is sold for. Marking experience changes how somebody reads a question and a mark scheme, which genuinely helps a student. It carries no access to grade boundaries, unreleased papers or your child's marks, and anyone implying that it does is describing something that does not exist. Awarding bodies do not publish examiner lists, so the claim cannot be verified by a parent at all. Ask which board, which component and which session, then weigh the answer against what you can check: subjects taught, levels taught, and how recently. One provider here publishes AED 650 an hour for a named premium tutor.

faqs.question: Can a provider say the regulator has approved its individual tutors?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises - initial approval, a maximum of six months to finish the permit and licence steps, and renewal at least thirty days before expiry. It is not a credential for an individual tutor, and the regulator does not vet tutors one by one. A page using a regulator's name that way is either confused or relying on a parent not checking. What an individual tutor should hold is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free and valid for two years. IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation and does not claim any.

faqs.question: Is a university student at the bottom of the rate range reasonable for Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. University students are expressly eligible for the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and for Standard Level consolidation, homework habits or MYP work a capable undergraduate at the AED 45-150 end of the published market range can be good value. Where it stops working is Higher Level, coursework and anything close to an exam. Somebody who sat the Diploma three years ago knows the content but not the mark scheme, and Higher Level Chemistry or Analysis and Approaches Paper 3 is where that shows. A reasonable split many families use: cheaper support for breadth, specialist hours for the subjects that decide the points total.

faqs.question: What should a free trial lesson tell me that a brochure cannot?
faqs.answer: Whether the tutor can find the real problem. Send the last marked piece of work beforehand, then listen for three things: whether they refer to it, who does most of the talking, and what is on the shared screen. The student's own working should be, not a slide deck. The hour should close with two or three specific things to practise and a sentence about the next session. Ask the conditions before booking - length, whether a card is needed, whether the trial tutor continues. With IB Gram the first lesson is free, those conditions are stated up front, and stopping afterwards costs nothing.

faqs.question: Why is coursework support priced as a block rather than by the hour?
faqs.answer: Because the work is not evenly spread. An internal assessment or an Extended Essay needs an intense start - scoping the question, reading the criteria, checking the method is viable - then quiet weeks while the student writes, then a feedback session on a draft. Billing that by the hour encourages meetings for their own sake. A block with a stated number of sessions set against the school's own deadlines costs less and fits the actual shape of the task. What the block must never include is text, data or analysis supplied by the tutor; the words and the results have to be the student's own.

faqs.question: What does an AED 799 monthly online package usually include in this market?
faqs.answer: That figure is a package advertised locally at eight sessions a month, which works out near AED 100 per session - budget-tier pricing. Read what sits inside it before comparing it with an hourly rate: session length, whether marking is included, whether the same tutor teaches every session, and what happens to unused sessions at month end. In-home monthly packages in the UAE have been advertised at AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour visits, with travel inside the price. Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour habit run AED 240-600 a month at the budget end and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

faqs.question: Should my child take Maths AA or AI if the plan is engineering abroad?
faqs.answer: Check the published entry requirements of the specific universities on the list, because that is the only authority that matters here. Engineering, physics and mathematics courses commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level, while business, psychology, design and several life-science routes accept either. Make the choice before the course starts: switching from Applications to Analysis at Higher Level after the first term of DP1 means covering algebra and calculus the class has already passed, which families here usually buy as ten to twenty extra hours. One conversation with the school's maths coordinator in Year 11 is the cheap version of this decision.

faqs.question: How many hours does the jump from IGCSE maths into Analysis and Approaches usually take?
faqs.answer: Families in this market typically buy a summer or first-term block of eight to fifteen hours, and the content is predictable: functions notation, algebraic fluency at speed, and the proof habits IGCSE Extended never required. The point of doing it early is price per mark. The same gap addressed in DP2, under deadline pressure and alongside the exploration, absorbs far more hours and returns less, because sessions turn into triage on past papers. If a first DP1 report shows an unexpected drop in maths, treat it as this gap until a diagnostic session says otherwise.

faqs.question: At what point should we stop paying a tutor who is not working out?
faqs.answer: Four sessions is a fair test; one is not. By the fourth there should be a named problem, evidence it is narrowing, and something written at the end of each session that the student can practise alone. If the sessions still consist of this week's homework being finished with help, the arrangement is a homework club at a specialist rate. Say so, and ask for a different tutor rather than a different approach - a mismatch of level or teaching style rarely resolves with more hours. Agreeing a four-session review before the second lesson makes that conversation ordinary instead of awkward.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education lessons add to what we already spend on IB tuition?
faqs.answer: They can, and families rarely budget for them. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. If a mark in one of them is weak, support has a hard limit: schools may not use different or additional content without prior Ministry permission, so a tutor works with the school's own material rather than a parallel course. Ask the school for that material first - it costs nothing, and it decides whether paid hours would help at all.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Ministry of Education equivalency file?
faqs.answer: Only by explaining it. Equivalency is the Ministry's process, and no provider performs it, speeds it up or guarantees an outcome. What is sourced: the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that five, plus one A-Level at no less than E or two AS-Levels. The American track asks for IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in SAT reading and writing, and at least 450 in SAT Math. For the IB Diploma no points figure appears here, because none has been read on the Ministry's own site. Check moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation authority.

faqs.question: Why is this delivered over live video rather than at a UAE address?
faqs.answer: Because of who is available, not what it costs. Tuition for UAE families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service offered only in India. Dubai recorded 227 private schools and 387,441 private-school students in 2024-25, with the IB at 7 per cent of enrolment, so a Higher Level Chemistry or Analysis and Approaches specialist is a narrow pool inside that. Matching by syllabus and level rather than by driving distance is what makes the right teacher reachable from Al Ain, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain. Shared-screen working also keeps the student's line-by-line working visible, which is where diagnosis happens.

faqs.question: Can we be put on a waiting list rather than matched with a generalist?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for Higher Level subjects that is often the better answer. Where no specialist covers the subject, level and slot, we say so and give a date rather than filling the gap with somebody teaching outside their level. An hour with the wrong tutor is the most expensive hour in this market: it is paid for once, then paid for again when the work has to be redone. Where a wait is unworkable - six weeks to the first paper, for instance - we will say what is available and what it cannot cover, so the decision stays yours with the limitation stated plainly.

faqs.question: Does the hourly rate change as the May session gets closer?
faqs.answer: Availability changes more than the rate does. The scarce thing in February and March is a Higher Level specialist with an evening slot free, not a willingness to quote. Bestimate's 2026 figures put specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month, and that is the band families reach when they start late and buy intensively. Booking the same total hours from September costs the same per hour and returns more per hour, because sessions can build understanding rather than triage past papers. If you are starting late, say so plainly: the plan for six weeks out is a different plan, not a compressed version of the same one.

best-ib-online-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the free lesson, then decide what the hour is worth
best-ib-online-tutor.closingBody: The honest version of this page is short. There is no published ranking of IB tutors in the UAE, the market advertises an online hour anywhere between AED 45 and AED 650, and the only measurement a parent gets before paying is a trial lesson. So use it. Send the last marked piece of work, name the subject and level, pick two evening windows on Gulf Standard Time, and watch one hour for who talks, what is on the screen, and whether the lesson ends with something specific to practise. Lessons are one-to-one over live video. The first one is free, its conditions are stated before you book, and if no specialist is free for your child's subject we will tell you that instead of selling you a substitute.

intro.heading: There is no official ranking, so here is what can actually be checked
paragraphs: Nobody publishes a league table of IB tuition in the Emirates. KHDA inspects schools in Dubai, the Department of Education and Knowledge licenses them in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates them in Sharjah, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Not one of those bodies rates a tutor, a tuition company or an hour of teaching. A provider calling itself the strongest option in the market is describing an opinion, and there is no register anywhere that would confirm or contradict it.

What the system does publish is a great deal, and almost none of it appears on the pages currently ranking for this search. Your child's school has an inspection report under the authority that licensed it. The IB publishes an assessment criterion list for every subject, with letters and a mark allocation beside each one. It publishes a word or page limit for every written component. Cambridge and Pearson publish entry deadlines months before the papers. The Ministry of Education publishes what a certificate must show before a UAE university will accept it. Those are the documents a judgement can rest on.

So this page treats the word best as a question about fit rather than rank. The fit question has three parts. Does the tutor know the criteria your child's work is marked against, by letter and by mark? Does the plan respect the deadlines the school and the board have already set? And is the arrangement lawful here, which in the Emirates means a private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 for an individual, and a separate permit entirely for a business with premises and staff.

The market itself makes this harder than it should be. Dubai had 227 private schools and 387,441 private-school pupils in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, and the International Baccalaureate accounted for 7% of that roll against 37% on UK curricula. Most tutors in this market trained on GCSE and A-Level. Seven more private schools open in Dubai for 2026-27, three of them International Baccalaureate, adding 16,846 places. Demand for Higher Level teaching is growing faster than the pool of people who have taught it.

IB Gram delivers tuition for UAE families as one-to-one online teaching over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service we run in India only, and nothing on this page should be read as an offer to attend a UAE address. The trade is deliberate: instead of whoever lives within a tolerable drive of your community, a family in Al Barsha or Khalifa City or Al Nuaimiya is matched to the person who has taught that subject at that level. The first lesson carries no charge, no card details are taken, and nothing obliges you to continue.
