sections.heading: The diagnostic you have already paid for
paragraphs: Most UAE families buy their first tutoring hours on a feeling, and the feeling is usually accurate about the subject and wrong about the cause. Before any money moves there are five pieces of evidence already sitting in the household or in the school office, all of them produced at no additional cost, and together they say whether paid hours are the right purchase and which code to spend them on. Reading them is the highest-return half hour in this entire process.

The Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint report is the earliest of them. Cambridge offers Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and the report is externally marked, which makes it the only objective read a family gets two years before an IGCSE entry. It says nothing about Extended-tier content, so it cannot justify a two-year weekly block. It can absolutely justify six targeted hours on a named strand, which is the difference between spending AED 1,500 in Year 8 and AED 9,000 in Year 11.

The two documents that matter most, though, are the marked mock script and the statement of entry. The script tells you which question types bleed marks, which is the only diagnosis worth paying for; a tutor who starts from a marked script rather than from a topic list earns the first hour back immediately. The statement of entry tells you the code, the tier and the components, so the specialist you hire matches the paper the candidate will actually sit. Add the forecast grade, which for the Cambridge March 2027 series is due from the school on 27 February 2027, and you have a written statement of what the subject teacher expects.

The pattern to avoid is the one this market rewards: booking a weekly hour in six subjects because results felt disappointing. That is the most expensive possible response and the least likely to work, because it spreads attention across codes with completely different failure modes. Triage against the evidence, fund one or two codes properly, and revisit at six hours. If the evidence does not point anywhere, the honest answer is that tutoring is not yet the right spend, and we will say that.

sections.heading: Command terms are where Cambridge marks quietly leave the room
paragraphs: A large share of the marks a UAE Cambridge candidate loses are not lost to ignorance. They are lost to answering a different question from the one printed. State, describe, explain, calculate, suggest and evaluate each have a defined expectation in the mark scheme, and each has a characteristic failure: a described answer where an explanation was wanted collects a fraction of the available marks even when every fact in it is correct. This is the most coachable thing in the entire qualification, and it is the reason a specialist hour can move a grade band faster than a term of content revision.

The pattern repeats across codes with its own local flavour. In Chemistry 0620 the six-mark extended response is answered as a list of true statements rather than a linked chain of cause and effect. In Biology 0610 a process is named where a mechanism in sequence was required. In Physics 0625 the formula is recalled correctly and the unit is dropped, or the rounding happens two lines before the final answer. In Mathematics 0580 the method mark is thrown away because a step done mentally was never written down. In English 0500 the directed-writing task names an audience and a form, and the composition ignores both.

Diagnosing this needs a marked script, not a topic list, which is why the mock paper is worth more to a tutor than anything a parent can describe over the phone. The work itself is unglamorous: rewrite the same six-mark answer four times against the published command-term expectation until the structure is automatic. It does not feel like tutoring and it is where most of the recoverable marks in a Cambridge IGCSE year actually live.

One caution on materials. Cambridge syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge, and no tutor should be supplying them to you as downloads. A tutor references them, cites the official page and works from what the school has legitimately provided to the candidate. If a provider's selling point is a library of papers and mark schemes to hand over, that is a copyright problem rather than a feature, and it tells you something about the rest of the operation.

sections.heading: Five subjects, not six: dropping a Cambridge entry to save money
paragraphs: Families triaging a nine-subject Year 11 budget reach the same question eventually: can we drop one. Academically that is a school conversation. Financially and administratively there is a harder constraint, and it is the Ministry of Education equivalency file that a UAE-based candidate will eventually need. Getting this wrong is cheap to do and expensive to discover, because it is usually discovered at an admissions desk.

As reported from the Ministry's July 2026 clarification, the British-track route asks the candidate to pass five subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. The point that catches UAE families is the exclusion: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. A page currently ranking for this query states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The Ministry's clarification, as reported, says five, and the exclusion is what makes the counting feel like six.

The practical rule that follows is simple. Secure five accepted subjects at the reported minimum first, then triage. A humanity is usually the safest thing to drop once the five are safe; a science or maths almost never is, because every later route asks for them and replacing one costs far more than the tutoring you avoided. Equivalency is a Ministry process, not something IB Gram performs, guarantees or expedites, and nothing on this page should be read as implying tutoring is required for it. Verify the current requirements on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate before acting on any figure, including the ones here.

The budget version of this is worth stating plainly. Funding tutoring across nine subjects is the most expensive plan available and the least effective. Funding it across the two codes that are both at risk and structurally necessary, while confirming that five accepted subjects are secure, is the plan that costs least and protects most. That is an arithmetic decision made against the entry form, not a judgement about anybody's ability.

sections.heading: What a missed Cambridge date costs, counted in series rather than in hours
paragraphs: Cambridge runs its IGCSE assessment in series, and a series is a door that closes. That single fact governs the cost of every scheduling decision a UAE family makes, because a slip does not usually produce a late fee. It produces a wait, and a wait means another entry, another revision block and another set of funded hours. Cambridge's exam timetable page sets out a June series and a November series, and the board also publishes key dates for a March series, which is the clearest worked example of how far ahead the real deadlines sit.

Take the March 2027 series as that example. The exam period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, but final entries are due on 27 November 2026, more than two months before the first paper. Forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027. Results reach centres on Cambridge Direct on 13 May 2027, and certificates follow in late June. A family deciding in January to fund serious support is deciding after the entry has already been locked and shortly before the forecast grade goes in.

There is one further trap that costs more than any of the others and is almost never mentioned. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone's timetable was used. A revision plan built on the wrong zone's dates is a plan that can lose a paper outright. Ask the school's exams officer which zone the centre sits in and work from that timetable only.

The planning consequence for a budget is the one worth keeping. Hours bought twelve weeks out are bought at the middle of the market band and spread across a sensible week. Hours bought three weeks out are bought at the top of the band, in doubled sessions, from whoever happens to be free, and they are competing with the school's own revision timetable for the same tired evenings. The date is what makes the hour expensive, not the tutor.

sections.heading: Results, remarks and a November resit: the arithmetic after the papers
paragraphs: Results day is where the most expensive decisions of the whole process get made, usually in a hurry and often while the family is out of the country. Pearson's published pattern gives a sense of the clock: June 2026 International GCSE results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge's March 2027 results reach centres on Direct on 13 May 2027, with certificates in late June. Whichever board your child sits, two windows open on results day and both shut quickly.

The first is the enquiry about results, the review or remark route, which runs through the school rather than through the parent and carries a deadline set by the board. It is worth considering when a grade sits one mark-band below everything else the candidate has produced all year, and it is worth nothing when it is being used as a substitute for accepting a result. The school's exams officer is the only person who can submit it, which makes the first call on results day a call to the school, not to a tutor.

The second is the resit decision, and here the arithmetic is uncomfortable but clear. A resit means a fresh entry in a later series, a revision block running alongside the first term of the next course, and an opportunity cost measured in attention rather than money: the Year 12 content being taught while the Year 11 paper is being re-prepared. Priced honestly, a resit almost always costs more in total than the tutoring that would have prevented it would have cost in February. That is not an argument for panic buying; it is an argument for buying earlier and smaller.

The third thing to do on results day is administrative and nobody enjoys it. Open the equivalency file. Check that five accepted subjects at the reported minimum grade are present, remembering that Arabic and Islamic education sit outside that count, and confirm the current requirement on moe.gov.ae rather than on any landing page, including this one. Certificates arrive weeks after results, and an admissions deadline that needs a certificate does not care which week it is.

sections.heading: What no fee buys: the honesty line around Cambridge coursework and practicals
paragraphs: Some things in this market are for sale and should not be. At least one provider ranking in this search sells completed Internal Assessments outright. The same logic is applied to IGCSE coursework components, and it is the single fastest way to end a candidate's entry. A tutor teaches, explains, models an approach, asks the questions a marker would ask, and gives feedback on work the candidate produced. A tutor does not write coursework, does not redraft it to completion, and does not supply text to be submitted under somebody else's name.

That boundary holds across the Cambridge components where it matters most. In English 0500 a tutor can teach the directed-writing form and mark a practice piece against the band descriptors; the composition submitted is the candidate's. In Business 0450 and History 0470 a tutor can interrogate an argument and point out an unsupported claim; the writing stays with the student. In the sciences, practical skills assessed through the practical test or the alternative to practical paper are prepared through technique, data handling and past question practice, while the apparatus and the invigilated conditions remain the school's responsibility.

The materials boundary runs alongside it. Cambridge syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are Cambridge's property. A tutor cites them and links to the official page; a tutor does not distribute them as a download library, and a provider advertising one is advertising a copyright problem. The same applies to anything described as leaked, advance or inside information about a paper, which no legitimate tutor has and no parent should want.

None of this is a disclaimer bolted to the end of a sales page. It is the practical reason the honest version of this service is worth paying for. No tutor can promise a particular grade, and anybody selling one is selling something else. What a specialist hour can do is make the difference between a candidate who knows the content and a candidate who can convert it into marks under a named command term, inside a timed paper, in the zone their centre actually sits in. That is the product, and it is the only one we sell.

process.title: Send the entry form and one marked paper
process.description: Two documents start this properly: the statement of entry, which carries the Cambridge code, the tier and the components, and the most recent marked script with its mark scheme. Together they replace a guess with a diagnosis. A family who sends these gets an accurate answer about availability and cost; a family who describes the problem gets an average.

process.title: A trial lesson at no charge
process.description: Thirty minutes, one-to-one over live video, with no card details taken and no obligation to book a block. The purpose is diagnostic rather than promotional: the tutor works through a question the candidate got wrong and names the habit behind it. If the match is wrong, say so and we will change the tutor or tell you honestly that the specialist you need is not free.

process.title: A written target, then a counted block
process.description: Before money moves, the target gets written down: the code, the question types, and what the tier allows. The block is then counted backwards from the series rather than forwards from today, and quoted as a total so you know the figure before the first session. Sessions sit in Gulf Standard Time around the school day, with Ramadan and holiday weeks handled separately.

process.title: Review at six hours against what was written
process.description: Six paid hours in, there should be something to read: session notes, annotated questions, and a marked piece of the candidate's own work showing the habit changing. If there is not, the honest conclusion is that the plan or the match is wrong, and the review exists to say so rather than to renew automatically. Blocks can be paused during school exam weeks.

process.title: Hand back to the school calendar
process.description: The last stage is deliberately a stop. Once the forecast grade is in and the paper is close, the school's own revision timetable should own the candidate's evenings, and extra paid hours start competing with sleep. We will tell you when we think that point has arrived, which is the part of this that costs us money and is still the right advice.

whyPoints.title: The price is on the page
whyPoints.description: Market bands in AED, each attributed to the provider or rate table that published it and dated October 2026, sit in the open on this page rather than behind an enquiry form. Three of the strongest competitor pages in this search publish no figure at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. A family should be able to sanity-check a quote before they make a call.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the code, not to the subject
whyPoints.description: We match on the Cambridge syllabus code from the statement of entry, because 0580 and 0607 are different syllabuses and a general maths tutor is poor value for the second. If no specialist for your code is free at the hour you want, we say that rather than substituting somebody who will teach the paper they know instead of the paper your child sits.

whyPoints.title: Online because of the pool, not to cut corners
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are part of our India service only. The reason is supply: a Computer Science 0478 or Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 specialist is a small population in the Emirates, and smaller still if they must also live near one community. Removing the journey widens the pool and removes travel from the rate.

whyPoints.title: Sourced numbers, with the gaps admitted
whyPoints.description: Every regulatory and calendar fact on this page is attributed: u.ae for the regulator map and the permit, KHDA for the fee position and the mandatory subjects, Cambridge for the series dates, Pearson for the results pattern. Where a figure could not be verified, it is absent rather than estimated, and that includes IB session dates, which we do not publish.

whyPoints.title: An independent platform, with no claimed approvals
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. We hold no accreditation, licence, partnership or endorsement from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, we claim none, and we occupy no office in the UAE. Named schools appear here as school-system context only. Anyone claiming regulator approval for private tutoring is worth a second question.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line, stated before you pay
whyPoints.description: A tutor here teaches, reviews and gives feedback on the candidate's own work. Coursework is not written, redrafted to completion or supplied. No grade is promised, no outcome is guaranteed, and past papers and mark schemes are referenced and linked rather than distributed. That boundary is why the service is worth paying for rather than a footnote on the way out.

faqs.question: What does a Cambridge IGCSE home tutor cost per hour in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Market rates run roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180 to 500 for a visiting one-to-one arrangement, and AED 200 to 450 and above for a named syllabus specialist. Budget options advertise lower: EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table shows in-home at AED 180 to 350. Those are market figures as published by each source and read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices. What moves your own number is the syllabus code, the tier and how many weeks are left.

faqs.question: Why does a Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 tutor cost more than an English 0500 tutor?
faqs.answer: Supply, not difficulty. English as a First Language 0500 has the deepest teaching pool in the Emirates, so real options exist around AED 150 and providers compete on price. Physics 0625 above grade 6 needs somebody who has taught the Extended theory and, ideally, marked the practical-route paper, and that is a far smaller group across the UAE. The same logic puts Computer Science 0478 and Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 at the top of the band, because pseudocode marking and three-discipline teaching are specialist skills rather than general ones. Scarcity sets the rate before anybody looks at your child's work, which is also why identifying the code first saves money.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Cambridge IGCSE tutor to our address in the UAE?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE lesson runs one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school day. Home visits are part of our India service only, and no tutor is dispatched to a UAE address. The reason is the pool rather than the cost: a specialist for a scarce Cambridge code is unlikely to live within a short drive of any one community, so insisting on proximity means accepting a generalist. Removing the journey means the only constraint is the syllabus code. The limits are stated honestly too: laboratory work, apparatus handling and invigilated conditions stay with the school.

faqs.question: Is a monthly package better value than paying by the hour?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the month contains. Advertised UAE packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, and Bestimate estimates AED 600 to 1,200 monthly at the mid band for a weekly hour. Before signing, ask two questions. What happens to unused sessions, and does the month include school-holiday weeks. A UAE month holding Eid, a half-term and a travel week is not a month of teaching, and a package priced on calendar weeks rather than taught sessions quietly transfers that loss to you.

faqs.question: How many Cambridge IGCSE subjects should we actually fund tutoring for?
faqs.answer: One or two, almost always. Funding a weekly hour across six or nine subjects is the most expensive plan available and the least likely to work, because the codes have completely different failure modes and the candidate's attention is finite. Triage against evidence you already hold: the marked mock script, the end-of-Year-10 paper and the forecast grade. Fund the codes that are both at risk and structurally necessary, usually maths and one science, and confirm that five subjects the Ministry accepts are secure. Then review at six hours. A humanity is usually the safest thing to leave unfunded once the five are safe.

faqs.question: Should we pay for tutoring in Year 10 or wait until Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is cheaper for the same result, and that is arithmetic rather than sales talk. The same number of hours spread over two years is bought at the middle of the market band instead of the top, leaves room to change tutor if the first match is wrong, and attacks method habits rather than just drilling past papers. By January of Year 11 the entry is locked, the forecast grade is weeks away, and a family is buying doubled sessions from whoever is free. The date is what makes an hour expensive. The tutor is usually the same person either way.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 worth paying a specialist for?
faqs.answer: Yes, because 0607 is a different syllabus rather than a variant of 0580. A graphic display calculator is expected throughout and the assessment leans on investigation, modelling and written justification alongside manipulation. A competent 0580 tutor who has never taught 0607 will teach what they know, the candidate will practise the wrong paper style, and the original gap will still be there in February. That is not dishonesty, it is mismatch, and it is the most common waste we see in UAE maths tutoring. Send the statement of entry so the code is known before anybody is booked.

faqs.question: What does the MoHRE private tuition permit tell me about the rate I am quoted?
faqs.answer: That no part of the premium is licensing. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. So the permit is a legal baseline rather than a quality mark. It certifies permission to charge, not the ability to teach Extended-tier Cambridge content.

faqs.question: How do I find out which Cambridge syllabus code my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: From the statement of entry the school issues ahead of the series, not from the school prospectus and not from the subject list in a parent portal. The statement carries the code, the tier and the components, which is exactly the information that decides who should teach the hour. If it has not arrived yet, the exams officer can tell you, and the same conversation is the moment to ask which of Cambridge's six administrative zones the centre sits in, because that decides which version of the timetable your revision plan should be built on.

faqs.question: Is a small group class cheaper than one-to-one for Cambridge IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, usually a third to a half of the one-to-one rate per student. Whether it is better value depends on one thing: does the group share your child's code and tier. A group mixing Core and Extended candidates, or mixing 0580 with 0607, teaches to the middle and the marginal candidate learns least. Groups work well for content coverage and badly for the thing most UAE candidates actually need, which is line-by-line work on their own marked script. If the diagnosis is command-term technique, a group will not reach it.

faqs.question: Does a cheaper tutor end up costing more by the time the papers arrive?
faqs.answer: Often, and the mechanism is specific rather than vague. An advertised rate well below the qualified band has usually had something removed: preparation time, marking turnaround on practice papers, a written record of each session, or a replacement if the tutor stops answering in April. Those are real costs and somebody absorbs them. Twelve hours at AED 120 re-teaching content a candidate already knew is dearer than two at AED 400 that identify the actual habit, because the marks the hours were bought to recover are still missing in June. Judge the hour by what it leaves behind.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Cambridge alternative to practical paper over video?
faqs.answer: Yes for the paper, no for the laboratory. The alternative to practical paper assesses understanding of experimental method, data handling, graph work, sources of error and improvements to a procedure, and all of that is taught well over live video with a shared screen and past questions. What a screen cannot do is run a titration, handle apparatus or provide invigilated conditions, and where a candidate is on the practical-test route the school's laboratory remains the only place that work happens. Tell us which route the entry carries and we will say plainly what the sessions can address.

faqs.question: What happens to the money we have spent if the Cambridge entry deadline is missed?
faqs.answer: The hours are not wasted, but the timetable is. A missed entry does not usually produce a late fee; it produces a wait for a later series, which means another entry and in practice another funded revision block alongside the next course's first term. For the March 2027 series Cambridge published final entries as due on 27 November 2026, with the exam period from 3 February to 4 March 2027, so the real deadline sits months before the paper. The exams officer holds that date, not the family, which is why it is worth asking about in September.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to resit in a later series than to add tutoring now?
faqs.answer: Priced honestly, almost never. A resit means a fresh entry, a revision block running against the first term of the next course, and an opportunity cost measured in attention rather than dirhams: Year 12 content taught while a Year 11 paper is re-prepared. Compared with a counted block bought twelve weeks before the original paper at the middle of the market band, the resit route is more expensive in total and more disruptive. That is an argument for buying earlier and smaller rather than for panic buying, and no tutor can promise a particular outcome in either direction.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards the five subjects the Ministry asks for?
faqs.answer: No. As reported from the Ministry's July 2026 clarification, the British track asks for five subjects passed in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. They remain mandatory in school under KHDA rules regardless of the licensed curriculum. One page ranking for this query states six IGCSE subjects; the exclusion is what makes five feel like six. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae before acting on it.

faqs.question: What should one paid hour of Cambridge IGCSE tuition actually produce?
faqs.answer: Something you can read afterwards. Shared-screen notes, at least one annotated exam question showing the method the marker wanted, and a single written next step for the week. Six paid hours in there should also be a marked piece of the candidate's own work showing a named habit changing: units retained, method lines written down, a six-mark answer built as a chain rather than a list. If none of that exists after six hours, the plan or the match is wrong and the review conversation should say so rather than renewing the block automatically.

cambridge-igcse-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the code on the entry form, not with a quote
cambridge-igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: The cheapest useful thing you can do today costs nothing: find the statement of entry, write down the Cambridge syllabus codes and the tier, and dig out the last marked script with its mark scheme. Send those two things and you will get a straight answer about which specialist fits, what the market band for that code looks like, and whether anybody is free at the hour you want. The trial lesson is thirty minutes, one-to-one over live video, with no card details taken. If the honest answer is that tutoring is not yet the right spend, we would rather say that than sell you a block.

intro.heading: The Cambridge year is already timetabled, so start from the dates
paragraphs: A parent searching for a Cambridge IGCSE tutor in the UAE almost always has a trigger: a mock script that came back two grades down, a report that says working below expectation, or a statement of entry covered in numbers nobody at home recognises. The first useful thing to know is that the year is already timetabled. Cambridge publishes the series, the school submits the entries, the centre is allocated a timetable zone, and a subject teacher will write a forecast grade on a date the school has already chosen. Tuition works inside that frame or it works badly.

So this page is organised by date rather than by promise. It walks a Cambridge series backwards, from the first paper to the week the entries closed, and it names what can still be changed at each point along the way. It uses the board's published key dates for the March 2027 series as the worked example, because those dates are documented and because the fourteen-week gap between the final entry deadline and the first paper is the fact most families in this market discover far too late to use.

The second thing this page does is translate. Syllabus codes such as 0580 and 0625 are not labels; they describe which questions appear and in what form. Component numbers tell you which papers are sat and therefore which technique matters. Core and Extended are different papers with different grade ranges, not two speeds of one course. A parent who can read those three things can judge for themselves whether a tutor knows the course, which is a better filter than any marketing page, this one included.

Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, to families anywhere in the Emirates. IB Gram does not operate a visiting-tutor service in the UAE; that is offered only in India. The reason to prefer the online format here is not cost. It is that a Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 Extended entry needs someone who teaches the supplement content and the alternative to practical paper, and in Al Ain, Ajman or Fujairah that person is unlikely to live twenty minutes from your door.

What follows is specific on purpose. There are AED figures taken from published market sources with the month they were read, a command-word table that explains why a student who knows the content still lands on a grade 5, the KHDA rules covering the three mandatory UAE subjects, the permit a private tutor must hold, and a plain account of what a tutor may and may not touch on an assessed piece. Where a figure could not be sourced from a document anyone can open and check for themselves, it is simply not on the page at all.
bullets: Final entries for the published Cambridge March 2027 series closed on 27 November 2026, fourteen weeks before the first paper
Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable
A Core entry makes only the lower part of the grade scale available, and the tier is decided on the school's own evidence
Published UAE rates for secondary tuition run from about AED 45 to AED 650 an hour, depending on the provider model
Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum is licensed

cambridge-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Cambridge runs a continuous route from Year 7 to Year 13, and the decisions taken at each stage narrow the next one. These are the four stages UAE families ask about, with what each one actually commits a student to and where it bites locally.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, assessed by Checkpoint tests in English, mathematics and science. Checkpoint is diagnostic rather than a certificate, and the scores are the clearest early evidence a school uses when it decides tier placement for Year 10. Work at this stage is about closing arithmetic and writing gaps while they are still cheap to close.
programmes.countryNote: UAE centres run Checkpoint in March, May or October. Families arriving from an Indian or American curriculum often meet it in their first term here, and a weak paper in a subject the student has simply never been taught gets misread as ability rather than coverage.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Core tier
programmes.description: The Core components of a tiered syllabus, taught over two years and examined in a single series. Core content is a subset of the full syllabus and only the lower part of the grade scale is available. It is the right entry for a student who needs accuracy and security rather than reach, and the sensible target is the top of that range.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE a Core entry quietly becomes a sixth-form question, because published entry grades for AS Level courses often sit above the Core ceiling. Raise it with the school in the autumn of Year 11, with marked Extended-style work in hand, not in the spring once the entry has gone.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Extended tier
programmes.description: Core plus supplement content, examined on the Extended components, with the full grade range available including the top grades. The supplement is not harder versions of the same questions; it is additional material, and it is usually the part a student who has been coasting has never met. Hours here go to the supplement and to the long structured questions.
programmes.countryNote: This is the common entry at UK-curriculum schools across Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah. The failure mode is an Extended entry defended against the school's evidence, where marks leak across the whole paper instead of being banked at the top of the lower tier.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The two-year route many Cambridge IGCSE students continue into, examined in the June and November series and also in the March series at allocated centres. Entry grades are set by the school and are normally expressed in IGCSE grades, which is why a tier decision taken in Year 10 reaches further forward than most families expect it to.
programmes.countryNote: Sixth-form places in the UAE are offered on IGCSE results, and the statement of results is accepted before certificates arrive in late June. A student who misses an entry grade in one subject may have a November resit available, but those results do not land until January.

cambridge-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Cambridge gives every syllabus a four-digit code, and the code rather than the subject name is what a tutor needs. The descriptions below say what each course assesses and where marks are usually lost, so you can tell quickly whether a tutor is talking about your child's course.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Written papers split by tier, with a calculator and a non-calculator paper in each on the current syllabus. Marks leak at the method stage: a correct final answer with no working scores less than a wrong answer with a visible, awardable method. Sessions here are part-mark drills on past questions rather than fresh teaching.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (0607)
subjects.description: A different course from 0580 despite the shared subject name, with a graphics-calculator paper and an investigation-style component at Extended. Students who transfer between UAE schools sometimes change code mid-course, which is the one situation where past papers from the wrong syllabus actively mislead.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 Extended by students heading for A Level Mathematics, and the clearest early indicator of whether that route will be comfortable. Content overlaps the first term of AS, so the hours spent here do double duty for a student who is continuing.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Theory papers by tier, plus either a practical test or the written alternative to practical paper. Electricity and the equation-rearranging topics cost most of the lost marks. The alternative to practical is a reading and reasoning paper and is taught well over video; the practical test needs the school laboratory.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic, organic reaction pathways and the extended electrolysis questions are where Extended candidates separate from Core ones. The practical and alternative-to-practical components follow the same split as physics, and the same honest limitation applies to the laboratory paper.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: A content-heavy syllabus where marks go to command words rather than knowledge: describing a process when the question asked for an explanation. Sessions work best on marked past-paper sections with the mark scheme open beside the student's own script.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences (0654 and 0653)
subjects.description: The double and single award routes for students not taking three separate sciences. Content is drawn from all three disciplines, so a tutor has to work outside one specialism, and a school's choice between the two routes affects what a sixth form will accept afterwards.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500 and 0990)
subjects.description: Reading and directed writing, assessed against criteria that reward control rather than length. The common fix is not vocabulary but structure: answering the question asked, in the form the task specifies, and keeping a response inside the brief it was given.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510, 0511 and 0991)
subjects.description: The codes differ in how speaking is treated, which is a detail worth confirming on the statement of entry. Progress comes from timed writing tasks marked against the criteria, not from general conversation practice, which is what most informal help defaults to.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450) and Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Both reward applied answers: a point, an explanation, then a judgement tied to the case material in front of the student. Marks are lost to generic answers learned from a revision guide and reproduced whatever the question stem actually says.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode, data representation and a theory paper that trips strong programmers who have never written an algorithm by hand. Sessions are mostly written-answer practice rather than coding, which surprises families who expected the opposite of that.

subjects.name: Arabic (0508 and 0544)
subjects.description: Two separate Cambridge courses, placed by the school according to the student's background. An Arabic grade is a qualification in its own right, but it is not counted among the five accredited subjects the Ministry of Education looks for on the British track.

cambridge-igcse-tutor.regionsTitle: Where your child's school sits, and which authority holds its file
cambridge-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Delivery is identical in all seven emirates, because the lesson runs over live video. What differs is the authority that licenses the school, which decides what a parent can look up about it, and how thin the local pool of a visiting Cambridge specialist would be. These notes are about those two things.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Schools answer to KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate and publishes inspection reports parents can read. Dubai had 227 private schools in 2024-25 serving 387,441 students across 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum the largest single share, so Cambridge entries here are routine.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Press-reported professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which is why a teacher may decline an evening request from a parent in their own class.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK. The practical difference is distance: the list of visiting specialists willing to drive out for a tiered science entry is short, and the published market rate carries that drive inside it. Online removes the drive and widens the list to whoever teaches the syllabus code.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not only inspection sits with the emirate. Useful to know when a school reshuffles an option block.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. Families moving between Ajman and Dubai mid-course often find option blocks differ, which can change which Cambridge subjects are available and occasionally the syllabus code itself.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Entries run through the school's own centre, so confirm the timetable zone with the exams officer rather than assuming it matches a Dubai school's.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the Ministry of Education. Fujairah appears in almost no UAE tutoring content at all, which is a fair proxy for how many visiting specialists work here. Live online sessions on Gulf Standard Time make the local pool irrelevant to who teaches your child.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under the Ministry of Education, and the smallest of the seven markets. Where a subject and tier combination is uncommon, the realistic options are one-to-one online or a weekly drive to another emirate, and this page is clear about which of the two IB Gram provides.

schoolClusters.note: Students supported here sit Cambridge entries alongside KHDA's mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons, which schools timetable on a forty-minute unit. Inspection reports for each school are published by the regulator and are worth reading before any money is spent on tuition.

Schools in this cluster are licensed by ADEK. Cambridge and Pearson entries both appear across it, so the first question in any match here is which board and which syllabus code the centre has entered a student for, rather than which of the two boards is preferable.

Regulated by SPEA in Sharjah and by the Ministry of Education in Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain. Option blocks are narrower in smaller cohorts, which is where an uncommon subject and tier combination becomes genuinely hard to staff locally.

cambridge-igcse-tutor.modesIntro: Four formats cover almost every Cambridge request that arrives, and the right one depends mostly on how many weeks remain before the first paper. All four run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and none of them involves anyone travelling to a UAE address.

modes.title: Two-year build across Years 10 and 11
modes.description: A weekly hour per subject from the start of Year 10. This is the only format that can genuinely influence the tier decision, because it produces marked Extended-style work before the autumn entry conversation happens. It is also the cheapest version of the same outcome, since nothing has to be rebuilt later under time pressure.

An evidence pack ready for the Year 11 tier conversation

modes.description: Booked once the series date is known and the weeks are countable. Twelve weeks out the plan rebuilds topics; six weeks out it is marked past papers and answer shape; the final fortnight is retrieval and timing only. The whole block is written down at the start so nobody is improvising in April.

No new content inside the last two weeks
Review at the mock and again four weeks out

modes.title: Single-component clinic
modes.description: For one named problem: the alternative to practical paper, the long structured questions on an Extended theory paper, or the directed-writing task in First Language English. Usually four to six sessions, ending when the marked work shows the component holding up rather than when a package runs out.
bullets: One component, named from the statement of entry

Four to six sessions is the usual length

modes.description: For Year 9 students, and for families who have just moved here and met Checkpoint in their first term. The work is coverage repair: finding the topics a previous curriculum never taught, so that a tier decision in Year 10 is made on ability rather than on gaps nobody has audited.

sections.heading: What a Cambridge statement of entry fixes, and what is still open
paragraphs: The document that settles most arguments at home is the statement of entry. The exam centre issues it before each series, and it lists, for every subject, the syllabus code, the tier, the component numbers and the candidate number. Parents who have been guessing which course their child is on stop guessing the moment they read it. A tutor should ask for it in the first conversation, because an hour planned against the wrong tier is wasted even when the teaching inside it is good, and that waste is invisible until a mock comes back.

Three things on that sheet are effectively closed once the final entry deadline has passed. The syllabus code is closed: 0580 and 0607 are different courses with different question styles, and a school cannot swap one for the other in April. The exam centre is closed, which is what fixes the timetable version your family should be working to. The tier is closed in practice, because a change needs the centre to submit an amendment supported by the school's own evidence, and most schools will not do that in the final term.

What remains open is everything a tutor can actually reach: the number of past papers your child has marked under time, whether a command word is understood, whether working is written down in a form an examiner is able to award, and the order in which topics get revisited. That is a narrower list than most families expect and a far more useful one. The table separates the two columns, so a first session goes to the open one instead of to a complaint about the closed one.

sections.heading: Counting a series backwards from the day the entries close
paragraphs: The one date most families never see is the final entry deadline. For the Cambridge March 2027 series the board publishes final entries as due on 27 November 2026, with the exam period running from 3 February to 4 March 2027. Fourteen weeks separate the two. A parent who starts looking for help in January is therefore working inside a frame that was locked in late November by a member of staff they have probably never met, on the strength of coursework and mock marks from the autumn term.

Counting backwards changes what you should be asking for. Twelve weeks out, a weekly hour can still rebuild a topic from the ground up. Six weeks out, the gain comes from marked past-paper sections and from writing answers in the shape a mark scheme rewards. Two weeks out, the only safe work is retrieval and timing: no new content, nothing that shakes a student's confidence days before a paper. The same AED per hour buys three genuinely different services depending on where in that count it is spent.

The table lists the published milestones for that series in date order, with the thing a household should have finished by each one. The board's own guidance is the authority on the dates; your centre is the authority on which of them apply to your child. Results for the March series reach centres on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June, which means a family planning a summer move needs the statement of results rather than the certificate for an application.

sections.heading: Three series in a year, and the one most UAE families are never offered
paragraphs: Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series. Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests sit separately, in March, May and October. The Cambridge March series also exists and is used by particular centres; its 2027 exam period runs from 3 February to 4 March. Most UAE schools work to June, because that is where the academic year lands, and a parent generally discovers the alternatives only when something has already gone wrong in one subject.

Series choice belongs to the school, not the family, and it is made at entry. Where it matters most is after a result. A June candidate who misses a grade in one subject has the Cambridge November series available in the same calendar year, but a student who needs that grade for a sixth-form place starting in September does not, because November results reach students in January. Knowing that in advance is the difference between a plan and a scramble in the week results arrive.

The consequence for tuition is simple arithmetic. A June-series student has the whole UAE school year ahead of them and can be taught properly across Years 10 and 11. A November resit candidate has a compressed block running across the summer and the first term, usually with school lessons no longer covering that content at all. Both are workable jobs. They are not the same job, and they should not be quoted, planned or staffed as though they were.

sections.heading: Six administrative zones, and why the timetable you downloaded may not be yours
paragraphs: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and its guidance for exams officers is unusually blunt about the consequence: it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and the board states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam because the wrong version was used. A Cambridge administrative zone is an administrative fact about the centre rather than about the country, so two UAE schools are not automatically in the same one.

In practice this is the most common planning error a tutor sees. A parent searches for the timetable, finds a PDF, pins it to the fridge and books sessions around it. Two of the subject dates turn out to be an hour out and one is a day out. Sessions end up scheduled on the morning of a paper. The fix costs nothing at all: ask the exams officer which zone the centre sits in and which version of the timetable it is working to, then plan the last fortnight from that document and nothing else.

It also explains something families find suspicious. A cousin in another country sits the same paper at a different local time, and a classmate who transferred in remembers different dates entirely. Neither is evidence of a leak or an administrative error. Zoning exists so that papers are sat inside a controlled window across many time zones at once. For a UAE household the working rule is to treat the centre's own document as the only calendar and anything found through a search engine as a draft.

sections.heading: Reading a component number before you buy an hour
paragraphs: Parents are handed component numbers and given no translation. On a Cambridge science syllabus the numbering follows a pattern which, once learned, tells you most of what a session should cover. Odd and even pairs separate Core from Extended on the written theory papers, and a practical test and a written alternative to practical paper sit at the end of the list. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and its chemistry and biology equivalents are all numbered on that same shape.

This matters commercially because one subject name hides two different pieces of work. A student entered for the practical test needs laboratory technique and a teacher who can coach method at a bench. A student entered for the written alternative needs something quite different: reading a described experiment, identifying the controlled variable, completing a results table, criticising a method they never performed themselves. One of those is taught over video without compromise. The other needs the school laboratory, and an honest tutor says so in the first conversation.

Cambridge IGCSE Maths 0580 works on the same tier-split logic, with a calculator and a non-calculator paper in each tier on the current syllabus. Confirm the component numbers from the statement of entry rather than from a syllabus PDF found online, because syllabuses are revised and the version your child sits is the one the centre entered them for. The table gives the pattern to expect; your child's own entry gives the fact you should plan against.

sections.heading: The tier conversation to have before the autumn entry goes in
paragraphs: Most Cambridge IGCSE subjects are tiered. The core and extended tier split is not two difficulty settings of one exam; they are different papers with different grade ranges, and the entry decides which range is available to a candidate. A school places a student on the evidence it holds: end-of-Year-10 results, topic tests and how the student copes when a question is unfamiliar. That decision is usually taken in the autumn of Year 11, which is precisely why October is when the conversation is worth having.

Families get into difficulty in two opposite directions. The first is a Core entry made for a student who was quietly improving all summer, which caps a grade below the level a sixth-form course asks for. The second is an Extended entry defended by a parent against the school's evidence, where the student then loses marks steadily across the whole paper instead of securing the top of the lower tier. Neither of those is fixed by buying more hours the following April.

What tuition is genuinely good for here is producing evidence before the entry is submitted. Six to eight weeks of marked work on Extended-style questions, with the marks shown to the subject teacher, is an argument a school can act on. After the deadline the work changes shape: on a Core entry the job is to secure the top of that tier cleanly, which is a real and respectable outcome rather than a consolation prize, and it needs different hours from a reach attempt.

sections.heading: Command words: where Cambridge marks are quietly lost
paragraphs: A student who knows the content and still comes out at grade 5 is usually answering a different question from the one that was asked. Cambridge questions are built on command words, and each one has a mark scheme behind it expecting a particular shape of answer. State wants a fact and no reasoning. Explain wants a mechanism, and will not award the bare fact. Suggest expects a plausible answer applied to a context the student has not seen before and cannot have revised.

This is the single most repairable cause of lost marks, and it stays repairable late in the year because it needs no new content. A session takes four questions the student has already attempted, reads the command word, counts the marks on offer and rewrites the answer to that shape. Two or three weeks of that work moves scripts that have plateaued for a term. It is also why marked past papers matter more than worked solutions: the student has to see where their own sentence failed to earn a mark.

The table pairs common command words with what a mark scheme tends to reward and the failure a tutor sees most often. It is a diagnostic rather than a revision list. Used properly, a parent can read a marked mock script beside it and tell the difference between a child who does not know a topic and a child who knows it and is writing the wrong kind of sentence about it. Those two problems need completely different hours.

sections.heading: What Cambridge IGCSE support costs across this market
paragraphs: Published UAE rates for an hour of secondary tuition run from roughly AED 45 at the budget end to AED 650 at the top of the market, and the spread is not arbitrary. It tracks who is teaching, whether the hour includes marking, and whether anyone has to travel. Budget online hours are generally taught by university students. Specialist IGCSE and IB hours in this market are published between about AED 200 and AED 450, and a visiting tutor's rate carries the travel inside it.

Monthly packages seen in this market include online blocks around AED 799 for eight sessions and visiting-tutor blocks between AED 1,599 and AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. A Dubai cost survey estimates monthly spend for a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are market figures from the sources named, read in October 2026, and not IB Gram's price list.

Two things are worth checking before any of that is paid. First, whether the quoted hour is sixty minutes or a school period of forty, since KHDA itself calculates mandatory-subject time on a forty-minute unit and some providers quote on the same basis. Second, what the rate includes: marking a past paper properly takes a tutor twenty to thirty minutes outside the lesson, and a rate that excludes it is not the cheaper rate it appears to be. Ask for both in writing.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor in this market, set against one-to-one online
paragraphs: The honest version of this comparison starts with what a visiting tutor genuinely offers. Someone in the room can read a hand-written page without a camera angle, can reach for a textbook, and can hold the attention of a young student who drifts on a screen. For a Year 7 or Year 8 Cambridge Lower Secondary student that is a real argument, not a weak one. Published UAE rates for a visiting hour run roughly AED 180 to 500, with the travel priced inside the number.

The cost of that model is the tutor pool. A family in Al Ain or Fujairah choosing from the people willing to drive to them is choosing from a short list, and that list rarely contains a specialist who can teach the Extended supplement and the alternative to practical paper for a tiered science syllabus. Travel also eats the evening: a four o'clock session needing a forty-minute drive each way costs the tutor two hours and the household a fixed slot it cannot move.

IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one online Cambridge IGCSE tuition over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, in every emirate. IB Gram does not operate a visiting-tutor service in the UAE; that is offered only in India. The trade is specific. You give up the person in the room and you gain a specialist matched to the syllabus code and tier, plus a session that can shift by thirty minutes when traffic or a school event intervenes. The table sets the two formats side by side.
