sections.heading: Results day, a statement of results, and the fortnight that follows
paragraphs: Cambridge releases results to centres first, on Cambridge Direct, and the centre passes them on to candidates. For the March 2027 series the published date for results on Direct is 13 May, with certificates issued in late June. Pearson's International GCSE pattern is comparable in shape: its June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The pattern worth taking from all of this is that certificates always trail results by weeks.

That gap is the thing a family should plan around. Schools and universities asking for evidence in the days after results will accept the statement of results, and nobody needs to wait for a certificate before accepting an offer or registering for a sixth-form course. Families travelling during the UAE summer should decide before they leave who in the household can log in, who will read the statement properly, and who will contact the exams officer if a grade looks out of line with the marked work.

Queries about results run through the centre rather than the family, and they run on a short clock. If a grade sits a mark or two under a boundary on a paper where the student's own marked work was consistently stronger, that is the case to put to the exams officer within days. A tutor's useful contribution at that point is evidence: marked scripts, timed papers and a record of where the student was scoring. It is also why keeping the marked work matters.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies beside a Cambridge option block
paragraphs: A Cambridge timetable in the UAE does not run on its own. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum a school is licensed to teach, and KHDA's published requirements had to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. For a Year 11 student carrying nine Cambridge subjects, these are additional timetabled lessons, additional homework and, in Arabic, an additional set of assessments to prepare for.

The rules are specific enough to matter to a tutoring plan. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Mandatory-subject time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, with the advice that no mandatory lesson should run shorter than twenty-five minutes, and teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education need the appropriate KHDA permission to teach them.

There is one constraint parents should know before buying outside help for these three subjects. For the mandatory UAE subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. Support for them is therefore about the school's own material, the school's own assessments and study technique, rather than an alternative course taught in parallel. Where the real pressure on a household is Cambridge grades, the answer is often timetable triage instead of putting more subjects under paid tuition.

sections.heading: Equivalency, the tutor's permit, and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Three compliance points come up in nearly every first conversation. The first is Ministry of Education equivalency. On the British track, as reported when the ministry clarified its requirements in July 2026, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education not included among those five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Verify it on moe.gov.ae before relying on it.

The second is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published anywhere official.

The third is academic honesty, and it is the one that ends school careers rather than costing money. A tutor teaches, explains, questions and gives feedback on work a student has already produced. A tutor does not author an assessed piece, redraft one to completion, or supply sentences for it. Where a provider offers a finished coursework piece for a fee, the student carries the malpractice risk and the provider keeps the money. Ask any tutor what they will refuse to do; the answer tells you what you are actually buying.

process.title: Send the statement of entry
process.description: Or the timetable the centre gave you. It carries the syllabus code, the tier, the component numbers and the candidate number, and it is the only document that settles which course your child is actually on. Everything after this step is built from what it says.

process.title: Say which weeks are left
process.description: The series date, the school's mock window and any travel. A plan counted back from a real date is a different thing from a general offer of help, and the number of weeks decides whether the first session rebuilds a topic or goes straight to a marked past paper.

process.title: A trial session on a question that went wrong
process.description: Thirty minutes, at no charge and with no card details taken, built around a specific question your child lost marks on. You hear whether the tutor knows the syllabus code, and your child hears whether the explanation lands. Both matter, and only one of them shows up in a profile.

process.title: Confirm the tutor, the slot and what is included
process.description: In writing: the length of the hour in minutes, whether marking between sessions is included, and the rate. Forty-minute school periods and sixty-minute hours are both quoted in this market, and that is the single most common misunderstanding about what tuition costs.

process.title: Review at the mock, then again four weeks out
process.description: Two fixed checkpoints rather than a vague promise of progress. The mock script shows whether the plan is working. The four-week review decides what gets dropped, because by then the honest question is which topics to abandon rather than which ones to add.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the syllabus code, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: 0580 and 0607 are different courses, and 0625 Core and 0625 Extended are different papers. The match starts from the code and tier on your child's entry, which is why the statement of entry is the first thing asked for and the last thing a general tutoring enquiry ever mentions.

whyPoints.title: Dates taken from the board, not from memory
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page are cited from those boards' own published key dates and timetables, with the month they were read. IB session dates are deliberately absent: the IB's site blocks automated checking, so no unverified exam date is published here at all.

whyPoints.title: Marked work between the sessions
whyPoints.description: Watching a worked solution feels productive and changes little. The student attempts the question, the tutor marks it against the mark scheme, and the next session starts from where the marks were lost. That loop is slower to set up, and it is what moves a script that has plateaued.

whyPoints.title: One-to-one, so the hour goes where the marks went
whyPoints.description: A group class moves at the pace of its weakest understanding of each topic. One student means a session can abandon its own plan when a marked script shows the real problem is unit discipline rather than the topic everyone at home had assumed it was.

whyPoints.title: A straight answer when nobody is free
whyPoints.description: Uncommon subject and tier combinations sometimes have no specialist available in the week you want to begin. You are told that, with the realistic alternatives, instead of being matched to whoever happens to be free. A mismatch costs more than a fortnight's wait does.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary stated before you book
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on work the student has produced. Nobody here authors an assessed piece or redrafts one to completion, and any provider willing to do that is handing the student a malpractice risk while quietly keeping the fee.

faqs.question: Our centre mentioned an exam period in February. Which Cambridge series is that?
faqs.answer: That is the March series. Cambridge publishes it alongside June and November, and for 2027 the exam period runs from 3 February to 4 March. Entries for it closed on 27 November 2026, forecast grades were due on 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. Not every centre uses this series, so the only reliable confirmation is your school's exams officer. If your child is in it, the planning year effectively ends in January rather than in the spring.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge syllabus code is my child entered for, and where can I read it?
faqs.answer: On the statement of entry the exam centre issues before each series. It lists every subject with its syllabus code, the tier and the component numbers. The code matters because a subject name hides different courses: Mathematics 0580 and International Mathematics 0607 ask different questions and reward different preparation. If the sheet has not arrived yet, the exams officer can confirm the codes by email. Any tutor quoting for the subject without knowing its code is quoting for a course they have not actually seen.

faqs.question: What do the component numbers on a Cambridge statement of entry mean?
faqs.answer: They name the papers your child will sit. On a tiered science syllabus the written theory papers are split between Core and Extended by number, and a practical test and a written alternative to practical paper sit at the end of the list. Knowing which of those two your child is entered for changes the teaching completely: one needs laboratory method, the other needs reading a described experiment and criticising it. Confirm the numbers from the entry rather than from a syllabus PDF found online.

faqs.question: Why do two Cambridge candidates in different countries sit one paper at different times?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable. The board's guidance to exams officers is explicit that the correct version for the zone must be used, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. For a family this produces one practical rule: plan the final fortnight from the document your centre gives you, and treat any timetable found through a search as a draft.

faqs.question: Our son is on the Core tier in 0580. What grade does that cap him at?
faqs.answer: A Core entry makes only the lower part of the grade scale available, because he sits the Core components and those papers cannot award the top grades. That is a real constraint on sixth-form courses whose published entry grades sit above it. The moment to argue a change is the autumn of Year 11, with six to eight weeks of marked Extended-style work to show the subject teacher. Once the final entry has gone in, the useful target is the top of the Core range, secured cleanly.

faqs.question: Our school asked for a forecast grade in February. What is it used for?
faqs.answer: It is the subject teacher's predicted outcome, submitted to Cambridge by the centre on the board's own date, and used in administering the series rather than in setting your child's result. The grade itself comes from the scripts. It is still worth caring about, because the evidence a teacher has in front of them in February is the marked work from the autumn term and the mock. That is the window in which a student can change what the teacher sees.

faqs.question: There are eleven weeks until paper one. What can still be changed?
faqs.answer: A good deal, provided the work is targeted. Eleven weeks is enough to rebuild one or two weak topics and then spend the back half on marked past-paper sections and answer shape. What it is not enough for is re-teaching a whole syllabus, and any plan implying otherwise is selling hours rather than a result. The sequence that works is topic repair first, marked papers next, and retrieval and timing only during the final fortnight before the paper.

faqs.question: What does a Cambridge command word such as 'suggest' actually ask for?
faqs.answer: It asks for a plausible answer applied to a context the student has not seen before, which is exactly why it cannot be answered from memory. Each command word has an answer shape behind it: state wants a fact with no reasoning, describe wants what happens without the cause, explain wants the mechanism, and calculate wants working and units as well as a number. Learning those shapes is the fastest repair available to a student who knows the content and still lands on a grade 5.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge science component stands in for the laboratory, and can it be taught over video?
faqs.answer: The written alternative to practical paper, which sits at the end of the component list on the tiered science syllabuses. It is a reading and reasoning paper: a described experiment, a controlled variable to identify, a results table to complete, a method to criticise. All of that is taught well over live video. The practical test itself needs the school laboratory and a teacher at the bench, and no online provider should pretend otherwise to win the booking.

faqs.question: When do Cambridge results reach a candidate, and when does the certificate follow?
faqs.answer: Results go to the centre first on Cambridge Direct, and the centre releases them to candidates. For the published March 2027 series, results reach centres on 13 May with certificates issued in late June. Pearson's pattern is comparable: its June 2026 International GCSE results went to centres on 19 August and to students the following day. The practical point is that certificates always trail results by weeks, and schools and universities accept the statement of results in the meantime.

faqs.question: A grade sits one mark under a boundary. What can be done, and how quickly?
faqs.answer: Queries go through the exam centre rather than the family, and the window is short, so the conversation with the exams officer should happen within days of release. What helps the case is evidence: marked past papers, timed scripts and a record of where your child was consistently scoring. Keep that work rather than clearing it out after the exams. A tutor's contribution at this stage is the paper trail, and there is nothing to assemble if it was thrown away in June.

faqs.question: Which figure should we budget for one Cambridge IGCSE subject in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Published rates in this market run from about AED 45 an hour at the budget end to AED 650 at the top, with qualified subject tutors online between roughly AED 150 and AED 300 and IGCSE specialists between about AED 200 and AED 450. A Dubai cost survey puts monthly spend for a weekly one-hour session between AED 600 and AED 1,200 in the middle band. Those are market figures from the sources named, read in October 2026, and not IB Gram's own prices.

faqs.question: The lessons are described as one-to-one. Where do they actually take place?
faqs.answer: Over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the student at their own desk anywhere in the Emirates. IB Gram does not operate a visiting-tutor service in the UAE; that is offered only in India. The gain is the match: a tiered science entry needs someone who teaches that syllabus code and tier, and the chance that such a person lives twenty minutes from a family in Al Ain or Fujairah is low. Written working is shared on screen or photographed and marked.

faqs.question: Our daughter has six Cambridge IGCSEs and one is Islamic Education. Does the ministry count all seven?
faqs.answer: On the British track, as reported when the Ministry of Education clarified its requirements in July 2026, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among those five. The count would therefore be taken from her other subjects. Verify the rule on moe.gov.ae before relying on it, and note that at least one ranking UAE site publishes a six-subject version that does not match the clarification.

faqs.question: Can we see the permit a private tutor holds, and what should it say on it?
faqs.answer: Ask for it. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Its code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Someone offered to rewrite my son's Cambridge coursework for a fee. What is wrong with that?
faqs.answer: The piece has to be his own work, and a submission produced by somebody else is malpractice. The student carries that risk, not the person who was paid for it. A tutor can teach the skill, question the argument, point at a weak paragraph and explain what the criteria reward, all on a draft your son has already produced himself. Nobody here authors an assessed piece or redrafts one to completion, and a provider willing to do it is selling your son a problem.

faqs.question: Our revision block runs through Ramadan and Eid. How do sessions get rearranged?
faqs.answer: Timings move rather than stopping. Schools shorten the day during Ramadan, energy is lowest in the late afternoon, and the Eid break removes a run of days from a counted-back plan. The usual pattern is to move sessions earlier or to after iftar, to put content-heavy work before the month and retrieval work inside it, and to write the lost sessions back into the plan rather than quietly losing them. Agree the revised slots before the month begins.

faqs.question: If no specialist covers my child's subject and tier, what are we told?
faqs.answer: That nobody is available, and what the realistic alternatives are: a short wait for a named tutor, a different slot that opens one up, or a different format for the component in question. Uncommon combinations, such as an Extended entry in a smaller option subject, are where this happens. Matching a student to whoever is free costs more than a fortnight's wait, because the hours go on the wrong paper and the family concludes tuition does not work.

cambridge-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Start from the date, not from the search
cambridge-igcse-tutor.closingBody: If you take one habit from this page, take the habit of asking for the statement of entry and the centre's own timetable version before anything else. Those two documents give you the syllabus code, the tier, the components and the real number of weeks left, and they turn a vague worry into a plan with dates attached to it. Send them with your first message, say which subject went wrong and how it went wrong, and the trial session can go straight to a question your child lost marks on. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, in every emirate.

intro.heading: What a parent can actually verify about an IB tutor in the Emirates
paragraphs: Parents searching for a certified IB tutor in the UAE are looking for a filter. The word promises that somebody independent has already checked this person, so you do not have to. Part of that promise is real and part of it is not, and sorting the two takes about ten minutes of questions before any money moves. The real part is legal: private tutoring here is permit-regulated, and the permit is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The part that is not real is the implication that the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or a UAE education authority hands out a tutoring licence to individuals. They do not. They license schools, approve exam centres and clear the teachers inside them.

That leaves four separate things bundled inside one marketing word. A permit to be paid for lessons. A teaching qualification from a university or an education ministry. A subject qualification, usually a degree in the thing being taught. And experience of the exact syllabus your child sits, which is a claim rather than a certificate and has to be tested instead of filed. Two of the four sit in a database somebody can look up. The other two are documents you should ask to see. None of them, on their own, tells you whether a person can teach Higher Level Chemistry to a sixteen-year-old who has stopped doing the homework.

The second half of the question is the system your tutor has to work inside, and it changes by emirate. Dubai's private schools answer to KHDA. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to ADEK. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The school's inspection report, published by whichever of those bodies holds its file, is the single most useful document a parent has before hiring anyone, because it is the only place a subject-level weakness is written down by somebody other than the school.

Running beside all of this are the subjects the Ministry requires regardless of curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international programme the school is licensed to teach, with rules on language of instruction, on separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups, and on using content the Ministry has not permitted. Any honest page about Arabic and Islamic Education tutoring has to say that a tutor here works from the school's material, not a bespoke syllabus of their own.

On delivery, this page is blunt. IB Gram arranges online IB tuition in the UAE: one-to-one lessons over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen and the student's own files open. We do not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the Emirates. Visiting tutors are a service we run in India only. The trade is deliberate: instead of choosing from whoever can reach your community before 6pm, you choose a Physics HL or Economics HL specialist and the commute disappears from the bill. Last reviewed October 2026.

certified-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: IB Gram covers the four IB programmes, but the credential question changes as the stakes rise. A PYP parent is usually asking about literacy and number confidence. A Diploma parent is asking about marks, deadlines and whether outside help is allowed. Each programme below carries a note on how it sits inside the UAE regulatory picture.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is inquiry-led and has no external examination, so progress is reported through teacher judgement, portfolios and the exhibition in the final year. Tutoring at this stage is diagnostic rather than exam-driven: reading fluency, number facts, written structure and the habit of explaining an answer. A tutor working on PYP should be able to describe how a unit of inquiry is built, because that is the shape of everything the child is asked to do in class.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, PYP schools still deliver the Ministry's mandatory subjects from the earliest years, and KHDA requires separate Arabic classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils. A PYP parent asking about a certified tutor is often really asking about Arabic, where the school's stream placement matters more than the tutor's CV.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, marked out of eight each, with no public examination unless the school enters students for eAssessment. This is where families most often discover a gap, because criterion-based marks do not convert neatly into the percentages parents are used to reading. A tutor who knows the MYP can explain why a child who understands the content is losing marks on criterion D, which is usually about applying knowledge to an unfamiliar context.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools run MYP to Year 9 and then switch to IGCSE, so the transition year is the one that needs attention. The emirate regulator approves the curricula a school offers, which is why option blocks differ between a Sharjah school and a Dubai one even inside the same group.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal assessment carries real weight in most subjects, and the written papers are set by the IB rather than the school. This is the programme where the certification question matters most, because a tutor is working alongside assessed coursework that must be the student's own and that the school's coordinator has to declare as authentic.
programmes.countryNote: The International Baccalaureate accounts for roughly seven in a hundred of Dubai's private-school pupils, a small share of the largest private-school market in the country. That scarcity, not price, is the real reason a Higher Level specialist is harder to book in the Emirates than a GCSE maths tutor.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a service-learning element and a language development component. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools and is frequently misunderstood as a lighter Diploma, which it is not. The Diploma courses inside it are examined identically, so tutoring for a CP student looks the same as tutoring for a DP student in that subject.
programmes.countryNote: Because the CP is rare locally, a parent cannot assume a tutor has seen one. Ask specifically whether they have taught the Diploma courses the CP student is taking rather than the programme label, and check with the school how the reflective project is supervised before anyone outside the school reads a draft.

certified-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: Subject descriptions below are written around where marks are lost, because that is what a credential cannot tell you. A tutor with a physics degree and a teaching qualification may still have never marked an IB-style data-analysis question. Ask which board, which syllabus and how many cohorts, for the exact subject and level your child sits.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency carry this course, and Higher Level adds a third paper that rewards students who can hold a long argument together. The exploration is worth a fifth of the grade and is lost on weak personal engagement and unexplained notation, not on difficult mathematics. Ask a tutor which exploration topics they have seen marked down and why.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use dominate. Students who moved from IGCSE often underestimate how much of the mark depends on interpreting output rather than producing it, and on writing a conclusion in context. Graphical calculator technique is examinable in practice, so a tutor who cannot drive the same model as your child is working at a disadvantage.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Marks are lost in two predictable places: uncertainty and error analysis in the scientific investigation, and the extended-response questions where a definition is given but not applied. Higher Level adds depth rather than breadth, so a student who is shaky on the core will not be rescued by extra content. Practical write-up conventions need teaching explicitly.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium account for most of the lost marks, and the investigation is where a strong candidate separates from an average one. The common failure is a method that cannot generate enough data to analyse. A tutor may question a student's method and point to the published criteria; choosing the investigation is the student's own job.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms decide the grade here more than recall does. Students who write everything they know about a topic score less than students who answer the verb in the question. Data-based questions on unfamiliar experiments reward comprehension rather than memory, and that skill is teachable in a handful of sessions with the right past material.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, evaluation and the internal assessment commentaries drive the grade. Commentaries fail on article choice and on word-limit discipline long before they fail on theory. Higher Level adds quantitative demands that catch students who chose the subject expecting an essay course. Real UAE and Gulf examples make evaluation sharper than textbook cases do.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application rather than tool recall is what the markers reward, and the case study at Higher Level punishes students who have not practised reading a long stimulus under time pressure. The internal assessment needs a real organisation and real evidence, which is where families in the Emirates have a genuine advantage worth using.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the Paper 1 guided analysis are the two components that move a grade fastest. Students lose marks by summarising a text instead of analysing how it works and by choosing global issues that are too broad to sustain ten minutes of speech. Timed writing practice with marked feedback is the whole intervention.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Script fluency, listening and the productive skills decide these courses. For students in the Emirates there is an added complication: the Ministry's mandatory Arabic lessons at school are a separate requirement from IB Arabic, with their own content rules. A tutor should be clear which of the two a session is addressing before it starts.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions, tracing algorithms by hand and the internal assessment product are the pinch points. Students who code well in Python often lose marks because the examination expects a specific pseudocode style rather than working software. The internal assessment needs a genuine client, documented, and the documentation is marked as heavily as the artefact.

certified-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: Regulation is the one part of UAE schooling that genuinely changes with the emirate, so the notes below are written around who holds the file rather than around commute times. Lessons are delivered over live video everywhere in this list, which is why the tutor pool does not shrink as you move north.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA oversees the quality of private education in the emirate and publishes the inspection reports families should read first. With 227 private schools and 17 licensed curricula, two schools a few minutes apart can run entirely different option blocks and assessment calendars.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools here, and its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. That rule is the reason the obvious first choice of tutor is often not available.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Al Ain sits under ADEK alongside Abu Dhabi rather than under a separate authority. IB cohorts are smaller inland, so Higher Level groups can be tiny and a subject the school cannot staff is a common reason families look outside it.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Curriculum approval sitting locally is why a Sharjah school's subject offering can differ from a sister school in Dubai.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority, so there is no local inspection portal to browse. Ask the school directly for its most recent report and for which board it enters candidates with.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Families here often drove to Dubai for tuition before online delivery made the drive unnecessary.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Fujairah's private schools fall under the federal Ministry of Education. Diploma cohorts on the east coast are small, which makes subject-specialist cover the main constraint rather than cost, and makes a video link the only realistic way to reach an HL specialist.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Umm Al Quwain also sits with the federal Ministry of Education. Many students commute to schools in Sharjah or Ras Al Khaimah, so a realistic session start time is governed by the school run rather than by anything the regulator does.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai holds the largest concentration of IB World Schools in the country, spread from Emirates Hills to Al Barsha and Dubai Silicon Oasis. Students we support sit the Diploma at schools like these, and their published KHDA inspection reports are the quickest way to see which departments are carrying the school.

The capital's IB provision is concentrated on the islands and in the newer communities inland. ADEK publishes the inspection outcomes, and its staff-ethics position on teachers tutoring their own students is worth knowing before you ask the school for a recommendation.

schoolClusters.note: IB cohorts thin out quickly north of Dubai, and a Higher Level group of four or five students is normal. That is the single strongest argument for a video link rather than a local search, because the subject specialist simply may not live within driving distance.

Most Diploma families start with one subject and add a second only if the first is clearly working. A written note after each session records what was covered, which also means a coordinator's question about outside support can be answered honestly.

sections.heading: What the word "certified" can and cannot mean for an IB tutor here
paragraphs: No UAE authority and no examination board issues a credential called certified IB tutor. The International Baccalaureate authorises schools to deliver its programmes; it does not license private individuals to tutor them. KHDA, ADEK and the Sharjah Private Education Authority license schools and set conditions on the people who teach inside them, which is a different thing from clearing a freelancer who teaches your child over video on a Tuesday evening. So when a provider calls a tutor certified, the only useful response is three questions: certified in what, by whom, and may we see it?

Four distinct things get bundled into that one word. The first is legal permission to be paid for private lessons in the UAE, which is a permit from MoHRE and which says nothing at all about teaching quality. The second is a teaching qualification such as a PGCE, a B.Ed or a national teaching licence, which proves training in how to teach but not knowledge of the syllabus your child sits. The third is a subject qualification, normally a degree, which proves content knowledge well beyond Higher Level. The fourth is experience of the exact course, board and option your child is entered for, and that fourth one is not a certificate at all.

The practical consequence is that two of the four can be looked up and two have to be shown or tested. Ask for the permit record from the tutor's own MoHRE account. Ask for the degree certificate with the awarding university and year. Ask which board, which syllabus and how many cohorts, then test the answer by asking for a trial lesson built on a question from the current syllabus rather than a get-to-know-you chat. A tutor who has taught the course will reach for the command term and the mark scheme without being prompted. One who has not will talk about the topic.

sections.heading: The one certificate UAE law does require
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the Emirates is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the federal portal states that it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so this page quotes no amount; a figure circulating online could not be traced to an official source.

The application itself is ordinary. MoHRE's service is listed as the issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, the website and the e-services system, with no fee shown and a stated completion time of two working days. The permit carries a code of conduct that bars a tutor from serving students affiliated with their own school. ADEK private school rules point the same way in Abu Dhabi: press reporting of its professional-ethics framework describes a prohibition on private and charter school staff providing paid tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that framing should be checked against the current ADEK document before anyone relies on its exact wording.

What this means for a family is narrower than it first looks. A private tutor permit in Dubai comes from MoHRE, not from KHDA, and it tells you the lessons are lawful rather than good. A tutoring business with premises and staff is a different legal animal again and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram operates no premises in the UAE and holds no such permit, which is exactly why we describe what we are instead of borrowing a status we do not have.

sections.heading: Which authority holds your child's school file
paragraphs: Five bodies regulate private schools across the seven emirates. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, which includes Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages reviewed for this project, and the Sharjah authority by one, which tells you how little of this reaches parents.

Two of those authorities do more than inspect. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's bodies approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so what a school is allowed to offer is settled locally rather than nationally. The federal baseline is lighter than parents assume: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, provided they adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is the rule underneath every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement.

For a tutoring decision, the inspection report is the document that earns its reading time. A KHDA inspection rating is a judgement about a whole school, not about the department your child sits in, and the useful detail is inside the report rather than on the cover. Attainment describes where students have reached; progress describes movement from their own starting point. A school can be strong overall and still have one subject where progress is flat for two years running, and that single line is a better reason to hire a specialist than any grade on a report card. If you live in one emirate and the school is in another, the school's regulator is the one that counts.

sections.heading: Why a claim of regulator approval deserves a second look
paragraphs: The most dangerous sentence available to a UAE tutoring website is one that places a regulator's name immediately before the word approved. It reads as a licence and it usually is not. The permit KHDA issues in this space is an Educational Services Permit for a training institute, granted to an organisation with premises in Dubai, with initial approval first, a cap of six months to finish the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested ahead of expiry. It is a real document with real conditions, and a company with no premises in the emirate cannot hold it. Borrowing the name of it is a misrepresentation rather than marketing.

The boards work the same way. The International Baccalaureate authorises schools to deliver its programmes and trains teachers who work in them. Cambridge International and Pearson appoint exam centres and publish rules those centres must follow. None of the three issues anything to a tutoring platform. A page claiming otherwise is either confused about its own status or hoping you will not ask. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation with the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, the Sharjah Private Education Authority or the Ministry of Education, and holds no permit or accreditation from any of them. We run no office, centre or branch anywhere in the Emirates.

Three related habits in this market are worth treating with the same suspicion. A star rating a provider has written about itself, with no countable reviews behind it, is a self-serving number rather than evidence. A statistic without a sample size, a date and a method behind it is decoration, which is why no satisfaction percentage or average tutor score appears on this page. And a tutor described as a current examiner should be asked, politely, for the board and the year, because examiner status cannot be inferred and does not come with access to marking, boundaries or unreleased papers. What we publish instead is narrow and checkable: the permit position, the qualification, the board and syllabus taught, and the fact that lessons happen over video.

sections.heading: The UAE subjects that run beside the IB, and who may teach them
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to deliver, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. This sits on top of a federal rule that private schools need not follow any specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. A Diploma student in Dubai is therefore carrying six IB subjects plus a set of national requirements, and the timetable pressure is real.

The organisation rules are specific enough to be worth quoting to any tutor who claims to cover these subjects. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is delivered in Arabic for Arab students and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises a minimum of 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson.

There is one constraint that reshapes what Arabic and Islamic Education tutoring can honestly offer. For the mandatory subjects, using any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. A tutor who advertises their own bespoke Arabic programme for these lessons is describing something the rules do not permit. The honest version is narrower and more useful: work from the school's own scheme and set material, build reading fluency, script control and answer structure, and leave the content selection where the Ministry has put it. Schools are also required to ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the KHDA approval those subjects require.

sections.heading: Where the honesty line sits on the IA, the Extended Essay and TOK
paragraphs: A tutor may teach the skill, discuss a plan the student has proposed, ask questions about a draft the student has produced, point at the published criteria, and mark practice work. A tutor may not supply sentences for assessed coursework, restructure the student's text, or hand back a version to submit. The student's work has to be their own, and the school's coordinator has to declare that it is. This is not a house rule we invented to be awkward; it is the line the IB's academic-honesty regulations draw, and crossing it puts the student's diploma at risk rather than the tutor's reputation.

That line has a practical shape in a session. The student opens their own file and shares the screen. The tutor reads what is there, asks what the method was meant to show, asks where the criterion is being met, and says plainly when it is not. The student makes the changes afterwards, in their own words, in their own file. Nothing is typed into the document by the tutor and nothing is sent back rewritten. A short written note of what was discussed goes to the family, which has a second use: if a coordinator asks what outside support was involved, there is an honest and specific answer rather than a shrug.

Supervision is the other boundary parents miss. The Extended Essay has an appointed supervisor at the school who signs the reflections, and a tutor is an additional reader, never a replacement for that person. The TOK essay belongs to the TOK teacher. One UAE-facing site in this market advertises finished internal assessments for sale at a four-figure price in dirhams; that is an academic-integrity breach and a malpractice trigger for the student who buys it, and it is the clearest possible reason to ask what a provider actually does before paying. We also do not reproduce or hand out syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. We reference the official sources and link to them.

sections.heading: The school system a tutor has to fit into
paragraphs: Dubai's private sector enrolled 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum taking 37 per cent of pupils, Indian curricula 26 per cent, American 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate about seven in a hundred. Read that last figure twice. The IB is a minority programme inside the country's largest private-school market, which is the real reason an experienced Diploma teacher is harder to find than a GCSE maths tutor, and why price is the wrong first question. Scarcity of people who have taught the course is the binding constraint.

The sector is also moving. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four following a UK curriculum and three offering the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. New IB places are good news for admissions. They do nothing for teacher supply in the short run, because new schools recruit from the same pool of experienced Diploma teachers everyone else is recruiting from.

What all of this means for a tutoring plan is specific. The subject your child needs help with may not be the subject the school is strongest in, and the inspection report is where that shows up. A school that is excellent in English and only acceptable in mathematics will produce exactly one kind of parent enquiry. Because delivery is online, the match is made on syllabus fit rather than on which community the tutor lives in, so a family in Fujairah and a family in Jumeirah are choosing from the same specialists at the same rate.

sections.heading: Which board sets the dates, and why the centre's zone matters
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after working from the wrong one. That single rule explains a conversation UAE parents have every year: two cousins at different schools sitting the same paper at different times, and both schools being right.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, so any plan should be built from the board's live timetable rather than from a date copied onto a tutoring page and left there.

On the IB this page deliberately stops short. UAE schools sit the May session, and the November session exists as a second route. We are not publishing an IB examination or results date here, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unverified date is worse than none: a family that plans six weeks of revision around a wrong week has lost the six weeks. Ask the school's IB coordinator or read ibo.org directly. One thing is constant across all three boards. The IB exam entry deadline, like the Cambridge and Pearson ones, is set months before the first paper, and it is the school that submits entries, not the family.

sections.heading: Equivalency: the paperwork that follows the certificate
paragraphs: Equivalency is the Ministry of Education process that converts a foreign school certificate into something a UAE university or employer can act on, and it is the step families forget until results day has passed. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which surprises most parents.

For the American track the requirements are tests rather than subject counts. English proficiency is shown by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT; mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. One page currently ranking for these searches tells UAE candidates they must take six IGCSE subjects. The published rule is five. Getting that number right is worth more to a family than any amount of reassuring prose, and it is the kind of error that should make you check everything else on a page.

On the IB, this page publishes no figure at all. The source that sets out both the British and American tracks states no IB points threshold, so a Ministry of Education equivalency certificate requirement for the Diploma has to be confirmed on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before anyone plans around it. Two further points. Equivalency is not something IB Gram performs, submits or influences, and no tutoring is required for it. Any page suggesting that tuition smooths a regulatory process is selling urgency rather than teaching.

sections.heading: What to ask before the first paid lesson, and what we say when nobody is free
paragraphs: Five questions settle most of this. Which permit do you hold, and may I see the record? What is your teaching or subject qualification, from which institution, in which year? Which board and syllabus have you taught, and for how many cohorts? What will you not do with my child's internal assessment? And can the first session be built around a question from the current paper rather than an introduction? A tutor who has taught the course answers the fifth question with enthusiasm, because it is the part of the job they are good at. Hesitation there is more informative than any certificate.

The honest part most providers leave out is coverage. Some subject and level combinations have very few experienced teachers anywhere in the Emirates: Higher Level Physics, Computer Science, Economics HL in an exam term, and the smaller language B courses. When no UAE-resident specialist is available for the slot you need, we say so. The alternative we offer is an India-based IB specialist teaching the same syllabus over the same video link in the same Gulf Standard Time slot, and we tell you that is what is happening rather than hiding it behind a local-sounding phone number. If neither works, we will say that too.

One last thing, because enquiry forms about children collect more than people realise. We ask for the school, the programme, the subject, the level and the year group, because the match cannot be made without them. We do not need a photograph, a full report card or a medical history to arrange a trial lesson, and a provider asking for those without explaining why is worth a question. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on personal data protection sits behind this, and the privacy link on every page sets out what is kept and how to have it deleted.

If the subject is no longer where the problem is, we say so and change it. Pausing during exam weeks or travel is normal and does not cost anything.

whyPoints.description: We publish what can be evidenced and name what cannot. A permit, a qualification, a syllabus taught and a cohort count are checkable. A regulator's endorsement of a private tutor is not available in the UAE, from anybody, so you will not read it here. That distinction is the whole point of this page.

whyPoints.title: Regulator detail that matches your emirate
whyPoints.description: KHDA, ADEK, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge and the federal Ministry of Education each govern different schools. We tell you which one holds your school's file, what it actually approves, and which document to read before deciding tuition is the answer.

whyPoints.title: A firm line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question and give feedback on work the student has produced. No text is supplied, no file is edited, no coursework is produced on a student's behalf. A short written record of each session exists partly so that a coordinator's question about outside support can be answered with specifics.

whyPoints.description: Because lessons are delivered over live video, the pool is not limited to people who can reach your community before dinner. A family in Umm Al Quwain and a family in Dubai Marina choose from the same Higher Level specialists, and the travel cost that sits inside a visiting tutor's rate is simply absent.

whyPoints.description: Every figure on this page comes from a named source: the federal portal, KHDA documents, Cambridge and Pearson's own date publications, the Dubai media office. Where a number is not verifiable, including the IB session dates, we leave the space empty and say why rather than filling it with something plausible.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you commit
whyPoints.description: If no UAE-based specialist covers your subject, level and slot, you are told at the enquiry stage, along with the alternative and where the tutor would be teaching from. No local-sounding phone number, no office address in the Emirates that does not exist, and no pretence that every combination is always covered.

faqs.question: Is there such a thing as a certified IB tutor?
faqs.answer: Not as a single credential. The International Baccalaureate authorises schools to deliver its programmes and trains teachers who work inside them; it does not license private tutors, and neither does any UAE education authority. What exists instead is a bundle of separate things: a MoHRE private tuition work permit, a teaching qualification, a subject degree and documented experience of the syllabus your child sits. A provider using the phrase should be able to say which of those four they mean. If the answer is vague, the word is doing marketing work rather than describing a document somebody issued.

faqs.question: What qualification should a certified IB tutor actually hold?
faqs.answer: For Diploma teaching, look for a degree in the subject plus either a recognised teaching qualification or several cohorts of classroom experience with that exact course. The degree proves content depth beyond Higher Level. The teaching qualification proves training in how to explain things. Neither proves knowledge of IB command terms, published criteria or the way marks are allocated in that subject, which is why the cohort question matters most. Ask which board, which course, which years, and which option topics they have taught, then judge the answer in a working first session rather than on paper.

faqs.question: Which document proves a tutor may legally charge for lessons in the UAE?
faqs.answer: The private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The federal portal states it is granted free of charge for two years. Individuals offering private tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you see quoted online with caution. The permit covers legality, nothing more. It says nothing about subject knowledge, teaching skill or whether the person has ever seen an IB mark scheme.

faqs.question: Can a tutoring company describe itself as certified by a UAE authority?
faqs.answer: Only if it holds the specific permit it is referring to and can show it. The relevant one in Dubai is a KHDA Educational Services Permit, issued to a training institute with premises, with initial approval first, a six-month window to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal. A platform with no premises in the emirate cannot hold that permit. IB Gram does not hold it, operates no centre in the Emirates, and has no accreditation or partnership with KHDA, ADEK, the Sharjah authority, the Ministry of Education or any examination board.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a separate credential to teach the Diploma rather than IGCSE?
faqs.answer: No separate licence exists for either, which is exactly why the experience question carries the weight. The practical difference is large. IGCSE rewards coverage and clean examination technique across a two-year syllabus. The Diploma adds internal assessment with published criteria, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and papers written by the IB rather than the school. A tutor who has taught IGCSE for a decade may have never marked a Diploma investigation. Ask about the specific course and level, not the board, and ask what they would look at first in a weak draft.

faqs.question: If the specialist teaching my child is not resident in the UAE, what certification applies?
faqs.answer: The MoHRE permit regime applies to people providing private tutoring in the UAE, so a tutor resident elsewhere is working under the rules of the country they live and pay tax in. That is one reason we say plainly where a tutor is based rather than implying a local presence. For a family, the questions that then matter are qualification, syllabus experience and timing: lessons run over live video in Gulf Standard Time either way, and an India-based IB specialist teaching the same course is often the only way to cover a scarce Higher Level subject.

faqs.question: Is paying someone to proofread an Internal Assessment against the rules?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what proofreading means in practice, which is why the word is best avoided. A tutor may read work the student has written, ask questions about the method, point to the published criteria and say where a criterion is not being met. The student then makes changes themselves, in their own words. If somebody rewrites sentences, restructures paragraphs or returns a polished version ready to submit, that is no longer feedback and it puts the student's diploma at risk. The school's coordinator has to declare the work is the student's own.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need KHDA approval to teach Arabic or Islamic Education?
faqs.answer: The requirement sits on schools rather than on private tutors. KHDA requires schools to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate approval to teach those subjects, and that approval attaches to the post inside the school. A private tutor working with your child in the evening is in a different position, but a real constraint still applies to the content: for the mandatory subjects, using different or additional material without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited. So a tutor should be working from the school's own scheme, not a programme of their own design.

faqs.question: Why is lesson time for the mandatory UAE subjects counted in 40-minute units?
faqs.answer: Because that is the unit KHDA uses to calculate instructional time for Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Schools may vary the actual lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. For parents this explains a timetable oddity: two schools can meet the same requirement with very different-looking weeks, one with short daily lessons and one with longer blocks. It also explains why squeezing extra IB revision into the school day is not something a school can simply decide to do.

faqs.question: Which emirates have no education regulator of their own?
faqs.answer: Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Private schools in those three are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority, so there is no local inspection portal to browse the way Dubai families browse KHDA's. Dubai has KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. If your school sits with the Ministry, ask the school directly for its most recent report and for the board it enters candidates with.

faqs.question: Do the seven new private schools opening in Dubai for 2026-27 make a specialist easier to find?
faqs.answer: For admissions, yes. The 2026-27 intake adds seven schools, four following a UK curriculum and three offering the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened in 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. For tutoring, not in the short term. New schools recruit experienced Diploma teachers from the same pool every existing school draws on, so the number of people who have taught Higher Level Chemistry for several cohorts does not rise because a building opened. Scarcity of experience, not capacity, is what makes a specialist hard to book.

faqs.question: Does a tutor with more certification charge more per hour?
faqs.answer: Usually, though the market pays for scarcity rather than for paperwork. Published UAE rates run from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online and university-student tutors, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist, with named or examiner-level tutors advertised higher again. Those are figures published by other providers, not ours. A permit costs nothing to hold, so it adds nothing to a rate; a decade of marking Diploma investigations is what the upper band is actually paying for.

faqs.question: Can a tutor speak to my child's subject teacher or attend a school meeting?
faqs.answer: Only if you arrange it and the school agrees, and it is worth asking. A tutor who has read the school's own feedback works faster than one guessing from a report card. What a tutor should not do is approach the school independently, present themselves as part of your child's provision, or ask a teacher for material the school has not released. In Abu Dhabi there is a further wrinkle: ADEK's professional-ethics position bars school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, so that particular arrangement is not available.

faqs.question: What does the Ministry ask American-curriculum students for that it does not ask of IB students?
faqs.answer: The published American-track requirements are test scores rather than subject counts: English proficiency through a 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. The same published guidance sets out the British track as five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus an A-Level at E or two AS-Levels. It states no IB points threshold, so confirm the Diploma position on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: What should we have in writing before any money changes hands?
faqs.answer: Four things. The tutor's qualification and the awarding institution, the board and syllabus they have taught and for how many cohorts, their permit position, and what they will and will not do with assessed coursework. Add the practical terms: session length, the rate, what happens to a lesson cancelled at short notice, and who to contact if the match is wrong. The trial session comes before any of this costs you anything, covers one subject, and needs no payment details. If a provider will not put the first four in a message, that is the answer.

Tell us the school, the emirate, the subject and the level, and we will send the credential position in writing before anything is booked. intro.heading: What you are actually buying when you pay more for a certified IGCSE tutor
paragraphs: Nobody certifies IGCSE tutors. Cambridge International awards qualifications to candidates and accredits exam centres; Pearson does the same for its International GCSE. Neither body issues a licence to a private tutor, and no UAE authority issues a subject teaching certificate to one either. So when an advertisement in this market promises a certified IGCSE tutor in the UAE, it is pointing at something else: a teaching qualification earned abroad, a university degree in the subject, a professional development award, seasonal marking experience, or the one document UAE law genuinely requires, the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Each of those sits at a different point on the AED 45 to AED 650 an hour this market charges, and only some of them change what happens inside a lesson.

That is why this page is organised around money rather than badges. Private tutoring here runs on a permit: Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, MoHRE grants it free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications made through its smart app, website or e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without that permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, no amount belongs on this page.

The permit is the legal floor rather than a measure of teaching quality. It establishes that a person may lawfully charge for lessons in the UAE. It says nothing about whether they have taught Cambridge IGCSE 0580 at Extended tier, whether they can read a Paper 6 mark scheme aloud and explain why a correct answer scored zero, or whether they know that your daughter's school sets its coursework deadline ten weeks before the board does. Those are the things that move a grade, and none of them appears on a certificate. A family paying AED 250 an hour deserves to know which of them that money buys, which is what the tables below set out tier by tier.

Market rates read in October 2026 spread across five recognisable bands. Budget online tutoring starts low: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit higher, with Unitors publishing IGCSE rates from AED 150. A tutor who travels to a family costs AED 180 to 500 once travel is inside the price, on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table. Subject specialists run from AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. At the top of the market BartyED publishes AED 650 an hour. Each of those is that provider's own published figure rather than ours.

Teaching arranged through IB Gram is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school run, prayer times and the bus. Nobody is sent to a UAE address; home visits are a service we run only in India. That is a decision about supply, not about saving money. A family in Al Barsha choosing from everyone willing to drive to Al Barsha on a Tuesday evening is choosing from a very short list, and the list gets shorter the rarer the subject. A family choosing online one-to-one IGCSE lessons is choosing from every specialist free at that hour, which is how a Computer Science 0478 or Accounting 0452 request gets filled at all.
