sections.heading: Where the marks actually go: criteria, limits and weightings
paragraphs: Not one competitor page in this market names a single assessment criterion or its mark allocation. That is where the most useful conversation with a student starts, because a mark out of 20 that a student cannot break down is a mark they cannot improve. The IB publishes the criteria, the letters and the marks attached to each. A student who knows that personal engagement is worth three marks and use of mathematics is worth six will spend their last week on the right half of the document.

Take the Mathematics exploration, which is 20% of the grade in both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, at HL and SL alike. It carries five criteria: presentation worth four, mathematical communication worth four, personal engagement worth three, reflection worth three, and use of mathematics worth six, for twenty marks in total. Most Dubai students we see lose the bulk of their marks on reflection and personal engagement, not on the mathematics, because nobody told them those words have defined meanings in a rubric.

The sciences changed shape with the current guide: a single Scientific Investigation, assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each for twenty-four, inside a three-thousand-word limit. The failure mode is almost always criterion A. A research question that cannot be answered with equipment a school in Dubai actually has produces thin data, and thin data caps the other three criteria no matter how well the student writes.

The core components have hard limits that are worth taping to a desk: four thousand words for the Extended Essay, one thousand six hundred for the TOK essay, nine hundred and fifty for the exhibition commentary across three objects. Examiners stop reading at the limit. A student who writes five thousand words has not written more essay; they have written four thousand words of essay and a thousand words nobody will ever read.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an IA, EE or TOK essay
paragraphs: This is the part of the market that needs saying out loud. One site competing for these searches openly sells completed Internal Assessments for a four-figure sum in AED. That is not tutoring. It is academic misconduct under IB regulations, it puts a diploma at risk rather than a grade, and the student carries the consequence while the seller keeps the money. We will not do it, and no reputable tutor in Dubai will either.

The rules themselves are not vague. A student's coursework must be their own work, the supervisor signs an authenticity declaration, and the student declares the same. Help is permitted and expected: that is what a supervisor is for. What is not permitted is another person producing text, data, code or structure that then appears in the submitted work. The test a tutor should apply before every intervention is simple. Could the student have arrived at this themselves after the explanation, or did I hand it to them finished?

In practice this makes coursework sessions more useful rather than less. Reading a student's own draft against criterion C and explaining what critical thinking means in the rubric teaches something transferable. Supplying a paragraph teaches nothing and risks everything. The table below is the boundary we work to, and it is worth reading before you brief any tutor in Dubai, ours or anyone else's, because a tutor who offers to write it for you has told you what they are.

One practical consequence for families: keep the drafts. A student who can show the progression of their own work has an answer if authenticity is ever questioned, and version history in a document is the cheapest insurance available in a Diploma year.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency and attestation for Dubai's IB and IGCSE leavers
paragraphs: A qualification earned in Dubai is not automatically usable in Dubai. For a UAE university place, a government job or a professional licence, a student generally needs a certificate equivalency from the Ministry of Education, and the documents behind it have to be attested. Not one competitor page in this market mentions equivalency at all, which is a remarkable omission given that it is the administrative step most likely to delay a Dubai school leaver by a month at exactly the wrong time.

The requirements are published by the Ministry and they differ by curriculum, so check the current list on the Ministry's own smart services rather than relying on a tutoring site, including this one. The pattern is stable even when the detail moves. The British route is assessed on a minimum number of IGCSE or GCSE passes at specified grades together with AS and A Level results, with subject requirements attached. The IB route is assessed on the full Diploma rather than individual subject certificates, which is one more reason an E in TOK or the Extended Essay matters beyond the point total.

The work that takes time is not the application; it is collecting the paperwork in the right order while the school's registrar is still at their desk. Transcripts, transfer certificates and school stamps are far easier to obtain in May than in late July, and a name spelled differently on a passport and a certificate is a correction that takes weeks. Families who moved to Dubai mid-school should also chase the leaving certificate from the previous school at the point of leaving, not years later from another country.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural Studies alongside the IB
paragraphs: Every private school in Dubai teaches Ministry-mandated subjects next to its international curriculum, and almost no tutoring site mentions them. Arabic is compulsory, taught as a first language to Arabic-speaking students and as an additional language to everyone else, with the requirement continuing further up the school for Arabic speakers. Islamic Education is compulsory for Muslim students. Moral, Social and Cultural Studies, the framework that brought moral education and social studies together, runs for all students.

These subjects produce two distinct problems for IB and IGCSE families, and they need different answers. The first is a Diploma student with six subjects, the core, and two Ministry subjects timetabled on top, where the real constraint is hours in a week rather than ability in any one course. The second is a student who arrived in Dubai in Year 8 with no Arabic, placed in a class where most peers have had five years of it, and asked to be assessed alongside them.

Neither is solved by adding another tutored subject on top of a full timetable. The first is a scheduling problem: look at where the Ministry subjects sit in the week and protect the two evenings that are left for coursework rather than filling them. The second responds to short, frequent sessions on script, high-frequency vocabulary and reading fluency, which is a different teaching model from an hour a week on a Diploma subject.

Worth knowing for planning: these subjects appear on a Dubai school report and in inspection judgements, and Arabic attainment is reported separately for first-language and additional-language students in the KHDA inspection report. If a report shows Arabic as the weakest subject in a phase, that is a known pattern across the emirate rather than a verdict on your child, and it is usually a question of teaching time rather than aptitude.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the school calendar and when revision actually happens
paragraphs: A revision plan written without the UAE calendar in it will not survive contact with the year. Dubai private schools follow a unified academic calendar: a start in late August, a winter break around a fortnight in December, a spring break of similar length, and an end to the year in the first days of July. Those breaks are where intensive work actually fits, and they are also when families travel, so the useful conversation is which half of the break is being kept at home.

Ramadan matters more than any of it for an exam-year student. School days shorten during the holy month, timings move, energy patterns change completely, and the month shifts roughly eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar. Ramadan 1448 is expected to begin in mid-February 2027, subject to the moon sighting, which drops it directly onto the mock-examination and coursework-deadline window for anyone sitting the May 2027 IB exam session.

The practical answer is to move work rather than lose it. Coursework drafts should be finished before the month starts, because a student fasting through a school day will not produce their best four thousand words in it. Sessions during Ramadan work better after Iftar or early in the morning than at the usual 5pm slot, and because our lessons are online, moving a Dubai student's weekly hour to a post-Iftar time costs nothing more than finding a tutor whose own evening suits it. We schedule around it as a matter of course and ask families in January, not in week one of the month.

After Eid comes the compressed run to the papers. For a May candidate that is roughly six weeks, which is enough to fix technique and sharpen two or three topics and is not enough to learn a syllabus. Plan on that basis in October, and the February crunch is a busy month rather than a crisis.

process.title: Send the report, and the KHDA grade for the school
process.description: Start by sending your child's last school report, the marked script if you have one, and the subject-level judgements from the KHDA inspection report for the school. Those three documents tell us whether the problem is the class, the technique or a specific topic, which decides what kind of tutor you actually need.

process.title: A short diagnostic on the real paper
process.description: Before any plan, a tutor spends part of a first session on a question from the actual paper your child will sit, at the actual level. What they get wrong, and more usefully how they get it wrong, sorts the losses into content, command terms and timing. That sorting is the plan.

process.title: Matched by syllabus code and exam board
process.description: We match on the specifics: Analysis and Approaches HL rather than maths, Cambridge IGCSE 0580 Extended rather than IGCSE, Scientific Investigation rather than coursework. Because lessons are online, the match is made on who teaches that syllabus and is free in your slot, not on who can drive to your area by five.

process.title: A free trial, then a fixed weekly slot
process.description: The first session is a free trial so your child can decide whether this particular tutor is someone they will talk to. If the answer is no, say so and we match again; a student who will not ask a question has not got a tutor. After that, a fixed weekly slot on Gulf Standard Time.

process.title: Reviewed against the school's own calendar
process.description: Progress is checked against the next thing the school will actually assess, not against a generic timeline. When no specialist is free for a niche HL subject, we say so and give you an honest wait rather than offering a general tutor in the right-sounding subject.

whyPoints.title: The inspection report comes first
whyPoints.description: Most tuition decisions in Dubai are made from a worry rather than a document. We start from the KHDA inspection report and your child's marked work, because that is how you find out whether you are buying a specialist, an exam-technique coach, or nothing at all.

whyPoints.title: Rates you can check against the market
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are published by other people and attributed to them, so you can verify every line. Nobody else competing for these searches publishes a rate table in dirhams at all, and three of the main pages publish no price in any currency.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes, levels and boards, named
whyPoints.description: A match on 0580 Extended with a non-calculator Paper 2 is a different job from a match on 4MA1 Higher, and Analysis and Approaches HL is not Applications and Interpretation SL. Every match is made on the code and level your child is entered for, and we tell you which tutor examines what.

whyPoints.title: The coursework line in writing
whyPoints.description: Our tutors mark a student's own draft against the published criteria and explain what the next band needs. They do not write, edit or supply work for submission. The boundary is on this page so you can hold us to it, and so you can ask the same question of anyone else you consider.

whyPoints.title: One timezone, no commute
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so a session begins at the minute it was booked and moves the same evening when a school fixture gets in the way. No part of your fee pays for Sheikh Zayed Road at six o'clock.

faqs.question: What is KHDA and how does it rate private schools in Dubai?
faqs.answer: KHDA is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the regulator for private education in Dubai. It inspects every private school in the emirate each year and publishes the report. Schools are judged against six performance standards, including students' achievement, teaching and assessment, and leadership, each graded on a six-point scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Good is the standard Dubai expects, so Acceptable is the floor rather than a middling result. Inside students' achievement, the report grades attainment and progress separately for each phase and subject, which is the level of detail worth reading before you hire anyone.

faqs.question: My child's school is rated Very Good, so does tuition make any sense?
faqs.answer: Often yes, for a reason the headline band hides. A school rated Very Good overall can be graded lower in one subject in one phase, because a band summarises six standards across the whole school and your child sits in one class. Read the subject-level judgements for your child's phase rather than the headline, and compare them. If Mathematics is graded below English in the same phase, the class is more likely to be the constraint than your child is. If every subject is strong, the honest answer is usually that the gap is homework discipline or one unfixed topic, not teaching.

faqs.question: What is the difference between attainment and progress in a Dubai inspection report?
faqs.answer: Attainment measures how students perform against the standards of the curriculum they follow. Progress measures how far they have moved from their own starting points. The combination is what tells you something. Good attainment with weaker progress describes a capable cohort being carried rather than stretched, which is the pattern that quietly costs a bright student a 7. Weaker attainment with strong progress describes a group climbing fast, where patience often beats intervention. Read both grades for your child's subject and phase, then test the pattern against the last piece of marked work that came home.

faqs.question: How much do IB and IGCSE tutors charge per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai, as published by other providers, run from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online or university-student tutors, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for a tutor travelling to a home with the drive priced in, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist. Named or examiner-level tutors are published as high as AED 650. Those are market figures attributed to the providers who published them, not our price list; our own rate depends on subject, level and tutor, and starts with a free trial.

faqs.question: Is online tuition actually cheaper than hiring a home tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Usually, and the saving is structural rather than a discount. A rate for a tutor travelling to a Dubai address has the drive built into it, which is why published home-visit rates sit around AED 180 to 500 while online specialist rates sit around AED 150 to 300. You also stop paying for time nobody teaches in. The bigger difference is not price: a visiting tutor has to come from whoever can reach your area, while an online match comes from whoever teaches your child's exact syllabus. For HL subjects in Dubai, that is the difference that moves a grade.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit to teach?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and every regulatory source we checked states that the permit itself carries no fee. Residents who are employed elsewhere generally need their employer's consent as part of the application, and tutoring at a scale that becomes a business needs a proper licence instead. Ask any tutor you are considering whether they hold a current permit. A tutor who cannot answer that question clearly has told you something about how they operate, whatever their subject knowledge looks like.

faqs.question: Should a quoted hourly rate in Dubai include VAT, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Ask, in writing, before the first invoice. UAE VAT registration becomes mandatory once taxable turnover passes AED 375,000 a year, so some tutors and agencies are registered and charge it, and others are below the threshold and do not. That means two quotes of the same number can mean two different final costs. Request a written statement of whether the rate is inclusive or exclusive, and ask for a tax invoice if the provider is registered. The same question applies to monthly packages, where the number of contact hours is often the detail that is quietly left out.

faqs.question: When are the IB and IGCSE exam sessions that Dubai students actually sit?
faqs.answer: Dubai IB candidates sit the May session, with the IB's candidate registration deadline falling in mid-November beforehand and results released in early July. A November session exists and is used mainly for retakes. Cambridge IGCSE runs a June series, with centre entries closing in late February and results in mid-August, and a November series with results in mid-January. Edexcel International GCSE adds a January series, with results in early March. Your school sets its own internal entry deadline weeks before the board's, so the exams officer is the person to ask for the dates that actually bind you.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Internal Assessment without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards, pressure-test whether a research question can be answered with reachable data, mark a student's own draft against the published criteria, and say what the next band needs. A tutor may not write, rewrite or edit text that appears in the submitted work, supply a dataset or a bibliography, or hand over a topic as a finished package. Coursework carries an authenticity declaration signed by both student and supervisor. Keep the drafts: version history is the simplest evidence that the work progressed from your child's own hands.

faqs.question: How many marks is the IB Mathematics exploration worth, and where are they lost?
faqs.answer: The exploration is 20% of the grade in both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, at HL and SL, and it is marked out of twenty across five criteria: presentation four, mathematical communication four, personal engagement three, reflection three, and use of mathematics six. Students who lose marks rarely lose them on mathematics. They lose them on reflection and personal engagement, because those phrases have defined meanings in the rubric that nobody explained, and on communication, where notation drifts between sections. Reading the criteria with a tutor before writing is worth more than editing afterwards.

faqs.question: What is MoE equivalency and when should a Dubai family start it?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is the Ministry of Education's recognition of a foreign qualification for use in the UAE, needed for most local university places, government roles and professional licences. The requirements differ by curriculum and are published on the Ministry's smart services, so check them there rather than on any tutoring site. The British route is assessed on IGCSE or GCSE passes together with AS and A Level results; the IB route is assessed on the full Diploma rather than individual certificates. Start collecting transcripts and stamps in the term before you need them, while the school registrar is still available.

faqs.question: Do Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies still apply if my child does the IB?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private schools in Dubai teach Ministry-mandated subjects alongside their international curriculum, whatever the programme. Arabic is compulsory, as a first language for Arabic speakers and as an additional language for everyone else, and Islamic Education is compulsory for Muslim students. Moral, Social and Cultural Studies runs for all students. For a Diploma candidate this is usually a timetable problem rather than an academic one: six subjects plus the core plus Ministry subjects leaves fewer free evenings than families assume, so protect the ones that remain for coursework rather than booking them.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to a post-Iftar time during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we plan for it rather than reacting to it. School days shorten during Ramadan and the usual late-afternoon slot stops working, so we move sessions to after Iftar or to early morning. Because lessons are delivered online, moving a Dubai student's weekly hour needs only a tutor whose own evening suits the new time, with no travel to rearrange. The more important piece is sequencing: Ramadan 1448 is expected to begin in mid-February 2027, which lands on mock season, so coursework drafts should be finished before the month starts.

faqs.question: Which maths route should my child take, Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: It depends on the degree, and the decision is made in Year 11 rather than in DP1. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic, proof-heavy route and is what engineering, mathematics, physics and most economics programmes expect at Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics with technology throughout, and suits business, design, social sciences and life sciences. Check the entry requirements of specific universities your child is likely to apply to, including UAE institutions, before choosing. A strong IGCSE Extended grade keeps the Analysis and Approaches HL option open; a mid grade effectively closes it.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for my child's subject and level?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we give you a realistic wait. Niche combinations genuinely run short at peak times, with HL Chemistry, HL Economics and Paper 3 work the usual pressure points in Dubai between January and April. The dishonest move would be to offer a general science tutor for HL Chemistry and hope you do not notice until the third session. Instead you get the actual position, an estimate of when a specialist frees up, and, when it helps, a shorter diagnostic session with someone who can at least sort the lost marks into categories while you wait.

faqs.question: How do online lessons work if the tutor is not in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Lessons run over live video, one to one, with a shared screen and a digital whiteboard. Timing is set in Gulf Standard Time, so a 6pm Dubai slot is a 6pm Dubai slot regardless of where the tutor sits, and most sessions are booked from 5pm once the school bus has arrived. Work happens on the real paper: a past paper opens on screen, both people annotate it, and the file is still there the following week. Written notes follow each session saying what was covered and what comes next, which is also what makes a handover possible if a tutor ever changes.

dubai.closingHeading: Read the report, then decide what you are buying
dubai.closingBody: The useful order for a Dubai family is almost always the same. Read the KHDA inspection report for your child's school and find the subject-level judgements for their phase. Ask the subject teacher which topics lost marks in the last timed assessment. Then decide whether you need a specialist for an HL paper, a technique coach for exam conditions, or a plan rather than a tutor. If one of the first two is the answer, send us the marked script and the report and we will match on the syllabus code and level your child is actually entered for, with a free trial lesson first, delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

experienced-ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are tutors currently teaching IB subjects for UAE families. Read the line that says which syllabus and which level they last taught, and which session that cohort sat. That line, rather than a number of years, is what tells you whether the experience matches the paper your child is sitting.

intro.heading: Experience, measured against the system your child studies inside
paragraphs: Parents who search for an experienced IB tutor in the UAE are usually trying to filter out one specific risk: paying for somebody who knows the subject but not the examination. Those are different jobs. A graduate chemist can explain redox clearly. Only somebody who has taught the Diploma version of redox to several cohorts knows that the marks sit in the state symbols and the balanced half-equations, and that a student who explains it fluently out loud can still lose four marks in writing. Experience, in this market, means experience of where marks are awarded.

In the UAE a second layer sits above that. Your child's school is licensed and inspected by a body that depends on the emirate. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge does the same in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah those authorities approve fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so they reach further than an inspection grade. A tutor who has worked here knows which body holds your school's file, and therefore which documents you can reasonably ask the school to show you.

A third layer surprises families who have moved from Europe or South Asia. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and the federal position is that private schools must cover Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies whatever else they offer. Those lessons take up real timetable minutes beside Higher Level maths and the Extended Essay. An experienced tutor plans the week around them rather than discovering them in March.

The supply problem behind this search is arithmetical. Dubai's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37% of the roll, Indian at 26%, American at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. The Diploma is a minority programme inside a very large market, and Higher Level sciences and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches are a minority inside that minority. Seven new private schools open in Dubai for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. Places are being added faster than experienced Diploma teachers are.

That is why IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video rather than sending anybody to an address in the Emirates. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Online delivery is not a compromise on the promise in this page's title; it is the only way a family in Mirdif or Mirfa reaches the person who has taught their exact paper, instead of the best-qualified adult inside a twenty-minute drive. Sessions are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school run and prayer times, and move to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan.

The rest of this page is written to be used rather than admired. It sets out how to count a tutor's experience, what the emirate regulators control, which kinds of experience evidence what, how diagnosis differs from more practice papers, what the market charges and who published those numbers, and where the line sits between teaching a student's coursework and producing it.

experienced-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: An experienced tutor treats the four IB programmes as four different jobs, because the assessment model changes at each stage. A Primary Years student needs the habits that survive the move into subject teaching. A Diploma student needs marks in named components by a dated deadline. The notes below say what each programme asks of a UAE family in particular.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three usually at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries internally assessed work marked by the teacher and moderated externally, and externally marked papers that decide most of the grade. Experience here means knowing how a component weighting converts into a revision plan: time spent on a paper worth 35% is not interchangeable with time spent on one worth 20%.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, and a smaller number of candidates sit November. Registration and internal coursework deadlines are set months before either window, by the school rather than by the tutor. A tutor who has run two-year plans here already knows that the heaviest coursework weeks collide with mock season and, in some years, with Ramadan.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against published criteria, with a Personal Project in the final year. Marks come in criterion bands rather than percentages, which is why a parent can see 6 out of 8 on one criterion and 3 out of 8 on another in the same report and have no idea which to worry about. Experienced teaching here is largely translation: turning criterion language into a specific thing the student does differently next week.
programmes.countryNote: Many UAE schools run the MYP only to Year 10 or 11 and then move students into the Diploma, which makes the Year 11 to DP1 summer the single most useful tutoring window in the whole programme. Families who move between emirates mid-programme often find criterion reporting styles differ between schools even under the same authority.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led units with no external examination, which makes a weak maths or literacy foundation easy to miss until secondary school. Useful support at this stage is quiet and specific: number facts, place value, sentence structure, reading stamina. There is no syllabus code to teach to, so experience shows in whether the tutor can name the gap in one sentence and give the parent something measurable to watch over four weeks.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons begin in the primary years, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Non-Arab families often meet Arabic as an additional language here for the first time and need to know which stream their child sits in.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is offered by relatively few schools in the region, so tutors with genuine experience of it are rarer than tutors with experience of the Diploma. If a school offers it, ask who in the tutoring market has supported the reflective project before, because its requirements are not the Extended Essay's.
programmes.countryNote: Because the route is uncommon locally, a UAE family choosing it should check how the certificate will be presented for Ministry of Education equivalency and for the universities on their list, and verify that with the attestation authority rather than with a tutoring company.

experienced-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: Experience is subject-shaped, not general. The notes below say what each course actually assesses and where UAE students most often lose marks, so you can judge whether a tutor's stated experience lines up with the paper your child is sitting rather than with the subject's name.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof-heavy route, and the one most competitive university courses expect. Higher Level adds a third paper built on extended problems rather than recall. Marks go missing in method communication: a correct answer with no visible working scores less than a wrong answer with a clear method. Experienced teaching here spends time on how an answer is written, not only on whether it is right.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led work, with heavy graphical calculator use. Students who chose it to avoid proof often underestimate the data handling at Higher Level. The usual failure is treating a modelling question as arithmetic and never interpreting the result in context, which is where the marks sit. Route choice between AA and AI should be checked against the entry requirements of the actual universities on the list.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields reward precise definitions; the data-based questions reward reading a graph rather than remembering an equation. Higher Level depth is where Standard Level habits break. The scientific investigation is marked against published criteria, and students lose marks for a weak research question long before anything goes wrong with the data. Online sessions use shared screens for working, which suits physics well.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium carry the most marks and the most confusion. Papers punish loose notation: missing state symbols, unbalanced half-equations and answers given to the wrong number of significant figures. Higher Level adds depth rather than breadth, so a student who is secure at Standard Level can still be a long way from a Higher Level grade without targeted work on the extra content.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content volume is the trap. Students who revise by rereading notes do well in class tests and badly in papers, because the questions ask for application to unfamiliar contexts and for command terms answered exactly. Experienced teaching trains the difference between describing a process and explaining it, and keeps the internally assessed investigation moving while the syllabus is still being taught.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks that prose cannot recover. Higher Level adds quantitative work that surprises students who chose the subject as an essay subject. The internally assessed commentaries need current articles and genuine theory applied to them, not a summary of the news. UAE students often write strong evaluation and still lose marks for an unlabelled axis or a missing definition.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with tools that must be applied rather than described. The common pattern is a student who can define every acronym and cannot use one on an unseen company. Higher Level questions demand sustained evaluation with a judgement actually made. Marks are also lost to answers that ignore the command term and write everything the student knows about the topic.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis under time pressure, plus oral and written components built on the student's own chosen texts. The usual gap is technique spotting without argument: a list of devices with no claim about meaning. Experienced teaching here works on the thesis sentence and on how an oral is structured, because the student is assessed on a performance that cannot be redrafted.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: A language-acquisition course that many UAE students take alongside English-medium schooling, which makes level choice genuinely difficult. Receptive skills are tested on authentic texts, and productive skills on text types with conventions that must be obeyed. Marks go missing when a student writes a good essay in the wrong text type, or ignores audience and purpose in the task instruction.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.levels: Ab initio, B SL and B HL
subjects.description: The subject most often sat alongside the mandatory school Arabic lesson, and the one families least expect to need support with. Progress depends on script fluency and on vocabulary built for the assessed text types. In Dubai, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, so knowing which stream a child is in matters before any support is planned.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Theory assessed on paper, plus a solution developed by the student. Students who code confidently still lose marks on paper questions about algorithms, data structures and systems design, because the written answer has conventions of its own. Higher Level adds abstract data structures and a case study that has to be read early rather than skimmed in the final term.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition, both assessed against published criteria and both capable of moving the final points total through the core. Students treat it as an opinion piece; it is an argument with examples that have to do work. Support here is strictly discussion and feedback on the student's own drafts, which is also what the honesty rules require.

experienced-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: This is a federal market with seven different school-system experiences inside it. The notes below say what changes about finding experienced Diploma support depending on where a family lives, because the regulator, the number of IB schools and the realistic session time are not the same in Dubai as in Fujairah.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The deepest IB market in the country and the one with the most published data: 227 private schools and 17 curricula in 2024-25, with the IB at 7% of the roll. Depth of market does not mean depth in your subject, because three of the seven schools opening for 2026-27 are IB and recruit from the same teacher pool.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation here, and its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. That single rule removes the most obvious local option for many families, which is why experienced support is usually found outside the school rather than inside it.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, but with far fewer IB schools than the island, so Higher Level cohorts can be very small. A student may be one of three or four taking a Higher Level science, which limits how much in-class differentiation is possible and makes one-to-one work on paper technique more valuable than more content coverage.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education here and approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Many families commute to schools in Dubai, so the realistic start time for a weekday session is later than a Dubai-resident family's, and two shorter sessions often work better than one long one.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority, so the inspection vocabulary a parent reads differs from Dubai's. IB provision is thin locally and several families travel to Sharjah or Dubai, which makes evening scheduling the binding constraint on any tutoring plan.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education and approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Distance from the Dubai school belt is the practical issue: a visiting specialist in a niche Higher Level subject is close to unobtainable, while a live video session with one costs the same here as anywhere else in the country.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under federal Ministry of Education supervision, on the east coast and separated from the main school corridor by the mountains. Cohorts are small, subject choice at Higher Level is limited by what the school can staff, and travel time makes in-person arrangements with a subject specialist impractical rather than merely expensive.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: The smallest private-school market in the federation, also supervised by the Ministry of Education. Families here tend to be choosing between a local school and a commute, and the tutoring question is usually about covering a subject the nearest school cannot staff rather than about topping up a subject it teaches well.

schoolClusters.note: Students we support attend IB schools across the emirate, from Emirates Hills and Al Barsha to Dubai Festival City and Mirdif. The practical difference between them, for a tutoring plan, is which Higher Level subjects each actually runs in a given year and when internal coursework deadlines fall, both of which the school publishes to parents.

ADEK's school file and its staff ethics rules shape the options here more than anything else. Families typically want a specialist outside the school for a Higher Level subject, scheduled after a long school run, and want it to survive a move between Khalifa City, the island and Al Ain without changing tutor.

Three different regulators cover this stretch: SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Smaller IB cohorts are the norm, so the gap a tutor is asked to fill is more often subject coverage than exam polish.

experienced-ib-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways of working cover almost every request a UAE family makes of an experienced tutor. All three run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The difference between them is how much of the year they occupy and what the tutor is being asked to carry.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one across the year
modes.description: One or two sessions a week in the same subject with the same tutor, following the school's sequence and arriving at the exam with the content already consolidated. This is the pattern in which a tutor's experience compounds, because they see the same student's errors repeat and can name the cause rather than the symptom. It also absorbs the school's internal deadlines without a scramble.

modes.description: A defined number of sessions in the weeks before a session, built around past-paper technique, command terms and timing per mark. It is the right purchase when the content is largely known and the marks are being lost in the writing. It is the wrong purchase when a whole unit is missing, because no amount of paper practice will teach content that was never covered.

sections.heading: Experience in the Diploma is counted in cohorts, not calendar years
paragraphs: Ask a tutoring company how experienced its tutors are and you will usually be told a number of years. That number is nearly useless on its own, because the Diploma runs on a two-year cycle and the unit of experience is the completed cohort: a group taken from subject choice through the internal assessment and the mocks to the papers and the results. Two years of teaching can mean one DP1 group and one DP2 group who were never the same students, which is not the same as having followed one set of students all the way through.

The second thing to count is sessions sat. UAE schools sit the May session, and a smaller number of candidates sit November. A tutor who has taught for five years has seen four or five May sessions if the teaching was continuous and in the same programme, and possibly none at all if those years were spent on IGCSE or on a national curriculum. Years spent teaching a subject at a different level are real experience of the subject and no experience at all of the assessment your child faces.

The third is variation. Ten years in one school means ten years under one coordinator's internal deadlines, one reporting style and one exam centre's arrangements. That is deep experience of a single setting. A tutor who has worked across schools and emirates has seen different internal deadlines, different inspection vocabularies and the practical fact that two students sitting the same qualification can be on different timetables because their centres sit in different administrative zones. Both kinds of experience are useful; they answer different questions, and it is worth knowing which one you are buying.

sections.heading: A growing school sector does not grow experienced Diploma teachers at the same rate
paragraphs: The published numbers for Dubai explain why experienced Diploma teaching is scarce even in a market this large. In 2024-25 the emirate had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula. The UK curriculum accounted for 37% of the roll, Indian for 26%, American for 14% and the International Baccalaureate for 7%. Most private-school teachers in the emirate therefore work in a system that is not the Diploma, and a parent who assumes that a large school market implies a deep Diploma bench is reasoning from the wrong number.

Growth makes it tighter rather than looser. Seven new private schools open in Dubai for 2026-27, four following the UK curriculum and three the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. Six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. Three new IB schools have to staff Diploma classes from the same pool everybody else recruits from, and experienced teachers move between schools when they do. For a family, that shows up as a change of subject teacher in DP2, which is the worst year in which to have one.

There is one number moving the other way. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, under an economic incentives package the emirate valued at AED 1.5 billion. A fixed school bill is the one part of an education budget a family can plan around, which makes it a sensible anchor for deciding what, if anything, to spend on tutoring and when to spend it.

sections.heading: Experience of one emirate is not experience of all seven
paragraphs: Private schools in the UAE are not regulated by a single body, and the differences are substantive rather than administrative. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, which includes Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah and the Department of Knowledge does so in Ras Al Khaimah, and both of those bodies approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

That last point is worth sitting with. In two emirates the regulator signs off the assessment methods a school uses, not only the quality of its teaching. A parent in Sharjah or Ras Al Khaimah can therefore ask the school which methods have been approved for their child's year group, and a tutor who has worked in those emirates will know that this is a reasonable question rather than an awkward one. In Abu Dhabi, the relevant local knowledge is different again: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school.

This matters for the search you are running because it determines what good advice sounds like. A tutor whose whole career was in Dubai may describe inspection in KHDA's vocabulary to a family whose school is supervised federally, where that vocabulary does not apply. The useful test is simple: ask which authority holds your school's file and what that authority controls. An experienced tutor will name the body, say what it approves, and point you at the authority's own published material rather than paraphrasing it.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from any of these bodies, and no tutoring company that is not a licensed training institute with premises should imply otherwise. What we do is name the right regulator and explain what it governs.

sections.heading: Teaching, assessing and tutoring are three different kinds of experience
paragraphs: The word experience is doing at least four jobs in this market, and separating them is most of the work of choosing well. Classroom experience is experience of pacing a syllabus for thirty students and meeting a coordinator's deadlines. Assessment experience is experience of how a criterion is applied rather than how it reads. Tutoring experience is experience of diagnosing one student quickly and teaching to their gaps. Experience of the UAE system is experience of regulators, mandatory subjects, zones and equivalency. A tutor can have a great deal of one and almost none of another.

We do not describe tutors as examiners for a board, because current examining status is something a provider would have to be able to evidence and most of the market cannot. There is also a boundary that matters more than the label: assessment experience tells you how marks are awarded, and it gives nobody access to unreleased papers, mark schemes or grade boundaries. Any suggestion otherwise should end the conversation. The honest version of the claim is narrow and still valuable: somebody who has applied a criterion repeatedly can tell your child what the criterion actually requires in writing.

The practical move is to ask questions whose answers cannot be improvised. Which topic did your last cohort lose the most marks on, and why? What do you do in the first forty minutes with a new student? What does a strong criterion-B response contain that a middling one does not? How would the plan change if my child dropped from Higher to Standard Level? Vague answers to those questions are not a sign of modesty.

sections.heading: Experience shows up as topic-level diagnosis, not as more past papers
paragraphs: The clearest difference between an experienced tutor and a capable graduate appears in the first session with a real script in front of them. A capable graduate sees a wrong answer and reteaches the topic. An experienced teacher sees a pattern and asks a diagnostic question, because the same wrong answer has several different causes and each one needs a different fix. Rounding errors, a calculator left in radians, a misread command term and a genuinely missing concept all look identical in a mark total.

This is where more past papers stop helping. Papers are a measuring instrument. Doing another one tells you that the student is still losing marks; it does not tell you why, and a student who does five papers a week without analysis simply rehearses the same errors with increasing confidence. The useful sequence is narrow and repetitive: find the cause, teach the specific thing, then test the same question type cold a week later to see whether the fix held.

Diagnosis is also what makes an honest conversation about timing possible. If a student is losing marks on command terms, six weeks is plenty of time to change the outcome, because command-term discipline can be taught quickly and rehearsed. If a whole unit was never covered, six weeks is a different proposition and a family deserves to be told so before they pay for it. An experienced tutor will tell you which of those two situations you are in after reading the work, not after ten sessions.

sections.heading: The subjects an experienced tutor already knows are on the timetable
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum in Dubai private schools, and the federal position is that private schools must cover Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies whatever curriculum they otherwise follow. KHDA's requirements on these subjects were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 as the equivalent point for schools whose year begins in April. A tutor who has worked here does not need to be told that these lessons exist.

The rules around them are specific, and they limit what any outside tutor can properly do. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language is used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Schools are also required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

Two further details change how a week can be planned. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and the guidance advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run for at least 25 minutes. For these subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is prohibited. The honest consequence is that an outside tutor supports a student's understanding and their work for the school's own course; they do not substitute a syllabus of their own.

For a Diploma family the practical point is time. These lessons occupy timetable minutes that a revision plan has to work around, and a tutor who ignores them will propose a week that does not exist. Ask which Arabic stream your child is in before anything is scheduled.

sections.heading: The questions an experienced tutor asks in DP1 because the equivalency office will ask them later
paragraphs: Ministry of Education equivalency is the step that decides whether a school-leaving certificate is recognised for use in the UAE, and it is routinely discovered late. An experienced tutor working with a UAE family raises it in the first year, not the last term, because the documents come from different bodies on different timetables and because some of the requirements can only be satisfied by sitting a test that has to be booked in advance.

The British-track requirements were set out publicly in July 2026: a student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That last clause is where a competitor page has gone wrong by telling UAE candidates they need six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five, excluding those two.

For the American track the same reporting set out English proficiency as a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in SAT Math before applying. For the IB Diploma we publish no points threshold at all, because we have not read one on an official Ministry page and an unsourced number in this position is worse than no number. Verify it on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority, and treat any tutoring company that quotes one without a source with suspicion. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring company performs, guarantees or speeds up, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

sections.heading: The boundary an experienced tutor has already been asked to cross
paragraphs: Every tutor who has worked in this market for any length of time has been asked, politely and usually late at night, to do slightly more than teach. The internal assessment is due on Sunday, the student is struggling, and the parent would like the tutor to tidy it up. The answer has to be the same every time, and knowing how to give that answer without losing the family is itself a form of experience. The reason is not squeamishness. Work that must be the student's own is declared as the student's own by the student and their school, and a breach is an academic-honesty matter that can cost a diploma.

There is a market for the other thing. A page found in this research sells finished internal assessments at AED 3,750. That is a service we will not provide at any price, and the practical risk to a family is not the money. Submitted work that is not the student's own exposes the student to a malpractice finding at the point where the qualification is being awarded, which is the worst possible moment for it to surface.

What a tutor may properly do is substantial, and families often underestimate it. A tutor can explain what each criterion asks for and how many marks hang on it. They can interrogate a research question until it is answerable with the data a school can actually collect. They can read a draft the student has written and say which criterion is weak and why. They can teach the statistics, the lab technique or the referencing convention. They can ask the questions a supervisor asks, and they can tell a student that a section is not yet good enough without rewriting it for them.

The distinction holds for papers too. We reference official syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes and point to where a board publishes them; we do not reproduce or supply those materials. Both halves of that position come from the same place: the student's work and the board's material belong to the student and the board, not to the tutor.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges for experience, and what each band actually buys
paragraphs: Three of the six pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. The figures below are other providers' published rates, read in October 2026, with the provider named. They are the market, not our price list. We publish them because a parent cannot judge whether an hourly rate is reasonable without knowing the bands, and because the relationship between price and experience in this market is real but loose.

Budget online tuition runs from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between about AED 150 and 300; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A visiting tutor at a UAE address runs higher, between roughly AED 180 and 500, with Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table putting in-home work at AED 180 to 350 and some home tutors at AED 200 to 500. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level work sits around AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650. Monthly packages appear too: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

The useful question is what moves a rate inside those bands. Level does, because Higher Level in a scarce subject has fewer people able to teach it. Scarcity of the subject itself does, which is why a Higher Level Physics or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches specialist is harder to book than an English one. Format does, because travel is paid for whether or not it appears as a line on the invoice. Time of year does, because demand rises as a session approaches. Years of experience correlate with price less tightly than any of those, which is precisely why the number of years is a poor thing to buy on.

IB Gram does not publish a rate card on this page. What we do publish is the market, the fact that the first lesson is a free trial with no payment taken beforehand and no obligation to continue, and a quoted figure in AED in writing before anything is booked.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor against live online, when experience is the scarce thing
paragraphs: Searches for an experienced IB tutor in the UAE are often really searches for somebody who will arrive at the door. That is a reasonable thing to want and a real market: the published in-home band runs from roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, and monthly in-home packages of four two-hour visits appear at AED 1,599 to 1,799. The honest answer is that IB Gram does not provide it anywhere in the Emirates. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and no page of ours will tell a UAE family otherwise.

The case for online delivery here is not about convenience. It is about what a distance filter does to a pool that is already thin. Requiring a tutor to be physically present at a given address at 5pm on a Tuesday selects for adults who live nearby and are free then. Requiring that they have taught Higher Level Physics through several cohorts selects for a much smaller group, scattered across the country and beyond it. You can satisfy one condition or the other. For common subjects the two groups overlap enough that it hardly matters; for Higher Level sciences, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, Economics at Higher Level or a less-taught language, they barely overlap at all.

The arithmetic of time favours online too, in a way that shows up in the plan rather than the invoice. A visiting arrangement bundles travel into the evening at both ends, which pushes families towards one long weekly session. Live video makes two shorter sessions a week practical, and for consolidation work two thirty-minute contacts usually beat one ninety-minute block. Rescheduling behaves differently as well: a missed slot can move within the same week rather than waiting for the tutor's route to come round again.

Where in-person genuinely wins is with a young child who needs an adult in the room, or a student who cannot work independently on a screen. We say so rather than arguing against it. The table sets out what changes between the two arrangements when the thing you are buying is experience.
