sections.heading: When nobody with that experience is free, and what we say instead
paragraphs: No provider in the researched set discloses a coverage limit, which is a strange silence in a market where niche Higher Level subjects plainly outnumber the people able to teach them. Our position is to say it plainly. Some requests cannot be matched immediately, and the common ones are predictable: Higher Level Physics and Chemistry in exam term, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, a less widely taught language, Computer Science at Higher Level, and any request for a specific weekday slot between four and six in the afternoon Gulf Standard Time, which is when most of the country wants a lesson.

When that happens there are four honest options and we will tell you which apply. A different slot with the right specialist, often earlier or later in the same week. A short wait, with a date rather than a vague assurance. A generalist who can hold the content while the specialist slot opens, described as exactly that and not dressed up as a specialist. Or nothing from us, with the reason stated, which is better than an unsuitable match billed at a specialist rate.

What we will not do is put a tutor in front of your child on the basis that they are free. A mismatch costs more than the fee: it costs the weeks during which the real problem went undiagnosed, and in DP2 those weeks are not recoverable. This is also why the first lesson is a trial, with no payment taken before it and no obligation afterwards. The trial exists so that the diagnosis arrives before the commitment, and so that a family who was told their child's problem is command terms can hear whether the tutor reaches the same conclusion from the same script.

If the match turns out to be wrong after a few sessions, say so and we will change it. Judging a tutor on one session is unfair to both sides; judging them on a term is expensive. Three or four sessions is usually enough to see whether the diagnosis was right and whether the student is doing something differently as a result.

process.title: Tell us the school, the subject and the component
process.description: The school tells us which authority holds its file and which internal deadlines apply. The subject and level tell us who could teach it. The component tells us what the work is: a Higher Level paper, an internal assessment criterion, a command-term problem. Those three facts are what turn a request into a match rather than a referral to whoever is free.

process.title: Send recent work rather than a description of it
process.description: A marked script, a report or a draft is worth more than a summary of how things are going. Experienced tutors read scripts for patterns: rounding, units, command terms, blank final parts, criterion losses. The diagnosis that comes out of twenty minutes with real work is what the trial lesson is then built around, so the first session starts at the problem.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson before paying anything
process.description: The first lesson is a trial, with no payment taken beforehand and no obligation to continue. Watch for one thing: does the tutor name the cause of the lost marks and give your child something specific to do differently? A pleasant hour of revision is not a diagnosis. You will have a figure in AED in writing before any paid session is booked.

process.title: Agree a plan with dates attached to it
process.description: A plan should name the component, the sessions per week, what the first four weeks will cover and which of your school's deadlines it is built around. Ramadan slots, mock weeks and the exam block go in at this point rather than being absorbed later. If the time available is too short to change the outcome, this is where you should be told.

process.title: Review after three or four sessions, and change the match if it is wrong
process.description: Three or four sessions is long enough to see whether the diagnosis held and whether the student is working differently. We would rather change the tutor at that point than let a mismatch run to the end of term. Tell us what is not working and the next match is made on that information rather than on availability.

whyPoints.title: Experience quoted in cohorts and sessions
whyPoints.description: You will be told which syllabus and level a tutor last taught, and which session that cohort sat, instead of a round number of years. That is the information that tells you whether the experience matches your child's paper, and it is specific enough to be wrong, which is why most of this market avoids giving it.

whyPoints.title: The regulator named correctly for your emirate
whyPoints.description: KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Department of Knowledge and the federal Ministry govern different schools and different things. We name the one that holds your school's file and say what it controls. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from any of them and says so, which is more than several pages in this search can claim.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure attributed and dated
whyPoints.description: The rates on this page are other providers' published numbers, read in October 2026, with the provider named. We do not present them as ours and we do not invent a median. Three of the six competitor pages in this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in a currency UAE families do not pay in.

whyPoints.title: A coursework line that does not move
whyPoints.description: Tutors explain criteria, interrogate research questions and give feedback on drafts the student wrote. Nobody supplies text or finished coursework, at any price. There is a market in this region doing the opposite, and the risk of buying it lands on the student at the moment their qualification is awarded.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated once, plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing for working and notes kept afterwards. Nobody is sent to a UAE address; home visits are a service we run only in India. Saying this clearly is how a family avoids discovering it after a payment has been made.

whyPoints.title: Unavailability disclosed, not disguised
whyPoints.description: If no specialist is free for the subject, level and slot you need, you will be told that, with the options and a date. A mismatch costs more than the fee because it costs the weeks in which the real problem went undiagnosed, and in the second Diploma year those weeks do not come back.

faqs.question: How many Diploma cohorts does ten years of IB teaching actually cover?
faqs.answer: Four or five, if the teaching was continuous and in the same programme. The Diploma runs on a two-year cycle, so a complete cohort means taking a group from subject choice through the internal assessment and mocks to the papers and results. Ten years of continuous Diploma teaching also means nine or ten May sessions seen. The figure drops sharply if some of those years were spent on another curriculum, at a different level, or in a non-teaching role. Ask for cohorts and sessions rather than years, and ask which subject and level each one was in.

faqs.question: Does teaching experience from another country transfer to a UAE IB classroom?
faqs.answer: The subject and assessment part transfers almost entirely. A Higher Level Chemistry teacher from Singapore or the UK knows the same syllabus, the same criteria and the same places marks are lost. What does not transfer is the system around it: which authority licenses your school, that Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies sit on the timetable beside the Diploma, how Ministry of Education equivalency works, and that exam centres are allocated to administrative zones. Those take a year or two of working here to learn, and they are the part a family notices when planning a week or a document file.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who taught IGCSE for years automatically experienced with the Diploma?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the most common mismatch in the market. The subject content overlaps, so the tutor will be comfortable explaining the material. The assessment does not overlap. Internal assessment criteria and their mark allocations, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay, Higher Level paper 3 and the points structure are all specific to the Diploma, and a strong IGCSE teacher may never have taught any of them. If your child is in DP1 or DP2, ask which Diploma cohorts the tutor has taught and which components they have marked work against.

faqs.question: What should an experienced tutor already know about our school before the first session?
faqs.answer: Which authority holds its file, so advice is given in the right vocabulary. Which board it uses for IGCSE if a younger child is involved, since Cambridge and Pearson set different papers and different dates. Which Higher Level subjects it actually runs this year, because the published list and the staffed list are not always the same. When its internal coursework deadlines fall, which the school sets rather than the IB. And which Arabic stream your child sits in. A tutor who asks those questions at the start is working from the system your child is actually inside.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects have the thinnest supply of experienced teachers in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Physics and Chemistry, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Computer Science at Higher Level and the less widely taught languages. The reason is structural: the IB accounts for roughly 7% of Dubai's private-school roll, so Diploma teachers are a minority of a large teaching market, and Higher Level specialists in those subjects are a minority of that minority. Expect a shorter list of candidates, less flexibility on the afternoon slot everybody wants, and a genuine wait at exam time. That scarcity is also the strongest argument for delivering lessons online.

faqs.question: Our child's school opened this year. Does that change the experience we should look for?
faqs.answer: It changes what the school can give you and therefore what you need from outside it. Dubai added six private schools in 2025-26 and opens seven more for 2026-27, three of them IB. A new school is staffing Diploma classes from the same pool as everybody else, and in the first cohort there is no local history of what the internal deadlines look like in practice or how a mock compares with the real thing. A tutor who has taken several cohorts through, anywhere, supplies exactly that missing pattern.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether a tutor knows which authority inspects our school?
faqs.answer: It matters for the advice you get. KHDA oversees private education in Dubai, ADEK handles licensing and accreditation in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA regulates Sharjah and the Department of Knowledge regulates Ras Al Khaimah, while the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority also approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A tutor who names the wrong body is describing a school system your child does not attend.

faqs.question: What does experience with the Internal Assessment look like in a session?
faqs.answer: It looks like criterion letters and numbers rather than general encouragement. An experienced tutor can say which criterion a draft is losing marks under, how many marks that criterion carries, and what a stronger response to it contains in writing. Before data collection they interrogate the research question until it is answerable with what a school lab can actually produce, which is where most of the eventual damage is done or avoided. They read what the student has written and feed back on it. They do not supply text, and the work submitted is the student's own throughout.

faqs.question: Can an experienced tutor predict the grade our child will finish with?
faqs.answer: No, and an offer to do so is a reason for caution rather than confidence. What experience does buy is a realistic read of distance: which components are costing marks, whether the cause is content, technique or timing, and whether the weeks remaining are enough to change it. That read is useful precisely because it is honest about the cases where it is not enough. No tutor should promise a score, a points total or a grade improvement, and no provider should publish a success statistic without saying how many students it covers and when it was measured.

faqs.question: How much more does the UAE market charge for an experienced subject specialist?
faqs.answer: Published rates read in October 2026 put budget online tuition at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300, and IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. TutorChase publishes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. A visiting tutor at a UAE address sits at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's 2026 table at AED 180 to 350. Those are other providers' figures, not ours. Level, subject scarcity, format and time of year move a rate more than years of experience do.

faqs.question: Does a tutor's experience change the permit they need to teach privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: No. The requirement is the same whatever the experience. Private tuition work permits were introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and it covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own channels, where the service is listed with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and the permit's code of conduct also restricts tutoring students from the tutor's own school.

faqs.question: Does experience of Arabic and Islamic Education matter if our child only needs maths help?
faqs.answer: It matters for the plan, not for the maths. Those lessons are mandatory alongside the licensed curriculum in Dubai private schools and they occupy real timetable minutes, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. A tutor who does not know they are there will propose a week that does not fit. It also matters if you later want support in them: schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in three of those subjects, teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education need the appropriate KHDA approval, and using different or additional content needs prior Ministry permission.

faqs.question: Has an experienced tutor seen the Ministry of Education equivalency paperwork before?
faqs.answer: Somebody who has taken UAE cohorts through to results will have watched families go through it, which is why the question gets raised in DP1 rather than after results day. The British track, as reported in July 2026, asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. For the IB Diploma we publish no points figure, because none has been read on an official Ministry page. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: What experience of the November session should we ask about?
faqs.answer: Ask directly whether the tutor has taught a November cohort, because most UAE candidates sit May and a tutor's experience often follows that pattern. The practical differences are in the calendar rather than the content: internal deadlines, mock timing and the revision block all sit in different months, and a student retaking after May has a compressed run at it. Cambridge and Pearson also run their own November series for IGCSE, with dates published on their sites. We do not publish IB session dates here, because they should be confirmed with your school's coordinator.

faqs.question: If the right specialist lives outside our emirate, how does the lesson actually happen?
faqs.answer: Over live video, one-to-one, in a Gulf Standard Time slot agreed with you. The tutor and student share a screen and work on the same page, so a maths solution or a chemistry mechanism is written out and annotated rather than described. Work can be photographed and marked up in the session, and the notes stay available afterwards. Nothing about the arrangement depends on which emirate anyone is in, which is the point: it is how a family in Fujairah or Ras Al Khaimah reaches a Higher Level specialist at the same rate as a family in Dubai.

faqs.question: How many sessions should we watch before judging whether the experience is real?
faqs.answer: Three or four. One is too few to be fair, and a term is an expensive way to find out. In the trial lesson, which is free and taken before any payment, look for a named cause rather than a general diagnosis: command terms, units, timing per mark, a specific criterion. By the third or fourth session the student should be doing something identifiably different, and you should be able to say what it is. If you cannot, tell us and the match changes.

faqs.question: What happens when no tutor with that experience is free in the week we need?
faqs.answer: We say so. The predictable shortages are Higher Level Physics and Chemistry in exam term, Higher Level Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, Computer Science, the less widely taught languages, and the weekday slot between four and six in the afternoon. The options are a different slot with the right specialist, a short wait with an actual date, a generalist described honestly as a holding measure, or nothing from us with the reason given. Putting a free tutor in front of your child is how families lose the weeks during which the real problem goes undiagnosed.

experienced-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Start by making the experience specific
experienced-ib-tutor.closingBody: Tell us the school, the subject, the level and the component that is costing marks, and send a recent marked script or draft. We will name the authority that holds your school's file, say who could teach that component and which cohorts they have taken through, and arrange a free trial lesson with no payment taken beforehand. If the time left is too short to change the outcome, or if nobody with the right experience is free in the slot you need, you will hear that instead of a sales pitch. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; home visits are a service we run only in India.

experienced-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE at the tiers UAE centres actually enter. Each profile names the syllabuses taught through to a final series, so a match can be made on the code printed on your child's statement of entry rather than on a subject label alone.

intro.heading: Experience in IGCSE is counted in series, not in years
paragraphs: Ten years in a classroom and ten IGCSE series are not the same quantity. Most UAE centres enter their main cohort for one series a year, usually June, so a school teacher's decade covers roughly ten sets of entries, ten mock windows and ten results days. A tutor who also prepares November candidates and private candidates for the March series sees the calendar from more angles in less time. When a family asks for an experienced IGCSE tutor in the UAE, the useful question is not how long someone has taught. It is how many times they have stood at each of the dates that cannot be moved.

Those dates are public and they are not negotiable. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with a March series as well, and it allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, warning that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after reading the wrong one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sits in May or June and again in November. For the Cambridge March 2027 series the board published a final entry deadline of 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, and the exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027. The entry closes before the exam period even begins.

That geometry is what separates a tutor who has run the year from one who has not. An inexperienced plan works through the syllabus in the order the textbook prints it and arrives at paper technique in April. An experienced plan reads the statement of entry first, notes which components carry the coursework and practical marks and when the school wants them, and schedules the irreversible things first. The tier decision, the coursework deadline and the entry itself all have owners who are not the tutor and not the parent, and every one of them closes earlier than families expect.

Delivery matters less than people think and more than providers admit. Every lesson IB Gram arranges for a family in the Emirates is one-to-one and delivered over live video. Home visits are part of what we do in India, not here, and no tutor is sent to a UAE address. The reason is not cost. A family in Fujairah looking for someone who has taken Chemistry 0620 candidates through four series is choosing from a national pool rather than from whoever is within a half-hour drive, and in the final term the hour that would have gone to the drive goes to a timed paper instead.

What follows is the IGCSE year laid out backwards, from the last paper to the first conversation in Year 10, with the market rates UAE providers publish, the permit a tutor must hold, the five windows that open around results day, and the Ministry of Education equivalency rule that reaches back into subject choices made two years earlier. Every figure is attributed to whoever published it and dated. Where the source is a board, the official timetable is the thing to read before acting, because provisional dates get revised and ours are not a substitute for your centre's.

experienced-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Four stages matter to a UAE family searching for IGCSE help, and they are not all taught the same way. Two are boards, one is the year before the course, and one is the eighteen months after it. The tutor who is experienced in one of them is not automatically experienced in the next.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE is the route most British-curriculum centres in the Emirates enter. Subjects are identified by a four-digit code - 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry - and several are tiered, with a Core entry carrying a lower ceiling than an Extended one. The syllabus is revised on a published cycle, so a tutor working from a specification two versions old will teach content that has moved paper or dropped out. The code on the statement of entry, not the subject name, is what fixes the content.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable version for each. A Dubai centre and a cousin's centre in another country can sit the same syllabus on different days. The board states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used, which makes checking the version a parental job and not only an exams officer's.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses its own codes - 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4PH1 for Physics, 4CH1 for Chemistry - and its own tiering where the subject has it. Exams are available in May or June and again in November each year. The specifications and the assessment structures are not interchangeable with Cambridge, so past-paper work on the wrong board teaches question styles your child will not meet and command terms used slightly differently.
programmes.countryNote: The November series is the part UAE families use most and understand least. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and the November 2025 series released results to students on 22 January 2026. That turnaround is what makes a November entry a usable repair for a single grade rather than a full year lost, provided the entry is made in the summer window rather than discussed in October.

programmes.name: Year 9, the year before the course
programmes.description: Year 9 is where subject and tier decisions are shaped, and it is the cheapest point in the whole sequence to change anything. A student who leaves Year 9 secure in algebraic manipulation and in writing to a command term starts Year 10 doing IGCSE work rather than catching up on the arithmetic underneath it. Most families do not think about tutoring this early, and the ones who do spend fewer hours later.
programmes.countryNote: In the Emirates, Year 9 is also where the Ministry of Education equivalency question begins, because the five subjects the Ministry counts are drawn from the set a student is about to choose. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among those five, which means a nine-subject timetable can still leave a thin count if the options are chosen without that rule in view. It is a two-minute conversation in Year 9 and a problem in Year 11.

programmes.name: IGCSE into A Level or the IB Diploma
programmes.description: The grades decide the next route, and the gap between an IGCSE grade and the first term of a post-16 course is real. A Core-tier Mathematics award rarely supports a Higher Level or an A Level in a quantitative subject, and a comfortable grade 6 in a science often still leaves a student short on the extended-response writing their new course asks for in week three. Support here is bridging, not revision.
programmes.countryNote: Conditional offers from UAE and overseas sixth forms frequently hang on one grade, which is why the November series and the review-of-marking window both matter so much in August. A family deciding in September that a resit is needed has usually already missed the entry. The sequence has to be mapped before results day, not after it.

experienced-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects UAE families most often ask for by name, with the code that fixes the content and the place marks are usually lost. A tutor who has taken the subject through a series can name the second of those without being asked.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Cambridge Core and Extended; Pearson Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The tier decision lives here more than anywhere else. Extended carries topics Core never meets, and a Core entry caps the award. Marks go on method lines left unwritten, on rounding instructions ignored, and on the last two parts of a structured question where the candidate ran out of planned time rather than understanding.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or single tier by specification
subjects.description: Practical skills are assessed in writing. Candidates lose marks describing a method without a control variable, misreading a graph axis prefix, and giving a numerical answer without a unit. The alternative to practical paper rewards a student who has planned experiments on paper, which is exactly what can be taught over a shared screen.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or single tier by specification
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic and organic reaction conditions take most of the lost marks, followed by the qualitative analysis tables candidates try to recall rather than read. A tutor who has marked the paper knows which stated observations earn a mark and which are description without chemistry in them.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or single tier by specification
subjects.description: The content is learnable and the marks are lost in language. Command terms separate describe from explain from suggest, and a candidate who answers all three the same way scores on one of them. Data-handling questions on unfamiliar organisms reward process, not memory, and that process can be drilled.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500 / 4EA1)
subjects.levels: Single tier; coursework route where the centre offers it
subjects.description: Directed writing and the comparative or summary task carry most of the swing. Candidates lose marks on register, on lifting phrasing from the passage, and on a response that answers the content of the question but not its form. Where a centre has chosen a coursework route, the school's internal deadline arrives well before the board's.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450 / 4BS1)
subjects.description: Case-study application is the whole paper. Marks go to candidates who quote the stimulus back as evidence and to those who evaluate rather than list. A strong student who writes general business theory with no reference to the company in front of them is scoring in the bottom band of the mark scheme.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478 / 4CP0)
subjects.levels: Single tier; programming assessed inside the written papers
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables are where the marks are, not the language a student happens to know. Candidates lose marks writing syntactically valid code that answers a different question, and on logic questions where a truth table would have taken less time than the paragraph they wrote instead.

subjects.name: Economics (0455 / 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy earns marks on its own: labelled axes, a shifted curve and a new equilibrium identified. Beyond that, the evaluation marks go to candidates who say which effect dominates and why, rather than listing advantages and disadvantages and stopping at the comma.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Mathematics
subjects.levels: Taken alongside IGCSE Mathematics in stronger sets
subjects.description: Entered by centres that want a bridge into A Level or Higher Level work. It is the clearest example of why tutor supply is thin in any single emirate: a UAE centre may have two sets in the whole school, and a tutor who has taken candidates through it is rare enough that a national pool over video is the only sensible place to look.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.levels: Mandatory alongside the licensed curriculum in Dubai private schools
subjects.description: KHDA requires these in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum a school is licensed to teach, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and specified languages of instruction. They sit in the same Year 11 week as IGCSE revision, which makes them a timetabling problem as much as a teaching one.

experienced-igcse-tutor.regionsTitle: Where UAE IGCSE families sit, and what that changes
experienced-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: The syllabus is identical across the Emirates. What differs is which authority holds the school's file, how far a session start slips when the commute is bad, and how thin local supply is for a given code. All three change the plan, and only the first one appears on a school website.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Licensed and inspected by KHDA, and the emirate with the deepest IGCSE market. Mock windows cluster in January, which is also when a 4pm start becomes a 4.40pm start by car. Taking the hour over video is how families keep the mock-feedback week intact.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Island-to-mainland travel decides when a session can realistically begin, so a plan built on a 5pm start in Saadiyat is in practice a plan built on 6pm, three evenings a week, for a whole term.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education here and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A Sharjah centre's assessment arrangements are therefore signed off locally as well as by the exam board, which is worth knowing before assuming a Dubai timetable applies.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Falls under ADEK alongside Abu Dhabi, with fewer IGCSE centres. A private-candidate entry sometimes means sitting the papers in another city, which is a travel and accommodation question to settle at the entry deadline in the autumn rather than in the week of paper one.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: No emirate-level regulator of its own: the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Families here often sit at a centre in a neighbouring emirate, which changes nothing about the syllabus and a great deal about exam-morning logistics.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in RAK and, like Sharjah, approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Specialist subject supply is thinner here than in Dubai, which is where online one-to-one IGCSE tuition stops being a convenience and becomes the only route to a particular code.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised federally by the Ministry of Education. An east-coast family that needs a tutor who has taken Chemistry 0620 candidates through several series is choosing from a national pool over video, because the local pool for that code may be nobody at all.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised federally. The smallest private-school market in the country and the clearest argument for matching on a code rather than on proximity: the question is not who is nearby, it is who has taught 4MA1 Higher to a final series.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai's private sector reported 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum the largest single share at 37 per cent. That is why IGCSE tutor demand in January is concentrated here, and why a January request for a scarce code is competing with every other family in the emirate.

Centres here answer to ADEK, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school. That single rule is why 'your child's own teacher, privately' is not an offer a UAE family should accept in this emirate.

Sharjah's authority and RAK's Department of Knowledge both approve assessment methods as well as fees, while Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the Ministry of Education. Centres are fewer and further apart, so the entry question and the exam-centre question are both settled earlier here.

experienced-igcse-tutor.modesIntro: Three shapes of booking, decided almost entirely by how many weeks remain before paper one. The same tutor and the same syllabus sit behind all three; what changes is how much of the course is still open to being rebuilt rather than only revised.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one across Years 10 and 11
modes.description: One session a week per subject, running with the school's scheme of work rather than ahead of it or behind it. This is the only booking shape where the tier decision, the coursework calendar and the forecast grade are all still in play, which makes it the cheapest version of the same outcome. It is also the version where a mock result becomes information rather than a shock.

modes.description: A fixed number of hours, planned backwards from the first paper and allocated by where the marks actually are rather than by which topics feel uncomfortable. Twelve weeks out this can still reshape a grade across two or three subjects. Six weeks out it should concentrate on one subject and one component, because spreading the same hours across four subjects at that point buys very little in any of them.

modes.description: The fortnight after results day carries three decisions on short clocks, and they interact. A review of marking may not conclude before the next series' entry closes, so the resit entry sometimes has to be made as insurance. Sessions in this window are short, frequent and aimed at whichever of the three routes the family chooses, including the bridging work for a post-16 course that starts in days.

sections.heading: What a UAE family is really testing when they ask how experienced a tutor is
paragraphs: The question behind the question is whether this person has been in the room for the parts of the year that cannot be repeated. Teaching content well is a skill most graduates of a subject can learn. Knowing that the school's coursework deadline sits three weeks before the board's, that the forecast grade is formed from a mock marked in January, and that a Core entry closes the ceiling in a way no amount of April revision reopens - that is a different kind of knowledge, and it is only acquired by having been surprised by it once.

So the useful test is not a number of years. It is a conversion. Ask how many series the tutor has taken candidates through in your child's subject and board, and how many of those were November or March rather than June. Ask what they do in the first session with a statement of entry. Ask what they would check if a mock came back eleven marks below a forecast. A tutor with four series behind them in 0620 will answer those three questions in specifics within a minute; a tutor with none will answer with method and philosophy.

The table below converts the claims providers actually make into the thing a parent can use. None of these claims is dishonest in itself. The problem is that they are not comparable to each other, and the UAE market prices them as though they were, with published rates running from AED 33 an hour to AED 650 an hour for what is described in the same four words.

sections.heading: The IGCSE course counted backwards: twenty-four months on one page
paragraphs: Start at the last paper and walk backwards. The thing families discover too late is that the sequence is not a gentle ramp with an exam at the end. It is a series of gates, each with a different owner, and each one shuts earlier than the one you were worrying about. The tier gate shuts at the entry deadline. The coursework gate shuts at a school deadline set before the board's. The forecast-grade gate shuts when a mock is marked in January, months before anything a family would call revision has begun.

The ownership column is the one to read twice. A tutor owns none of these gates. A parent owns almost none of them. The centre's exams officer owns the entry, the subject teacher owns the forecast and the coursework mark, and the board owns the timetable and the zone it belongs to. What an experienced tutor adds is a calendar that treats those owners as fixed points and arranges teaching around them, and the habit of asking for the documents that prove what the fixed points are.

The windows below are expressed in months before paper one of a June series, because that is the sitting most UAE centres enter. For a November series, subtract roughly seven months from every row and expect the summer holiday to land inside the heaviest preparation block. For the Cambridge March series, the entry deadline falls in the autumn of the previous year - the board published 27 November 2026 for a March 2027 sitting - which puts the gate before most families have thought about the exam at all.

sections.heading: The syllabus code is the first question, and the statement of entry is the only answer
paragraphs: A subject name tells a tutor almost nothing. Physics could be Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1, Core or Extended, with or without a separate practical route, in a centre that sits in one of six Cambridge zones. Each of those combinations has different papers, different weightings and different question styles. Past-paper work on the wrong board is not neutral: it teaches command-term habits the real mark scheme does not reward and builds timing instincts for a paper your child will not sit.

The document that settles it is the statement of entry, which the centre issues ahead of the series and which lists the syllabus code, the components and the tier. Until that exists, the next best source is the exams officer, not the class teacher and not the school website, because the website usually names a curriculum rather than a specification. An experienced tutor asks for the statement of entry in the first message. A tutor who starts teaching without it is making an assumption on your child's behalf.

The mapping below is a starting point for the subjects UAE families ask about most. Treat it as orientation and confirm each code against the board's current specification, because specifications are revised on a cycle and a code can change its components between cohorts. The column that matters most is the last one: the component with a clock of its own, running ahead of every written paper, and the one families most often discover late.

sections.heading: Where the eleven weeks between the last paper and results day actually go
paragraphs: A June candidate finishes in the second half of June and hears nothing until late August. Pearson released June 2026 results to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. That gap is roughly eleven weeks of silence during which most UAE families are out of the country, and the single most common mistake made in it is assuming that nothing is happening and therefore nothing needs arranging.

What is happening is marking, standardisation and the setting of grade boundaries for that series. Boundaries are fixed for the papers actually sat, not carried over from last year, which is the technical reason a mock boundary is a guide and never a promise. It is also why the honest answer to 'what grade will my child get' is a range with a method behind it rather than a number. A tutor who gives you a number is telling you about their confidence, not about the marking.

What a family can usefully do in those eleven weeks is short and specific. Know which day results arrive and who will be reachable in which time zone. Know the centre's process for releasing a mark breakdown by component. Know, before leaving, what the next series' entry deadline is and who can make the entry if the family is abroad. Those three answers take an afternoon in June and are close to impossible to assemble from a hotel in August, when the exams office is at its busiest.

sections.heading: Results day, and the five windows that open and shut around it
paragraphs: Results day is not an endpoint, it is the start of several short clocks running at once. Each has a different owner, and the two that matter most cannot be started by a parent at all: a review of marking is requested by the centre, not by a family, and an entry for the next series is made by a centre too. A family that spends results day deciding how to feel has usually spent the first of those clocks.

The order below is the order experience teaches. Before anything is paid for, check the statement of results against the statement of entry, component by component. A missing component, a wrong tier or an absent-marked paper is caught in that comparison and nowhere else, and it is a more common cause of an unexpected grade than a marking error. Then ask the centre for the mark breakdown, because knowing whether the loss sat in one paper or spread across all of them decides whether a review, a resit or neither is the sensible move.

Boards publish the deadline for each of these services per series, and the windows are measured in days rather than weeks. We do not publish the specific dates here because they change by series and by board; the centre's exams officer and the board's own enquiries-about-results page are the two places to get them. What an experienced tutor contributes is the sequencing - which clock to start first, and which decision can be made as insurance while another is still pending.

sections.heading: The November and March series, and what a second sitting costs in time
paragraphs: The IGCSE calendar has more doors than families assume, and the useful consequence is that a single disappointing grade rarely needs to cost a year. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with a March series as well, and it publishes key dates for each. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sits in May or June and in November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. The IGCSE November series is the door UAE families use most.

The arithmetic that matters is the arrival date of the new grade, not the exam date. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A student who resits in November therefore starts Year 12 in September on a conditional basis and confirms it in January, which most sixth forms will accommodate if they are told in August. Cambridge gave 13 May 2027 for March 2027 results on Direct, with certificates in late June, which is why the March series suits a private candidate adding a subject ahead of a university application cycle rather than a mainstream cohort.

Two practical cautions. Not every subject or centre offers every series, and the Cambridge March series in particular is not universally available, so the first call is to the exams officer rather than to the board. And the entry deadline for the next series frequently falls before a review of marking on the last one concludes, which is why experienced families make the entry as insurance and withdraw if the review succeeds. That decision is easier to make in August with the whole sequence drawn out than in September with half of it discovered.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies keep running through the exam term
paragraphs: In Dubai, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. They do not pause for IGCSE revision. For a Year 11 student in April, that is several lesson periods a week that belong to subjects outside the series, in the term when every other hour is being counted.

There are structural details here that change what tutoring can even look like. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with schools allowed to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advice that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes.

The constraint most relevant to tutoring is about material. For these subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited. A tutor cannot simply bring a better worksheet to a Social Studies session the way they might to a Chemistry one. The honest offer is support with the school's own material, the language demands of it, and the study skills around it - and a frank statement that the content itself is set elsewhere. KHDA also requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects in school, which is a school-level credential and not something a private tutor holds.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges for experience, and when the money arrives too late
paragraphs: UAE providers publish rates across a range of more than twenty to one for what is advertised in the same words. The figures below are what each provider states, read in October 2026, and they are the market rather than our price list. IB Gram does not publish an hourly figure on this page: the trial lesson and the consultation are where a quote for a specific subject, tier and number of weeks is given, because an honest number depends on all three.

The column that is missing from every competitor rate table is the one about timing. An hour bought in Year 10 and an hour bought six weeks before paper one are not the same product. The early hour can still change which tier is entered, whether coursework is banked properly and what the forecast grade is built on. The late hour can only reorder revision and sharpen technique on content already learned. Both are worth buying; they are not worth the same, and a provider who quotes one rate all year is not pricing the difference.

Monthly packaging is where comparison breaks down fastest. Rates seen in this market include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, and Bestimate's Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Before comparing any two of those, convert both to an hourly figure and ask what a cancelled session does to it.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor against live one-to-one online when the paper date cannot move
paragraphs: Parents searching for an experienced IGCSE tutor in the UAE usually picture someone at the dining table. It is worth answering that honestly. In this market, a visiting tutor is real, widely available and priced at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with the drive included in the hour. What it buys is presence and supervision, which for a younger or easily distracted student is a genuine good. What it costs is pool size, and in a tiered, code-specific subject the pool is the whole argument.

IB Gram delivers to UAE families as one-to-one online tuition over live video, and does not send anyone to a UAE address; home visits are part of what we do in India. The case for that is not convenience. A family in Ras Al Khaimah who needs someone with four series of 0580 Extended behind them is choosing from a national pool over video, or from whoever drives there, and those two sets are not the same size. In the final term there is a second effect: the hour that would have gone to travel goes to a timed section instead.

The comparison below is about what actually differs, not about which is better in the abstract. Both are one student with one teacher on one syllabus. The variables are supply, rescheduling, what a parent can inspect afterwards, and whether the arrangement survives a November entry that runs across the summer and into the autumn term.

sections.heading: Who may legally charge you for a lesson, and how a parent checks
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the Emirates is permitted work, not unregulated work. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page for it lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Two consequences follow for a UAE family. The first is that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, so asking to see a permit is a reasonable question rather than an awkward one. No fine schedule is published, so anyone quoting you a specific figure for the penalty is repeating something unverified. The second is that the permit carries a code of conduct, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school.

A tuition centre with premises is a different legal animal again: in Dubai that needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That permit belongs to the institute, not to the individuals teaching in it. IB Gram holds no regulator permit of that kind and does not claim one, and nobody in this market should describe their tutors as approved by a UAE authority unless they can produce the document. Where the tutor teaching your child is outside the UAE, they are governed where they are, which is a question worth asking rather than assuming.

sections.heading: Coursework and practicals in the week before a school deadline
paragraphs: This is where the line sits, and it is worth stating plainly because two providers in this market cross it. A tutor teaches, questions, explains a mark scheme and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not supply finished assessed work, does not edit a piece until the sentences are theirs rather than the candidate's, and does not sit beside a student dictating. One ranking site in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright. Buying that is a malpractice finding against the student, not against the seller.

In practice the honest version is more useful anyway. A session on a coursework draft looks like this: the student reads their own paragraph aloud, the tutor asks which assessment criterion it is aimed at, and the student discovers that the paragraph describes where it was supposed to analyse. The redrafting happens afterwards, by the student, with the criterion in front of them. That is slower than a rewrite and it is the only version that survives a conversation with a moderator.

The practical components deserve their own answer, because families reasonably ask how a screen can teach laboratory work. For Cambridge sciences the practical skills in many centres are assessed through the alternative to practical paper, which is a written paper about method, variables, apparatus, tables and graphs. That is taught well over video, because what it rewards is planning on paper. Where a centre runs a practical examination or a coursework route instead, the honest division is that the school owns the bench time and the tutor owns the write-up skills and the interpretation of results.

sections.heading: The Ministry of Education equivalency file is assembled from Year 9 choices
paragraphs: Ministry of Education equivalency is the process that converts a foreign school certificate into something UAE institutions can read, and for British-track students it has a specific shape. The requirements as reported in July 2026 are that a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

The detail that catches families is which subjects count. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. A student with nine IGCSE entries, two of which are Arabic and Islamic Education, is not counting nine towards that rule. One ranking competitor in this market publishes a six-subject requirement for UAE candidates; the sourced figure is five. The point is not to score against a rival page, it is that the number is checkable and that a wrong number here produces a real problem in a real office.

For the American track the same clarification sets out English proficiency through a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, with at least 450 in SAT Math before applying. It states no IB points threshold, which is why no honest page should publish one without reading it on moe.gov.ae. IB Gram does not perform equivalency and does not guarantee its outcome; the Ministry and the emirate attestation channel own that process. What a tutor can do is ask the question in Year 9, when the subject set is still being chosen, instead of in Year 13, when it is not.

sections.heading: When nobody with that experience is free in the week you want
paragraphs: The honest limit is worth publishing because no competitor in this market publishes theirs. Supply for a given code at a given hour is finite. Further Mathematics, Computer Science 0478, Economics at Extended tier and the Pearson modular routes all have thin coverage in any one emirate, and a request made in the second week of January - the week UAE mock results come back - is competing with every other family in Dubai's 227 private schools for the same small group of specialists.

What we do when that happens is say so. If no specialist in your child's code and tier is free at the hour you need, you are told that, rather than being matched to a generalist who will discover the specification in the first session. Where it helps, we propose the nearest honest alternative: a different slot with the right specialist, a short diagnostic block with someone who has taught the adjacent code while a slot opens, or a plan the family can run themselves for three weeks with a review at the end of it. Sometimes the answer is that six weeks before paper one, one subject done properly beats three done thinly.

The lesson from the calendar applies here as well. Scarcity is a timing problem more than a supply problem. The same specialist who is unavailable in January was free in September, and the family who asked in September paid the same hourly figure for an hour that could still change the tier. If you are reading this in autumn, the useful action is to ask now for the subject you expect to be hardest in the spring, rather than waiting for a mock to confirm what the Year 10 reports already suggested.

process.title: Send the statement of entry, or the codes
process.description: The first thing we ask for is the document that fixes the content: the statement of entry, or failing that the syllabus codes from the exams officer. With 0620 Extended and a listed alternative to practical paper on the page, a plan can be written. With 'IGCSE Chemistry' alone, it cannot.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the specialist
process.description: One lesson with the tutor who would actually teach the course, at no charge and with no card required. It is diagnostic as much as introductory: the tutor works through a past question with your child and comes out able to name where the marks are going, which is the thing you are buying.

process.title: A plan written backwards from the series
process.description: Hours are allocated from the paper date backwards, with the school's internal coursework deadlines and the mock window marked first. You get the plan in writing, including what it does not cover. If the entry deadline has already passed and the tier is locked, the plan says so rather than implying otherwise.

process.title: Weekly sessions with the mock as the checkpoint
process.description: Sessions run to the plan, with notes you can read. The January mock is the formal review point: the script is read question by question, the three recurring losses are named, and the remaining hours are reallocated. A plan that survives a mock unchanged was not reading the mock.

process.title: Re-plan at results, whichever way it goes
process.description: Before results day we agree who checks the statement of results against the statement of entry, what the centre's process is for a mark breakdown, and what the next series' entry deadline is. If a review or a resit follows, the sequencing is already drawn. If it does not, the bridging work into the next course starts instead.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the code, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: A tutor is proposed because they have taught 0580 Extended or 4PH1 through to a final series, and the match names which series. Subject-name matching is how a family ends up doing Cambridge past papers for a Pearson entry, which is a waste of the best weeks of the year.

whyPoints.title: Plans that start from a published date
whyPoints.description: Every plan is anchored to a date someone else published: your centre's entry deadline, the board's timetable for your zone, the school's coursework deadline. That makes the plan checkable. A plan anchored to nothing but enthusiasm cannot be audited by a parent, which is precisely why it reads so well.

whyPoints.title: A line we do not cross on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Feedback, questioning and criterion-by-criterion review of the student's own draft, and nothing beyond it. We will not supply finished coursework and we will not edit a piece until the voice is no longer the candidate's. The exposure of crossing that line sits with your child, which is why the answer is the same every time.

whyPoints.title: Delivered live online, one-to-one
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with shared-screen notes you can read afterwards. Home visits are part of what IB Gram does in India and not here, which we state on this page rather than after you have asked twice.

whyPoints.title: What we say when the specialist is not free
whyPoints.description: If nobody with the right code and tier is available at the hour you need, you hear that in the first reply. The alternative offered is named for what it is - a different slot, an adjacent specialism, or a short self-run plan with a review - rather than presented as the same thing.

whyPoints.title: Figures attributed, or not published
whyPoints.description: Every AED range on this page carries the provider who published it and the month it was read. Where a number could not be verified - IB session dates, the penalty for tutoring without a permit, an IB points threshold for equivalency - it is left out and the official source is named instead.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE series will a tutor with eight years in UAE classrooms actually have sat?
faqs.answer: Most UAE centres enter their main cohort once a year, usually June, so eight school-based years is roughly eight sets of entries, eight mock windows and eight results days in that subject. It can be fewer if the years were split across curricula or year groups. A private tutor of the same vintage may have seen more, because November entries and private candidates add sittings. Ask for the conversion directly: how many series, in which subject, on which board, and how many of them were November or March rather than June. The number is usually smaller than the years, and it is the number that matters.

faqs.question: What should we ask in the first ten minutes to test whether a tutor's IGCSE experience is real?
faqs.answer: Three questions separate people quickly. First: what do you want from us before the first lesson? An experienced answer is the statement of entry or the syllabus code, not 'a bit about your son'. Second: what would you check if a mock came back eleven marks below the forecast? The useful answer names components and question types, not motivation. Third: which of the components in this subject has a deadline earlier than the written papers? Someone who has run the year answers that instantly, because they have been caught by it. Vague, warm answers to all three are the signal.

faqs.question: Why does an experienced tutor want the syllabus code before agreeing to a plan?
faqs.answer: Because the subject name does not determine the content. Physics could be Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1, Core or Extended, with practical skills assessed in a written alternative or through a practical examination. Those combinations have different papers, different weightings and different question styles, and past-paper practice on the wrong one builds timing instincts for a paper your child will never sit. The code sits on the statement of entry the centre issues before the series. Until that exists, the exams officer is the right person to ask - not the school website, which usually names a curriculum rather than a specification.

faqs.question: Our son's first paper is twenty-two weeks away. What does experience change at that distance?
faqs.answer: At twenty-two weeks almost everything is still open, and that is the point. Coursework and practical skills can be banked properly rather than rescued. The January mock is still ahead, so the forecast grade is being built from evidence that can still be improved. If the entry has not been submitted, the tier argument can still be made with evidence behind it. An experienced plan at this distance spends the early weeks on technique over content already taught, not on racing ahead of the school. The revision block is scheduled last, because it is the only part that works no matter when it happens.

faqs.question: Which two documents should we send a tutor before the first lesson?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry and the most recent marked assessment. The first fixes the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the components, which is everything a plan is built from. The second shows where marks are actually going, which is not the same as where your child feels weak. A marked mock script is worth more than a school report, because a report gives a grade and a script gives the question numbers. If the statement of entry has not been issued yet, the syllabus codes from the exams officer will do, with the tier confirmed separately.

faqs.question: Is the March series open to every Cambridge subject and every exam centre?
faqs.answer: No, and that is the first thing to check rather than assume. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, and publishes separate key dates for a March series, but availability depends on subject and on the centre. For the March 2027 series Cambridge published a final entry deadline of 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027 and an exam period from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Your exams officer can say whether your centre offers it for your child's subject; the board's key-dates document sets the timings once it does.

faqs.question: Where do the eleven weeks between the last paper and results day actually go?
faqs.answer: Into marking, standardisation and the setting of grade boundaries for that series. Pearson released June 2026 results to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, which is roughly eleven weeks after the papers. Boundaries are fixed for the papers actually sat rather than carried over, which is the technical reason a mock boundary is a guide and never a promise. Nothing a family does in that window touches the marks. What it can do is settle who is reachable on results day, how the centre releases a mark breakdown, and what the next entry deadline is.

faqs.question: If a grade looks wrong on results day, what happens in the first forty-eight hours?
faqs.answer: Check the statement of results against the statement of entry, component by component, before anything else. A missing component, a wrong tier or a paper recorded as absent is caught there and nowhere else, and it is a more common cause of a surprising grade than a marking error. Then ask the centre for the mark breakdown, which shows whether the loss sat in one paper or across all of them. Reviews of marking and access to scripts are requested by the centre, not by a family, inside a window the board publishes per series and measured in days.

faqs.question: Does a resit entry have to be made before we travel in August?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, and that is the practical argument for drawing the sequence out in June. The entry deadline for the next series can fall before a review of marking on the last one concludes, so experienced families make the entry as insurance and withdraw it if the review succeeds. Entries are made by the centre or by an approved centre accepting private candidates, which means someone has to be reachable and able to authorise it. Agree before you fly who does that, which email address they use, and what the centre's cut-off is for instructions received from abroad.

faqs.question: Our daughter missed a June paper through illness. What is the honest sequence from here?
faqs.answer: Start with the centre, same week. The school holds the evidence process and the relationship with the board, and what is possible depends on which component was missed and how much of the subject was completed. If a special-consideration route does not resolve it, the November series is the usual repair: Pearson's November 2026 timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. That means a Year 12 place is normally held conditionally and confirmed in January. Tell the receiving sixth form in August rather than in September.

faqs.question: Does doubling the weekly hours in the last month actually buy anything?
faqs.answer: Less than families hope, and sometimes less than one hour used better. In the last month the content is taught; what moves marks is timing, command-term discipline and question selection under pressure. Those improve through short, frequent, timed practice with feedback, not through longer sessions. Four extra hours a week spread across four subjects at that stage usually produces four slightly calmer subjects and no grade change. The same four hours on the single component carrying the biggest loss has a chance. The honest version of this advice costs us revenue, which is why so few providers give it.

faqs.question: Is an experienced tutor in the UAE teaching from our living room or over video?
faqs.answer: Over video. Every lesson IB Gram arranges for a family in the Emirates is one-to-one and delivered live online, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with shared-screen notes you keep afterwards. Home visits are part of what we do in India, not here. The reason is supply: a family in Fujairah or Ras Al Khaimah who needs someone with several series of a specific code behind them is choosing from a national pool over video rather than from whoever drives there. In the final term there is a second gain, which is that the travel hour becomes a timed-practice hour.

faqs.question: May a tutor rewrite a clumsy paragraph in our son's IGCSE coursework?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor can ask which assessment criterion that paragraph is aimed at, read the criterion with him, and let him discover that it describes where it was meant to analyse. The redrafting is his, afterwards, with the criterion in front of him. Editing until the sentences are the tutor's rather than the candidate's is malpractice, and the finding lands on your son, not on the tutor. Providers in this market do sell finished assessed work. The slower version is also the better teaching, because a criterion understood once transfers to the next piece and a rewritten paragraph does not.

faqs.question: Our Social Studies teacher set material we cannot find. Can a tutor bring their own instead?
faqs.answer: Not for that subject. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, so a tutor cannot substitute a better worksheet the way they might in Chemistry. What is available is support with the school's own material, the language demands inside it and the study skills around it. KHDA also requires that school teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold the appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects, which is a school credential and not something a private tutor carries. Ask the class teacher for the material first.

faqs.question: Ramadan sits across our mock window this year. What moves and what does not?
faqs.answer: Session timing moves; board dates do not. Schools commonly shorten the day during Ramadan, and families shift tutoring to the late evening after Iftar or to the early afternoon. Because lessons are delivered online, a session can move to any free slot in Gulf Standard Time without a drive attached to it, which is the main practical advantage in that month. What cannot move is the entry deadline, the coursework deadline or the paper date. The plan is therefore built so that the irreversible work sits outside the Ramadan weeks and the revision, which is schedulable, sits inside them.

faqs.question: Nobody with ten years of 0620 behind them is free on Tuesdays. What happens then?
faqs.answer: You are told that in the first reply rather than matched to a generalist who will meet the specification in your lesson. The alternatives are named for what they are: a different slot with the right specialist, a short diagnostic block with someone who has taught the adjacent code while a slot opens, or a three-week plan the family runs with a review at the end. Supply for a specific code at a specific hour is finite, and it is tightest in the second week of January when mock results arrive. Asking in September for the subject you expect to be hardest in spring avoids most of this.

faqs.question: Does a tutor who has only taught A Level count as experienced for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the gap is specific. A Level experience brings subject depth well above what the IGCSE papers ask for, which helps with explanation and with bridging into the next course. What it does not bring is the mark scheme at this level, where credit is awarded for a method line, a named control variable or a command term answered in its own terms rather than for the best physics in the room. A tutor used to A Level marking often over-teaches and under-scores a candidate. Ask when they last marked a full set of IGCSE scripts in that subject.

experienced-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Start from the date, not from the search
experienced-igcse-tutor.closingBody: If you are looking for an experienced IGCSE tutor in the UAE, the first useful step is not comparing hourly rates. It is finding out which board and series your child is entered for, which syllabus code sits against each subject, and which components have deadlines ahead of the written papers. Send us the statement of entry, or the codes from the exams officer, and the most recent marked assessment. We will come back with a specialist in that code, a free trial lesson with the person who would actually teach it, and a plan counted backwards from the paper date - including an honest statement of what, at this point in the calendar, is already fixed.

expert-ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma and MYP subjects to families across the seven emirates over live video. Each profile names the subject and the level taught, because a Higher Level specialist and a Standard Level generalist are not interchangeable, whatever the hourly rate says.

intro.heading: Two kinds of expertise, and the one UAE parents have no way to test
paragraphs: Subject expertise is the part of this that parents already know how to judge. A tutor either understands how Biology Higher Level Paper 3 is marked or they do not, and two lessons will usually settle it. The part nobody has a test for is the second system your child sits inside: a private school licensed by an emirate authority, carrying mandatory Ministry subjects beside the Diploma, entered for examinations by an awarding body that puts its centre into a timetable zone, and finishing with a certificate that needs federal equivalency before a UAE university registrar will read it. An expert IB tutor in the UAE works inside all of that rather than around it.

Five bodies regulate private schools in this country, and which one holds your child's school file depends on the address. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, Al Ain included. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same in its emirate, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority goes further still, approving tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

That reaches a tutoring plan faster than it sounds. If the authority above your child's school signs off the curriculum and, in two emirates, the assessment methods too, then a tutor who proposes to replace the school's scheme of work is proposing something the school is not free to accept. The same applies to the mandatory UAE subjects: for Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies, KHDA states that the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the MoE, is strictly prohibited. A tutor who does not know that will offer you material a Dubai school cannot use.

Scale is the other half of the picture. Dubai's private sector held 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7% of enrolment. Seven more private schools open for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, adding 16,846 places after a 6% rise in enrolment the year before. A programme that covers roughly one pupil in fourteen in the emirate with the deepest private market is a thin pool once you narrow to one Higher Level subject, and thinner again once you narrow to the hour after the school run.

So this page is built the way the system is built. It names the authority above your child's school and what it approves, reads the school week in the 40-minute units KHDA actually counts, sets out the mandatory subjects and the rules around them, separates a tutoring permit from a qualification from an examiner claim, publishes what the market charges in AED with the sources attached, and ends at the equivalency file. Teaching is delivered as one-to-one online IB tuition over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the Emirates; that service exists only in India.
