expert-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: Four IB programmes run in UAE private schools, and each one meets the emirate authority at a different point. The notes below are about that contact: who inspects it, what sits alongside it on the timetable, and what the programme needs from outside support in this country rather than in general.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units, no external examinations, and an assessment culture built on teacher judgement and the exhibition in the final year. Reports describe learner attributes rather than percentages, which is why PYP parents often cannot tell whether a child is behind until the move into MYP exposes it. Support at this stage is diagnostic: reading fluency, number sense, and the written English a later Language A course assumes.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai a PYP school still owes the mandatory UAE subjects, so a Year 4 timetable carries Arabic, Islamic Education for Muslim pupils and Social Studies beside its units of inquiry. KHDA requires Arab and non-Arab pupils to be taught these in separate classes, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited. Parents who assume an international primary curriculum means an international timetable are usually surprised by how much of the week is already committed.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, criterion-related assessment marked out of 8 per criterion, and a Personal Project in the final year. Because MYP reports marks against criteria A to D rather than a percentage, a pupil can look stable for three years and then hit the Diploma without ever having sat a timed paper of Diploma length. The common failure is unfamiliarity with examination conditions, not with content.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools run MYP to Year 9 and then switch the cohort to IGCSE, so a Sharjah or Dubai family can face a mid-school change of awarding body as well as of assessment style. That decision usually belongs to the school and its authority rather than to the parent, and it changes what a tutor should be doing in Year 9: building timed-paper technique and a syllabus-coded vocabulary the MYP never asked for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries internally assessed work worth a fixed share of the grade and externally marked papers worth the rest. The Diploma's difficulty in practice is scheduling: four or five internal deadlines, a 4,000-word essay and mock examinations all land inside about seven months of the second year.
programmes.countryNote: A UAE Diploma candidate carries the mandatory Ministry subjects on top of the six, so the week is fuller than the IB's own guidance assumes. The Diploma also ends in a certificate that the federal Ministry of Education has to equate before a UAE university will treat it as a secondary-school qualification, and no IB points threshold for that process has been read on moe.gov.ae, so nobody should publish one. Check it with the Ministry directly.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a service-learning element and a language-development component. It suits a student who wants IB subject rigour in two or three areas without carrying six. Assessment is a mix of IB-marked Diploma components and the career-related provider's own.
programmes.countryNote: CP is offered by a small number of UAE schools, so a family choosing it is usually choosing a specific school rather than a programme. The equivalency route for a CP leaver is the question to ask the Ministry before Year 12 rather than after results, because the certificate is not the Diploma and should not be assumed to attract the same treatment. Ask the school's coordinator to put the answer in writing.

expert-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: An expert IB tutor in the UAE is a subject specialist first. The notes below are deliberately about marks rather than about enthusiasm: what each course assesses, and the place where UAE candidates most often lose ground. Higher Level and Standard Level are treated as different jobs, because they are.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof-heavy route, and the one most engineering and economics faculties expect. Higher Level adds the option-free extended content and a third paper. Marks leak in unstructured questions where a correct answer carries no method, and in the exploration, where students pick a topic too large to analyse inside the mark scheme.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-permitted work. The calculator is not optional, and candidates who have not learned their own model's statistical menus lose time they cannot recover. The common error is treating it as the easier course: Higher Level Applications is a demanding statistics syllabus, not a reduced version of Analysis.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields, waves and the quantitative core, with Higher Level extension inside most themes. UAE candidates commonly arrive from an IGCSE course that rewarded recall and then meet papers that reward derivation. Uncertainty treatment in the internal investigation is a reliable place to find missing marks.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity across the two-year syllabus, with organic mechanisms and energetics carrying disproportionate weight in practice. Higher Level widens every topic rather than adding separate ones. The scientific investigation needs a question narrow enough to control, which is where most of the avoidable marks go.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Concept-led content with heavy terminology and a data-handling paper that rewards reading the stem precisely. Command terms decide the mark: 'outline' and 'explain' are not the same instruction, and candidates who answer the question they expected rather than the one printed lose whole bands.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, assessed partly through the portfolio of commentaries on real news articles. Diagrams must be labelled to earn marks, and evaluation has to weigh rather than list. Higher Level adds quantitative work that catches out students who chose the subject to avoid calculation.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools, techniques and theory applied to real organisations, with a research project at Higher Level and a written commentary at Standard Level. The subject looks approachable and marks badly when answers stay descriptive. Application to the named organisation, not general theory, is where the grade is decided.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis, a comparative essay at Higher Level, the individual oral and the learner portfolio. For the many UAE candidates working in English as an additional language, the barrier is rarely comprehension; it is building an argument about form and effect under timed conditions.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic runs in two directions in UAE schools: as a Diploma language course and as a mandatory Ministry subject. The Diploma course is assessed by the IB; the mandatory lessons follow Ministry content that a school may not substitute without permission. A tutor should know which of the two a family is asking about.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Computational thinking, systems and a solution-development project. Higher Level adds abstract data structures and the case study, which changes the revision shape entirely because the case study is published in advance. Students who leave the project until the second year rarely recover the marks.

expert-ib-tutor.regionsTitle: The seven emirates, and the authority above each school
expert-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: Where you live changes which authority holds your child's school file, how deep the local IB cohort is, and what time a weekly session can realistically start. These notes are about those three things rather than about scenery, because they are what actually shapes a tutoring plan.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA oversees the quality of private education here, across 227 private schools and 387,441 pupils in 2024-25, with seventeen curricula in the market. Three of the seven schools opening for 2026-27 are IB. Deep cohorts, the widest subject coverage, and the heaviest traffic penalty on any travelling tutor.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff, as reported in the press, bar teachers from paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school, which is the one local rule most likely to affect an informal arrangement.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, with a smaller private market than the island. Families here routinely find a Higher Level science or economics specialist scarce locally, which is where online delivery stops being a compromise and starts being the only way to reach a subject specialist at all.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Many Sharjah families attend school in Dubai, so the commute rather than the regulator usually decides whether a 4pm or a 7pm session is realistic.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority, so inspection and curriculum questions go to the Ministry. The local IB cohort is small and spread thin, and travelling tutors quote accordingly once the Dubai-Ajman run is priced in.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Distance from the Dubai school belt makes a visiting Higher Level specialist genuinely hard to arrange twice a week, whatever the advertised rate.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education supervision, an east-coast school run, and the smallest IB pool in the country. A live video lesson removes the mountain road from the arithmetic entirely, which is the only thing that makes a Physics Higher Level specialist available to a Fujairah family on a Tuesday evening.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under Ministry of Education supervision. Many secondary pupils travel to Sharjah, Ajman or Dubai for school, so the evening window opens late. Session times here are set by the return journey rather than by the school bell, and a plan that ignores that collapses in the first fortnight.

schoolClusters.note: The deepest IB market in the country, inspected by KHDA, with published inspection reports a parent can read before enrolling or before hiring anyone. Pupils we support attend schools across this cluster; the point of naming them is that a tutor should know which authority inspects the school and what its last report said about the relevant subject.

ADEK territory, where the licensing and accreditation of private schools sits with the emirate. Diploma cohorts are smaller than Dubai's and subject coverage at Higher Level is patchier, which is the practical reason online matching matters more here than it does on Sheikh Zayed Road.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.note: A mixed market of IB and British-curriculum schools under SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and the federal Ministry elsewhere. Fewer schools means fewer local specialists, and a longer evening once the commute home is counted.

expert-ib-tutor.modesIntro: Four ways families use an IB specialist, all of them delivered as one-to-one online IB tuition over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The first one exists because of this page's subject: before anything is taught, somebody has to read the system the student is sitting inside.

modes.title: A two-session school-system read
modes.description: The opening block is diagnostic in two directions. One session covers the subject: a past-paper question set, marked against the real criteria, to find where the marks are going. The other covers the system: which authority inspects the school, what its last published report said, which awarding body and series the student is entered for, what the school's own internal deadlines are, and how much of the week the mandatory Ministry subjects already hold.

modes.description: The default pattern: one or two sessions a week with the same IB Higher Level subject specialist, scheduled in the evening window the family actually has. Lessons run over live video with a shared screen and annotation, so working through a mark scheme line by line is possible in a way it is not across a kitchen table with one copy of the paper.

sections.heading: What a UAE parent is actually hiring when they search for an expert IB tutor
paragraphs: Expertise in this market splits into four things, and parents can verify two of them. Subject depth and assessment literacy show up inside two lessons. Legal standing is checkable if you ask. System knowledge, the fourth, is the one nobody tests for, and it is the one that decides whether the plan survives February.

The reason it matters is sequencing. A tutor who knows Chemistry Higher Level perfectly but does not know that the school's internal scientific-investigation deadline falls six weeks before the IB's own upload window will build a revision plan that collides with coursework. A tutor who does not know the family's school runs the Cambridge March series will prepare for a June paper. Neither failure is a subject failure.

The table below is the shortlist test worth running. Three of the four rows can be settled by asking a direct question before the first paid hour. The fourth is settled by listening: a tutor who has taught UAE candidates will name the authority above your school without being prompted, and will ask for the school's internal deadline list rather than the syllabus.

One more distinction is worth drawing before any money changes hands. A platform's expertise and a tutor's expertise are different objects, and parents are usually sold the first while hiring the second. A well-run service can match accurately, disclose a permit position and hold a replacement policy, and still put a Standard Level generalist into a Higher Level slot because nobody else was free that week. So the question to ask is not what the company knows. It is what the named person teaching your child on Tuesday has taught before, at which level, and how many times.
bullets: Ask which authority inspects the school; an expert answers without looking it up
Ask for the school's internal deadline list, not the published syllabus
Ask which awarding body and series the student is entered for
Ask what the mandatory UAE subjects take out of the week

sections.heading: The authority above your child's school, and what it actually approves
paragraphs: Private schools in the UAE answer to one of five bodies, and the differences between them are larger than parents expect. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi. SPEA regulates private education in Sharjah, and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does so in its emirate. For Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah the federal Ministry of Education plays the supervisory role.

Two of those authorities reach further than inspection. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. So a parent in Al Khan asking why the school will not adopt a different assessment pattern is asking a question the school cannot answer on its own. There is also a federal floor underneath all of it: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

For a tutoring plan this settles three things. First, where to read the inspection report, because each authority publishes its own and the bands are not interchangeable between them. Second, who sets the mandatory-subject requirement that is already eating weekly time. Third, which body a parent writes to when a school's arrangement for a Diploma subject looks wrong. None of that sits in the IB's own documentation, because none of it is the IB's business.

sections.heading: Three IB schools open in Dubai this year: the first-cohort problem
paragraphs: Dubai's private sector is growing fast enough to change what a new Diploma cohort looks like. Seven private schools open for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 places. Six opened during 2025-26, and enrolment rose 6%. For most families that is good news about fees and commutes. For a DP1 student it creates a specific, unglamorous problem.

A new IB school has no departmental archive. There is no shelf of marked internal assessments from previous years to show a student what a top-band investigation looks like, no record of how the school's own predicted grades have tracked against final results, and no teacher in the room who has taken a cohort through the second year at that site. The teaching may be excellent and the systems may still be two years from settled.

That changes what outside support is for. In an established school the useful tutor fills a subject gap. In a first cohort the useful tutor supplies the institutional memory the school does not yet have: what a criterion-A mark band actually reads like, how long a 4,000-word essay really takes from question to final draft, and which internal deadlines slip when four of them land in the same fortnight. It is also a reason to ask the coordinator directly how many of the teaching team have examined or taught the second year before. A new school that answers that question openly is usually the better bet of the two.
bullets: Ask how many of the Diploma teaching team have taught the second year at that school
Ask to see exemplar internally assessed work; a first cohort usually has none of its own
Treat the first set of predicted grades as untested rather than wrong
Expect internal deadlines to move, and build the revision plan with slack in it

sections.heading: The school week in 40-minute units, and where a session can actually sit
paragraphs: KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. That is a piece of regulatory plumbing nobody puts on a tutoring page, and it explains something parents find baffling: why a timetable with six Diploma subjects, Theory of Knowledge and three mandatory subjects has so little air in it.

The practical consequence is that the hour you are buying is competing with a week that is already allocated. A Diploma student in a Dubai school is carrying Arabic, Islamic Education where applicable and Social Studies on top of six courses, each of those lessons counted in units the school has to account for. Add a 40-minute commute from Sharjah or Al Nahda and the usable evening starts later than the school bell suggests.

So the scheduling question is not what time suits the tutor. It is which slot survives mocks, Ramadan and the fortnight when two internal deadlines collide. Sessions that sit immediately after a long commute get cancelled; sessions in the last hour before bed get attended and not absorbed. The table is the honest version, built from school finish times and the hours UAE families actually report as workable. Two shorter sessions a week usually beat one long one in an exam year, for the same reason a school does not teach Physics in a single three-hour block.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies: the content rule nobody mentions
paragraphs: These subjects are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. They are not optional extras for an IB family, and they are not marked by the IB. They appear on the school report, and they take weekly time.

The rules around them are specific. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is taught in Arabic for Arab pupils; non-Arab pupils receive Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Schools must also ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach these subjects.

The line that matters most for tutoring is the content rule: for these subjects, the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the MoE, is strictly prohibited. A tutor cannot bring a better scheme of work to an Islamic Education lesson. Support has to run on the school's own set material, aimed at the school's own assessments. Any provider offering an alternative curriculum for these subjects is describing something a Dubai school is not permitted to use.

sections.heading: Permit, qualification, examiner: three claims, and the one we will not make
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school pupils aged 15 to 18 and university students. The official route is MoHRE's own service, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, no amount should be quoted to you.

A permit is not a qualification, and neither is a company permit. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That permit says a centre may operate. It says nothing about whether the person in front of your child has taught Higher Level Economics.

The third claim is the one this page declines. IB Gram does not describe its tutors as IB or Cambridge examiners, because current examiner status is not something we can evidence for an individual, and because examiner status is routinely used to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content that no examiner has. What we will tell you is the subject, the level and the teaching history, and the ADEK position worth knowing: its professional-ethics rules, as reported in the press, prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges, and which band buys a specialist
paragraphs: These are market rates, published by other providers, not IB Gram's price list. Reading them matters because the spread is enormous and the labels are unregulated: the same hour is advertised at AED 45 and at AED 650, and nothing in either advert explains the difference. Figures below are drawn from competitor pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, as read in October 2026.

Monthly patterns in the same market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Set that against school fees that KHDA confirmed in May 2026 will not increase for private schools in Dubai for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

The useful question is not which band is cheapest but which band buys a subject specialist at the level your child is taking. Below roughly AED 150 an hour the market is largely university students and generalists, which can be the right purchase for Standard Level consolidation and is a poor one for Higher Level content. IB Gram does not publish an hourly list on this page; the first lesson is free, with no card required, and the rate is quoted for the actual subject and level after that.

sections.heading: A tutor at a UAE address against live one-to-one online
paragraphs: Home tutoring is a real market here and the question deserves a straight answer. A visiting tutor in Dubai or Abu Dhabi charges between roughly AED 180 and AED 500 an hour, often with a two-hour minimum, and the pool a family can actually draw from is whoever is willing to drive to that address in the evening traffic. For a Standard Level maths top-up that pool is usually adequate. For Chemistry Higher Level, or Computer Science, or Economics Higher Level in Fujairah, it frequently contains nobody.

IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one online IB tuition over live video. Tutors are not sent to a UAE address; home visits are part of the service only in India. The case for the online format here is not that it is a cheaper substitute. It is that the constraint which decides the outcome is subject match at the right level, and geography is what breaks subject match. An Al Ain family gets the Higher Level specialist rather than the nearest available adult.

There is a second, duller advantage. A shared screen is better than a shared table for the specific work that moves IB grades: putting a mark scheme and a student's script side by side, annotating in two colours, and saving the result so the student can re-read it the night before. Session recordings and notes survive; a kitchen-table conversation does not. A student who can re-read last week's annotated script before this week's lesson arrives already halfway through it.

sections.heading: Three bodies set the dates, and one gives your centre a zone
paragraphs: UAE families often sit two awarding bodies across one school career, and the calendars behave differently. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential that the correct version of the timetable for your zone is used, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used.

The Cambridge March 2027 series shows why entry deadlines sit so far ahead of the papers: the examination period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due 27 November 2026, forecast grades 27 February 2027, results on Direct 13 May and certificates in late June. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official PDF is what a plan should be built on.

For the IB, this page deliberately stops short. UAE schools sit the May session, and that is the right anchor for a two-year plan, but ibo.org blocks automated checking and no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. So no IB date is published here. Ask the school's IB coordinator, or read ibo.org directly, and treat any tutoring website that prints precise IB dates without a source as having guessed.

sections.heading: The equivalency file: five subjects, grade E, and two exclusions
paragraphs: A UAE secondary certificate needs federal equivalency before universities here treat it as one, and the requirements are published per curriculum track. On the British track, a student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five.

That five-subject rule is worth knowing precisely, because at least one page ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. On the American track, English proficiency is met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying.

For the IB there is a gap, and this page leaves it a gap. The source that sets out the British and American tracks states no IB points threshold, so no IB equivalency figure is published here and none should be taken from a tutoring site. Open the file with the Ministry or your emirate's attestation authority in the first year of the Diploma rather than after results day, and let the official channel tell you what the certificate needs. IB Gram describes this process; it does not perform it, submit it or guarantee its outcome, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the test a tutoring provider cannot half-pass
paragraphs: Internally assessed work is the student's own, and the IB treats a breach as malpractice with consequences that fall on the candidate rather than on the provider who caused it. That asymmetry is the whole reason to be strict about it. A provider in this market advertises finished internal assessments at AED 3,750; buying one risks a diploma for the price of a few tutoring hours, and there is no version of that trade that favours the family.

The permitted boundary is narrower than most advertising implies, and it is also genuinely useful. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what a criterion descriptor is asking for, help a student narrow a research question to something the mark scheme can reward, discuss a plan before data is collected, and give feedback as questions on a draft the student produced. A tutor may not supply sentences for submission, rewrite a paragraph into its final form, hand over a finished piece of coursework, or take a Personal Project off a student's hands.

Two practical habits keep a family on the right side of it. Keep the student's own drafts dated, so authorship is demonstrable if a coordinator asks. And declare outside support honestly when the school asks about it; the question exists precisely so that legitimate tutoring can be acknowledged. Schools are also not permitted to receive reproduced syllabus documents, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables from a tutor; those are cited and linked from the official sites, not handed over as downloads.

process.title: Tell us the school, not just the subject
process.description: The first message should name the school, the emirate, the year group, the subject and the level. That tells us which authority inspects the school, which awarding body is likely in play, and how much of the week the mandatory Ministry subjects already hold. It takes a parent two minutes and removes a fortnight of guessing.

process.title: A free first lesson with a marked diagnostic
process.description: The first lesson costs nothing and requires no card. It is not a sales call: the tutor sets real past-paper questions, marks them against the published criteria, and says where the marks are going. If the diagnostic shows the problem is scheduling or coursework sequencing rather than content, we say so.

process.title: Read the school's calendar before the plan is written
process.description: We ask for the school's own internal deadline list, the mock window and the examination series the student is entered for. Internal deadlines are set by the school, not the IB, and they are what a revision plan collides with. The plan is then built backwards from those dates.

process.title: Fix a slot that survives March
process.description: A weekly slot is chosen against the commute, the after-school timetable and Ramadan hours rather than against the tutor's convenience. Sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan without a change in rate. A slot that only works in October is not a slot.

process.title: Review against marks, and change the tutor if needed
process.description: Progress is reviewed on marked work and on the criteria that are still costing bands, not on how the lessons felt. If the match is wrong, a different specialist takes over and the diagnostic carries across so the new tutor does not start from nothing.

whyPoints.title: The authority above your school is named, not implied
whyPoints.description: Every plan starts by identifying which of the five bodies holds the school's file and what its published report says about the relevant subject. IB Gram holds no permit, approval or accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and does not claim any.

whyPoints.title: Matched on subject and level, not on distance
whyPoints.description: Tutors are matched to the course and the level, so an Al Ain or Fujairah family reaches the same Higher Level specialist a Dubai family does. Where no specialist is free for a subject and level, we say that plainly rather than putting a generalist in the slot and hoping.

whyPoints.title: The mandatory subjects are treated as real
whyPoints.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies sit on the timetable because the school's licence requires them, and support for them runs on the school's own set material. For these subjects KHDA prohibits different or additional content without prior MoE permission, so no substitute scheme is offered.

whyPoints.title: Figures carry a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, read in October 2026, and presented as the market rather than as our price. No satisfaction percentage, star rating or score statistic appears here, because none could be produced with its sample size and method.

whyPoints.title: Coursework support stops where honesty does
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, explain criteria and give feedback on the student's own drafts. Nothing is supplied for submission, and we would rather lose the booking than put a diploma at risk. Dates we cannot source, including IB session dates, are left off the page rather than guessed.

faqs.question: What does expertise in the UAE school system actually consist of?
faqs.answer: Four things, in practice. Knowing which of the five authorities inspects your child's school and what its report said. Knowing what the mandatory Ministry subjects take out of the week, and that their content cannot be substituted. Knowing which awarding body and series the student is entered for, and that Cambridge allocates centres to one of six timetable zones. And knowing that an IB or IGCSE certificate needs federal equivalency before a UAE university treats it as a secondary qualification. A tutor can be excellent at Chemistry Higher Level and know none of this, which is how plans collide with coursework deadlines in February.

faqs.question: Is there a public register where I can look up an IB tutor's credentials?
faqs.answer: No single register exists. There are three separate things to check and none of them is one list. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is the legal permission to tutor privately; ask the tutor to show it. A teaching qualification is a document the tutor holds and can send you. IB course experience is not registered anywhere, so it is established by asking how many cohorts they have taught at that level and by a marked diagnostic in the first lesson. Treat any claim you cannot test as unproven, including examiner claims.

faqs.question: Does the authority that inspects my child's school also sign off its assessment methods?
faqs.answer: In two emirates, yes. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so assessment arrangements are not the school's alone to change. KHDA in Dubai oversees the quality of private education and sets mandatory-subject requirements including instructional time. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. In Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools directly. That is why a tutor proposing to replace the school's scheme of work is often proposing something the school cannot accept.

faqs.question: Dubai is adding 16,846 private school places. Does that make a Diploma specialist easier to find?
faqs.answer: Not immediately. Seven private schools open for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three IB, and six opened the year before while enrolment rose 6%. More school places create more Diploma candidates faster than they create experienced Diploma teachers, and the IB accounts for about 7% of Dubai's private-school enrolment, so the specialist pool for one Higher Level subject stays thin. Expansion helps with fees, choice and commute times. It does not solve the problem of finding someone who has taught Computer Science Higher Level through a full second year.

faqs.question: Our school's Diploma cohort is its first. Who holds the past papers and the mark archive?
faqs.answer: Nobody at the school yet, and that is the honest answer worth planning around. A new IB school has no shelf of previously marked internal assessments to show a student what a top band reads like, no history of how its predicted grades have tracked against final results, and often no teacher on site who has taken a cohort through the second year there. Ask the coordinator how many of the teaching team have. Outside support in a first cohort is largely supplying that missing institutional memory: exemplar standards, realistic timelines and criterion-level feedback.

faqs.question: Does a 40-minute school lesson mean a tutoring session should be 40 minutes too?
faqs.answer: No. The 40-minute unit is a regulatory measure, not a pedagogical one: KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that no mandatory subject lesson runs under 25 minutes. For one-to-one work, 60 minutes suits weekly consolidation and 90 suits exam-technique or coursework sessions where a full paper has to be marked and reworked. During Ramadan, shorter post-Iftar sessions usually work better than long ones.

faqs.question: Is Islamic Education taught in English for a non-Arab child, and does that change the tutoring?
faqs.answer: For non-Arab pupils, KHDA requires Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies to be taught in the school's licensed-curriculum language, which in most IB schools means English. Arab pupils receive Islamic Education and Arabic as a first language in Standard Arabic, and the two groups must be taught in separate classes; combined classes are strictly prohibited. It changes tutoring in one specific way: support should match the stream and language the school has placed the child in, and work from that stream's set material rather than a translation of the other one.

faqs.question: Why does IB Gram not describe any of its tutors as an IB examiner?
faqs.answer: Because current examiner status is not something we can evidence for an individual, and an unevidenced claim is worth nothing to you. The claim is also often used to imply privileged access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, which no examiner appointment provides. What we will tell you instead is checkable: the subject, the level, how many cohorts the tutor has taught, and a marked diagnostic in the free first lesson. If another provider makes the examiner claim, ask what evidence exists for the named subject and component.

faqs.question: A tutor says they hold a KHDA permit. What is that permit actually for?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly for a centre rather than a person. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute: initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That permit says premises may operate. It says nothing about the individual teaching your child. The permit that covers an individual giving private lessons is the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Ask which of the two is being referred to, and ask to see it.

faqs.question: What should a tutoring quote show me in writing before we pay anything?
faqs.answer: Six things. The named subject and level, not just the board. The session length and the rate per session, with whether VAT is included and a TRN if one is held. The tutor's permit position. Who teaches if that tutor becomes unavailable. The cancellation terms, including who absorbs a late cancellation. And the conditions attached to any free trial, stated on the same page as the word free. If a quote arrives without the subject level on it, the provider has not yet matched anyone to your child.

faqs.question: Which price band buys a subject specialist rather than a general tutor?
faqs.answer: In the UAE market, specialist IB and IGCSE support is advertised around AED 200 to AED 450 or more an hour, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's specialist band at 200 to 450+. Qualified but curriculum-general teachers sit roughly AED 150 to AED 300 online, with Unitors quoting IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Below about AED 150 the market is mostly university students, which can suit Standard Level consolidation and rarely suits Higher Level content. Those are other providers' published figures, read in October 2026, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: Are these lessons online, and why does IB Gram not offer visits in the Emirates?
faqs.answer: All UAE teaching is one-to-one online IB tuition over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are part of the service only in India. The reason is not cost: it is that subject match at the right level is what changes marks, and geography is the thing that breaks subject match. A family in Al Ain or Fujairah reaches the same Higher Level specialist a family in Dubai does. A shared screen also beats one printed copy of a mark scheme between two people, and the annotated version survives the session.

faqs.question: How do I tell an exam date that is sourced from one that is guesswork?
faqs.answer: Check whether the page names the awarding body's own document. Cambridge publishes key dates per series: for March 2027 the examination period is 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries 27 November 2026, forecast grades 27 February 2027 and results on Direct 13 May. Pearson publishes final and provisional timetables, with the November 2026 International GCSE timetable running to 19 November 2026. For the IB, ibo.org blocks automated checking, so no IB date appears on this page at all. A site printing precise IB dates without citing ibo.org has guessed.

faqs.question: Should we handle the Ministry of Education equivalency file ourselves?
faqs.answer: Yes, through the official channel, and start it in the first Diploma year rather than after results. The requirements are published per track: the British route needs five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at E. No IB points threshold has been read on moe.gov.ae, so do not accept one from a tutoring website. IB Gram describes the process and does not submit, perform or guarantee it, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

faqs.question: A tutor offered to take my son's Extended Essay from first draft to finish. Should we accept?
faqs.answer: No. Internally assessed work must be the student's own, and the consequences of malpractice fall on the candidate rather than on whoever offered the shortcut. One provider in this market advertises finished internal assessments at AED 3,750; that risks a whole diploma. What a tutor may legitimately do is teach the content, explain what each criterion is asking for, help narrow a research question, discuss a plan before data is collected, and return feedback as questions on a draft your son produced. Keep his dated drafts, and declare outside support when the coordinator asks.

faqs.question: Our child's school is inspected by the Ministry rather than KHDA. Does that limit anything?
faqs.answer: It changes where you read the inspection report and who you write to, not what your child can achieve. The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, so inspection and curriculum questions go federal rather than to an emirate authority. What does differ is local supply: these emirates have the smallest IB cohorts in the country, so a Higher Level specialist is genuinely hard to arrange locally twice a week. Online delivery removes that constraint, which is why it matters more here than in Dubai.

expert-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the school, then the subject
expert-ib-tutor.closingBody: If you are looking for an expert IB tutor in the UAE, the useful first message names the school and the emirate as well as the subject and the level. That tells us which authority inspects the school, which awarding body and series are in play, and how much of the week is already committed to the mandatory Ministry subjects. The first lesson is free, with no card required: a real diagnostic on past-paper questions, marked against the published criteria, and an honest answer about whether the problem is content, technique or the calendar. Lessons then run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the slot chosen to survive March.

fujairah.tutorsIntro: These are tutors open to Fujairah families this term, filtered to the IB Diploma and to Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE. Each card shows the syllabus a tutor has actually taught, the components they have marked, and their availability in Gulf Standard Time. If the specialist your child needs is not shown, name the subject and we will say plainly what the wait looks like.

intro.heading: Start with who inspects the school, not with who lives nearby
paragraphs: Fujairah is the only emirate whose coastline faces the Gulf of Oman, and the Hajar mountains stand between it and the rest of the country. That geography shapes tuition here more than anything else does. The private-school set in the emirate is small, the cohort for any single IB subject is smaller again, and a student taking Chemistry HL or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL may be one of three or four in the whole year group. There is frequently no local specialist in that subject at all. Not because the east coast lacks good teachers, but because the arithmetic of a small cohort never produces one.

Private schools in Fujairah are inspected by the federal Ministry of Education. Not by KHDA, which parents in Dubai quote at each other, and not by ADEK, which does the same job in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. Sharjah has its own authority, SPEA. On the east coast the inspecting body is the ministry itself, applying the national inspection framework with the same six judgement bands used across the country. The report it produces is the most useful free document a Fujairah parent holds, because it separates attainment from progress and judges both subject by subject and phase by phase. Read properly, it names the two subjects worth spending money on.

The report will not do your thinking for you. A judgement of Acceptable in secondary mathematics does not mean your child is fine. It means a cohort met the minimum standard the framework defines, across a year group holding thirty students with very different starting points, and a weaker student can sit a long way below that line without anyone writing it down. The framework judges a school. You are deciding about one student sitting one paper in one series. Those are different questions, and the distance between them is exactly where one-to-one teaching earns its fee.

Every lesson IB Gram arranges for a family here runs online, one to one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. We say that in the first hundred words because the alternative on this coast is not really an alternative. Driving a Chemistry HL specialist from Sharjah over the Wadi Ham road twice a week is either not going to happen or is going to be paid for in travel time dressed up as teaching. Online one-to-one tuition in Fujairah buys the specialist instead of the commute.

So this page is built around the inspection question, because in Fujairah that question decides everything downstream: what the school can realistically cover, which subjects are carried by one teacher rather than three, and whether the gap in front of you is a whole-cohort pattern or personal to your child. Below you will find the six bands and what each one implies for a parent, the regulator map of the east coast, market rates in AED with every figure attributed, the May session counted backwards month by month, assessment weightings by paper, the Internal Assessment criteria letter by letter, the academic-honesty line a tutor does not cross, and the Ministry of Education equivalency route into UAE universities.
bullets: Fujairah's private schools answer to the Ministry of Education; Khor Fakkan and Kalba, minutes up the same coast road, are Sharjah and fall under SPEA.
Market rates for a qualified online subject tutor in the UAE run roughly AED 150-300 an hour; visiting tuition runs AED 180-500 once travel is inside the fee.
IB results for the May session are published on 6 July; registration for that session closes with your school in mid-November of the year before.
A Maths exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria, A to E; the science investigation is marked out of 24 across four.
Arabic, Islamic Studies and UAE Social Studies are ministry requirements sitting alongside the IB or IGCSE timetable rather than inside it.
Lessons run online, one to one, over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the recording and annotated script kept by the student.

fujairah.programmesIntro: Four programmes cover almost every Fujairah student who asks us for help: the IB Middle Years Programme, the IB Diploma, Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. The transitions between them are where marks disappear, because each one assesses differently and the east coast rarely has two teachers in a subject to smooth the handover.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, and converts the total to a 1-7 grade using published boundaries. There are no papers in the IGCSE sense until the optional eAssessment in MYP 5. The habit it builds is extended, criterion-referenced writing: a student is rewarded for method, communication and reflection, not only for the right answer. Students who are strong here tend to be the ones who later write a clean Internal Assessment, because the criteria vocabulary is already familiar.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students in Fujairah usually hit their first real wall at the move into DP mathematics, where a criterion-marked investigation is replaced by a timed Paper 1 with no calculator. Because year groups on the east coast are small, the MYP 5 class and the DP 1 class are often taught by the same person, so a gap in algebraic fluency can travel intact from one to the other. We diagnose from MYP criterion A and C scores before assuming the problem is the new course.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject is graded 1-7, and TOK with the Extended Essay together contribute up to three bonus points, for a maximum of 45. Twenty-four points is the Diploma pass threshold, subject to the IB's conditions on failing conditions and minimum grades. Most of the grade is external: written papers sat in the session, with the internally assessed component worth 20-30% depending on the subject.
programmes.countryNote: The practical problem for a Fujairah DP student is subject-level isolation. Full Diploma provision is concentrated in Dubai, Sharjah and Abu Dhabi, so east-coast families are either commuting across the mountains, boarding, or studying in a small cohort where one HL subject has a single teacher and no second opinion. An IB Diploma tutor on the UAE east coast is therefore usually the student's only source of component-specific feedback: the second reader on an exploration, and the person who has marked Paper 3 before.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses assessed by syllabus code, with Core and Extended tiers in several subjects. Mathematics 0580 splits into Core, capped at grade C, and Extended, which reaches A*. Sciences run as separate 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology, or as Co-ordinated Sciences 0654. Most science syllabuses now assess practical skills through a written alternative-to-practical paper rather than a live examined practical, which matters for any student preparing outside a school laboratory.
programmes.countryNote: Tier entry is the decision that catches Fujairah families, and it is made by the school in late February for the June series. A student entered for 0580 Core cannot be awarded above a C however well the paper goes, and the entry is not easily reversed afterwards. A Cambridge IGCSE 0580 tutor who has taught both tiers can tell you by November whether Extended is realistic, which is early enough to matter. We ask for the mock script, not the mock grade, to make that call.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's International GCSE runs the same two-year span with different codes and a different rhythm: Mathematics A is 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1, English Language A 4EA1. There is a January series as well as the summer one, which gives a student a second sitting inside the same school year. Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher, with papers of equal weight rather than one calculator-free paper carrying a disproportionate share.
programmes.countryNote: Mixed-board timetables are common on the east coast, because small schools pick whichever syllabus suits the staff they have. A Fujairah student can easily sit Cambridge sciences and Edexcel mathematics in the same summer, with two different formula booklets and two different grade scales. An IGCSE tutor in Fujairah needs to know which board owns which subject before the first session, so we take the exact codes from the school's entry list rather than guessing from the textbook.

fujairah.subjectsIntro: These are the IB Diploma subjects Fujairah families ask about most, and each description names what the component actually assesses rather than restating the subject title. Where a subject is commonly taught by a single teacher in a small east-coast cohort, a second specialist reading the same work is worth more than extra hours.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency under time pressure, with HL carrying proof by induction, complex numbers and a separate Paper 3 of long structured investigations. A Maths Analysis and Approaches HL tutor spends most of the first month on Paper 1 technique, because the no-calculator paper is where a capable student most often loses marks they already know how to earn.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use, with the graphic display calculator central rather than incidental. HL adds matrices, graph theory and more demanding statistical inference. The common failure is treating AI as the easier route: the content differs from AA rather than sitting below it, and several engineering and mathematics degrees still expect AA.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Paper 1 splits into multiple choice and a data-based section; Paper 2 is extended response and carries 44% of the grade. Organic mechanisms and energetics are where east-coast students most often stall. An IB Chemistry HL tutor works from the student's own marked scripts, because the recurring loss is command-term precision rather than missing content.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields reward careful algebra; the data-based questions in Paper 1B reward reading a graph properly. HL extends into rigid-body mechanics, induction and quantum phenomena. Students who arrive from MYP science without strong equation manipulation tend to lose marks in rearrangement and unit work rather than in physics.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of terminology plus a demanding scientific investigation. The syllabus is organised around unifying themes, so a question can cross topics a student revised separately. Marks go missing in explain and outline questions where an answer lists facts without connecting them to the stated context.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three Internal Assessment commentaries of up to 800 words each, worth 20% at HL and 30% at SL, plus the HL-only Paper 3 at 30% with its quantitative and policy-evaluation questions. The commentary is where most of the recoverable marks sit, because it is graded on the application of a single key concept, not on the quality of the news article chosen.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with Paper 1 built on a pre-released case and Paper 2 on unseen stimulus and quantitative tools. The Internal Assessment differs by level: HL writes a research project on a real organisation, SL a commentary on supporting documents. Evaluation, not description, is the examiner's demand in the higher mark bands.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is a guided analysis of an unseen non-literary text, 2h15 at HL and 1h15 at SL. Paper 2 is a comparative essay on studied works. HL adds the 1,200-1,500 word HL Essay. Students in the UAE often have stronger literary than non-literary reading, so Paper 1 is usually the priority.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic A treats Arabic as a language of literature and textual analysis; Arabic B is acquisition, assessed through listening, reading, writing and an individual oral. Choosing between them affects both the DP grade and the ministry's expectations, and the choice is harder to reverse than families assume.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper 1 covers system fundamentals and computational thinking; HL adds abstract data structures and a case study published annually. The solution development component rewards a documented design process. Self-taught coders routinely lose marks on documentation and testing rather than on code.

fujairah.igcseSubjectsIntro: Fujairah's private schools lean towards IGCSE at Years 10 and 11, often with a mixed board list. These are the syllabuses we are asked for most, with the codes to check against your school's entry sheet before anything else is agreed.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: The tier decision dominates everything. 0580 Core is capped at grade C; Extended reaches A*. Edexcel 4MA1 splits Foundation and Higher across two equally weighted papers. Most lost marks in the Extended paper are in algebraic fractions, transformation of graphs and multi-step problems where working is not shown.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
igcseSubjects.description: A bridge course for students heading to A-level or DP mathematics, covering calculus, trigonometric identities, vectors and series. It is taught in very few east-coast schools, so students often sit it with minimal timetabled support, which makes it one of the most common online requests we receive.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism are the reliable difficulty, followed by the alternative-to-practical paper, which asks students to design and critique an experiment in writing. Working through past alternative-to-practical papers transfers directly, because the question types repeat across series.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry decide the grade more than any other topic, and a student who cannot do mole calculations confidently will cap out regardless of how much organic chemistry is memorised. Qualitative analysis tables and ionic equations are the other reliable mark sources.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Definitions have to be exact, and extended-response questions reward structured answers over long ones. Students lose marks on genetic crosses, transport in plants and the data-interpretation questions that ask them to describe a trend before explaining it.

igcseSubjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
igcseSubjects.description: Three sciences compressed into a double award, usually chosen so a student can keep a broad subject list. The compression is the problem: topic coverage per hour is high and there is little classroom time to revisit anything. Revision has to be timetabled against the syllabus, not against the textbook chapters.

igcseSubjects.name: First Language English (0500) and English as a Second Language (0510)
igcseSubjects.description: 0500 assesses reading passages and directed writing; 0510 assesses listening, reading, writing and speaking for second-language users. Placing a student in the wrong one is common in schools with mixed intakes, and it is a decision worth checking against a timed piece of writing rather than a teacher's impression.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
igcseSubjects.description: Both reward structured evaluation and a worked diagram. In Economics the diagram is the answer, not decoration, and an unlabelled axis costs marks every time. Business Studies questions carrying eight or more marks need an applied judgement tied to the case, not a general advantage-and-disadvantage list.

fujairah.regionsTitle: Fujairah, the east coast and the places the regulator map changes
fujairah.regionsIntro: Fujairah emirate runs along the Gulf of Oman from Dibba in the north to the Omani border in the south, with inland pockets reached through the mountain passes. Several places on this coast are not in Fujairah at all, which changes who inspects the school and which term dates apply.

regions.name: Fujairah city, Faseel and Sakamkam
regions.note: The emirate's centre of gravity: the corniche, the port and most of its private schools. Nearly every private-school option within a short drive is here, which means one disappointing option in a subject leaves very little to switch to.

regions.name: Dibba Al-Fujairah
regions.note: The northern end of the coast, where a single town is split three ways between Fujairah, Sharjah and Oman. Dibba Al-Fujairah tuition requests usually come from families with a 40-minute school run each way and no appetite for a second one in the evening.

regions.name: Qidfa and Mirbah
regions.note: Coastal villages between Fujairah city and the Sharjah exclaves, served mainly by ministry schools. Families here are the clearest case for online tuition: the specialist does not exist within reach, and the coast road is the only way in or out.

regions.name: Al Aqah and Sharm
regions.note: The northern hotel strip, with a working population on shift patterns. Scheduling matters more than subject choice for these families, and a fixed evening slot that survives a parent's rota is worth more than a nominally cheaper hour.

regions.name: Masafi
regions.note: A mountain village on the road to Ras Al Khaimah, split between the two emirates. Either side is inspected by the federal ministry, so the emirate boundary changes the address and the term calendar more than it changes the inspection framework.

regions.name: Bithnah and Wadi Ham
regions.note: The inland route through the Hajar mountains towards Sharjah, and the road any visiting tutor would have to drive. In practice it is the reason a twice-weekly visit from a Sharjah specialist prices itself out before teaching starts.

regions.name: Al Hayl and the inland valleys
regions.note: Small settlements behind Fujairah city, where school choice narrows to whatever is reachable in the morning. Connectivity is good enough for live video, which is the only part of the equation that has improved in the last few years.

regions.name: Khor Fakkan and Kalba
regions.note: Both are Sharjah exclaves on the east coast, 20 to 40 minutes from Fujairah city, and both are inspected by SPEA rather than the ministry. A parent comparing two schools across that line is comparing reports written under different authorities.

schoolClusters.city: Fujairah city and the east coast
schoolClusters.note: The emirate's private-school list is short and mostly British or Indian curriculum through to IGCSE. That is the whole point of this page: a short list means a small cohort, a small cohort means one teacher per subject, and one teacher per subject means no second opinion on an HL script.
schools: Our Own English High School, Fujairah

schoolClusters.note: The nearest alternatives across the mountains, and the schools east-coast families most often transfer into when a subject list runs out. Note that these sit under SPEA in Sharjah and under the federal ministry in Ras Al Khaimah, so the reports read differently even where the framework is shared.
schools: Scholars Indian School, Ras Al Khaimah

schoolClusters.note: Where full Diploma provision is actually concentrated, and where a Fujairah family relocating or boarding for Years 12 and 13 usually ends up looking. A student who stays on the east coast and studies online is competing with these cohorts in the same session, which is the honest reason component-level teaching matters.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School, Arabian Ranches

fujairah.modesIntro: Three ways families here actually book. All three are delivered online, one to one, over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, and all three produce a written record the student keeps. Group classes are not offered, because the whole argument for working online from the east coast is getting undivided specialist attention.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one by syllabus component
modes.description: A fixed slot with one tutor, planned against the specific component the evidence points at rather than the subject as a whole. sections.heading: Who inspects your child's school in Fujairah, and what the band actually tells you
paragraphs: Fujairah's private schools are inspected by the federal Ministry of Education, which applies the national school inspection framework used across the country. The framework issues a single overall judgement on a six-point scale: Outstanding, Very Good, Good, Acceptable, Weak and Very Weak. Acceptable is defined as the minimum standard, not as a middling result, and that single word is the one most often misread by parents on the east coast.

The reason it is misread is that the judgement describes a school, averaged over a cohort. Your decision concerns one student sitting one paper in one series. A school judged Good can hold a mathematics department that has lost two teachers in a year, and a school judged Acceptable can have a strong single teacher in the subject your child is weakest at. The overall band is where to start reading, not where to stop.

What to do with it is practical. Find the overall band, then find the subject-level attainment and progress judgements for your child's phase, then compare the two. Where the subject judgement sits below the school's overall band, the school knows it has a problem and is probably working on it. Where attainment is acceptable but progress is weak, the cohort is coasting. Where progress is strong and attainment is low, the teaching is working and the starting point was simply behind. Those three patterns call for three different tutoring plans, and only the last one is mostly about time.
bullets: Read the overall band first, then the subject and phase judgements underneath it.
Acceptable means the minimum standard was met, which is a floor rather than reassurance.
Attainment and progress are judged separately; the combination is what tells you something.
A subject judged below the school's overall band is the one to spend on first.

sections.heading: Reading a Ministry of Education inspection report as a tutoring brief
paragraphs: The framework judges six performance standards. Most parents read the first and skim the rest, which wastes the useful half of the document. The standards cover students' achievement; their personal and social development and innovation skills; teaching and assessment; the curriculum; the protection, care, guidance and support of students; and leadership and management. Each one has a practical consequence for a family deciding whether to buy tuition and what to buy.

Standard one is where the subject gets named. Standard three tells you whether marking is specific enough for your child to know why a mark was lost, which is the single most common reason a capable student plateaus. Standard four explains option blocks, and it is the standard that answers the question Fujairah parents ask most often: why is the subject my child wants not on the list? A narrow curriculum judgement in a small school is usually a staffing arithmetic problem rather than a policy choice.

Standard six matters more here than it would in Dubai. In a school with one teacher per IB subject, leadership and staffing judgements translate directly into continuity. A departure mid-year in a cohort of four HL students is not a gap the school can cover internally. That is the scenario where an outside specialist stops being an enhancement and becomes the only continuous reader of the student's work across the two years of the Diploma.

One more habit worth forming: read the report your school received two cycles ago alongside the current one. Inspection reports list recommendations, and the useful question is not what the school was told to improve but whether the same recommendation appears twice. A repeated recommendation in the subject your child is weakest at tells you the gap is structural and is unlikely to close inside the two years you have. A recommendation that has disappeared tells you the department has capacity and that your money is better spent elsewhere.

sections.heading: The regulator map of the east coast: the Ministry, SPEA and the Omani border
paragraphs: Nowhere else in the country is the question who regulates this school harder to answer than on this coast. Fujairah emirate is inspected by the federal Ministry of Education. Khor Fakkan and Kalba, both well inside the east coast and both a short drive from Fujairah city, are Sharjah exclaves and fall under the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Dibba is divided between Fujairah, Sharjah's Dibba Al-Hisn and Oman's Dibba Al-Baya, which puts three education systems inside one town.

This is not pedantry. The regulator sets the inspection cycle, publishes the report in its own format, governs fee increases and issues the circulars that decide term dates and Ramadan timings. Two families living ten minutes apart can be working to different calendars and reading differently structured reports about schools they are directly comparing. A parent who assumes Dubai's rules apply because Dubai's rules are what the internet discusses will get the details wrong.

For tuition the practical consequences are smaller but real. Lesson scheduling has to follow the school's actual calendar rather than a national average, which is why we ask which authority publishes your school's term dates before fixing a weekly slot. Certificate attestation and equivalency, by contrast, are federal: the Ministry of Education handles those for every emirate, so a Khor Fakkan family and a Fujairah city family follow the same route there even though their schools answer to different inspectors.

The map also explains a pattern we see in enquiries. Families in Qidfa and Mirbah often have schools in two emirates within the same half-hour drive, and they compare an inspection report written by SPEA with one written by the ministry as though the two documents were interchangeable. They are not, in format or in publication cycle, even where the underlying standards are shared. If you are weighing two schools across that line, compare the subject-level attainment and progress judgements rather than the headline band, because those are the parts that mean the same thing in both reports.

sections.heading: What private tuition costs around Fujairah, in AED and with sources
paragraphs: Most competitor pages for this query publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not a currency any UAE family transacts in. Below are the AED bands we can attribute, taken from what providers publish and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table. They are market rates, not ours. IB Gram does not publish an hourly price list, because the right answer depends on the subject, the level and how many weeks remain before the session.

Two things distort these bands on the east coast. The first is travel. Any figure for a visiting tutor already has a drive priced into it, and from Fujairah that drive is longer than the lesson for most specialists. The second is scarcity: in a thin market the rate for a rare subject is set by availability rather than by qualification, which is how a generalist ends up charging specialist money for Chemistry HL. Monthly packages circulate too, commonly around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits.

What to do with the table is simple. Decide which band the teaching your child needs actually sits in, then check that what you are quoted matches that band rather than the band above it. A homework supervisor at AED 60 an hour is good value for homework supervision and poor value for an exploration that needs criterion-level feedback. Ask what the tutor has marked, not how many years they have taught.

sections.heading: A tutor in the room versus one-to-one online, measured from the east coast
paragraphs: Parents searching for a home tutor in Fujairah are asking a reasonable question, and it deserves a straight answer before anything is sold. Visiting tuition works where the specialist lives nearby. In Fujairah the specialist for a less common IB subject usually does not. Dubai and Sharjah are roughly 130 to 150 kilometres away by road, through either the Wadi Ham pass or the coast and Masafi routes, and a round trip of two to three hours sits around a 60-minute lesson.

That arithmetic produces one of two outcomes. Either the family pays for the drive, which is why visiting rates run to AED 500 an hour, or the family settles for whoever is local, which usually means a generalist covering three sciences. Neither is a good trade for an HL student. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses, and visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. Every lesson for a family here is delivered online, one to one, over live video.

The honest case for working this way is not that online is universally better. It is that the choice on this coast is between a specialist on a screen and a generalist in the room, and for a single named component the specialist wins. There are real losses: a tutor on video cannot read body language as well, and a student who will not engage without someone physically present is a poor fit. We would rather say that than pretend the format is costless.
