ib-diploma-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Most families arriving on this page have a DP1 or DP2 student, but the Diploma is not the only shape the IB takes in a UAE school. These are the four routes we support, and what each one means once the Ministry's own subject requirements are added to the timetable.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, one from each group with limited substitution, three taken at Higher Level and three at Standard Level. Each subject is graded 1 to 7, giving 42 points, with up to three more from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge taken together, for a maximum of 45. Twenty-four points is the floor, but the award also depends on separate Higher Level and Standard Level point thresholds, on no grade 1 appearing anywhere, and on CAS being completed and evidenced. Most of the grade sits in external papers; a fifth or so of several subjects is marked in school and moderated by the IB.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE the Diploma runs inside a school year shaped by the emirate authority and by the Ministry's mandatory subjects, so a DP student is carrying Arabic, Islamic Education or Social Studies on top of the six. That matters when you pick a weekly tuition slot: the evening is shorter than the subject list suggests, and Ramadan moves the whole school day for several weeks of the DP2 revision run.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme course candidate
programmes.description: A student can be registered for individual DP subjects rather than the full Diploma, receiving certificates for the courses sat. The subject teaching, the papers and the internally assessed components are the same, and the grading is the same 1 to 7 scale. What changes is that there is no 45-point total, no core requirement and no failing-condition arithmetic, because there is no Diploma being awarded. Universities read the certificates subject by subject, which makes the choice of which subjects to take unusually consequential.
programmes.countryNote: UAE families end up here for practical reasons: a mid-Diploma arrival from another curriculum, a serious illness in DP1, or a student who needs two strong Higher Levels for a named course rather than a full Diploma. Because the Ministry of Education's equivalency route is written around complete certificates, check the position with the school registrar and the Ministry's own channel before committing to the course route.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, the run-up to DP1
programmes.description: The two years before the Diploma are where the level choice is really made. MYP 4 and 5 use criterion-based assessment with achievement levels rather than examination papers, so a student can arrive in DP1 having never sat a timed paper under external conditions. The gap shows up first in Mathematics and the sciences, where Higher Level assumes fluency the criteria did not have to test, and second in extended writing against a word limit and a deadline.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools run the MYP and the Diploma on one campus, which is an advantage: the subject-choice meeting happens with teachers who know the DP option blocks. Use it. Ask in MYP 5 which Higher Levels the school can actually timetable next year, because the honest answer is sometimes narrower than the brochure and it is better heard a year early.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines at least two DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a service-learning element, personal and professional skills, and language development. It is graded differently from the Diploma: the DP courses keep the 1 to 7 scale while the career-related study is reported on its own terms. Students take it when they want recognised depth in two academic subjects alongside a vocational qualification rather than six academic subjects at once.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is offered by a small number of UAE schools, and university recognition varies by institution and by country, so the course-by-course conversation with an admissions office matters more here than on any other route. We support the DP course components; the career-related study belongs to the school and its partner provider.

ib-diploma-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects UAE families ask for most often, with what the assessment actually rewards. Online IB Diploma tuition in the UAE works subject by subject and level by level, so the first question we ask is never 'which year' but 'which paper, and which criterion'.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most UAE engineering and economics applicants need. Higher Level adds proof, deeper calculus and an extra paper, and the marks go on method shown rather than answers reached. The exploration is marked in school and moderated, and the commonest loss is a piece of correct mathematics with no genuine personal engagement or reflection attached to it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-heavy work, with the graphical display calculator assumed rather than tolerated. It suits business, psychology and design routes, but some UAE and overseas university courses still specify Analysis and Approaches, so the route choice should be checked against the named programme before DP1 begins, not in DP2.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Marks are lost in two predictable places: multi-step questions where no working is shown, and the internally assessed investigation where uncertainty is reported as a number with no account of where it came from. Higher Level adds topics and a longer paper, and the step up in algebraic fluency catches students arriving from criterion-assessed MYP science.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics generate most of the panic, but the grade usually turns on data handling and on the scientific investigation, which carries about a fifth of the subject. A Higher Level Chemistry tutor in Abu Dhabi spends as much time on how the method was justified as on the chemistry itself, because that is where the criteria put the marks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the trap. Students revise the recall and under-practise the command terms, so answers describe where the question said explain or evaluate. The investigation rewards a narrow, well-controlled question over an ambitious one, and the students who choose narrow in DP1 are reliably calmer in DP2.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks, and so does the evaluation sentence that most students leave out. Higher Level adds quantitative demands and a further paper. The internally assessed commentaries need current articles and tight word discipline, and choosing the article badly costs more marks than writing the commentary badly.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools applied to a real organisation, not recited. The common failure is a candidate who can define a framework and cannot use it on the case material in front of them. The internally assessed project needs an organisation that will actually supply information, which in the UAE is worth settling early rather than optimistically.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis, the individual oral and, at Higher Level, an essay on a studied text. The oral is where preparation shows most clearly, because it is built around a global issue and two chosen extracts. Practice has to happen on texts that are not the assessed ones, which is a boundary we keep to deliberately.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic can be a Diploma subject in its own right at either language level, which is separate from the Arabic lesson the Ministry requires every private school to run. Families frequently discover the two are different things in DP1. Arabic B rewards structured writing against the text types the guide lists, and oral fluency practised aloud rather than read.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source work, essay structure and, at Higher Level, a third paper on a regional option. The internally assessed historical investigation is where students lose most: the source evaluation section is short, specific and heavily weighted, and a strong narrative with weak evaluation does not score.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies have to be used as evidence for an argument, not listed. The experimental study written up for internal assessment is tightly specified, and candidates lose marks for an inexact replication or a results section that reports without interpreting. Higher Level adds extra topics and a further paper.

ib-diploma-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Which authority sits above your child's school depends on the emirate, and so does what that authority controls. Lessons reach all seven emirates the same way, over live video, so the differences below are about regulation, school supply and what time a session can realistically start.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA oversees the quality of private education here, across 227 schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25. Diploma supply is the deepest in the country, but a 4pm session still depends on Sheikh Zayed Road, which is exactly why an online slot starts when your child sits down.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and is named by almost no tutoring site in this market. Island and Khalifa City families often have one or two realistic Diploma schools within reach, which narrows subject choice before tuition is even discussed.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, with far fewer IB World Schools than the capital. Higher Level specialists are the pinch point rather than general subject help, and the drive that a visiting tutor would have to make is the reason an online specialist usually wins on both time and choice.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education here and approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. An IB Diploma tutor in Sharjah therefore has to work with a school calendar the authority has signed off, not an invented one.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman. Families often commute to Sharjah or Dubai for a Diploma place, so the evening slot is set by the return journey rather than by the school bell, and a fixed online time removes that variable.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and, like Sharjah's authority, approves curricula and assessment methods. Diploma cohorts are small, which makes an unavailable Higher Level option more likely and a specialist outside the emirate more useful.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education territory on the east coast, with the longest distances to a large IB cohort. This is where the visiting-tutor model breaks down first: there is no pool to draw from within a sensible drive, whatever rate a family is willing to pay.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised federally by the Ministry of Education. The practical answer for a Diploma student here is online teaching with a specialist, planned around a commute that frequently crosses two emirates each school day.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai holds the country's largest Diploma cohort, spread across schools that run the IB alone and schools that run it beside another curriculum. Programme offers change year to year, so confirm the current Diploma subject list with the school or against KHDA's own published listing before you plan a two-year route.

The capital's Diploma schools sit under ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation in the emirate. Cohorts are smaller than Dubai's, so Higher Level option blocks are tighter and a subject combination that works on paper may not exist on the timetable. Ask before the choice form, not after.

Diploma places are fewer and further apart, which is the single clearest argument for teaching online rather than searching for a tutor nearby.

This is the arrangement that holds a weak Standard Level above the 9-point threshold.

sections.heading: What the phrase 'Diploma home tutor' actually buys in the UAE right now
paragraphs: Three different services answer this one search. The first is an individual tutor who holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit and drives to your community; the permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The second is a tuition centre with premises, which in Dubai is a different legal animal again and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. The third is one-to-one tuition delivered over live video, which is what IB Gram provides to every family in the Emirates.

The visiting option is the one the search phrase implies, so price it properly. Published market figures for a visiting tutor in Dubai run from about AED 180 to AED 350 an hour at the mid tier and up to AED 500 for independent home tutors, with monthly visiting packages advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Online bands sit below that: budget providers publish hourly figures from AED 33 to AED 65, qualified subject tutors from AED 150, IB specialists from around AED 200 to AED 450, and one premium provider publishes AED 650. The gap between the visiting band and the online band is not teaching quality. It is a car crossing the city at 5pm.

What that travel costs a Diploma family is not only money. It is the twenty minutes at the start of a session that belong to the road rather than to Paper 2, the cancelled lesson in a week with a sandstorm, and the hard geographic limit on who can teach your child at all. Families in Fujairah, Umm Al Quwain or Al Ain feel this first: whatever rate you are willing to pay, the pool of people who can reach you and who have taught Higher Level Chemistry under IB moderation is very small.

IB Gram's position is plain. We teach UAE families one-to-one over live video, with screen sharing for the student's own work, and visiting tuition remains a service we run only in India. The first lesson is a free trial, with no card details taken, and if the fit is wrong we change the tutor rather than argue about it. What you give up is somebody in the room. What you get is the person who actually teaches your child's subject at your child's level, on a slot that starts on time in Gulf Standard Time.

sections.heading: Where the 45 points come from, and which of them tuition can move
paragraphs: A Diploma grade is not one number arrived at in one way. Six subjects are graded 1 to 7, giving a maximum of 42, and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are read together to add up to three more, for 45. Inside each subject the marks split again: most of the grade comes from external papers marked by examiners who have never met your child, and a substantial slice, commonly around a fifth in the sciences and mathematics, comes from work marked by the school teacher and then moderated by the IB. Parents who understand that split ask much better questions at parents' evening.

The practical consequence is that different parts of the Diploma respond to different things. Paper technique responds quickly to coaching, because command terms, mark allocation and timing are learnable skills and a student who writes 'describe' answers to 'evaluate' questions can be retrained inside a term. Internally assessed work responds slowly, because it depends on a method chosen months earlier and on data the student actually collected. The core responds only to being started early. CAS responds to nothing at all except being done and evidenced.

This is also where an honest tutor has to be clear about limits. Nobody can promise a point total, and a provider promising a point total is describing something outside its own control: the papers are externally marked, the internal marks are moderated, and grade awards sit with the IB. What tuition can do is improve the work that goes into each component before it is marked, and give you a forecast based on work actually seen. A forecast that moves down after a bad mock is more useful than one that never moves.

Use the table below as the map of who marks what. It is also the quickest way to see why 'my child needs a tutor' is rarely the right sentence: what a Diploma student usually needs is a specific component fixed, and the component tells you what kind of help to buy.

sections.heading: The failing conditions nobody explains until February of DP2
paragraphs: Twenty-four points is the number families know. It is not the only test. A candidate can clear 24 and still not be awarded the Diploma, because the award also depends on how those points are distributed and on whether the core and CAS were completed. Every year, UAE DP2 families discover this in the spring, when a coordinator sits them down and explains that two low Standard Levels and an unfinished Theory of Knowledge essay have put the whole award at risk even though the total looks survivable.

The conditions are published, stable and genuinely useful to read in DP1 rather than DP2. Fewer than 24 points in total is a fail. A grade E in Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay is a fail on its own. A single grade 1 in any subject at either level is a fail. Three or more grade 2s is a fail, as is four or more grades of 3 or below. Higher Level and Standard Level carry separate floors: fewer than 12 points across the Higher Levels fails, and fewer than 9 across the Standard Levels fails. CAS requirements not met fails. Because the list can be refined between cohorts, confirm the version that applies to your child with the DP coordinator, who has the current handbook.

Read as a set, these conditions change what good tutoring looks like. The instinct is to put money behind the subject the student loves and is already strong in, because progress there is visible and pleasant. The arithmetic says otherwise: the award is usually threatened by the two or three subjects nobody is discussing, and by a core component that was left until the term it was due. One hour a week on the weakest Standard Level does more for the Diploma than a third hour on the strongest Higher Level.

It also changes what you should ask at a report cycle. Not 'how is she doing in Economics', but 'read me the six grades and the two core grades, and tell me which failing condition is closest'. Any tutor worth paying should be able to answer that for the subject they teach, and should tell you plainly when the answer is 'this is not the subject putting the Diploma at risk'.

sections.heading: Who decides what across a UAE Diploma year
paragraphs: This is the table we wish every Diploma family had in DP1. Almost every frustration that reaches us is really a misreading of who holds a particular lever. A parent spends three weeks trying to get a Higher Level added when the option block closed in June. Another asks a tutor to speak to the school about a predicted grade, which is not a conversation a paid tutor should be having. A third assumes the IB sets the Internal Assessment deadline, when the date that binds is the one the school set months earlier so it can mark and moderate before uploading.

The emirate authority sits further away from your daily decisions than its reputation suggests. It licenses and oversees the school, and in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah it also approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. What it does not do is award your child's points or set your coursework dates. The IB awards the grades and sets the external framework. The Ministry of Education sets the mandatory subject requirement and, at the end, handles equivalency of the certificate. MoHRE governs whether the tutor may be paid at all.

Inside all of that, the school holds most of the levers that matter week to week: the option blocks, level changes, exam entries as the registered centre, predicted grades, and the internal calendar for the core and the Internal Assessments. That concentration is why the single most valuable thing a UAE parent can do in the first term of DP1 is ask the coordinator for the school's own written deadline calendar, and then plan everything, including tuition, backwards from it.

The right question to ask a prospective tutor is therefore not 'can you get her to a 7'. It is 'given that the school owns these decisions, what exactly will you change?' An honest answer is narrow and specific: the quality of the work before each of those decisions is made.

sections.heading: Option blocks: why your school may not teach the Higher Level your child needs
paragraphs: Dubai's private sector taught 387,441 students across 227 schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with UK curriculum schools at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, American at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. That last figure is the one Diploma families feel. A sector this large still produces small DP cohorts per school, and a small cohort cannot timetable every Higher Level against every other one. The result is the option block: a grid where Physics sits in the same column as Economics, and a student who wants both is told to choose.

Supply is improving rather than solved. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. More IB schools eventually means more Diploma cohorts and more option combinations. It does nothing for a student already in DP1 whose timetable clash is live this term, and outside Dubai and Abu Dhabi the arithmetic is tighter still: in Al Ain, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain a family may have one realistic Diploma school within reach.

A clash cannot be solved by tuition, and no honest provider should pretend otherwise. A candidate is registered for the Diploma by an IB World School, so the subjects your child sits are the subjects the school enters them for. What tuition can do is make the forced choice survivable: carry the subject the student had to take at a level they can hold, protect the Higher Levels they did get, and keep the Higher Level point floor of 12 in view while doing it. Where a school cannot staff a Higher Level specialist for the subject it does run, a subject specialist outside the emirate is often the only realistic support available.

If you are still in MYP 5, this is the conversation to have a year early. Ask which Higher Levels the school expects to timetable, ask which combinations have failed to run in recent years, and ask what happens if too few students pick a subject. The answers are usually given honestly when asked in February and defensively when asked in September.

sections.heading: Your child's school is the examination centre, and that changes your deadlines
paragraphs: A Diploma candidate does not register with the IB. The school does, as the examination centre, and that single fact reorganises the family calendar. Exam entries are made by the school by the school's deadline. Subject and level changes have to be processed by the school through registration, which is why a request made in the same term as the problem is often possible and the same request made later is often not. Internally assessed work has to reach the school early enough for the teacher to mark it and for the IB to moderate, so the deadline that binds your child is the school's date, not the one on any published IB schedule.

This page publishes no IB session or results date. That is deliberate: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so nothing could be verified for this project, and an unverified date on a tutoring page is worse than no date at all. Your DP coordinator holds the authoritative calendar for your cohort. What is safe to say is that UAE schools sit the May session, that a November session also exists, and that the internal deadlines sit months ahead of the papers.

If you want to see how early entry deadlines really are, look at the examination boards that do publish. Cambridge International's March 2027 series runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades on 27 February 2027 and results released on Direct on 13 May. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it 'cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam' if the wrong zone timetable was used. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November, with the November 2026 timetable running to 19 November 2026 and June 2026 results reaching students on 20 August 2026. Those are sibling-subject facts for a family with an IGCSE child, and they illustrate the general rule: the administrative deadlines are months before the papers.

The practical move is dull and effective. In the first term of DP1, ask the coordinator for three things in writing: the internal deadline calendar for every Internal Assessment and core component, the date by which a level change must be requested, and the session the school intends to enter your child for. Pin tuition to those dates. A tutor who plans around a published external timetable instead of your school's internal one will be late twice.

sections.heading: Predicted grades, and the request a tutor should refuse
paragraphs: Predicted grades are issued by your child's subject teachers and signed off by the DP coordinator. Universities use them to make conditional offers, so for a UAE family applying to the UK, the US, Canada or into the region, these numbers arrive before any real results exist and do a great deal of work. They are not negotiable in the way parents sometimes hope, and they are not a reward for effort. They are a professional judgement based on evidence: mock papers sat under conditions, Internal Assessment drafts, classwork, and the teacher's read of trajectory.

What this means for tuition is a question of timing. Support that arrives before the evidence is gathered can genuinely change the prediction, because the mock paper that gets marked in November is the mock paper the prediction rests on. Support that arrives after predictions are issued changes the final grade, which still matters enormously, but it will not retrospectively improve an offer already made on a lower number. Families who come to us in DP1 about a subject that is drifting are usually surprised at how much of the prediction is still in play; families who arrive after offers have landed are often really asking about the final session, and should be told that plainly.

There is a line here that a paid tutor must not cross. A tutor should not contact your child's school to argue for a higher prediction, should not coach a student to present work that is not theirs as evidence, and should not offer to supply coursework that lifts a teacher's judgement. Any of those turns a legitimate service into interference in a school's professional process, and in the coursework case into academic malpractice with consequences that land on the student rather than on the provider. The acceptable version is narrow and effective: better work, produced by the student, in front of the teacher making the judgement.

What we will give you is our own forecast, based on the work the tutor has seen, with its reasoning attached and its uncertainty admitted. Where it differs from the school's prediction, the useful conversation is about which pieces of evidence the two of you are each looking at. That is a conversation a coordinator will have. A demand for a different number is not.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies beside six Diploma subjects
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed for, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. At federal level the position is the same in substance: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. A Diploma student in the UAE is therefore carrying nine demands on a timetable designed for six, and this is the most common reason a weekly tuition slot has to be chosen rather than simply added.

The detail matters if you are buying support for these subjects. KHDA requires schools to run separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, classes for Arabs and non-Arabs must be organised separately, and combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Schools must also ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

Two of those rules shape what outside support can honestly offer. First, placement is the school's decision, so a tutor cannot move a child between the first-language and additional-language streams, and should not promise to. Second, for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, which means a tutor should be working through the material the school is actually using rather than importing a parallel course. We treat that as a hard limit, not a preference.

There is also a time arithmetic worth doing before you buy anything. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Add those periods to six Diploma subjects, the core and CAS, and the evening that is left is narrow. Our advice to DP2 families is usually to keep Ministry-subject support short and targeted, and to protect the hour that is doing the heaviest Diploma work.

sections.heading: What the market charges for Diploma support, and what the travel inside it buys
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. So here are the AED bands as other providers publish them, read in October 2026, with the source attached to each row. These are market figures, not an IB Gram rate card: we quote after the free trial lesson, when we know the subject, the level and how many hours the plan actually needs, because a quote given before that is a guess dressed as a price.

The pattern in the table is consistent. A visiting hour costs more than an online hour at every tier, and the difference is the car. Budget providers publish online rates from AED 33 to AED 65, qualified subject tutors from AED 150, IB and IGCSE specialists from roughly AED 200 to AED 450, and one premium provider publishes AED 650. Visiting rates start around AED 180, run to AED 350 in the mid band and up to AED 500 for independent home tutors. Monthly packages are advertised both ways: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits.

Put the number next to your school fee rather than next to nothing, which is the comparison that actually helps. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For most families the tuition decision is therefore being made against a known, flat school fee, and the sensible unit of comparison is the weekly hour across a term, not the hourly rate in isolation. One Higher Level hour a week for a term is a different commitment from two visits a week in the exam year.

Two practical cautions. Ask any provider whether the quoted figure includes VAT and get the answer in writing; we will not characterise the tax treatment of tuition fees in the UAE on a web page, because that is a question for the Federal Tax Authority's own guidance. And treat a discount offered against a promised outcome with real scepticism, because the outcome is not in the provider's gift: papers are externally marked and grades are awarded by the IB.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor against live one-to-one online, for a Diploma family
paragraphs: This is the comparison the search phrase deserves, so here it is without the sales tone. A tutor in the room has real advantages: a younger child concentrates better with an adult beside them, nothing depends on the wifi, and a parent can hear what is happening from the next room. For primary and lower secondary work those advantages are often decisive, and families who choose a visiting tutor for a ten-year-old are not making a mistake.

The Diploma changes the weighting. By DP1 the student is sixteen, the work is subject-specific to the point of being component-specific, and the question stops being 'who is good with children' and becomes 'who has taught this syllabus at this level and knows how this component is marked'. Geography is a poor filter for that. An online pool lets a family in Al Ain or Ras Al Khaimah work with the Higher Level Chemistry specialist rather than the nearest available science graduate, and screen sharing happens to suit Diploma work unusually well: the student's own document, annotated live, with the notes and the recording kept for revision.

There are honest trade-offs. A live video lesson needs a quiet room and a working connection, and a student who will not open their own file is harder to manage remotely than in person. We mitigate that in dull, practical ways: a fixed weekly slot, written notes after each lesson so a parent can see what happened, and a change of tutor rather than a negotiation if the fit is wrong. What we do not do is send someone to a UAE address, and the table below is the honest version of why.

One more point that only shows up over two years. Diploma families in this region move: a job changes emirate, a summer runs long in another country, a school place opens in Dubai in January. A visiting arrangement ends every time that happens and the search starts again. An online arrangement survives it, with the same tutor, the same plan and a new school calendar to work against.

sections.heading: The core, its limits, and the line a paid tutor does not cross
paragraphs: The Diploma core is where tutoring in this market goes wrong, and it goes wrong commercially rather than accidentally. One page ranking in this cluster sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is not a grey area: assessed work must be the student's own, a candidate signs to that effect, the coordinator declares it, and the consequence of a breach falls on the student in the form of a malpractice finding, not on the provider who took the fee. Any offer to hand back a finished Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Internal Assessment should end the conversation.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial, and worth spelling out because the honest version is often more useful than the dishonest one. A tutor can argue with a research question until it is answerable in 4,000 words. A tutor can read the student's own draft and give written feedback on structure, argument, use of sources and referencing. A tutor can teach the uncertainty treatment a scientific investigation needs, or check whether the mathematics in an exploration is actually at the level the criteria expect. A tutor can mark practice work against published criteria so the student knows what the words mean. In every case the student writes, revises and submits, and the school supervisor runs the reflection sessions and signs the work off.

The limits in the table are worth knowing before the drafting starts, because most core disasters are timetable failures rather than ability failures. An Extended Essay has a word limit and a required pattern of supervised reflection; a Theory of Knowledge essay answers a prescribed title in a fixed number of words; the exhibition is a short commentary on three objects. These are small documents with long lead times, and the students who come unstuck are almost always the ones who started late rather than the ones who wrote badly. Figures here follow the current guides as schools are teaching them, and you should confirm the exact limits for your child's cohort in the subject guide the school holds.

We also will not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables. They belong to the boards, your school has legitimate access, and we reference and link rather than redistribute. A provider offering a library of board material as a selling point is telling you something about how it handles other people's rules.

process.title: Tell us the school, the six subjects and the three levels
process.description: Not a form about aspirations. We want the school's name, the six subjects with Higher and Standard Level marked, the last report or mock grades, and the school's internal deadline for the next Internal Assessment. That is enough to say which component is actually at risk, and whether tuition is the right purchase at all.

process.title: One free trial lesson with the subject specialist
process.description: The trial is a real lesson in the real subject with the tutor who would teach the term, not a sales call. One lesson, no card details taken, no obligation afterwards. Your child should finish it able to tell you one specific thing they now understand, and if they cannot, say so and we will try a different tutor.

process.title: A two-year map pinned to your school's own dates
process.description: We build the plan backwards from the school's internal calendar for the Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge components, not from a published external timetable. The map says which weeks are for content, which are for papers, and where the core has to be sitting by each school deadline.

process.title: Weekly lessons, with notes a parent can read
process.description: The same tutor at the same time each week, with written notes after each lesson covering what was taught, what the student got wrong and what they should practise. Notes exist so a parent is never dependent on a teenager's summary of a lesson, and so the next tutor would not start from nothing.

process.title: A review at every school report, and a swap if the fit is wrong
process.description: At each report cycle we read the six grades as a set against the failing conditions, and tell you which one is nearest. If the subject we teach is no longer the one putting the Diploma at risk, we will say that. If the tutor and the student are not working, we change the tutor rather than renegotiate the hours.

whyPoints.title: Chosen for the subject and the level, not for the drive
whyPoints.description: A Higher Level component is a specialist problem. Teaching over live video means a family in Fujairah or Al Ain is matched on who has taught the syllabus and knows how the component is moderated, instead of on who can reach the house by 5pm. That is the whole argument for the format, and it holds for Diploma work in a way it does not for primary work.

whyPoints.title: The regulator map, written down, because you need it
whyPoints.description: KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and the federal Ministry elsewhere. We name the authority, explain what it governs and link to its own pages. We claim no approval, accreditation or partnership from any of them, because IB Gram holds none and that phrase is the most misused one in this market.

whyPoints.title: A coursework boundary we put in writing
whyPoints.description: Teaching, feedback and review on the student's own work: yes. Producing assessed work for a candidate: never, in any subject, at any price. We say this on the page rather than in a terms document because one page ranking for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments, and a parent deserves to know which kind of provider they are speaking to.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built around a UAE week
whyPoints.description: Sessions sit in Gulf Standard Time, move after Iftar through Ramadan, pause for Eid and the long summer, and follow the family when a job or a holiday moves them to another time zone. Nothing about that is remarkable. It is just what a UAE school year requires, and it is easier to deliver when nobody has to drive.

whyPoints.title: Numbers with a source, or no number at all
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to the provider or rate tracker that published it, with the month it was read. Every regulatory statement comes from u.ae, KHDA or MoHRE. There is no satisfaction percentage, no average score and no IB exam date, because we could not verify those and an unsourced figure on a tutoring page is worth nothing to you.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency and paperwork pointed at the official channel
whyPoints.description: Ministry of Education equivalency for an IB Diploma is a Ministry process, not a service a tutoring platform performs or guarantees. We describe what the reported requirements are for the curricula where they have been published, decline to invent an IB points figure that has not been read on moe.gov.ae, and point you to the Ministry and your school registrar.

faqs.question: What exactly stops an IB Diploma from being awarded?
faqs.answer: More than a low total. The published failing conditions include fewer than 24 points overall, a grade E in Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay, a grade 1 in any subject, grade 2 awarded three or more times, grade 3 or below awarded four or more times, fewer than 12 points across the Higher Levels, fewer than 9 across the Standard Levels, and CAS requirements not being met. Each is separate, so a candidate can clear 24 points and still miss the award on distribution alone. Ask your DP coordinator for the version that applies to your child's cohort, since the handbook is the authoritative source.

faqs.question: Can a grade E in Theory of Knowledge cost my child the whole Diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes. A grade E in Theory of Knowledge or in the Extended Essay is a failing condition in its own right, independent of how many points the six subjects produced. It is the condition families least expect, because the core is the part of the Diploma that feels optional while six subjects are shouting for attention. The practical defence is timing rather than brilliance: get the essay started early, keep the supervised reflection sessions on schedule, and treat the core deadlines as the first fixed dates in DP1. Most E grades are produced by a fortnight of panic, not by weak thinking.

faqs.question: How do the three bonus points from the core get added up?
faqs.answer: The six subjects produce a maximum of 42 points, seven per subject. The Extended Essay grade and the Theory of Knowledge grade are then read together against a matrix that awards up to three further points, which is how the scale reaches 45. The two core components are not added separately, so a strong Extended Essay can partly compensate for a weaker Theory of Knowledge grade and the reverse. The matrix also interacts with the failing conditions, since an E in either component fails the Diploma regardless of points. Your coordinator holds the current matrix for your child's cohort.

faqs.question: My son has 23 points in his mock results. What does that number mean?
faqs.answer: It means there is work to do and time to do it, not that the Diploma is lost. Mocks are set and marked by the school, usually harshly on purpose, and they are the evidence predictions rest on. Twenty-three is one point under the minimum, so start with distribution rather than the total: add the Higher Level points and check they reach 12, add the Standard Levels and check they reach 9, and look for any grade 1 or a cluster of 2s and 3s. The cheapest point to recover is almost always in the weakest Standard Level, which is usually the subject nobody is discussing.

faqs.question: The timetable puts Physics against Economics. Can tuition fix a subject clash?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider who says otherwise is selling something it cannot deliver. Option blocks belong to the school, and a candidate is registered for the Diploma by an IB World School, so the subjects sat are the subjects the school enters. Small Diploma cohorts are the cause: with the IB at roughly 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment, a single school cannot timetable every Higher Level against every other. What tuition can do is make the forced choice work, by holding the substitute subject at a level the student can sustain and protecting the Higher Level point floor while they do it.

faqs.question: Who issues the predicted grades my child's university offers depend on?
faqs.answer: The subject teachers, signed off by the DP coordinator. They are a professional judgement based on evidence already gathered: mock papers sat under conditions, Internal Assessment drafts, and classwork. That is why timing matters more than effort here. Support in DP1 and early DP2 can genuinely change a prediction, because it changes the work the prediction will be based on. Support arriving after offers have been made mainly changes final grades instead. A tutor should never contact the school to argue for a higher number, and should refuse if asked: that is interference in a school's own process.

faqs.question: Does my child sit the Diploma exams at their own school, or somewhere else?
faqs.answer: At the school, which is the registered examination centre and the body that makes the entries. There is no route for a family to enter a child for the full Diploma directly, which is different from International GCSE, where private candidate entry through a centre does exist. Practically, this means the school's deadlines bind you: entries, level changes and the upload of internally assessed work all run through it. Ask the coordinator in writing which session your child is entered for, and the date by which any level change has to be requested.

faqs.question: Does the school have to be told we have hired a private tutor?
faqs.answer: There is no general requirement to tell a school that you pay for lessons, and plenty of UAE families do without mentioning it. Two things do matter. First, assessed work must be the student's own, and the coordinator declares that, so anything a tutor touches has to stay inside teaching and feedback on the student's draft. Second, Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff are reported to bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct to similar effect. Verify that against the current ADEK policy before relying on it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with CAS, or is that off limits?
faqs.answer: CAS carries no points, but the Diploma is not awarded if its requirements are not met, which makes it the cheapest possible way to lose two years of work. A tutor cannot do CAS: the experiences are the student's and the reflections have to be theirs. What outside support can reasonably do is help a student build the habit of writing reflections when something happens rather than in June, and plan CAS time so it does not collide with coursework deadlines. The CAS coordinator at the school is the person who signs off completion, and they should be asked each term what is outstanding.

faqs.question: What share of a Diploma subject grade comes from work done inside school?
faqs.answer: It varies by subject, but the pattern is consistent enough to plan around. In the sciences and mathematics the internally assessed component is commonly around a fifth of the subject grade; in some language and arts subjects the internal share is higher. That work is marked by the teacher and then moderated by the IB, so a generous school mark can move after moderation. The planning consequence is simple: internal components are decided months before the papers, they respond slowly to help, and they are the part of the grade a late-arriving tutor can least influence.

faqs.question: Is a two-year Diploma support plan affordable beside a UAE school fee?
faqs.answer: Do the arithmetic weekly rather than hourly. Published market bands put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour and an IB specialist at roughly AED 200 to AED 450, with visiting rates above both because travel sits inside the fee. One Higher Level hour a week across a term is a very different commitment from two visits a week in the exam year. KHDA also confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, so most families are planning against a flat school fee. We quote after the free trial, not before.

faqs.question: Our search was for a home tutor. What does IB Gram actually provide?
faqs.answer: One-to-one lessons over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing so the student's own work can be annotated during the lesson. Visiting tuition is a service we run only in India, so nobody will arrive at a UAE address, and we would rather say that on the page than on the phone. For Diploma work the trade is usually favourable: instead of whoever teaches your subject within a short drive, your child works with someone who has taught that syllabus at that level and knows how the component is marked.

faqs.question: Does a retake in a later session make sense if the Diploma is not awarded?
faqs.answer: It is often the right answer, and it is a decision to make with the coordinator rather than alone. A candidate can re-sit subjects in a later session, with the registration going through the school as the examination centre, and coursework components are handled differently from papers, so the first question is which part of the grade actually failed. Weigh the university position too: some offers can be deferred and some cannot. We publish no session or results dates on this page, because IB dates could not be verified for this project, so get the calendar from your coordinator.

faqs.question: Is Arabic a subject my child can take as part of the Diploma itself?
faqs.answer: Yes, and families regularly discover in DP1 that this is a separate thing from the Arabic lesson the Ministry requires every private school to run. Arabic can be taken as a Diploma language subject at either level, assessed like any other subject on the 1 to 7 scale. The mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies provision is a different obligation, placed by the school, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and specifying the language of instruction for each. Ask the school which of the two you are actually being asked about before buying support.

faqs.question: Which authority should I ask about my child's school, and which about the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Four different bodies, four different questions. The emirate authority deals with the school: KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The IB deals with grades, components and the award. The Ministry of Education deals with equivalency of the final certificate. MoHRE deals with whether a tutor may be paid, through the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years.

faqs.question: My daughter is a November session candidate. Does that change anything?
faqs.answer: It changes the whole internal calendar, which is why it is worth saying early. The IB runs two sessions a year and most UAE schools sit the May one, so a November cohort is working to deadlines that sit out of step with the school around them, including mock timing, coursework upload windows and when university applications need predicted grades. The content and the components are the same. We will not publish session or results dates here, because no IB date could be verified for this project, so plan from the written calendar your school issues for your child's cohort.

ib-diploma-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the component, not with the hours
ib-diploma-home-tutor.closingBody: Most families arrive asking how many hours a Diploma student needs. The better first question is which component is actually at risk, because the answer decides everything else: a leaking Paper 2 is a different purchase from a late Extended Essay, and a Standard Level sliding towards a 3 may matter more to the award than the Higher Level everyone is worrying about. Send us the school, the six subjects with levels marked, the last report and the next internal deadline. We will tell you what we think is at risk, book one free trial lesson with the specialist who would teach it, and say plainly if we think the hour is not worth buying yet.

intro.heading: Who actually decides what your child studies
paragraphs: An IB Diploma online tutor in the UAE teaches one Diploma Programme course, one student at a time, over live video. That is the whole mechanism: no travel, no centre, no group. What makes the job different in this country is not the teaching. It is the number of bodies holding authority over your child's two years. The school holds the programme authorisation from the IB. The emirate authority holds the school's licence and approves what it charges. The federal Ministry of Education decides what the finished certificate is worth for a UAE university or a government post. A tutor who cannot tell those apart spends your money arguing with the wrong one.

Most families arrive at this search after a report card that sits below a predicted grade, and they assume the cause is effort. Often the cause is structural. Dubai's private sector carried 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, and the International Baccalaureate accounted for 7 per cent of that enrolment, against 37 per cent UK and 26 per cent Indian curricula (Dubai Media Office, January 2025). Seven per cent is a thin pool. It means a school may run one Higher Level class in a science, that class may have one teacher, and if your child is out of step with that teacher there is no second set to move into.

Above the school sits an authority that differs by emirate, and parents routinely address the wrong one. Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so the reach is wider than inspection alone.

None of those authorities marks your child's work. The IB sets the assessment, the school's own coordinator sets the internal deadlines that in practice govern the Diploma year, and the subject teacher marks the Internal Assessment before the IB moderates the sample. That split explains why so much tuition money is wasted: a family pays for Higher Level content when the mark is actually being lost in a coursework process the school owns and the tutor can only work around. It also explains why we ask for the school's deadline sheet on the enquiry, not after you have paid for a block of hours.

IB Gram delivers all of this as one-to-one online lessons over live video. There is no visit, no centre and no UAE address involved, and we say so before anyone pays. The reason is not cost. It is that a Diploma family in Fujairah or Khalifa City needs a specialist in the one course their child is registered for, and matching on subject beats matching on driving distance every time. The rest of this page is the regulatory and school-system detail behind that choice: who decides what, who may legally teach your child, what the market charges, and where a tutor must stop.

ib-diploma-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Four IB routes matter to a UAE Diploma family, because the one your child is on determines what a tutor can usefully do. Most enquiries are about the two-year Diploma, but course candidates, students still inside the Middle Years Programme and Career-related Programme students all reach us, and each needs a different plan.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across the IB's subject groups, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus the core of Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Higher Level carries more taught content, an extra paper in several subjects and a heavier expectation of independent reading. The grade a student finishes with is built from externally marked papers plus internally assessed coursework that the IB moderates.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE the binding constraint is usually the school's option blocks rather than the IB's own rules. A school running one Higher Level set in a subject cannot offer a second route through it, and a timetable grid decides whether two sciences and a second language can coexist. Online tuition is how a family reaches a specialist in the exact course and level their child is registered for, including combinations their own school teaches to only a handful of students.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme course candidate
programmes.ageRange: Ages 16-19 · one or more individual DP courses
programmes.description: A student takes individual Diploma Programme courses and receives a result for each, without the full Diploma award. The teaching, the papers and the Internal Assessment are the same as for a Diploma candidate in that subject. What is absent is the obligation to carry six subjects and the core, which changes the workload and the revision strategy substantially.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools use this route for students who move in late, who carry a heavy mandatory-subject load, or whose previous system left a gap that cannot be closed inside two years. Families should ask the coordinator in writing what a course result means for the universities they are targeting, and should raise Ministry of Education equivalency separately, because the course route and the full Diploma are treated as different documents.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against published criteria rather than by terminal examination, finishing with the Personal Project. Marking uses criterion letters and achievement levels, so a student can hold strong grades without ever having sat a timed paper of Diploma length. The step into DP1 is therefore a step in assessment style as much as in content.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to Diploma transition is the single most common reason a UAE family books tuition in the first term of DP1. Students arrive fluent in criterion language and short of examination stamina, particularly in Mathematics and the sciences. Work here is best done in the summer between the two programmes or in the first eight weeks of DP1, before the first Internal Assessment deadline lands on top of it.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller number of Diploma Programme courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project and a core that includes personal and professional skills. Students sit the same papers as Diploma candidates in the DP courses they take, so subject tuition is identical in substance even though the overall award is structured differently.
programmes.countryNote: Fewer UAE schools run the Career-related Programme than the Diploma, so a CP student needing help in a particular DP course is often the only one in their school taking it. That is precisely the gap live online lessons close. Parents should check with the Ministry of Education's own channels how a CP award is treated for equivalency, and should not rely on a tutoring provider's summary of it, including ours.

ib-diploma-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma Programme courses UAE families ask for most often, with the level pattern and the point where marks are usually lost. Arabic appears because it is on almost every UAE timetable, whether as a Diploma language or as a Ministry-required subject sitting beside the six.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency, calculus and proof, with a heavier analytic load at Higher Level. Marks go missing in the extended response questions, where a student who can execute a technique cannot choose it unprompted. The exploration is marked against criteria that reward genuine mathematical reasoning over presentation, and that is where most rushed explorations lose ground.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-dependent work, with Higher Level adding substantial statistical inference. The common error is treating it as the easier route; the graphical calculator work is unforgiving and the interpretation marks demand sentences, not numbers. Students placed here by their school often need the modelling vocabulary taught explicitly rather than absorbed.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields reward precise definition and consistent units, and the Higher Level extension questions assume the Standard Level material is automatic. Marks are lost on explanation chains that stop one step early, and on data analysis where uncertainties are quoted without reasoning. The internal assessment needs a question narrow enough to generate a real relationship.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are where Higher Level separates from Standard Level, and where most UAE students arrive having memorised outcomes rather than mechanisms. Calculation questions punish rounding discipline. The internal assessment goes wrong when the chosen variable cannot be controlled with school apparatus, which is a planning fault a tutor can catch early.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the obstacle, not difficulty, and the command terms decide the mark: outline, explain, distinguish and evaluate each want a different shape of answer. Higher Level adds depth in physiology and genetics. Data-based questions reward reading the axes before the question, a habit that can be trained in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks, and most lost marks come from unlabelled or unexplained ones. Higher Level adds quantitative work that students from criterion-based systems find unfamiliar. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries built on published news articles, where the article choice decides the ceiling of the mark before any writing happens.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools, techniques and theories have to be applied to the stimulus rather than recited, and examiners reward answers anchored in the given organisation. Higher Level extension content appears in the longer paper. The internal assessment at Higher Level requires primary research, which needs planning months before the deadline a school usually announces.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis, the individual oral and the written work reward a repeatable analytical method rather than literary enthusiasm. Students lose marks by summarising a text instead of arguing about how it works. The global issue chosen for the oral determines how much there is to say, so it is worth examining before the student commits to it.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic appears twice in a UAE student's week: as a Diploma language course and, separately, as a Ministry-required subject. The two have different purposes and different assessment. Diploma Arabic rewards structured written response and oral fluency; the mandatory stream follows Ministry content that schools may not alter without prior permission.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The core is where school-set deadlines bite hardest, because both components run alongside six subjects. The Extended Essay has a supervisor appointed by the school and a word ceiling of 4,000 words. Support here is feedback on the student's own drafts and on their research question, and nothing that places a tutor's sentences inside the submission.

ib-diploma-online-tutor.regionsIntro: The regulator changes when you cross an emirate boundary, and so does the density of Diploma provision. These notes name the authority for each emirate and what that means for a family looking for Higher Level support. Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain are included because they are almost never mentioned by anyone selling tuition here.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. The largest private sector in the country, with 227 schools and 17 curricula in 2024-25, and the deepest Diploma provision. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees would not rise for 2026-27, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new schools, three of them International Baccalaureate.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which is the single most useful fact an Abu Dhabi parent can know before accepting an offer.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under the Department of Education and Knowledge. Diploma provision is thinner than on the island, so a student needing a specific Higher Level science or a second modern language frequently has no local option at all. This is the clearest case in the country for live online lessons matched on the course rather than on distance.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which u.ae describes as regulating private education in the emirate and which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That approval scope matters: a Sharjah family querying a programme change is dealing with an authority that signs off curriculum, not only quality.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here sit with the federal Ministry of Education, which u.ae states plays a supervisory role for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Diploma places exist but are few, and families commonly commute to Dubai or Sharjah. Evening online sessions avoid a second road journey after a long school run.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which u.ae states regulates private education and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses and assessment methods. Diploma coverage is limited to a small number of schools, so Higher Level sets are small and a timetable clash can remove a subject entirely.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under the Ministry of Education for private-school supervision. The east coast has the least Diploma provision in the country and the longest journeys to a specialist, which is why no agency operating on driving radius serves it properly. Live video removes the journey from the arithmetic completely.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the Ministry of Education. Families here are usually choosing between a local school on another curriculum and a daily commute to Sharjah or Dubai for the Diploma. Where the Diploma is being carried at a distance, the tuition should not add more travel to the week.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai holds the country's deepest Diploma provision, and the 2026-27 intake adds three more International Baccalaureate schools among seven new openings. Even so, individual Higher Level sets are small, and students in the same subject at two of these schools can be working to deadlines weeks apart because internal calendars are set school by school.

Abu Dhabi's Diploma schools answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge, whose staff ethics rules bar a teacher from tutoring students enrolled at their own school. Al Ain has markedly fewer Diploma options than the island, so a student there with an unusual Higher Level combination is often the only one in their year carrying it.

ib-diploma-online-tutor.modesIntro: Three shapes of arrangement cover almost every Diploma enquiry we take from the UAE. All three are delivered as one-to-one lessons over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and all three are built around the school's own deadline calendar rather than a fixed curriculum of our own.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one across DP1 and DP2
modes.description: One or two sessions a week in a single course, running with the school's scheme of work rather than ahead of it. The tutor sees the marked class assessments, so the plan adjusts as the school's own data arrives. This is the arrangement that fixes content gaps, because it has the time to find them.

sections.heading: What a UAE family is actually buying when they search for a Diploma tutor
paragraphs: An IB Diploma online tutor in the UAE is a specialist in one Diploma course, working with one student over live video, usually in sixty-minute sessions. The phrase hides the real question, which is almost never who can teach Biology. It is which parts of this arrangement can still be changed, and by when. By the time most UAE families type it, the subjects are chosen, the levels are registered, the Internal Assessment title is approved and the first paper is a fixed number of weeks away. A useful answer starts by naming what is still movable.

What is movable is narrower than it looks, and that is good news, because it tells you where the money should go. Content gaps close: a student who never understood equilibrium can be taught equilibrium. Technique closes faster still, because command terms, mark allocations and the difference between describe and explain are learnable in weeks. Coursework quality improves through feedback on the student's own drafts. What does not move is the registration, the option block, the level the school entered, the internal deadline calendar or the examination window. Anyone implying otherwise is selling something that is not theirs to sell.

So the first session in a sensible arrangement is diagnostic rather than motivational. The tutor reads the most recent marked paper, the current coursework draft and the school's own deadline sheet, then says which of the three is costing the most marks. That conversation needs the school's documents, which is why we ask for them at enquiry rather than after payment. It also needs someone who has taught the course at the level in question, not a graduate meeting the syllabus for the first time. Because lessons are delivered online in Gulf Standard Time, the specialist can be matched to the course instead of to a postcode.

sections.heading: The Diploma your school offers is a smaller thing than the Diploma
paragraphs: The IB publishes subject groups and levels. Your child's school publishes option blocks, and those are not the same document. A school builds a timetable grid from the teachers it has, then places subjects on lines; a student may take one subject per line. The consequence is that a perfectly reasonable combination becomes impossible, not because the IB forbids it but because two courses were put on the same line in a year when few students wanted both. Parents who do not know this spend a year believing their child chose badly.

Level availability works the same way. Higher Level in a subject exists only if the school has enough students and a teacher to run the set. With the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment, and far less than that in the northern emirates, Higher Level sets in the smaller subjects are frequently one class of a handful of students. If that class does not suit your child, there is no second class. The same arithmetic decides whether a school offers both Mathematics routes, or quietly runs one.

This is where outside tuition earns its fee and where it cannot help, and the honest version of the distinction is worth having before you pay anyone. A tutor cannot add a course to the school's blocks, cannot change the level the school registered, cannot extend an internal deadline and cannot alter which Mathematics route a student was placed in. A tutor can teach the content of either route, close the gap between the level taught and the level examined, and give a student in a one-teacher set a second explanation of the same material from someone who has taught it many times.

sections.heading: Who decides what: the IB, the emirate, the Ministry and the school
paragraphs: Four different parties hold the decisions that shape a UAE Diploma, and almost every frustrated phone call we hear is aimed at the wrong one. The IB decides what the courses contain and how they are assessed. The emirate authority decides whether the school may operate, what it may charge and, in two emirates explicitly, what curricula and assessment methods it may use. The school decides the timetable, the sets, the internal deadlines and the predicted grades. The federal Ministry of Education decides what the certificate is worth once it exists.

Knowing the boundaries is practical, not academic. A fee dispute goes to the emirate authority, not the IB. A question about whether a school may run the Diploma at all goes to the school's own coordinator and the IB's published list of schools, not to the regulator. A missed internal deadline is a school matter and no regulator will intervene in it. A question about whether the finished Diploma will be recognised for a UAE public-sector post or a federal university belongs to the Ministry of Education's equivalency channel, and it should be asked at the start of DP1 rather than after results.

The reason this sits at the front of a tutoring page is that the answer determines what you should be buying. If the problem is a timetable constraint, extra hours in the subject will not fix it and a conversation with the coordinator might. If the problem is that the certificate needs to satisfy a UAE requirement nobody has checked, then the urgent task is a document, not a lesson. If the problem is genuinely that the student cannot do equilibrium, buy the lessons. We would rather lose an enquiry by saying that than take money for the wrong thing.

sections.heading: The permit question changes when the tutor is not in the country
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is a permitted activity, not an informal favour. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and u.ae lists eligible applicants as teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Two consequences matter to a parent. The first is that individuals giving private lessons without that permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no honest page can quote an amount. The second is the own-school rule. The permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school, and press reporting of ADEK's professional-ethics rules describes Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff as prohibited from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their school. An offer of your child's own teacher, privately, is an offer to turn down.

The third situation is the one nobody writes about, and it is the one that applies to most online tuition. A subject specialist teaching from outside the UAE over live video is not in a UAE employment relationship, so a UAE private tuition work permit does not attach to them at all. That is not a loophole to hide behind; it is a fact to disclose. It is why our enquiry form asks nothing about a tutor's residency and everything about what they have taught, and why we tell a family where their tutor teaches from before the trial lesson rather than after it. A tuition business with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again, needing a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute.
