sections.heading: The core: who supervises Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the Internal Assessments
paragraphs: The Diploma core is where school authority is at its strongest and where paid help is at its most dangerous. Every piece of it is supervised by a member of school staff, submitted through the school, and declared as the student's own work. The Extended Essay has a supervisor the school appoints. The Theory of Knowledge essay is written on a prescribed title and overseen by the school's Theory of Knowledge teacher. Each subject's Internal Assessment is set, supervised and marked inside the school before the IB moderates a sample of the marks.

That structure sets the boundary for a tutor precisely. Teaching is allowed: how a research question is narrowed, what a criterion is actually asking for, why one method generates data and another does not, how an argument is structured, what an examiner reads first. Feedback on the student's own draft is allowed, and it is the most valuable hour a coursework student can buy. What is not allowed is any arrangement where words that are not the student's reach the submission, where a tutor edits a paragraph into its final form, or where a draft comes back improved rather than annotated.

We put this in writing because the UAE market contains providers that cross the line openly, including one that advertises finished Internal Assessments at a fixed price. A student who submits that is exposed to an academic-misconduct finding that no refund repairs, and a family that paid for it has bought a risk rather than a grade. Our rule is simple and it is on every page: the student types every word, the school's supervisor stays the supervisor, and a tutor who is asked to do otherwise says no and tells us. Nothing about that is a marketing position. It is the condition of the award.

sections.heading: Your child's school is the examination centre, and an online tutor is not
paragraphs: For a Diploma student in the UAE, the school is the examination centre. It holds the registration, enters the candidate, manages the upload of coursework, receives the results and handles any enquiry upon results afterwards. No tutoring provider does any part of that, and a family should treat an offer to handle entries as a warning sign rather than a service. What a tutor can do is ask, in the first session, whether the entry is correct at the level the student is actually working at, because an entry error found in October is fixable and one found in April is not.

The boards make the same point about timetables in their own documentation. Cambridge International runs its International GCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong timetable was used. Pearson Edexcel offers International GCSE in May or June and November, and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series.

The entry deadlines sit far earlier than families expect. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series place final entries on 27 November 2026 for an examination period running from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due on 27 February 2027 and results on Direct on 13 May. That is a worked example of a pattern that holds everywhere: the paperwork closes months before the paper. For the IB's own sessions we publish no date on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and we will not restate a date we could not verify. Ask the coordinator, or read it on ibo.org.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and the degree at the end of it
paragraphs: The Mathematics decision is the single most consequential subject choice in a UAE Diploma, and it is frequently made by the school's set placement rather than by the family. The two routes are not an easy one and a hard one. Analysis and Approaches is built on algebraic technique, calculus and proof. Applications and Interpretation is built on modelling, statistics and technology, and its Higher Level statistical inference content defeats students who chose it expecting less work. Both exist at Higher and Standard Level, giving four distinct courses with four different examination shapes.

The reason to settle it early is university admission, and the reason to be careful about advice is that admissions requirements are published by universities, not by tutoring companies. Engineering, physical sciences, mathematics, economics and many computer science programmes commonly expect the analytic route, often at Higher Level. Programmes in business, social sciences, design and the health professions frequently accept either. None of that is a rule we can state on a family's behalf. The only safe method is to read the specific requirement on the admissions page of each named programme, including UAE universities, and to do it in DP1 while a change is still administratively possible.

A tutor's useful role here is diagnostic and then practical. Before the choice closes, a specialist can give the student a short piece of work from each route and tell you which one the student can actually sustain for two years, which is more informative than a preference expressed in Year 11. After the choice closes, the tutor teaches the registered course and nothing else, because the registration is the school's and the examination follows it. We will say clearly when a family has arrived too late to change route and the better use of money is making the registered route work.

sections.heading: Six Diploma subjects plus the subjects the Ministry requires
paragraphs: A UAE Diploma student does not carry six subjects and the core. They carry six subjects, the core, and the subjects their school's licence obliges it to teach. Federal rules state that private schools are not required to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. In Dubai, KHDA's mandatory-subject guidance makes this concrete: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are required in all private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with the requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The detail decides where the hours go. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should last at least 25 minutes. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language.

Two practical points follow for anyone planning tuition. First, the week is fuller than a six-subject diagram suggests, so a tuition plan that ignores the mandatory timetable will be abandoned by November. Second, for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, and schools must ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach them. That is a real limit on what outside support can offer in those subjects, and a reason to ask the school what support it already provides before paying anyone for it.

sections.heading: What Diploma-level online hours cost in the UAE market
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranked tutoring pages for these searches publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in a currency UAE families do not transact in. The figures below are market rates published by other providers and rate trackers, read in October 2026. They are not our price list, and no figure here is ours. Our own arrangement starts with a trial lesson and a consultation, after which a family is quoted for a specific course, level and session pattern, because an hour of Higher Level coursework feedback and an hour of Standard Level revision are not the same product.

What drives the number is scarcity rather than quality signalling. A Higher Level specialist in a subject your emirate barely teaches costs more than a generalist because there are fewer of them, not because the hour contains more minutes. Session length changes the arithmetic as well: a ninety-minute coursework session is usually better value than two forty-five-minute ones, because reading a draft and discussing it does not divide neatly. Monthly packages circulate too. Published examples include AED 799 a month online for eight sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Set those numbers beside the school fee rather than against nothing. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run at roughly AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. A family that knows those bands can tell an unusual quotation from a normal one, which is the entire purpose of printing them.

sections.heading: A tutor at a UAE address against live one-to-one online, for a Higher Level subject
paragraphs: Families search for a tutor who will come to the house because that is the familiar model, and the question deserves a straight answer rather than a redirect. A visiting tutor in the UAE is drawn from whoever can reach your address inside a reasonable drive. In Dubai that pool is large for Mathematics and the sciences at Standard Level and thin for Higher Level in anything less common. In Al Ain, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain it is thin for almost everything Diploma-related. The rate reflects the travel: published in-home bands run from AED 180 to AED 500 an hour.

IB Gram does not offer visits anywhere in the Emirates. Our UAE service is one-to-one online tuition over live video, and home visits exist only in India, where the logistics and the tutor base are different. We state that before payment because the alternative is a family discovering it afterwards, and because the choice is defensible on its merits rather than needing to be hidden. The thing a Diploma family is short of is not proximity. It is a specialist in the one course their child is registered for, at the level they were entered at.

The comparison below is written for a Higher Level subject, because that is where the two models diverge most. For Standard Level revision in a widely taught subject, a good local tutor who arrives on time is a perfectly sensible choice and we will say so. For Higher Level Chemistry, Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Economics coursework or a second modern language, the matching problem dominates everything else, and a model that searches the whole timetable instead of a twenty-minute radius wins on the only axis that matters.

process.title: Tell us the course, the level and the school's dates
process.description: The enquiry asks for the subject, whether it is Higher or Standard Level, the emirate, the school and the next internal deadline. Send the most recent marked assessment if you have it. That is enough for us to say whether a specialist is free, and what a sensible first block looks like.

process.title: We say what is available, including when it is not
process.description: If no specialist in that course and level is free in the window you need, we say so rather than offering a near-match. Where the only available specialist teaches from outside the UAE, we name that before the trial lesson, with the time zone they work in and what they have taught.

process.title: A trial lesson that diagnoses rather than sells
process.description: The first session is spent on the student's own work: a marked paper, a coursework draft, a class test. The tutor reports back on where marks are actually being lost, which is not always where the family expected. You decide afterwards whether to continue.

process.title: A plan built backwards from the school's calendar
process.description: Sessions are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school's internal deadlines, the mandatory-subject timetable and Ramadan hours where relevant. The plan names what will be covered before each deadline, so you can see what you are paying for and when.

process.title: Written notes, and a review you can act on
process.description: Each session ends with a short note naming what was covered and what to practise, which you can forward to the subject teacher. We review the arrangement against the school's own marks, and we will tell you when more hours would add nothing.

whyPoints.title: The regulatory position is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: We name KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Department of Knowledge and the Ministry of Education, explain what each one decides, and link the sources. We hold no permit, accreditation or relationship with any of them and say so. Nobody ranking for these searches writes that sentence, and it is the one a parent should look for.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the course, not on the postcode
whyPoints.description: A Diploma family's real shortage is a specialist in one registered course at one level. Delivering online means the search covers the whole timetable rather than a driving radius, which is why Al Ain, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah families get the same shortlist as Dubai families.

whyPoints.title: The coursework line is written down
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own drafts. No text from a tutor reaches a submission, the school's appointed supervisor keeps that role, and we decline requests that cross the line. One provider in this market sells finished Internal Assessments; that is the risk we exist to be the opposite of.

whyPoints.title: Prices quoted as the market's, dated and attributed
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is somebody else's published rate, read in October 2026, with the publisher named. Our own number comes after a trial lesson, for a specific course and session pattern. We do not print a figure we cannot stand behind for the arrangement in front of us.

whyPoints.title: Dates we could not verify are left blank
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates here come from the boards' own pages. No IB session or results date appears, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unverified date on a planning page is worse than no date. Ask the school's coordinator, or read it on ibo.org.

whyPoints.title: Availability disclosed before payment
whyPoints.description: If the specialist you need is not free, you hear that at the enquiry. If the only specialist available teaches from outside the UAE, you hear that too, with their teaching history and time zone. No competitor in this market discloses a coverage limit, and concealing one is how families end up with a near-match.

faqs.question: What does an IB Diploma online tutor do that my child's subject teacher cannot?
faqs.answer: Three things, mostly. A tutor works with one student, so the diagnosis is specific rather than classwide: they can find out in one session that a Chemistry problem is actually an algebra problem. They work at the student's pace through material the class has already passed, which a teacher with a scheme of work cannot do. And they give sustained feedback on coursework drafts against the published criteria. What they cannot do is change the registration, the level, the option block or a deadline. Those belong to the school, and a tutor who claims influence over them is overselling.

faqs.question: Which authority licenses my child's Diploma school, and does it have any say over the IB?
faqs.answer: It depends on the emirate. Dubai's private schools sit with KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain with ADEK, Sharjah with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the Ministry of Education. Those bodies license the school, oversee quality and, in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah explicitly, approve fees, curricula, programmes, courses and assessment methods. None of them sets Diploma content or marks the papers; that is the IB's. So a fee question goes to the emirate authority and a syllabus question goes to the school's coordinator.

faqs.question: Is a tutor teaching my child from outside the UAE breaking any UAE rule?
faqs.answer: No. The UAE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, applies to individuals providing private lessons inside a UAE employment relationship. Someone teaching over live video from another country is not in one, so the permit does not attach to them. What you should insist on is disclosure: ask where the tutor teaches from, which boards and levels they have taught, and which time zone they will work in. A provider that routes you to a tutor abroad without saying so, or hides it behind a local-looking number, is concealing something it could simply have told you.

faqs.question: My son's school only teaches Physics at Standard Level. Can he still sit Higher Level?
faqs.answer: That decision belongs to the school, not to a tutor, and it turns on whether the school will enter him at Higher Level and support the extra content. Some schools will agree for a strong student with a clear university reason; many will not, because the set, the taught hours and the Internal Assessment supervision all have to exist. Ask the coordinator in writing early in DP1, when a change is still administratively possible. If the school agrees, outside lessons can cover the Higher Level extension content. If it does not, no amount of tuition changes the entry.

faqs.question: Who actually sets the Internal Assessment deadlines my daughter keeps missing?
faqs.answer: Her school does. The subject teacher and the IB coordinator build an internal calendar that stacks coursework deadlines across six subjects plus the core, and those dates are the ones that govern her year. They are not the IB's dates and no regulator will move them. The practical response is to get the whole calendar in writing at the start of the year and plan backwards from it, which is the first thing we ask for at enquiry. A coursework session four weeks before a draft is due is worth several in the final week.

faqs.question: Can a tutor look at a Theory of Knowledge essay before it goes in?
faqs.answer: Yes, as feedback on her own draft, and that is a legitimate and useful hour. A tutor can interrogate the knowledge claims, test whether the examples do any work, point out where an argument skips a step and explain what the assessment criteria reward. What a tutor must not do is choose her position, supply paragraphs, or return a version that reads better than the one she sent. The school's Theory of Knowledge teacher remains the person overseeing the work, and the essay is submitted as her own. If a provider offers more than feedback, that is the signal to stop.

faqs.question: Does my child need a Ministry of Education equivalency file if the plan is a UK university?
faqs.answer: A UK university applies its own admissions requirements and does not ask for UAE equivalency. The equivalency route matters when the certificate has to be recognised inside the UAE: a federal or local university application, a government post, or some professional registrations. Plans change, which is why the sensible move is to ask the Ministry of Education's own channel, or the emirate attestation authority, what would be required in DP1 rather than after results. Keep the documents the school issues. IB Gram does not perform equivalency, cannot submit it for you, and should not be your source for its requirements.

faqs.question: How many Diploma points does the Ministry of Education require for equivalency?
faqs.answer: We will not print a number, because we could not read one on an official UAE source and an invented threshold on a planning page causes real harm. What is published and sourced is the British track: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from those five, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. For the IB, ask the Ministry of Education through moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation channel and get the answer in writing.

faqs.question: The school placed my daughter in Applications and Interpretation. Could that block a UAE engineering degree?
faqs.answer: It might, and the only way to find out is to read the requirement on each programme's own admissions page, including UAE universities. Engineering and the physical sciences commonly expect the analytic route, often at Higher Level, while business, social science and design programmes frequently accept either. Set placements are made by schools for timetable and attainment reasons and can sometimes be revisited early in DP1, so raise it with the coordinator now rather than in DP2. A diagnostic session in each route will also tell you which one she can realistically sustain for two years.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education still have to be on the timetable alongside six Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Yes. Federal rules require private schools to teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's mandatory-subject guidance applies that in Dubai with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Schools must also run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, as combined classes are prohibited. The practical effect is that a Diploma week is fuller than a six-subject diagram suggests, so any tuition plan has to be built around the real timetable.

faqs.question: What should I ask a UAE tutor to show me before I pay for anything?
faqs.answer: Four things. Their MoHRE private tuition work permit if they are teaching from inside the UAE, and the name of the school or employer they work for. Which examination board, course and level they have actually taught, with specifics rather than a list of logos. Where they will be teaching from and in which time zone. And their written position on coursework: what they will do with an Internal Assessment draft and what they will refuse. If any of the four produces vagueness, that is your answer. Also decline any offer involving your child's own classroom teacher.

faqs.question: We move between emirates for work. Does the Diploma registration follow the school or the student?
faqs.answer: The registration sits with the school that entered the candidate, so a move between emirates means a move between IB schools and a transfer of records, coursework progress and predicted grades. The new school's coordinator decides what carries over, and the regulator changes too, since you may be moving from KHDA oversight to ADEK or SPEA. Start the conversation with both coordinators before the move, not after. Tuition continuity is the easy part here: an online arrangement follows the student across an emirate boundary without changing anything about the lesson.

faqs.question: Can lessons run after Iftar during Ramadan, and does the school year shift around it?
faqs.answer: Yes to the first. UAE school hours shorten during Ramadan and household rhythms change, so we move slots later and run post-Iftar sessions where a family prefers them. On the second, the examination calendar does not move for Ramadan: the boards publish their series dates independently, and internal school deadlines are set by the school. The planning implication is to pull coursework work earlier rather than hoping for a quiet fortnight. Families who schedule around Ramadan in January rather than in the week before it keep their momentum.

faqs.question: If no Higher Level specialist is free in the UAE for my child's course, what then?
faqs.answer: We tell you, at the enquiry, before anybody pays. The options at that point are an honest few: wait for the slot you need, take a different pattern such as one longer fortnightly session, or work with a specialist who teaches from outside the UAE over live video, in which case we name where they teach from and what they have taught. What we will not do is put a generalist in front of a Higher Level student and describe them as a specialist. A near-match in a Diploma subject wastes a term you cannot get back.

faqs.question: Where does the school's responsibility end and ours begin on examination entries?
faqs.answer: The school holds the registration, enters the candidate, manages coursework upload, receives results and handles any enquiry upon results. Your part is checking that the entries match reality: the right courses, the right levels, the right session. Ask for written confirmation of the entered levels in the first term, because an error found early is fixable and one found near the papers usually is not. The boards' own deadlines show why: Cambridge's published key dates put final entries for the March 2027 series on 27 November 2026, months before the first paper.

ib-diploma-online-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the system, then buy the hour
ib-diploma-online-tutor.closingBody: A Diploma in the UAE is shaped by four parties: the IB, the emirate authority, the Ministry of Education and your child's school. Work out which of them holds the problem you actually have, and the next step becomes obvious. If it is a timetable constraint, write to the coordinator. If it is a document question, ask the Ministry's own channel. If it is genuinely that a Higher Level topic was never understood, tell us the course, the level and the school's next deadline, and we will say what is available. All UAE lessons are one-to-one online over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, and we will tell you before the trial lesson where your tutor teaches from.

intro.heading: What the Diploma asks for, and what the Emirates ask on top
paragraphs: The IB Diploma Programme is not a syllabus a tutor can approach subject by subject and hope the rest looks after itself. Your child is carrying six subjects drawn from six groups, three of them at Higher Level, and a core of three parts - the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service - that no single subject teacher owns. Forty-two of the forty-five available points come from the subjects; the last three come from the core. A tutor who has only ever taught one subject in isolation will miss where the total actually leaks.

Sitting on top of that is a school system with its own requirements. Whichever emirate your child studies in, a local authority licensed the school, approved its curriculum and published a judgement on it. In Dubai that authority is KHDA. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain it is ADEK. In Sharjah it is the Sharjah Private Education Authority, in Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge, and in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools directly. Those five bodies decide things your child's Diploma coordinator cannot.

They also decide what else is on the timetable. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are compulsory in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school holds a licence for, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the content and the language of instruction differ. A Diploma student here is therefore not studying six subjects and a core. They are studying six subjects, a core, and a set of ministry subjects that sit outside the points total while still taking up weekday hours and homework evenings.

Then there is the paperwork that arrives after the grades. A school-leaving certificate has to be recognised in the Emirates before it opens a place at a UAE university, and the Ministry of Education runs that equivalency process curriculum by curriculum. For British-track students the requirements are published and specific: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count of five, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. For the Diploma, no points threshold appears in any source we are able to cite, so this page publishes none.

What follows sets out that whole frame: the Diploma's own arithmetic, the authority above your child's school, the ministry subjects beside it, the permit a paid tutor needs to charge for lessons here, and the honesty rules governing what any of that help may touch. Market figures are given in AED with the provider named and the month they were read. Lessons from IB Gram are delivered one-to-one over live video, which is how a family in Umm Al Quwain reaches a Higher Level Chemistry specialist rather than whoever happens to be willing to drive out there on a Tuesday.

ib-diploma-tutor.programmesIntro: IB Gram covers the Diploma Programme and the two routes immediately around it, because the choices that decide a Diploma total are usually made two or three years before DP1 starts. Each note below says what the programme is, then what the UAE system adds to it that an overseas guide will not mention.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, one from each of Groups 1 to 5 plus a sixth from Group 6 or a second subject from Groups 1 to 4. Three are taken at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, each graded 1 to 7. Alongside them sit the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an internally marked, externally moderated assessment component, and the school - not the IB - sets the dates those are due.
programmes.countryNote: In the Emirates the Diploma is the smaller of the mainstream options: the IB accounted for 7 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25, against 37 per cent on UK curricula and 26 per cent Indian. That share shapes tutoring. A school running one Diploma cohort may have a single teacher for a Group 4 Higher Level, and a family north of Sharjah may find no Diploma school within a sensible commute at all.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme course candidate route
programmes.description: A student may take individual Diploma subjects and receive course results for them without registering for the full Diploma. There is no requirement to spread across all six groups, no Higher Level quota, and the core is not compulsory, so no point total out of 45 is issued. Subjects are examined and graded on the same 1 to 7 scale by the same examiners, and internal assessment still applies to each one.
programmes.countryNote: UAE families reach this route for two reasons. Either the school cannot staff a sixth subject the student wants, or a Higher Level is going badly enough in DP2 that the full Diploma is at risk. Before moving, ask the coordinator in writing what course results mean for the universities on your child's list and for a Ministry of Education equivalency file, because the answer differs by destination and is not something a tutoring provider can settle for you.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The five-year programme that feeds the Diploma inside IB continuum schools. Assessment runs against four published criteria per subject, marked in school on a 1 to 8 scale per criterion rather than by external examiners. Students take a broad spread of subjects, with language acquisition, sciences, individuals and societies, mathematics, arts, design and physical and health education all running at once, and a Personal Project in the final year.
programmes.countryNote: The step from MYP 5 into DP1 is where most UAE Diploma tutoring requests begin. The content gap is smaller than parents fear; the assessment gap is larger. A student used to criterion-marked tasks set by their own teacher meets externally marked papers written around command terms for the first time, and in a school whose Diploma cohort is new, there may be no archive of past student work for a teacher to show them.

ib-diploma-tutor.subjectsIntro: A Diploma timetable is built by group, not by subject, so this grid is laid out the way your child's choices were actually made. Each entry names what the group covers in UAE schools, where the marks go missing, and which parts a tutor can usefully take on. The three core requirements are listed last, because they are where families most often discover help is needed late.

subjects.name: Group 1: Language A - Language and Literature, or Literature
subjects.description: Usually English in UAE international schools, with Arabic A, Hindi and other languages offered as school size allows. Assessment combines timed papers on unseen and studied texts with an individual oral and, at Higher Level, an essay on a studied work. Marks are lost on comparison and on sustained argument rather than on reading comprehension.

subjects.name: Group 2: Language acquisition - Arabic B, Arabic ab initio, French B, Spanish B
subjects.levels: HL and SL; ab initio is SL only
subjects.description: The one group where a UAE mandatory subject can also earn Diploma points, if the school streams Arabic so that a student's level matches a Group 2 course. Assessment is listening, reading, writing and an individual oral. Non-Arab students starting from very little are the natural ab initio candidates, and that decision is made in DP1, not DP2.

subjects.name: Group 3: Individuals and societies - Economics, Business Management, History, Psychology, Global Politics
subjects.description: Essay-marked subjects where command terms decide the mark. Students who write everything they know about a topic score below students who answer the question asked. Each subject carries its own internal assessment - a commentary, a research project or a case study - and the Higher Level papers add an extra component rather than simply more content.

subjects.name: Group 4: Sciences - Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Computer Science, Sports Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: The hardest group to staff in a small UAE cohort and the one most often behind a tutoring enquiry. All share a practical scheme of work and an internally assessed investigation the student designs themselves. Marks go on evaluation and on uncertainty handling, not on recall, and the Higher Level syllabus adds whole topics rather than deeper versions of the same ones.

subjects.name: Group 5: Mathematics - Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route for students heading towards engineering, physics, economics at a quantitative university or mathematics itself. Proof, algebraic fluency and calculus carry the papers, one of which is sat without a calculator. The exploration is marked against published criteria and is where many otherwise strong students drop several points by choosing a topic with nothing to analyse.

subjects.name: Group 5: Mathematics - Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-assisted work, with every paper calculator-permitted. It is not the easy route and it is not a lesser qualification; it is a different one. Before choosing it, check the entry requirements of the specific university courses on your child's list, because some quantitative degrees name Analysis and Approaches explicitly.

subjects.name: Group 6: The arts - Visual Arts, Music, Theatre, Film
subjects.description: Portfolio and performance-assessed subjects, with written and curatorial components that catch students out because they are graded as rigorously as an essay. A Diploma student may instead take a second subject from Groups 1 to 4 here, and in smaller UAE schools that is often the only option on the timetable.

subjects.name: Core: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece in one subject, supervised by a school teacher and marked externally from A to E. It contributes to the three core points through a matrix shared with Theory of Knowledge. A grade E is a failing condition for the Diploma, which is why the research question matters more than the writing.

subjects.name: Core: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed through an essay on a prescribed title, written to a 1,600-word limit, and an exhibition of three objects with a commentary of roughly 950 words. It has no subject grade of its own; it is graded A to E and combines with the Extended Essay for the final three points. Students who treat it as an opinion piece score badly.

subjects.name: Core: Creativity, Activity, Service
subjects.description: A portfolio of experiences and at least one longer project, with reflections, signed off in school as complete or not complete. It carries no points and cannot be skipped: an incomplete record is a failing condition. The useful tutoring contribution here is time management against the school's own deadlines, nothing more.

ib-diploma-tutor.regionsTitle: Where the Diploma is actually taught, emirate by emirate
ib-diploma-tutor.regionsIntro: Diploma availability is uneven across the Emirates, and that unevenness is the real reason a family starts looking for outside help. The notes below say which authority publishes the inspection material you can read, and what Diploma subject choice realistically looks like on the ground. Figures on new schools and places come from KHDA announcements for the 2026-27 intake.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The deepest Diploma market in the country and the only one where a student can usually find their sixth subject on the timetable. KHDA licenses and inspects the schools, publishes the reports you can read before paying for anything, and confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for 2026-27.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Diploma provision is concentrated on the island, Khalifa City and Al Raha, so Group 4 Higher Level choice narrows quickly outside those clusters.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK rather than a regulator of its own, which surprises families who have moved from Dubai. The Diploma cohort in any one Al Ain school tends to be small, so a student wanting a less common Higher Level is often the only candidate in their year taking it, with no study group and one teacher.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Subject availability therefore depends on an approval process at emirate level, not only on what a school would like to open. Many Sharjah families commute to Dubai schools, which pushes tutoring slots late into the evening.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority, so there is no local inspection portal to read. Diploma places are few, and families often enrol in Sharjah or Dubai instead. Online delivery removes the commute from the tutoring decision entirely, which matters more here than it does further south.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. Diploma provision exists but is thin, and a student who wants a Group 6 arts subject or a second language may have to take a course candidate route instead of the full Diploma.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised federally by the Ministry of Education, with the smallest international school sector of the seven emirates and effectively no choice of Diploma school. Families here are the clearest case for one-to-one online teaching: the nearest subject specialist for a Higher Level science is not within driving distance of anywhere in the emirate.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai's Diploma provision runs across Emirates Hills, Al Barsha, Arabian Ranches, the Festival City corridor and Mirdif. KHDA's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools - four on UK curricula and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. More schools is not yet more Higher Level science teachers.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School - Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.note: Diploma provision licensed by ADEK clusters on Abu Dhabi island, Khalifa City, Al Raha and Saadiyat. Students we support attend schools across this group. Cohorts are smaller than Dubai's, which is why a Diploma student here more often needs a specialist for exactly one subject rather than general academic support.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi
The British International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.note: Diploma schools thin out sharply north of Dubai. Sharjah's provision is regulated by SPEA, while schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah fall under the federal Ministry of Education. A family in Ras Al Khaimah choosing the Diploma is usually choosing it at one particular school, with the subject list that school can staff.

ib-diploma-tutor.modesIntro: Four arrangements cover almost every Diploma request we receive from the Emirates. All of them run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and all of them are built around your child's school calendar rather than ours, because the internal deadlines that drive the year are set in school.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one in a single subject
modes.description: One specialist, one subject, a fixed weekly slot for a term at a time. This is what most Diploma families need and it is deliberately narrow: a Chemistry Higher Level tutor who also claims Economics and Maths Analysis and Approaches is usually a general tutor wearing three hats. Progress is judged against the school's own assessment points, not a separate curriculum invented by us.
bullets: 45, 60 or 90-minute sessions depending on the subject
Reviewed with you every six weeks against school assessments
Session notes written up and shared the same evening
Slot held through Ramadan at a post-Iftar time if you want it

modes.title: Core supervision blocks
modes.description: Short blocks of sessions around the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the subject internal assessments, timed to your school's internal deadlines. The work is teaching and feedback: discussing a research question, explaining what a prescribed title is asking, reading a draft and asking the questions an examiner would. Every word submitted stays your child's own, and we will tell you if a request crosses that line.
bullets: Research question and method discussed before the writing starts
Criteria explained letter by letter with their mark allocations
Draft read and questioned, never rewritten
Word and page limits checked against the subject's published guidance

modes.title: Transition support into DP1
modes.description: A block of sessions between IGCSE, MYP or Grade 10 and the start of the Diploma, aimed at the assessment gap rather than the content gap. Most of the work is command terms, unfamiliar problem solving and the independent design expected in an internal assessment. It is the cheapest intervention in the two years and the one families most often skip.
bullets: Subject-by-subject diagnostic before the first session
Past-paper technique using the official syllabus the school names
Six to twelve weeks, usually across the summer
A written handover note for the first term of DP1

sections.heading: What a Diploma tutor has to know that a general subject tutor does not
paragraphs: Parents searching for an IB Diploma tutor in the UAE are usually one subject into the problem. Chemistry is going badly, or the maths exploration has stalled, and the obvious move is to find somebody who knows that subject. That is necessary and it is not sufficient. The Diploma awards points on a fixed arithmetic, carries internal deadlines the school sets rather than the IB, and runs inside a school licensed by an emirate authority with its own requirements bolted onto the week. A tutor who knows only the subject is working blind on three of those four things.

The practical difference shows up in what a tutor asks in the first session. A subject-only tutor asks which topic is hard. A Diploma specialist asks which six subjects your child took, which three are Higher Level, what the Extended Essay subject is, when the school's internal coursework deadlines fall, what the January mock produced and whether predicted grades have already gone to universities. Those answers change the plan completely. Twelve weeks of Chemistry help before a mock is a different purchase from twelve weeks spent rescuing a Group 3 Higher Level that is dragging the total under the award threshold.

It also changes what the help is allowed to be. The Diploma's academic-honesty rules bind the student, and the declaration your child signs covers outside assistance. A paid tutor can teach the physics, model the technique, read a draft and ask hard questions about it. The words, the data and the argument stay the student's own. A family offered anything more than that has been offered a route to a malpractice investigation, and the research behind these pages found one provider in this market selling finished internal assessments outright at a published price.
bullets: Ask a prospective tutor which group your child's weak subject sits in
Ask when the school's internal assessment deadline falls, not the IB's
Ask what the tutor will not do with a draft, and listen to the answer
Ask whether they have taught the Higher Level, not just the subject

sections.heading: The six groups, and the choices your child has already locked in
paragraphs: A Diploma timetable is assembled from six groups, and by the time a parent is reading a tutoring page the assembly is finished. One subject comes from each of Groups 1 to 5. The sixth comes from Group 6, the arts, or is a second subject from Groups 1 to 4 where the school can staff it. Three of the six are taken at Higher Level, with more taught hours and extra assessment components, and three at Standard Level. Changing any of it in DP2 needs the coordinator's agreement and usually the registration to have not yet closed.

That structure explains most of what goes wrong. A student who took two sciences and no arts subject has a heavier practical load and two internal investigations to design rather than one. A student who chose Analysis and Approaches because it sounded more impressive, without checking whether their university courses asked for it, has bought a calculator-free paper they did not need. A student whose school offered only one Group 3 subject is studying it whether or not it suits them. None of this is fixable by working harder at the subject in isolation.

The group structure also interacts with the mandatory UAE subjects in one useful way. Group 2 is language acquisition, and a school that streams Arabic properly can place a student in a Group 2 Arabic course that earns Diploma points while satisfying part of the ministry requirement. Islamic Education and Social Studies have no such route: they sit outside the 45 points entirely. Knowing which of your child's weekly Arabic hours can count and which cannot is the single most useful question to put to the coordinator.

sections.heading: Forty-five points, and where every one of them comes from
paragraphs: The Diploma total is simple arithmetic that almost nobody explains to parents. Each of the six subjects is graded 1 to 7, giving 42 points. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are each graded A to E and combine in a single matrix worth up to three further points. Creativity, Activity, Service carries no points at all but must be recorded as complete. Forty-two plus three is the 45 that gets quoted in newspapers, and the three that come last are the ones families notice last.

Two misunderstandings cost real points. The first is that a Higher Level subject is worth more than a Standard Level one. It is not: both are graded out of 7, and Higher Level simply demands more taught hours, more syllabus and an extra assessment component for the same ceiling. The second is that a grade 7 is a fixed percentage. It is not: boundaries are set per session after marking, which is exactly why no honest tutor will tell you what mark your child needs on Paper 2 to secure one.

The core is where the arithmetic turns sharp. Three points sounds negligible until a university offer sits at 38 and the subjects have delivered 36. A grade A in both the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge is the difference, and both are written in DP1 and early DP2, long before anyone is thinking about offers. That is the strongest argument for spending tutoring money early rather than in the last term, when only exam technique is still movable.

sections.heading: The conditions under which a Diploma is not awarded
paragraphs: Most families know the figure 24 and assume it is the whole rule. It is one condition among several. A student can clear 24 points and still not be awarded the Diploma, because the IB applies a set of separate conditions covering the core, the spread of low grades and the balance between Higher and Standard Level. Those conditions are published in the IB's assessment procedures, they are revised from time to time, and the current year's wording is something your child's coordinator holds and should be asked for directly.

The shape of them is worth understanding before any tutoring money is spent, because it changes where the money should go. A single grade 1 anywhere, a failing core grade, an incomplete Creativity Activity Service record, or too many grade 2s concentrated at Higher Level can each stop the award on their own. That is why a competent plan looks at the weakest subject rather than the one the student most enjoys improving, and at the core rather than the subject already sitting on a 6.

It is also why we will not quote an exact set of thresholds on a web page. Numbers published without the current source attached are how one competitor in this market came to state the wrong subject count for a Ministry of Education requirement. Ask the coordinator for the award conditions in writing, read them against your child's predicted grades, and then decide which two subjects or which core component actually need paid hours. A tutor who has taught the Diploma will do that reading with you in the first session.
bullets: A failing grade in the Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge can stop the award
An incomplete Creativity, Activity, Service record can stop it as well
Low grades concentrated at Higher Level are treated differently from the same grades at Standard Level
Academic misconduct is handled separately and can remove the award entirely
Get the current conditions from the coordinator rather than from any tutoring site

sections.heading: Which authority sits above your child's Diploma, and what it approves
paragraphs: The IB authorises a school to teach the Diploma. A UAE authority licenses that school to operate at all, approves what it teaches and publishes a judgement on how well it does so. Those are different powers held by different bodies, and conflating them is the most common error in tutoring copy aimed at this market. Five authorities cover the seven emirates, and the one above your child's school decides fees, curricula and, in some emirates, assessment methods.

This matters when a family moves. A Dubai inspection report does not follow a child to Sharjah, and the approval route for a new subject in Sharjah or Ras Al Khaimah runs through the emirate authority rather than the school alone. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, which quietly rules out the arrangement many families would otherwise prefer. That rule has been press-reported rather than read by us from a current policy document, so verify it against ADEK's own publication before relying on it.

What none of these authorities does is set your child's grades. Paper weightings, internal assessment criteria, moderation and grade boundaries belong to the IB. No UAE regulator approves, accredits or licenses a tutoring provider to teach the Diploma, and any page claiming such status is describing something that does not exist for an individual tutor. A tuition business with premises and staff in Dubai is a different case: it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry.

sections.heading: The ministry subjects sharing a Diploma timetable
paragraphs: Private schools in the Emirates are not obliged to follow a particular curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must follow the Ministry's general regulations. That federal baseline is why a Diploma student in Dubai carries subjects that contribute nothing to their 45 points. KHDA's requirements for the mandatory subjects applied from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April, and they are more prescriptive than most parents realise.

The rules reach into how classes are formed and what language they run in. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; non-Arabs study Islamic Education and moral, social and cultural studies in the language of the school's licensed curriculum.

Two further details matter for planning tutoring hours. Instructional time for the mandatory subjects is calculated in 40-minute lesson units, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and any mandatory subject lesson is advised to run at least 25 minutes. And for these subjects the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, so a tutor cannot simply bring their own Arabic worksheets. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic in Dubai schools must hold the relevant KHDA permission to teach those subjects.

sections.heading: Coming into DP1 from IGCSE, MYP or an American high school
paragraphs: The IGCSE to IB Diploma transition is the busiest tutoring request of the UAE summer, and it is usually misdiagnosed. Parents describe it as a content gap, so they buy content. The gap that actually bites is assessment: a student who scored A* by executing well-practised methods on predictable questions meets unfamiliar problems, command terms that instruct the examiner as much as the candidate, and an internal assessment they are expected to design without being told what to do. The content catches up in weeks. The habits take a term.

Each starting point fails differently, which is why a generic bridging course is poor value. An IGCSE mathematician moving to Analysis and Approaches hits a non-calculator paper and a proof requirement. An IGCSE Combined Science student moving to a single Group 4 subject hits the independent investigation. An MYP 5 student hits externally marked papers for the first time. An American Grade 10 student moving into Group 1 hits comparative analysis under time. Naming the specific failure point is most of the work, and it can be done in one diagnostic session.

There is a timing argument too. Support delivered between Year 11 and DP1, or in the first eight weeks of DP1, is cheaper per point recovered than anything bought in DP2, because the internal assessments and the Extended Essay have not yet been submitted. By February of DP2, the only things still movable are exam technique and the final drafts. Families in the Emirates who have moved curriculum once already, which is most of them, tend to understand this faster than the brochures assume.

sections.heading: What Diploma tuition costs in the UAE market
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. So here are IB Diploma tutor rates in AED, read from each provider's own public pricing in October 2026 and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. These are market figures attributed to the providers that published them, not a price list of ours. They tell you what band your enquiry sits in before anyone quotes you.

The bands are wide for a reason, and the reason is rarely quality alone. A university student teaching Standard Level content and a subject specialist who has taught the Higher Level syllabus for a decade are doing different jobs, and so are an online hour and a two-hour visit that includes a drive across Dubai. Monthly packages seen in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist support in an exam year.

Set those figures against the rest of the bill rather than in isolation. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. A family already paying a Diploma school fee is deciding how to spend a marginal few thousand dirhams a year, and the answer is usually fewer hours on the right subject rather than more hours spread thin. sections.heading: A visiting tutor in the Emirates, or one-to-one over live video
paragraphs: Searches for a Diploma tutor in this market still mean, to most families, somebody at the dining table twice a week. That arrangement exists here and it is widely sold, at AED 180-500 an hour with travel inside the rate and usually a two-hour minimum to make the journey worth making. It has real advantages: a teenager cannot close a laptop on a person sitting beside them. It also has one structural limit that matters more in the Emirates than almost anywhere else.

The limit is the tutor pool. A visiting arrangement selects from whoever teaches your child's subject within a tolerable drive of your address in the evening traffic. For Group 1 English or Standard Level Biology in Dubai, that pool is adequate. For Physics Higher Level in Al Ain, Computer Science in Ras Al Khaimah, or Theory of Knowledge supervision anywhere north of Sharjah, it is often empty. Online IB Diploma tuition in the UAE selects instead from every specialist whose working hours overlap Gulf Standard Time, which is a far larger set and the honest reason we deliver this way.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the Emirates; that service runs only in India. Lessons here are one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for working through a paper, the session recorded if you want it and a written summary afterwards. For a Diploma family the practical gain is that the match is made on subject and level rather than on postcode, and a cancelled slot costs nobody a wasted drive. sections.heading: The core, and the line a paid tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Extended Essay supervision and Theory of Knowledge support are the two requests where a tutoring arrangement most often goes wrong, because the help a student needs and the help that breaks the rules look superficially similar. Both components are the student's own work, declared as such, and both are supervised inside the school by a teacher who signs for the process. A paid tutor sits outside that process and must behave accordingly: teaching the subject, explaining the criteria, discussing a research question, reading a draft and asking the questions an examiner would ask.

What that rules out is simple to state. No tutor supplies text that ends up in a submission. No tutor chooses the research question, collects the data, builds the argument or rewrites a paragraph into something better than the student could produce. No tutor edits a piece to completion. These are not house style preferences; outside assistance beyond legitimate teaching is a malpractice matter for the student, and the consequence falls on them rather than on whoever took the fee. Our research into this market found a provider advertising finished internal assessments for sale, which is exactly the offer to walk away from.

Within those limits there is a great deal a specialist can usefully do, and the published limits are a good place to start a first session. Criteria letters with their mark allocations, the word and page ceilings for each component, and the school's own internal deadlines together make a plan. Most students who lose core points lose them to a weak research question chosen in a hurry and a timetable that left no room for a second draft - both problems a tutor is allowed to fix, and both problems best fixed in DP1.

sections.heading: Who may be paid to teach your child, and what equivalency asks later
paragraphs: Private tuition in the Emirates is a permitted activity with a permit attached. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the smart app, website or e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published, so no figure belongs on a page like this, and a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source. What a parent can reasonably do is ask. A UAE-resident tutor can show the permit; an overseas tutor teaching your child over video is a different arrangement, and we tell you which one you are being offered before the first paid session rather than after it.

Equivalency comes later and belongs to the Ministry of Education, not to any tutoring provider. The British-track requirements are published: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. On the American track, English is demonstrated by IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in SAT reading and writing, and mathematics by at least 450 in SAT Math. For the Diploma, verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority directly. We describe the process; we do not run it, and tuition is not a requirement of it.

faqs.question: How many subjects does the IB Diploma require, and how are Higher and Standard Level split across them?
faqs.answer: Six subjects, one from each of Groups 1 to 5, with the sixth taken from Group 6, the arts, or as a second subject from Groups 1 to 4. Three of the six are studied at Higher Level and three at Standard Level. Higher Level carries more taught hours, more syllabus and usually an extra examination component, but it is graded on the same scale of 1 to 7, so it is not worth more points. Students taking four Higher Levels do so by agreement with the school and carry the extra load for no additional points.

faqs.question: Where do the final three points on top of the forty-two subject points come from?
faqs.answer: From the core. The Extended Essay is graded A to E by an external examiner, Theory of Knowledge is graded A to E from the essay and the exhibition together, and the two grades combine in a single matrix worth up to three points. Creativity, Activity, Service earns nothing but must be recorded as complete. So 42 points come from the six subjects and three from the core, giving the 45 everyone quotes. Those last three are written and submitted in DP1 and early DP2, long before results matter, which is why they are the cheapest points to protect.

faqs.question: Can my daughter count her school's Arabic lessons as one of her six Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking the coordinator directly. Group 2 is language acquisition, and a school that streams Arabic by level can place a student in a Group 2 Arabic B or ab initio course that earns Diploma points while also meeting part of the mandatory requirement. Arab students may be able to take Arabic as a Group 1 Language A subject instead. Islamic Education and Social Studies have no such route and sit outside the 45 points entirely. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in these subjects, so the stream your daughter is in affects the answer.

faqs.question: What can stop a Diploma being awarded even when a student reaches twenty-four points?
faqs.answer: Several separate conditions apply alongside the points total. A failing grade in the Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge, an incomplete Creativity Activity Service record, a grade 1 in any subject, or low grades concentrated at Higher Level can each prevent the award on their own, and academic misconduct is handled separately. The IB publishes these conditions in its assessment procedures and revises them from time to time, so the version that matters is the current one your child's coordinator holds. Ask for it in writing and read it against the predicted grades before deciding where tutoring hours should go.

faqs.question: Is the Diploma Programme actually taught in every emirate?
faqs.answer: No, and the gaps shape what tutoring a family needs. Dubai has the deepest provision, and the International Baccalaureate accounted for 7 per cent of its private-school enrolment in 2024-25. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have established Diploma schools under ADEK. Sharjah, Ajman and Ras Al Khaimah each have a small number. In Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain there is effectively no choice of Diploma school. Where provision is thin, subject choice narrows and a student may be the only candidate in their year taking a particular Higher Level, with one teacher and no study group.

faqs.question: My son wants to take four Higher Levels. Is that permitted, and is it sensible?
faqs.answer: It is permitted with the school's agreement, and plenty of UAE students do it. Whether it is sensible depends on what it is for. Four Higher Levels bring more taught hours, more syllabus and an extra assessment component each, for no additional points beyond the 7 available in every subject. Universities set their offers in points and in named subjects, not in a count of Higher Levels. If a specific course requires a fourth Higher Level, take it. If the reason is that it looks stronger on paper, the same effort spent protecting a weak subject and the core usually returns more points.

faqs.question: Can a student in the UAE sit the IB Diploma as a private candidate without being enrolled at a school?
faqs.answer: The Diploma is awarded through schools the IB has authorised, and registration for examinations is made by the school, not by a family. Internal assessment, the Extended Essay and Creativity Activity Service all require supervision inside the school, so there is no straightforward private-candidate route comparable to entering an IGCSE at a centre. Families whose circumstances rule out school enrolment should ask an authorised school directly, and should treat any provider offering to arrange the Diploma without a school with real caution. Other qualifications have genuine private-candidate routes; the full Diploma does not work that way.

faqs.question: What is the Theory of Knowledge exhibition, and how does it differ from the essay?
faqs.answer: They are two separate assessments feeding one grade. The exhibition asks a student to choose three objects, link each to an internal assessment prompt and write a commentary of roughly 950 words explaining how knowledge works in each case. The essay is a 1,600-word response to a prescribed title set by the IB for that session. Students usually find the exhibition harder to start and the essay harder to finish. Together they produce a grade from A to E, which combines with the Extended Essay grade in the matrix worth up to three points.

faqs.question: My child left IGCSE with an A in maths and is struggling in DP1. What actually changed?
faqs.answer: The assessment changed more than the content did. IGCSE rewards accurate execution of methods a student has practised on predictable question types. Analysis and Approaches asks for proof, reasoning and progress on unfamiliar problems, and one of its papers is sat without a calculator. The exploration then asks for an independent piece of mathematics with nothing prescribed. A student with strong technique and no habit of unfamiliar problem solving looks as though they have lost ability; they have met a different demand. Eight to twelve weeks of problem-led work usually restores the position, and it is cheaper in DP1 than in DP2.

faqs.question: Our school is running the Diploma for the first time next year. What should we ask it?
faqs.answer: Ask which subjects it can staff at Higher Level, not which appear in the brochure, and how many students are expected in each. Ask who will supervise Extended Essays and in which subjects, since supervision capacity is the usual bottleneck in a first cohort. Ask what archive of past student work and marked exemplars teachers can show your child, because a new cohort has none. Finally, ask which authority licensed the school and read its most recent published judgement. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds three new International Baccalaureate schools, so this question is live for a good number of families.

faqs.question: How do predicted grades work for a Diploma student applying to university from the Emirates?
faqs.answer: Predicted grades are produced by the school, subject teacher by subject teacher, and sent with the application. They are not negotiable by a family and not something a tutoring provider can influence by asking. What moves them is evidence: mock results, internal assessment marks and classwork in the term before applications go out. That is why the useful window for tutoring sits before the predictions are made rather than after. Once the predictions are issued, the remaining work is converting them into final grades, which is a different and narrower job.

faqs.question: Which part of the Ministry of Education equivalency file can a Diploma family prepare in advance?
faqs.answer: The document-gathering part. Attestation of certificates, transcripts and identity documents takes time and is largely independent of results, so it can be started while your child is still in DP2. What cannot be prepared in advance is the requirement itself: the British-track rules are published in detail, while no Diploma points threshold appears in any source we can cite, so verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority before assuming anything. No tutoring provider performs, guarantees or speeds up this process, and tuition is not a condition of it.

faqs.question: We can fund tuition in two subjects, not six. Which two should they be?
faqs.answer: Start with whichever subject most threatens the award rather than whichever is most enjoyable to improve. A grade 1, a Higher Level sitting on a 2, or a core component heading for a low letter does more damage to a total than a 5 that could become a 6. Then look at the core, because the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are worth three points between them and are usually unsupervised in practice. A specialist can make that call properly in one session once they have the six subjects, the levels and the most recent school assessment data.

faqs.question: We expected a tutor at the kitchen table. What does a live video Diploma lesson do instead?
faqs.answer: It changes who is available rather than what happens in the hour. A visiting arrangement selects from whoever teaches the subject within a tolerable drive, which is adequate for Standard Level English in Dubai and often empty for Physics Higher Level in Al Ain. Teaching over live video selects from every specialist whose hours overlap Gulf Standard Time. In the session itself you get a shared screen for working through a paper, an optional recording and a written summary. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the Emirates; that service runs only in India.

faqs.question: Does Creativity, Activity, Service need any help from a tutor?
faqs.answer: Not teaching, no. It carries no points and is signed off in school as complete or not complete, and the activities and reflections have to be entirely the student's own. What goes wrong is almost never effort; it is record-keeping. Students complete experiences and never write the reflections, then discover in DP2 that the portfolio is short and the coordinator cannot sign it off. An incomplete record can stop the Diploma being awarded. If a tutor contributes anything here, it is diarying the reflections against the coordinator's deadlines, which costs very little.

faqs.question: Does my child sit the Diploma exams at their own school?
faqs.answer: In almost every case, yes. The school is the examination centre, it registers candidates with the IB, and it holds the deadline that closes registration months before the papers are sat. Families who move emirate or country mid-programme should raise this with both coordinators early, because transferring a registration is an administrative process with its own cut-off. We do not publish IB session or results dates on this page: those come from your coordinator or from ibo.org, and a date copied from a tutoring site is not a date worth diarying.

ib-diploma-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the structure, then buy the hours
ib-diploma-tutor.closingBody: An IB Diploma tutor in the UAE is worth paying for once you know which of the 45 points are actually at risk and which part of the system is holding them back - a group choice made in DP1, a core component with no deadline against it, a Higher Level nobody at the school can staff properly, or a transition that was never bridged. Send the six subjects, the three Higher Levels and the emirate, and the first free trial lesson will tell you which of those it is. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, and we will say before you book if the right specialist is not UAE-resident.

intro.heading: What an IB DP home tutor costs in the UAE, and what the money is really buying
paragraphs: The phrase covers three different purchases. The first is a subject rescue: a Higher Level science or Mathematics grade that fell at the first mock and needs weekly attention for eighteen months. The second is a component purchase, bought in a block: four hours of Internal Assessment supervision, six on the Extended Essay, three on a Theory of Knowledge essay. The third is a technique purchase in the final term, where the content is known and the marks are being lost to timing, command terms and unfinished papers. These three jobs cost very different amounts, and the commonest budgeting mistake a UAE family makes is to buy the first when the evidence points at the third.

The UAE market publishes enough to price all three. A generalist or university-student tutor working online advertises from AED 33 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. A qualified subject teacher online runs roughly AED 150 to AED 300; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A tutor who travels to a UAE address is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table sitting at AED 180 to AED 350. Declared specialists in IB, IGCSE and A-Level sit at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, TutorChase quoting AED 270, and a named or examiner-tier tutor can reach AED 650, as BartyED advertises. Those are market figures collected in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

Four things move a Diploma quote inside those bands, and only one of them is about the tutor's biography. Scarcity does most of the work: a Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level teacher or a Chemistry HL option specialist is simply rarer than a Standard Level Business Management tutor, and rarity sets the rate. Proximity does the rest. A search that filters by what is reachable within a thirty-minute drive of Mirdif or Al Reem Island returns a short list, and a short list prices up. Exam proximity is the third: the same hour is dearer in February than in September because everyone wants the same ten weeks. Format is the fourth, and it is the only one a family controls outright.

This is where the honest answer to the search matters. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are something we offer only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, timetabled in Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own script, criteria sheet and mark breakdown on a shared screen. The point is not that online is a cheaper substitute. The point is that it detaches the price from the postcode: a family in Ras Al Khaimah or Khalifa City gets the Physics HL specialist the subject needs rather than whoever happens to be free within driving distance that evening, and nobody is paying for the drive.

What follows prices the Diploma the way it is actually assessed. There is a rate table with its sources named, an audit of all six Diploma slots that says plainly where paid hours change an outcome and where they do not, a Higher and Standard Level comparison read as a spending decision, component blocks costed at published market rates, four real-shaped UAE family budgets, the academic-honesty boundary that protects the money you spend, and the two UAE bills nobody puts on a tutoring quote: the Ministry subjects running alongside the Diploma and the equivalency file a graduate needs afterwards.
