sections.heading: Which authority sits above your child's Diploma school, and what it reaches into
paragraphs: Private schools in this country are not regulated federally in one place. Dubai sits with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah sits with the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge. The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The reach of these bodies goes beyond inspection. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Dubai's authority confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. So the Diploma your child sits is an IB programme delivered inside a nationally regulated shell.

For a parent choosing tuition, three practical things follow. First, the inspection report you should read is published by the authority that licenses your school, not by a tutoring company. Second, no tutoring provider is approved by any of these bodies to teach the Diploma, and a claim of that kind on a tutoring site is a reason to close the tab. Third, the authority that licenses your school is the one whose rules decide what Arabic and Islamic Education your child has to carry alongside six IB subjects.

sections.heading: Why a UAE school can run only some Higher Levels
paragraphs: A school offers a Diploma subject at a given level when three things line up: the school is authorised by the IB to run the programme, it has a teacher for that subject at that level, and enough students choose it to justify a block on the timetable. In a large Dubai school all three usually hold. In an Al Ain, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah school with a Diploma cohort of thirty, the third condition fails routinely, and the subject appears at Standard Level only, or in a combined class taught across both levels.

Option blocks are the mechanism families collide with. The school groups subjects into columns and a student picks one subject from each column. Two choices in the same column cannot both be taken, whatever the student's ability or intentions. This is a timetabling constraint, not an academic judgement, and it is normally finalised in the spring before DP1 starts. Dubai is adding seven private schools and 16,846 places for 2026-27, three of them IB schools, which widens provision across the emirate without changing the arithmetic inside any single school's blocks.

What a family can actually do about it falls into a short list. Ask for the block structure in writing before choices are made, not after. Ask whether a combined Higher and Standard Level class is planned, because that changes how much content the Higher Level students get taught directly. Ask whether the school will support a subject taken outside the timetable, and on what terms. And if the answer closes a university route, plan for the content to be covered elsewhere with clear eyes about what that does and does not change on the transcript.
bullets: Ask for the option blocks in writing before DP1 subject choices close
Ask whether Higher and Standard Level will be taught in one combined class
Ask how many students are in the Higher Level set for your child's subject
Ask which subjects were withdrawn last year for low numbers, and why

sections.heading: The Diploma week, with the mandatory UAE subjects already in it
paragraphs: The IB publishes guided teaching hours for Diploma subjects: 240 for a Higher Level subject and 150 for a Standard Level one, with 100 hours for Theory of Knowledge and around 40 hours of student work for the Extended Essay. Add six subjects and the core together and the school's timetable is close to full before anything local is added. Then the local requirement arrives.

Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. The authority's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit; schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

For tuition planning, two consequences follow. A Diploma student in Dubai has less discretionary evening time than the subject-hours arithmetic suggests, so booking three subjects at two sessions a week produces a timetable nobody can revise inside. And tutoring for the mandatory subjects is a different purchase with a different constraint: for these subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, so a tutor works from the school's approved material rather than bringing a syllabus of their own.

sections.heading: Criterion letters, marks and limits, component by component
paragraphs: Internal assessments are marked against lettered criteria with published mark allocations, and almost nothing on this search result tells parents what they are. This matters because the criteria are not weighted evenly. In the Extended Essay, critical thinking carries more than three times what presentation carries. In the mathematics exploration, use of mathematics carries more than personal engagement and reflection combined. A student who polishes the formatting of an Extended Essay and leaves the analysis thin has spent effort in the cheapest place on the rubric.

Word and page limits are equally under-discussed. The Extended Essay stops at 4,000 words. The Theory of Knowledge essay is capped at 1,600 and the exhibition commentary at 950. A history investigation runs to 2,200 words, a science investigation to 3,000, and the Higher Level English essay sits between 1,200 and 1,500. Examiners are not required to read beyond a limit, so the conclusion a student placed after the cut-off may simply not be marked.

A tutor's legitimate work here is narrow and valuable: explain what each criterion rewards, show the student where their own draft currently sits against it, and ask the questions that make the student revise it themselves. The marks in the table below should be checked against the current subject guide through your child's coordinator, because the IB revises guides subject by subject on different cycles and a figure that was right for last year's cohort may not be right for this one.

sections.heading: What a paid tutor may touch, and what your child signs
paragraphs: Every piece of assessed Diploma work is submitted with an authenticity declaration, and supervisors sign to say the work is the student's own. Supervision sessions for the Extended Essay are recorded in school, and coordinators ask directly about outside assistance. A tutor who treats that as paperwork is a risk to your child, because the consequence of a malpractice finding lands on the student, not on the tutor.

The honest boundary is easy to state. A tutor may teach the content, explain the criteria, question an argument until the student sees the weakness, model a worked example on a different problem, mark a timed paper against the mark scheme, and give written feedback on a draft the student produced. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite sections into their own words, correct a draft to the point where the judgement is theirs, select the research question on the student's behalf, or hand over material presented as the student's own thinking. One provider in this market advertises finished internal assessments for sale. That is a malpractice trigger and a straightforward reason to avoid them.

Two practical tests help a parent stay the right side of this. First, could your child explain every sentence in the submitted work, including why it is there? If not, somebody else's thinking is in it. Second, would you be comfortable if the coordinator read the tutor's feedback notes? Feedback that names criteria and asks questions passes that test. Feedback that contains replacement sentences does not.
bullets: Legitimate: teaching content, explaining criteria, marking against a mark scheme
Legitimate: questions, worked examples on other problems, written feedback on the student's draft
Not legitimate: supplied text, rewritten sections, a research question chosen for the student
Not legitimate: anything the student could not explain to their supervisor unaided

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges for a Diploma hour
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranked pages on this search publish no price at all, and two of the others quote in US dollars. So here are the AED bands the market actually publishes, each attributed to whoever published it and read in October 2026. These are market rates, not an IB Gram price list. Our own position is that a trial lesson comes first and a figure follows the consultation, because what a Diploma family needs varies from one subject in DP1 to core supervision plus two Higher Levels in the final term.

The spread is wide and it is not random. The bottom of the range buys a university student who recently did the subject, which can work at Standard Level and rarely holds at Higher Level. The middle buys a qualified subject teacher. The top buys scarcity: a Higher Level Chemistry or Physics specialist who can teach the investigation as well as the papers. Monthly packages seen in this market run from around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions to AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits at an address.

What to do with these numbers is compare like with like. Ask what the hour contains: is the internal assessment feedback inside the rate or billed separately, who marks the practice papers, what happens to a cancelled session, and is the quote per hour or per 45-minute period. Two quotes AED 150 apart often describe different products, and the cheaper one sometimes turns out to cost more per point by the end of DP2.

sections.heading: An hour over live video against an hour at a UAE address
paragraphs: The honest question behind most searches on this topic is whether a tutor in the room is better. Here is the straight answer for a Diploma family in this country. A tutor who travels to a UAE address charges for the travel, needs a minimum session length to make the journey worth it, and can only be someone who happens to live within a reasonable drive. In a country where Higher Level Chemistry and Physics specialists cluster around a handful of school belts, that last constraint decides the quality of the teaching more than anything else on the invoice.

IB Gram delivers Diploma tuition in the UAE as one-to-one lessons over live video. There is no visiting-tutor service in any emirate; home visits are something we offer only in India. The reason is the one above: a family in Fujairah, Ras Al Khaimah or Al Ain gets a Higher Level specialist in the subject they actually need, rather than the best available person within a 25-minute drive. A shared whiteboard also suits Diploma work unusually well, because the session leaves behind a written record of the working, which a kitchen-table session does not.

What live video does not do well is worth saying too. Practical work belongs in the school laboratory, and a tutor can teach the investigation design and the data analysis but not run the experiment. A student who will not sit still for a screen needs a different plan. And a very young learner is a different proposition entirely from a seventeen-year-old with a mock paper in front of them. For Diploma students, the format is a good fit; for everyone, it should be tested in a trial lesson before money changes hands.

sections.heading: The equivalency file a Diploma leaver opens, and the number we will not print
paragraphs: A Diploma earned in the Emirates does not automatically carry a UAE recognition stamp. For applications to local universities and for several employment routes, the Ministry of Education issues an equivalency certificate for a secondary school certificate obtained under an international curriculum. The process is run by the Ministry and the emirate attestation channels, not by a school and certainly not by a tutoring company, and nobody should be charging you to perform it.

For the British track the requirements are published and specific. A student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One provider ranking on these searches states that UAE candidates need six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong, and that error has been copied around this market for a while. For the American track, English proficiency can be shown with 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics needs at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

For the IB Diploma itself we will not publish a points threshold, because we have not read one on an official Ministry page. That is an unsatisfying answer and it is the correct one: a wrong number here costs a family an application cycle. Check the requirement on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation channel, keep the IGCSE certificates from Year 11 because they sit in the same file, and open the file around results rather than after the first university deadline has passed.

process.title: Tell us the school and the authority above it
process.description: The first thing we ask is which school and which emirate, because that tells us the licensing authority, the mandatory subject load, the option-block style and the internal deadline culture. A Diploma student at a Sharjah-regulated school and one at a KHDA school in Al Barsha are planning around different weeks.

process.title: Send the subject combination, the levels and the session
process.description: Six subjects, which three or four are Higher Level, whether your child is a full Diploma or course candidate, and which examination session they are entered for. We also ask for the school's internal deadline list for internal assessments and the Extended Essay, because that calendar decides the order of work.

process.title: One diagnostic piece of work
process.description: A recent marked paper or a current draft, whichever matters more. We read it against the published criteria and come back with what is costing marks: content gaps, command-term misreading, criterion coverage or timing. This is also where we say honestly if tuition is not the right purchase yet.

process.title: A trial lesson at no charge, then a plan
process.description: One free trial lesson with the proposed tutor, with no payment taken and no card details needed to book it. If the match is wrong you say so and we try again or step back. If it works, you get a written plan naming subjects, session count per week, and what the first half-term is meant to change.

process.title: Weekly sessions with a written record
process.description: Lessons run over live video at a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot, with a short written note after each one: what was covered, what to practise, what is due at school next. The slot moves for the examination block, Ramadan timings and the school's mock window rather than being billed through them.

process.title: Reviewed against the school's own reports
process.description: Every half-term we compare what the school reports with what the sessions show. If the gap is closing, hours come down. If a subject has stabilised and the core has not, hours move. Tuition that never reduces is tuition nobody is measuring.

whyPoints.title: The school system is explained, not assumed
whyPoints.description: This page names which authority licenses your child's school, what that authority approves, how the mandatory UAE subjects sit in a Diploma week, and where a family can push. No competing page on this search names ADEK at all, and two mention the Dubai authority only inside a lead-capture widget.

whyPoints.title: Criteria and mark allocations in writing
whyPoints.description: Criterion letters, mark totals and word limits for the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge components, the mathematics exploration, the science investigation and the history investigation, with a clear instruction to verify them against the current subject guide. These are what internal assessment marks are actually decided by.

whyPoints.title: AED figures with a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Market rates are published here in the currency UAE families transact in, attributed to whoever published them and dated October 2026. Where we do not have a sourced number, including any IB points figure for Ministry equivalency, the page says so instead of inventing one.

whyPoints.title: A stated position on academic honesty
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions, marks and gives feedback on work the student produced. Nothing is supplied, rewritten or finished on the student's behalf, and we say so in detail because at least one provider ranking on these searches sells finished internal assessments.

whyPoints.title: Specialists reachable from any emirate
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, so a Fujairah or Ras Al Khaimah family can work with a Higher Level specialist in the subject they need rather than whoever lives nearby. Where no specialist is free for a combination, we say that rather than substituting a generalist.

whyPoints.title: Hours planned to come down
whyPoints.description: Plans are written with an end in view: a diagnostic first, a named target for the half-term, then a review against the school's own report. Diploma tuition that runs at the same intensity from DP1 to the final paper is usually a billing arrangement rather than a plan.

faqs.question: How many subjects does the Diploma require, and how many have to be at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Six subjects: one from each of the first five groups and a sixth from the arts or a second subject from groups one to four. Three of the six run at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, and some schools allow a fourth Higher Level where the timetable permits it. Each subject is graded 1 to 7, giving 42 points, with up to three more from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together. Your child's coordinator confirms the exact combination registered, which matters because what is registered, not what is attended, is what gets graded.

faqs.question: Where do the three extra Diploma points come from, and can tuition help earn them?
faqs.answer: They come from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, which are considered together on a published matrix rather than scored separately. Strong performance in both can add up to three points; weak performance in both can fail the Diploma outright regardless of subject grades. Tuition helps by teaching what the criteria reward, narrowing a research question that is too broad, and giving criterion-by-criterion feedback on drafts the student has written. It cannot supply text or choose the question, and both components are supervised in school with recorded sessions, so the work has to be genuinely the student's.

faqs.question: What is creativity, activity, service, and does my child need tutoring for it?
faqs.answer: It is the third part of the Diploma core, running across both years in three strands, and it carries no points. It is signed off by the school's coordinator rather than marked, and an incomplete record can cost the Diploma even where the points total is comfortable. No, it does not need tutoring, and anyone offering to manage it for a fee is selling something your child is supposed to do themselves. The practical risk in UAE schools is the reflective record rather than the activities: students do plenty and document almost none of it until the deadline is close.

faqs.question: Two of my child's Diploma choices sit in the same option block. What can be done?
faqs.answer: Nothing a tutor can fix, so deal with it inside the school first. Option blocks are a timetabling structure: one subject per column, and two subjects in the same column cannot both be taken. Ask the coordinator whether the block can be rebuilt, whether the subject runs in another column in alternate years, and whether the school will support the subject outside the timetable. If the answer closes a university route, the realistic options are a different subject at the same level, the same subject at a lower level, or covering the content separately while understanding what that does and does not change on the transcript.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a full Diploma candidate and a course candidate?
faqs.answer: A full Diploma candidate takes six subjects across the groups plus the core and receives a points total out of 45. A course candidate takes individual Diploma subjects and receives a certificate for each, with no points total and no requirement to cover all six groups. UAE schools use the course route for mid-programme arrivals and for students whose combination will not fit the blocks. It changes tutoring priorities completely: there is no points total to protect, so hours go to the specific subject grades universities will read rather than to balancing a weak sixth subject.

faqs.question: Which failing conditions can cost the Diploma even when the points total looks safe?
faqs.answer: The points total is necessary but not sufficient. The published conditions cover matters such as an incomplete creativity, activity and service record, a grade 1 in any subject, repeated low grades at Higher Level, and an E in Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay. A student can therefore clear the points bar and still not be awarded the Diploma. Ask your child's coordinator for the current list in writing early in DP2, because every one of those conditions is visible months in advance and most are fixable while there is still time.

faqs.question: Who decides the predicted grades that go on a university application?
faqs.answer: Your child's subject teachers, through the school, not a tutor and not the IB. Predicted grades are the school's professional judgement based on the work it has seen, and they are submitted with the application while the real examinations are still months away. A tutor's useful contribution is indirect: better work in front of the teacher before predictions are set. Anyone who implies they can influence a prediction is describing something they do not control. If a prediction looks wrong, that conversation belongs with the subject teacher and the coordinator, in that order.

faqs.question: Which group does Arabic sit in for the Diploma, and what does that choice change?
faqs.answer: Arabic A can serve as a group one language for an Arab student, and Arabic B is a group two second-language course. The choice changes the assessment entirely, from literary analysis in one case to oral and written language work in the other. Separately from the Diploma, Dubai private schools must run Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. So the two questions parents tend to merge, which Diploma language group and which school Arabic stream, are genuinely different questions with different answers.

faqs.question: Can my child take a Standard Level subject a year early as an anticipated subject?
faqs.answer: Some schools allow one Standard Level subject to be completed and examined at the end of DP1, which lightens the final year. Whether it is available depends on the school rather than the student, so ask the coordinator before assuming it. The trade-off is real: an anticipated subject moves an examination into a year that already carries the Extended Essay and the first internal assessments. For a student who is comfortable in that subject it can work well. For a student already stretched, it concentrates pressure in the wrong year.

faqs.question: May a tutor be present for the Individual Oral or the Theory of Knowledge exhibition?
faqs.answer: No. Those are assessed events run by the school, and an outside adult has no place in them. What a tutor can legitimately do beforehand is teach the criteria, run practice questions on different material, and give feedback on the student's own preparation notes. For the oral in particular, rehearsing with unseen extracts is useful and rehearsing a script is counter-productive, because the marks follow the quality of the live analysis. The school sets the conditions for both components and the coordinator is the person to ask about anything procedural.

faqs.question: What does my child declare when coursework is submitted, and where does a paid tutor stand?
faqs.answer: Assessed work is submitted with an authenticity declaration, and the school's supervisor signs to confirm it is the student's own. Extended Essay supervision sessions are recorded, and coordinators ask about outside assistance directly. A tutor is permitted in that picture as a teacher: content, criteria, questions, marked practice and written feedback on the student's draft. A tutor is not permitted to supply text, rewrite sections or make the judgements. The test a parent can apply at home is simple: can your child explain every sentence they submitted, and why it is there?

faqs.question: How does a Diploma lesson work over live video when the working is on paper?
faqs.answer: A shared whiteboard carries the working, and both people write on it. Your child photographs a handwritten attempt before the session so the tutor can read it in advance, or works live on the board while talking through the steps. Past papers are worked under timed conditions and marked against the mark scheme afterwards. The session leaves a written record of the board, which a kitchen-table lesson does not. What live video cannot do is run a laboratory experiment; the practical belongs at school, while the design and the data analysis are taught online.

faqs.question: Which published AED figures can we check a Diploma tuition quote against?
faqs.answer: The ones on this page, each attributed to whoever published it and read in October 2026. Budget online tuition is advertised from AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik and from AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya; Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200; TutorChase quotes AED 270; Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table runs from AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists; BartyED publishes AED 650. Those are other companies' figures, not ours. Use them to judge whether a quote is inside the market, then ask what the hour actually contains before comparing two numbers.

faqs.question: Our school is being inspected during the first Diploma year. Does that affect my child?
faqs.answer: Usually less than the staffroom suggests, but two things are worth knowing. Inspection weeks compress teaching time and can push internal deadlines, so check whether any internal assessment dates have moved. And the published report that follows is the single most useful document you will read about the school, because it separates attainment from progress and comments on teaching by phase. Read it from the authority that licenses your school rather than from a tutoring site, and read the subject detail rather than only the headline band.

faqs.question: Can a Diploma student add a fourth Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: The Diploma allows four Higher Levels where the school's timetable supports it, and it is not automatically a good idea. Each Higher Level carries 240 published guided teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, so a fourth one adds the equivalent of a whole extra subject's teaching alongside the core and, in Dubai, the mandatory UAE subjects. The students who manage it are usually strong, well organised and not relying on tuition to hold three other subjects up. Ask the coordinator what the school's experience of it has been with recent cohorts.

faqs.question: The shortened Ramadan timetable lands on top of the DP2 mocks. How should the plan change?
faqs.answer: Sequence it rather than fight it. School days shorten, energy shifts later, and the mock window often sits close by. We move sessions to post-Iftar slots where that suits the household, reduce session length and raise frequency so concentration holds, and keep the heaviest timed-paper work for after Eid. What should not slip into that period is coursework with a school deadline immediately after the break, so the realistic plan brings internal assessment drafts forward by a fortnight and leaves Ramadan for consolidation and short, focused paper practice.

faqs.question: Which authority attests a Diploma transcript, and what should we not take on trust?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation channels handle equivalency and attestation for international secondary certificates. No school and no tutoring company performs it, and nobody should charge you to arrange it. What not to take on trust is any points figure for the IB Diploma published on a commercial site, including this one: we have not read an official Ministry threshold, so we do not print a number. The British-track requirements are published and specific, and one competing page on these searches states the subject count wrongly. Verify on moe.gov.ae.

ib-dp-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the school's own paperwork, then one trial lesson
ib-dp-tutor.closingBody: Before paying anyone, read two documents: your school's latest inspection report from the authority that licenses it, and the internal deadline list for your child's internal assessments and Extended Essay. Those two tell you more about whether tuition will help than any tutoring website can. Then send us the school, the emirate, the six subjects with their levels and the examination session, plus one recent marked paper or current draft. We read it against the published criteria, propose a tutor, and run one trial lesson at no charge with no card details taken. If the match is wrong, say so and nothing is owed. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time.

Where a profile says nothing about marking experience, that is the honest answer rather than an omission.

intro.heading: What a parent is really asking for when they search for an IB examiner tutor
paragraphs: A search for an IB examiner tutor in the UAE is a search for insight into the marking, not for a different syllabus. The syllabus is public. The subject guides are public. What is not public, and what families sense they are missing, is the procedure that turns a piece of work into a number: who reads it, what they are instructed to reward, when that reading happens, and how a mark can still move after it leaves the classroom. That procedure has dates attached to it, and those dates are the most useful thing a UAE family can plan around.

IB Gram does not call a tutor an IB examiner unless the tutor has produced evidence of the appointment and it is current. Examiner appointments are made session by session, they carry confidentiality obligations, and they bring no advance sight of papers, mark schemes or boundaries. A provider implying otherwise is either confused about how IB papers are marked or selling something it cannot deliver. What marking experience genuinely transfers is literacy in the instruction sheet: how a command term narrows an answer, why a markband rewards one sentence and ignores another, and how long a competent response actually needs to be.

That literacy only pays if it arrives in time. An exploration cannot be rescued the week it is due. A Higher Level choice cannot be unwound after the entry deadline has passed. A mock paper is a diagnosis, not a verdict, but only if someone reads it against the criteria within a fortnight of it coming back. So this page is organised as a calendar, counted backwards from the week the marking begins, with the dates each board actually publishes set beside the ones only your school can give you.

Delivery is the part we are blunt about. Tuition for UAE families is one-to-one online IB tuition over live video. IB Gram does not send anyone to a villa, an apartment or a compound anywhere in the Emirates; home visits are a service offered only in India. The reason is not cost. A family in Al Ain or Khor Fakkan who insists on someone in the room is choosing from the adults who happen to live within a twenty-minute drive. The same family online is choosing from specialists who have taught that exact Higher Level paper for years, and a shared screen is where marked work is actually read line by line.

The rest of the page covers the marking chain, the calendar counted backwards, the dates Cambridge and Pearson have published, what command terms instruct a marker to look for, how IB internal assessment moderation works, what the UAE market charges at each tier and who published those figures, where the academic-honesty line sits, and what the Ministry of Education equivalency file asks for once the papers are over. Figures are attributed. Dates we cannot source are left blank rather than guessed.

ib-examiner-tutor.programmesIntro: The four IB programmes differ most in who does the marking. One ends in externally marked papers, one in a reflective project, one in internally assessed units sampled by the IB, and one in an exhibition nobody outside the school ever grades. That difference decides what tutoring can and cannot change.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Most of the grade comes from papers marked externally by IB examiners who never meet the candidate. The rest comes from internal assessment marked by the class teacher and moderated by the IB on a sample. The two routes fail differently: a paper is lost to technique and timing, an internal assessment is lost to a research question that was never going to work.
programmes.countryNote: The May session is the one UAE schools sit, and it collides with Ramadan in some years and with Eid in others. Diploma families here also carry Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies on the same timetable, because an emirate regulator requires them regardless of the licensed curriculum. Plan the Diploma year as a UAE year, not a generic one.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses taken alongside a career-related study, a reflective project, a personal and professional skills course, service learning and a language development portfolio. The Diploma courses inside it are marked exactly as Diploma courses are, with the same papers and the same external examiners. The reflective project is assessed against its own published criteria and moderated. Students often misread the programme as lighter; the marked components are not.
programmes.countryNote: Career-related provision in the UAE is thinner than Diploma provision, and a family may be the only one in a school taking a particular pairing. That makes a specialist outside the building more useful than a generalist inside it, and it is the usual reason a Career-related student here ends up online.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked by the school on an eight-point scale, with optional externally marked eAssessments at the end of Year 11. The criteria language carries straight into the Diploma: a student who has been taught to read criterion wording in the Middle Years Programme arrives in Year 12 already fluent in the thing most Diploma students learn late and expensively.
programmes.countryNote: Many UAE schools run the Middle Years Programme and then switch to Cambridge or Pearson qualifications at 16, so a student can leave criterion-based marking for mark schemes within a single summer. That switch is the commonest cause of a sharp, temporary grade drop in Year 11 here.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry across six themes, ending in the Exhibition. There is no external marking at all: no examiner reads a Primary Years student's work, and no mark leaves the school. Assessment is the teacher's judgement, recorded against learning outcomes the school itself sets within the IB framework. Support at this stage is about reading, number fluency and the habit of explaining a method out loud.
programmes.countryNote: A Primary Years cohort in Dubai or Abu Dhabi still sits Arabic and Islamic Education under the emirate regulator's rules, taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils. For most UAE families, the Exhibition year is the first time a child is asked to defend an argument in front of adults.

ib-examiner-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma courses UAE families most often ask about, described by where the marks actually go missing rather than by syllabus headings. Availability varies by week; if nobody is free at the level you need, we say so rather than substituting a generalist.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level adds a third paper and a markedly harder proof and calculus load. Marks go missing in method lines that are never written down, in unjustified steps a marker cannot award, and in an exploration whose mathematics is decorative rather than doing any work. Command-term discipline matters here more than speed.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology-led, modelling-led, and routinely underestimated. Candidates lose marks by reporting a calculator output without the model it came from, by rounding before the final step, and by writing conclusions that the data does not support. The exploration here rewards a real data set with real problems in it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The written papers punish loose definitions and reward units, directions and clearly labelled diagrams. Uncertainty treatment is where internal assessment marks drain away: a well-run experiment with no serious evaluation of its limitations sits in the middle band however neat the graph looks.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium carry most of the Higher Level difficulty. Markers award correctly balanced equations, state symbols and explicit reasoning chains; they cannot award an answer that is right in the student's head. The investigation needs a variable that can actually be controlled in a school laboratory.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume hides the real problem, which is command-term reading. A question asking students to outline is answered with an essay; one asking them to explain is answered with a description. The investigation rewards a biological question with enough replicates to say anything statistically.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are marks, and unlabelled axes throw them away. Higher Level adds quantitative demands that reward working shown line by line. The internal assessment commentaries are lost on article choice more often than on analysis: an article with no identifiable policy intervention cannot carry the criteria.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools are taught, application is marked. Candidates who name a framework without placing it inside the stimulus material score in the lower bands. The Higher Level research project needs a real organisation, primary access and a question narrow enough to answer in the word limit.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper responses reward a controlled line of argument over coverage. Markers follow a thesis; they cannot follow a tour of every device in the extract. Higher Level adds an essay whose marks sit in sustained comparison rather than in summary.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions and tracing tables are marked precisely, and improvised notation loses marks that the logic had already earned. The internal assessment needs a client who exists and a success criterion that can be tested, not a project the student found interesting in September.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies are evidence, not content to be recited. Markbands reward a research study used to support a specific claim about behaviour, with its methodological limitations named. Essays lose marks to unargued breadth, and the experimental study loses them to a design that cannot be replicated from the write-up.

ib-examiner-tutor.regionsTitle: Where UAE candidates sit, and when a session can realistically start
ib-examiner-tutor.regionsIntro: Your address decides which authority holds your child's school file, how far the examination centre is, and what time an evening session can honestly begin. None of that changes the marking, but all of it changes the plan. Session times below are the ones families in each emirate usually settle on.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA licenses the schools here and Dubai holds the country's largest IB cohort. For families in Jumeirah, Arabian Ranches or Dubai Hills, a school finish plus the drive home usually means 6pm or 7pm Gulf Standard Time is the first slot anyone will actually attend.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK holds the school file in Abu Dhabi, and it is the regulator no competitor page in this market bothers to name. Island and Khalifa City families often sit a long bus route, so sessions on the island commonly start after 6.30pm and run to 8pm.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, with far fewer IB places than the island. A Higher Level specialist is rarely within driving distance of Zakher or Al Jimi, which is precisely the case where a screen beats a car and a wider tutor pool beats a shorter commute.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education here and approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods, not just inspection outcomes. Many Sharjah families commute into Dubai for school, so the usable evening window often opens after 7pm.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Ajman's private schools sit under the federal Ministry of Education. Families here frequently drive to Sharjah or Dubai for an IB place, and the return leg decides whether a weekday session is realistic at all or whether weekends work better.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also Ministry of Education territory, and the emirate with the thinnest local IB provision. Weekend mornings tend to hold better than weekday evenings once a Sharjah or Dubai school run is already in the diary twice a day.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah. Distance from the Dubai school cluster makes local specialist cover unreliable, and the examination centre itself can be a long drive, which matters on the morning of a paper.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Fujairah's schools fall under the Ministry of Education, with the east coast and Khor Fakkan adding travel to everything. Live video removes the mountain road from the arithmetic, which is the single largest saving an east-coast family makes.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai's IB schools are concentrated along the Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail spine, which is why a 5pm session is a different proposition in Emirates Hills than in Deira. Students we support attend schools across this cluster, and the subject gaps we are asked to fill most often are Higher Level Chemistry, Physics and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches.

ADEK territory, with the Diploma concentrated on the island and in the newer suburban schools. Students we support here travel further to school than their Dubai counterparts, so evening sessions start later and weekend blocks before mocks are more common than weekday ones.

Provision thins quickly north of Dubai, and families mix IB and British tracks across the same household. Students we support in this cluster sit under three different authorities depending on which emirate the school is licensed in, which changes the inspection report but not the awarding body.

sections.heading: What an IB examiner tutor means, and the four things it cannot mean
paragraphs: An IB examiner is a subject teacher appointed by the IB to mark a specific component in a specific session. Appointments are made session by session. Assistant examiners mark scripts against a mark scheme they are trained on; team leaders check a sample of their examiners' marking for standard; moderators look at samples of internally assessed work from schools and adjust where a school has been generous or severe. All of them sign confidentiality undertakings before they see anything.

So an IB examiner tutor is a tutor who has done that work and can explain what it taught them. That explanation is genuinely valuable. Someone who has marked four hundred responses to the same question knows which phrasing the markband rewards, how long a full answer runs, and which plausible-sounding answer earns nothing. That knowledge is transferable and it is hard to acquire any other way.

Four things the badge cannot mean. It cannot mean advance sight of a paper, because papers are secure material and examiners receive them with the rest of the world. It cannot mean knowledge of the boundaries, because boundaries are set after the marking. It cannot mean influence over who marks your child. And it cannot be assumed to be current: an appointment held for one session in 2019 is a line on a curriculum vitae, not a live role. Ask which component, which level and which session, and ask what evidence exists. A provider that will not answer those three questions has told you what you needed to know.
bullets: Ask: which component, which level, which session, and how recently
Secure material reaches examiners on the same schedule as everyone else
Moderators see sampled school work, not an individual child's file
A past appointment is experience, not a current credential

sections.heading: How a piece of your child's work becomes a grade
paragraphs: Two different machines run in parallel through the Diploma, and families routinely confuse them. One is internal: the class teacher awards a mark against published criteria, the school submits a sample to the IB, and an IB moderator decides whether the school's marking matched the standard. If it did not, an adjustment is applied to the whole cohort rather than to one student. The other is external: the student's work goes to an examiner who has no connection to the school, marks it against a mark scheme, and never speaks to anyone involved.

This matters because the two machines respond to different kinds of help. Internal assessment is won early, in the choice of question, the design of the method and the quality of the data. Once the work is submitted to the school, nothing a tutor does can change the mark; the only remaining variable is whether the school's marking was accurate, and that is between the school and the moderator. External components are won late, in technique, timing and command-term reading, which is exactly what the final twelve weeks are for.

The table below sets out who touches what. Read it as a map of where effort pays. An hour spent interrogating a research question in the first term of the second year is worth several hours spent polishing prose a fortnight before the school's deadline, because by then the question has already decided the ceiling. The reverse holds for the papers: there is very little point rehearsing paper technique in the first term of the first year, when the student has met a third of the content and none of the pressure. Matching the kind of help to the kind of component is most of what a plan is for.

sections.heading: The Diploma years, counted backwards from the week marking begins
paragraphs: Most tutoring is bought in the wrong month. A family that starts in February of the final year is buying technique work, which is real but bounded; a family that starts in the first term of the first year is buying the decisions that set the ceiling. Neither is wrong, but they cost differently and they deliver differently, and nobody in this market publishes the sequence that would let a parent choose deliberately.

So here it is, counted backwards from the week examiners start reading. The anchor is deliberately not a calendar date, because the IB publishes its session dates through schools and we do not restate a date we cannot source. Your child's coordinator can give you the exact window in writing, and should. What does not change from year to year is the order of the milestones and the gap between them.

Two of these deadlines are effectively irreversible. Final exam entries fix subject, level and session; after that date a Higher Level that is not holding becomes a Higher Level your child sits. And the school's internal submission deadline for assessed work ends a tutor's involvement in that component completely. Everything else in the list can be adjusted, which is a useful thing to know in January when a mock result looks frightening.

The milestones families most often miss are the two in the middle of the first year, because nothing visible happens on either date. Subject selection and the first internal assessment window produce no grade and no report, so they generate no alarm, and yet they constrain the whole of the second year. The milestone families over-react to is the mock, which produces a number and therefore produces panic. Reading the list in order makes it obvious which of the two patterns a household is in, and that is usually enough to redirect the next three months of spending.

sections.heading: The dates you can diary today, and the ones that come from your coordinator
paragraphs: Cambridge and Pearson publish their series dates openly, and a UAE family can put them in a calendar this afternoon. The IB publishes its session dates to schools, and this page will not restate an IB exam or results date, because the only authority for one is the IB itself or your child's coordinator. That distinction is worth more than a confident guess: a wrong date in a revision plan is worse than a blank one.

Cambridge adds a complication nobody warns parents about. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the timetable. Cambridge's own guidance tells centres it is essential to use the correct version and says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. If you have printed a timetable from the internet rather than taken one from your child's exams officer, you may be holding the wrong document.

The March series is the clearest illustration of why entry deadlines sit so far ahead of the papers. For Cambridge's March 2027 series the exam period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, but final entries were due on 27 November 2026 and forecast grades on 27 February 2027. The entry window closes more than two months before the first paper. Pearson, similarly, publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series and revises them, which is why every plan should link the live official timetable rather than a copy.

sections.heading: IB command terms: the instruction sheet a marker is working from
paragraphs: Every IB question opens with a command term, and the command term is not decoration. It tells the examiner what kind of response earns credit, which means it also tells the student what kind of response is a waste of ink. A question asking a candidate to state is asking for a name or a value and nothing else; a paragraph of explanation attached to it earns no extra mark and costs minutes that the evaluate question at the end of the paper needed.

This is the single most teachable thing an examiner-informed tutor brings, and it is almost absent from the pages competing for this search. It is also measurable. Give a student ten past-paper questions, have them underline the command term before writing anything, and the pattern of lost marks usually resolves into two or three repeated misreadings rather than a content gap. Those misreadings are fixable in weeks.

The table lists the terms that recur across Diploma subjects with the instruction each carries. The definitions are the IB's own, published in the subject guides; the third and fourth columns are what the pattern of lost marks actually looks like in practice. Students should learn these the way they learn vocabulary, because in a timed paper there is no time to work out what is being asked.

One habit is worth building above all the others. Before writing anything, the student underlines the command term and writes the number of marks beside it, then decides how many distinct points the answer needs. That takes ten seconds and it prevents the two commonest failures at once: a paragraph where a line was wanted, and a line where a reasoning chain was wanted. Tutors here are asked to insist on it from the first session, including in the first Diploma year, when it is still cheap to make it automatic.

sections.heading: Moderation and grade boundaries: the two things nobody can tell you in advance
paragraphs: IB internal assessment moderation is widely misunderstood by families and occasionally by schools. The school marks its own cohort against the criteria, submits a sample to the IB, and a moderator reads that sample to judge whether the school applied the standard correctly. Where the school has been generous, marks come down; where it has been severe, marks go up. The adjustment is applied at cohort level, so a single student's mark can move because of how their classmates' work was marked, not because of anything in their own.

The practical consequence is counterintuitive. A high teacher-awarded mark is not a result, it is a prediction, and a parent who treats it as banked may get an unpleasant surprise in July. The only defence is work that is strong on its own terms: a research question with a real variable in it, data that was genuinely collected, and an evaluation that names the method's limitations honestly. Moderators are reading for whether the criteria were met, and work that plainly meets them is hard to adjust downwards.

Grade boundaries are the second thing nobody can promise. They are set after marking is complete, by senior examiners reading the evidence of how the cohort performed on that particular paper, which is why they move between sessions. Any tutor who offers to tell you what a 7 will require next summer is describing last year's boundary or inventing one. The honest version is a range from recent sessions, with the warning that it is history rather than a target, and a plan built on being clear of the line rather than near it.
bullets: A teacher-awarded internal mark is provisional until moderation is complete
Adjustments apply across a cohort, not to an individual student's file

sections.heading: What an examiner-badged tutor costs in the UAE market
paragraphs: Examiner experience is the single largest premium in this market, and most pages competing for this search publish no number at all. Three of the six main competitors quote no price whatsoever, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. The table below is the market, in AED, with each figure attributed to whoever published it. It is not an IB Gram price list.

Read it as five tiers with five different things being sold. At the bottom you are buying company and patience, which drills practice questions adequately and reads a markband poorly. In the middle you are buying someone who has taught the course and marked class work against the criteria, which covers most Standard Level needs. At the top you are buying scarcity plus a claim, and the claim is the part worth interrogating before you pay the difference.

For context, Dubai's school fees were frozen for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package, announced in May 2026, so the tutoring line is the one in a UAE family's education budget that is still moving. IB Gram's own answer to the pricing question is a free trial lesson of 45 minutes, one per family and with no card details taken, followed by a written quote for the hours actually proposed. Rates depend on subject, level and tutor, and quoting a single number for all of them would be dishonest.

sections.heading: Why this is taught online, and what that does to an exam-year plan
paragraphs: IB Gram delivers tuition to UAE families as one-to-one online IB tuition over live video. There is no in-home service anywhere in the Emirates; that option exists only in India. The honest reason is the shape of the specialist market. There are a limited number of adults in this country who have taught Higher Level Chemistry to the current guide and marked work against its criteria, and the chance that one of them lives twenty minutes from a particular villa in Al Ain or Ajman is small.

The format also suits what examiner-informed teaching actually involves. Most of the value is in reading a marked script together: the student's own paper on screen, the criteria beside it, the tutor annotating as the reasoning is traced. That works better shared on a screen than passed across a kitchen table, and it leaves a recorded artefact the student can revisit the night before a paper. The same session can pull up a past-paper question and a markband in seconds.

In an exam year, the scheduling argument becomes the decisive one. A visiting tutor consumes an evening at both ends, which is why so many of them insist on a two-hour minimum: the travel has to be worth someone's time. An online slot can be 45 minutes on a Tuesday and 90 on a Saturday, moved after Iftar during Ramadan, and held while a family is travelling. During the final twelve weeks, that flexibility is what keeps a plan alive.

sections.heading: Academic honesty gets stricter, not looser, when a tutor has marked papers
paragraphs: Somewhere in this search results page is a provider selling finished internal assessments. One of them publishes a price for them. That is not tutoring; it is malpractice under the IB's academic-honesty rules, and the consequences land on the student, not the seller. A candidate found to have submitted work that is not their own can lose the diploma. No tutor who has actually moderated coursework would go anywhere near it, because they have seen what detection looks like from the other side of the desk.

The permitted line is clear and we will put it in writing. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain what a criterion is asking for, discuss a research question the student has proposed, rehearse a method, and comment on a draft the student has produced. A tutor may not supply sentences for an internal assessment, rewrite a paragraph of an Extended Essay, hand back a finished exploration, or sit beside a student and dictate. Where the boundary is reached, the session stops and we say so.

There is a disclosure side too. Your child's coordinator may ask whether outside help was used, and the right answer is the true one: tuition in the subject, with feedback on the student's own work. Schools are untroubled by that. What troubles them is work whose register changes halfway down a page. Keeping drafts, dated, is the student's own best protection, and it costs nothing. If a provider ever suggests that the disclosure question has a clever answer, treat that as the end of the conversation rather than as advice.
bullets: Permitted: subject teaching, criteria explanation, method rehearsal, feedback on the student's own draft

sections.heading: Results day, enquiry upon results, and the November decision
paragraphs: Results arrive through the school first and then to candidates, and the hours after that are busier than most families expect. Three decisions can be sitting on the table at once: whether to ask for a grade to be looked at again, whether to enter the November session, and whether a university offer still stands. Each has its own deadline, and the first two are short.

An enquiry upon results is the formal route for asking the IB to review a mark, and it is submitted by the school rather than by a parent. There are different categories of enquiry, there is a fee, and there is a window that closes quickly after results are released. We do not publish the date, because the IB sets it per session. What we tell families to do is ask the coordinator for the exact deadline in writing before results day, so the decision is made on evidence rather than in a rush.

The November session is a real option rather than a consolation. It gives a candidate roughly a term to rebuild one or two subjects while the rest of the diploma stands, and an examiner-informed read of the original script is the most useful input to that decision. Before committing, check what the university offer actually requires and whether it will hold for a January result, because the answer varies by institution and by country. Check too which components are retaken and which carry forward, since that decides whether the term's work is a whole course or two papers.
bullets: An enquiry upon results is submitted by the school, not by the family
Ask the coordinator in writing for the session's enquiry deadline before results day
