sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and the figure we will not publish
paragraphs: A UAE-recognised secondary certificate is a separate piece of paperwork from an IB diploma or a set of IGCSEs, and it is what a UAE university or a federal employer asks to see. The Ministry of Education equivalency process converts a foreign qualification into that recognition. It is not something a tutoring company performs, guarantees or speeds up, and no amount of tuition is required for it.

The British-track requirements are published and specific. A student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five subjects. One page currently ranking in this market tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects; the published figure is five, and getting that right matters more than any marketing line on the page.

For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with at least 450 in SAT Math. For the IB diploma there is a points threshold, and this page will not print a number for it, because we have not read one on the ministry's own site. Open the file in the final year, ask the school registrar which documents they issue and which you must attest yourself, and verify the current requirement at the official channel rather than from a tutoring page.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in the same marking term
paragraphs: A UAE Diploma student is not only a Diploma student. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and the federal position behind that is that private schools must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies whatever else they offer. These lessons sit on the same timetable as Higher Level Physics, in the same week as an internal assessment deadline.

The rules around them are more specific than most parents realise. Schools must run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and schools are advised that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes.

For tutoring, two constraints follow. Material is tightly controlled: using different or additional content for these subjects without prior permission from the ministry is prohibited, so a tutor works with the school's own scheme rather than importing a syllabus. And teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education need the appropriate approval from the regulator to teach those subjects, which is a credential worth asking about specifically. The planning point is simpler: when a Diploma family builds a revision block, these subjects are already in the week, and pretending otherwise is how a plan collapses in March.

process.title: Tell us the component, not just the subject
process.description: A message saying Chemistry Higher Level, Paper 2 technique, mocks in January is worth three messages saying help with science. Name the subject, the level, the board where it is not the IB, the session your child is sitting, and what the last marked piece of work came back as. That is enough to know whether a specialist is free.

process.title: Free 45-minute trial lesson
process.description: One per family, with no card details taken beforehand and no obligation afterwards. A specialist in that subject and level works through a recent piece of marked work with your child, over live video. You get a short written read on what the marks say, whether or not anything is booked after it.

process.title: A plan counted backwards
process.description: Before hours are agreed, we write down the dates that are already fixed: the school's internal deadlines, the mock window, the entry deadline and the session. The plan then works backwards from those rather than forwards from today, which is the difference between buying hours and buying a sequence.

process.title: Weekly sessions with session notes
process.description: A fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time with the same tutor, and a short note after each lesson saying what was marked, which command terms were misread and what the student is practising next. The notes are the record you use to judge whether the hours are working.

process.title: Review at the mock, and again at twelve weeks
process.description: Two scheduled points where the plan is reopened rather than continued by default: when mock papers come back, and twelve weeks before the first paper. Frequency, subject mix and session length all change at those reviews, and sometimes the honest recommendation is fewer hours in one subject and none in another.

whyPoints.title: Marking experience stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Examiner or moderator experience appears on a tutor profile only where it has been evidenced to us, with the component and the level named. Where a tutor has no marking history, the profile says nothing rather than reaching for a vaguer word. You can ask which session an appointment covered before the first paid lesson.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is the plan
whyPoints.description: Hours are planned backwards from entry deadlines, school submission dates, the mock window and the session itself. That is why this page is built as a calendar and not as a list of benefits. A plan that ignores the deadline it is working towards is a diary of lessons rather than a strategy.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed
whyPoints.description: Each AED rate on this page carries the name of whoever published it and the month we read it. Nothing here is presented as an IB Gram price except the free trial, and that comes with its conditions stated: 45 minutes, one per family, no card details. Statistics without a source do not appear.

whyPoints.title: A teaching service, in writing
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, explains criteria, rehearses methods and comments on the student's own draft. A tutor does not produce assessed work in any form, at any price, and will stop a session that drifts towards it. In a market where one provider sells finished internal assessments, that boundary is worth stating plainly.

whyPoints.title: Honest unavailability
whyPoints.description: Some subject and level combinations have no specialist free in a given week. When that happens we say so and give you a realistic date, rather than putting a generalist in the slot. A Higher Level paper taught by someone who has not taught it wastes the hours and the window at the same time.

faqs.question: What does it actually mean when a tutor is described as an IB examiner?
faqs.answer: It should mean the IB appointed that person to mark a specific component in a specific session. Appointments are made session by session and carry confidentiality obligations. Assistant examiners mark scripts, team leaders check their examiners' standard, and moderators sample internally assessed work from schools. Ask which component, which level and which session, and ask what evidences it. The badge does not mean advance sight of papers, knowledge of boundaries, or any influence over who marks your child. On this site, a tutor is only described as an examiner where that appointment has been evidenced to us.

faqs.question: Can a tutor with marking experience tell us what the grade boundaries will be?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone who offers to is either quoting history or inventing a number. Boundaries are set after marking is finished, by senior examiners looking at how candidates performed on that particular paper, which is why they move between sessions. A useful tutor will show you the range boundaries have occupied in recent sessions and explain that it is history rather than a target. The planning consequence is practical: build towards being comfortably inside a band rather than a mark above where last year's line happened to fall.

faqs.question: Does examiner experience give a tutor early sight of the exam papers?
faqs.answer: It does not. Examination papers are secure material and examiners receive them on the same schedule as everyone else, under confidentiality undertakings they sign before any appointment begins. Someone who hints otherwise is describing something that would be a serious breach rather than a service. What marking experience does give is familiarity with how a question type has been marked in the past, which is legitimate and genuinely useful. If a provider suggests access to unreleased material, that is a reason to walk away rather than to pay more.

faqs.question: Who moderates the mark my child's teacher awards for an internal assessment?
faqs.answer: The class teacher marks the work against the published criteria, the school submits a sample to the IB, and an IB moderator reads that sample to judge whether the school applied the standard correctly. The moderator is not reading your child's file specifically; they are checking a school's marking. Where a school has been generous, marks come down across the cohort, and where it has been severe they go up. That is why a high teacher-awarded mark is a prediction rather than a result until moderation is complete.

faqs.question: Can a moderated internal assessment mark go down as well as up?
faqs.answer: Yes. Moderation adjusts in both directions, and the adjustment is applied at cohort level rather than to an individual. A student can see their mark move because of how their classmates' work was marked. The only real defence is work that plainly meets the criteria on its own terms: a research question with a genuine variable in it, data actually collected, and an evaluation that names the method's limitations rather than praising the experiment. Work like that is difficult to adjust downwards, because a moderator can see the criteria being met.

faqs.question: Which deadline in the exam year is the last one a family can still influence?
faqs.answer: The final exam entry deadline. Once entries are submitted, subject, level and session are fixed, so a Higher Level that is not holding becomes a Higher Level your child sits. It typically falls six to eight months before the first paper, and your school submits it against the board's date. The other effectively irreversible point is your school's internal submission deadline for assessed work, after which a tutor can do nothing further on that component. Everything else in the year can be adjusted.

faqs.question: How far back from the first paper does a sensible plan start?
faqs.answer: It depends on what you want the money to buy. Starting in February of the final year buys technique and timing, which is real but bounded. Starting in the first Diploma year buys the decisions that set the ceiling: the maths route, the Higher Level pattern, and a research question that can survive a failed first attempt. Most families here start after the January mocks, and the useful version of that is a diagnosis within a fortnight of the papers coming back, followed by a twelve-week block planned by paper rather than by topic.

faqs.question: What does a command term such as evaluate instruct a marker to reward?
faqs.answer: Evaluate asks for an appraisal that weighs up strengths and limitations and reaches a judgement. A marker is looking for both sides and a supported conclusion, so an answer listing only strengths sits in the lower bands however accurate it is. State asks for a name or value with no explanation. Explain asks for reasons, with each link in the chain written down. Discuss asks for competing positions, then a weighing of them. Learning these the way vocabulary is learned is one of the cheapest grade improvements available, because in a timed paper there is no time to work out the instruction.

faqs.question: Why do two answers containing the same facts score differently?
faqs.answer: Because a mark scheme rewards a particular shape of response, not the presence of correct information. A reasoning chain with one link left implicit loses the mark for that link even when the student clearly understood it. A comparison written as two separate descriptions earns the description marks and misses the comparison ones. Marks also go to units, state symbols, labelled axes and shown working, all of which are easy to omit under time pressure. This is why reading a marked script line by line usually explains a grade better than re-reading the textbook.

faqs.question: What happens to my child's script between the exam and the grade?
faqs.answer: Written papers go to an examiner with no connection to the school, who marks against a mark scheme they have been trained and standardised on, while senior examiners check samples to keep the standard consistent. Internal assessment stays with the school's mark until a moderator has read a sample. Once marking is complete, senior examiners set the boundaries for that session from the evidence of how the cohort performed, and grades are awarded. Nothing a family does during that period changes anything, which is why the work has to be finished before it starts.

faqs.question: What does an examiner-badged tutor charge in the UAE, and is the premium worth it?
faqs.answer: The top of this market is published at AED 500 to 650 and above; BartyED lists AED 650. Below that, specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and qualified subject teachers online start around AED 150 to 300 by Unitors' published rates. All figures were read in October 2026. The premium is worth paying where the claim is evidenced and the need is genuinely Higher Level technique. For Standard Level content gaps, a qualified teacher at a third of the price usually does the same work.

faqs.question: Why is this delivered online rather than by someone sitting beside my child?
faqs.answer: Because the specialist pool is national and the driving radius is not. A limited number of adults in this country have taught Higher Level Chemistry to the current guide and marked work against its criteria, and the odds that one lives twenty minutes from a particular address in Al Ain or Ajman are poor. IB Gram does not offer in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Online also suits the work itself, since most of the value is in reading a marked script together on a shared screen.

faqs.question: Where is the honesty line when the tutor has marked that component before?
faqs.answer: Exactly where it is for any other tutor, and someone with marking experience usually guards it harder because they have seen detection from the other side. Permitted: teaching the content, explaining what a criterion asks for, discussing a question the student has proposed, rehearsing a method, and commenting on a draft the student has produced. Not permitted: supplying sentences for an internal assessment, rewriting a paragraph of an Extended Essay to completion, or handing back finished assessed work. Keep dated drafts, and answer your coordinator's question about outside help specifically and truthfully.

faqs.question: Which exam dates can we diary now, and which have to come from the school?
faqs.answer: Cambridge and Pearson publish theirs. Cambridge's March 2027 series runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due 27 November 2026 and forecast grades 27 February 2027; results reach Cambridge Direct on 13 May 2027. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. IB session and results dates come from your coordinator or the IB itself, and this page does not restate a date it cannot source.

faqs.question: Does the Cambridge zone my child's centre sits in change their timetable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this catches families out. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the series timetable. Cambridge's guidance for exams officers states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. Take the timetable from your child's exams officer rather than from a search result, and check the zone label on the document before building a revision plan around it.

faqs.question: After results, how long is the window for asking the IB to look again?
faqs.answer: Short, and set by the IB for each session. An enquiry upon results is submitted by the school rather than by a parent, there are different categories of enquiry, and a fee applies. We do not publish the deadline because it varies by session and we will not guess one. The useful move is to ask your coordinator in writing, before results day, for the exact date and the categories available. That way the decision is made on an examiner-informed read of the script rather than in a panic.

faqs.question: Does my child need Ministry of Education equivalency before a UAE university application?
faqs.answer: A UAE-recognised secondary certificate is what a UAE university or federal employer asks for, and the Ministry of Education equivalency process is how a foreign qualification becomes one. Open the file in the final year, because document collection and attestation take longer than families expect. For the British track the published rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects. Verify current requirements at the official channel; no tutoring is required for any of it.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education marks go through the same external marking as Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: No. They sit outside the IB's assessment entirely and are governed by the emirate regulator and the federal ministry instead. They are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, with Standard Arabic required as the language of instruction in defined cases. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Using different or additional content without prior ministry permission is prohibited, so a tutor works from the school's own scheme rather than bringing their own material.

ib-examiner-tutor.closingHeading: Start from the date, not from the subject
ib-examiner-tutor.closingBody: If your child sits papers next session, the first useful conversation is not about subjects at all. It is about which dates are already fixed: the school's internal submission deadlines, the mock window, the entry deadline, and the session itself. Tell us those and the component you are worried about, and we will tell you honestly whether a specialist is free and what the remaining weeks can realistically change. The trial lesson is free, 45 minutes, one per family, with no card details taken. If nobody is free at the level you need, we will say so and give you a date rather than filling the slot.

intro.heading: Two rulebooks sit behind every home tuition decision in the UAE
paragraphs: Search for IB home tuition in the UAE and the results argue about price, hours and tutor quality. Almost none of them mention the two rulebooks a family is actually working inside. The first is the permit system: private tutoring here is licensed work, and the person teaching your child is meant to hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The second is your child's school system, where an emirate authority decides which curriculum may be taught, which subjects are compulsory beside it and how many weekly minutes those subjects take.

Those two rulebooks decide more than they appear to. They decide who may legally sit in your living room and charge for an hour of teaching. They decide whether the teacher your child already trusts is permitted to take your money at all. They decide how much of the week is committed before a tutor is booked, because Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies run alongside the Diploma in Dubai regardless of the licensed international curriculum. And at the end of Year 13 they decide what a Diploma has to become on paper before a UAE university admissions office will read it.

IB Gram's own position is worth stating before anything else. Lessons are delivered live online, one-to-one, over video, on Gulf Standard Time. No tutor attends a UAE address; home visits are a service we run only in India. That is not a workaround for the permit rules, and it is not a compromise. A Diploma student sitting Chemistry at Higher Level needs a Chemistry Higher Level teacher, not the best-qualified person willing to drive to Mirdif on a Tuesday evening in October. Online one-to-one is how a family in Fujairah gets the same specialist a family in Jumeirah gets.

The rest of this page is built to be used rather than skimmed. It sets out who may tutor privately and what to ask them for, which authority sits above your child's school and what that authority controls, how the mandatory ministry subjects are organised, what the UAE market charges and what the travel inside that charge is really worth, where the line sits on coursework, what the Ministry of Education asks for at equivalency, and which exam dates are genuinely published. Every figure carries its source. Where a date could not be verified at source, the page says so rather than guessing.

One caveat belongs at the top. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and nothing here should be read as implying one. Schools are named because they are the system your child sits inside, not because they are clients. Where a regulator's rule is quoted, the authority is named so you can read the original instead of taking our summary of it on trust.

ib-home-tuition.programmesIntro: The IB runs as a continuum, and in the UAE each stage of it sits beside a set of subjects the regulator requires. The four programmes below are described as a UAE parent meets them: what the stage assesses, and what the local school system adds on top of it.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations. Teachers assess through units of inquiry, portfolios and an exhibition in the final year. Tuition at this stage is almost never about exam technique; it is about reading fluency, number sense and the written expression a child will need two programmes later. Parents usually come to us after a parent-teacher meeting rather than after a report card.
programmes.countryNote: A PYP school in Dubai still has to deliver Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies to KHDA's weekly time requirement, and the Arabic strand is where PYP parents most often ask for separate support. Because there is no external paper to aim at, the useful measure is whether a child can read an unfamiliar Arabic passage aloud and answer questions on it without help.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and reported as a 1-7 grade through published boundaries. Students lose marks less for not knowing content than for not answering the command term in front of them. The personal project in the final year is the first piece of long independent work most students have attempted.
programmes.countryNote: Many UAE families use the MYP's final year as the decision point between staying with the IB and moving to IGCSE, because a sizeable share of their neighbours' children sit Cambridge or Edexcel papers instead. That decision is worth making on the subjects a school can actually staff at Higher Level, not on reputation. The mandatory ministry subjects continue through the MYP unchanged.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries internally assessed coursework alongside the papers, and the coursework is marked by the teacher and moderated externally. The common failure is not a weak subject but a timetable collision between three internal assessment deadlines and the mock papers.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma is a minority route in the UAE: in Dubai the IB accounted for roughly a 7% share of private-school enrolment in 2024-25. That is the whole reason Higher Level specialists are hard to find inside a driving radius, and the reason an online match beats a local one for subjects such as Physics HL, Economics HL and Arabic A. Equivalency paperwork then matters for UAE university applications.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines at least two DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is offered by far fewer schools than the Diploma, so students on it are often the only candidate in their year taking a particular DP subject at Standard Level.
programmes.countryNote: A CP student in the UAE frequently needs exactly one thing: a specialist in the single DP course their school runs for a handful of candidates. That is the clearest case for online one-to-one tuition in the country, because the local pool for one Standard Level subject in one school is effectively nobody. Equivalency for a CP leaver should be checked with the Ministry before applications open, not after.

ib-home-tuition.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects UAE families ask for most, with what each one actually assesses and where the marks tend to go. Every description is about the paper set and the coursework, because that is what a tutor can change in a term.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The calculus-heavy route, and the one most UAE engineering and economics applicants are told to take. Higher Level adds an options-free but deeper syllabus and a third paper of extended problem solving. Marks go on unjustified steps and on proof questions that students treat as calculations. The exploration is where a strong mathematician often underperforms.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-assisted work, with a graphical calculator expected throughout. It is not the easy route; Higher Level statistics and the third paper's extended investigation defeat students who chose it to avoid calculus. Check the course requirement published by the universities on your child's list before switching from Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields reward precision with units and vector direction; students lose marks writing correct physics in the wrong notation. Higher Level extends the syllabus and adds data-analysis demands in the final paper. The internal assessment stands or falls on whether the method actually controls what it claims to control.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are the usual pressure points, and the ones Higher Level students most often ask for weekly help with. The internal assessment is a design problem before it is a chemistry problem, which is why it is worth starting a year before the deadline rather than a month.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the trap. Students revise terminology and then lose marks on application questions set in unfamiliar contexts and on data interpretation from a study they have never seen. Command terms do most of the damage: outline, explain and evaluate each want a different shape of answer.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries more marks than students expect, and the written commentaries need real published articles rather than convenient ones. Higher Level adds quantitative demands that catch out students who chose Economics as an essay subject. Evaluation, not description, separates a 5 from a 7.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A case-study subject where marks are lost by answering in general terms rather than from the stimulus provided. The internal assessment requires genuine primary or secondary research on a real organisation, and UAE students often pick a company they cannot actually get information about.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper on unseen non-literary texts are where UAE students most often need structured practice, especially those who have moved between curricula. Higher Level adds an extended essay-length paper. Analysis of how a text works, rather than what it says, is the skill being marked.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic sits in two places at once for most UAE students: as an IB language subject and as a KHDA mandatory subject with its own ministry curriculum. First-language and additional-language students are taught separately at school and should be supported separately out of it, because the expectations and the language of instruction differ.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Few UAE schools staff this at Higher Level, so candidates are often one of two or three in a year group. The solution requires working code and documented testing, not a description of an idea, and students underestimate how long the development stage takes once school deadlines are set.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The core is where Diploma points are quietly won and lost. TOK is assessed on an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay; the Extended Essay is a supervised piece of independent research. Both are marked on the student's own thinking, which sets a hard limit on what any tutor may contribute.

ib-home-tuition.regionsTitle: Who regulates where: the emirates, grouped by authority
ib-home-tuition.regionsIntro: Tuition is delivered online everywhere below, so the practical difference between these places is not travel time — it is which authority sits above the school, what that authority controls, and how thin the local pool of IB specialists is.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA licenses the curriculum, inspects the school and sets the mandatory-subject requirements every private school must meet. It also issues the Educational Services Permit a tuition centre with premises needs. The largest school market in the country, and still a minority IB one.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff restrict paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the same school, which narrows the list of people you may legitimately hire from inside your child's school.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK, not a separate authority, which surprises families who have moved from Dubai. A smaller school list means fewer schools running the full Diploma subject spread, so a Higher Level specialist for a minority subject will almost always be matched online rather than locally.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Fee and curriculum approval sitting with the emirate means the school, not a parents' group, is the reliable source on what your child will sit.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education here with the same approval powers over fees, curricula and assessment methods as Sharjah's authority, across a much shorter school list. Families here are the clearest beneficiaries of a tutor pool that is not limited by driving distance.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman. Many families commute to Dubai or Sharjah for school, so the usable tuition slot is late: after the drive home, after dinner, and often after a younger sibling's bedtime. Evening-only availability is the norm, not a request.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under the federal Ministry of Education. The smallest private-school market in the country, which makes online delivery less a preference than the only way to reach a Diploma subject specialist at Higher Level on a weekday evening at a sensible rate.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education territory, on the east coast and separated from the western emirates by a mountain drive. Any model that depends on a specialist travelling to the family twice a week fails here on arithmetic alone, whatever the hourly rate quoted.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai's IB schools sit inside a market of 227 private schools teaching 17 curricula, so two children on the same street can be entered for entirely different papers. Ask which programme and which year group a school actually runs at Higher Level before assuming a subject is available.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, under ADEK
schoolClusters.note: Families in this cluster name a mix of IB, British and American schools when they contact us, which is a fair picture of the emirate. ADEK's ethics rules are the reason a request for your child's own class teacher, paid privately, is one we decline rather than negotiate.

Fewer schools, longer commutes and smaller Diploma cohorts. A student can be one of three candidates in a Higher Level subject, which changes what tuition is for: not remediation, but the specialist conversation a three-student class cannot always sustain.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the term
modes.description: A fixed hour each week in one subject at one level, with the tutor working from the school's own scheme of work and deadline list rather than a generic plan. This is what most Diploma families book first, usually in a single subject, and it is the pattern that makes a difference over two terms rather than two weeks.

sections.heading: What a UAE family is really asking for when they search for home tuition
paragraphs: The phrase means a specialist, one child and no classroom. It rarely means that someone must physically be in the house. When families explain the request, the three things they describe are a tutor who knows the exact paper their child sits, an hour that survives contact with a UAE school day, and a person they can hold to account. Travel is a means to those ends, and in this country it is an expensive one.

The market offers four ways to get there. An individual tutor who travels to the family, at the top of the published rate bands because the drive is inside the fee. A tuition centre with premises, which is a licensed business rather than an individual and needs its own permit. A group class, cheaper but fixed to somebody else's pace. Or live one-to-one online, which separates the specialist from the postcode entirely. IB Gram does the fourth, and only the fourth, for families in the UAE.

So the honest answer to the search is this. You can buy IB home tuition in the UAE in the literal sense, at between roughly AED 180 and AED 500 an hour according to published market rates, and some families will decide the physical presence is worth it. What you cannot reliably buy that way is a Higher Level specialist in a minority subject on a Tuesday evening in your own community. The IB is a 7% share of Dubai's private-school enrolment. The specialist your child needs is usually not the nearest one, and online one-to-one is how that stops mattering.
bullets: What families ask for: the right specialist, a workable hour, someone accountable
What they usually do not need: a car journey built into the hourly rate
Published rates for a visiting tutor: roughly AED 180-500 an hour
How IB Gram delivers it in the UAE: live video, one-to-one, nothing else

sections.heading: Who the law permits to tutor your child privately
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work with a licence attached. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is issued through MoHRE, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone offering private lessons without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting you a dirham figure for the penalty is quoting something that cannot be checked.

The eligible categories are wider than most parents assume. They include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The route is MoHRE's own service, listed as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days and no fee published.

What this means at your end is a question, not a worry. Ask any tutor you are about to pay whether they hold the permit, and ask what subject and level they actually teach rather than what they can cover. The table below sets out each category and what is reasonable to ask for before the first paid hour. It applies to a tutor at the door and to a tutor on a screen equally: the permit is about the work, not the format.

sections.heading: The own-school rule, and the offer worth turning down
paragraphs: One request comes up more than any other: can we hire the teacher who already teaches the class? It is an understandable instinct and it runs into the rules. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. This has been press-reported rather than read by us in the current ADEK policy document, so verify the exact wording with the school before relying on it.

The conflict is easy to see once it is named. The same adult would be setting the classwork, marking the assessment that feeds the report, and being paid privately by the family whose child is being marked. Add internally assessed coursework to that, where the teacher is both supervisor and moderated marker, and the position becomes untenable for the teacher long before it becomes a problem for the family. An offer that leads with your child's own teacher, privately, is an offer to put a teacher's employment at risk.

The practical consequence is small. A tutor from outside the school is better placed anyway, because they can say the unpopular thing about a topic choice or a predicted grade without a staffroom to go back to. What matters is that they teach the same syllabus and level, work from your child's actual deadline list, and never become a second marker of work the school will moderate. That is the brief we match against, and it is why we decline the own-teacher request rather than quietly route around it.

sections.heading: Which authority sits above your child's school, and what it approves
paragraphs: Five bodies cover private schools in the UAE and most search results name none of them. In Dubai, KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The part that matters for planning is what these authorities control beyond publishing an inspection judgement. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is approval over what your child studies and how it is assessed, not only over how well the school did last year. KHDA, in parallel, sets the mandatory-subject requirements every private school must meet and issues the permit a tuition centre with premises needs in order to trade.

There is a federal baseline underneath all of it. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but they must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That single rule is why an IB school in Dubai still timetables Arabic and Islamic Education, and it is the reason a tuition plan built only around six IB subjects usually misses the two the school report will also carry.

sections.heading: The ministry subjects already sitting on your child's timetable
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required its current arrangements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For an IB family this is the single most overlooked line in the week. Six Diploma subjects plus the core is already a full load, and the KHDA mandatory subjects are additional to it rather than instead of something.

The organisation rules are specific enough to plan around. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit; schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

Those language rules carry into tuition. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; non-Arabs are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Schools must also ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. And for these subjects specifically, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, which is why our support here works from the school's own materials.

sections.heading: Dubai's school market in numbers, and the specialist problem it creates
paragraphs: Dubai published the figures that explain why finding an IB specialist locally is harder than the size of the city suggests. In 2024-25 the emirate's private schools taught 387,441 students across 227 schools offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum holding a 37% share of enrolment, Indian 26%, American 14% and the International Baccalaureate 7%. The market is enormous and it is also fragmented, which is a different problem from scarcity.

Growth is not changing the ratio quickly. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. KHDA also confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family budgeting tuition alongside fees, a fee freeze is the most useful planning fact of the year.

Put the two together and the practical conclusion is straightforward. In a market where the IB is a minority board spread thinly across 227 schools, the number of teachers in your community who have taught your child's specific Higher Level paper recently is small, and the number of those willing to drive to you at a sensible rate is smaller still. sections.heading: What home tuition costs in the UAE, and what the travel inside it is worth
paragraphs: Most pages competing for this search publish no price at all, and the ones that do quote dollars. Here are the published bands in dirhams, attributed, as of October 2026. Budget online tuition, often delivered by a university student, runs from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour. A qualified subject tutor online sits around AED 150 to AED 300. A visiting tutor at a UAE address runs AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is inside the fee. An IB or IGCSE subject specialist is quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and named premium tuition reaches AED 650.

These are market rates published by other providers, not an IB Gram price list. Monthly packages seen in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Ask any provider in writing whether the quoted figure includes VAT before comparing two numbers.

The column worth studying is the one nobody prints: how many minutes of teaching sit inside the money. A visiting tutor billing 90 minutes in a UAE evening is covering a drive, a lift, a greeting and a settling-in period from the same fee. That is not dishonesty, it is geography, and it is why the in-home band starts above the online specialist band rather than beside it. Decide what you are buying with the difference.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor against live one-to-one online, under UAE conditions
paragraphs: This is the comparison the search is really about, so here it is without the sales pitch. A tutor physically present has real advantages: a younger child stays on task more easily, written work can be checked over a shoulder, and some students simply engage better with a person in the room. Those advantages are worth paying for at primary and lower secondary level, and a family that chooses them is not making a mistake.

They weigh differently for a Diploma student. At Higher Level the binding constraint is not attention, it is expertise: whether the adult teaching your child has taught that paper, marked that coursework and seen where candidates lose marks on it. Within a 20-minute drive of most UAE communities, the number of people who meet that description for a given subject is tiny. Widen the radius to anywhere with a stable connection and the constraint disappears. That is the whole argument for the online model, and it is an argument about supply rather than about screens.

The practical details matter as much as the principle. An online slot can start after Maghrib, after homework, or at 7am before school, where a visiting tutor is held to one window in evening traffic. A missed session is rescheduled rather than written off. Work lives on a shared screen the student can reopen. And if a subject is genuinely not covered, you get told that in the first conversation instead of discovering it in week three.

sections.heading: Coursework, honesty and the line a paid tutor must not cross
paragraphs: This section exists because the same search results that sell tuition also sell finished coursework. One site in this market advertises completed internal assessments at AED 3,750. Buying one puts a student at risk of an academic malpractice finding, which is a far worse outcome than a disappointing mark, and it is the reason the boundary belongs on the page rather than in a terms-and-conditions link.

The rule is simple to state. Assessed work must be authored by the student. A tutor may teach the subject content and the technique, question a topic choice before months are spent on it, explain what the published criteria actually reward, mark a practice task of the same type, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not supply text for insertion, choose and model the whole piece end to end, or act as a second marker of work the school will moderate.

There is a copyright line beside the honesty one. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson. We reference them and link to the official source; we do not host them, reproduce them or supply them. If a provider offers your child a library of unreleased papers, that is a warning sign about everything else they say, and it is worth walking away from the quote entirely. The table below sets out the boundary component by component, in the plain words a parent can use when briefing a tutor for the first time.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and the number we will not invent
paragraphs: Equivalency is the step that turns a school-leaving qualification into a certificate the UAE recognises, and it is almost entirely absent from the pages competing for this search. For the British track the requirements were reported in July 2026: a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two details in that are worth more than the rest. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which matters because a competing page ranking for these queries tells UAE parents six IGCSE subjects are needed. And for the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in SAT Math before applying.

For the IB Diploma specifically, we publish no points threshold. The reporting we have read does not state one, and an equivalency figure that has not been read on the Ministry's own pages is not a figure worth putting in front of a family making university plans. Check it on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation channel, and start early: document attestation has its own timetable and it is not a process any tutoring provider performs on your behalf or can accelerate.

sections.heading: The exam year as it is actually published, and the dates we leave blank
paragraphs: Registration deadlines sit months before the papers, and they are the dates families miss. Cambridge International's March 2027 series is the clearest worked example in the public record: final entries are due 27 November 2026, the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. The entry deadline is more than two months before the first paper, which is why a decision about tiering or a subject drop has to be made in the autumn.

Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in June and November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. One detail catches UAE centres specifically: every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams run in May or June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026.

For the IB, this page deliberately prints no date. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no session or results date in this project has been confirmed at source, and publishing an unverified exam date to a family planning a revision block would be worse than publishing nothing. UAE schools sit the May session; confirm the window, the upload deadlines and the results date with your child's IB coordinator or on the IB's own pages, and build the plan backwards from what they tell you.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the hour
process.description: One message with four facts is enough to start: the subject, whether it is Higher or Standard Level, the board and year group, and the evening that actually works after the school run. Vague requests produce vague matches, so the more specific the brief, the better the first proposal will be.

process.title: We check the permit and the subject evidence
process.description: Before a tutor is proposed we confirm the permit position and what they have actually taught at that level, not what they are willing to cover. You may ask to see the permit yourself. A tutor who has never taught your child's Higher Level paper is not a match, however strong they look on paper.

process.title: One free trial lesson, 45 minutes
process.description: The trial is a single 45-minute session, free, with no card details taken and nothing to cancel. It is a teaching session rather than a sales call: bring a marked past paper or a piece of returned coursework, because the fastest diagnosis comes from something a teacher has already written on.

process.title: A fixed weekly slot, built around school deadlines
process.description: Once a match works, the slot stays the same each week and the tutor works from your child's own unit order and internal deadline list. Coursework dates are written in at the start so the week of three deadlines is planned for in September rather than survived in February.

process.title: A different tutor, or an honest no
process.description: If the match is wrong, say so and we change it; nobody improves with a tutor they dread. If no specialist is free for the subject, level and hour you need, we say that in the first conversation. An unavailable subject is a disappointing answer, and it is better than a filler tutor at full rate.

whyPoints.title: The specialist, not the nearest available adult
whyPoints.description: The IB is a minority board in the UAE, so the pool of local teachers who have taught your child's exact Higher Level paper is small. Matching online removes the driving radius from the decision, which is the one change that reliably improves the quality of the person teaching.

whyPoints.title: The permit question answered before you pay
whyPoints.description: Private tutoring in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. We check the position before proposing a tutor and you may ask to see it. Most competing pages do not mention the permit at all, which tells you how often it gets checked.

whyPoints.title: Rates you can check against someone else's price page
whyPoints.description: Every dirham figure on this page is attributed to the provider or research that published it, with the month stated. Nothing here is presented as our price list. If a number cannot be sourced, it is not printed, which is the opposite of the usual practice in this market.

whyPoints.title: The coursework line stated plainly
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback; the internal assessment, Extended Essay and TOK essay stay the student's own work. That boundary protects your child from a malpractice finding, and it is published here rather than buried, because this market contains people selling finished coursework.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No star ratings, no student counts, no grade promises and no regulator badges. IB Gram holds no approval or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and says so on the page rather than hoping nobody asks.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that fits a UAE week
whyPoints.description: Slots sit on Gulf Standard Time around the real school day, including after Maghrib and during the shortened Ramadan timetable, and early-morning sessions before school for families whose evenings are already full. Nothing depends on anyone crossing the city at 5pm.

faqs.question: Does IB home tuition in the UAE mean somebody comes to the house?
faqs.answer: Not with us. IB Gram delivers one-to-one IB tuition live online, over video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, and no tutor attends a UAE address. Home visits are a service we run only in India. The phrase is kept because it is what parents search, and the underlying request is almost always a specialist for one child rather than a visitor. In the UAE market a visiting tutor is quoted at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside the fee, and a share of that hour is spent on the journey rather than on teaching your child.

faqs.question: Which categories of UAE resident can hold a private tuition work permit?
faqs.answer: The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, under the service listed as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, with a stated completion time of two working days. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can we simply hire my child's own class teacher for paid lessons?
faqs.answer: It is the most common request and the answer is no. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's school. Treat that as press-reported and confirm the current wording with the school. The conflict is obvious once named: the same adult would set the work, mark the assessment that feeds the report, and be paid by the family whose child is being marked. A tutor from outside the school can also be more candid.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a licensed tuition centre and an individual tutor?
faqs.answer: They are different legal animals. An individual providing private lessons needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit. A tuition operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which starts with initial approval, allows a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and is renewed annually with the request made at least 30 days before expiry. The distinction matters when you compare quotes: a centre is carrying premises costs and a business licence, an individual is not, and neither arrangement tells you anything about teaching quality on its own.

faqs.question: What does it mean when a tuition company says it holds a KHDA permit?
faqs.answer: It should mean one specific thing: an Educational Services Permit issued to a training institute operating from premises in Dubai. If a provider implies more than that, ask which permit, issued when, and for which subjects, and expect a permit number. IB Gram does not hold one and does not claim one, because we operate no UAE premises; our lessons are delivered online. Be especially careful with phrasing that attaches a regulator's name to the tutors rather than to a business licence. No UAE authority accredits individual private tutors as a quality mark, and any page suggesting otherwise is describing something that does not exist.

faqs.question: Why does the Ministry set the content for Arabic and Islamic Education lessons?
faqs.answer: Because those subjects sit under a federal requirement rather than under the school's licensed international curriculum. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but they must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. KHDA's guidelines go further: for the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. For tuition that has a practical consequence. Support for these subjects works from the materials your child's school already uses, rather than from a parallel syllabus bought in from elsewhere.

faqs.question: How much weekly time does a Dubai school give to the mandatory UAE subjects?
faqs.answer: KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary the length of a lesson provided the total weekly time is met, and the guidelines advise that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. The current arrangements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For an IB family the useful conclusion is that these hours are already committed before tuition is booked, so a weekly tuition slot has to fit around a timetable that is fuller than six Diploma subjects suggests.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education classes separated by first language?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the rule is explicit. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; non-Arab students are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Out-of-school support should respect the same split, because a first-language student and an additional-language student are not working towards the same thing.

faqs.question: With 227 private schools in Dubai, why is a Higher Level specialist still hard to find?
faqs.answer: Because the market is fragmented rather than scarce. In 2024-25 Dubai's 227 private schools taught 387,441 students across 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37%, Indian at 26%, American at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at a 7% share. A tutor who lives nearby is statistically more likely to know a different board than yours. Narrow that to one subject at Higher Level, in one evening slot, within a 20-minute drive, and the available pool is close to empty. Matching online removes the driving radius from the problem, which is the only variable a family can actually change.

faqs.question: Will school fees rise next year while we are also paying for tuition?
faqs.answer: For Dubai, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That is a Dubai decision and does not automatically apply in other emirates, where fee approval sits with the local authority: Sharjah's authority and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge both approve tuition fees directly. Ask your school rather than assuming, and treat a fee freeze as the year to budget a tuition block if one is needed.

faqs.question: What does a visiting tutor's hourly rate include that an online rate does not?
faqs.answer: The journey, mostly. Published UAE bands put a visiting tutor at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and the gap is largely travel, waiting and the risk that traffic eats the slot. Inside a 90-minute booking, a visiting tutor may teach for 60 to 70 minutes once the drive, the lift and settling in are taken out. That is geography rather than bad faith. The question to ask yourself is whether physical presence is worth that difference for your child's age and subject.

faqs.question: Should we pay by the hour or buy a monthly package of sessions?
faqs.answer: Compare the total, not the headline rate. Packages advertised in the UAE market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits, while Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Before committing, ask what happens to unused sessions, how much notice a reschedule needs, and whether the quoted figure includes VAT. Get the answers in writing, because this is where the published prices in this market most often contradict each other.

faqs.question: Where do I check the Ministry's equivalency requirements for an IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: On moe.gov.ae, or through the attestation channel for your emirate. We deliberately publish no IB points threshold, because the reporting we have read does not state one and an unverified figure is worse than none for a family making university plans. For the British track the position was reported in July 2026: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, plus one A-Level at no less than E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or can speed up on your behalf.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does the Ministry count, and at what grade?
faqs.answer: Five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates, each at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, as reported in July 2026. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five required subjects, which is worth knowing because a competing page ranking for UAE tutoring queries states that candidates here must take six IGCSE subjects. Those subjects remain compulsory at school under KHDA and federal rules even though they sit outside the equivalency count. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae before building a subject choice around it, since reported rules can be updated.

faqs.question: Why will you not publish the IB exam dates for the next session?
faqs.answer: Because we could not verify them at source. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a revision plan built on a date we guessed would be worse than no date at all. UAE schools sit the May session. Confirm the exam window, the coursework upload deadlines and the results date with your child's IB coordinator or on the IB's own pages, then plan backwards from the first paper. Cambridge and Pearson dates are published and sourced, and appear on this page with the source named.

faqs.question: Why does Cambridge publish six different timetables for the same exam series?
faqs.answer: Because every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and each zone gets its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. For a UAE family this matters most for private candidates and for anyone cross-checking dates found on a forum. Get the timetable from the centre entering your child, confirm the zone, and treat any date circulating without a zone attached as unusable.

faqs.question: Can a tutor look at a draft of the Extended Essay before it is submitted?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits, and the limits are the point. A tutor may teach research skills, discuss sources, teach referencing and argument structure, and give feedback on what the student has already written. A tutor may not supply text for insertion, model the whole piece end to end, or act as a second marker of something the school will moderate. The Extended Essay is supervised by a teacher at the school, and that supervision is part of the assessment record. Anything arriving already written is a malpractice risk for the student, which is a far worse outcome than a middling mark.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor to show me before the first paid lesson?
faqs.answer: Four things. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, since private tutoring in the UAE requires one. Which board, subject and level they have actually taught, with the year group named rather than a list of everything they could cover. How they will work with the school's own deadline list, because coursework dates drive the term. And where they stand on assessed work, in plain words. A tutor who answers all four without hesitation is usually the one worth booking, whatever the hourly rate, and the questions cost nothing to ask during a trial session.

ib-home-tuition.closingHeading: Start with one subject, one hour and the questions above
ib-home-tuition.closingBody: If you have read this far, you already know more about the rules around IB home tuition in the UAE than most pages competing for the search will tell you. The next step is small: name the subject, the level and the evening that works, and we will say honestly whether a specialist is free for it. The trial is one 45-minute lesson, free, with no card details taken. Bring a marked past paper or a returned piece of coursework, because that is the fastest way for a teacher to see what is actually going wrong. If nobody is available for your subject and hour, you will be told in the first conversation.

Each card shows the subject, whether the tutor works at Standard or Higher Level, and the coursework component they supervise. Lessons run live online, one student to one teacher.

intro.heading: Nobody prices the driving, so start there
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in the UAE is a person who travels to a flat or villa and teaches one student in their own room. The market for that service is real, it is well established, and published rates for it run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour. What almost no provider breaks out is the share of that figure that pays for the journey. A tutor who drives from Mirdif to Dubai Marina for a sixty-minute lesson spends closer to two and a half hours on the engagement. The rate has to cover all of it, because nobody absorbs an hour of Sheikh Zayed Road for free.

That single piece of arithmetic drives most of the decisions a UAE family makes about tuition. It explains why in-home rates sit above online ones for the same qualification. It explains the minimum two-hour session, which exists so the travel is amortised over something. It explains why a cancellation at 4pm costs the full fee when the tutor is already on the road. And it explains the quiet constraint underneath the whole model: the tutor your child gets is drawn from whoever teaches that subject and happens to live within a tolerable drive, which in a scarce subject such as Mathematics AA Higher Level or Chemistry Higher Level is a very short list.

IB Gram does not run a visiting-tutor service in the Emirates. Home visits are something we offer only in India. For families here, every lesson is delivered live online, one-to-one, over video, with a shared screen and a document both people write on. We target the phrase "IB home tutor in the UAE" because that is what parents type, and we would rather answer the question properly than pretend a different question was asked.

The honest case for the online format is not that it is cheaper, although at market rates it usually is. It is that removing the drive removes the radius. A family in Khalifa City is no longer choosing between the two Economics Higher Level teachers who live nearby; they are choosing from everyone who teaches Economics Higher Level and can take a 7pm slot on Gulf Standard Time. For a programme where a single subject at Higher Level can decide a university offer, matching on the guide beats matching on the map.

What follows is the full cost picture: what the UAE market charges and who published those figures, where tutoring budgets leak, which marks are cheapest to recover and which are expensive, how the spend should be phased across two Diploma years, and what the permit rules do to the price you are quoted. Every AED figure on this page is a market figure with a source attached. None of them is an IB Gram price list, because we quote after the trial lesson, once we know the subject, the level and the deadline.
