ib-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the Diploma subjects UAE families ask for most, at Higher and Standard Level. Each teaches one-to-one over live video and plans from three dates: the next Internal Assessment deadline, the mock window, then the papers. Tell us the date you are working towards and the subject, in that order.

intro.heading: The IB year runs backwards from the first paper
paragraphs: An IB online tutor in the UAE teaches one named subject, one-to-one, over live video, usually in a weekly sixty- or ninety-minute slot set to Gulf Standard Time. Nothing arrives at a UAE address. The lesson runs on a shared screen with the student's own worked solutions, the school's assessment schedule and a marked past paper open beside each other. That part is simple. The part UAE families get wrong is timing, because the Diploma is a dated qualification and the dates that matter are not the ones printed on the exam timetable.

Count what a Year 13 student has already handed in before the first paper of the May session: a mathematics exploration, a scientific investigation for each science taken, an Extended Essay of up to 4,000 words, a TOK exhibition, a TOK essay of up to 1,600 words, an individual oral in each language, and whatever internal mocks the school used to form predicted grades. Every one of those carries a deadline set by the school months earlier, and in most subjects a fifth to a third of the final marks are already fixed by the time study leave begins.

So the useful question is not what a tutor costs. It is what has to be finished, and by when. A family starting in DP1 is buying feedback on work that still counts towards the grade. A family starting in March of DP2 is buying paper technique, which is worth having and is a smaller lever. Both purchases are legitimate; they are not the same purchase. The second is the one most UAE parents make by accident, because the first internal deadline arrives while the school year is still being described as a settling-in period.

The UAE calendar then takes its own bites out of whatever plan survives. The academic year opens in late August or early September, and timetables settle over a fortnight. UAE National Day holidays remove a week in early December. Winter break removes about three more. Ramadan shifts roughly eleven days earlier each year, so it has been crossing the mock and revision window rather than a quiet stretch: school days shorten, afternoons are low-energy, and real study moves to the hours after Iftar. Sessions move with it, into post-Iftar sessions agreed in advance rather than cancelled week by week, and Eid al-Fitr then takes the last clear week before the papers.

One honesty note, since the rest of this page is built on dates. Cambridge International and Pearson publish their timetables and key dates openly, and every Cambridge and Pearson date below is taken from the board's own page with the source named. The IB does not make its session dates available to automated checking, so no IB exam date and no IB results date appears anywhere on this page. For those there are exactly two sources worth using: ibo.org and your child's own Diploma Programme coordinator, who also owns every internal deadline that matters more than the exam date does.
bullets: The May session is the one almost every UAE Diploma cohort sits; November exists and a minority use it for retakes.
Cambridge runs June and November series plus a March series used by some centres, and entries close months ahead of the papers.
Deadlines for the exploration, investigations, Extended Essay, TOK exhibition and TOK essay are set by the school, not the IB, and differ between campuses in the same emirate.
Ramadan moves about eleven days earlier each year, which has pushed it into the mock and pre-exam window.
Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, in all seven emirates including Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain.
Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies sit in the same school week, mandated federally and detailed by KHDA in Dubai.

ib-online-tutor.programmesIntro: The IB is four programmes and each one puts its pressure in a different place. A PYP parent is working to a report cycle. An MYP parent is working to a personal project and, in many UAE schools, to IGCSE entries instead. A Diploma parent is working to a dated session. Here is where each clock actually sits.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP sets no external examinations, so its calendar belongs to the school: units of inquiry, report cycles, and the Year 6 exhibition. Tuition at this stage is about the mechanics that later get blamed on the Diploma, which are number fluency, reading stamina and the structure of a written answer. The exhibition is the honest marker to watch, because it is the first time a child has to run a long piece of self-directed work to a deadline without being chased through it each week.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, PYP schools sit inside the KHDA inspection framework and carry the Ministry's mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies from the earliest years. For a family arriving in Year 3 with no Arabic, that is the gap which compounds, because progress is measured against classmates who began in FS1. Starting an hour a week in primary costs a fraction of repairing it in Year 10.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP is criterion-referenced and reported on a 1 to 8 scale per criterion, which is why a parent can see a 5 and not know what is missing. Its fixed point is the personal project in the final year. Where a school runs the full MYP to Year 11, the calendar is internal and flexible. Where it runs optional MYP eAssessment, there is an external deadline to plan against, and the school will say which model it uses.
programmes.countryNote: Many UAE schools licensed for the IB continuum switch their Year 10 and 11 cohorts to Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE instead of running MYP 4 and 5 to the end, which changes the calendar completely: entries, tiers and zone-specific timetables arrive two years earlier than a continuum family expects. Ask the school in Year 9 which route the cohort will take, because the answer changes when tuition is useful.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, usually three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The maximum is 45 points, of which up to three come from the TOK and Extended Essay combination, and the award of the Diploma requires at least 24 points together with a set of pass conditions your coordinator will explain in writing. Two years looks long until you lay the internal deadlines out: the coursework load peaks in the second half of DP1 and the first term of DP2, well before revision begins.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma is a minority route inside the UAE system, at roughly 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25 against 37% UK and 26% Indian curricula. That matters practically: in most emirates the pool of local teachers who have examined or taught a specific Higher Level option is small, and it thins sharply outside Dubai and Abu Dhabi. Live online one-to-one is how a family in Fujairah reaches the same specialist a Jumeirah family does.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a service-learning element and a language development strand. It is assessed against a different set of components from the Diploma, and the reflective project carries a deadline set by the school in the same window as the Diploma cohort's Extended Essay. Universities treat it on its own terms, so the entry requirements for a target course should be checked before Year 12 subject choices are signed off.
programmes.countryNote: Few UAE schools are authorised for the CP, and the regulator's own school listing is the place to confirm whether a campus offers it rather than a league table or a tutoring page. Where a UAE student does take it, the two Diploma courses inside the programme are examined on the same session dates as everyone else's, so the backwards calendar on this page applies to them unchanged.

ib-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each subject loses marks in its own place, and a first session should find that place with a marked past paper rather than a conversation. The weightings below follow the assessment models in current use; confirm them against your child's own subject guide, because the IB revises guides on a rolling cycle and a tutor who quotes last decade's structure is a warning sign.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is the non-calculator paper and it punishes algebraic fragility rather than ignorance. At Higher Level the two long papers carry 30% each, Paper 3 carries 20% and the exploration 20%. The component students have practised least is Maths AA Paper 3, the extended investigation, which means a fifth of the grade is routinely left to improvisation.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The calculation is usually right and the sentence explaining what it means is missing. Statistics, modelling and confident use of the graphical calculator carry the course, and the exploration is 20% of the grade. Students who move here from Analysis and Approaches in DP2 need the modelling vocabulary far more than they need extra technique.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Under the current science model Paper 1 is 36%, Paper 2 is 44% and the scientific investigation 20% at both levels. Uncertainty handling and significant figures cost more marks than the physics does. The Higher Level extensions in fields and quantum are where a late start becomes visible first, because they assume fluency the student never built.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms lose marks on notation: missing curly arrows, missing lone pairs, missing charges. The data-based questions in Paper 1B reward a repeatable method for reading a graph. The 3,000-word investigation is marked on four criteria worth six marks each, and evaluation is the weakest criterion in almost every draft we see.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms decide the mark. Outline, explain and evaluate want three different structures and students write the same paragraph for all three. In the investigation, statistical treatment is the fastest available gain: error bars that mean something, a justified test, and the difference between correlation and causation stated rather than implied.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Definitions are the cheapest marks on the paper and the most often skipped. Diagrams earn credit only when labelled and referred to in the prose. Higher Level Paper 3 asks for policy judgement with calculation attached. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on recent news articles, each with a tight word ceiling your teacher will confirm.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The research project replaced the old commentary and it fails on scope rather than on writing: too broad a question, no usable data. Paper 1 is built on a pre-released case study, so the preparation window is published months ahead and is routinely wasted. Your coordinator will confirm the current word ceiling for the project.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is an unseen guided analysis and students describe content instead of analysing choices. The Individual Oral is effectively decided by extract selection before anyone speaks. At Higher Level the essay of roughly 1,200 to 1,500 words is a separate component with its own school deadline, usually in the first term of DP2.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The solution carries a larger share of the grade at Standard Level than at Higher, and most students under-document rather than under-code: no design overview, no test plan, no client evidence. Higher Level Paper 3 rests on an annually released case study, which gives a fixed and published window to prepare it in.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic A
subjects.description: In language acquisition, Paper 2 carries half the grade as listening and reading, Paper 1 is the written task at 25% and the individual oral the remaining 25%. Arabic A students are simultaneously meeting the Ministry's mandatory first-language requirement, so the same hours serve two purposes and should be planned once.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The TOK essay is 67% of the TOK grade and the exhibition 33%; the Extended Essay is graded A to E. Together they contribute up to three points to the Diploma total, which is the margin a great many conditional offers are missed by. Both run on school deadlines in the first half of DP2.

ib-online-tutor.regionsTitle: Where in the UAE these sessions actually happen
ib-online-tutor.regionsIntro: Delivery is online everywhere, so geography stops deciding which tutor you can reach and starts deciding only when the session can start. What varies by emirate is the regulator, the dominant curriculum, and how late the school run finishes. Those three things shape the slot.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Inspected by KHDA, with 227 private schools and 17 curricula recorded for 2024-25 and seven new schools approved for 2026-27, three of them IB. School runs across Al Barsha, Jumeirah and the Marina mean 16:30 slots are tight; 17:30 and 19:00 hold better through the term.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Inspected by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Island and Khalifa City commutes push realistic weekday starts to 17:30. ADEK's professional-ethics rules also bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school, so the tutor should be unconnected to the campus.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, with a smaller Diploma cohort than Abu Dhabi island and correspondingly fewer local Higher Level specialists. Live online is usually the only route to a Chemistry HL or Economics HL teacher, and the 90-minute drive that would otherwise be priced into an in-home rate disappears.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Many families commute into Dubai schools, so sessions land after a long return journey and work better at 19:00 or on a Saturday morning.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority. The IB footprint is small, Ajman Academy being the reference point, so subject coverage at Higher Level depends on reaching beyond the emirate, which is exactly what a live video session does.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Private education is regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge. RAK appears in effectively none of the competing tutoring pages, which tells you how thin local provision is. Families here routinely book two shorter evening sessions rather than one long one, because the school day ends earlier.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the Ministry of Education, on the east coast and two hours from the Dubai IB cluster. Nobody is driving that twice a week at a sensible price, which is why one-to-one online is not a compromise here but the only version of specialist tuition that exists.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under Ministry of Education supervision, and the emirate least served by the tutoring market. Students often attend school in Sharjah or Ajman, so the session has to sit after a cross-emirate commute. Late slots and weekend mornings are the two that survive a full term.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai campuses whose Diploma cohorts sit the May session
schoolClusters.note: KHDA-inspected schools where internal deadlines for the exploration, investigations and Extended Essay typically fall between the second half of DP1 and the first term of DP2. Dates differ by campus, which is why the coordinator's written internal calendar beats any generic plan.

ib-online-tutor.modesIntro: Four ways families use the hours, matched to where they are in the two years. The distinction is not luxury against budget. It is whether you are protecting coursework marks, closing a prior-learning gap, or buying paper technique in the last stretch.

modes.title: A fixed weekly slot through the term
modes.description: One subject, one tutor, the same time each week, booked in Gulf Standard Time so it survives the school run instead of competing with it. Term-time sessions follow the school's own sequence of topics, which means the tutor needs the scheme of work in week one. The slot is the thing families lose first and regret most: by October the workable evening hours are taken.

modes.description: Three or four sessions placed at the points where a piece of assessed work actually turns: question feasibility, data collected, first full draft, final criterion check. sections.heading: What an IB online tutor in the UAE does with the time that is left
paragraphs: An IB online tutor in the UAE is one subject specialist working with one student over live video. The format matters less than the sequencing. A first session that is worth paying for ends with a dated list: the next internal deadline, the mock window, the last date on which new content can sensibly be introduced, and the two topics in that subject where the student is currently losing the most marks.

Online delivery is what makes the specialist reachable at all. A family in Fujairah looking for a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level teacher is not choosing from the people who live within a thirty-minute drive; they are choosing from everyone who can be on a call at 17:30 Gulf Standard Time. The same holds for Physics HL, Economics HL and Arabic A, which are among the hardest Higher Level courses to staff anywhere outside Dubai and Abu Dhabi.

What tuition does not do is create time. No tutor can move an Internal Assessment deadline, sit beside a student in the exam hall, or deliver a two-year Higher Level option in four weeks. Hearing that said out loud in the first conversation is a reasonable test of whoever you are talking to, and it is the opposite of what the thinner end of this market offers.

The honest version of the offer: one free trial lesson, in one subject, arranged before any payment, with the tutor your child has been matched to rather than with a sales desk. If no specialist in that subject and level is free in your slot, that is said at that point rather than after you have paid. Availability transparency is not a feature; it is the minimum.

sections.heading: Twenty-four months, counted backwards from the first paper
paragraphs: The Diploma runs twenty-four months and its assessment is spread across roughly the last fourteen of them. Reading the two years forwards, as a syllabus, hides that completely. Reading them backwards from the first paper of the May session puts every decision in the order a family actually has to take it, and it exposes how early the expensive mistakes get made.

The first third is about gaps rather than content. A student arriving from Cambridge IGCSE, from the MYP, or from a CBSE or American middle school carries a specific deficit, and it is almost always one of three: algebraic fluency for Analysis and Approaches, the structure of an extended written answer, or handling uncertainty in practical science. Closing those in DP1 is cheap. Discovering them in DP2 is not, because by then they compete with coursework for the same evenings.

The middle third is coursework, and that is where the recoverable marks live. The second half of DP1 and the first term of DP2 carry the exploration, the scientific investigations, the Extended Essay drafts and the TOK exhibition. An hour spent on the student's own draft against the published criteria in that window is the highest-value hour available in the whole programme, and also the one with the strictest rules about what a tutor may touch.

The last third is technique. From the mocks onwards almost nothing new should be introduced. Sessions get shorter, more frequent and built around marked questions under time, with an error log the student keeps rather than the tutor. The table below is the version of this plan we send to families who write in asking what they should be doing right now.

sections.heading: The deadlines your child's school sets, not the IB
paragraphs: Almost every deadline that decides a Diploma grade is set by the school. The IB owns the exam session and the upload windows; the coordinator owns the dates your child actually works to, and two campuses in the same emirate will differ by weeks. Ask for the written internal calendar in September of DP1. Most schools keep one, and most families never request it.

The ceilings themselves are published by the IB in each subject guide, and they are the part a tutor can be concrete about. An Extended Essay is a maximum of 4,000 words with a recommended forty hours of student work and a named Extended Essay supervisor inside the school. The TOK essay is a maximum of 1,600 words on one of the prescribed titles the IB releases per session. The TOK exhibition commentary runs to 950 words. The scientific investigation that serves as the Internal Assessment in Biology, Chemistry and Physics is capped at 3,000 words and carries 20% of the subject grade at both levels. The mathematics exploration has a recommended length in pages rather than words. Confirm each against the current guide, because the IB revises them.

Those numbers change how an hour gets used. A 1,600-word essay does not fail on vocabulary; it fails because the argument answers a different question from the prescribed title it was written against. A 3,000-word investigation loses its marks in the evaluation criterion, not the introduction. Knowing where the marks sit is the whole difference between an hour spent proofreading and an hour spent on the thing being assessed.
The table is the reference version. Treat the windows as typical rather than universal, and overwrite them with your own school's dates the moment you have them in writing.

sections.heading: Cambridge and Pearson dates you can put in a calendar today
paragraphs: Most UAE Diploma students sat Cambridge or Pearson IGCSEs two years earlier, and plenty of younger siblings are in that year now. Those two boards publish their dates openly, which makes them the part of the calendar a family can plan against this week rather than guess at.

The pattern is consistent. Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, plus a March series used by some centres. The Cambridge March 2027 series is the clearest worked example of how far ahead entries close: final entries are due 27 November 2026 for an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results released on Direct on 13 May 2027 and certificates in late June.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams run in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables for later series, which is precisely why every date here should be checked against the live official PDF rather than trusted from a tutoring page, this one included.

One Cambridge detail is worth more to a Gulf family than all the rest. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, the board states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and it adds that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. Ask the exams officer which zone your school sits in, then download that version and no other.

sections.heading: Entries, zones and the student nobody entered
paragraphs: An entry is an administrative act performed by a centre, and it is the most expensive thing on this page to get wrong, because missing it does not cost marks. It costs a whole session.

For a student at an IB World School or a Cambridge or Pearson centre in the UAE, the school enters the candidate, selects the components and, in tiered subjects, selects the tier. Three things slip. A subject dropped or added after the entry deadline is the first. Tiering is the second: a Cambridge IGCSE candidate entered for the Core paper cannot be awarded above the Core grade ceiling however well the paper goes, and parents discover that on results day. The third is the practical or alternative-to-practical component in sciences, which has to match the way the school teaches the course.

Families who have left a school, moved mid-cycle, or are educating at home must enter through an approved examination centre themselves. Centres set their own internal deadlines, earlier than the board's, and their own fees. Start that conversation a full term before the published deadline. The later Ministry of Education equivalency file depends on certificates issued in the student's legal name exactly as the passport spells it, so a mismatch caught at entry costs an email and a mismatch caught at attestation costs months.

None of this is tutoring and a tutor who raises it is not selling you anything. It belongs here because the search that brought you to this page is usually made in the same week a parent has worked out that the calendar exists and that nobody walked them through it.

sections.heading: Ramadan, National Day and where the hours actually are
paragraphs: A tuition plan is a statement about a diary, and the UAE diary has a shape that a European or Indian template does not. Mapping it before booking is what stops a four-week block quietly becoming two.

The year opens in late August or early September. Timetables, clubs and school transport settle over the first fortnight, which is the only stretch of the year when a good weekly slot is easy to get. UAE National Day holidays take a week out of early December. Winter break takes roughly three more, and because no new teaching happens across it, those are the strongest coursework weeks in the entire Diploma.

Ramadan is the one that moves. It shifts about eleven days earlier each year, so it has been landing across the mock and pre-exam window rather than a quiet period. School days shorten across the emirates, afternoons are low-energy, and serious study moves to the hours after Iftar. Sessions move with it into post-Iftar sessions, usually shorter and more frequent, agreed in advance instead of cancelled week by week. Eid al-Fitr then removes the last clear revision week before study leave, which is why the fortnight before it is the one to protect.

Summer is a different problem: availability is fine and time zones are not. Families travelling to the UK, India, Pakistan, Jordan or Egypt keep sessions by moving the slot rather than dropping it. One session a fortnight through July and August holds ground that otherwise takes three weeks of September to recover.

sections.heading: Six weeks to the first paper: what still moves
paragraphs: Most people searching for an IB online tutor in the UAE are already inside the last two months. That is late rather than hopeless, and the useful answer is specific: some things move in six weeks and some do not, and knowing which is which decides whether the money does anything.

What moves is technique and recall. Paper timing moves, usually within three timed attempts. Command-term accuracy moves, and it is pure margin: a student who writes a description when the paper asked for an evaluation is losing marks that have nothing to do with knowing the content. Layout marks in calculation subjects move, because method credit is given for the line being shown. The error pattern from the mock moves, if it is logged and attacked rather than merely described.

What does not move is a Higher Level option taught from scratch, a Maths AA Paper 3 topic met for the first time in April, or coursework that has already been submitted. A tutor who agrees to all three inside six weeks is selling hours rather than outcomes, and that is worth noticing before you pay for a block.

The shape of the sessions should change as well as the content. Two short slots a week with a marked paper between them beats one long slot, because the marking is where the learning happens. In the final week, run one session and then stop: at that point sleep and question sequencing are worth more than another topic.

Six weeks is also long enough to fix something administrative, which is often the cheapest available win. Check the entry is correct, check the zone-correct timetable, check which calculator model the subject permits, and check whether the student knows the order in which they intend to attempt the questions in each paper.

sections.heading: Where the marks go missing when revision starts in March
paragraphs: The pattern repeats across cohorts and it is diagnosable per subject, which is why a first session should include a marked past paper rather than a conversation about confidence.

In Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 is the non-calculator paper and it exposes algebraic fragility rather than missing knowledge. At Higher Level the two long papers carry 30% each, Paper 3 carries 20% and the exploration 20%, so a student who has never attempted a full Paper 3 investigation is leaving a fifth of the grade to improvisation. In Applications and Interpretation the loss sits elsewhere: the calculation is right and the sentence interpreting the output in context is missing.

In the sciences, the current model puts Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and the investigation at 20% at both levels, and the marks go missing in the data-based questions of Paper 1B and in the evaluation criterion of the investigation. Chemistry students lose organic marks on notation rather than chemistry. Physics students lose uncertainty marks on arithmetic. Biology students lose marks to command terms, writing one paragraph shape for outline, explain and evaluate alike.

In the essay subjects the failure is structural. Economics students who have not learned to define before explaining lose the cheapest marks on every question, and Higher Level Paper 3 then asks for policy judgement with calculation attached. English A Language and Literature students write about what the text says rather than what the writer chose to do with it, and in the Individual Oral the extract choice has usually decided the grade before the student speaks.
None of that is fixed by more hours. It is fixed by a marked script, a named pattern, and three weeks of attacking that one pattern.

sections.heading: Results, enquiry upon results, and the file that opens afterwards
paragraphs: Results week has its own short calendar, and the windows for doing something about a grade are measured in days. They are owned by the school rather than by the family, which is the detail that catches people out.

If a grade looks wrong, the route is an enquiry upon results, and it is submitted by the school's coordinator rather than by a parent. There is a deadline, it sits close to release, and a fee applies by route. A remark can move a grade down as well as up, so the subject teacher's read of the script matters before anything is submitted. Ask the coordinator in the same week, in writing, and ask what evidence they hold.

The November session exists and a minority of UAE candidates use it, usually to retake one or two subjects. Entries close well before those papers, so the decision belongs in the week after results rather than in September, and it has to be taken alongside the university conversation instead of after it. A deferral request made early reads very differently from one made in late August.

Then the Ministry of Education equivalency file opens, and this is the step UAE families most often meet unprepared. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count of five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. For the American track, mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math and English proficiency is evidenced by IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section. No IB points threshold appears on this page, because we have not read one on the Ministry's own site; ask the Ministry or the emirate's attestation authority directly. Equivalency is a process your family completes through the official channel, and no amount of tutoring is required for it.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the deadline is Friday
paragraphs: The pressure point in the Diploma is predictable. A coursework deadline is three days away, the draft is not working, and the family is at the exact moment when it is most likely to buy something it should not.

What a tutor may do is teach, question and give feedback on work the student has produced. Reading a draft against the published criteria and naming which criterion is underserved is legitimate, and it is most of the value available in that week. Rehearsing a reflection session with the Extended Essay supervisor is legitimate. Teaching the statistics a student needs in order to handle their own data set is legitimate. Marking a timed question and explaining the mark scheme is legitimate.

What a tutor must never do is supply any part of assessed work. Not a paragraph of an Extended Essay, not an analysis section for an investigation, not a rewrite that comes back as prose the student did not author. There are operators in this market selling finished Internal Assessments at four-figure AED prices; one competitor page researched for this project advertised exactly that. Buying one is malpractice under the IB's academic-honesty rules, the student carries the consequence, and the consequence can be the Diploma itself.

Two practical tests for a family. Ask what the tutor will do with a draft: an answer about criteria is a good sign, an answer about improving the writing is not. Then ask whether the student could explain their own method, line by line, in a conversation with their teacher. Every IB coursework component is submitted through the school with authenticity checks attached, and a student who cannot defend their own work has a problem no tutor can fix on the Thursday night.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in the same week
paragraphs: Every private school in the UAE teaches these alongside its licensed international curriculum, which means a Diploma student's week is not six subjects plus the core. Families planning tuition hours routinely leave them out of the arithmetic and then wonder where the evenings went.

The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. In Dubai, KHDA requires these subjects in all private schools regardless of the international curriculum licensed, with its requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The organisation rules are specific and they explain the timetable your child actually has. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and KHDA states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and the guidance advises that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes.

Two constraints follow for tuition. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education in Dubai schools are required to hold appropriate approval from KHDA for those subjects, so ask what a tutor's experience with the mandatory stream actually is. And the use of different or additional content for these subjects without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, which means support here works the school's own material rather than importing a parallel course from elsewhere.

process.title: Tell us the date, then the subject
process.description: Start with what you are working towards: the next internal deadline, the mock window, or the session itself. Add the subject, the level, and the school. Three lines is enough. The date decides what kind of help is worth buying, and it changes the answer more than the subject does.

process.title: We match one specialist, not a shortlist
process.description: You are sent one tutor who teaches that subject at that level, with the reason for the match stated. If nobody is free in your slot for a Higher Level option, you are told that in the same reply rather than offered a near-enough alternative. A near-enough tutor costs a term.

process.title: A free first lesson that produces a plan
process.description: One free trial lesson, in one subject, with the matched tutor, arranged before any payment. It ends with a dated plan: the next deadline, the two weakest topics, the session length and the slot. If the match is wrong, say so and we change it before anything is booked.

process.title: A fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Sessions are booked at the same time each week, in Gulf Standard Time, so they survive the school run and the autumn diary. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video, with the school's scheme of work open. A written note follows each session naming the next target.

process.title: Reviewed at each deadline, not each term
process.description: The plan is checked at the points the calendar sets: after the Internal Assessment deadline, after the mocks, and at six weeks out. That is when session length and frequency change. Reviewing in December because December arrived is how families pay for hours that no longer match the need.

whyPoints.title: Dates before promises
whyPoints.description: The first thing we ask for is the date you are working towards, because it determines whether coursework feedback or paper technique is the right purchase. No tutor on this platform will tell you that six weeks and two years need the same plan, and no one will quote you a grade.

whyPoints.title: Delivered online, said plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, in every emirate. Nobody travels to a UAE address, and we do not pretend otherwise in order to match a search phrase. Home visits are a service we run in India only. In the UAE, online is what reaches a Higher Level specialist from Fujairah.

whyPoints.title: Sources named, numbers dated
whyPoints.description: Every Cambridge and Pearson date on this page comes from the board's own published page, read in October 2026. AED figures quoted anywhere on this site are market rates attributed to whoever published them. Where a figure is not verified, such as an IB session date, it is left off rather than guessed.

whyPoints.title: One specialist per subject and level
whyPoints.description: A Chemistry Higher Level teacher and a Chemistry Standard Level teacher are not interchangeable, and neither covers Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches. Matching is by subject and level, and where a student needs two subjects, that is two tutors rather than one generalist stretched across both.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question and give feedback on the student's own drafts against the published criteria. No part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay is ever supplied by a tutor. This market contains operators who sell finished coursework; that route risks the student's Diploma and we will not compete on it.

whyPoints.title: Honest about coverage
whyPoints.description: Where no UAE-based specialist is free for a niche Higher Level subject, you are told at the point of enquiry, along with what is available instead and how the session would run. A disclosed coverage limit is worth more than a confident silence followed by a mismatched tutor.

faqs.question: When should an IB student in the UAE start working with an online tutor?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families do, and the reason is the coursework calendar rather than the exams. The highest-value window is the second half of DP1 and the first term of DP2, because the mathematics exploration, the scientific investigations, the Extended Essay drafts and the TOK exhibition are all live then, and those marks are banked long before study leave. A student who begins in DP1 is buying feedback on work that still counts. A student who begins in March of DP2 is buying paper technique, which is a genuinely smaller lever. If you are choosing a term, choose the one that contains a deadline.

faqs.question: How late in DP2 can online IB tuition in the UAE still change a predicted grade?
faqs.answer: A predicted grade is formed from the evidence the school holds, mostly the mocks and internal assessments, so it changes when that evidence changes. Realistically, work that lands before the mock still moves the prediction; work that lands after it moves the final result rather than the prediction. Online IB tuition in the UAE started eight to ten weeks before mocks can show up in a predicted grade. Started in April, it is aimed at the paper, not the prediction. Tell the tutor which of the two you are chasing, because the session plans differ completely.

faqs.question: Which IB deadlines are set by my child's school and which by the IB?
faqs.answer: The IB sets the exam session and the windows in which the school must upload candidate work. The school sets everything your child actually experiences as a deadline: when the exploration is due, when the Extended Essay draft is handed to the supervisor, when the TOK essay is collected, when the mocks run. Those dates differ between two campuses in the same emirate, sometimes by several weeks. Ask the Diploma Programme coordinator for the written internal calendar in September of DP1, and plan tuition against that document rather than against anything a tutoring site tells you is typical.

faqs.question: When do Cambridge and Pearson run their exam series?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, plus a March series used by some centres. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. Those are the boards' own published positions, read in October 2026. The IB, by contrast, runs the May session that almost every UAE school sits and a November session used by a minority. We do not print IB dates here because they could not be verified from the IB directly; your coordinator and ibo.org are the sources for those.

faqs.question: Why does the entry deadline fall months before the exam?
faqs.answer: Because entries drive logistics: paper allocation, zone timetables, access arrangements and component choices all have to be fixed before material is printed and shipped. The Cambridge March 2027 series shows the gap clearly. Final entries are due on 27 November 2026 for an exam period that runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027. That is a little over two months between the entry deadline and the first paper, and a subject added after it is simply not sat. If a subject or tier change is under discussion at home, raise it with the exams officer well before the deadline, not after the mock results arrive.

faqs.question: What is a Cambridge exam zone, and why does the timetable version matter?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the timetable. The board states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For a UAE family this is a two-minute task with a very large downside: ask the exams officer which zone your school is in, download that version of the timetable, and work from it alone. Timetables circulating in parent groups are frequently the wrong zone, and a missed paper is not a mark problem.

faqs.question: How does the tuition schedule change during Ramadan and Eid?
faqs.answer: School days shorten across the emirates, afternoons become unproductive, and serious study moves to the hours after Iftar. Sessions move with it: shorter and more frequent, scheduled as post-Iftar sessions and agreed a fortnight in advance rather than cancelled week by week. Ramadan shifts about eleven days earlier each year, which has pushed it into the mock and pre-exam window rather than a quiet part of the year. Eid al-Fitr then removes the last clear revision week before study leave, so the fortnight before it is the one worth protecting with extra sessions rather than the week after.

faqs.question: How many weeks does an Internal Assessment take from idea to final draft?
faqs.answer: Plan on a term rather than a fortnight. A workable sequence is two to three weeks settling a question that can actually be answered with available data, two to three weeks collecting or sourcing that data, two weeks on a first full draft, then a criterion check and a revision pass. Compressing it is where the marks go, because the evaluation criterion rewards reflection that only exists if something went wrong early enough to be discussed. A tutor in that window tests feasibility first and only then reads drafts, which is the opposite order to the one panicking families usually want.

faqs.question: How long does the Extended Essay take, and when should the first reflection session happen?
faqs.answer: The IB recommends around forty hours of student work for an essay of no more than 4,000 words, and schools generally run the first reflection session with the Extended Essay supervisor late in DP1 once a research question exists. Treat that session as the real deadline, because a question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words is the single most common structural failure and it is cheapest to fix before any reading is done. Tutoring here is question feasibility, source quality and rehearsal for the supervisor conversations. The writing is the student's own, start to finish.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the TOK essay without crossing the academic-honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor can unpack the prescribed title, test whether the argument answers that title rather than a neighbouring one, press on the quality of the real-world examples, and point out where the 1,600 words are being spent on description instead of analysis. What a tutor cannot do is supply any of the prose. If feedback comes back as replacement sentences rather than questions and criterion references, that is not teaching, and the student is the one who carries the malpractice risk under the IB's rules, not the tutor.

faqs.question: What happens if a grade looks wrong on results day?
faqs.answer: The route is an enquiry upon results, and the school's coordinator submits it rather than the family. There is a deadline that sits close to release, measured in days, and a fee depending on the route chosen. Before asking for it, ask the subject teacher what the script and the internal evidence suggest, because a remark can move a grade down as well as up. Put the request in writing in the same week, and run the university conversation in parallel rather than waiting for the outcome. Deferral requests made early read very differently from those made in late August.

faqs.question: Is the November session a realistic option after a disappointing May?
faqs.answer: For one or two subjects, often yes. A minority of UAE candidates use the November session as a retake route. The constraints are administrative rather than academic: entries close well before those papers, the school or an approved examination centre has to make them, and a retake has to be agreed with whichever university holds the offer. The decision therefore belongs in the week after results, not September. The teaching plan for a retake looks different too: it starts from the actual script and the enquiry outcome rather than from the syllabus.

faqs.question: When in the final year should we start the Ministry of Education equivalency file?
faqs.answer: Begin gathering documents before results, and open the file as soon as certificates exist. The slow parts are rarely the academic requirements; they are attestation of documents issued in another country and name mismatches between a certificate and a passport. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Levels. Verify your own case with the Ministry or the emirate's attestation authority, because no tutoring platform should be your source for a regulatory process.

faqs.question: Does the MoHRE private tuition work permit apply to an online tutor?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals providing private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you see quoted with suspicion. MoHRE's own service page is the place to check the current position for a tutor resident in the UAE.

faqs.question: How do lessons work if the specialist is not based in the UAE?
faqs.answer: The same way they work if the tutor lives in Dubai: one-to-one over live video, in a slot set to Gulf Standard Time. For niche Higher Level subjects the pool of UAE-resident specialists is genuinely thin outside Dubai and Abu Dhabi, and when nobody local is free we say so at the point of enquiry and tell you where the tutor is working from. What we will not do is present a non-UAE tutor as a local one, or route a UAE family to a foreign phone number without saying what it is.

faqs.question: Can we pause sessions during mocks and the heaviest coursework weeks?
faqs.answer: You can, though it is usually the wrong instinct. Mock fortnight is when a tutor is most useful, because a marked mock script is the best diagnostic available all year and it expires quickly as a teaching tool. The weeks worth pausing are the ones immediately after a major upload, when the student has nothing live to work on. A better default is to change the shape rather than stop: 45 minutes on a marked script during mocks, then back to the normal slot once the results and the feedback are in hand.

faqs.question: Do Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies take time away from Diploma revision?
faqs.answer: They occupy real timetable hours, so yes, and the arithmetic should be done before you book tuition. These subjects are required in UAE private schools regardless of the international curriculum licensed, and in Dubai KHDA sets out how they run: separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a Diploma student that is several periods a week that revision cannot use, which is an argument for planning the weekly tuition slot around them rather than against them.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an exam-year student need, and when should that rise?
faqs.answer: One weekly session per subject through the term is the normal shape, and it should rise at two specific points rather than gradually. The first is the month before a coursework deadline, when a second session a week buys criterion-level feedback on successive drafts. The second is after the mocks, when the useful pattern becomes two shorter slots a week with a marked paper between them. Going to three or four sessions a week in the final fortnight rarely helps, because at that stage the limiting factor is marked practice and sleep rather than contact hours.

ib-online-tutor.closingHeading: Start from the date, then book the hours
ib-online-tutor.closingBody: Send three lines: the subject and level, the school, and the date you are working towards. That might be an Internal Assessment deadline in three weeks, the mock window, or the first paper of the May session. We match one subject specialist at that level, arrange one free trial lesson in that subject before any payment, and if nobody is free in your slot we say so in the same reply. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, in every emirate. Bring the coordinator's internal calendar to the first session if you have it; it is worth more than anything else you could send us.

intro.heading: Private tuition is a regulated arrangement here, not an informal favour
paragraphs: Most families start looking for IB private tuition in the UAE in the week after a report card. The search is usually about one subject, because Chemistry HL has slipped from a 5 to a 4 or Mathematics has stopped making sense. The arrangement you are about to enter, though, has a legal and administrative shape that nobody at the school will walk you through. Knowing that shape before you pay anyone changes the questions you ask, and it changes which providers survive those questions.

Three separate systems meet inside a single private tuition arrangement. The first is federal: private tutoring runs on a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and u.ae states that individuals offering private tutoring without that permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. The second is the emirate. Whoever licensed your child's school, whether that is KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah or the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, also decides what else your child must study, and in two emirates approves the curriculum and the fees as well. The third is the IB itself, whose academic-honesty rules fix how close any tutor may come to an Internal Assessment.

None of that makes private tuition hard to buy. It makes it checkable. A tutor who holds the permit can say so and name the category it was issued under. A provider with premises in Dubai can produce an Educational Services Permit number from the training-institute route. A platform teaching from outside the country can say that in one sentence instead of routing a UAE parent to a foreign dialling code. The providers that fail those three questions tend to be the same ones quoting a price in US dollars and showing a star rating nobody can trace to a countable review.

IB Gram works to one model in the UAE. A parent describes the subject, the level and the deadline; we match one subject specialist; lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Nobody travels to a UAE address, and we state that on every country page we publish, because implying a visit we do not make is the most common misrepresentation in this market. What a Dubai or Sharjah family gets instead is a tutor chosen for the syllabus rather than for the driving distance: a Physics HL specialist who has taught the current assessment model, not whoever happens to cover your community on a Tuesday evening.

The rest of this page is the system, laid out in the order it affects you. Who may legally give private tuition. Who licensed the school. What the Dubai market looks like in numbers. What the market charges by the month. What information you should hand over at enquiry and what you should keep back. Which teaching material may properly change hands. The Ministry subjects that run beside the Diploma. The equivalency file your child will eventually need. And the exam calendar that decides whether tuition is already running or still being arranged.

ib-private-tuition.programmesIntro: IB Gram covers the IB programmes a UAE private school is likely to run. Each one meets the emirate regulator differently, because the licence that permits the programme carries the Ministry-subject requirement with it, and that is usually where a private tuition plan has to make room in an already full week.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units built around six subject areas, with the exhibition in the final year as the first piece of extended independent work a child produces. There are no external exams, so progress is read from the school's own reporting against the learner profile and the unit objectives. Private tuition at this stage is almost always about reading fluency, number sense or written English, and the useful version is short, frequent and tied to the unit the class is on.
programmes.countryNote: In a Dubai private school the Ministry subjects start here, not at secondary. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies sit in the timetable from the primary years, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, so a parent arranging Arabic support needs to know which stream their child is in before anyone quotes an hourly rate.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four published criteria, each marked out of 8, which is why an MYP report reads nothing like an IGCSE one. A student can hold a 6 in a criterion and a 3 in the one next to it, and the average hides the problem. The Personal Project in the final year is the first assessed independent task with a real supervision process attached to it.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP route into DP1 is where UAE families most often arrive at private tuition, because criterion marks do not convert into a predicted Diploma grade and nobody tells a parent that until October of DP1. Two of the three new IB schools opening in Dubai for 2026-27 add more MYP cohorts to an already small specialist pool.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, marked out of 45 points in total. Every subject carries an internally assessed component alongside the written papers, and the internal work is set by the school's own calendar rather than the exam board's. The May session is the one UAE schools sit, with November available for retakes at some centres.
programmes.countryNote: The IB accounted for a 7% share of Dubai's private-school roll in 2024-25, the smallest of the four main curricula in the emirate, which is exactly why a Higher Level specialist is harder to find locally than an A-Level or CBSE one. It is also the programme whose equivalency position a UAE family should check on moe.gov.ae early rather than in Year 13.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller set of DP courses taken alongside a career-related study, with personal and professional skills, service learning, language development and a reflective project making up the core. Students sit the same DP examinations in the subjects they take, so the tuition need is identical in those subjects, with the reflective project needing process supervision rather than teaching.
programmes.countryNote: Far fewer UAE schools are licensed for the CP than for the DP, so check the school's own programme listing with the emirate authority before assuming it is on offer. Where it runs, the career-related study is usually delivered with a local partner institution, and tuition is sensible only in the examined DP subjects.

ib-private-tuition.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects UAE families most often arrange private tuition for, with what each one actually assesses. A request is matched on syllabus and level rather than on a general subject label, because Biology HL and Biology SL sit different papers with different weightings and the hours needed are not the same.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries the whole course. HL adds Paper 3, a long problem-solving paper where marks go to students who cannot sustain an argument over several linked parts. The exploration is marked against criteria A to E for a total of 20 marks, and personal engagement and reflection are where most UAE students lose them.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use, with the graphical calculator expected rather than optional. Students who moved from CBSE or an American system often arrive strong on computation and weak on interpretation, and the marks sit in the interpretation. Check the route against the entry requirements of the universities on your child's list before switching.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields decide the grade, and the HL extensions are where a strong MYP student is most likely to stall. Data analysis is assessed throughout, not only in the internal work, so uncertainty handling and graph treatment need practising weekly rather than revisiting before the mock.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics generate most of the tuition requests we see from UAE families. Marks are lost on precision of language, on failing to state conditions and on treating a multi-step calculation as arithmetic rather than as chemistry with units attached to every stage.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the trap. Students revise breadth and get caught by command terms, because explain, outline and discuss earn different answers from identical knowledge. Statistical treatment of data in the internal work is the other recurring weakness, and it is fixable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation carry the paper marks. The internally assessed commentaries need current articles with real policy content, which is where students stall first, and HL adds a quantitative paper that rewards consistent working rather than memorised definitions.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application separates grades: students who can place a tool against a decision score, and students who describe the tool do not. HL has a longer assessed written task, and the case-study paper needs timed practice because reading the material thoroughly is itself a timed skill.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the written assessments need a line of argument sustained across texts, which is a different skill from the essay writing most UAE schools teach in Year 11. HL adds the essay component, and planning time is the single most useful thing a tutor can impose.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: A language acquisition course, not a literature one, and students placed in it from an EAL background often sit at the wrong level. Productive skills carry the grade, so writing in the specified text types and speaking under timed conditions are where the sessions should go.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Which Arabic course a student sits depends on the stream the school placed them in, and in a Dubai private school that placement follows the KHDA requirement for separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. A tutor has to match the stream and the school's own material rather than importing a parallel course.

ib-private-tuition.regionsTitle: Where your child's school sits, and which authority answers for it
ib-private-tuition.regionsIntro: Private tuition questions change by emirate, because the authority that licensed the school is not the same everywhere and neither is what that authority controls. Lessons reach every emirate the same way, over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so the geography below matters for the paperwork and the school calendar rather than for scheduling.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA oversees private education in the emirate and publishes the mandatory-subject guidance that fixes Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in every private school timetable. It licensed 227 private schools in 2024-25 across 17 curricula, and seven more open for 2026-27.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and sets professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff, including the position on teachers tutoring their own students. It is the one regulator the competing pages in this market never mention.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, with a smaller IB cohort than Abu Dhabi island, which makes a local Higher Level specialist genuinely scarce. Online delivery is the practical answer here rather than a preference, and UAE University admissions requirements are worth reading before subject choices are locked.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education and, unlike KHDA, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A tuition plan built on another emirate's assumptions can therefore miss what the school is actually approved to teach this year.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here sit under the federal Ministry of Education, which u.ae describes as playing a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Parents read the Ministry's general regulations rather than an emirate inspection handbook.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education and, like Sharjah, approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. The emirate appears in none of the competitor pages reviewed for this project, which is a fair indication of how little IB-specific support is marketed here.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Federal Ministry of Education supervision, a small private-school sector and a long drive to the nearest IB specialist. Families here are the clearest case for one-to-one online tuition, since subject match is decided by syllabus rather than by what sits within an hour's drive.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under federal Ministry of Education supervision, with the smallest private-school sector of the seven emirates. Diploma students typically travel to Sharjah or Dubai for school, which pushes any evening tuition slot later than families expect.

schoolClusters.note: The largest IB cluster in the country, and the one where the gap between curricula is most visible. Students we support attend schools across the emirate; a tutor is matched to the syllabus and board the school actually teaches, which is worth confirming from the school rather than assuming from its name.

ADEK-regulated, with a smaller Diploma cohort than Dubai and a correspondingly thinner local specialist pool at Higher Level. Students we support attend schools in both cities, and the practical constraint is usually the school run finishing late rather than tutor availability.

A mixed curriculum picture across SPEA, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and federal Ministry of Education supervision. IB provision is concentrated in a few schools, so families here most often ask for subjects their school cannot staff deeply.

ib-private-tuition.modesIntro: Three shapes of private tuition cover almost every request that reaches us from the UAE. All three run one-to-one over live video, and the choice is really about what the deadline is and whether the problem is teaching, pace or process.

modes.title: A held weekly slot
modes.description: One subject, one tutor, the same time each week, booked against the school's own assessment calendar rather than against a generic syllabus order. This is the version that moves a grade, because it lets a tutor see the same misconception twice and fix the cause instead of the symptom. Most UAE families start with one subject and add a second only once the first is stable.
bullets: Session notes shared after each lesson, in one document per subject
Timed questions set between sessions, marked against published criteria
Slots on Gulf Standard Time, including post-Iftar timing during Ramadan
Paused for school exam weeks rather than paid for and missed

modes.title: A block before a session
modes.description: Three to six weeks of concentrated work when the first paper is close and the diagnosis is already clear. The structure is fixed: a past paper under timed conditions, a marking walkthrough against the published criteria, then targeted teaching on what the paper exposed. It is the most expensive way to buy tuition per point gained, which is a reason to start earlier rather than an argument against it.
bullets: Two or three sessions a week instead of one
Papers sourced from the school or the board's own channel, never a downloadable archive
A written list of the topics that are still costing marks
An agreed stopping point, so the block does not drift into the exam week

modes.title: Coursework process coaching
modes.description: For the Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the Personal Project. The student is the author throughout. The tutor asks questions, points at the criterion wording, explains what a criterion is rewarding and says plainly when a plan will not reach it. Nothing is supplied as text for the student to submit, and the school supervisor stays the authority on the process.
bullets: Criterion wording read together, with the mark allocation stated
Feedback given as questions and as references to the criteria
The student's own supervisor and school deadlines treated as the controlling calendar
A written record of what was discussed, available to the school on request

sections.heading: Who may legally give private tuition in the UAE
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE runs on a permit. The federal government introduced the private tuition work permit through Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae describes it as granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee, gives a two-working-day completion time, and takes applications through the MoHRE smart app, the website and the e-services system. That is the whole official process: a form, no money, two working days. Any provider telling you the paperwork is expensive or slow is describing something else.

Eligibility is broader than most parents expect. u.ae lists teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students among those who may apply. The permit carries a code of conduct, and this is where the detail becomes useful to a parent. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and says the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Confirm the current wording against ADEK's own policy before treating it as settled, but take the direction seriously.

What this leaves you with is a short set of questions, each of which has a specific answer. Which category was the permit issued under, since a university student and a registered schoolteacher are not the same proposition for Higher Level work. Does the employer approval the category requires exist. Does your child's own school employ this person. And treat any provider that uses an authority's name as a credential, without a permit or licence number you can read, as making a claim it has not evidenced. u.ae is explicit that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so anyone quoting you a figure is guessing.

sections.heading: Which authority licensed your child's school, and what else it controls
paragraphs: The u.ae private-schools page sets out the complete map, and it is worth reading once because the competing pages in this market do not. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in that emirate, the Department of Knowledge does the same in Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in the emirates of Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Five bodies, seven emirates.

The difference between them is not cosmetic. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, which means curriculum and fee approval sits with the emirate rather than with the school's head office. A Dubai family reading a KHDA inspection report and a Sharjah family reading an approved curriculum list are looking at different kinds of document, and advice written for one does not transfer cleanly to the other. For the three emirates under federal supervision, the reference point is the Ministry's general regulations rather than an emirate handbook.

Underneath all of it sits one federal rule that explains the mandatory subjects. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That single sentence is why a school licensed for the IB still has Ministry subjects in the timetable, and why those subjects turn up in a tuition conversation that started about Chemistry. Before arranging anything, find out which authority licensed the school, what it publishes, and which of its requirements your child is currently meeting.

sections.heading: Dubai's private-school numbers, and what they do to tutor supply
paragraphs: Dubai's private school sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum on 37% of enrolment, Indian on 26%, American on 14% and the International Baccalaureate on 7%. Those four numbers explain more about the tutoring market than any price list does. The IB is the smallest of the four main curricula in the emirate, so the pool of adults who have taught a current Diploma syllabus is correspondingly small, while the pool marketing itself as able to teach it is not.

The sector is also growing in a direction that matters. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. Three new IB schools means three new sets of Diploma cohorts recruiting from the same thin specialist pool. On the cost side, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

For a parent, the practical consequence is to stop treating subject tutoring as a local search. A family in Al Barsha looking for Mathematics AA Higher Level is not choosing between the specialists in Al Barsha; it is choosing between everyone who can teach that syllabus at a time the family can sit down. That is the whole argument for one-to-one online delivery, and it is why IB Gram matches on syllabus and level rather than on postcode. It also explains why the scarce skills are specific: HL Paper 3 technique and Internal Assessment process coaching, not general subject help.

sections.heading: Private tutor, tuition centre, platform: four arrangements, four obligations
paragraphs: Parents use private tuition to mean any paid help outside school, but the four common arrangements are different legal animals with different things you can ask to see. An individual tutor needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit. A tuition operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which starts with initial approval, allows a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and requires annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. Those are two separate regimes, and a provider that conflates them is worth a second question.

A matching platform is a third thing again. It introduces a tutor and takes responsibility for the match, the records and the replacement when a match fails, and the tutor's own permit position remains the tutor's. The honest version of that model tells you where the tutor is based before you book. The fourth arrangement is school-run support, which sits inside the school's own licence and is usually the cheapest option on the table, though it is group teaching by the staff whose teaching your child has already had.

IB Gram is the third kind, and says so. One-to-one lessons are delivered over live video to families across the UAE, we name the tutor and their location before the first session, and we do not operate premises in the country. Home visits are a service we run only in India. If a provider's answer to where the lessons happen is vague, that vagueness is the answer: in this market the gap between what is advertised and what is delivered usually sits exactly there, alongside a foreign phone number and a price in dollars.
