intro.heading: A primary parent is not buying hours. They are buying timing.
paragraphs: Search for an IB PYP home tutor in the UAE and you will find page after page offering subjects, levels and hourly rates. Almost none of them answer the question a primary parent actually has, which is when. Your child has no entry deadline, no paper one, no results day. The Primary Years Programme is deliberately built that way: it reports against descriptors rather than marks, and it keeps the first externally dated qualification years out of sight. The effect on parents is predictable. Support gets bought in reaction - after a report, after a comment at a conference, three weeks before the Exhibition - rather than in advance of anything.

There is a calendar, though. It is just a school calendar rather than an examinations calendar, and nobody publishes it from a parent's side. A UAE primary year normally opens in late August or early September, breaks for a fortnight around the winter holidays, runs a long second term into the spring, loses teaching days to Ramadan and Eid, and finishes in late June or early July. Schools licensed on an April-start year sit on a different rhythm again. Inside that frame sit the dated items that genuinely matter to a seven-year-old: the first reading assessment, the two parent-teacher conferences, the mid-year benchmark window many schools now run, the portfolio review, and in the final year, Exhibition presentation week.

Reading that calendar forwards tells you when the school will tell you something. Reading it backwards tells you when to act. A child who is a year behind in reading fluency in Grade 2 does not need an emergency in May; they need two short sessions a week from September, when the teaching weeks are intact and the child is not tired. A Grade 5 student heading into the Exhibition does not need a crash course in presentation the week before; they need help with research questions and note-making roughly ten weeks out, while the inquiry can still change shape.

The second thing a primary parent is timing is the exit. The PYP finishes and something external starts: MYP 1 with its criterion marks out of eight, or a British-track Year 7 that leads to Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE entries, or an American-track middle school. Each of those has a real, published deadline somewhere down the line - Cambridge, for instance, took final entries for its March 2027 series on 27 November 2026, months before the papers themselves. A primary parent does not need to meet that deadline. They need to know it exists, because it is the first point at which a date stops being negotiable.

So this page is organised as a calendar rather than a catalogue. It covers what each PYP year produces and when, how to read the Exhibition backwards, which primary-stage assessments in UAE schools carry published windows, how the Ramadan timetable moves the teaching weeks, what the market charges and when families tend to buy, and what the Ministry of Education will eventually ask for at the far end of school. Where IB Gram is concerned the delivery answer is short: one-to-one tuition over live video, anywhere in the Emirates, and no visit to a UAE address.

ib-pyp-home-tutor.programmesIntro: The PYP runs for six or seven years and behaves differently at each end of it. Grouping it by stage, rather than treating it as one block, is what makes a dated plan possible - the Early Years have no assessment worth planning around, and the exit year has one that governs everything.

programmes.name: Early Years of the Primary Years Programme
programmes.ageRange: Ages 3-6 - FS1 to Year 1, or Pre-KG to Grade 1
programmes.description: Inquiry through play, spoken language, phonological awareness and the first idea that a numeral stands for a quantity. Nothing here is assessed in a way a tutor can revise towards, and any provider offering exam technique at this stage is selling something that does not exist. What one-to-one time buys is conversation: an adult who waits for a four-year-old to finish a sentence, names things precisely, and repeats a counting game until the quantity stops needing to be counted.
programmes.countryNote: Early Years rooms in the Emirates are among the most linguistically mixed classrooms anywhere, with children arriving from five or six home languages. A child who is quiet in FS2 is often not behind at all but silent in a second language. The dated items are the two parent conferences, and the useful move is to ask at the first one whether the silence is language or comprehension, before a label is attached to it.

programmes.name: Lower primary - the reading years
programmes.ageRange: Ages 6-8 - Year 2 to Year 3, or Grade 1 to Grade 2
programmes.description: Decoding becomes fluency, fluency becomes comprehension, and number bonds become written method. This is the only window in the whole of school where a reading gap can be closed cheaply, because the gap is still measured in months rather than years. Two short sessions a week through a full term usually does more than a single long weekly hour, because the skill being built is automaticity and automaticity needs frequency.
programmes.countryNote: Most UAE primary schools run a reading assessment in the first weeks of term and again before the mid-year report, which gives a parent two comparable numbers roughly five months apart. Those two numbers are the cheapest diagnostic available in the country and they are free. Ask for the band, the date it was taken and the instrument used, then plan the hours against the gap rather than against the comment on the report.

programmes.name: Middle primary - the written method years
programmes.ageRange: Ages 8-10 - Year 4 to Year 5, or Grade 3 to Grade 4
programmes.description: Fractions, decimals, formal written methods for multiplication and division, comprehension of texts the child cannot fully decode by sight, and the first pieces of extended writing. Marks are not the issue; habits are. A child who still counts on fingers in Grade 4 is not slow, they are carrying an unfinished job from Grade 2, and that job takes about a term of short, regular sessions to finish properly.
programmes.countryNote: A majority of UAE international primaries now sit a standardised benchmark test in a mid-year window, often January, and report the result as a standardised score alongside the descriptors. That window is the natural point to start or stop paid support, because it produces the only comparable number of the year. Booking hours in September and reviewing them against the January result is a cleaner plan than reacting to the June report.

programmes.name: The exit year and the Exhibition
programmes.description: One extended, student-directed inquiry presented to an audience, plus the transition into criterion-marked work. The Exhibition is the first time a child owns a piece of work end to end: the question, the research, the evidence, the structure and the delivery. It is also the first point where adult help can tip from teaching into doing, which is why the boundary is worth settling in writing before the first session.
programmes.countryNote: Exhibition presentation week is set by your school, not by the IB, and in most UAE schools it falls in the second half of the year, which puts the research phase squarely across the Ramadan weeks in several years of the cycle. Ask the PYP coordinator for the presentation date in September rather than in March. It is the one primary date worth writing into a family calendar twelve months ahead.

ib-pyp-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Primary subjects are worth choosing by the dated milestone they feed rather than by the label on the report. Each of the areas below is tied to something that happens at a known point in the UAE school year, which is what makes it possible to say how many weeks of support it needs.

subjects.name: Reading fluency
subjects.description: Words read correctly per minute, and whether the child can still answer a question about what they read. UAE schools test this early in term one, which gives a start point. Fluency responds to frequency rather than to session length, so two twenty-five minute slots beat one long hour.

subjects.name: Reading comprehension
subjects.description: Inference, retrieval and sequencing - the three things benchmark tests in UAE primaries weight most heavily. A child who decodes well and still scores low is almost always losing marks on inference, which is taught by talking about texts rather than by reading more of them.

subjects.name: Writing: sentence to paragraph
subjects.description: Sentence boundaries, tense consistency, then paragraphing. The mid-year report is where this surfaces, because teachers describe it in prose rather than scoring it. Bring a piece of your child's unedited writing to a first session; it says more than any assessment summary.

subjects.name: English as an additional language
subjects.description: Academic vocabulary rather than conversational English. A child fluent in the playground can still miss the language of instruction - compare, justify, in order to. This is the single most common reason a bright primary child in the Emirates reads as underperforming on a benchmark test.

subjects.name: Number sense and mental calculation
subjects.description: Number bonds, place value and recall. Unfinished recall in Grade 2 reappears as slow written method in Grade 4 and as fraction confusion in Grade 5. It is the cheapest gap to close and the most expensive to leave, and it closes in about a term of short regular sessions.

subjects.name: Fractions, decimals and percentages
subjects.description: The point where UAE primary maths stops being arithmetic. Equivalence is the actual obstacle, not procedure. This is the topic most likely to be flagged in a January benchmark score and the one most often still unresolved at MYP 1, where it immediately costs criterion marks.

subjects.name: Measurement, shape and data handling
subjects.description: Reading scales, converting units and interpreting a graph someone else drew. Data handling is where the PYP and the MYP overlap most directly, so time spent here in Grade 5 pays off inside the first term of MYP 1 rather than years later.

subjects.name: Science skills inside the units of inquiry
subjects.description: Fair testing, variables, recording and drawing a conclusion the evidence supports. PYP science is not a syllabus to be revised, so support is about method. The same method is what MYP criterion B and C ask for, under different names.

subjects.name: Research and note-making
subjects.description: Turning a broad interest into an answerable question, finding two sources that disagree, and taking notes that are not transcription. This is the work of the ten weeks before Exhibition presentation week and it is the part most often skipped in favour of making the slides look finished.

subjects.name: Speaking to an audience
subjects.description: Pace, eye contact, handling a question the student did not expect, and finishing inside the time allowed. Rehearsal with an adult who interrupts with questions is worth more than a dozen silent run-throughs, and three or four sessions in the fortnight before presentation week are usually enough.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Script, high-frequency vocabulary and the sentence patterns the ministry framework uses. Dubai private schools must timetable this regardless of the licensed curriculum, and the material comes from the approved framework, so support means practice and consolidation rather than a parallel course.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first language
subjects.description: A separate stream with separate expectations. KHDA requires schools to teach Arab and non-Arab groups in separate classes for Arabic as a first language, so a child's stream is set by the school and support must match the stream rather than the year group.

subjects.name: Islamic Education
subjects.description: Taught in Standard Arabic for the Arab stream and in the school's curriculum language for non-Arab students. Teachers of this subject need approval from KHDA to teach it, which is a useful question to ask of anyone offering primary support in the subject.

subjects.name: Self-management and the homework hour
subjects.description: Not a subject on any report, and frequently the actual problem. Where the bag is packed, when the homework happens, how long before a break - a fortnight of structure here often removes the need for subject support altogether, which is the honest answer in more primary cases than providers admit.

ib-pyp-home-tutor.regionsTitle: The emirates, read as calendars rather than as catchment areas
ib-pyp-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Delivery is identical across the country, because every lesson runs over live video. What changes by emirate is the regulator behind your child's school, the shape of the term dates, and the hour of the evening at which a primary child is still able to learn anything.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The deepest primary IB pool in the country, regulated by KHDA, which also publishes the mandatory-subject framework in the most detail. The competitive hour here is the one straight after the school bus, roughly 4pm to 5.30pm, and it books out first in term one rather than in the spring.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of children enrolled at their own school, so a primary tutor here is by design somebody from outside the classroom. Khalifa City and Yas commutes push sessions past 5pm.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a smaller set of primary IB schools and a longer drive between them. Online delivery removes the geography problem entirely: an Al Ain family gets the same reading specialist as a family on Reem Island, at the same hour, without anyone counting kilometres on a Tuesday evening.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves curricula, programmes and assessment methods as well as fees. Families commuting to Dubai schools often run the whole primary week on Sharjah term dates and Dubai traffic, which makes a fixed post-dinner slot more reliable than an after-school one.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here answer to the federal Ministry of Education rather than to an emirate authority. The practical consequence for a primary plan is a shorter list of local specialists and a stronger case for video delivery, particularly for Arabic as an additional language at the lower primary stages.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah, approves curricula and assessment methods rather than only inspecting. RAK primary families often sit outside any local tutoring market at all, which is exactly the gap a dated online plan fills.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under the federal Ministry of Education. The east coast has almost no primary IB tutoring market, and a request for a Grade 4 fractions specialist is not a request a local network can fill. Live video is not a compromise here; it is the only version that exists.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised federally by the Ministry of Education. Term dates follow the federal calendar, which matters during Ramadan, when the school day shortens and the only usable teaching block for a primary child moves to the hour after Iftar.

schoolClusters.note: These schools run the PYP at primary level and set their own Exhibition presentation weeks, their own benchmark windows and their own conference dates. Two schools three kilometres apart can differ by a month on all three, which is why a plan is built from your school's calendar rather than from a generic one.

ADEK-regulated primaries, where the professional-ethics position on staff tutoring their own students is the clearest in the country. Conference and report dates here tend to sit a fortnight off the Dubai pattern, so a family moving between the two emirates mid-year inherits a different calendar as well as a different regulator.

A short list, long distances between them, and in several cases the nearest alternative primary IB school is in another emirate. Families here are the ones for whom the travel arithmetic in the comparison table below decides the question on its own.

ib-pyp-home-tutor.modesIntro: Primary support works best when the shape of the booking matches the point in the year. Four shapes cover almost every primary request we see, and the difference between them is a calendar difference rather than a price difference.

modes.title: The term-time weekly anchor
modes.description: One or two short sessions a week, held at the same hour, running for a full term and reviewed against the next dated item - a reading check, a benchmark window, a report. This is the default for a reading or number gap at lower primary, because the skill being built needs frequency rather than duration and a primary child's attention does not survive a long evening hour.
bullets: Twenty-five to forty-five minutes, matched to the child's age rather than to a standard hour
Same slot each week so it survives the school run and bedtime
Reviewed at the next dated school assessment, not at a random four-week mark
Short written note to the parent after each session, not a monthly report

modes.title: A dated block before Exhibition week
modes.description: A fixed number of sessions counted backwards from your school's Exhibition presentation date, starting at roughly ten weeks out and ending with rehearsal in the final fortnight. The sequence is research question, sources, notes, structure, then delivery. Booked this way the block has a finish line, which is the main reason primary families do not drift into paying for support that has stopped having a purpose.
bullets: Ten weeks out: narrowing the question into something answerable
Six weeks out: two sources that disagree, and notes that are not transcription
Three weeks out: structure, and cutting what does not answer the question
Final fortnight: rehearsal with interruptions and a timed run

modes.title: Holiday blocks: winter, spring and summer
modes.description: Intensive short blocks in the breaks, when the school is not setting work and the child is not tired. The winter fortnight and the first two weeks of the summer are the two most productive windows in the UAE primary year for closing a reading or number gap, because sessions can run in the morning rather than at the end of a school day.
bullets: Morning slots, which no term-time plan can offer a primary child
Daily or alternate-day frequency for two to three weeks
Best used for automaticity work - recall, fluency, written method
Finishes before term restarts, so it does not become an open-ended commitment

modes.title: The exit bridge into MYP 1
modes.description: A short run of sessions across the final term of Grade 5 and the first weeks of MYP 1, aimed at the one real change: work starts being marked against criteria out of eight instead of described against descriptors. Students who understand what criterion B is asking for before the first graded task lose far less time in term one of MYP 1.

sections.heading: A PYP child has no exam date, and that is the whole planning problem
paragraphs: Search volume for an IB PYP home tutor in the UAE is driven almost entirely by two moments: a report landing, and the Exhibition appearing on a school newsletter. Neither of those is a good moment to start. By the time a report says a child is working towards expectations, the term that produced the judgement is already over, and by the time Exhibition week is on a newsletter the inquiry is usually half-built. The Primary Years Programme has no external examination, no entry deadline and no results day, so the planning signals a secondary parent takes for granted are simply absent.

What exists instead is a thin set of dated items, most of which schools publish but parents rarely collect in one place. Early Years has two parent conferences and a portfolio. Lower primary adds a reading assessment, usually sat in the first weeks of term one and again before the mid-year report. Middle primary adds a standardised benchmark window, commonly in January. The exit year adds the one date that genuinely cannot move, Exhibition presentation week, which the school sets rather than the IB.

Collecting those dates is a ten-minute job and it changes what support costs, because it converts an open-ended worry into a finite block. A reading gap identified against a September assessment can be worked on for a term and re-measured in January against the same instrument. A fractions gap flagged by a January benchmark has a full second term in front of it. An Exhibition has ten usable weeks before presentation if the question is settled early, and two if it is not. None of that is visible from a report comment on its own.

The table below is the version of the PYP that a parent can actually plan against: what each year produces, the one item in it that carries a date, and the thing paid hours are usefully spent on in that year. It is deliberately not a list of subjects. At primary level the year matters more than the subject, because the same reading gap costs about a term of short sessions in Grade 2 and most of a school year in Grade 5.

sections.heading: The UAE primary year counted in weeks that can actually be taught
paragraphs: A UAE school year looks like forty weeks on paper and behaves like rather fewer. Term one opens in late August or early September and the first fortnight is settling rather than teaching. A fortnight disappears around the winter break. Ramadan shortens the school day for several weeks, and the days either side of Eid and of National Day are effectively gone. Add the examination and assessment weeks the school itself runs and the number of weeks in which a primary child can absorb new work steadily sits closer to thirty.

That arithmetic matters because primary gaps close by repetition, not by intensity. A child who needs two short sessions a week for a term needs about twenty-four of them. There are only two or three places in a UAE year where twenty-four consecutive useful weeks exist, and all of them start in September or early January. A plan that starts in April is not a smaller version of the same plan; it is a different plan, with different aims, and it should be sold as such.

The second thing the arithmetic changes is pricing behaviour. Primary demand in the Emirates peaks twice - the fortnight after term one reports and the month before Exhibition week - and both peaks sit in the parts of the year with the fewest usable weeks left. Families who book in September buy the same number of hours into a far better calendar. Nothing about the hourly rate changes; the weeks do.

Schools licensed on an April-start academic year, of which the Emirates has a number, invert the whole table. Their long teaching block runs from April through the summer, their mid-year sits in the autumn, and KHDA's own mandatory-subject requirements were set to apply from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, which for those schools meant April 2026. If your child's school starts in April, read every window below shifted by roughly seven months.

sections.heading: The Exhibition, read backwards from presentation week
paragraphs: The PYP Exhibition is the only hard deadline in the Primary Years Programme and it is the one piece of primary work most parents misjudge. The misjudgement is consistent: families treat it as a presentation, and so they ask for help in the fortnight before presentation week, when the only thing left to change is the slides. The Exhibition is a piece of research. The marks that exist in it, and more importantly the learning in it, are won eight to ten weeks earlier, at the point where a vague interest becomes an answerable question.

Each school sets its own presentation week and its own internal checkpoints, and the IB sets neither. That is why the first thing to do in September of the exit year, not in February, is ask the PYP coordinator for the presentation date and the school's internal milestone dates. With that date in hand the whole block becomes countable, and a parent can see immediately whether the ten useful weeks fall before or across Ramadan - in several years of the cycle they fall across it, which is the single biggest practical constraint on Exhibition planning in the Emirates.

The boundary question matters more here than anywhere else in primary school, because the Exhibition is the first piece of work a child owns outright. A tutor may teach research method, ask questions that expose a weak argument, model note-making on a different topic, and rehearse the delivery. A tutor may not choose the question, find the sources, write the notes, structure the argument or edit the student's text into something the student could not have written. That line is not a formality; it is the habit that keeps the same child out of trouble six years later when an Internal Assessment carries real marks.

Read backwards, the block has a natural shape, and the table below is the version we work to. The weeks are approximate because schools differ, but the order does not change: question, sources, notes, structure, delivery. Families who start at week ten rarely need the fortnight of emergency sessions. Families who start at week two almost always do, and there is a limit to what those sessions can honestly achieve.

sections.heading: Checkpoint, not examinations: the dated primary assessments some UAE schools run
paragraphs: Parents often assume the first externally dated assessment in a child's life is an IGCSE or a Diploma paper. For a number of UAE primary children it arrives much earlier, because many schools in the Emirates run Cambridge Primary or Cambridge Lower Secondary alongside or instead of a wholly school-based programme, and those come with published test windows. Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Those are real, published windows with real administrative deadlines behind them.

This matters to a PYP family in two situations. The first is a transfer: a child moving from a PYP school to a Cambridge primary curriculum mid-year may walk into a Checkpoint window a few weeks later. The second is a mixed-provision school, of which the Emirates has several, where the primary years carry Cambridge assessment even though the school is also an IB World School at another stage. In both cases the family suddenly has a date, and the date behaves like a date - the school enters candidates, and entries close well before the tests are sat.

The broader lesson is about how to tell a sourced date from a guess. Cambridge publishes its series dates and makes a point of the fact that every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and that the correct zone timetable must be used - it says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an examination after the wrong version was read. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them. Any page that gives you an IB examination date without naming the source is guessing, and we will not do it here: IB session and results dates should be confirmed with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org before anything is planned around them.

For the overwhelming majority of PYP families none of these dates apply yet. The point of knowing them is that they are the first examples of a kind of deadline the PYP does not contain, and the habit of asking who set a date, where it is published and when it was last revised is one worth acquiring at primary level rather than in Year 11.

sections.heading: The first deadline that binds is an entry deadline, not an examination
paragraphs: Ask a parent of a Grade 3 child when their first unmovable educational deadline is and most will say the first public examination, years away. That is the wrong answer. The first thing that genuinely cannot be moved is an entry deadline, and entry deadlines sit months in front of the papers they belong to. Cambridge's March 2027 series is the clean worked example: the examination period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, but final entries were due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades on 27 February 2027, results on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June.

Three months separate the entry deadline from the first paper in that series. A family that discovers in January that their child was never entered has no remedy, and the school holds the entry rather than the parent. This is the mechanism a primary parent should understand years early, because it is the only part of the system where attention, not ability, is what determines the outcome.

Pearson behaves similarly on a different rhythm. Its International GCSE papers are available in a May or June series and a November series each year; the November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables for future series and revises them, so the live official timetable is the only version worth planning against.

sections.heading: Grade 5 into MYP 1, planned across twelve months instead of one August
paragraphs: The move out of the PYP is the largest change in a primary child's school life and it is almost always handled in the last fortnight of the summer holiday. The reason is understandable - nothing in the exit year forces the question. The consequence is that students meet criterion-marked work for the first time in week three of MYP 1, discover that a six out of eight is a good mark rather than a 75 per cent, and spend a term recalibrating while the content moves on without them.

The change is narrow enough to prepare for properly. PYP work is described against descriptors; MYP work is marked against four criteria, each out of eight, in every subject group. A student who has seen what criterion B asks for, and who understands that the four criteria are not weighted equally in every task, loses far less time. None of that needs a year of tuition. It needs a handful of sessions in the final term of Grade 5 and two or three in the first weeks of MYP 1, which is why we sell it as a bridge rather than as a course.

The academic gaps that actually cost criterion marks in MYP 1 are predictable and short: equivalence between fractions, decimals and percentages; reading a graph somebody else drew; writing a conclusion that refers to the evidence; and taking notes that are not transcription. Each of those is a PYP skill with an MYP name. Working on them in Grade 5, where they are familiar, is cheaper and calmer than meeting them again in MYP 1 under an unfamiliar mark scheme.

The table reads the exit year backwards from the first day of MYP 1. It is not a tuition schedule - most of the rows are conversations with the school rather than paid hours. That is intentional. Several of the most useful moves in the exit year cost nothing, and a page that pretends otherwise is selling rather than advising.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and the date the rule started biting
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies whatever international curriculum it is licensed for, and KHDA's own guidance set a date for the current requirements: they were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For a primary parent that date is the reason the subjects may look different from the way an older sibling experienced them.

The detail that most changes a primary week is the arithmetic. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time in a 40-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary the length of a lesson provided the total weekly time is still met, and the guidance advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. So a primary timetable can legitimately deliver the same weekly total as three longer lessons or five shorter ones, and the version your school chose changes when in the day your child is doing Arabic - and therefore what a late-afternoon tuition session is competing with.

Two further rules shape what support can honestly look like. Classes for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies must be organised separately for Arab and non-Arab students, and combined classes for both groups are not permitted, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic are required to hold the relevant approval from KHDA. And for the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is not allowed, which means credible primary support here is consolidation and practice of the approved material rather than a parallel syllabus of somebody's invention.

The practical reading of all this for a primary family is simple enough. If your child's difficulty is Arabic script or vocabulary, short frequent sessions on the school's own material work. If the difficulty is that Arabic sits at the end of a long day and nothing is going in, the fix is the timetable rather than a tutor, and that is a conversation with the school.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and National Day: where the primary hours actually are
paragraphs: Ramadan moves earlier in the Gregorian calendar each year, which means that over a primary child's time in the PYP it travels across the whole second half of the school year. In some years it sits well before Exhibition season and in others it lands directly on top of the research weeks. Planning a primary year without checking where it falls is the most common scheduling mistake families and providers make in the Emirates.

The school day shortens during Ramadan and homework loads generally come down with it. For a fasting older child that is a straightforward adjustment, but primary children are mostly not fasting, and what actually changes for them is the household rhythm: later dinners, later bedtimes, and a long flat stretch in the late afternoon when nothing useful is going to be learned. The workable slot for a primary child in Ramadan is normally the hour after Iftar, and sessions should be shorter rather than longer. Thirty focused minutes after Iftar is worth more than a sixty-minute slot at five o'clock that the child sleeps through.

The content should change too. Ramadan weeks are poor weeks for introducing anything new and good weeks for consolidation - recall practice, reading aloud, going back over written methods that are nearly secure. A plan that treats the Ramadan block as a pause in new content and a push on automaticity comes out of it ahead, whereas a plan that tries to keep the September pace loses the fortnight after Eid as well.

Two other dates eat primary teaching weeks quietly. Eid itself takes several days plus the travel either side, and the UAE National Day period at the start of December removes days from the end of the long first block, usually in the week families had mentally reserved for catching up before term one reports. Both are published a year ahead on the federal calendar. Marking them in September is the difference between a plan with thirty usable weeks and a plan that assumed forty and quietly fails in March.

sections.heading: Reports, conferences and portfolios: what to ask for, and when
paragraphs: The PYP reports in prose, which is a strength educationally and a problem practically, because prose does not tell a parent how far behind their child is. A report that says a child is working towards expectations in reading is describing a judgement, not a measurement, and the measurement nearly always exists somewhere in the school. Asking for it is the highest-value ten minutes of the primary year.

At the first conference of the year, usually in the autumn, three questions get you most of what you need: which reading instrument the school uses and what the band means in months or years; whether a standardised benchmark is sat and in which window; and whether the teacher's concern is comprehension, language or attention, because those three have different remedies and only one of them is helped by subject tuition. Ask for the date each number was taken, not just the number. A reading age from April is a different thing from a reading age from September.

At the mid-year conference the useful question is comparative. You now have two dated points on the same instrument, so the question is whether the gap is closing, holding or widening, and the answer determines whether hours continue, change shape or stop. This is also the point to ask what the January benchmark score was in standardised terms, because a standardised score is comparable across years in a way a report descriptor is not.

The portfolio is worth more attention than it usually gets. It is the only place where a parent can see the trajectory of their child's own work rather than somebody's summary of it. Two pieces of unedited writing six months apart will tell you more about progress in writing than any report paragraph, and they are the most useful thing a parent can bring to a first tutoring session. Where a provider offers a diagnostic assessment of its own instead, ask what it adds to the two dated school measurements you already have for nothing.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges for primary one-to-one, and when families buy
paragraphs: Primary tutoring in the Emirates is priced far less transparently than secondary tutoring, partly because providers are reluctant to publish a rate for an eight-year-old that sits close to the rate for a Diploma student. The figures below are the ones providers have themselves published, read in October 2026, and they are the market rather than IB Gram's price list. Where a band is attributed it is attributed because that provider printed it.

At the lower end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, both online and both generally staffed by university students at that price. A qualified subject tutor working online sits higher: Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. A tutor travelling to the address costs more, because the travel is inside the rate - Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and the wider home-tutor market runs to AED 500. Specialist and examiner-experienced tutors run from AED 200 to 450 and above, with BartyED at AED 650 at the top. Monthly packages in the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four in-home two-hour sessions.

Two things about those numbers are specific to primary. The first is that the rate is poorly correlated with what a primary child needs, because what a seven-year-old needs is frequency and patience rather than subject depth, and frequency is the thing the top of the market is least set up to deliver. The second is that session length should come down rather than up at primary age, which means an hourly rate is the wrong unit of comparison - two twenty-five minute sessions a week is a different purchase from one sixty-minute session, and it is usually the better one.

The timing column in the table is the part no competitor publishes. Primary demand in the Emirates is concentrated in two short windows, and both of them are late in the calendar. Booking the same hours in September does not reduce the rate, but it does buy a far better set of weeks to spend them in, which is the only discount actually available at primary level.

sections.heading: A tutor travelling to a UAE address against one-to-one live video, on a dated plan
paragraphs: The phrase parents type is home tutor, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a redirection. A visiting tutor for a primary child in the Emirates has genuine advantages: a young child is often more settled with an adult in the room, a parent can see what is happening, and nothing depends on a connection. The costs are equally real. The travel is inside the rate, the pool is limited to whoever can reach your community at the hour you need, and the hour you need is the contested one.

That last point is where the primary case differs from the secondary one. A primary session has to happen early - after the school bus and before a child stops being able to concentrate, roughly between four and six in the evening. A visiting tutor can serve one family in that window, maybe two if they live close together. Which means the visiting market around any given community is not a market of specialists; it is a market of whoever is nearby at five o'clock. For a Grade 4 fractions gap that may be fine. For Arabic as an additional language in Fujairah, or research coaching before an Exhibition, it frequently is not.

IB Gram's answer is one-to-one tuition over live video, into every emirate, timed to Gulf Standard Time. Visiting tutors are a service we run in India and not in the Emirates, and we would rather say that in the second paragraph of a page than in the small print of a contract. What the online model buys for a primary family is the thing a dated plan actually needs: the same tutor in the same slot for a whole term, two short sessions rather than one long one because nobody is driving, a recording or written note after each session, and a specialist chosen for the gap rather than for the postcode.

The comparison below is framed on what a dated primary plan needs, because that is the honest basis for the decision. It is not framed on effectiveness in the abstract, which neither model can prove, and we have not put a number on anything we cannot source.

sections.heading: Academic honesty starts in Grade 5, not in Year 12
paragraphs: There is a market in the Emirates for completed coursework. At least one site ranking for IB terms sells finished Internal Assessments outright, at a four-figure dirham price. A primary parent will not meet that market for years, but the habits that make a family vulnerable to it are formed much earlier, in the week an Exhibition is due and a child is nowhere near finished.

The Exhibition is where the boundary is first tested, because it is the first piece of work a primary child owns from question to delivery. The permissible help is substantial and worth paying for: teaching research method, asking the questions that expose a weak claim, modelling note-making on a different topic, showing a child how to tell a source that disagrees with them from a source that is simply wrong, and rehearsing a presentation with interruptions. What is not permissible is anyone else choosing the question, gathering the sources, taking the notes, structuring the argument or editing the student's words into something they could not have written themselves.

That line is drawn the same way in everything that follows. An IB tutor may teach the skills an Internal Assessment needs and give feedback on a student's own draft; an IB tutor may not produce it. A tutor may teach the structure of an Extended Essay and ask why a conclusion does not follow; a tutor may not write it. Any provider offering the other version is offering the student an outcome that can be taken away from them later, and a primary parent who has already settled the Exhibition boundary is far better placed to recognise that offer when it arrives.

Our own position is published rather than implied. Tutors working through IB Gram teach, question, model and give feedback on the student's own work. We do not produce assessed work, we do not supply board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads - those belong to the boards and should be read on their own sites - and we do not describe a tutor as an examiner for any board without evidence of current status.

sections.heading: The Ministry file opens years later, and the habit starts now
paragraphs: At the end of school, a UAE family that wants a local university place generally needs the Ministry of Education to recognise the qualification their child holds. For the British track the requirements are published and specific: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five required subjects. One provider ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates need six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five.

For the American track, English proficiency can be shown by a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics by at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB Diploma there is no figure published in this project, because none could be read on a Ministry source. Anyone quoting you an IB points threshold for equivalency should be asked where it is published, and the answer should be a Ministry page rather than a tutoring site.

A Grade 2 parent does not need any of this. What they need is the habit it implies, which is to keep the paperwork as it is generated rather than reconstructing it at eighteen. Reports, certificates, transfer certificates and attested documents from a school a family has already left are far harder to obtain afterwards, and families who move between emirates or countries mid-primary are the ones who find that out the expensive way. Equivalency is also not a service any tutoring provider performs, guarantees or should charge for - it runs through the Ministry and the emirate attestation authority, and nothing about it requires tutoring.

The table sets out what each track has to show, with the IB row marked honestly as unpublished here. It is in a primary-level page for one reason: it is the far end of the calendar this whole page is built on, and it is the only part of it where a document from Grade 5 can still matter.

process.title: Send us the dates, not just the worry
process.description: The school's term dates, the conference dates, the benchmark window and - in Grade 5 - the Exhibition presentation week. Four dates and a sentence about what is going wrong is enough for us to say honestly whether paid hours are the right answer and when they should start.

process.title: Bring the two numbers the school already has
process.description: A reading band or standardised score with the date it was taken, and a piece of your child's unedited writing. Those cost nothing, they exist in almost every UAE primary, and they tell a tutor more in five minutes than a paid diagnostic does in an hour.

process.title: A free first lesson, one per family
process.description: One introductory one-to-one session at no charge, before any payment is taken and with no card required. For a primary child it is as much about whether the child will talk to this adult as about the subject. If the answer is no, we try a different tutor rather than asking you to persist.

process.title: A dated block, with a finish line
process.description: We write the plan as a number of sessions ending at a specific school date - the January benchmark, the mid-year conference, Exhibition presentation week. Open-ended primary tuition is how families end up paying for months after the gap closed.

process.title: Review against the school's next measurement
process.description: Not against our own assessment. When the next dated school number arrives we compare it to the one we started from and decide together whether to continue, change shape or stop. Stopping is a legitimate outcome and we will say so when it is the right one.

process.title: If no specialist is free, we say so
process.description: For narrow primary requests - Arabic as a first language at lower primary, for instance - the right tutor is sometimes not available for the slot you need. We will tell you that and offer a waiting list rather than putting a generalist in front of your child and charging for it.

whyPoints.title: The plan is dated, not open-ended
whyPoints.description: Every primary plan we write ends at a date your school set: a benchmark window, a conference, a presentation week. It makes the hours countable in advance and it makes stopping a normal decision rather than an awkward conversation.

whyPoints.title: Session length is set by the child's age
whyPoints.description: Twenty-five to forty-five minutes for primary, twice a week rather than once, because fluency and recall build on frequency. No travel is involved, so splitting a weekly hour into two costs nothing extra in time.

whyPoints.title: Delivery is stated on the page, not in the small print
whyPoints.description: One-to-one lessons over live video into every emirate, timed to Gulf Standard Time. Visiting tutors are a service IB Gram runs in India only. You will not find a promise of a doorstep visit anywhere on this site for a UAE address.

whyPoints.title: Figures are attributed or absent
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page belongs to the provider that published it, read in October 2026. We publish no satisfaction percentage, no star rating and no IB examination date, because none of those could be sourced to a standard we would want quoted back at us.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary is published
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question, model and give feedback on the student's own work. They do not produce Exhibitions, Internal Assessments or essays, and they do not supply board papers or mark schemes as downloads. At primary level that boundary is a habit being taught, not a legal formality.

whyPoints.title: No regulator is claimed as a sponsor
whyPoints.description: KHDA, ADEK, SPEA and the federal Ministry of Education are described on this page because they shape your child's school. None of them approves, accredits or endorses IB Gram, and any provider telling you a regulator has approved its individual tutors is describing something that does not exist.

faqs.question: Does an IB PYP home tutor in the UAE actually come to the villa, or is the lesson on video?
faqs.answer: The lesson is on video. IB Gram delivers one-to-one PYP tuition over live video into every emirate, timed to Gulf Standard Time, and visiting tutors are a service we run in India rather than in the Emirates. We use the phrase home tutor because it is what parents search for, and the honest translation is a tutor who works with your child at home over a screen. For a primary child the practical gain is that one weekly hour becomes two shorter sessions, since nobody is paying for a drive across Dubai between families at five in the evening.

faqs.question: There is no PYP examination, so what is there to plan a tutoring calendar around?
faqs.answer: Four things, all of which your school already publishes. The reading assessment in the first weeks of term one. The two parent-teacher conferences. The standardised benchmark window most UAE primaries run, commonly in January. And in the final year, Exhibition presentation week. Those are the dated items a primary plan is built from. Collecting them takes one email to the class teacher, and it converts an open-ended worry into a finite block of sessions with a review point. Without them, support gets bought in reaction to a report comment, which is the most expensive way to buy it.

faqs.question: When in the UAE school year should primary support actually start?
faqs.answer: September, in most cases. A UAE primary year contains roughly thirty genuinely teachable weeks once the settling fortnight, the winter break, Ramadan, Eid and the school's own assessment weeks are taken out, and the longest uninterrupted run of them is the block from September to mid-December. A reading or number gap needs about twenty-four short sessions, and there are only two points in the year where twenty-four useful weeks still exist. Starting in April is not a shorter version of the same plan; it is a different plan with narrower aims, and it should be described that way.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the PYP Exhibition should we bring in a tutor?
faqs.answer: About ten, counted back from your school's presentation week. The sequence that works is question at ten weeks, sources at eight, notes at six, structure at four, rehearsal in the last fortnight. Families who come to us two weeks out are asking for help with slides, which is the only thing still movable at that point and the least valuable. Ask the PYP coordinator for the presentation date in September rather than February - it is set by the school, not by the IB, and in several years of the cycle the research weeks land across Ramadan.

faqs.question: What is the Cambridge Primary Checkpoint and when is it sat?
faqs.answer: It is an external test at the end of the Cambridge primary stage, and Cambridge publishes test series in March, May and October each year, with Lower Secondary Checkpoint on the same windows. Several UAE schools run Cambridge primary provision alongside or instead of a purely school-based programme, so some PYP families meet it on transfer. The school enters candidates and the entry closes well before the tests are sat. If your child's school runs it, ask which series and which administrative zone timetable applies, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones.

faqs.question: My daughter is in Grade 3. How far away is her first externally dated examination?
faqs.answer: Between one and five years, depending entirely on the pathway. If her school runs Cambridge primary provision she may meet a Checkpoint series within a year or two. If she stays in the MYP, the first externally marked qualification is years away and the MYP's own assessment is largely school-based before that. If she moves to a British track, the first binding date is a Year 11 entry deadline. The useful thing to know now is that the date which actually cannot move is an entry deadline, not an examination, and that the school submits it rather than the parent.

faqs.question: Which deadline does a Grade 5 family really need in the diary?
faqs.answer: Exhibition presentation week, and nothing else. It is the only hard date in the Primary Years Programme and your school sets it, so it is not published anywhere you could look it up. Everything else in the exit year arranges itself around it: the research block sits in the ten weeks before, rehearsal in the final fortnight, and the MYP transition conversations before and after. The second date worth having is the first graded task in MYP 1, which usually arrives within six weeks of the new year starting and is where criterion marking first becomes real.

faqs.question: Does the Primary Years Programme produce a certificate the Ministry of Education will attest later?
faqs.answer: No. The PYP produces school reports, a portfolio and an Exhibition, not an externally awarded qualification, so there is nothing from the primary years for an attestation authority to act on. What matters later is the school-leaving qualification: the published British-track rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. Verify any requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority, because no tutoring provider performs or guarantees equivalency.

faqs.question: How does the shortened Ramadan school day change a primary tutoring slot?
faqs.answer: It moves it later and makes it shorter. Primary children are mostly not fasting, but the household rhythm shifts: later dinners, later bedtimes, and a flat stretch in the late afternoon when very little is going in. The slot that works is the hour after Iftar, at thirty focused minutes rather than sixty. Content should change too - Ramadan weeks are poor weeks for new material and good ones for consolidation, so recall practice, reading aloud and revisiting written methods that are nearly secure. Ramadan moves earlier each year, so check where it falls before planning a term.

faqs.question: What should we ask for at the first parent-teacher conference of the year?
faqs.answer: Three things, with dates attached. Which reading instrument the school uses and what the band means in months or years behind. Whether a standardised benchmark is sat, and in which window. And whether the teacher's concern is comprehension, language or attention, because those have different remedies and only one of them is helped by subject tuition. Ask when each number was taken - a reading age from April is a different thing from one taken in September. Those answers are free, they exist in almost every UAE primary, and they are better than any paid diagnostic.

faqs.question: How much does primary one-to-one tuition cost per hour in the UAE market?
faqs.answer: Published rates read in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45 to 650 an hour. EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52 online; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150; Bestimate's Dubai table puts a tutor travelling to the address at AED 180-350, with the wider home market to AED 500; specialists run AED 200-450 and above, and BartyED at AED 650. Those are other providers' figures, not ours. At primary level the hourly rate is also the wrong unit - two twenty-five minute sessions a week is a different purchase from one long hour.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to book primary hours in September than in May?
faqs.answer: The rate does not change. The weeks do, and at primary level the weeks are what you are buying. September buys the longest uninterrupted teaching block in the UAE year, roughly twelve or thirteen weeks before the winter break, with a child who is not yet tired and a school that is still introducing new content. May buys the tail end of a year, with reports written and attention gone. Primary demand in the Emirates peaks after term one reports and again before Exhibition season, which means most families buy in the two windows with the fewest usable weeks left.

faqs.question: When did Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies become compulsory in Dubai primary timetables?
faqs.answer: The subjects have long been required, but KHDA's current requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. That date is why the subjects may look different from an older sibling's experience. KHDA counts instructional time in a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length as long as the weekly total is met, and advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Arab and non-Arab groups must also be taught in separate classes for these subjects.

faqs.question: Our move from Dubai to Abu Dhabi happens in January. How should that change the primary plan?
faqs.answer: Expect three changes. The regulator changes from KHDA to ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi. The calendar changes, because conference and report dates in Abu Dhabi schools often sit a fortnight off the Dubai pattern, and your child may arrive after the benchmark window has passed. And the paperwork matters more than families expect: reports and transfer documents from a school you have left are harder to get afterwards, so collect them before the move rather than after. Online tuition itself continues unchanged in the same slot.

faqs.question: Is a parent allowed to help with the PYP Exhibition, and where does that help stop?
faqs.answer: Helping is expected; doing is not. A parent can talk through whether a question is answerable, drive a child to a library, listen to a rehearsal and ask awkward questions. A parent should not choose the question, find the sources, take the notes, structure the argument or tidy the writing into something the child could not have produced. The Exhibition is the first piece of work a primary child owns end to end, and the boundary set here is the same one that governs Internal Assessments and Extended Essays years later. Settling it early is worth more than the marks involved.

faqs.question: What happens if no primary specialist is free for the slot we want?
faqs.answer: We say so and offer a waiting list. Narrow primary requests are the ones most likely to run out of coverage - Arabic as a first language at lower primary, for instance, or Islamic Education for the Arab stream, where KHDA also requires school teachers of those subjects to hold approval from the authority. The alternative on offer across this market is a generalist put in front of a seven-year-old at a specialist rate, which we would rather not do. We will also tell you honestly when the useful answer is a timetable conversation with the school instead of paid hours.

faqs.question: Does a tutor teaching my eight-year-old over video need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-based. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its app, website or e-services. Anyone providing private lessons without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

faqs.question: If we only have twelve weeks before the summer break, what can realistically change?
faqs.answer: Automaticity, and little else. Twelve weeks of two short sessions is about twenty-four sessions, which is enough to move reading fluency, number bonds or a written method from shaky to secure, because those respond to frequency. It is not enough to change comprehension or extended writing, which develop over years rather than terms. The honest plan for a short run is to pick one measurable thing, work on it daily or near-daily, and hand the summer a child who no longer has to think about it. Then start the next block in September, where the long weeks are.

ib-pyp-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start with four dates, not with an hourly rate
ib-pyp-home-tutor.closingBody: Send us your school's term dates, the two conference dates, the benchmark window and - if your child is in the exit year - Exhibition presentation week. We will tell you honestly whether paid hours are the right answer for the gap you are describing, when they should start, how many of them the calendar can usefully hold, and which school date they should be reviewed against. The first one-to-one lesson is free, one per family, with no payment taken and no card required beforehand. Lessons run over live video into every emirate, at a time that survives the school run and bedtime, and nobody is sent to a UAE address.

intro.heading: Nobody prices primary tuition, so start with the hour
paragraphs: Search for an IB PYP tutor in the UAE and you will find agency pages that name a price for the Diploma, mention the Primary Years Programme in one line, and move on. That is not an accident. Secondary tuition sells itself on a number: a grade, a paper weighting, a university offer. Primary tuition has none of those, so the people selling it fall back on adjectives. A parent is then asked to pay AED 200 an hour on faith, for a child who cannot report back on what happened in the lesson.

This page takes the opposite approach. It starts with the hour as a unit, publishes what UAE providers advertise for primary work, and sets out what should be inside a 45-minute session, minute by minute, so you can check afterwards whether you got it. Every AED figure here was read from another provider's own page or from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table in October 2026. None of them is an IB Gram price. We quote after the trial lesson, once somebody has actually met the child and knows whether thirty minutes twice a week beats forty-five minutes once.

The PYP changes the arithmetic in a way parents are rarely told. There is no external IB examination in the Primary Years Programme, no grade boundary to chase and no internal assessment to supervise. What a tutor is working on instead is narrow and measurable: decoding, reading fluency, number fact recall, handwriting stamina, written sentence structure, and the English of a child who is learning the language of instruction at the same time as the content. Those things respond to short, frequent, well-aimed sessions. They respond badly to a sixty-minute block at the end of a long school day.

The UAE adds a second layer that no generic primary tutoring page covers. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA's own guidelines require separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, specify the language of instruction for each group, and prohibit any different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission. A family budgeting for primary tuition is usually budgeting for two different things: the PYP subject groups, and an Arabic stream that may be the real reason the reports look uneven.

The scale is worth holding in mind while you read the numbers. Dubai alone had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with IB programmes accounting for 7% of enrolment and UK curriculum schools 37%. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for 2026-27, and Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them running International Baccalaureate programmes, creating 16,846 new places. More PYP classrooms are opening than there are PYP-experienced teachers living within driving distance of them. That single fact is why IB PYP tutor searches in the UAE increasingly end in a live video lesson rather than a car journey.
