ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are IB Diploma and MYP specialists who teach UAE students online each week. Each one lists the subjects and levels they examine at, the syllabus they teach from, and the hours they hold open on Gulf Standard Time. Read the level before the biography.

intro.heading: Nobody publishes the price, so here it is
paragraphs: Ask six UAE tutoring providers what an IB tutor costs and three of them will not answer. We fetched and read the pages ranking for this search in October 2026: half publish no figure at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, a currency no family in Dubai or Abu Dhabi pays a tutor in. One competitor's own frequently-asked-questions block poses the question and then declines to answer it. That silence is not modesty. It is how a quote of AED 400 an hour gets accepted by a parent who had no way of knowing AED 220 would have bought the same lesson.

So this page starts with the number. IB tuition rates in AED, across the UAE, split by tier and format, with the provider who publishes each band named beside it. Market rates for a qualified subject specialist teaching online run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour. An IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist sits closer to AED 200 to AED 450. An in-home one-to-one visit, once the tutor's travel is priced in, runs AED 180 to AED 500. A named examiner at the premium end has been advertised at AED 650. Those are market figures from published competitor pages and from Bestimate's Dubai rate survey, not IB Gram's price list.

Once you can see the bands, the useful question changes. It stops being how much and becomes what moves the number. Six things do, and only two of them are about the tutor's seniority: the level your child sits at, how scarce that subject is in the UAE, how close the May session is, whether the hour includes travel, how long each session runs, and whether you are buying teaching or marking. A Maths AA HL tutor costs more than a Maths AI SL tutor for a reason that shows up in the assessment structure, not in a biography.

The second half of the value question is what the hour defends. A Diploma grade is built from components with fixed weightings: the Internal Assessment is 20% of the final mark in Mathematics and in each of the sciences, and 20% at Higher Level in Economics. Paper 3 carries 20% of the HL Mathematics grade and 30% of HL Economics. Those percentages are what you are paying to protect, and they are the reason a cheap generalist hour and an expensive specialist hour are not the same product even when the clock runs the same length.

IB Gram sells one format in the UAE: one-to-one tuition delivered live online, over video, with screen sharing and a shared whiteboard. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the Emirates; home visits are a service we run only in India. That is a deliberate choice rather than a limitation, and the comparison table further down makes the case in cost-per-contact-hour terms. A family in Al Reem Island gets the Chemistry HL specialist who matches their syllabus rather than whichever qualified teacher happens to live inside a thirty-minute drive at 4pm.

Everything below is organised the way a budget decision actually gets made: the rate, what drives it, what a year totals, where the money gets wasted, and what the assessment structure means for which hours are worth buying. The regulators, the MoE equivalency paperwork, the academic-honesty boundary and the Ramadan scheduling question all carry a cost implication too, and each gets its own section rather than a footnote.

ib-tutor.programmesIntro: The IB runs as four separate programmes, and the price of help differs sharply between them because the assessment load does. A PYP parent is usually buying confidence and English fluency; a DP parent is buying defence of fixed component weightings under a hard deadline. Here is how each sits in the UAE, and what it costs to support.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary enquiry with no external examinations, assessed through the exhibition in the final year. There is no syllabus to revise and no paper to practise, so tutoring here is diagnostic: reading fluency, number sense, written expression and the habit of explaining reasoning aloud. Sessions are short, usually 40 to 45 minutes, because attention rather than content is the constraint.
programmes.countryNote: UAE PYP families pay the lowest rates in this market, commonly in the AED 100-200 band for an online specialist, because no examination expertise is being bought. The pressure point is the Year 6 transition into MYP, where English and maths expectations rise faster than most reports suggest. KHDA-inspected schools in Dubai publish their PYP outcomes in inspection reports, which is a free diagnostic most parents never read.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria per subject, each scored 0-8, with eAssessment available in the final year. Criterion-referenced marking is where MYP students lose ground: a strong answer written against the wrong criterion scores badly. Tutoring works best when it is spent decoding command terms and criterion wording rather than re-teaching content the student already holds.
programmes.countryNote: MYP is the cheapest point in the UAE to fix a problem and the one families most often skip. Market rates sit around AED 150-250 an hour online. Arriving at Year 11 with weak algebra and then buying AED 400 Diploma hours to repair it is the single most expensive sequence in this market. Several Dubai and Sharjah schools run MYP alongside IGCSE, so check which route your child is actually on before booking.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across three Higher Levels and three Standard Levels, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Points run to 45, with the core contributing up to 3. Every subject carries an Internal Assessment with published criteria and fixed weightings, and Higher Level adds a third paper in several subjects. This is where specialist rates are justified and where generalist hours stop working.
programmes.countryNote: DP help is the most expensive tier in the UAE, commonly AED 200-450 an hour online for a subject specialist, rising at the premium end where named examiners have been advertised at AED 650. UAE schools sit the May session almost universally, so demand and rates both tighten from January. Entries close with the IB in mid-November, which is the last comfortable point to change a subject or a level without cost.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: DP courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project, a language component and personal and professional skills. Students take fewer DP subjects, so each one carries more weight in a university application. The reflective project needs the same supervision discipline as an Extended Essay and is frequently left unsupported because schools are still building expertise around it.
programmes.countryNote: CP is thinly offered in the UAE, which makes specialist help scarce and therefore priced closer to the DP band than the subject load alone would suggest. Scarcity is the driver, not difficulty. CP students heading for UAE universities should check equivalency requirements with the Ministry of Education early, because the certificate structure is less familiar to admissions offices than a full Diploma.

ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: Not every IB subject costs the same to support, and the reason is supply rather than difficulty. A subject taught in forty UAE schools has a deep local tutor pool and competitive rates. A subject taught in four has neither. Below are the subjects UAE families book most, with what each assesses and why it prices where it does.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator. HL adds Paper 3, worth 20% of the grade, built from extended problem-solving on unfamiliar contexts. A Maths AA HL tutor is the most requested and most expensive single booking in the UAE market, and the one where a generalist hour visibly fails.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use, with graphical calculator work in every paper. SL AI is the most commonly mis-chosen course in the UAE because some engineering and economics programmes expect AA. The route decision is worth more than several tutoring hours and should be made in Year 11, not in Year 12.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and the scientific investigation at 20%. Organic mechanisms and energetics generate most of the UAE demand. HL and SL sit the same paper structure, so the premium on an HL tutor reflects the extra content depth and the higher expectation on the investigation, not a different assessment shape.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Same 36/44/20 split as Chemistry. Marks disappear in the data-based section of Paper 1 and in uncertainty handling, which is a skill rather than a topic and therefore teachable quickly. Physics HL tutors are scarcer in the UAE than Chemistry HL tutors, and rates reflect that.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Concept-led syllabus assessed across the same three components, with extended-response questions in Paper 2 that reward precise terminology. Biology is well supplied in the UAE, so it is usually the cheapest science hour to buy. Most students need command-term discipline rather than more content.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three Internal Assessment commentaries of 800 words each, marked against five criteria worth 14 marks apiece. The IA is 30% of the SL grade and 20% at HL, where Paper 3 adds a further 30%. Diagram accuracy and key-concept linkage are where UAE students lose marks most predictably.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, the Individual Oral, and at HL a 1,200 to 1,500 word HL Essay worth 20%. Many UAE students are strong readers in English as an additional language and still underperform on Paper 1 because unseen analysis under time is a separate skill from comprehension.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with a pre-released case for Paper 1 and an Internal Assessment built on a real organisation. Well supplied across the UAE and therefore mid-priced. The common failure is description where the criteria ask for evaluation, which is a writing habit fixable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Programming, abstract data structures and the solution-development Internal Assessment. Offered in relatively few UAE schools, which makes the local tutor pool shallow and the rates firm. Online matching is the only practical route to a tutor who has examined the current syllabus at HL.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Arabic runs as a language A or language B inside the Diploma for many UAE students while also satisfying Ministry of Education requirements. The two roles pull in different directions, and families frequently discover the mismatch late. Specialist help is thinly advertised relative to demand across all seven emirates.

ib-tutor.regionsTitle: Emirate by emirate: what the market charges where you live
ib-tutor.regionsIntro: Rates are not uniform across the UAE, and the variation is driven by tutor supply rather than by family income. Dubai has the deepest pool and the widest spread. The northern emirates have the thinnest, which is where online matching changes the available price most sharply. Here is how each one sits.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The deepest tutor supply and the widest rate spread in the country, from AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 for a named examiner. KHDA inspects the private schools here and publishes band ratings you can read before booking anything.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK regulates private schools in the capital and in Al Ain. Supply is good for mainstream Diploma subjects and thin for HL sciences and Computer Science. Island commutes push in-home visits into longer, more expensive blocks, which is why families on Saadiyat and Al Reem move online first.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: SPEA is the regulator, and the IB school count is far smaller than Dubai's. Families often commute across the Dubai border for school, so a 4pm session is unrealistic and a 6.30pm start is normal. Local specialist supply at HL is limited, so rates hold firmer than Dubai's despite lower demand.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK. A smaller, more settled school market with very few IB Diploma options, which means almost no local HL subject specialists. Online is not a convenience here; it is usually the only way to reach a tutor who has taught the current syllabus.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Schools fall under the federal Ministry of Education. Ajman Academy anchors the small IB presence. The local private-tuition market is priced below Dubai's but offers very little choice at Diploma level, so families accept a generalist or look outside the emirate.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Federal Ministry of Education oversight, with RAK Academy carrying most of the IB demand. No competitor page in this market mentions Ras Al Khaimah at all, which tells you how thin the advertised supply is. Rates are negotiable; qualified availability is not.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: East coast, federal Ministry of Education oversight, and effectively no advertised IB tutoring market. Families here are the clearest case for online delivery: the realistic alternative is a tutor driving across the Hajar mountains, priced accordingly, or no tutor at all.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: The smallest private-school market in the country and another federal Ministry of Education emirate. Diploma-level demand is low in absolute terms and nearly impossible to match locally, so the whole cost comparison collapses into online or nothing.

schoolClusters.note: The largest concentration of IB World Schools in the country and the reason Dubai sets the national rate. Most of these schools sit the May session, publish KHDA inspection outcomes, and set their own Internal Assessment deadlines in the autumn term of Year 13.

ADEK-regulated, with a smaller IB footprint than Dubai and noticeably less local supply at Higher Level. Island and Khalifa City commutes are the practical reason capital families book evening sessions rather than afternoon ones.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.note: SPEA regulates Sharjah; Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain fall under the federal Ministry of Education. A handful of schools carry nearly all the IB demand in this cluster, which is why local specialist rates do not fall even where household budgets are tighter.

ib-tutor.modesIntro: Four booking patterns cover almost every UAE family, and they differ in cost by a factor of ten across a year. Choosing the pattern matters more than negotiating the hourly rate, because the pattern decides how many hours you buy. All four are delivered one-to-one and live online.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one
modes.description: One hour a week on a fixed slot, running with the school term. Across a UAE academic year that is roughly 36 sessions, not 52, once half-terms, Eid holidays, exam weeks and the summer break are removed. This is the cheapest sustainable pattern and the right default for a single SL subject that is slipping rather than failing.

sections.heading: What an IB tutor actually costs in the UAE
paragraphs: The table below is the thing this market will not publish. Every band in it comes from a provider's own page or from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring rate survey, and the provider is named beside the figure. These are market rates across the UAE, not IB Gram's prices. We quote per family after a free trial lesson, because a Maths AA HL booking in Year 13 and a PYP reading booking are not the same product and a single headline rate would mislead on both.

Read the table as a supply map rather than a quality ladder. The budget tier is mostly university students and non-specialist graduates teaching online, and it genuinely works for homework supervision and PYP confidence. The qualified-specialist tier is where IB-specific knowledge begins: someone who has taught the current syllabus, knows what the markscheme rewards, and can tell you which paper your child is losing marks in. The premium tier buys examining experience, and it is worth paying for in a narrow set of cases rather than as a default.

The in-home row deserves attention because it is the one most UAE families start from. An in-home hour in Dubai runs AED 180 to AED 500, and the top of that band is not a better teacher. It is the same teacher with a Sheikh Zayed Road commute priced into your lesson. A tutor who can fit three visits into an evening charges differently from one who can fit five online sessions into the same evening, and that arithmetic lands in your invoice rather than theirs.

Two figures circulating in this market should be treated carefully. Monthly packages are advertised at AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, which work out to very different hourly equivalents, so convert before comparing. And the private tutor permit issued through MoHRE is free of charge across every regulatory source we checked, so a quote carrying a permit or licensing fee is carrying a line item that does not exist.

sections.heading: The six things that move the hourly rate
paragraphs: Level comes first. Higher Level costs more than Standard Level everywhere in this market, and the premium is structural rather than snobbery. HL Mathematics adds Paper 3, worth 20% of the grade, built from extended problem-solving on contexts the student has not seen. HL Economics adds a Paper 3 worth 30%. HL English replaces part of the Paper 2 weighting with a 1,200 to 1,500 word HL Essay. A tutor who can teach those components is a smaller population than one who can teach the SL course, and small populations price firmly.

Scarcity comes second, and it is the factor families underestimate most. Biology is taught in dozens of UAE schools and the tutor pool is deep, so a Biology SL hour is competitively priced. Computer Science HL is offered in relatively few, so the pool is shallow and the rate holds. The same applies to Arabic A at Diploma level and to Theory of Knowledge supervision. Scarcity has nothing to do with how hard a subject is to learn and everything to do with how hard it is to staff.

Timing is third. UAE schools sit the May session almost universally, so demand across the country rises from January and peaks in March and April. Specialists fill their Gulf Standard Time evening slots first, and a family arriving in March is choosing from what is left at the price it is left at. The same tutor, the same subject, the same hour, booked in September, is both cheaper and available at a better time of day.

Format, duration and purpose finish the list. An in-home hour prices the commute; an online hour does not. A 90-minute session usually carries a lower effective hourly rate than a 60-minute one because the tutor's setup cost is spread further. And buying marking is cheaper than buying teaching: a criterion-by-criterion read of an Internal Assessment draft is a shorter, more concentrated piece of work than teaching a topic from scratch, and should be priced that way.

sections.heading: One-to-one online against the UAE in-home market
paragraphs: Home tutoring is the phrase UAE parents search, so it deserves a straight answer rather than a redirect. A private tutor arriving at a Dubai or Abu Dhabi address is a real and widely sold service. It costs AED 180 to AED 500 an hour in the Dubai market according to Bestimate's survey and the home-tutor listings we read. It removes the need for your child to manage a video call. It also means the tutor pool shrinks to whoever is willing to drive to your area at the hour you need, and it means you are paying for a car on Al Khail Road.

IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one online tuition instead, and the choice is not a cost-saving dressed as a philosophy. The constraint that matters at Diploma level is matching: a Chemistry HL student needs a Chemistry HL teacher who knows the current scientific investigation criteria, and there may be very few of those within a thirty-minute drive of Khalifa City or Victory Heights. Online removes the drive from the equation entirely, which widens the pool from one neighbourhood to the whole roster. Home visits are a service we run only in India.

The table compares the two honestly, including where in-home wins. Younger students who need physical presence and supervision do better face to face, and a family with unreliable home connectivity should weigh that seriously. For Diploma subjects at Higher Level, where the specific specialism is the whole point, online one-to-one wins on cost per contact hour, on pool depth and on scheduling flexibility, and it wins by enough that the comparison is not close.

One practical note on effectiveness, since it is the question behind the question. A well-run online lesson is not a video call with a textbook on screen. It is a shared whiteboard, a past paper annotated live, a markscheme opened beside the student's own answer, and a recording the student can revisit. Those four things are harder to do at a dining table than on a screen, which is why the format comparison does not run the way most parents expect.

sections.heading: What a full year of IB tuition adds up to
paragraphs: Hourly rates mislead because nobody buys one hour. The number that matters is the annual total, and it depends almost entirely on the pattern you choose rather than on the rate you negotiate. The table converts the market bands into the four patterns UAE families actually book, using the number of sessions a UAE academic year really contains once Eid holidays, half-terms, school examination weeks and the summer break are taken out. That figure is about 36 weekly sessions, not 52, and using 52 overstates a year's cost by nearly a third.

The spread in that table is the entire argument of this page. A weekly SL subject at the qualified-tutor rate and a twice-weekly HL commitment at the specialist rate differ by a factor of roughly four. Both are reasonable purchases. They are reasonable for different children in different years, and a family that books the second when the first would have done has not bought better teaching, only more of it. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, which lines up with the annual arithmetic here.

Notice how cheaply the Internal Assessment block comes in. Six hours of criterion-referenced feedback spread across the IA cycle costs less than two months of a twice-weekly HL commitment and defends a component worth 20% of the final grade in Mathematics and in each science. For families who want one high-value intervention rather than a standing arrangement, that is the one to buy. It is also the pattern that most often gets skipped, because it does not feel like tutoring.

A last point on package pricing. Advertised monthly bundles in this market, AED 799 for eight online sessions or AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, are easier to compare once you divide. The first is roughly AED 100 an hour. The second is roughly AED 200 to AED 225 an hour. Those are very different products at very different prices, and the monthly headline hides it. Divide before you decide.

sections.heading: Where UAE families waste tutoring money
paragraphs: The most common waste is buying the wrong level of tutor. A capable graduate at AED 120 an hour can rebuild Year 10 algebra very effectively, and cannot teach Paper 3 of Maths AA HL. A specialist at AED 400 can teach Paper 3 and is an expensive way to supervise homework. Families routinely buy the second for the first job, pay four times over, and conclude that tutoring does not work. Match the tier to the task and the same budget covers more ground.

The second waste is starting without a diagnosis. A student who is losing marks because of command-term misreading needs a different intervention from one who has a genuine content gap in energetics, and the two look identical on a report card. One free trial lesson spent on a recent paper, with the markscheme open beside it, will usually identify which. Buying twenty hours before anyone has read the student's actual script is how families end up re-teaching topics the student already knew.

The third waste is group classes bought for an individual problem. Group tuition is genuinely cheaper per hour and genuinely useful for shared content delivery. It cannot address one student's specific pattern of lost marks, because the pattern is specific. Paying a lower hourly rate for an intervention that does not touch the actual problem is the most expensive form of saving in this market.

The fourth is timing, and it compounds all three. Help bought in September is cheaper, better scheduled and spread across enough weeks to change habits. The same spend compressed into April buys the leftover slots at the tight end of the market and arrives too late for anything except past-paper drill. If your child's Year 12 report was weak, the expensive month to act is not this one. It is the one four months before the May session, when every family in the UAE reaches the same conclusion at the same time.

sections.heading: HL and SL weightings: what the money is defending
paragraphs: Every hour you buy is defending a component with a fixed percentage attached to it, and the percentages are public. Families who know them spend differently from families who do not, because the arithmetic tells you where an hour pays back. A student two marks below a boundary in a component worth 44% of the grade is in a different situation from one struggling with a component worth 20%, and no amount of general revision resolves that distinction.

The table sets out the component structure for the subjects UAE families book most. Two patterns are worth noticing. First, Higher Level does not simply mean more content; in several subjects it means an additional paper with its own technique, and Paper 3 is the component students most often meet unprepared. Second, the Internal Assessment is a large, early, controllable chunk of the grade in almost every subject, and it is marked against published criteria months before any examination. It is the most predictable marks on the page.

That second point drives a specific recommendation. If your budget allows one intervention rather than a year of sessions, put it on the Internal Assessment, early, with the criteria open. A 20% component assessed against four or five named criteria, with a draft deadline set by your own school, is the single most improvable part of a Diploma grade. Papers sat in May under timed conditions are not nearly as responsive to a late spend.

One caution about grade boundaries. Boundaries move between sessions, and no tutor can tell you how many marks a 7 will need in next May's Chemistry paper. Anyone quoting a precise target mark for a future session is guessing. What a tutor can do is tell you which components your child is currently losing marks in and roughly what those marks are worth, which is a more useful thing to know and the honest version of the same conversation.

sections.heading: Internal Assessment criteria, letter by letter
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market names a single Internal Assessment criterion, which is remarkable given that the IA is 20% of the grade in most Diploma subjects and the criteria are published. Students lose IA marks for structural reasons, not mysterious ones: a reflection section that describes instead of evaluating, a research design with no stated control of variables, an Economics commentary without a labelled diagram. Each of those is a named criterion with a known mark allocation.

The table lists the criteria and marks for the components UAE families most often ask about. Mathematics runs to 20 marks across five criteria, and criterion E, use of mathematics, carries 6 of them, which is why a sophisticated topic poorly executed scores worse than a modest topic handled precisely. The sciences run to 24 marks across four criteria of 6 each, so evaluation is worth exactly as much as data analysis, and it is the one students leave until the last evening.

Read the right-hand column as a cost argument. Every item in it is a fixable, specific, teachable thing, and most of them are fixable in a single session of criterion-referenced feedback. That is why the six-hour IA clinic appears so cheap in the annual cost table relative to what it protects. A student who understands that reflection is worth 3 marks in Mathematics and that it must evaluate rather than narrate will write a different final section without needing anyone to write it for them.

Word and page limits belong in the same conversation, because exceeding them costs marks for nothing. The Extended Essay is capped at 4,000 words. The TOK essay runs to 1,600. Each Economics commentary is 800 words. The English HL Essay sits between 1,200 and 1,500. Mathematics IAs are guided toward 12 to 20 pages. These are not stylistic suggestions, and a student who discovers them in the final week loses time they could have spent on criterion E.

sections.heading: Why the same help costs more in February than in September
paragraphs: The UAE runs on the May session. A handful of students sit November, usually retakes or students who have moved between hemispheres, but the overwhelming majority of Diploma candidates in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah sit in May, which means the entire country's tutoring demand follows one calendar. That single fact has a price consequence most families meet only when they try to book.

Counted backwards, the year looks like this. Schools close their May-session entries with the IB in mid-November, which is the last comfortable point to change a subject or drop from HL to SL without administrative cost. Internal Assessment drafts are due on dates each school sets for itself, typically across the autumn and early spring of Year 13. Examinations run through May. Results arrive in early July, and November-session results in the first days of January. Universities in the UAE and abroad work to their own deadlines inside that window.

The pricing pattern follows directly. September and October are the loose part of the market: specialists have open Gulf Standard Time evening slots, families are not yet competing, and a weekly arrangement bought now has 30 or more sessions ahead of it. From January the same roster fills, the good evening slots go first, and what remains in March is the leftover inventory at the tight end of the band. Nothing about the teaching changes. The availability does, and availability is what sets the price.

Ramadan sits inside this and is worth planning for rather than working around. Sessions move comfortably to post-Iftar timing, and many UAE families find the late-evening slots are the most productive of their year because the house is quiet and the school day has been shortened. The error is leaving the conversation until the week Ramadan begins, by which point the post-Iftar slots are the most contested hours on the whole roster.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Studies and UAE Social Studies: the line nobody budgets for
paragraphs: Families budget for Maths HL and Chemistry HL and then discover a different problem entirely. Private schools in the UAE teach Ministry of Education subjects alongside the international curriculum: Arabic for both native and non-native speakers, Islamic Studies for Muslim students, and UAE Social Studies. These sit outside the Diploma points total for most students, which is exactly why they get neglected, and they still appear on school reports and still affect progression.

The tutoring market reflects that neglect. Competitor pages in this cluster barely mention Arabic at all, and the advertised supply of specialist Arabic help is thin relative to the number of UAE families who need it. That imbalance means rates for genuinely qualified Arabic support do not sit at the bottom of the market the way the subject's absence from marketing copy might suggest. Scarcity prices the same way here as it does in Computer Science HL.

The complication for Diploma families is that Arabic can occupy two roles simultaneously. A student may take Arabic A or Arabic B as a Diploma language, scoring toward the 45 points, while the same subject also sits in the school's Ministry of Education provision. Those two purposes pull in different directions, and a tutor who is strong on one is not automatically strong on the other. Ask which role you are buying support for before agreeing a rate, because the answer determines who is the right tutor.

A practical sequencing note. Non-native Arabic learners who start in Year 11 or Year 12 are usually trying to compress several years of language exposure into a short window, which is slow and therefore expensive. The same support bought in MYP, when there is no examination pressure attached, costs less per hour and far less in total. This is the clearest case in the whole UAE market for spending early rather than spending more.

sections.heading: What a tutor may not do, at any price
paragraphs: There is a line in IB assessment that money does not move, and families deserve to know exactly where it sits. A tutor may teach content, explain criteria, model technique on a different problem, ask questions about a draft, and give written feedback against the published criteria. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite, edit or supply any part of an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a TOK essay or any other assessed coursework. The student authors every word that is submitted.

This is not a cautious house rule. The IB requires candidates to authenticate their own work and treats a breach as malpractice, with consequences that fall on the student rather than on whoever sold the service. A grade withdrawn after an authentication investigation cannot be bought back at any rate, and the damage lands in a university application cycle that will not wait.

We say this plainly because the market does not. One provider in this cluster openly sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750 each. Treat that price with real scepticism: it is not a tutoring service, it is an integrity breach with a price tag, and a family paying it is buying risk rather than help. Any provider offering to produce assessed work for your child should be treated the same way, however it is phrased.

The honest alternative is also better value. Six hours of criterion-referenced feedback on a student's own Internal Assessment costs less than a single purchased IA at that advertised figure, carries no authentication exposure, and leaves the student able to do the same thing again in the next subject. The tutor reads, questions and comments; the student writes. That boundary is where the useful work actually happens.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency, attestation and the cost of finding out late
paragraphs: A Diploma or a set of IGCSEs is not automatically enough for a UAE university place or a government-sector role. The Ministry of Education operates a certificate equivalency process, and it has requirements about subject totals, the presence of specific subjects, and attested documentation. Zero competitor pages in this cluster mention it. It is the single most expensive thing a UAE family can discover in July rather than in Year 11.

The practical shape is this. Equivalency looks at the qualification structure, not just the grades, and it has expectations about how many subjects were taken and which ones. Documents generally need attestation, which is a paperwork chain rather than an academic one, and chains take time. Fees and processing times are set by the Ministry and change, so check the current requirements directly with the Ministry of Education or your school's registrar rather than relying on any tutoring site, including this one.

What this has to do with tutoring is subject choice. A student who drops a subject in Year 12 to protect a points total, or who sits fewer subjects than the equivalency route expects, may have solved an academic problem and created an administrative one. That is a conversation for mid-Year 11, before entries close with the IB in mid-November of Year 13, and it is worth one careful hour with someone who knows both systems rather than a scramble after results.

The cost of finding out late is not a tutoring bill. It is a deferred university year, a retake session, or a supplementary qualification bought under time pressure, any of which dwarfs a year of weekly sessions. For the price of a single specialist hour, a family can establish early whether their child's subject spread satisfies both the Diploma they are sitting and the equivalency route they will need. Very few families do this, which is why it belongs on a page about value.

sections.heading: What the free trial is for, and what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: The free trial lesson exists to answer a question a biography cannot: does this particular tutor work with this particular student. Use it properly. Send a recent marked paper, a current Internal Assessment draft, or the last school report, and ask the tutor to work through the actual lost marks rather than introduce themselves. By the end of that hour you should know which component is leaking marks and roughly what those marks are worth, and you should be able to judge whether the quoted rate is reasonable for the work required.

It also tells you something about the provider. A tutor who spends the trial on rapport and generalities is not the tutor to buy exam-term hours from. A tutor who opens the markscheme beside the student's own script, points at where criterion D was described rather than evaluated, and names what to practise next has already demonstrated the thing you would be paying for. That is a cheaper way to assess a quote than three paid sessions.

Now the part nobody advertises. Sometimes no specialist is free. Computer Science HL, Arabic A at Diploma level, TOK supervision and Theatre are thin everywhere, and in a March exam crunch the matching roster for a niche HL subject can genuinely be full. When that happens we say so, give an honest date, and suggest what to do in the meantime, which is usually a defined block of past-paper work with a closely adjacent specialist rather than a general tutor pretending to cover it. A waiting date you can plan around is worth more than a match that does not fit.

Scheduling is the last practical piece, and in the UAE it is a real constraint rather than an afterthought. Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time and the realistic window is 4pm to 9.30pm on weekdays, later during Ramadan when post-Iftar slots open up. Families who travel between the Emirates and abroad over the summer keep the same tutor and shift the clock. Families who pause for mock examinations tell us in advance and resume on the same slot. None of that costs extra; it just needs saying early, because the good slots are allocated to whoever asked first.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the deadline
process.description: Not just the subject. Maths AA HL and Maths AI SL are different bookings with different rates, and a Year 13 student with an Internal Assessment due in six weeks is a different job from a Year 12 student slipping in October. The level and the deadline decide which tier of tutor you actually need.

process.title: Send one real piece of evidence
process.description: A marked past paper, a current IA draft or the latest school report. One real script tells a subject specialist more than a long conversation does, because it shows where the marks are going rather than where the student feels weak. Those two are frequently different, and the gap is where money gets wasted.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson and judge the diagnosis
process.description: One hour, one-to-one, live online, at no cost. Ask the tutor to work through the lost marks on the script you sent. You are assessing whether they can name the component, the criterion and the fix. If they can, the quoted rate is worth considering. If they cannot, you have lost nothing.

process.title: Choose the pattern, then agree the rate
process.description: Weekly single subject, twice-weekly HL, a defined exam block or an IA feedback clinic. The pattern determines your annual total far more than the hourly figure does, so settle it first. We quote after the trial, against the pattern and level you have chosen, with no package you have to buy into.

process.title: Lock the slot and review at the half-term
process.description: Fixed weekly time on Gulf Standard Time, with Ramadan and travel handled by moving the clock rather than changing tutor. At each half-term, check progress against the component you set out to defend. If the pattern is wrong, change it then. Paying for sessions that are not moving the component is the most common slow leak.

whyPoints.title: The rates are on the page
whyPoints.description: Half the pages competing for this search publish no figure and the rest quote dollars. The AED bands in the table above come from named providers and a published Dubai rate survey, so you can price a quote before you accept it. We quote our own fees after the free trial, against your child's actual level.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus and level, not by postcode
whyPoints.description: Because lessons are online, the tutor pool is the whole roster rather than whoever can drive to Al Ain or Fujairah by 5pm. A Chemistry HL student gets a Chemistry HL teacher who knows the current scientific investigation criteria. In the northern emirates that is often the only way such a match exists at all.

whyPoints.title: Weightings and criteria stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Tutors work from the component percentages and criterion mark allocations rather than general revision. Knowing that criterion E carries 6 of the 20 marks in a Mathematics IA, or that evaluation is worth a full 6 in a science investigation, changes which hour is worth buying and in what order.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Coaching, questioning and criterion-referenced feedback on work the student writes. No drafting, no editing, no supplying any part of an IA, EE or TOK essay. One provider in this market sells completed IAs; we name that as the integrity breach it is rather than competing with it.

whyPoints.title: Honest about availability and timing
whyPoints.description: Niche HL subjects genuinely run short in a March crunch, and we give a date rather than a vague reassurance. Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, move to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan, and follow families who travel. Everything is one-to-one and live online across all seven emirates.

faqs.question: How much does an IB tutor in the UAE cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Market rates across the UAE run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor teaching online, and AED 200 to AED 450 or more for an IB specialist teaching Higher Level. Budget online tutoring starts far lower, from around AED 45 to AED 65 on EdFlik's published rates. In-home visits run AED 180 to AED 500 in the Dubai market according to Bestimate's survey, because the tutor's travel is priced into the hour. The premium end, where named examiners are advertised, has been published at AED 650. Those are market figures from named providers, not IB Gram's fees. We quote after a free trial lesson, against your child's subject and level.

faqs.question: Why does a Higher Level tutor cost more than a Standard Level one?
faqs.answer: Because Higher Level is a different assessment, not just more content. HL Mathematics adds Paper 3, worth 20% of the grade, built from extended problem-solving on unfamiliar contexts. HL Economics adds a Paper 3 worth 30%. HL English replaces part of the Paper 2 weighting with a 1,200 to 1,500 word HL Essay on a studied text. The population of tutors who can teach those specific components is much smaller than the population who can teach the Standard Level course, and smaller populations price more firmly. The premium is supply and specialism rather than seniority, which is why it is worth paying at HL and wasteful at SL.

faqs.question: Is the price quoted per hour or per lesson, and does VAT apply?
faqs.answer: Ask, because the market is inconsistent. Some UAE providers quote per hour, some per 90-minute session, and monthly packages quote neither clearly. An advertised AED 799 monthly bundle covering eight online sessions works out near AED 100 an hour, while an AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 in-home bundle of four two-hour visits works out near AED 200 to AED 225 an hour. Convert everything to a per-hour figure before comparing. On VAT, treatment depends on the provider's registration status and how the service is structured, so get the position confirmed in writing before you commit rather than assuming the headline figure is the final one.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in the UAE rise as the May session gets closer?
faqs.answer: Effective rates do, even where published ones do not. UAE schools sit the May session almost universally, so the whole country's demand follows one calendar. In September and October specialists have open evening slots on Gulf Standard Time and a weekly arrangement has 30 or more sessions ahead of it. From January the roster fills, the best slots go first, and what a family finds in March is the remaining inventory at the tight end of the band. The teaching has not changed. Availability has, and availability is what sets the price. Booking in the autumn term is the cheapest decision available in this market.

faqs.question: Is online IB tuition genuinely cheaper than hiring a home tutor in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the reason is mechanical rather than promotional. An in-home hour in the Dubai market costs AED 180 to AED 500 because it prices the tutor's commute into your lesson; a tutor who can fit three visits into an evening must charge differently from one who can fit five online sessions into the same evening. Online delivery removes the drive from the invoice. It also widens the tutor pool from one neighbourhood to the whole roster, which matters most at Higher Level where the specific specialism is the point. IB Gram delivers one-to-one online tuition across the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: How many sessions should we book before deciding whether it is working?
faqs.answer: Start with the free trial, then buy a defined block rather than an open commitment. Six to eight sessions is enough to see whether the specific component you set out to defend is moving, provided you agreed at the outset which component that was. Families who book twenty hours up front, with no diagnosis and no named target, have no way of judging value at session twelve. Review at the half-term against the actual assessment component, not against a general feeling. If the pattern is wrong, change the pattern then; if the tutor is wrong, change the tutor. That review discipline saves more money than negotiating the rate.

faqs.question: What hidden extras catch UAE parents off guard?
faqs.answer: Four recur. Permit or licensing fees, which should not exist at all, since the MoHRE private tutor permit is free of charge across every regulatory source we checked. Travel surcharges on in-home visits, sometimes quoted separately and sometimes folded into a higher hourly rate. Minimum package commitments that make a single trial impossible to judge. And material or platform fees added to an hourly figure that looked competitive. Ask for the all-in cost per contact hour, in AED, in writing. A provider who will not give you that number in a single figure is a provider whose number you cannot compare with anyone else's.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two IB subjects, and does that save money?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it saves less than families expect. A tutor genuinely strong in both Maths AA HL and Physics HL exists, and using one for both is simpler to schedule. But the pairing has to be real: a Chemistry specialist stretching into Biology HL is covering content rather than teaching it, and you are paying specialist rates for generalist work. The saving from consolidating is mostly administrative. The risk is that one subject gets the strong half of the tutor and the other gets the weaker half, which costs marks in a component with a fixed weighting. Match each subject to its own specialism and treat the scheduling as a separate problem.

faqs.question: Is private IB tuition in the UAE worth the cost at all?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what you buy and when. A defined block aimed at a named component with a known weighting, bought in the autumn term, is good value. Twenty open-ended hours bought in April with no diagnosis is not, and it is the version most families end up with. The highest return in this market is usually six hours of criterion-referenced feedback on an Internal Assessment, because the IA is 20% of the grade in Mathematics and the sciences, is marked against published criteria, and is due months before any examination. No tutor can promise a grade, and anyone who does is telling you something useful about themselves.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in the UAE need a permit, and does it affect what we pay?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and the permit route runs through MoHRE. Every regulatory source we checked agrees the permit itself is issued free of charge, so it should not appear as a line on your quote. Published reporting on penalties is thin, and the Ministry has not specified fine amounts, so treat any figure circulating online as unverified. What matters for you commercially is simple: a permit is a compliance matter for the tutor, not a cost to pass on. If a quote carries a permit, licence or registration fee, ask what it is for and expect a weak answer.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write or complete my child's Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider offering to is selling you risk. The IB requires candidates to authenticate their own work, and supplying assessed coursework is malpractice with consequences that fall on the student, not the seller. A tutor may teach the content, explain the criteria and their mark allocations, model technique on a different problem, question a draft and give written feedback. The student writes every submitted word. One provider in this market openly advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; that price should be read as a warning rather than an offer. Six hours of proper feedback costs less and leaves the student able to do it again unaided.

faqs.question: What does IB Gram charge, and is the first lesson really free?
faqs.answer: The trial lesson is free, one-to-one and live online, with no package attached and nothing to cancel afterwards. We quote after it rather than before, because a PYP reading booking and a Maths AA HL exam-term block are different pieces of work and a single headline rate would misprice both. What you can do before speaking to anyone is read the market bands in the table above, which are drawn from named providers and a published Dubai rate survey, and work out what a reasonable figure looks like for your child's level. Walking into a quote with that context is the whole purpose of this page.

faqs.question: Our child has six weeks until the exams. Is it too late, and what will the final stretch cost?
faqs.answer: Six weeks is enough to change technique and not enough to rebuild content, so buy accordingly. A defined block of 10 to 15 hours spent on past papers with the markscheme open, targeting the components your child is measurably losing marks in, is the right purchase. At market specialist rates of AED 200 to AED 450 that is roughly AED 2,000 to AED 6,750. Expect the top of the band and the less convenient slots, because March and April are the tightest weeks in the UAE calendar. What does not work at this point is starting new content or booking an open weekly arrangement with no target component.

faqs.question: How do Arabic and Islamic Studies affect our tutoring budget?
faqs.answer: More than most families plan for. Private schools in the UAE teach Ministry of Education subjects alongside the international curriculum, including Arabic, Islamic Studies for Muslim students and UAE Social Studies. These usually sit outside the Diploma points total, which is exactly why they get neglected until a report card forces the issue. Advertised supply of specialist Arabic help is thin relative to demand, so rates do not sit at the bottom of the market. The cheap fix is timing: a non-native Arabic learner supported during MYP costs far less in total than one compressing years of language exposure into Year 12 under examination pressure.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for our child's subject?
faqs.answer: We tell you, give a date, and suggest something useful for the interval. Computer Science HL, Arabic A at Diploma level, Theatre and Theory of Knowledge supervision are thin across the whole market, and in a March crunch a niche Higher Level roster can genuinely be full. The honest options are a defined block of past-paper work with a closely adjacent specialist, or waiting for a date we can actually commit to. What we will not do is hand you a general tutor and describe them as a subject specialist, because you would discover the difference three sessions in, having paid specialist rates for it.

faqs.question: Does the Ministry of Education equivalency process mean we need extra tutoring?
faqs.answer: Not usually extra hours, but it does change subject choices, which is more consequential. The Ministry of Education runs a certificate equivalency process with expectations about qualification structure, subject totals and attested documentation, and it is the thing UAE families most often discover in July rather than in Year 11. A student who drops a subject to protect a points total can solve an academic problem and create an administrative one. Check current requirements directly with the Ministry or your school's registrar, well before entries close with the IB in mid-November of Year 13. One careful hour then is worth more than a scramble after results.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan without an extra charge?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the time to arrange it is several weeks ahead rather than the week it begins. Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, and during Ramadan the late-evening post-Iftar window often turns out to be the most productive of the whole year: the house is quiet, the school day has been shortened, and the student is not arriving straight from a commute. Moving the clock costs nothing. The practical constraint is that post-Iftar slots are the most contested hours on the roster, so families who ask late get what is left. Travel over Eid is handled the same way, by pausing or shifting rather than changing tutor.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects do UAE families pay for tutoring in most often?
faqs.answer: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the single most requested and most expensive booking in this market, driven by Paper 1 without a calculator and by Paper 3. Chemistry and Physics follow, where the 36/44/20 component split concentrates demand on data handling and the scientific investigation. Economics generates steady demand because three commentaries of 800 words each carry 30% of the Standard Level grade. English A Language and Literature is requested more than families expect, because unseen Paper 1 analysis under time is a separate skill from reading comprehension. Computer Science and Arabic are requested less but cost more, purely because supply is thin.

ib-tutor.closingHeading: Price the help before you buy it
ib-tutor.closingBody: You now have what this market withholds: the AED bands a UAE family actually faces, who publishes each one, what moves a rate from AED 150 to AED 450, and what a year of each booking pattern totals. Use it to judge any quote you are given, including ours. Send a recent marked paper, take the free trial lesson, and ask the tutor to work through the lost marks rather than introduce themselves. Every lesson is one-to-one and live online on Gulf Standard Time, across all seven emirates, with a hard line against touching assessed work. If the autumn term is still ahead of you, this is the cheapest month of the year to start.

ib-tutor-cost.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma and IGCSE subjects to UAE families over live video, in evening slots set in Gulf Standard Time. Each profile names the syllabus and the components the tutor teaches, because a rate only means something once you know which paper it buys.

intro.heading: What a UAE family is actually paying for when they price an IB tutor
paragraphs: Ask five providers what an IB tutor costs in the UAE and you will get figures between AED 45 and AED 650 an hour. That spread is real, and it is published: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, Unitors from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, TutorChase AED 270, and BartyED AED 650. All of those were read in October 2026. None of them is our price list, and none of them explains itself. The useful question is not which number is right. It is which forces produced the number, because those forces are the part you can actually plan around.

Four of them sit with institutions. The emirate authority that licensed your child's school decided which curriculum that school may run, which decides which syllabus a tutor has to know. The federal Ministry of Education, applied in Dubai through KHDA's mandatory-subject guidance, put Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies on the timetable beside the IB, whatever curriculum the school is licensed for. MoHRE decided who may lawfully take money for private lessons, under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and made that permit free for two years. Cambridge International, Pearson and the IB organisation own the entry deadlines and the exam windows, which decide the weeks in which demand for a specialist hour spikes.

The fifth force is arithmetic. Dubai's private schools held 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering 17 curricula. UK-curriculum schools took 37 per cent of that enrolment, Indian 26 per cent, American 14 per cent, and the International Baccalaureate 7 per cent. Seven per cent of 387,441 is roughly 27,000 pupils, spread across every year group from the Primary Years Programme to the second Diploma year. The number of adults in the Emirates who have taught Chemistry at Higher Level, or marked a Mathematics exploration, is a small fraction of a small fraction. Scarcity at Higher Level is the clearest single driver of the top AED bands, and no fee regulation touches it.

What is not a driver is licensing. The private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years and is open to school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. A permit is a legal floor, not a quality signal, and a provider implying that paperwork is what makes an hour expensive is describing the wrong thing. What makes an hour expensive is somebody who has taught your child's exact component, repeatedly, and knows where that paper loses marks.

This page is organised around those forces rather than around a price list. It publishes the UAE market bands and names who published each, sets out which authority governs which emirate and what each one does and does not approve, works through the Ministry subjects that sit on the timetable already, and counts the exam calendar from the published entry deadlines. Lessons from IB Gram are delivered one-to-one over live video. Home visits are something we offer in India, not in the Emirates, and the comparison later on makes the case for the online format on its merits.

ib-tutor-cost.programmesIntro: Four IB programmes run in UAE schools, and each one meets the regulators differently. The programme your child is in changes what tutoring can usefully do, what the school must already provide, and where the published rate bands apply.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations, so there is no entry deadline and no results day to count backwards from. Support here is about reading fluency, number sense and the written and spoken work that transdisciplinary units ask for. Sessions are short, usually 45 minutes, and the measure of progress is the school's own reporting rather than a grade.
programmes.countryNote: PYP pupils in Dubai already sit Arabic and Moral, Social and Cultural studies lessons under KHDA's mandatory-subject rules, with Arab and non-Arab groups taught separately. That matters for a tutoring budget: the school is required to deliver those hours, so outside support should be practice and feedback on the school's own content rather than a second syllabus bought in parallel.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks against criteria A to D, each out of 8, in every subject. Students who have never seen a numerical percentage can reach Year 11 without a clear picture of where they stand. Useful tutoring at this stage is criterion translation: what a 5 in criterion C looks like compared with a 7, and what has to change in the work itself.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students in the UAE face a decision Year 11 makes expensive if it is left late. Some UAE schools move MYP students into the Diploma, others into IGCSE, and the Ministry's equivalency rules count five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3. A family who finds out in Year 12 that the subject count is short is paying for the dearest kind of catch-up.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Higher Level courses carry more content, an extra paper in several subjects, and internal assessment marked against published criteria. This is where the UAE's published specialist bands of AED 200 to 450 and above apply, and where the teaching pool is thinnest.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in the Emirates carry two timetables at once: the IB's, and the Ministry subjects their school is required to deliver. A Dubai Diploma student may be sitting Arabic lessons that cannot use outside content without prior Ministry permission. Any plan for IB Diploma tutoring in Abu Dhabi or Dubai has to fit around that, not pretend it is absent.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs DP courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. Fewer UAE schools offer it, which makes the subject-specialist pool for its DP components narrower again. Support usually concentrates on the DP courses inside the CP and on the reflective project's process, which is the student's own work throughout.
programmes.countryNote: CP students applying to UAE universities need to know what their certificate shows and what the Ministry of Education equivalency route asks of it. The British and American tracks have reported requirements; the IB figure is not something we will publish without reading it on moe.gov.ae. Ask the school's coordinator and the attestation channel before building a plan on an assumption.

ib-tutor-cost.subjectsIntro: Rates vary by subject far more than most parents expect, and the variation follows how many adults in the Emirates can teach the component rather than how hard the subject is. These are the Diploma and IGCSE subjects UAE families ask for most.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: AA Higher Level is the course that most often sits behind a request for an IB Maths AA HL tutor in the Emirates. Paper 3 at HL asks for extended investigative problems, which is where students who can do routine questions come apart. The exploration is marked against criteria A to E and loses marks on personal engagement and reflection more often than on the mathematics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI carries statistics, modelling and a graphical-calculator workload that AA does not. UAE engineering and medicine applicants are often advised towards AA, so the route choice is worth settling in Year 11 rather than Year 12. The pool of teachers confident in AI HL statistics is smaller than for AA, which shows up in the rate.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Higher Level adds content and a practical and data-analysis demand that is hard to rehearse without a teacher who has marked it. Organic mechanisms and energetics are the recurring loss points. The scientific investigation is the student's own work; a tutor's role is teaching the method and giving feedback on drafts the student has written.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Physics rewards consistent use of command terms. Students lose marks by describing when the paper said explain, and by dropping units in multi-step working. HL electromagnetic induction and circular motion are the sections that most often need rebuilding from the start rather than revising.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Biology at Higher Level is a volume problem as much as a comprehension one. The marks tend to go on precision of terminology and on data questions where students interpret a graph loosely. A tutor's highest-value hour here is usually spent on past-paper data responses rather than on content recall.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides a large share of Economics marks, and HL adds quantitative questions that catch students who never practised the arithmetic. The internal assessment commentaries must each use a published article the student found, within the word limit, and are where a late start becomes expensive.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and Paper 1 guided analysis need a method, not more reading. Students who narrate the text instead of analysing the writer's choices plateau at a predictable mark. Support works best as structured rehearsal of the oral and timed Paper 1 practice with feedback.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study questions reward applying a tool to the stimulus rather than defining it. HL extension topics and the business research project are the two places students most often need help with process. The project is the student's own, and support means teaching research method and reading drafts.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The Core and Extended split is a decision with consequences for Diploma entry, because an Extended grade is what most IB schools expect before Higher Level maths. Published rates for a qualified online subject tutor start around AED 150 an hour, which makes IGCSE tutor cost in Dubai the cheapest serious intervention in the whole sequence.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics and Chemistry
subjects.description: Cambridge and Pearson set different papers, different practical arrangements and different syllabus codes for what parents call the same subject. Knowing which board and which syllabus code your child sits is the first thing a tutor should ask, and a provider who says they cover every board without naming one has not asked.

ib-tutor-cost.regionsTitle: The seven emirates, and who regulates each one
ib-tutor-cost.regionsIntro: Which authority sits above your child's school changes what is published about that school, who inspects it, and which channel answers a question about fees or curriculum. It does not change the price of a private lesson, which no authority approves.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA licenses and inspects Dubai's private schools, and holds the mandatory-subject guidance that places Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies on every licensed curriculum. Dubai held private school fees flat for 2026-27 and is adding 16,846 places across seven new schools, three of them IB.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
regions.note: ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school, which is a conflict question rather than a pricing one. Verify the current wording with ADEK.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees as well as curricula, programmes and assessment methods. That breadth is often misread: SPEA approves what schools may charge and teach, and has nothing to approve in a private tutoring agreement.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. Families here often hold places at schools across the Dubai or Sharjah border, which makes a late-afternoon slot hard to protect and an evening slot over live video easier to keep.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: RAK's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah, approves fees, curricula, courses and assessment methods. The IB cohort here is small, so the realistic route to a Higher Level specialist is a tutor who is not in Ras Al Khaimah at all.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Fujairah's private schools sit under the federal Ministry of Education. Diploma subject choice is narrower than on the west coast, and families frequently find that no local provider teaches the component they need. The honest answer there is a scheduled online slot rather than a long drive.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Umm Al Quwain is also supervised federally by the Ministry of Education. With the smallest private-school roll in the country, published tutoring rates for the emirate are effectively absent, and a provider quoting a local in-home figure is quoting travel rather than teaching.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai holds the country's deepest IB cluster, which is why the specialist market concentrates here and why rates quoted to Dubai families are the ones most often repeated nationally. Students we support attend schools of this kind; the names are given for context only.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, under ADEK
schoolClusters.note: The capital's international schools mix IB, British and other curricula under ADEK licensing. Families here more often ask about the own-school tutoring rule than about the hourly figure, because the ethics position reported for Abu Dhabi school staff rules out the most obvious option.

Outside Dubai and Abu Dhabi the number of schools running a full Diploma falls sharply, and with it the local supply of Higher Level teachers. Published in-home rates in these emirates reflect distance more than expertise, which is the practical argument for teaching over video here.

ib-tutor-cost.modesIntro: Three ways of buying teaching cover almost every UAE enquiry, and each carries a different exposure to the forces above. All three are delivered one-to-one over live video, with the slot fixed in Gulf Standard Time.

modes.title: A weekly slot held for the year
modes.description: One hour a week with the same tutor, in a slot that survives the school term. Published indicative monthly figures for this pattern run from AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle of the market, according to Bestimate's 2026 rate table. The value of the pattern is continuity: the tutor sees the work accumulate instead of meeting it cold.

modes.title: A component block before an internal deadline
modes.description: A short, dense run of sessions aimed at one assessed component: a scientific investigation, a mathematics exploration, an Economics commentary. Buying a block is usually cheaper than a year of weekly hours and lands more marks per dirham, provided it starts early enough for the student to write, be given feedback, and revise their own drafts.
bullets: Four to eight sessions, planned against the school's internal deadline
Teaching the criteria and the method, feedback on the student's own drafts

modes.title: An exam-session sprint
modes.description: Timed-paper practice and feedback in the weeks before a published session. This is the most competitive window in the UAE market, because every family wants the same evening hours at the same time. Published specialist exam-year monthly estimates reach AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above, which is the clearest reason to book the slot before the window opens.
bullets: Past-paper work under time, marked against the published criteria

sections.heading: Where the number on an IB tuition quote actually comes from
paragraphs: An IB tutor cost in the UAE sits somewhere between AED 33 and AED 650 an hour in published material, and the tutor explains only part of that range. Four institutional decisions arrive before any provider opens a conversation with you, and each one narrows or widens the pool of people who could teach your child's component. Reading the quote against those four decisions is the difference between negotiating a price and understanding one.

The first is the licence your child's school holds, which is issued by KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. That licence decides the curriculum, and the curriculum decides which syllabus a tutor must know in detail. The second is the federal requirement, applied in Dubai through KHDA's mandatory-subject guidance, that Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies run alongside whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for.

The third is MoHRE's private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which decides who may lawfully charge for lessons at all. The fourth belongs to the examination boards: Cambridge International and Pearson for IGCSE, and the IB organisation for the Diploma. They own the entry deadlines and the exam windows, and those windows concentrate demand into a few weeks each year. The fifth force is not a decision but a count, and it is the one that moves the top of the range: how many adults in the Emirates have actually taught the component you need.

sections.heading: The permit is free, which tells you what you are really buying
paragraphs: The private tuition work permit in the UAE is granted free of charge for two years. That single fact disposes of a common assumption. Licensing costs a tutor nothing, takes two working days through MoHRE's app, website or e-services system, and is open to school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Whatever is in a rate of AED 400 an hour, it is not the cost of a licence.

What the permit does establish is that the person teaching your child is doing so lawfully. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you; a provider who names an amount is inventing one. The permit also carries a code of conduct, and reporting on Abu Dhabi indicates that teachers must not tutor students affiliated with their own school. So a private tuition permit in the UAE is a floor, and a conflict rule, and nothing else.

This is why the right questions at enquiry are about teaching rather than status. Which category under Resolution 710 applies to the person who will take the lesson. Which board and syllabus code they have taught, and for how many cohorts. Which components of that syllabus they have marked. A tuition business with premises in Dubai is a different legal object again: it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, renewed annually, and holding one says nothing about any individual in the building.

sections.heading: Dubai held school fees flat. Nothing holds tutoring rates flat
paragraphs: On 22 May 2026 KHDA confirmed that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a family budgeting a Diploma, that is a fixed line in a document that has very few fixed lines. It is also the clearest illustration of where regulation reaches and where it stops: a school's fee needs approval, and a tutor's fee does not.

The supply side moved at the same time. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. Six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. More IB places is good news for admission and neutral-to-negative news for tutoring prices in the short run, because new schools recruit experienced IB teachers out of the same pool that families are trying to hire from in the evenings.

Put the lines side by side and the planning conclusion is straightforward. The part of the education bill that is approved by an authority is stable this year. The part nobody approves is the part that will move, and it will move most in the weeks around published entry deadlines and exam windows. A family who commits a weekly slot in September is buying from a looser market than a family who starts looking in February, and that is a function of the calendar rather than of anyone's goodwill.
