sections.heading: Why one IB hour is scarcer than another, and what scarcity does to the rate
paragraphs: Subjects do not cost what their difficulty suggests. They cost what their supply allows. UK-curriculum schools hold 37 per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment, so the number of adults in the city who have taught IGCSE Mathematics is large, and IB tutor rates in AED for that work start at the bottom of the qualified band. The IB's 7 per cent share means the Diploma pool is an order of magnitude smaller before you narrow it by subject, and narrowing it by level and component shrinks it again.

A worked example makes the point. A request for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level requires someone who has taught the HL content, is comfortable with Paper 3's extended problems, and has supervised explorations against criteria A to E. Each of those conditions removes most of the remaining candidates. The last condition removes almost everyone who has only tutored rather than taught. That is the mechanism behind a published specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and above, not an assertion that the subject is harder than Biology.

The same logic runs in reverse at the budget end. General homework support for lower secondary can lawfully be given by a university student holding the free permit, so supply is wide and the published figures start as low as AED 33 an hour. Neither band is a judgement about anybody. They are two different markets that happen to share a word. A parent who asks for the price of a tutor is asking a question that does not have one answer; a parent who asks for the price of Chemistry HL internal assessment supervision will get a number that means something.

sections.heading: What the UAE market publishes, and what a published figure leaves out
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible pages in this market publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. The table below collects what was actually published in dirhams in October 2026, with the provider or tracker named against each band. These are market figures. They are not IB Gram's prices, and no figure here should be read as a quotation from us.

The more useful column is the last one. A rate per hour tells you almost nothing on its own, because providers draw the boundary of the hour differently. Some count marking inside it and some outside. Some quote a 45-minute period and describe it as a session. In-home rates absorb travel, so a 60-minute visit in Dubai traffic can contain noticeably less teaching than its price implies. Monthly packages fix a session count without fixing what happens to a session nobody could use.

Before agreeing to anything, ask for the fee per 60 minutes of teaching, what sits outside that fee, the notice period for moving a lesson, and who absorbs the cost when a session is cancelled. Then compare. Two providers 40 per cent apart on the headline figure frequently sit within a few dirhams of each other once marking, rescheduling and session length are normalised, and the cheaper headline is sometimes the dearer hour. Ask as well when the rate was last changed and whether it holds for the full term you are booking, because a figure quoted in September that moves in February is not the figure you budgeted.

sections.heading: Which authority approves a fee, and which has nothing to say about yours
paragraphs: Sharjah's authority and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods for the schools they regulate. That is a genuinely broad remit, and it is routinely misread by parents and by provider websites into something it does not cover. Approval of a school's fee is not approval of a tutor's fee. No authority in the UAE approves, publishes or caps what a private tutor charges.

The practical value of knowing your regulator is different. It tells you which inspection report exists and where to read it, which channel answers a question about the school's curriculum or fee, and which rules bind the teachers your child already has. ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, and its professional-ethics position reported for private and charter school staff is the reason the obvious option, paying your child's own teacher, is the wrong one to pursue in the capital.

It also tells you which claims to disbelieve. A tutoring provider cannot be approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or an examination board in the way those words are usually deployed on a tutoring website. KHDA does issue an Educational Services Permit, but that is a permit for a training institute with premises, with initial approval first and a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps. IB Gram holds none of these, says so, and teaches over live video instead.

sections.heading: The Ministry hours already inside the fee you pay
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Those hours are already on your child's timetable and already inside the school fee you pay. Any tutoring budget should start by noticing that.

The rules are specific enough to be checkable. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic require appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

Two of these details should change how you read an offer. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes, so a provider matching a school's lesson length is not matching a tutoring hour. And the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the Ministry, is prohibited for these subjects. A provider advertising its own Arabic or Social Studies syllabus for a Dubai school pupil is advertising material the school could not adopt. Supporting the school's own content is legitimate; replacing it is not.

sections.heading: Equivalency: the cheapest thing to get wrong and the dearest to discover late
paragraphs: A Ministry of Education equivalency file is where a UAE family discovers whether two years of subject choices actually add up. The reported British-track rule is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That exclusion is the detail that catches families who counted them.

For the American track, the reported requirements are English proficiency evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics evidenced by at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test. A ranking page in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The reported rule is five. Publishing the right count matters more than publishing a confident one.

For the IB Diploma we will not publish a points threshold. The source that set out the British and American requirements states none, and we could not read an IB figure on the Ministry's own pages, so putting one here would be an invention dressed as guidance. Check with the Ministry channel and your school's Diploma coordinator. Nothing in this process requires tutoring, and no provider, including this one, performs or guarantees equivalency. What tutoring can do is make sure the subject count and grades that the file will need are in place while there is still time to influence them.

sections.heading: The dates we will print, and the ones we will not
paragraphs: Every spending decision in an exam year is really a date decision, and the dates belong to the boards rather than to the school or the tutor. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Its March 2027 series is published in full: papers from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries due 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June.

Read those two lines together and the planning point is obvious. The entry deadline sits more than two months before the first paper. A decision about whether your child is entered, and for which tier, has to be made while the teaching is still in progress. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone; Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask your exams officer which zone your centre sits in before you build a revision plan around a Cambridge exam zone timetable.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations run in May or June and in November. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, and provisional dates can be revised, so always open the live timetable rather than trusting a date restated on a website. For the IB Diploma we publish no session or results dates at all, because we could not read them from the IB itself.

sections.heading: Six checks, and where each one is actually answered
paragraphs: Most of what decides whether a tutoring arrangement was worth the money is settled before the first lesson, in answers a parent can get in one conversation. None of the six checks below needs a specialist to evaluate. Each has a weak answer that sounds reassuring, which is why the fourth column exists. A provider who answers all six plainly is telling you something about how the rest of the arrangement will run.

The permit question is first because it is binary and because the answer identifies the category of person teaching. The own-school question matters most in Abu Dhabi, where the reported ethics position for private and charter school staff bars paid tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school. The board question is the one families most often cannot answer: Cambridge and Pearson set different papers and different syllabus codes for subjects that share a name, and a tutor who has not asked which one your child sits has not started work.

The last two are about money and data. Settle in writing what the fee covers per 60 minutes, what sits outside it, the notice period for moving a session, and who absorbs a late cancellation. Then ask what personal information about your child is collected, why, and how to have it deleted; UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on personal data protection is the reason that question is reasonable, and a form that asks for a minor's school, grades and photograph without stating a purpose is the reason it is necessary.

sections.heading: Why a UAE family buys this online, and what that changes in the price
paragraphs: Searches for an IB home tutor are among the most common in this market, and the honest answer has two halves. The first half is what the market charges for a visiting arrangement: published UAE figures run from AED 180 to 350 on Bestimate's 2026 table and from AED 200 to 500 in home-tutor listings, with monthly packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Travel is inside those numbers whether or not it appears on the invoice.

The second half is what the travel costs in something other than dirhams. A tutor who must reach your address is a tutor drawn from a radius, not from the country, and the radius is what prices your subject. A family in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain searching inside a 30-minute drive is searching a pool that may contain nobody who has taught Chemistry at Higher Level. A family in Dubai searching the same way during the evening peak is paying for time spent on Sheikh Zayed Road. That is the mechanism, and it is why the published in-home bands sit above the online ones for the same qualification.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one IB tuition over live video everywhere in the Emirates. Home visits are part of our service in India and not in the UAE, and no arrangement here involves anyone arriving at a UAE address. What the format buys is selection: the family in Fujairah and the family in Emirates Hills choose from the same group of subject specialists, in an evening slot fixed in Gulf Standard Time, with the lesson recorded in the student's own notes rather than in a drive. Online IB tutoring in Dubai and in the northern emirates is the same product, which is not true of the alternative.

sections.heading: Academic honesty is a budget line, not a footnote
paragraphs: There is one purchase in this market that is worth nothing at any price, and it is sold openly. A page in this SERP offers a finished Internal Assessment for AED 3,750. A student who submits assessed work that is not their own is exposed to an IB malpractice finding, and a malpractice finding can cost the Diploma. No hourly saving elsewhere compensates for that, and no provider's reassurance changes what the IB does about it.

The boundary is not vague and it is not restrictive in a way that hurts teaching. A tutor may teach the assessment criteria and what each one asks for, work through examples that are not the student's task, help a student plan and narrow a research question, read a draft the student has written and say where it falls short of a criterion, teach the referencing convention, and rehearse the oral components. The student does the writing, the data collection, the analysis and the revision, every time.

What a tutor may not do is supply text, rewrite a passage into its final form, or hand over work for submission. There is a second line worth knowing about: IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are not ours to distribute, so we reference and link them rather than sending copies. A provider who offers a library of mark schemes as an inclusion in the fee is offering something they should not, and billing you for it.

process.title: Tell us the component, not just the subject
process.description: Send the board, the syllabus code where you have it, the level, and which part of the course is the problem. "Chemistry HL, Cambridge-style practical work, internal assessment due in six weeks" gets a useful match. "Science help" does not. The more precisely the need is described, the smaller the gap between the first tutor suggested and the right one.

process.title: We check the calendar before the diary
process.description: Your child's board and series decide which weeks matter. We look at the published entry deadline and exam window for that series, and the school's own internal deadlines for assessed components, before proposing a start date. A plan built on the calendar month rather than the board's dates usually buys hours in the wrong weeks.

process.title: A free trial lesson, with its conditions stated
process.description: One lesson at no charge, with the tutor who would teach the course, so the match is judged on teaching rather than on a profile. No payment is taken beforehand and there is no obligation to continue. If the fit is wrong, say so and we will propose a different tutor or tell you we do not have one.

process.title: Agree the fee and the terms in writing
process.description: Before the first paid session you get the fee per 60 minutes of teaching, what sits outside it, the notice period for moving a lesson, and what personal information we hold about your child and why. Market bands on this page are other providers' published figures; your own figure is confirmed in writing to you.

process.title: A fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, in a slot held for the term and set in UAE time rather than the tutor's. Post-iftar timing during Ramadan is a scheduling change, not a renegotiation. If a session has to move, the notice period you agreed applies to both sides.

process.title: Review each term against the component
process.description: Progress is read against the thing being assessed: the paper, the criterion, the component weighting. Each term we say what has moved, what has not, and whether the hours should continue, change shape or stop. A recommendation to stop is a real outcome and we will give it when it is the right one.

whyPoints.title: Every figure carries its source and its date
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page name the provider or rate tracker that published them and the month they were read. No figure is presented as ours, and no number appears without somewhere to check it. Three of the most visible pages in this market publish no price at all, and two more quote in US dollars.

whyPoints.title: We say what we are not
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no UAE office or centre. Naming a regulator and explaining what it does is useful to you. Implying it endorses us would not be.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is written down
whyPoints.description: What a tutor may teach, read and give feedback on, and what has to be the student's own work, is set out on the page rather than left to be negotiated under deadline pressure. That boundary protects the Diploma, which is the only thing the whole arrangement exists to defend.

whyPoints.title: Dates come from the boards, or not at all
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates here are taken from those boards' own published timetables and key-date documents. For the IB we publish no session or results date, because we could not verify one from the IB itself. A wrong date in a planning table is worse than a blank one.

whyPoints.title: Selection rather than proximity
whyPoints.description: Teaching over live video means the choice of tutor is made on who has taught the component, not on who can reach your area by 5pm. For Higher Level subjects in the northern emirates, that difference is the whole of the available choice rather than a preference.

whyPoints.title: An honest answer when we cannot help
whyPoints.description: Some components have very few experienced teachers anywhere, and sometimes the hour you need is already taken. We will tell you that, rather than fill the slot with somebody who has not taught it. Being told no in October is cheaper than finding out in March.

faqs.question: Who actually sets the price of an IB tutor in the UAE, and is any of it regulated?
faqs.answer: The provider sets it. No UAE authority approves, publishes or caps what a private tutor may charge. KHDA, ADEK, SPEA and the Department of Knowledge approve school tuition fees and curricula for the schools they regulate, and in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah that extends to courses and assessment methods, but none of them touches a private lesson fee. What regulation does is shape supply: the curriculum your school is licensed for, the subjects the Ministry requires alongside it, and who may lawfully be paid to teach privately. Published UAE market rates ran from AED 33 to AED 650 an hour in October 2026, which is what an unregulated market looks like.

faqs.question: The private tuition permit is issued free, so what is in a rate of AED 300 an hour?
faqs.answer: Not licensing. The MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years and issued in about two working days, so it costs a tutor nothing to be lawful. What sits inside a higher rate is scarcity of a specific kind: someone who has taught your child's exact component at that level, repeatedly, and has marked work against its criteria. That describes very few people in a country where the IB accounts for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment. Ask what the person has taught and for how many cohorts. If the answer is about certificates rather than components, the premium is buying the wrong thing.

faqs.question: Dubai capped private school fees for 2026-27. Should tutoring prices have moved too?
faqs.answer: They are unrelated mechanisms. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for 2026-27, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. That decision binds schools, which need fee approval. Tutoring has no approval step and no cap, so nothing obliges a provider to hold its rate. In the same period Dubai licensed seven new private schools adding 16,846 places, three of them IB, and new schools recruit experienced IB teachers from the same pool families hire from in the evenings. The fixed line in your budget this year is the school fee, not the tutoring.

faqs.question: Does KHDA or ADEK approve tutoring providers, and should I only use one that is?
faqs.answer: No tutoring provider can hold the approval that phrase implies. KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises in Dubai, which involves initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal. That permit is about a business and its building, not about any tutor inside it. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Neither body certifies individual tutors or online providers. A website claiming regulator approval for tutoring is describing something that does not exist, which is a reason to read the rest of its claims carefully.

faqs.question: If we move from Dubai to Abu Dhabi mid-Diploma, which authority's rules follow us?
faqs.answer: The authority follows the school, not the family. A Dubai school sits under KHDA; an Abu Dhabi or Al Ain school sits under ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation in the emirate. What changes on a move is which inspection report exists, which channel answers questions about fees and curriculum, and which professional-ethics rules bind your child's teachers. The Diploma itself does not change, and nor do the board deadlines. For tutoring, nothing changes at all: the fee was never approved by either authority, and lessons over live video continue unchanged across an emirate border or an international one.

faqs.question: Is an IB hour genuinely scarcer than an IGCSE hour in the UAE, or is that just marketing?
faqs.answer: It is arithmetic. Dubai's private schools held 387,441 students in 2024-25, with UK-curriculum schools at 37 per cent of enrolment and the IB at 7 per cent. Before you narrow by subject, the pool of adults who have taught the Diploma is far smaller than the pool who have taught IGCSE. Narrow it to Higher Level, then to a specific component such as Paper 3 or exploration supervision, and the remaining number is small. That is why published specialist bands sit at AED 200 to 450 and above while a qualified online IGCSE subject tutor starts around AED 150. The gap tracks supply, not difficulty.

faqs.question: Should we pay for Arabic or Islamic Education when the school has to teach them anyway?
faqs.answer: Start from what is already included. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and those hours are inside the school fee you already pay. Outside support is reasonable for practice, feedback and the school's own assessment tasks. It is not reasonable as a parallel syllabus: the use of different or additional content for these subjects without prior Ministry permission is prohibited. Also note that teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education in schools need appropriate KHDA approval, which is a useful question to ask of anyone offering to teach them privately.

faqs.question: Why is my child in a different Arabic class from their friend at the same school?
faqs.answer: Because KHDA requires it. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Arabic as a first language and for Islamic Education for Arab students, while non-Arab students take Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with KHDA advising at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson.

faqs.question: What subject count does an equivalency file actually need from an IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: Five. The reported British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. At least one ranking page in this market states six, which is a count worth checking before it shapes a subject choice. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation channel, because the consequence of a shortfall only appears at the end of two years.

faqs.question: Is there an IB points figure for UAE equivalency we can plan around?
faqs.answer: Not one we will publish. The July 2026 reporting that set out the British and American track requirements states no IB points threshold, and we could not read one on the Ministry's own pages, so any number here would be invention. The American-track requirements that are reported are English evidenced by IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT reading and writing 450, and mathematics evidenced by SAT Mathematics of at least 450. For the IB, ask the Ministry channel and your school's Diploma coordinator. Equivalency is a process we describe, not one IB Gram performs, arranges or guarantees for anyone.

faqs.question: Why will you not print the IB exam dates on a page about cost?
faqs.answer: Because we could not verify them. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project was confirmed from the IB itself, and a wrong date in a planning table is worse than no date. Cambridge and Pearson publish theirs and we use them: Cambridge's March 2027 series runs 3 February to 4 March 2027 with final entries due 27 November 2026, and Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs to 19 November 2026. For the Diploma, take the session dates from your school's coordinator or from ibo.org and build the spending plan on those.

faqs.question: What does the Cambridge zone system change about when we should buy hours?
faqs.answer: It changes which timetable your plan is built on. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone; Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone version was used. Two children in the same UAE city can sit the same paper on different days if their centres sit in different zones. Ask your exams officer for the zone before scheduling a revision block, because a block timed to the wrong version wastes the most expensive weeks in the year.

faqs.question: A teacher from my child's own school has offered paid evening lessons. Should we take it?
faqs.answer: Treat it with care, and check the school's position first. Reporting on Abu Dhabi indicates that ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and that teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. The conflict is obvious once stated: the same person would be teaching, assessing and privately charging for the same course. Verify the current rule with the school and the authority rather than relying on the arrangement being common.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a tutor's permit and a tuition centre's licence?
faqs.answer: They cover different objects. An individual's private tuition work permit comes from MoHRE under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is free for two years, and says the person may lawfully be paid for lessons. A tuition business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. A centre holding the second does not tell you anything about the individual teaching your child's hour, which is the thing to ask about.

faqs.question: How are lessons actually delivered to a family in the Emirates?
faqs.answer: One-to-one over live video, in a slot fixed in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send anyone to a UAE address; home visits are part of what we offer in India only. The published UAE market shows why the online format is the better buy here: travel-inclusive bands run from AED 180 to 500 an hour against online bands from AED 150 to 300 for comparable qualifications, and a visiting tutor is drawn from a driving radius rather than from the whole subject pool. A family in Fujairah and a family in Dubai choose from the same specialists on the same terms.

faqs.question: What happens to the cost if nobody is free for our subject and our hour?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and nothing is charged. Some components have very few experienced teachers in any market, and evening slots in the weeks before a published series are the ones everybody wants. In that case the options are a different hour, a short block aimed only at the component rather than a weekly slot, or a wait with a date attached. What we will not do is fill the slot with somebody who has not taught the component and let you discover it in the third lesson. An honest no in October costs less than the wrong yes in March.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an Internal Assessment without crossing the IB's honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can teach what each criterion asks for, work through examples that are not your child's task, help narrow a research question, read a draft your child has written and say where it falls short, teach the referencing convention and rehearse an oral. Your child does the writing, the data work, the analysis and the revision. Anything presented as finished work for submission is malpractice, and a page in this market openly sells a completed Internal Assessment for AED 3,750. The saving is irrelevant next to a malpractice finding, which can cost the whole Diploma.

Send the board, the level and the component, and we will tell you what is realistic or that we cannot help.

intro.heading: Near me, in a country with five school regulators
paragraphs: A proximity search is a cheap filter, and in the UAE it is also a misleading one. Dubai alone licensed 227 private schools in 2024-25, teaching 387,441 students across 17 different curricula, and the International Baccalaureate is a minority share of that enrolment. The nearest IB school to your address may be the only one for several districts. The nearest adult who has actually taught your child's exact subject at Higher Level may be nowhere within driving range. Distance predicts traffic well. It predicts nothing about whether anyone inside the radius has sat in front of that syllabus, marked that component, or read the examiner's report that explains where the marks went.

The second problem with a radius is that the UAE does not have one school system. It has five regulators, and which one holds your child's file depends on the emirate you live in rather than the curriculum the school teaches. Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Move thirty minutes up Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and the inspection framework, the fee-approval route and the published report all change hands.

There is a third problem, and it is the one that surprises families most. The closest qualified adult to your child is usually their own subject teacher at school. That is the one person who, on the published position, may not take the work. Gulf News has reported that the Department of Education and Knowledge's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct with the same restriction. Verify the current wording with the authority or the school before relying on it, but plan on the basis that it holds.

So here is what IB Gram actually does, in plain words, before you read another section. Tuition for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. We do not arrange home visits anywhere in the Emirates; that service exists only in India. There is no UAE office to drive to. The first session is a free 45-minute trial lesson, taken before any payment, so you judge the teaching rather than a profile. Coursework help is feedback and questioning on work the student has written; nobody here writes an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay.

This page is built for the parent who has already searched IB tutor near me in the UAE and wants the part the map leaves out: who is legally permitted to teach your child, what the market charges once travel is stripped out of the fee, how much of an evening a visiting tutor really consumes, which authority to ask for a school's inspection report, what Arabic and Islamic Education add to the week, when exam entries close, and what the Ministry of Education wants on file after the Diploma finishes. Every figure below is attributed to the body or the publication it came from.

ib-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: IB Gram covers the three mainstream IB programmes plus the Career-related Programme. What changes between them is not only the content but what the regulator in your emirate requires alongside it, and how much of the final grade sits in work marked inside the school.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The Primary Years Programme has no external examination, which makes it the stage where a proximity search misleads most. Nothing is riding on a paper, so families often wait. What is actually forming is the number sense, reading stamina and written explanation that Middle Years assessment will test two years later. Useful tuition at this stage is short, frequent and diagnostic: find the gap in place value or fractions, close it, and move on. Sessions run 30 to 45 minutes because attention, not timetable, is the limit.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in every private school from the primary years regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes organised for Arab and non-Arab students. A PYP family is therefore running two curricula at once from the start, and the Arabic strand is the one most often left unsupported until it becomes a Middle Years problem.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The Middle Years Programme marks against four criteria per subject, each lettered A to D and each with its own mark band, and the descriptors reward explanation and reflection as much as the right answer. Students who have been scoring well on content alone lose marks here for the first time and cannot see why. Tuition works best when it is aimed at a criterion rather than a topic: take the task the school has set, read the descriptor out loud, and rebuild the response against it.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years students in the UAE sit inside a school that is inspected on attainment and progress against both the programme standards and the emirate's own framework, whether that is a KHDA inspection rating in Dubai or an ADEK school rating in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. A Good or Very Good overall judgement is an average across the school, so it can sit comfortably on top of one department that cannot staff a subject properly.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is where the geography of tutoring breaks down completely. A student takes three subjects at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment marked in school and moderated externally. Finding someone nearby who has taught one of those six subjects is plausible. Finding someone nearby who has taught the specific Higher Level option your child's school chose, and marked its Internal Assessment, is mostly luck.
programmes.countryNote: UAE Diploma families carry an extra piece of administration no local search surfaces: the Ministry of Education equivalency file that converts a Diploma into a UAE-recognised secondary certificate for local university applications. The Ministry publishes explicit subject-and-grade rules for the British and American tracks. For the IB there is no points figure we are willing to print without reading it on moe.gov.ae, so treat any site that quotes one with scepticism and check the Ministry's own page.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs two or more Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a service-learning requirement and language development. It is offered by relatively few UAE schools, which makes the local tutor pool for its specific components very thin indeed. The Diploma courses inside it are marked exactly as they are for a full Diploma candidate, so the subject teaching is identical; the reflective project is where students need process coaching rather than content.
programmes.countryNote: Because few schools in the Emirates run it, a Career-related Programme family searching locally will often find nobody who has seen the reflective project assessment criteria at all. This is the clearest case for a national rather than a neighbourhood pool, and it is also the case where you should ask the Ministry of Education directly about equivalency rather than assume the Diploma rules transfer.

ib-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects UAE families ask for most, written as what the component actually demands rather than as a list of topics. Where a subject appears below with Higher Level named, the scarcity of a local specialist is the whole reason this page exists.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency carry the Higher Level paper, and the exploration is marked on criteria that reward genuine mathematical reasoning over presentation. Marks go missing in Paper 1 where no calculator is allowed and partial working is not shown. Students who arrived from a Middle Years course that leaned on a graphical display calculator feel this immediately.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-assisted problem solving dominate. The route is often chosen late and for the wrong reason. Before switching, check the published entry requirements of the specific university courses your child is aiming at, because some engineering and economics programmes name Analysis and Approaches. That check belongs in Year 11, not in the February of Year 13.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium account for most of the lost marks, and the scientific investigation is where able students most often underperform because the research question is too broad to control. The Higher Level extension topics are the single hardest thing to staff locally; this is the subject families most often cannot cover inside a driving radius.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields, circular motion and the unit-two mechanics work reward students who can convert a described situation into a free-body diagram quickly. Data analysis questions carry marks for uncertainty treatment that students skip under time pressure. Online lessons handle this well because the worked solution is built on a shared screen and stays available afterwards.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms decide the mark here more than in any other science. Explain, outline, suggest and evaluate each have a defined expectation, and a correct biological fact written against the wrong command term scores nothing. Tuition that drills the command term against the subject guide wording moves grades faster than more content revision.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, real-world application and the evaluation paragraph are the three marks students leave behind. The internal assessment commentaries must be built on recent news articles and kept inside a strict word limit, and the most common failure is a commentary that summarises the article instead of applying a named diagram to it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The case study paper rewards students who read the stimulus material as evidence rather than as background, and the Higher Level extension requires quantitative tools many candidates meet for the first time in Year 13. The project is marked on the quality of the research question and the use of primary or secondary data, not on the length of the appendix.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper on unseen non-literary texts are where UAE candidates with strong written English still lose marks, because both are assessed on close analysis of technique rather than on fluency. Preparation means repeated timed practice on unseen extracts with feedback on the analytical move, not on the vocabulary.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Arabic sits in two places for a UAE family at once: as an IB language acquisition subject with its own assessment, and as a Ministry-mandated school subject with its own class organisation and language-of-instruction rules. The two are marked differently and taught differently, and conflating them is the usual reason a strong student is doing badly in one of them.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case-study recall decides the extended-response marks, and most candidates carry too many cases at too shallow a depth. The fieldwork-based internal assessment needs a question narrow enough to collect real data against, which is harder in the Emirates than in the textbook examples and is worth planning with a specialist early.

ib-tutor-near-me.regionsTitle: What "near me" means in each emirate
ib-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: The same search produces a different result in each emirate, because the regulator, the school density and the realistic travel radius all change. Below is what a family in each place is actually working with, and which authority holds the school's file.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Regulated by KHDA, which published 227 private schools and 17 curricula for 2024-25 and confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for 2026-27. Highest school density in the country, so a local search returns the most results and the least filtering: plenty of generalists, few Higher Level specialists.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Distances between Khalifa City, the island and Al Reem mean an evening slot that works in September drifts by November, which is the practical argument against a tutor who has to drive at all.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, with a smaller IB school cluster than the coast. A family here searching for a Higher Level subject specialist within a sensible radius will frequently find nobody at all, and the fallback is usually a generalist who has not taught the component.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Many families live here and commute to a Dubai school, so the usable session window starts late and prayer times shape the evening.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. The local IB pool is small enough that proximity stops being a useful filter entirely, and the commute to a Dubai or Sharjah school already consumes the early evening.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Private education is regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which also approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. RAK is one of three emirates that returned zero mentions across the competitor pages reviewed for this page, which tells you how thin local coverage of these searches is.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the Ministry of Education. On the east coast, a search radius wide enough to include a subject specialist would include a mountain road, which is the clearest illustration on this page that distance and teaching quality are unrelated variables.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under Ministry of Education supervision. The smallest private-school market in the country, and the place where an online pool changes the answer most: the question moves from who is available here to who has taught this syllabus anywhere.

schoolClusters.note: The densest IB and IGCSE cluster in the Emirates, which is why Dubai families most often assume proximity solves the problem. Students we support attend schools across the city, and the pattern we see is a strong school with one department that cannot cover a Higher Level option in the year it is needed.

ADEK territory, with the IB and British clusters spread across the island, Khalifa City and Al Raha. Travel between them in the early evening is the reason families here move to live video first. Al Ain's smaller cluster means a subject-level specialist is rarely available locally at all.

Three different regulatory arrangements sit inside this cluster: SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Families often commute south to a Dubai school, which compresses the usable tuition window into a narrow evening slot.

modes.description: One subject, one tutor, the same time every week, booked around the school run rather than around a drive. The session follows your child's own school deadlines: the test on Thursday, the draft due at the end of the month, the topic the class is on now. A short written note after each lesson records what was covered and what to practise before the next one.

Past-paper questions are attempted under timed conditions by the student first, then marked and rebuilt against the published criteria. We reference official papers and mark schemes and link to the board's own site rather than redistributing them.

sections.heading: What a search for an IB tutor near me actually returns
paragraphs: A map result set is built from one input: a pin inside the area your screen is showing. Everything a parent actually wants to know sits outside that input. Whether the person has taught the Diploma rather than a national curriculum. Whether they have taught the subject at Higher Level rather than Standard. Whether they have ever marked the component your child is losing marks on. Whether they hold the permit the UAE requires. None of that is in the ranking signal, and none of it is in the distance.

The result set also reflects who has done the local marketing rather than who can teach. Agency pages built for a district name rank for that district name. A tuition centre with premises ranks because it has an address to verify. An independent teacher with fifteen years of Diploma Chemistry and no website does not appear at all. So the parent who searches IB tuition near me is reading a map of marketing spend, and reading it as a map of teaching quality.

The honest version is simpler. Proximity is only worth paying for if the thing you are buying has to be physically present. A violin lesson arguably does. A Mathematics exploration conversation does not: it needs a screen with the student's own working on it, a tutor who knows what criterion C is asking for, and an hour nobody has spent in a car. sections.heading: The nearest qualified adult is often the one person who may not take the work
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, not left to the market. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is issued through MoHRE, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without that permit is, in the Ministry's own words, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure appears on this page.

That eligibility list is where proximity collapses. The closest adult who already knows your child's syllabus, your child's teacher, and your child's actual weakness is their own subject teacher at school. Gulf News has reported that ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries the same restriction on serving students affiliated with their own school. We treat that as press-reported rather than as a quotation of policy, and any family relying on it should check the current ADEK document or ask the school directly.

Two practical consequences follow for a parent. First, never let a conversation start with the idea of hiring your child's own teacher privately, however convenient the drive. Second, the one checkable credential in this market is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and asking for it costs nothing. A tutor who holds it will show it. A tutor who deflects has told you something useful. The table sets out each category of person who might teach your child, where their permit comes from and what a parent can realistically verify.

sections.heading: Your address decides your regulator, and the regulator decides what you can ask for
paragraphs: Parents often assume the curriculum determines the oversight. It does not. The emirate does. A KHDA inspection rating covers a Dubai school whatever curriculum it teaches, and an ADEK school rating covers an Abu Dhabi or Al Ain one on a different framework. Sharjah's authority and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge go further than inspection: both approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. In Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools directly.

This matters to a tutoring decision in two concrete ways. It tells you where the inspection report lives, which is the single most useful free document a parent can read before spending anything. And it tells you who approved the fee schedule and the assessment arrangements, which is who to ask when the school's answer does not satisfy you. Across the competitor pages reviewed for this page, ADEK was named by nobody at all and Sharjah's authority appeared once, which is a fair measure of how little of this reaches parents.

Read the report at subject level, not at headline level. An overall judgement is an average across phases and departments. A school rated Very Good can hold one department that lost two specialists in August and is being covered by a generalist until January, and that is precisely the situation a parent diagnoses from the subject tables in the report rather than from the front page. The federal baseline sits underneath all of it: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

sections.heading: Distance to a tutor is not distance to a Higher Level specialist
paragraphs: A Diploma student takes six subjects, three of them at Higher Level, and the Higher Level extension material is where the grade is decided. The pool of adults who have taught that extension material, for that subject, and marked its Internal Assessment, is small in absolute terms anywhere in the world. Restricting it to a thirty-minute drive from a specific UAE address usually reduces it to zero, and a parent who does not know that reads the empty result as absence of need rather than absence of supply.

What happens next is predictable. The family hires the nearest available person who teaches the subject at any level, because the alternative looks like doing nothing. The sessions are pleasant, the content is revised, and the Higher Level paper still goes badly, because nobody in the room had seen the extension topics under exam conditions. This is the most common tutoring failure UAE families describe to us, and it is a supply problem dressed up as a motivation problem.

An IB Higher Level tutor online solves it by changing the search space rather than the search term. A family in Al Ain, Ras Al Khaimah or Fujairah gets the same pool as a family in Jumeirah. An IB Diploma tutor near me is a question about roads; a specialist in the component your child is losing marks on is a question about who has taught it. The list below is where we see local searches run out first, with the question to put to your school's IB coordinator before you spend anything.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges, and how much of it is the car
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. So here are the published AED bands, with the kind of provider that publishes each one and the date they were read. These are market rates, not an IB Gram price list. What IB Gram quotes depends on subject, level and session length, and it starts with a free trial lesson rather than a rate card you have to decode.

Read the bands as a function of two things: who is teaching, and what else is inside the fee. A university student working online sits at the bottom. A subject specialist who has taught the Diploma for a decade sits in the middle. A named examiner-led service sits at the top. The in-home band sits high for a reason that has nothing to do with teaching quality: the fee is carrying a car, a driver's hour and a fuel cost, and the parent is paying for all three at the teaching rate.

Monthly packages seen in this market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and roughly AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's published monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Set that against the KHDA confirmation of 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not rise in Dubai for 2026-27, and tuition is the part of the education budget still moving.

sections.heading: The hidden hour: what a visiting tutor costs in evening minutes
paragraphs: Cost in this market is usually discussed as a rate and almost never as time. That is the wrong unit for a school night. A UAE secondary student finishes the school run somewhere between half past three and half past five depending on the emirate and the bus route, needs food, and has homework the school set that day. The question is not what an hour costs. The question is how many of the remaining usable minutes the arrangement consumes, and how many of those minutes are teaching.

Do the arithmetic once and it settles the format argument without any marketing in it. Take a 60-minute lesson with a tutor who lives ten minutes away and arrives at six. Add the doorstep, the settling, the drink, the small talk with a parent and the pack-up: the household has given up roughly eighty minutes to buy sixty. Now move that tutor across a city in the five-to-seven window. The hour is unchanged, the arrival time is not, and a slot that drifts week to week is the slot that eventually gets cancelled.

Live video costs about sixty-five minutes of the evening for sixty minutes of teaching, and the five are spent logging in. It also produces artefacts a visit does not: a shared screen with the student's own working annotated on it, a worked solution that stays on file, and a recording of the explanation they can replay the night before the test. None of that is an argument that screens are warmer than rooms. It is an argument about where the minutes go.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies: the timetable nobody searches for
paragraphs: Every UAE family running an international curriculum is actually running two. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai's private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. The federal position sits underneath that: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

The rules are more specific than most parents realise, and they constrain tutoring directly. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic must be the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is delivered in Arabic for Arab students; non-Arab students take Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two further details matter. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length as long as the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. And for these subjects the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the Ministry of Education, is strictly prohibited. That last line is why a tutor supporting Arabic or Islamic Education should be working from the school's own prescribed material and the student's own set work, not from an imported workbook.

sections.heading: The exam timetable your postcode sits inside
paragraphs: Here is a geography fact about examinations that no local search will ever surface. Cambridge International allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, and the guidance to exams officers is blunt: it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Your child's paper time is therefore a function of where the centre sits, which is the one sense in which near me genuinely decides something.

The second thing nobody tells parents is how far in front of the paper the real deadlines fall. Take the Cambridge March 2027 series as the worked example, because its key dates are published. The exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027. Final entries were due on 27 November 2026, more than two months before the first paper. Forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. A family that starts looking for support in February is looking after the entry decision has already been made.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSEs run in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always open the live official PDF rather than trusting a restated date. For the IB we publish no session or results date here: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so confirm every IB date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org itself.

sections.heading: Academic honesty does not change with distance
paragraphs: There is a part of this market that sells completed Internal Assessments. One site found during the research for these pages advertises them at a fixed price. Buying one puts a student's entire Diploma at risk, because submitting work that is not their own is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the candidate, not the vendor. No proximity, convenience or price argument survives that. It is worth saying plainly on a page about finding a tutor, because the same search results contain both kinds of provider and they look alike from outside.

So here is the boundary IB Gram works to, in operational terms. A tutor may teach the underlying skill, explain what a criterion is asking for, model a different problem of the same type, ask the questions a supervisor would ask, read the student's own draft and say which descriptor it is not meeting, and help plan a research question that can actually be answered. A tutor may not write any part of the work, rewrite a passage into its final form, supply a near-match exemplar to be adapted, or produce data the student did not collect. IB Internal Assessment feedback means feedback, and it is given on the student's own writing.

The same restraint applies to materials. We reference IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and subject guides by citing them and linking to the official site; we do not reproduce or distribute them. A tutor who offers you a folder of mark schemes, a bank of completed exemplars or a topic-matched essay to work from is offering something that is either a copyright problem or an honesty problem, and often both. Ask the question directly at the trial lesson and listen to how fast the answer comes.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and the one number nobody should publish
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process that converts an international school certificate into a UAE-recognised one, and it is the piece of administration that most often surprises a family in the final year. The Ministry publishes explicit requirements for the British and American tracks. On the British track, a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

One detail in that rule is worth reading twice, because a ranking competitor page gets it wrong: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. A site telling UAE candidates they must take six IGCSE subjects is publishing an inflated figure. On the American track, English proficiency is demonstrated by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying.

For MoE equivalency for IB students there is no points figure on this page, and you should be wary of any page that gives you one. The source we read for the British and American tracks states no IB threshold, so printing one would be an invention. Check moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority directly. Equivalency is also not something IB Gram performs, submits or influences, and no amount of tutoring is required for it. Tuition is for the grades; the paperwork is a separate administrative track with its own official channel.
