sections.heading: Sitting the papers through the school, or as a private candidate
paragraphs: Most UAE students are entered by their school, which acts as the exam centre and owns the entry deadline. That deadline sits much earlier than families expect. Cambridge's published key dates for one March series show final entries due on 27 November, forecast grades due on 27 February, the exam period running from 3 February to 4 March, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. The entry closed more than two months before the first paper.

A private-candidate entry is the other route, and it exists for specific situations: a subject the school does not offer, a resit after the school has moved on, a child educated at home, or a student whose school declines an Extended entry the family believes the evidence supports. The entry is made through a centre that accepts private candidates, and the family carries the administration the school would otherwise have handled.

The complication is components. A subject with coursework or a supervised practical element is harder to enter privately, because somebody has to supervise and authenticate that work. In practice this pushes private candidates towards subjects assessed entirely by written paper, or towards the alternative-to-practical route where the specification offers one. Checking the specification before committing to a private entry saves a wasted series.

Coaching changes shape for a private candidate. Nobody is setting homework, nobody is marking mocks, and nobody is watching the deadlines. The coach ends up carrying the scheduling discipline the school would normally supply, which means the plan has to be written down with dates against it from the first session rather than drifting towards the exam.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in the same week as nine IGCSEs
paragraphs: A UAE timetable is fuller than a British one, and the reason is regulatory rather than academic. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. The federal position behind that is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies.

The organisational detail matters for any coaching plan. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language.

Instructional time is specified too. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Which means the hours are real hours out of a Year 11 week, sitting next to nine or ten IGCSE subjects and whatever revision the family has planned.

There is one firm limit on what outside support can do here. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited. So coaching in this space is about access skills rather than alternative material: reading fluency, formal register, structuring a written answer in Arabic, and understanding what the school's own assessment is asking for. Anything that looks like a substitute curriculum is outside the rules the school has to work within.

sections.heading: Arriving mid-course: moving into IGCSE from another system
paragraphs: UAE schools absorb transfers constantly, and an IGCSE block is an awkward thing to join halfway. The qualification is two years of cumulative content with a tier entry already submitted in some subjects, so a child arriving in Year 10 or Year 11 is joining a race partway round. The receiving school confirms placement, but the gap analysis is usually nobody's job, and that is where families lose a term.

The gaps are predictable by system of origin. A student from an Indian-curriculum school often arrives strong on procedural mathematics and weaker on extended written answers and data-response technique. A student from an American middle school usually has the writing but not the algebraic fluency Extended maths assumes. A student from a Ministry-curriculum school may be strong in Arabic and Social Studies and meeting English-medium science vocabulary for the first time.

Emirate authorities approve curricula school by school rather than harmonising them, so two licensed schools in the same emirate can follow different schemes of work for the same code. A transfer within the UAE is therefore not automatically smooth, and a transfer between emirates adds a change of regulator on top. Ask the receiving school which code each subject is entered for, and ask for the scheme of work rather than a reading list.

Coaching for a transfer student should start with a diagnostic rather than a syllabus. The useful first question is not what the child has covered but what the new specification assumes they already have. sections.heading: What IGCSE coaching costs across the UAE market
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which no UAE family transacts in. The figures below are IGCSE coaching rates in AED per hour as published by the providers named, read in October 2026. They are market rates, not IB Gram's price list, and they are set out so a parent can tell whether a quote is ordinary or exceptional before agreeing to it.

The range is wide for understandable reasons. At the bottom end sit university students and generalist online platforms. In the middle sit qualified subject teachers working online. Above that sit specialists in a particular board and tier, and above them a small premium tier of named practitioners. A home visit adds the travel to the hour, which is why in-home figures start higher than online figures for the same quality of teaching.

Two things move a quote more than anything else. The first is the month you start: a Year 11 family booking in February for a May or June series is buying scarce time, and scarcity sets prices. The second is the specificity of the ask. A generalist maths tutor is plentiful; an Extended-tier Additional Mathematics specialist who knows the current code is not, and the second one costs more because fewer people can do it.

IB Gram does not publish an hourly rate on this page because the honest answer depends on subject, tier and the time of year, and a number invented for a landing page helps nobody. What we do publish is the model: one-to-one over live video, a trial lesson at no charge with no card required and one per family, and a written plan before any block is agreed.

sections.heading: A coach in the room against a coach on a screen, under UAE conditions
paragraphs: Families searching for IGCSE coaching in the UAE often picture someone arriving at the villa on a Tuesday evening, and the market will sell that. It is worth understanding what it actually buys. A visiting coach is selected from the people willing to drive to your address in the evening peak, which in practice means a radius of perhaps twenty to thirty minutes. The teaching pool is defined by geography rather than by who knows the specification.

The travel also has a price, and it appears in the published figures: home-visit rates in this market start higher than online rates for comparable teaching, with Bestimate's range running from AED 180 to 350 and home tutors quoted from AED 200 to 500. Part of that difference is the drive. For families in Al Ain, Fujairah, Ras Al Khaimah or Umm Al Quwain the drive is long enough that the specialist simply is not available at any sensible price.

IB Gram delivers IGCSE coaching for UAE families as one-to-one tuition over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send a coach to an address anywhere in the Emirates; home visits are a service we run in India only. That is a straightforward trade: a family gives up a person in the room and gets a coach chosen for the board, the code and the tier rather than for the postcode, with no travel in the price and no cancelled session because of an accident on Sheikh Zayed Road.

The comparison below is the case on its merits rather than a sales argument. Some children genuinely do better with someone beside them, and a family who wants that should buy it locally with eyes open about the pool they are choosing from. Most IGCSE problems, though, are specification problems, and specification problems are solved by the right specialist on a screen more reliably than by the nearest available adult.

sections.heading: The UAE term year against an IGCSE series, counted in both directions
paragraphs: A British revision calendar does not map onto a UAE school year. Terms start in late August or early September, the long winter break lands in December, Ramadan moves earlier each year and shortens the school day while it lasts, and Eid takes a variable block out of the spring term. A coaching plan built on a generic calendar will schedule its hardest work in the weeks the family has least capacity.

Counting from the other direction, the dates that genuinely lock are set by the boards and published by them. Cambridge's key dates for one March series put final entries on 27 November, forecast grades on 27 February, the exam window from 3 February to 4 March, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and its June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day.

IGCSE coaching during Ramadan is a scheduling question rather than a pedagogical one. The school day shortens, energy drops in the afternoon, and the sensible move is to pull sessions later into the evening and to use the period for consolidation and past-paper marking rather than for new content. Families who plan that in September rather than discovering it in the second week lose nothing from the term.

The table reads the UAE year as a sequence of things the school is doing and things a coaching plan should be doing alongside. It is deliberately not a list of exam dates: board timetables are revised, Cambridge zones differ, and the only safe source for a specific date is the school's own zone timetable or the live official timetable on the board's site.

sections.heading: Coursework, past papers and the line a coach does not cross
paragraphs: This market contains businesses that sell finished assessed work. One of them offers completed Internal Assessments at a published price. For a student, accepting that is a malpractice finding and potentially the loss of the qualification; for the family it is money spent on a risk nobody disclosed. The boundary is therefore worth stating on a page about coaching rather than leaving to a terms-and-conditions link.

What a coach does is teach method, model technique on a different example, and give feedback on work the student has already produced themselves. What a coach does not do is supply text, sentences, structure written out for copying, or an improved version to be submitted. The practical test is simple: if the student could not explain every line of what they are submitting, it is not theirs, and an examiner asking a follow-up question will find that out.

Past papers and mark schemes sit in a related place. These are copyright documents belonging to Cambridge and Pearson. A coach can work through them with a student and cite where they came from; a provider should not be reproducing them as downloads or presenting unreleased material at all. Any provider offering a library of mark schemes as a selling point is worth a question about where those documents came from.

The same honesty applies to what we claim. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and nothing on this page should be read as implying one. We name those bodies to explain how the system works. Separately, private tuition in the UAE runs on a permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you either.

process.title: Send the statement of entry, or the codes in writing
process.description: The first thing we ask for is not a description of the problem but the board and code for each subject, ideally from the statement of entry. Without it a coach is guessing between Cambridge and Pearson specifications that look similar and examine differently. If the document has not been issued yet, the school office will confirm the codes by email.

process.title: A diagnostic session, not a sales call
process.description: One session on the subject in question, working through questions from the correct code at the entered tier. The output is a short written note: what is secure, what is not, and whether the tier entry looks right on the evidence. Families use that note in the conversation with the school as often as they use it with us.

process.title: Match to a coach by code and tier
process.description: We match on the specification rather than on location, which is the whole reason the delivery is online. A family in Umm Al Quwain and a family in Jumeirah draw on the same pool. Where a subject at a particular tier has no coach free at the requested time, we say so and give a date rather than filling the slot with a generalist.

process.title: A trial lesson at no charge, one per family
process.description: One lesson with the matched coach before anything is paid, with no card required at booking. The point is to see whether the child talks to this particular adult, which is not a thing any profile can tell you. If the match is wrong, we rematch once at no charge before any block starts.

process.title: A written plan with dates on it
process.description: Before a block is agreed, the plan is written down: number of sessions, the slot in Gulf Standard Time, the topics in order, the school deadlines and the series the work is building towards. Ramadan and the Eid break are placed in the plan at the outset. Plans change, but they change against a document rather than a memory.

process.title: Review at the mock, then again at entry
process.description: Two fixed review points rather than continuous reassurance. The mock script is the most honest diagnostic of the year and is read properly, question by question. The entry deadline is the second, because tier and series decisions stop being reversible there. Both reviews are written, so a parent can see what changed and why.

whyPoints.title: The code comes before the coach
whyPoints.description: Every match starts from the board and syllabus code on the statement of entry, because Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examine the same subjects differently. A coach working from the wrong specification can teach well for months and still leave a student unprepared for the papers they will actually sit.

whyPoints.title: Specialist pool instead of a driving radius
whyPoints.description: Delivery over live video means the choice of coach is not limited to whoever will drive to your address in the evening peak. For Extended-tier sciences, Additional Mathematics and the less common codes, that difference is the difference between a specialist and the nearest available adult, particularly outside Dubai and Abu Dhabi.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed, or not published
whyPoints.description: The AED rates on this page are market figures with the provider named and the month they were read. We publish no invented hourly price, no satisfaction percentage, no star rating and no outcome statistic, because a number without a source behind it is worth nothing to a parent comparing quotes.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary stated, not buried
whyPoints.description: Coaching here means teaching, modelling and feedback on the student's own work. We do not supply assessed work, redraft a submission to completion, or trade in mark schemes. That is a real difference from parts of this market, and it is stated on the page rather than left to a document nobody opens.

whyPoints.title: Built around the system, not around Britain
whyPoints.description: The regulator above the school, the mandatory UAE subject block, the Ministry of Education equivalency route and the Cambridge zone timetable all change what a sensible plan looks like. A plan copied from UK guidance will miss all four, and most of the guidance a UAE parent finds online is copied from UK guidance.

whyPoints.title: Availability disclosed before you pay
whyPoints.description: Where no coach is free for a subject at a tier and time, we give a date rather than filling the slot. Where a UAE-based coach is unavailable, we say which pool the match is coming from. No competing page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, and the limit is the thing a family needs to plan around.

faqs.question: Does IGCSE coaching have to follow the exact syllabus my child's school is licensed to teach?
faqs.answer: It has to follow the specification the school has entered your child for, which is a narrower thing than the school's licensed curriculum. The emirate authority approves the curriculum; the board and code decide what is on the paper. A school licensed for the UK curriculum might enter Cambridge for sciences and Pearson for mathematics in the same year group. So coaching should be built from the code on the statement of entry, not from the school's curriculum label. Ask the school office for the codes in writing before the first session if the statement has not been issued yet.

faqs.question: Our school entered my daughter for Cambridge, but her tutor has been teaching Edexcel material. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It matters more than it looks. Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE cover similar subject content but differ on paper structure, weightings, tiering language, practical assessment and grade scale. A past paper from the wrong board reads as plausible, so a student will work through it without noticing, and the questions that do not transfer tend to be the ones separating the top grades. Check the code on the statement of entry, then ask the coach to work only from that board's materials. If several months have gone on the wrong specification, a diagnostic session against the correct papers will show how much is genuinely transferable.

faqs.question: One of my children has letter grades and the other has numbers. Which scale does a UAE university actually read?
faqs.answer: Both, because they are different qualifications. Cambridge IGCSE reports A* to G. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports 9 to 1, and some Cambridge syllabuses are graded 9 to 1 for UK centres. Universities read each certificate against its own scale rather than converting between them. For a UAE file the number that matters is the Ministry of Education equivalency floor: as reported when the Ministry clarified requirements in July 2026, the British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3. Confirm the current rule on moe.gov.ae before relying on it.

faqs.question: If the school refuses an Extended entry we think the evidence supports, who can we take that to?
faqs.answer: The tier entry is the school's decision, made on internal assessment, so the first step is to ask what evidence it rests on and when it is reviewed. That question is more productive with evidence attached, which is what a coached block of timed Extended papers produces. If the conversation stalls, the school is licensed by an emirate authority: KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, or the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah those authorities also approve assessment methods.

faqs.question: Which of the IGCSE series makes sense for a resit, and how far ahead do we need to decide?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with a March series available in some regions, and Pearson offers May or June plus November. The decision point is the entry deadline rather than the exam. Cambridge's published key dates for one March series show final entries due on 27 November for a window running 3 February to 4 March, so the entry closes over two months before the paper. Pearson's November results have reached students in late January. Work backwards from the live official timetable on the board's own site, because provisional dates can be revised.

faqs.question: Does a school inspection report tell a parent anything useful about where to spend on coaching?
faqs.answer: More than the headline band does. Read the sections rather than the summary: attainment tells you where the cohort sits against curriculum standards, progress tells you what the school adds, and the two can disagree. High attainment with modest progress is the pattern where a capable child drifts. The judgement on assessment is the one most relevant to tier entry, because tier decisions rest on internal evidence. A weaker assessment judgement gives you a documented reason to ask how a Core entry was arrived at. A strong overall band does not mean no child in the school needs help.

faqs.question: We have just moved to Dubai from an Indian-curriculum school in Year 9. What does the jump into IGCSE involve?
faqs.answer: Usually a smaller content gap than families fear and a larger technique gap than they expect. Students arriving from CBSE or ICSE are often strong on procedural mathematics and less practised at extended written answers, data-response questions and the command-term discipline IGCSE marking rewards. The first priority is confirming which board and code the receiving school will enter each subject for, and whether the tier decision has already been made. A diagnostic session against the actual papers is worth more than a reading list. Expect roughly ten to sixteen weeks of support per affected subject before internal assessments settle.

faqs.question: Can a parent check that a coach is permitted to tutor in the UAE, and what should the permit cover?
faqs.answer: Private tuition here runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Ask to see it, and ask who the holder's employer is, because the permit carries a code of conduct. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount quoted at you as unverified.

faqs.question: Does the Ministry of Education count all nine of my son's IGCSE subjects, or only some of them?
faqs.answer: Only some. As reported when the Ministry clarified equivalency requirements in July 2026, the British track requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. At least one competing site in this market publishes six, which is a useful reminder to verify on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority rather than trusting a tutoring page, including this one.

faqs.question: The Arabic lesson is timetabled against my daughter's Chemistry option. What can coaching do about a clash like that?
faqs.answer: Nothing about the timetable itself, which is the school's to set under the terms of its licence. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA calculates the time on a 40-minute lesson unit with a minimum of 25 minutes per lesson. What coaching can do is recover the taught content she misses in the subject that loses out, working from the school's own scheme of work. Raise the clash with the school early: option blocks are easier to adjust in September than in February.

faqs.question: Ramadan falls inside our revision term. How should that change the coaching plan?
faqs.answer: Plan it in September rather than reacting in the second week. The school day shortens, afternoon capacity drops across the whole household, and Eid removes a variable block afterwards. The practical adjustments are to move sessions later into the evening, to use the period for consolidation and past-paper marking rather than new content, and to protect the weeks immediately after Eid for the heavier work. Written plans survive this better than informal arrangements, because everyone can see what was moved and where it landed. Session slots through Ramadan typically run after Iftar, in Gulf Standard Time as usual.

faqs.question: How many coached hours does one IGCSE subject usually absorb across Years 10 and 11?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is being fixed. A weekly slot across both years is roughly sixty to seventy sessions, which is the pattern that costs least per session and catches misconceptions within days. A targeted block starting in January of Year 11 for a May or June series is usually twelve to twenty sessions per subject, depending on how much content is secure. A single diagnostic plus a tier-evidence block before entry can be as few as six. Buying weekly from Year 10 is almost always cheaper than buying the emergency block families end up with in Year 11.

faqs.question: Can the same coach take Maths and Chemistry for one IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because a single coach sees patterns across both subjects that two coaches miss: the same weakness in rearranging formulae shows up in Chemistry calculations and in Extended maths. But the limit is the specification. A coach should hold the actual code for both, at the entered tier, rather than general competence in science and mathematics. Where that combination is not available at the time you want, two specialists matched to their own codes is the better outcome than one generalist covering both approximately.

faqs.question: Nobody is free for Business Studies at the time that suits us. What happens then?
faqs.answer: We say so and give you a date, rather than filling the slot with someone who does not hold the code. Where a UAE-based coach is not available for a subject at a tier and time, we tell you which pool the match is coming from before anything is paid, including when that is outside the Emirates. Evening slots between 17:00 and 19:00 Gulf Standard Time are the tightest, so a family with flexibility on the hour usually gets matched faster. No competing page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, which is exactly the information a plan needs.

faqs.question: Is coaching delivered the same way in Ajman and Umm Al Quwain as in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, because it is delivered over live video in all seven emirates. The coach is matched to the board, code and tier rather than to a location, so a family in Umm Al Quwain draws on the same pool as a family in Jumeirah. IB Gram does not send a coach to any UAE address; home visits are a service we run in India only. What does differ further north is the school commute, which pushes a realistic weekday start past 17:00 Gulf Standard Time, and the local supply of Extended-tier specialists, which is thin enough that video is the only route to one.

faqs.question: Do you coach the UAE mandatory subjects, or only the IGCSE option subjects?
faqs.answer: We work on the access skills around Arabic, and we are careful about the limit. For the mandatory subjects, KHDA guidance states that the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, and schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. So coaching here means reading fluency, formal register and structuring a written answer, built from the school's own material. It does not mean a parallel curriculum. If the subject is examined as Cambridge 0508 or 0544, the code decides the approach.

igcse-coaching.closingHeading: Start with the code, not with the panic
igcse-coaching.closingBody: Most IGCSE problems in the UAE are not teaching problems. They are system problems: a tier entry made on thin evidence, a coach working from the wrong board, a Ministry subject block nobody accounted for, an entry deadline that closed in November. Send us the statement of entry or the codes in writing, take a diagnostic session, and read the written note that comes out of it. If the answer is that the school has this covered and nothing needs buying, that is a useful answer too. If coaching does make sense, you will be buying it for a named code at a known tier, at a slot in Gulf Standard Time, with the plan and the dates written down before anything is paid.

Each profile names the syllabus codes they have taught and the papers they set practice on. Pick two, request a free trial lesson with both, and compare how each one handles the same past-paper question.

intro.heading: Start with the date on the entry form, not with the subject
paragraphs: Most searches for IGCSE home tuition in the UAE happen in one of two weeks of the year: the week January mock results come home, and the week in April when a parent counts the Fridays that are left. Both are late. Not fatally late, because a Year 11 student can still move several grades in twelve weeks of structured work. But late enough that the decisions with the longest reach have already been taken by somebody else. The tier on the entry form is fixed. The subject count is fixed. Any coursework mark is largely banked.

The useful opening question is not how to find a tutor. It is which series your child is sitting, and what should already be done. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with a March series used by centres in some regions, and Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November each year. Those are the only clocks that matter. Your child's centre sits in one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge is explicit that the zone decides which version of the timetable applies.

So this page is organised as a countdown rather than a brochure. It starts at paper one and walks backwards: the final entry deadline, the forecast-grade form, the coursework and practical windows, the twelve-week revision block, results day and the two short windows that follow it. Each milestone names who sets it, because roughly half are set by the board and half by your child's own school, and a parent who confuses the two tends to miss the one that could still have been acted on.

IB Gram delivers IGCSE home tuition as one-to-one online tuition. There is no visiting-tutor service anywhere in the Emirates; household visits are something we run only in India. That is said here rather than discovered in week three, and the first table below puts the two formats beside each other on price, travel and the size of the pool a family gets to choose from. For scale: market rates for a visiting tutor in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour once travel is inside the price, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, on figures published by Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table and by agencies including Unitors.

Nothing here assumes anything about your child's school except that it is a private school in the UAE. That means it answers to KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, or the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Those bodies touch a tutoring plan in two concrete ways. They set the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons that share your child's week with physics revision, and in Dubai and Abu Dhabi they publish inspection reports you can read before deciding whether the gap sits with your child or with the teaching.
bullets: Cambridge's final entry deadline for the March 2027 series fell on 27 November 2026, roughly ten weeks before the first paper.
Forecast grades for that same March series are due on 27 February 2027, after the exam period has already opened.
Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs to 19 November 2026; its June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026.
Core and Extended is a tier chosen on an entry form, not a difficulty setting a tutor can adjust in April.
Every lesson is delivered one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram runs no visiting-tutor service in the Emirates.

igcse-home-tuition.programmesIntro: IGCSE is one qualification with two main examining boards in the UAE and two tiers inside most of its subjects. The four routes below are the ones a UAE family actually meets, and each carries its own calendar. Find the one your child's school uses: the syllabus numbering tells you the board, and the board tells you which timetable, which entry deadline and which results date apply to your house.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The four-digit syllabus codes starting 0 are Cambridge: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English. Most sciences and mathematics are tiered, so a candidate is entered either for Core papers or for Extended papers, and the entry fixes which. Assessment is almost entirely by terminal written paper, which is why the revision block before the series carries so much of the grade and why the entry deadline matters more than parents expect.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the wrong zone timetable is the centre's risk, since it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper. Ask your child's exams officer, in writing, which zone the school sits in and for the zone-correct timetable PDF. UAE centres also have access to the March series as well as June and November, which widens the resit options a family has.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The codes beginning with a digit and two letters are Pearson: 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PM1 Further Pure Mathematics, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A. Grading runs on the 9 to 1 scale. Several Pearson subjects are available in a modular shape, where a unit can be sat in an earlier series and carried forward, which changes a revision plan completely: some of the marks are already on the table before Year 11 begins.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes International GCSE series in May/June and November, and its November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the next day; the November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also issues provisional timetables for future series, including International GCSE November 2027, so a UAE family should plan from the live official PDF rather than from a date copied off a tutoring page.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The two years before IGCSE are where the arithmetic, algebraic fluency and written structure that IGCSE papers assume are either built or quietly skipped. Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and those results are a far better predictor of an IGCSE grade than a school report, because they are externally marked against a published standard rather than against the rest of the class.
programmes.countryNote: In a UAE school a Year 9 Checkpoint result arriving in May or October is the cheapest early-warning signal a family will get. A weak Checkpoint mathematics mark in October of Year 9 is four school terms of runway before the first IGCSE paper, at a tutoring cost roughly a third of what the same gap costs to close in the February of Year 11. Most families only discover this after the expensive version.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level
programmes.description: The qualification many UAE IGCSE students move into, sat in the same June and November series pattern and in the same zone system. It matters at the IGCSE stage for one reason: sixth-form entry conditions are written in IGCSE grades, usually as a minimum in the subject plus a minimum in mathematics or English. The grade a Year 11 needs is therefore not an abstract target but a published number on a school's own admissions page.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3. That makes AS and A Level choices part of the same paperwork chain as the IGCSE grades, and worth sketching out before the Year 11 options form is signed.

igcse-home-tuition.subjectsIntro: Subjects are listed by syllabus code because that is the unit of work a tutor actually prepares for. 0580 and 4MA1 are both called IGCSE Mathematics and they are not the same paper, the same mark scheme or the same tier structure. Tell us the code from your child's exam entry or the front of their past-paper booklet and the match becomes a straightforward question.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 Cambridge, 4MA1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Extended papers carry algebraic manipulation, functions, trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles and probability trees that Core does not reach. Marks go missing in the same three places every series: unsimplified algebraic fractions, bearings questions where the diagram is never drawn, and multi-step problems abandoned halfway because no working was written down. Method marks are recoverable without the right answer, and most students do not know that.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics (0606, 4PM1)
subjects.description: The bridge subject for anyone heading to A Level Mathematics or an engineering route. Calculus, binomial expansion, logarithms and vectors appear here before they appear in the sixth form. The usual failure is treating it as harder 0580 rather than as a different habit: these papers reward setting up a problem symbolically before touching a calculator, and students trained on numerical substitution stall in the first five minutes.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 Cambridge, 4PH1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism are where the Extended tier separates from the Core, and where a UAE cohort usually loses the most marks. Circuit questions require reasoning about potential difference rather than recall. The practical paper and the alternative-to-practical paper test graph plotting, anomalous-result identification and precision of apparatus description, all of which can be practised on paper and all of which are routinely left until the final month.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 Cambridge, 4CH1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry, then organic chemistry, in that order of difficulty for most candidates. The recurring loss is in calculation presentation: an answer given without units, to the wrong number of significant figures, or with the limiting reagent never identified. Qualitative analysis questions on ion tests are nearly free marks and are nearly always under-revised because they feel like memorisation rather than chemistry.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 Cambridge, 4BI1 Pearson)
subjects.description: The content volume makes this feel like a reading subject, which is the trap. Extended papers ask for explanation chains, so a student who writes that stomata close in heat without linking water loss, guard-cell turgor and gas exchange gets one mark where three were available. Transport in plants, osmosis practicals and genetic-cross notation are the three topics most worth timetabling early.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (0654, 0653)
subjects.description: Common in UAE schools where a student takes sciences as one or two blocks rather than three separate subjects. The syllabus is a selected subset of the three single sciences, which means a tutor who teaches it from the single-science specification will cover material that is not assessed. Checking the exact syllabus code before the first lesson prevents paying for several hours of content your child will never be examined on.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500 Cambridge, 4EA1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended-response questions carry the bulk of the grade, and both are assessed on structure and register as much as on content. Most marks are lost by students who summarise rather than analyse, and by students who write long. A timed-planning routine, practised weekly from October, moves this subject more reliably than any amount of vocabulary work.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510, 0511)
subjects.description: Widely taken across UAE schools and often the subject that quietly decides a sixth-form or equivalency outcome. Reading comprehension questions reward precise lifting of the relevant phrase rather than paraphrase, and the writing tasks are marked against register, audience and task fulfilment. Speaking components are assessed internally by the school, so the school's own window, not the board's, sets that deadline.

subjects.name: Economics (0455 Cambridge, 4EC1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Diagram-led. A supply and demand diagram with unlabelled axes or no shift arrow earns nothing, however good the prose around it. Students who revise definitions and neglect diagram drills tend to plateau around the middle grades. Data-response questions also require quoting figures from the extract, which is a technique rather than knowledge and takes about three sessions to fix.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450 Cambridge, 4BS1 Pearson)
subjects.description: The case-study paper rewards application to the named business, and generic answers about motivation or cash flow score in the lowest band regardless of accuracy. Evaluation marks go to candidates who commit to a judgement and justify it. Ratio and break-even calculations are a dependable source of marks for a student who finds the written side harder.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478 Cambridge)
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and the theory of data representation. Students who code confidently in Python often lose marks because the paper wants Cambridge pseudocode conventions, not working code. Binary and hexadecimal conversion, logic gates and the fetch-execute cycle are high-frequency, low-cost topics that reward deliberate drilling in the twelve weeks before the papers.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First and as a Foreign Language (0508, 0544)
subjects.description: Taken alongside the international curriculum in UAE schools and examined in the same series as every other IGCSE. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, so a tutor must be matched to the correct pathway rather than to the subject name alone.

igcse-home-tuition.regionsIntro: The emirate your child's school sits in changes three practical things: which authority publishes the inspection report you can read, who approves the school's curriculum and fees, and how crowded the early-evening tutoring slot is locally. Delivery itself is identical everywhere, because lessons are one-to-one over live video. The notes below are about calendars and oversight, not about travel times.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA oversees the quality of private education in the emirate, and its mandatory-subject requirements applied from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Dubai had 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools in 2024-25, with 37 per cent on a UK curriculum, which is why Cambridge and Pearson entry deadlines dominate the local calendar.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, as press-reported in 2026, so the convenient option a parent is sometimes offered is the one to decline.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a smaller British-curriculum cohort than Abu Dhabi island. That matters at entry time rather than at lesson time: fewer local centres means fewer alternatives if a subject is dropped from a timetable, so confirming the entry list with the exams officer in November is worth more here than almost anywhere.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Curriculum approval sitting with the regulator is a useful fact for a parent: the subject list a school offers is not purely a school decision, so a mid-year subject change is rarely quick.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools here. For an IGCSE family that means inspection reporting is less locally granular than Dubai's, so the published evidence to lean on is the school's own results profile and the externally marked Checkpoint results rather than an emirate inspection band.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. Families here often sit exams at a centre some distance from home, which makes the zone-correct timetable and the exam-day logistics worth confirming in writing well before February.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under the federal Ministry of Education, with a small number of British-curriculum cohorts. The practical consequence for tuition is availability of specialist subjects rather than of tutors generally: Further Pure Mathematics or Computer Science may have no local specialist at all, which is precisely the case online delivery answers.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. The smallest IGCSE cohort of the seven emirates, and the clearest example of why a family should not be limited to tutors within driving distance: a single Extended-tier physics specialist may not exist inside the emirate in a given term.

schoolClusters.note: Students we support sit IGCSE at schools across this group, which run Cambridge and Pearson entries side by side. Several enter different boards for different subjects, so one household can be working to two timetables at once. Confirming board and tier per subject is the first thing a plan needs.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain cluster
schoolClusters.note: A smaller British-curriculum group under ADEK, where sixth-form entry conditions published by the schools themselves are the clearest statement of what IGCSE grades a student needs. Those published conditions make a better revision target than a general ambition to improve.

Sharjah, Ajman and Ras Al Khaimah schools where cohorts are smaller and specialist subject teaching is thinner on the ground. This is the cluster where a family most often finds that the subject they need help with has no local specialist available in exam term.

igcse-home-tuition.modesIntro: Four shapes of support, chosen by where you are in the countdown rather than by budget alone. A Year 10 family and a Year 11 family eleven weeks from paper one should not buy the same thing. All four are delivered one-to-one over live video, with a free trial lesson before any block is committed.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one across Years 10 and 11
modes.description: One or two sessions a week, running with the school's scheme of work rather than ahead of it, so that each topic is consolidated while it is still being taught. This is the cheapest way to arrive at the February of Year 11 without a backlog, and the format where a tutor can actually build the exam technique a paper rewards rather than patching content.

A past-paper question set after each topic, marked against the official mark scheme

modes.title: The twelve-week series block
modes.description: A fixed block running from roughly twelve weeks before paper one to the final study leave, built around papers rather than topics. Sessions move to two or three a week, each one anchored on a timed question set under exam conditions, with the marking done together so the student sees where the mark scheme actually awards credit.
bullets: Zone-correct timetable used to order the subjects by paper date
Timed sections rather than whole papers in the first six weeks
Mark-scheme reading as a taught skill, not an afterthought
A written stop rule for topics that are not worth more hours

modes.title: Coursework and practical-skills clinics
modes.description: Short, specific sessions on the components that are marked inside the school or that test practical reasoning on paper: the alternative-to-practical papers, graph and error analysis, and the planning and evaluation skills a science paper assesses. The student's own work stays the student's own work throughout; the session teaches the technique and reviews what the student has written.
bullets: Graph plotting, anomalous results and precision of description
Planning an investigation to the criteria a paper actually rewards
Feedback on a draft the student wrote, never text written for them
Your school's internal deadline treated as the hard date

modes.title: The between-series resit sprint
modes.description: For a student moving from a June result to a November entry, or from November to the following March or June. The window is short and the content is already taught, so the work is diagnostic: read the statement of results, identify which papers cost the grade, and spend the available weeks on those papers rather than on a full re-teach of the syllabus.
bullets: Component-level reading of the statement of results
Entry confirmed with the exams officer before any hours are bought
Plan written in weeks remaining, not in topics remaining
Explicit decision on which subjects are not worth re-entering

sections.heading: What a UAE family is actually buying when they search for IGCSE home tuition
paragraphs: A search for IGCSE home tuition in the UAE is a search for a private, one-to-one hour with somebody who knows the papers. The word home describes where the parent expects the lesson to happen, not what the lesson is. Once the format question is separated from the teaching question, the two can be answered honestly and in order, and the answers turn out to point in different directions for most families in the Emirates.

The market answer for a visiting tutor is a real one. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts a household visit at roughly AED 180 to AED 350 an hour, with independent visiting tutors advertising AED 200 to AED 500, and monthly in-home packages advertised around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. The price absorbs travel. So does the timetable: a tutor crossing Dubai at 5pm is not available for three other households that evening, which is why the pool a family can book from shrinks to whoever lives within reach of their address.

IB Gram does not run a visiting-tutor service in the UAE. Tuition here is delivered as one-to-one online tuition over live video, one student and one tutor, with household visits offered only in India. The trade that buys is the whole point: a family in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain chooses an Extended-tier 0625 physics specialist on the strength of what they have taught, not on the strength of their postcode, and the hour that would have gone on a drive goes on the paper instead.

The table below sets the options side by side. Group classes at a centre are included because they are genuinely cheaper and genuinely right for some students; school-run support is included because it is free and is the first thing a family should exhaust. The AED figures are what the market publishes, not an IB Gram price list, and each is attributed in the cost section further down.
bullets: Separate the format question from the teaching question before spending anything
Price a household visit including travel, not at the headline hourly figure
Ask what happens to the booking when a tutor's own timetable changes
Exhaust the school's own after-hours support before buying private hours

sections.heading: Three series a year, and finding the one your child is entered for
paragraphs: IGCSE is not an annual event. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, plus a March series used by centres in some regions, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. That means a UAE family may be working to any one of several different clocks, and most parents are surprised to learn which one their child is actually on.

The second thing to establish is the zone. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for that zone, and says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong timetable was used. A zone is not a detail for the exams officer alone. It changes the date of paper one, which changes the order a revision block should run in, which changes what a tutor should be teaching in March.

The third is the board, per subject. Plenty of UAE schools enter Cambridge for sciences and Pearson for mathematics, or the reverse, and a few enter different boards for different students in the same class. Since the syllabus code determines the paper structure and the mark scheme, a tutoring plan built on the wrong code is wasted work at full price. The front page of a past paper carries the code; so does the entry confirmation the school can print.

The table below gathers the dates Cambridge and Pearson have actually published, using the Cambridge March 2027 series as the worked example of how far ahead the administrative deadlines sit. Note what the dates show: the entry closes about ten weeks before the first paper, and the forecast-grade deadline lands after the exam period has opened. Confirm every date against the board's own live timetable before planning around it, since provisional timetables are revised.

sections.heading: Year 10, September: the four decisions that are cheap now
paragraphs: Twenty months before the papers, four decisions cost almost nothing to get right and a great deal to reverse. The first is the subject count. Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five. A competitor page currently ranking states that UAE candidates need six subjects; the sourced rule is five, excluding those two, and knowing the real number changes how a timetable is filled.

The second is the tier, which is covered in its own section below because it is the decision families most often discover too late. The third is whether any subject is available in a modular shape. Where Pearson offers units that can be sat in an earlier series and carried, a student can bank marks in November of Year 11 rather than carrying everything into one June fortnight, and that single structural choice does more for a nervous candidate than any amount of revision technique.

The fourth is evidence. A Year 9 Checkpoint result, externally marked in May or October, tells a family more about an IGCSE trajectory than two years of school reports, because it is measured against a published standard rather than against the class. If that mark is weak, Year 10 is four terms of runway at one session a week. The same gap addressed in February of Year 11 needs three sessions a week against a fixed date, and the bill reflects it.

None of this requires a tutor. It requires one twenty-minute conversation with the exams officer and one with the head of year, with four questions written down beforehand: which series, which zone, which board per subject, and which subjects are tiered. A family who has those four answers in September of Year 10 is better prepared than most families are in April of Year 11.
bullets: Ask for the entry list and the zone in writing, not in a corridor
Count the equivalency subjects at five, excluding Arabic and Islamic education
Ask whether any Pearson subject is available as carried units
Treat an externally marked Checkpoint result as the real baseline

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tier the entry form locks
paragraphs: In most Cambridge sciences and in 0580 mathematics, a candidate sits either Core papers or Extended papers. The decision is made by the school on the entry form, and once the final entry deadline has passed it is not a setting a tutor can change. Families regularly arrive in February asking for Extended-tier help for a student entered at Core, or the reverse, and the honest answer is that the useful work is now inside the tier the entry fixed.

The two tiers are not the same syllabus taught at different speeds. Extended carries content Core never covers, and the available grade range differs: Cambridge publishes Core as a C to G range and Extended as A* to E, so the ceiling is a structural fact rather than a matter of effort. Confirm the current range for your child's specific syllabus on cambridgeinternational.org before building a plan on it, because subject specifications are revised.

That makes the tier a sixth-form question as much as an IGCSE one. Most British-curriculum schools in the UAE publish A Level entry conditions in IGCSE grades, commonly a minimum grade in the subject itself. If that minimum sits above the Core ceiling, a Core entry closes the A Level route in that subject before the student has sat a paper. This is worth checking in Year 10, when a tier can still be argued, rather than after results day when it cannot.

The practical move is to ask the school, before the entry deadline, which tier each subject is being entered at and what evidence that choice rests on. Where the evidence is a single weak test in a topic that can be fixed, a case can be made. Where the student is genuinely more secure at Core, the right plan is a strong Core grade rather than a stretched Extended entry, and the table sets out what each choice means for the hours.

sections.heading: Ten weeks before the papers, the entry closes
paragraphs: The single most under-known date in a UAE IGCSE year is the final entry deadline. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries were due on 27 November 2026, roughly ten weeks before the exam period opened on 3 February 2027. The entry is submitted by the centre, not by the family, and it carries the subject list, the board and the tier. After it, the shape of the year is set and the only variable left is how well the student performs inside that shape.

The forecast-grade deadline is the one that confuses parents most. For the same March 2027 series, forecast grades were due on 27 February 2027, after the exam period had already started. The forecast is the school's professional estimate, used by the board for administrative purposes, and it is not a prediction a family should treat as a verdict. Its practical use to a parent is that it tells you what evidence your child's school is holding, which is usually the January mock.

Zones belong in the same conversation. Because Cambridge runs six administrative zones and says the correct zone timetable must be used, the exact date of each paper depends on where your child's centre sits. A revision block is only as good as the order it runs in, and the order comes from the timetable. Printing the zone-correct PDF and putting the paper dates on a wall calendar in November is a ten-minute job that makes every subsequent decision easier.

If the window has already closed and a subject was missed, there are still options, because UAE centres can access more than one series a year. Ask the exams officer whether a late entry is possible and what it involves, whether the subject can be taken in the next series, and whether the school will enter a student as a private candidate. None of those answers are a tutor's to give, which is exactly why a family should get them first.
bullets: Ask for the final entry deadline date for your child's series, in writing
Get the zone-correct timetable PDF rather than a generic one
Treat the forecast grade as evidence of what the school holds, not as a result
If a subject was missed, ask about the next series before buying hours

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and the components that keep their own clock
paragraphs: Not every mark is earned in the exam hall, and the components that are not run on deadlines set inside the school rather than by the board. Speaking components in language subjects are assessed by the school in a window the school chooses. Where a syllabus carries a coursework option, the school sets the submission date, often weeks before the board needs the marks. A family planning only around the exam timetable will walk past these dates without noticing them.

In the sciences, the practical side is usually examined on paper. Cambridge syllabuses offer a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, and both assess the same underlying skills: reading an instrument to an appropriate precision, plotting and interpreting a graph, identifying an anomalous result and explaining why it is anomalous, and describing a procedure precisely enough for somebody else to repeat it. These are teachable in a video lesson with a shared screen and a set of past-paper data, and they are routinely the last thing a student practises.

A note on what support means here. The student's own work must be the student's own work. A tutor can teach the technique, work through an example of the same type, read what the student has written and say where a method is incomplete or an explanation does not follow. A tutor must never author any part of a piece that carries marks, and IB Gram does not supply finished assessed work in any form. That boundary is the subject of its own section further down.

The practical ask of a school is short. Request the internal deadline for every non-examined component, in writing, at the start of the academic year, and request the practical paper code for each science. Those two pieces of paper let a revision plan include the components that are easiest to leave until it is too late, which is where a surprising number of grades are quietly lost.
bullets: Internal deadlines are the school's, and they usually land before the board's
Practical skills are examined on paper in most UAE science entries
Graph, precision and anomaly questions are drillable from past-paper data
Feedback on the student's own writing, never text produced on their behalf

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Ramadan inside the same revision term
paragraphs: A UAE revision plan has to share the week with subjects most tutoring pages ignore. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements applied from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, lets schools vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. Those hours are in the timetable before a single revision session is scheduled.

The organisational rules matter for matching a tutor. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies. A tutor must be matched to the pathway, not to the word Arabic.

Then there is the Hijri calendar, which no competitor page in this market accounts for. Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each Gregorian year, so the relationship between the fasting month and an exam series shifts annually. A revision block designed in September around steady weekly evening sessions can collide with a shortened school day, a changed family routine and, in some years, the exam period itself. Confirm the dates with your child's school rather than assuming last year's plan transfers.

The workable response is structural rather than heroic. Move the heavy analytical sessions away from the late afternoon and into post-Iftar slots or weekend mornings, shorten individual sessions and raise their frequency, front-load the content-heavy teaching into January and keep the Ramadan weeks for timed practice on material already covered. Shorter sessions on familiar ground hold up much better in that month than ninety minutes of new theory at 5pm.
bullets: Mandatory UAE subjects occupy timetabled hours before revision is scheduled
Arabic first-language and foreign-language pathways need different tutors
Ramadan shifts about eleven days earlier each year, so reuse no old plan
Shorter, more frequent sessions on covered material beat long new-theory blocks

sections.heading: Twelve weeks out: revision counted in papers, not in topics
paragraphs: Twelve weeks before paper one, a plan built from the syllabus contents page stops being useful. The syllabus lists everything equally; the papers do not. The work from this point is organised around components and the marks they carry, in the order the zone-correct timetable puts them, and the measure of a week is whether a timed question set improved rather than whether a chapter was read.

The method is unglamorous and it works. Take the mark scheme for a recent paper in the subject. Have the student attempt a timed section rather than a whole paper, because a full paper at week ten produces a demoralising score and no diagnosis. Mark it together against the official scheme, with the student saying where they think the marks sit before the tutor says. Log each lost mark by cause rather than by topic: misread question, no working shown, unit missing, method unknown, time ran out. Causes repeat, and the repeats are the plan.

Two rules keep a block honest. The first is a stop rule: a topic that has had three sessions and is still costing marks at the same rate is parked, and the hours move to a topic where marks come back faster. The second is that the last fortnight is not for new content. It is for the three things that still move a grade that late, which are reading the question properly, writing working that earns method marks, and finishing the paper. The table sets out how the twelve weeks usually divide.

One honest caveat: twelve weeks of focused work changes outcomes, and nobody can promise a particular grade from it. What a parent can reasonably expect is a weekly written note of what was attempted, what it scored against the official mark scheme, and what changed as a result. That record is also how you decide, after three or four weeks, whether this tutor is the right one for your child.

sections.heading: Results day, and the two windows that shut inside a fortnight
paragraphs: Results arrive as a statement, not as a certificate, and the two documents behave differently. Cambridge released March 2027 series results on Direct on 13 May 2027 with certificates following in late June. Pearson sent June 2026 results to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. For admissions purposes the statement of results usually does the work first; the certificate follows weeks later, and planning on the certificate date is how families miss deadlines.

Two windows then close quickly. The first is the enquiry about results, where a centre can ask the board to check a result. It is requested by the school, within a published deadline that is measured in days or weeks rather than months, and it requires component marks rather than a general feeling that the grade looks wrong. Read the component breakdown the same week the statement arrives, and ask the exams officer immediately if one component is wildly out of line with the rest.

The second is the re-entry window. Because Cambridge runs March, June and November series and Pearson runs May/June and November, a disappointing result does not mean waiting a year. The November Pearson timetable ran to 19 November 2026, which is a realistic target for a June candidate who decides in August. An IGCSE resit is a different job from a first attempt: the content is taught, so the work is component-level repair, and the entry has to be confirmed with the centre before any hours are worth buying.

The decision itself deserves a cold look. Re-entering five subjects to lift two grades is rarely the right trade; re-entering the one subject that blocks a sixth-form condition or an equivalency count usually is. Read the published condition, read the component marks, and pick the smallest set of entries that fixes the actual problem. That is a twenty-minute conversation that saves a term.
bullets: Read the component breakdown in the same week the statement arrives
An enquiry about results is requested by the centre, within a short published window

Re-enter the subject that blocks a condition, not every disappointing grade

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs across the UAE market, and how the date moves the number
paragraphs: IGCSE tuition rates in AED are published by almost nobody in this market, which is why parents end up comparing a quote against nothing. The table below sets out what providers in the UAE have actually published, by provider model rather than by brand quality, with the date each figure was read. These are market rates. They are not an IB Gram price list, and IB Gram's own position is a free trial lesson first and a quoted plan afterwards, so that a family sees a tutor teach before any money is involved.

What drives the number is less mysterious than it looks. Format comes first: a household visit absorbs travel, which is why the visiting-tutor band sits above the online band for the same level of tutor. Scarcity comes second: a tiered Extended science or Further Pure Mathematics specialist is simply rarer than a general mathematics tutor, and rarity prices. Timing comes third, and this is the part a countdown changes. Hours bought in February for a June series compete with every other family in the same position, while hours bought in September do not.

There is a cost to late buying that never shows in an hourly rate. A September start can run at one session a week for thirty weeks. A February start chasing the same gap needs two or three sessions a week against a fixed date, which is more hours at a tighter moment, with a smaller choice of tutor and less flexibility on the slot. The cheapest hour in an IGCSE year is the one bought early, and that is a calendar fact rather than a sales argument.

For context on the bill: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for Dubai private schools in the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is one of the few education costs in a Dubai household that did move, and the easiest one to size properly by deciding the number of sessions and the number of weeks before comparing anybody's hourly figure.
