sections.heading: The Ministry of Education equivalency file, opened before results day
paragraphs: For a UAE family, an IGCSE result is not only a school outcome. It is a line in a Ministry of Education equivalency file that a student may need for a UAE university or for employment paperwork later. The British-track requirement is specific: proof of five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The exclusion is the detail most pages get wrong. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five required subjects. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five, with those two outside the count. The number matters at the options stage in Year 10, because a student filling a timetable without knowing it can finish Year 11 a subject short of a requirement nobody mentioned to them.

The equivalency route for American-curriculum students sits alongside, and is worth knowing because UAE families move between systems. English proficiency is shown by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold is published in that source, so no IB equivalency figure should be trusted from any tutoring page, including this one, without a check on moe.gov.ae.

Two honest limits. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation; it is a Ministry process and the Ministry is the authority on it. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression. What a countdown can do is put the paperwork on the calendar in Year 11, so that a family is reading the requirement in November rather than discovering it in the week a university application is due.
bullets: Five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3
Arabic and Islamic education sit outside that count of five
One A Level at E, or two AS Levels at E, on the British track
Verify any IB points figure on moe.gov.ae; no sourced number exists here

sections.heading: Academic honesty when a school deadline is on Friday
paragraphs: Every tutoring market has a version of this, and the UAE IGCSE market has a visible one. Pages in this search results page sell finished assessed work, and one advertises completed Internal Assessments at a published price. For a student that is a malpractice finding and potentially a lost qualification. For a family it is money spent on a risk nobody explained. The line is worth stating in plain terms rather than leaving to an assumption.

Here is the boundary IB Gram works to. A tutor may teach the content, model a worked example of the same type, explain what a mark scheme rewards, read what the student has written and point out where a method is incomplete, an explanation does not follow or a source is missing. A tutor may not author any part of a piece that carries marks, may not rewrite a student's paragraph into their own prose, and may not submit anything. IB Gram supplies no finished assessed work, at any price, in any subject.

The practical test is simple enough to apply mid-session. If a lesson ends with text on the page that the student could not now explain, reproduce or defend to their teacher, something has gone wrong. If it ends with the student able to say why their second draft is better than their first, the hour did its job. That test also happens to be the one a school uses when a piece of work does not resemble the student who handed it in.

One related limit, and it is a copyright one. IB Gram does not reproduce or supply Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those materials are referenced and linked at cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com, where they belong, and where they are current. Practice in a lesson is done against the official material, accessed from the official source.
bullets: Teaching, worked examples and feedback on the student's own writing: yes
Producing, rewriting or submitting assessed work: never, at any price
Board materials referenced and linked, not reproduced or supplied
If the student cannot defend what is on the page, the session went wrong

process.title: Tell us the series, the board and the tier
process.description: Four answers from your child's exams officer start everything: which series they are entered for, which administrative zone the centre sits in, which board per subject, and which subjects are tiered. With those, a plan can be written in weeks remaining rather than in topics remaining, which is the only unit that matters this close to a dated exam.

process.title: A free trial lesson with two tutors
process.description: We shortlist on syllabus code rather than on subject name, and you meet two tutors for a free trial lesson each. Give both the same past-paper question. The useful comparison is not who is friendlier but who explains why a mark was lost in a way your child can repeat afterwards without help.

process.title: A plan with dates, not just topics
process.description: The first full session produces a written plan keyed to your child's paper dates: what gets covered in which weeks, which components are drilled when, where the school's internal deadlines sit, and the stop rule for a topic that is not repaying the hours. You get the plan in writing before the block is booked.

process.title: Weekly lessons, one-to-one over live video
process.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video with a shared screen, scheduled around Gulf Standard Time evenings and around the mandatory school subjects already in the timetable. Each session ends with a question set marked against the official mark scheme, and each lost mark logged by cause rather than by topic.

process.title: A milestone review, then a decision
process.description: At each calendar milestone, the entry deadline, the mock, the start of the twelve-week block, results day, we review what the marked work shows and either continue, change the plan or change the tutor. Three or four weeks of logged marks is enough evidence to judge a match, and a parent should expect to be given it.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is the plan
whyPoints.description: Most tutoring pages sell a tutor. This one starts at the date of paper one and counts back, because the entry deadline, the forecast-grade form, the internal coursework dates and the results window are what decide which work is still worth doing. A plan without those dates in it is a wish list.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes, not subject names
whyPoints.description: 0580 and 4MA1 are both called IGCSE Mathematics and they are different papers with different mark schemes and different tier structures. Matching on the code rather than the subject name is the difference between practice that transfers to the exam your child actually sits and practice that does not.

whyPoints.title: One pool, not one postcode
whyPoints.description: Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, so a family in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain is choosing from the same set of Extended-tier specialists as a family in Dubai. For Further Pure Mathematics or Computer Science that is often the difference between a specialist and the nearest generalist.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is written down
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, models and gives feedback on the student's own work. IB Gram supplies no finished assessed work in any subject and reproduces no board past papers or mark schemes as downloads. Both limits are published here rather than discovered when a school asks a student to explain their own writing.

whyPoints.title: Rates with their source attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page names the provider that published it and the month it was read, because three of six ranking competitors publish no price at all and two quote in a currency UAE families do not transact in. A family comparing quotes deserves a baseline, not an adjective.

whyPoints.title: Regulators named, never claimed
whyPoints.description: KHDA, ADEK, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, the Department of Knowledge and the federal Ministry of Education are described here because they shape your child's week and your paperwork. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from any of them, and says so rather than implying otherwise.

faqs.question: Which of the three IGCSE series will my child actually sit, and how do we find out?
faqs.answer: Ask your child's exams officer for the entry confirmation in writing. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with a March series used by centres in some regions, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Your child's school has entered them into one of these, subject by subject, and it is possible to be in different series or on different boards for different subjects. The confirmation also carries the tier for any tiered subject and the administrative zone of the centre, which is what decides the exact date of each paper.

faqs.question: What is the Cambridge March series, and can a UAE student use it?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a March series alongside June and November, used by centres in some regions, and the published key dates show how far ahead its administration sits. For the March 2027 series the exam period ran 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries were due 27 November 2026, forecast grades 27 February 2027, results on Direct 13 May 2027 and certificates in late June. Whether your child's centre offers it is a question for the exams officer rather than for a tutor, since entries are submitted by the centre. Where it is available it adds a third chance a year to re-sit a single blocking subject.

faqs.question: Who fills in the forecast grade, and does it change the final result?
faqs.answer: The school does, and no. A forecast grade is the school's professional estimate submitted to the board for administrative purposes, and for the Cambridge March 2027 series it was due on 27 February 2027, after the exam period had already opened. It does not set, cap or influence the grade a candidate earns from their papers. Its practical value to a parent is as a window into the evidence the school is holding, which is usually the January mock. If a forecast looks lower than you expected, the productive question is which mock components produced it rather than whether the forecast can be appealed.

faqs.question: We missed the entry window for a series. What are the options now?
faqs.answer: Go to the exams officer the same week, because every available option runs through the centre rather than through a tutor or a tutoring platform. Ask three things: whether a late entry is still possible for that series and what it involves, whether the subject can be taken in the next series, and whether the school will enter your child as a private candidate. UAE centres have access to more than one series a year, so a missed entry usually means a later sitting rather than a lost year. Settle the entry before buying any hours, so the work is aimed at a paper that exists on a date.

faqs.question: How long after the exams do certificates arrive, and will a university accept the statement first?
faqs.answer: The two documents arrive weeks apart. Cambridge released March 2027 results on Direct on 13 May 2027 with certificates in late June, and Pearson sent June 2026 results to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August. Admissions processes generally work from the statement of results first, with the certificate following for formal verification. The practical advice is to plan every deadline from the statement date, not the certificate date, and to tell any admissions office in advance that the certificate follows later. Confirm what each specific institution requires, since their rules differ and are theirs to set.

faqs.question: Can we move our daughter from Core to Extended partway through Year 11?
faqs.answer: Only before the final entry deadline, and the decision belongs to the school. The tier is recorded on the entry form, and for the Cambridge March 2027 series that form closed on 27 November 2026, roughly ten weeks before the first paper. Once entries are submitted, the papers your child sits are fixed. If you believe the tier is wrong, the conversation to have is with the head of subject in the term before the deadline, bringing evidence from marked work. After entries close, the useful work is building the strongest possible grade inside the tier that was entered.

faqs.question: Our son sits Pearson modular units rather than one final set of papers. How should that change the plan?
faqs.answer: It changes the plan more than anything else on this page. Where a Pearson subject is available in a modular shape, a unit can be sat in an earlier series and carried, which means some of the marks are already banked before the final series begins. The planning consequence is that each unit gets its own countdown and its own revision block, rather than everything converging on one fortnight. For an anxious candidate that is a structural advantage. Ask the exams officer which of your child's subjects are entered as units and which series each unit is sitting in.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a Year 11 student realistically need in the last twelve weeks?
faqs.answer: For one subject under pressure, two sessions a week through the diagnosis and re-teaching phases, dropping to one or two shorter sessions in the final fortnight, plus unsupervised timed papers in between. Three or four subjects at that intensity is not sustainable alongside school, and families who try it usually see the quality of the independent practice collapse. The better trade is to pick the one or two subjects where marks come back fastest, accept a smaller gain elsewhere, and protect enough unsupervised time for the student to sit papers to the clock on their own.

faqs.question: Our daughter is only in Year 10. Does starting now genuinely beat starting in Year 11?
faqs.answer: On cost and on options, yes. A Year 10 start runs at one session a week with the school's scheme of work, consolidating each topic while it is still being taught, so the student arrives in February of Year 11 without a backlog. A Year 11 start chasing the same gap needs two or three sessions a week against a fixed date. Year 10 is also the only point at which the tier and the subject count are still arguable, since both are locked by the entry form. The same gap costs materially less to close four terms out than ten weeks out.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan change when revision should happen for a June series?
faqs.answer: It changes when, not whether. Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each Gregorian year, so its position relative to an exam series shifts annually and last year's plan does not transfer. Confirm the dates and the school's adjusted timetable with your child's school. The structural response is to front-load content-heavy teaching into the weeks before, move analytical sessions out of the late afternoon into post-Iftar slots or weekend mornings, and shorten sessions while raising their frequency. Timed practice on material already covered holds up far better in that month than ninety minutes of new theory.

faqs.question: If my son resits in November, how does the new grade appear afterwards?
faqs.answer: Each series produces its own statement of results, so a November entry gives a separate result for that subject rather than overwriting the earlier one, and both sittings exist on the record. Universities and sixth forms differ in how they treat a resit, and some ask to see all attempts, so check the published condition rather than assuming. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran to 19 November 2026, which is a realistic target for a June candidate deciding in August. The entry must be confirmed with the centre before buying hours against it.

faqs.question: Which paper carries the practical marks in Cambridge sciences, and when should we start on it?
faqs.answer: Cambridge science syllabuses examine practical skills either through a practical test or through an alternative-to-practical paper, and the code for the specific paper is on your child's entry confirmation. Both assess the same things: instrument precision, graph plotting and interpretation, identifying and explaining anomalous results, and describing a procedure precisely. Those are teachable from past-paper data on a shared screen, with no laboratory required. Start them in the six-to-four week band at the latest, because this is the component most students leave until the final fortnight and it is one of the easiest places to recover marks.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with a coursework piece a week before the school's deadline?
faqs.answer: Teach, model and give feedback on what the student has already written. A tutor can explain what the criteria reward, work through an example of the same type, read a draft and say where a method is incomplete, an explanation does not follow or a source is missing. A tutor may not author any part of a piece that carries marks, rewrite a paragraph into their own prose, or submit anything. IB Gram supplies no finished assessed work in any subject at any price. The test to apply: if your child could not explain and defend every line to their teacher, the session went wrong.

faqs.question: At what point in Year 11 should we start the Ministry of Education equivalency paperwork?
faqs.answer: Before results day, not after. The British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Knowing that in November of Year 11 means you can check the subject count while something can still be done about it. The Ministry runs the process and is the authority on it; IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency, and tutoring is not required for it.

faqs.question: Can we verify a tutor's private tuition work permit before booking exam-term hours?
faqs.answer: You can and you should ask. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its app, website and e-services. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to book IGCSE hours in September than in April?
faqs.answer: Materially, yes, though not because the hourly rate moves. A September start can run at one session a week for thirty weeks, consolidating topics as they are taught. An April start chasing the same gap needs two or three sessions a week against a fixed date, which is more total hours bought at the point when the choice of tutor is narrowest and the evening slots are most contested. Scarcity also prices: a tiered Extended science or Further Pure Mathematics specialist is rarer than a general mathematics tutor, and rarest in the ten weeks before a series.

faqs.question: The page says home tuition, so where does the lesson actually happen?
faqs.answer: On a video call, one tutor and one student, with a shared screen for working through papers. IGCSE home tuition is the phrase UAE parents search, and it is answered here honestly: the market does have a visiting-tutor service, priced at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour once travel is inside the figure, and IB Gram is not that service anywhere in the Emirates. Household visits are something we run only in India. What online delivery buys is choice, because a family selects a specialist in the right syllabus code rather than the nearest available generalist.

igcse-home-tuition.closingHeading: Start with the date, then pick the tutor
igcse-home-tuition.closingBody: Before anything is booked, get four answers in writing from your child's exams officer: the series, the administrative zone of the centre, the board for each subject and the tier for each tiered subject. With those, a plan can be written in weeks remaining instead of topics remaining, and you can judge whether a tutor's practice material matches the papers your child will actually sit. Then take a free trial lesson with two tutors, give both the same past-paper question, and pick the one whose explanation your child can repeat the next day without help. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time evenings.

igcse-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE and International GCSE at Years 10 and 11, plus the Year 9 groundwork that precedes them. intro.heading: The system your child's IGCSEs sit inside
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in the UAE is, for most families, a search for one person: someone who knows the exact paper the child will sit and can get them ready for it. The complication is that the paper is not set in the UAE. It is written in Cambridge or in London, sat in a school licensed by one of five different authorities, and recognised afterwards by a federal ministry that applies its own subject count. Rates matter, but they matter second. Knowing which body controls what comes first, because that is what decides whether a tutor can help at all.

Private schools in Dubai answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge, and schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so their reach goes well past inspection. None of those five bodies writes an IGCSE syllabus, and none of them approves an individual private tutor.

Two boards dominate the classrooms. Cambridge International runs syllabuses with four-digit codes: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE specifications coded 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1. A school picks one board per subject and often splits them, so Cambridge sciences beside Pearson maths is an ordinary combination rather than an error. Running alongside whichever board the school uses, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies stay compulsory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA set the start of the 2025-26 academic year as the point by which its requirements had to be implemented.

Then there is the Ministry of Education equivalency file, which a UAE-educated leaver usually needs before a local university application. On the British track the Ministry asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. A page currently ranking for these searches tells UAE parents that six IGCSE subjects are required. The published clarification says five, and the difference is a year of a pupil's timetable.

IB Gram arranges this teaching as one-to-one online tuition over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a UAE address; visiting tuition is something we run in India only. The reason sits in the paragraphs above. A family in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain has almost no chance of finding a 0478 Computer Science teacher within driving distance, and a Dubai family should not have to accept a generalist because the Extended-tier Chemistry specialist happens to live in Mirdif. Live video takes the drive out of the decision and leaves the syllabus code as the thing that decides the match.
bullets: Five authorities, one federal ministry: KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.
Two boards, different papers: Cambridge 0580 and 0625 against Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 and 4PH1, with Cambridge grading in letters and Pearson in numbers.
Core or Extended is a tiering decision with a grade ceiling attached, and it is normally settled before the final entry deadline.
Five IGCSE subjects at grade E or 3 is the Ministry's British-track count, and Arabic and Islamic education sit outside it.
Private tutoring is permit-based: the MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years.
Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, so no travel time or travel charge is built into the hour.

igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Four qualifications and one destination cover almost every UAE British-curriculum timetable. The label on the school's prospectus is not always the label on the certificate, so the first job in any match is establishing which of these your child is actually entered for, and at which tier.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The most widely taught version in UAE schools. Subjects carry four-digit codes, and many are tiered: a Core route and an Extended route with different papers, different content and different grade ranges. Cambridge grades IGCSE in letters, A* down to G, with Core capped at C and Extended reaching A*. Exams run in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests for younger year groups in March, May and October.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. That single sentence explains why two UAE pupils at different schools can sit the same paper at different times, and why a revision plan should be built from the school's own timetable rather than a generic one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The second board a UAE school is likely to use, with specifications coded 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology and 4EA1 English Language A. Grading is numeric, 9 down to 1, and tiered subjects run Foundation and Higher rather than Core and Extended. Exams are available in May and June and again in November each year.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson confirms a November series each year and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each one, which is why a session table should link the live official timetable rather than restate dates that can still be revised. Its November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and pupils on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached pupils on 22 January 2026 - a useful marker for any UAE family weighing a retake.

programmes.name: Cambridge O Level
programmes.description: Still offered by some UAE schools, often alongside IGCSE in the same year group, and sat in the same June and November series. O Level assessment tends to lean harder on written examination and lighter on coursework than the IGCSE equivalent, which changes what a tutoring plan should spend its hours on.
programmes.countryNote: A family moving between UAE schools can find a child switching from IGCSE to O Level in the same subject mid-course, because the two sit side by side in this market. The content overlap is large but the components are not identical, so the first session after a move is spent on a component-by-component comparison with the new school's scheme of work rather than on teaching.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The two years before the IGCSE course begins, which in most UAE British-curriculum schools is where the setting decisions are taken that later determine the tier a pupil is entered for. Cambridge runs Checkpoint tests in March, May and October for schools that use them.
programmes.countryNote: This is the cheapest point in the whole sequence to fix a maths gap. A pupil who leaves Year 9 fluent in algebraic manipulation, index laws and rearranging formulae is a candidate for Extended-tier 0580; one who is not will be placed on Core, and the ceiling that follows is a placement consequence rather than an ability verdict. UAE schools finalise these sets in the summer term, so the useful window is February to June of Year 9.

programmes.name: Where IGCSE leads: IB Diploma or International A Level
programmes.description: Most UAE British-curriculum schools continue into International A Levels; a growing group switches pupils into the IB Diploma Programme instead. Either route reads the IGCSE grade profile as the entry evidence, and both make the Extended or Higher tier effectively a prerequisite in maths and the sciences.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, and six opened during 2025-26 while enrolment rose by 6%. For a Year 11 family this matters in one practical way: the post-16 destination may not be the school the child is in now, and a transfer application will be read against IGCSE forecasts made months before the papers are sat.

igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Codes first, because the code is what a tutor teaches to. The list below pairs the Cambridge syllabus with its Pearson Edexcel counterpart where the school is likely to offer both, and names the place in each subject where UAE pupils most often lose marks rather than content.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 · Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Cambridge Core candidates sit Paper 1 and Paper 3; Extended candidates sit Paper 2 and Paper 4. Pearson runs Foundation and Higher tiers over two papers. Marks go on method presentation, exact-value answers and the algebra that the Extended supplement adds on top of the core content.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (Cambridge 0607)
subjects.description: The graphics-calculator route, used by UAE schools that feed pupils into the IB Diploma. It assesses investigation and modelling alongside technique, and the unfamiliar component for most families is the paper that rewards setting a problem up rather than finishing a procedure.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 · Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Theory papers plus a practical component, which in most UAE centres is the alternative-to-practical paper rather than a timetabled practical exam. That paper tests apparatus description, variable control and graph work, all of which are examined technique and all of which teach cleanly over video.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 · Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles, concentration and ionic equations account for a large share of lost Extended-tier marks, followed by organic reaction conditions stated loosely. Qualitative analysis tables in the practical-alternative paper reward memorised observation language, which is a drillable thing rather than a talent.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 · Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content volume makes this feel like a memory subject, and that is where families misspend hours. The recoverable marks are in command-term discipline: describe against explain, a named example where one is demanded, and data-handling answers that quote figures from the stimulus.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0653 · 0654)
subjects.description: The two-award and single-award routes for pupils not taking three separate sciences. Topic coverage is narrower than the separate syllabuses but the examination style is identical, so a tutor must work from the right syllabus document or half the taught content will be off-specification.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500 · Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading responses carry the paper. Pupils lose marks by retelling the passage rather than selecting from it, and by writing in a register that ignores the stated audience. Where the school runs a coursework route, the academic-honesty boundary matters more than any examination technique.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 · 0511)
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language, and a decision the school usually takes rather than the family. It carries reading, writing and listening components, with an oral in the 0511 variant. For many UAE pupils the writing mark moves fastest once sentence-level accuracy is separated from vocabulary range.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450) and Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Both reward applied answers, which means naming the business in the case study and following a judgement through to a recommendation. UAE pupils often have strong commercial instincts and weak evaluation structure; one of those is quick to fix in weekly one-to-one time.

subjects.name: Geography (0460) and History (0470)
subjects.description: Source-handling and case-study precision decide these grades. Geography requires a named located example per topic rather than a general one, and History requires the source's provenance to be used, not just its content. Both are structural skills that respond to marked practice.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478) and ICT (0417)
subjects.description: Two of the hardest IGCSE subjects to staff anywhere in the UAE, which is precisely why online matching matters for them. Pseudocode conventions, trace tables and data-representation arithmetic are the usual mark sinks, and all three are better practised on a shared screen than on paper.

subjects.name: Arabic (0508 first language · 0544 foreign language)
subjects.description: Taken as an IGCSE subject by some pupils and as a Ministry-mandated school subject by all of them. The examination and the mandated school stream are not the same thing, and a tutoring plan should state which one it is for before the first session is booked.

igcse-home-tutor.regionsTitle: Your emirate, your regulator, and what each one changes
igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Delivery is identical in all seven emirates, because it happens over live video. What differs is the authority holding your child's school file, what that authority publishes, and how thin the local pool of subject teachers is if you were to look for a visiting tutor instead.

regions.name: Dubai (KHDA)
regions.note: The deepest published record in the country: inspection reports, school pages and the mandatory-subject guidelines are all readable before you spend anything. With 227 private schools and 387,441 pupils in 2024-25, Dubai also has the largest visiting-tutor market and the heaviest evening traffic working against it.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi (ADEK)
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Press reporting in 2025 described professional-ethics rules barring private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school, which is the one rule an Abu Dhabi family should check before accepting an offer from a familiar face.

regions.name: Al Ain (ADEK)
regions.note: Same regulator as Abu Dhabi island, a much smaller set of British-curriculum schools. Families here feel the subject-shortage problem first: a Core-tier maths tutor is findable locally, while an Extended-tier Physics or Computer Science teacher usually is not. Live video closes that gap without a 90-minute drive each way.

regions.name: Sharjah (SPEA)
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Assessment-method approval sitting locally is worth knowing: ask the school what it has signed off for coursework-bearing subjects before planning around them.

regions.name: Ajman (Ministry of Education)
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools here, so there is no emirate-level inspection archive to read. Ask the school directly for its own attainment data by subject. Many Ajman families also commute to Sharjah or Dubai schools, which pushes a realistic weekday session to 6pm Gulf Standard Time or later.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah (Department of Knowledge)
regions.note: RAK's own Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The British-curriculum school count is small, the local tutor pool smaller, and online matching is the only route to most Extended-tier science specialists.

regions.name: Fujairah (Ministry of Education)
regions.note: Supervised federally alongside Ajman and Umm Al Quwain. Distance from the Dubai-Abu Dhabi corridor makes a visiting specialist close to impossible to arrange twice a week at a sensible rate, which is why families on the east coast tend to arrive at online tuition by elimination rather than preference.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain (Ministry of Education)
regions.note: The smallest private-school market in the country and the clearest case for delivery over video. A pupil here can work with the same 0620 Chemistry specialist as a pupil in Jumeirah, at the same hour, with no travel premium added to the rate by either side.

schoolClusters.note: Pupils we support sit Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel papers at schools across the emirate. Boards differ by school and sometimes by subject inside one school, which is why the first question in any Dubai match is the syllabus code rather than the school name.

British-curriculum schools under ADEK supervision concentrate on Abu Dhabi island and in Khalifa City, with a thinner spread in Al Ain. Pupils in both places sit the same boards; what changes is how easily a parent can find a local specialist for a shortage subject.

Across Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah, Ajman and Fujairah the IGCSE cohort is spread thinly over a wide area. Three different regulatory regimes apply, and the practical consequence for families is the same one: the nearest tutor and the right tutor are rarely the same person.

igcse-home-tutor.modesIntro: Four ways families use one-to-one time, all delivered over live video in Gulf Standard Time. Most start with the first and add the second in the January before the papers. The fourth exists because the Ministry-mandated subjects run on their own rules and need their own treatment.

modes.description: A fixed slot each week with the same tutor, worked against the school's scheme of work and the syllabus document for the exact code. The tutor sees the pupil's own written working on camera, marks it live, and sets the next week from what the page showed rather than from a fixed curriculum.

modes.description: From January onwards, sessions switch to whole past papers sat under timed conditions and then marked against the official mark scheme in the following hour. The skill being built is mark-scheme literacy: reading what the command term demands and writing only that, which is where most of the recoverable marks sit.

modes.description: A short first session that establishes which board, which code and which tier the pupil is entered for, then puts a real past paper in front of them to find where the marks actually go. Families frequently discover at this point that the tier they assumed is not the tier on the entry.

modes.title: The Ministry-mandated subject stream
modes.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies sit beside the IGCSE timetable in Dubai private schools and carry rules of their own. KHDA states that for these subjects the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the MoE, is strictly prohibited, so support here means working the school's own material rather than bringing new content.

sections.heading: What families are actually asking for when they search for an IGCSE home tutor
paragraphs: The search phrase means one thing in practice: a parent wants a competent adult working one-to-one with their child on the IGCSE papers that child will sit, at a time that survives the school run. The word home in the phrase describes a setting, not a requirement. What parents are buying is attention and subject accuracy, and the setting only matters insofar as it affects those two things.

IB Gram delivers that as one-to-one tuition over live video. No tutor is sent to an address anywhere in the UAE; visiting tuition is a service we run in India only. That is a deliberate position rather than a limitation, and the argument for it is geographic. The UAE's IGCSE cohort is spread across seven emirates and a few hundred schools, while the supply of teachers fluent in Extended-tier 0620 Chemistry or 0478 Computer Science is concentrated in a handful of Dubai and Abu Dhabi neighbourhoods. A family searching by proximity is searching the wrong variable.

There is also a time argument that visiting tuition rarely makes openly. A tutor crossing Dubai at 5pm, or driving from Sharjah to Ajman after work, prices that journey into the hour and usually asks for a two-hour minimum so the trip is worth making. Online, a 60-minute session is a 60-minute session, a cancelled week costs nobody a drive, and a pupil who needs twenty minutes of help on one Paper 4 question can have exactly that.

The honest caveat is that a screen is not better at everything. A Year 10 pupil who cannot sit still without an adult in the room benefits from a physical presence, and a family who wants that should hire locally and ask to see the tutor's permit. For everything that turns on subject depth, examined technique and getting the right specialist at all, the comparison runs the other way, and the table further down this page sets out both sides of it.

sections.heading: Five authorities, one country: who holds your child's school file
paragraphs: No single body regulates private schooling in the UAE. Five do, split by emirate, and which one holds your child's school file determines what you can read about that school before spending money on tuition. This is the single most useful thing a UAE parent can know before comparing tutors, and it is absent from almost every page competing for this search.

Dubai's KHDA is the most transparent of the five. Inspection reports, school profiles and published guidance are all available, and the mandatory-subject requirements are set out in enough detail that a parent can predict the Arabic and Islamic Education load before enrolment. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah's SPEA and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge each regulate private education locally and, significantly, approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education.

The federal baseline underneath all five is narrow. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Everything else - which board, which tier, which papers - is the school's decision inside the frame its emirate regulator approves. That is why two UAE pupils in the same year group, two emirates apart, can be sitting different boards in the same subject.

What none of these authorities does is approve, accredit or license an individual tutor. That obligation sits with MoHRE and is covered further down. Any provider describing its tutors as approved by an education regulator is describing something that does not exist as a category, and that claim is the fastest way to identify a page worth distrusting.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: settle this before you book an hour
paragraphs: The most expensive mistake in IGCSE tutoring is buying hours against the wrong specification. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel teach overlapping content and examine it differently, with different paper structures, different tier names and different grading scales. A tutor who knows 0625 Physics inside out is still guessing at the mark allocation on 4PH1 until they read it.

Finding out takes one message. The school's exams officer or the subject teacher will confirm the board and the exact code per subject, and that information belongs in the first conversation with any provider. A school commonly splits boards by department, so a single answer for the whole timetable is usually wrong. Cambridge grades IGCSE in letters, A* to G. Pearson grades International GCSE numerically, 9 to 1. The two are not directly comparable, which matters the moment a family starts benchmarking a mock result against a sibling's or a cousin's.

Paper structure differs too. Cambridge 0580 Mathematics splits a non-calculator paper from a calculator paper, with Core candidates taking Papers 1 and 3 while Extended candidates take Papers 2 and 4. Pearson's Mathematics A runs Foundation and Higher tiers over two papers. In the sciences, most UAE centres route pupils through an alternative-to-practical paper rather than a timetabled practical examination, and that paper rewards apparatus description, variable control and graph construction, which are taught as examined technique rather than as laboratory work.

Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so a family planning around dates should work from the live official timetable rather than a figure copied onto a tutoring website. The same applies to any mark scheme or past paper: reference the board's own page and link out. Reproducing or distributing board material is a copyright problem, and no reputable provider should be supplying it as a download.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: a tiering decision with a ceiling attached
paragraphs: Tiering is the decision UAE families understand least and regret most. In a tiered Cambridge subject, the Core route and the Extended route are different papers covering different content, and they lead to different grade ranges. Core runs to grade C. Extended runs to A*. A pupil who needs an A for a sixth-form science place and is entered on Core has a ceiling problem, not a revision problem, and no amount of tutoring lifts a ceiling.

Schools make this decision for sound reasons. Extended papers are harder, and a pupil placed above their level walks out of a paper having attempted a third of it. The difficulty is timing: the placement is often made in Year 10 on the strength of Year 9 attainment, and a pupil who matures academically during Year 10 can be sitting in the wrong tier with nobody re-examining it. The entry deadline is the last point at which a school can change it, which makes that deadline the single most actionable date in the whole calendar.

Moving up a tier is not a formality either. Extended content is the core content plus a supplement, so a mid-year move means teaching the supplement from scratch while the class continues forward. Done in Year 10 it is comfortable. Attempted in the spring of Year 11 it competes directly with revision time, and the honest answer is sometimes that the tier should stay where it is and the pupil should aim at the top of the Core range instead.

Pearson handles the same problem with Foundation and Higher tiers and a single numeric scale, which makes the comparison slightly easier for parents to read but the decision no less consequential. Either way, the first thing to establish about any IGCSE pupil is which tier the entry says, not which tier the family assumed. Past papers must then be chosen to match: a Core candidate practising Extended Paper 4 is being discouraged for no reason, and an Extended candidate practising Core papers is being flattered.

sections.heading: The three Ministry subjects that run beside IGCSE
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA set the start of the 2025-26 academic year as the implementation point for its requirements, with April 2026 applying to schools whose year starts in April. No competitor page in the research set treats these subjects as anything more than a chip on a subject list, yet they occupy real timetable hours for every IGCSE pupil in the emirate.

The organisational rules are specific. KHDA states that for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies runs in Arabic for Arab pupils and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs. Schools are also required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach these subjects.

Instructional time is counted in 40-minute lesson units. Schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. That accounting is worth knowing when a family is deciding how long a tuition session should be: a school timetable built from 40-minute units does not imply a 40-minute tutoring hour is correct, and for examined IGCSE technique it usually is not.

The hard boundary is content. For these subjects, the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the MoE, is strictly prohibited. A tutor working in this stream therefore revises the school's own Ministry-set material, builds comprehension and written-answer structure, and does not substitute an alternative syllabus. Any provider offering its own Arabic or Islamic Education curriculum to a Dubai pupil is offering something the regulator has ruled out.

sections.heading: Is the tutor permitted to charge? The MoHRE private tuition permit
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-based. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and u.ae states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE will be subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you by anybody, including us.

The permit is granted free of charge for two years. That single fact disposes of a sales line some UAE families are told, which is that a higher hourly rate reflects licensing costs. It does not, because there are none. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school pupils aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two conditions sit on top of eligibility. Press reporting in 2025 described ADEK professional-ethics rules prohibiting private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi from providing paid private tutoring to pupils enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE code of conduct also barring service to pupils affiliated with the tutor's own school. A family should verify the current wording with ADEK before relying on it, but the direction is clear enough: hiring your child's own classroom teacher privately is the one arrangement to avoid.

A tuition centre is a separate legal animal. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram is a matching platform rather than a licensed training institute and holds no instrument from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE. The permit obligation rests with each individual tutor, and a parent is entitled to ask to see it before paying for a lesson.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs in this market, and who publishes the figures
paragraphs: Most pages competing for this search publish no price at all, and two of those that do quote US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. The table below collects what UAE providers have actually published in AED, read in October 2026. These are market rates from other people's rate pages. They are not IB Gram's price list, and they are here so a family can sanity-check a quote rather than accept one.

Three things drive the number. Depth in the specific code comes first: a teacher who marks Extended-tier 0620 weekly costs more than a graduate who studied chemistry, and for a pupil chasing an A* that difference is the whole purchase. Travel comes second, and it is invisible in the headline rate - it appears instead as a two-hour minimum or a quietly higher hourly figure. Scarcity comes third. Computer Science, Extended-tier Physics and first-language Arabic are hard to staff anywhere in the UAE, and a thin supply prices itself accordingly.

Monthly packaging is common in this market: roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions has been published, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visiting sessions. Bestimate's Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. A package is better value only if the sessions are used; families who pay monthly through a mock period and then travel for Eid routinely lose hours they have already bought.

There is a context figure worth holding alongside all of this. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a total of AED 2.5 billion. School fees are capped; tutoring rates are not regulated at all. That asymmetry is exactly why a published, attributed rate table is worth more to a parent than a reassuring sentence about value.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor or a specialist on screen: the comparison on its merits
paragraphs: This is the decision the search phrase implies, so it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales argument. A tutor sitting beside a pupil has advantages that are real: presence, the ability to notice a wandering attention span, and no dependence on a connection. Those advantages are worth most to younger or less independent pupils, and least to a Year 11 candidate working through Paper 4 under time pressure.

Set against them are three costs that visiting tuition carries whether or not anybody names them. The journey is priced into the hour. The tutor pool shrinks to whoever is within a sensible drive, which in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain can be nobody at all for a shortage subject. And the scheduling becomes rigid, because a slot that works for a tutor crossing the city at 5pm is the only slot available, regardless of the pupil's football training or the school bus arriving late.

Online removes all three. The pool becomes every specialist available at that hour rather than every specialist within 20 kilometres, which is how a family in Al Ain works with the same 0478 Computer Science teacher as a family in Dubai Marina. Scheduling becomes flexible enough to put a session after Iftar during Ramadan without anybody negotiating a drive. The pupil's own written working goes on camera and gets marked live, which for maths and the sciences is most of what a tutor does anyway.

What a family should ask before deciding is narrower than the general debate suggests: does a local specialist in this exact code and tier actually exist within reach, and if so, what does the journey add to the rate? Where the answer is yes and the premium is acceptable, hire locally and verify the permit. Where the answer is no, which it is for most shortage subjects outside Dubai and Abu Dhabi, proximity was never the variable worth optimising.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and the five-subject rule a ranking page gets wrong
paragraphs: A UAE-educated leaver applying to a local university normally needs an equivalency certificate from the Ministry of Education confirming that their qualification matches the national framework. For the British track, the published clarification is specific. A student must submit proof of one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3.

Two details inside that rule are worth a parent's attention. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which means a pupil counting them towards the total may be a subject short without knowing it. And the threshold is a floor, not a target: grade E or grade 3 clears equivalency, while a competitive university offer will ask for considerably more. Equivalency and admission are separate hurdles, and conflating them is how families end up buying tutoring for the wrong reason.

A competitor page ranking for these searches tells UAE candidates they must take six IGCSE subjects. The published requirement is five. We are not naming that page or making claims about it beyond this one correction, because the correction is the useful part: check the subject count against moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation channel rather than against a tutoring website, including this one.

For the American track the same clarification sets out an English requirement of a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with at least 450 in SAT Math before applying. For the IB Diploma, no points figure appears in the source we hold, so none is published here. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring provider performs, arranges or guarantees on a family's behalf, and nobody should be charging you a fee to handle it.

sections.heading: The IGCSE calendar, counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Nobody competing for this search publishes a session calendar, which is strange, because the dates decide what tutoring can and cannot still achieve. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson runs International GCSE exams in May and June and again in November each year.

The gap between entry and paper is the fact most families underestimate. Cambridge's published key dates for its March 2027 series put final entries on 27 November 2026 for an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. That series is run for a particular region rather than the UAE, and it is used here purely as the worked example, because it is the one Cambridge publishes a complete key-dates sheet for. The shape holds for the UAE's June and November series: entries close months before anybody sits anything.

Zones add a second layer. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam where the wrong zone timetable was used. A revision plan should therefore be counted backwards from the school's own timetable. Two cousins at different UAE schools can genuinely sit the same paper on different days.

Counted backwards, the practical sequence looks like this. Twelve weeks out, content coverage should be finished and the work should be whole timed papers. Eight weeks out, the pupil's repeat errors should be a written list rather than a feeling. Four weeks out, nothing new is taught and the only activity is papers and mark schemes. After forecast grades go in, a tutor can still change the examined result but can no longer change the prediction a university already holds, which is why January is a far better month to start than April.

sections.heading: Inspection bands: what Outstanding and Acceptable actually tell a parent
paragraphs: Dubai families have access to something most countries do not: a published, comparable judgement on their child's school. The bands run from Outstanding through Very Good, Good and Acceptable down to Weak and Very Weak. Parents read them as a verdict on teaching quality, which is roughly right at whole-school level and close to useless at the level of one pupil in one subject set.

A report judges the school. It does not judge your child's maths set, the teacher they were allocated in September, or the department that lost two staff in November. A school rated Very Good can run an excellent English department beside a struggling Physics one, and the subject-level judgements inside the report are where that shows. Read those pages rather than the headline band, and ask the school directly about the subject you are considering paying for.

The distinction between attainment and progress is the other one worth learning. Attainment describes where pupils are against curriculum standards; progress describes how far they have travelled to get there. A set with high attainment and weak progress is coasting, and that specific combination is the strongest single argument for stretch work rather than remediation. The reverse pattern, weak attainment with strong progress, usually means the teaching is working and patience is cheaper than tutoring.

Outside Dubai the picture thins. ADEK publishes ratings for Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah are regulated locally with less published for parents to read, and in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah federal supervision means there is no emirate-level archive at all. Where the published record is thin, ask the school for its own subject-level results data and for the last two years of IGCSE grade distributions. A school confident in its teaching will share them.
