igcse-home-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: Four programmes cover almost every UAE family who arrives at this page. Two are the IGCSE itself, under its two main boards, which behave differently on codes, tiering and session dates. One is the Years 7 to 9 stage that decides how much ground has to be made up in Year 10. One is what comes immediately after, because the tier chosen at 14 quietly sets what is possible at 17.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE is examined by syllabus code rather than by subject name, and the code is what a tutor needs: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English, 0455 Economics. Most subjects run two or three written papers plus, in the sciences, an alternative-to-practical or practical component. Many subjects are tiered, so the entry itself caps the available grade. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with a separate March series in some zones, and every centre sits inside one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge IGCSE is the dominant route in the UAE's British-curriculum schools, which carry 37% of Dubai private-school enrolment on 2024-25 figures published by the Dubai Media Office. For a UAE family that means two practical consequences: the school's exams officer, not the parent, submits the tier entry, and the centre's administrative zone decides which version of the timetable applies. Cambridge is explicit that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used, so the version matters as much as the date.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses its own codes, which is where families get caught: 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology. Tiering is labelled Foundation and Higher rather than Core and Extended, and the Foundation ceiling is lower than many parents assume. Papers are examined in May and June and again in November each year. The specification content, the number of papers and the assessment weighting differ from the Cambridge equivalent in the same subject, so a tutor working from the wrong board teaches the wrong emphasis even when the topic names match.
programmes.countryNote: Plenty of UAE schools run a mixed entry, Cambridge in some subjects and Pearson in others, often because a department changed specification between cohorts. The practical step for a UAE parent is to get the code for every subject from the exams officer in writing before booking any tuition. Pearson published the November 2026 International GCSE final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, and releases provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is always the one to work from.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The stage before IGCSE is where most of the eventual gap is created and the cheapest place to close it. Cambridge Lower Secondary runs Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and those results are commonly used inside UAE schools to advise on tier placement for Year 10. Algebraic fluency, the structure of an extended written answer and the discipline of a scientific method are the three things that separate a comfortable Year 10 from a punishing one. None of them is examined in a way that creates urgency, which is exactly why they get left.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE this stage also carries the mandatory subjects, which are not optional at any year group in a Dubai private school. A Year 8 student who is behind in Arabic as a first language carries that into Year 10 at the same time as nine IGCSE courses start. Families who act in Years 7 to 9 are usually solving one subject at a time; families who wait until Year 11 are solving nine subjects and a Ministry subject in the same term, under an entry deadline that has already passed.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The next stage is worth understanding while the IGCSE tier is still being decided, because sixth-form entry requirements are written in IGCSE grades. Most UAE schools ask for a specified grade in the subject itself before admitting a student to the A Level, and a higher one in Mathematics and the sciences. The jump in reading load and in the length of a written answer is real, and the students who find it manageable are usually the ones who learned to write to a mark scheme in Year 11 rather than to a word count.
programmes.countryNote: There is a second reason to look this far ahead from the UAE. Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks, as reported in the July 2026 clarification, for proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, on top of five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3. The A Level is therefore not only a university matter. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae before you rely on it.

igcse-home-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects UAE families most often ask for by name, with the codes attached. Ask the school for the exact code before the first lesson. A Cambridge 0620 Chemistry student and a Pearson 4CH1 Chemistry student sit different papers with different weightings, and a tutor who does not know which is which will teach the overlap and miss the difference.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The tier decides the grade ceiling, so this is the first conversation to have with the school. Marks are lost in predictable places: unsimplified surds, bounds and rounding, transformations of graphs, and the method marks thrown away by answers written without working. Extended and Higher add topics most Core students have never seen rather than harder versions of familiar ones.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level Mathematics, and the single best preparation for it. It introduces calculus, trigonometric identities and vectors at a depth 0580 never reaches. Students who sit it tend to find the first term of AS Mathematics familiar rather than alarming, which is most of the reason UAE schools offer it.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two theory papers plus a practical component, which in most UAE centres is the alternative-to-practical paper rather than a laboratory assessment. Marks concentrate in graph work, rearranging equations with units attached, and the experimental-design questions where the mark is for naming the controlled variable and how it is controlled, not for the result.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry are where grades are won and lost, followed by organic reaction pathways and the qualitative-analysis tests that reward memorised precision. Paper 6, the alternative to practical, is the component most consistently under-practised in UAE schools, because it is examined as technique rather than as content and so cannot be revised from notes.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The content volume is the trap. Biology rewards exact terminology and penalises the almost-right word, so students who summarise in their own language score below students who learned the specification's. Extended adds depth in transport, homeostasis and inheritance. Long-answer questions are marked against specific points, which is a skill separate from knowing the topic.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0653 / 0654)
subjects.description: The route for students taking science as one or two awards rather than three separate subjects. The content is narrower than the separate sciences but the paper technique is identical, and sixth-form entry requirements often read differently for a Combined Science grade. Worth confirming with the school before Year 11 if A Level sciences are the plan.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading-response questions carry the marks, and both are assessed on handling the source text rather than on general writing quality. Students lose marks by summarising when asked to analyse, and by writing in a register the task did not ask for. Timing is the other recurring failure: the longest question is rarely the one worth most per minute.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, with and without the oral endorsement
subjects.description: Widely entered across UAE schools, and widely underestimated. The reading tasks test precise lifting of detail rather than gist, the writing tasks are marked against the stated purpose and audience, and the speaking component has its own criteria. Students who speak English all day still lose marks on the structure of a formal letter or report.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagrams are the marks. A correctly labelled supply and demand diagram with the shift drawn and explained outscores a paragraph that says the right thing without one. Command terms discriminate sharply here, because explain, analyse and discuss each require a different structure, and a UAE cohort often meets that distinction for the first time in Year 10.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study application is what separates grades. Students who recite the theory and never refer to the business in the stem lose the application and evaluation marks every time. The calculation elements, break-even, cash flow and ratios, are straightforward marks that go uncollected because they are practised less than the written sections.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478) and ICT (Cambridge 0417)
subjects.description: Two different subjects that UAE parents regularly conflate. Computer Science examines algorithms, data representation and a programming paper; ICT examines practical use of applications under timed conditions with its own assessment pattern. A student strong in one is not automatically suited to the other, and the choice is usually made in Year 9.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508) and Arabic as a Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.levels: Separate syllabuses, not tiers of one
subjects.description: Which one applies is decided by the student's background, and KHDA requires Dubai schools to organise Arabic as a first language in classes separate from non-Arab groups. The two syllabuses assess different things at different levels, so support has to be matched to the one the school entered, using the school's own set material.

igcse-home-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: This is where an IGCSE page should be specific, because the regulator changes at the emirate border and so does what you can ask for. Below is every emirate, the body that holds your child's school file and the one local question worth asking before you book anything. Three of these emirates are mentioned by none of the competitor pages ranking for this search.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA territory, 227 private schools and 17 curricula on 2024-25 figures. The useful local detail: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees would not rise for 2026-27, so a tutoring budget this year competes with a frozen fee rather than a rising one.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools here. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which rules out the nearest obvious option for many families.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK, and the emirate's quieter school market makes the specialist shortage sharper. A family needing Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics or 0417 ICT locally is often choosing between a generalist nearby and a subject specialist on screen.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education here and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ask the school which assessment routes it is approved to run before planning a November entry or a resit.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority, so the reference point for mandatory subjects and general regulations is the federal one. Evening availability is the practical constraint for families commuting to Dubai or Sharjah.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and, like Sharjah, approves curricula, courses, activities and assessment methods. Distance to a specialist is the reason online delivery matters more here than in Dubai, not less.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education supervision, a small private-school market on the east coast, and the longest drive to anywhere else in the country. A proximity search for an IGCSE tutor near me returns very little here, which is a fact about the map rather than about the student.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. For a subject such as 0620 Chemistry at Extended tier, a household here has effectively no local specialist pool, and online IGCSE tuition in the UAE is the only route that puts one in front of the student at all.

schoolClusters.note: The largest concentration of British-curriculum schools in the country, which is why Cambridge and Pearson codes sit side by side across the city and sometimes inside one school. Students we support here are typically entered through their school as internal candidates.

ADEK territory, where the professional-ethics position on staff tutoring their own school's students genuinely narrows a family's local options. The usual consequence is that a parent looks outside the school, and then outside the neighbourhood.

Smaller markets with real IGCSE cohorts and far fewer subject specialists within driving distance. Families here ask about coverage first and price second, which is the right order given how thin the local pool is for tiered science and Additional Mathematics.

It is the format with the clearest ceiling, because there is only so much a block can rebuild.

Sessions work on command terms, mark-scheme structure, working shown for method marks, and the order in which a paper is attempted. This is the format that most often moves a grade without new content, and the one families reach for last.

modes.description: Two narrow windows where a few weeks of work changes what is available later. Before Year 10 the question is the tier entry and the algebra behind it. After Year 11 the question is the reading load and the length of a written answer at AS level, which is the gap most students meet unprepared.

sections.heading: Which jobs in an IGCSE year actually have to be done near you
paragraphs: Start by separating the tasks. In a UAE IGCSE year there are about seven things that matter administratively, and only three of them have any real geography. Sitting the papers is local, because a candidate has to be in a room on a date Cambridge or Pearson fixed. Ministry of Education equivalency and attestation are local, because they are handled through official federal and emirate channels. The mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons are local, because they happen inside the school day. Everything else, including the teaching, is not.

This is the part a family searching for an IGCSE home tutor near me in the UAE rarely gets told, because it is not in a tutoring company's interest to say it. A tier entry is changed by email to the exams officer. A past paper is marked on a shared screen. A scheme of work is tracked from anywhere. The one task that absolutely requires a physical presence, the examination itself, is the one task no tutor can help with on the day. If your child is being entered as a private candidate rather than through a school, finding an exam centre for private candidates in your emirate is the genuinely local problem, and it should be solved months ahead of anything else on this list.

The table below is the version of this page we would hand a parent who had ten minutes. Read down the second column: wherever it says no, distance is not buying you anything, and a distance filter is simply removing specialists from the list. Wherever it says yes, nothing on this page helps, and the right call is the school office or the relevant authority.

sections.heading: Five authorities, one country: who holds your child's school file
paragraphs: A UAE parent is working inside a federal system with emirate-level education authorities, and the differences between them are not cosmetic. The u.ae guidance on private schools sets out the map: KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi, the Sharjah Private Education Authority in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Competitor pages ranking for this search mention ADEK by name essentially never, which tells you how much of this market is written from Dubai.

The powers differ in ways that change what you can ask. ADEK's described role is the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi. KHDA's is enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and it is KHDA that publishes the mandatory-subject requirements every licensed Dubai school must implement. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities go further still and approve fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Underneath all of them sits a federal baseline: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

For tutoring this has one blunt implication. Nobody tutoring your child is approved, licensed or endorsed by any of these bodies, and any page that suggests otherwise is describing something that does not exist for individual tutors. IB Gram holds no approval from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and does not claim one. What these bodies give a parent is better than an endorsement: published information about the school, which you can read before deciding whether the problem in front of you is a teaching gap, a tier problem or a timetable problem.

sections.heading: The three Ministry subjects sharing the week with nine IGCSEs
paragraphs: No international curriculum exempts a student in a Dubai private school from Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies. The KHDA mandatory subjects guidance is explicit that these are required regardless of the licensed curriculum, and it set a timetable for schools to have the requirements in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. A family planning IGCSE tuition around nine subjects is usually planning around eleven or twelve.

The rules are more specific than most parents realise, and they constrain what any tutor can honestly offer. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and KHDA states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language. Schools must also ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential that attaches to a school post and not to a private tutor.

There is one more constraint worth knowing before anyone sells you material. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. That means honest one-to-one support in these subjects works from the school's own issued material and the techniques for handling it: script fluency, memorisation method, source handling, the structure of an extended written answer. A tutor offering a parallel Arabic curriculum of their own invention is offering something the regulation does not allow a school to use.

sections.heading: The forty-minute lesson unit, and where a sixty-minute tutorial fits
paragraphs: Here is a piece of the UAE system almost nobody writing about tutoring mentions. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit. Schools are permitted to vary the length of a lesson provided the total weekly time for the subject is met, and the guidance advises that no mandatory-subject lesson should run shorter than twenty-five minutes. That single detail explains a lot of what parents find confusing about a UAE timetable: why periods are not an hour, why a subject appears three times in one week and twice in the next, and why a school can restructure the day without reducing a subject.

It also explains why a sixty-minute tutorial is not simply one more lesson. A child who has already sat through eight or nine forty-minute units, two of which were mandatory subjects taught in a second language, arrives at 5pm with a different kind of fatigue than the timetable suggests. In practice the families who get the most out of one-to-one time make two adjustments. They put the hardest subject in the earliest slot the tutor can offer rather than the latest one the family can manage, and they split the week rather than stacking it, because two forty-five minute sessions on different evenings outperform one ninety-minute block for almost every student under sixteen.

The second adjustment is about what the hour is used for. A school lesson has twenty-two other students in it, so it is necessarily paced for the middle. A one-to-one hour is the only teaching in the week that can be paced for one student, and spending it re-delivering content the class already covered wastes the one thing it is uniquely good at. The most productive use is almost always the student's own work: last week's homework, the mock script, the question they got wrong, marked against the published criteria while they watch. That is a format that works better over a shared screen than across a kitchen table, because the annotated version survives the lesson.

sections.heading: The permit question: the tutor in your building and the centre on your street
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and this is the part of a near-me search where proximity carries a real risk rather than a real benefit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two things follow. First, individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, so a parent is entitled to ask to see the permit before the first lesson and should. No fine schedule is published, so any page quoting you an amount is inventing it. Second, the permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff separately prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. The most convenient option in the building, your child's own teacher, is frequently the one option the rules close.

A tuition centre is a different legal animal from an individual. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute: initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a real permit held by real premises, and it is not something an online platform or an individual tutor holds. IB Gram does not hold it, has no UAE centre and does not describe itself as licensed by any UAE authority. What we do is check the permit position of the person teaching your child before they teach them.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs in this market, read against a frozen school fee
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages ranking for this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family transacts in. So here are the figures, in AED, each attributed to whoever published it, read in October 2026. They are market rates and not an IB Gram price list. Our own position is a free trial lesson first: one lesson, with the tutor your child would actually work with, booked without payment details, so the decision about rate comes after you have seen the teaching rather than before.

Read the bands against the thing they compete with. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a Dubai family that is unusual breathing room: the largest education line in the household budget is flat this year. It is the single best moment in recent memory to fund two terms of targeted one-to-one in a subject that is slipping, rather than discovering in Year 11 that the entry is already in at Core tier.

What drives the number is not distance and not branding. It is three things: whether the tutor teaches the specific syllabus and tier or the general subject, whether the hour includes marking the student's own script against the published criteria, and whether travel is inside the rate. A tutor travelling to a UAE address is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour in this market precisely because the car is in the price. Removing the car does not make the teaching worse; it makes the selection pool national rather than local, which for Extended-tier sciences in Ras Al Khaimah is the difference between a specialist and whoever is free.

sections.heading: A tutor who travels, and a specialist on screen: the comparison on its merits
paragraphs: This is the comparison the search phrase deserves, made honestly rather than defensively. In-home tuition is a real service with real advantages. A younger child who will not sit still for a video call is better served by an adult in the room. A student who needs physical apparatus in front of them, or whose household has no quiet corner and no reliable connection, is better served by someone at the table. We are not going to pretend otherwise, and a page that did would be lying to you about something you can check in one lesson.

What in-home costs you is the size of the pool. The specialist for Cambridge 0620 Chemistry Paper 6 or 0606 Additional Mathematics is not distributed evenly across seven emirates, and a twenty-minute radius does not contain one everywhere. Applied in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain it contains almost nobody. The second cost is the hour itself: arrival, settling, the conversation at the door, and the slot being set by a tutor's route between households rather than by when a fifteen-year-old can still think. The third is continuity, because a visiting tutor cannot follow a family to their summer address, and the summer before Year 11 is where a lot of ground is quietly lost.

To be plain about what IB Gram does: we do not send a tutor to a UAE address, and we do not offer that anywhere in this country. Home visits are part of our India service only. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own script on a shared screen and the annotated version saved afterwards. We say so in the table rather than in the small print, because a parent who booked expecting a car at the gate has been badly served by whoever took the booking.

sections.heading: The IGCSE entry deadline sits months before the paper, and the zone decides the timetable
paragraphs: The calendar is where UAE families lose options they did not know they had. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May and June and again in November. The useful thing about having two series a year is that a weak result in one is not a lost year. The dangerous thing is that the administrative dates sit a long way ahead of the papers, and nobody chases a parent about them.

Take a published Cambridge series as the worked example. For the March 2027 series, Cambridge gives the exam period as 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Read that order again: the IGCSE entry deadline falls more than two months before the first paper. A tier decision, a subject added or dropped, a private-candidate registration, all of it has to be settled by then. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and then a final one, so the live official timetable on the board's own site is always the document to work from rather than a date restated on a tutoring page.

One more administrative trap belongs to Cambridge specifically. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. Six timetables exist for one series; exactly one of them is yours, and your centre knows which. Alongside that sits the UAE calendar itself: Ramadan shortens the school day and changes when a family can realistically work, which makes IGCSE revision in Ramadan a planning question rather than an afterthought. Count backwards from the paper, place the intensive work outside the fasting hours that suit your household, and put the entry deadline in the calendar the day the series is confirmed.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: five subjects, not six
paragraphs: If the plan includes a UAE university, equivalency is the paperwork that decides whether an IGCSE and A Level file is accepted. On the British track, the July 2026 clarification reported by Gulf Today states the requirement as proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, together with a pass in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. The detail parents most often get wrong is which subjects count: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That matters because at least one page ranking for these searches tells UAE candidates they must take six IGCSE subjects. The sourced position is five, with Arabic and Islamic Education outside the count. Getting this wrong in Year 9 produces a subject block built around a number nobody asked for, usually at the cost of the one subject the student actually wanted. On the American track the same clarification sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with at least 450 in SAT Math required before applying.

Two cautions, both of which matter more than the convenience of a round number. There is no IB points threshold published in that clarification, so no equivalency figure for the Diploma appears on this page; anyone quoting you one should be asked where they read it. And equivalency is not something IB Gram performs, submits or influences. We can explain what the published requirement says and help a student reach the grades it asks for. The file itself goes through the Ministry and the emirate attestation channel, and the current requirement should be verified on moe.gov.ae before any family makes a subject decision on the strength of it.

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments. It is worth saying plainly what that is: a malpractice trigger that puts the student's certificate at risk, not a shortcut. The same principle governs IGCSE coursework components, portfolios and controlled assessments. The work has to be the student's own. A tutor who teaches, questions, models a technique and gives feedback on a draft is doing the job. A tutor who writes a paragraph into a draft, edits it to completion or supplies a finished piece has made the student's submission dishonest and the certificate unsafe.

In practice the honest version is more useful anyway. On a coursework component, one-to-one time is best spent on the criteria: reading the published descriptors with the student, identifying which band their current draft sits in and why, and letting them redraft. On a practical or alternative-to-practical paper, it is spent on method, variables, sources of error and the shape of a conclusion that earns marks. On a written paper it is spent on command terms and mark-scheme structure, using the student's own script. None of that requires anyone to write anything for them, and all of it transfers to the next paper.

There is a related limit on materials. We do not reproduce or supply Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides. Those belong to the boards, they are available through official channels and your child's school, and we reference and link them rather than host them. What a tutor brings is the reading of them: what a command term is actually asking, where the marks sit in a long-answer question, and why an answer that sounds correct scored two out of five.

process.title: Tell us the code, not just the subject
process.description: The first message we need is the syllabus code and tier for each subject: Cambridge 0580 Extended, Pearson 4CH1 Higher, and so on. Your school's exams officer can confirm all of it in one email. Matching on the code rather than the subject name is the single step that prevents a tutor teaching the wrong specification's emphasis.

process.title: A free trial lesson, with the tutor who would teach
process.description: One lesson at no charge, with the specialist your child would actually work with rather than a sales call or a demonstration by somebody else. No payment details are needed to book it. The point is to let you watch an hour of teaching before you decide anything about rate, frequency or commitment.

process.title: A plan counted backwards from the series
process.description: After the trial the tutor sets out what the remaining weeks can realistically reach, component by component, counted back from the first paper rather than forward from today. If the honest answer is that a block cannot rebuild two years of Extended Mathematics, you will hear that before you pay for it.

process.title: Weekly lessons, with the student's own work at the centre
process.description: Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Each one works on the student's actual homework, mock script or past-paper attempt, marked against the published criteria on a shared screen. The annotated version is saved so revision later in the year starts from the marked work rather than from memory.

process.title: A change of tutor if the match is wrong
process.description: Sometimes a competent tutor and a particular student simply do not work. Tell us early and we rematch within the same subject and tier rather than asking anyone to persist out of politeness. We would rather move a student in week two than discover in week ten that nobody said anything.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code and tier
whyPoints.description: A Cambridge 0620 student and a Pearson 4CH1 student study different specifications with different weightings. We match on the code the school entered and the tier on the entry form, because a tutor working from the wrong board teaches the overlap and misses the difference, which is invisible until the paper.

whyPoints.title: Coverage that does not stop at the Dubai city limit
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means a household in Fujairah, Umm Al Quwain or Ras Al Khaimah is choosing from the same specialists as a household in Jumeirah. In the three emirates no competitor page in this market even mentions, that is the difference between a subject specialist and no option at all.

whyPoints.title: The regulatory picture explained, not implied
whyPoints.description: We name KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Department of Knowledge and the Ministry of Education, explain what each one does, and point at their own published guidance. IB Gram holds no approval, licence or accreditation from any of them, and does not pretend to. What we offer is the map, so you know which office to ring.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty stated before you ask
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question, model and give feedback on the student's own work. Nobody writes a coursework paragraph, edits a draft to completion or supplies a finished piece, and we do not reproduce or distribute past papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents. In a market where one ranking page sells finished assessments, that distinction is the product.

whyPoints.title: Figures with a source and a date attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to whoever published it and dated October 2026, and they are market rates rather than ours. No invented satisfaction percentage, no self-awarded star rating, no tutor headcount nobody can audit. If a number on an IB Gram page has no source, it should not be there.

faqs.question: We searched for someone to teach our son nearby - what exactly is being delivered instead?
faqs.answer: One-to-one lessons over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with your son's own work on a shared screen. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are part of our India service only. The trade is deliberate. A distance filter chooses from the specialists who can reach your community by five o'clock; removing it chooses from the specialists who teach your son's syllabus code and tier. For a tiered science or Additional Mathematics, those two lists are rarely the same list, and in the northern emirates the first one is often empty.

faqs.question: Which authority holds our child's school file if we live in Ajman?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education. The u.ae guidance on private schools sets out the map: KHDA regulates Dubai, ADEK regulates Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge regulates Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Practically, that means your reference point for mandatory subjects and general regulations is the federal one rather than an emirate authority's publications. It also means questions a Dubai parent would take to KHDA go instead to the school and to the Ministry.

faqs.question: Does the Sharjah authority really approve assessment methods as well as fees?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth knowing before you plan a resit. The u.ae guidance states that the Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a wider power than inspection. For a family in either emirate the useful question to the school office is which assessment routes it is approved to run, because that determines whether a November entry or a particular tier is actually available at your centre. Do not assume a route exists because another emirate's schools offer it.

faqs.question: What does a forty-minute lesson unit in the school timetable mean for a sixty-minute tutorial?
faqs.answer: KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than twenty-five minutes. That is why UAE periods are not an hour. For tuition it has two consequences. A student arriving after eight or nine such units, some taught in a second language, is more tired than the clock suggests, so the earliest slot available beats the latest one that fits. And two forty-five minute sessions on separate evenings generally outperform one ninety-minute block.

faqs.question: Can the Arabic teacher at our school tutor our daughter privately after hours?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and this is the most common disappointment in a near-me search. The MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct barring the holder from serving students affiliated with their own school. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff separately prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at that school. A registered school teacher tutoring outside school hours also needs the permit. So the nearest qualified adult is frequently the one person the rules exclude, which is worth knowing before you ask and put a teacher in an awkward position.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education counted in the five subjects the Ministry asks for?
faqs.answer: No. The July 2026 equivalency clarification reported by Gulf Today is explicit that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects on the British track. The requirement is a pass in five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. One page ranking for these searches tells UAE candidates they need six IGCSE subjects. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae before building a subject block around either number.

faqs.question: Our son is on the Core tier and the course he wants asks for a higher grade - can the tier be changed?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but it is a deadline question rather than a teaching question. The tier sits on the entry form the school's exams officer submits, and the final entry deadline falls months before the paper: for the published Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries were due 27 November 2026 against an exam period starting 3 February 2027. Before that date a change is administrative. After it, the ceiling is fixed for that series. Ask the exams officer in writing what the deadline is for your centre, then ask whether the Extended content can realistically be covered in the time left.

faqs.question: How do we check that a private tutor in the UAE is permitted to charge us?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit issued in that person's name, before the first lesson. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you are quoted as invented.

faqs.question: The tuition centre near our villa says it is licensed - licensed by whom, and for what?
faqs.answer: If it has premises and staff in Dubai, the relevant document is a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. That process runs initial approval first, then up to six months to complete the permit and licence steps, with annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. Ask to see it and check the expiry. It is a genuine permit, and it is specific to premises. An individual tutor does not hold one, and neither does an online platform. IB Gram does not hold it, has no UAE centre and does not describe itself as licensed by any UAE authority.

faqs.question: Why is the IGCSE entry deadline months before the exam, and what happens if it is missed?
faqs.answer: Because entries drive timetabling, question-paper despatch and centre logistics across six administrative zones, all of which happen before anyone sits down. The published Cambridge March 2027 series shows the gap clearly: final entries 27 November 2026, exam period 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades 27 February 2027, results on Direct 13 May. Miss the deadline and the realistic options are the next series or a late-entry route your centre may or may not have, at the centre's discretion. Ask your exams officer for the deadline the day the series is confirmed.

faqs.question: Cambridge sent six versions of one timetable - which one applies to us?
faqs.answer: The one for your centre's administrative zone. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. Your school knows its zone; ask the exams officer to confirm it in writing and work only from that version. Pearson handles this differently, publishing provisional timetables ahead of each series and then a final one, so always work from the live official document.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan change how we should plan IGCSE revision?
faqs.answer: It changes the shape of the week rather than the amount of work. School days are shortened, routines move, and the hours in which a teenager can concentrate shift for many households. The practical approach is to decide early which part of the day actually works for your family, place the demanding components there, and use the shorter school day for the lighter revision rather than for nothing. Planning IGCSE revision in Ramadan around a fixed exam window is a scheduling exercise, and families who do it in advance lose far less than families who improvise.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately do with an IGCSE coursework draft?
faqs.answer: Read it, ask questions about it, point at the published criteria and say which band it currently sits in and why, model the technique on a different example, and hand it back for the student to redraft. What a tutor must not do is write any part of it, edit it to completion or supply a finished version. The work has to be the student's own; anything else makes the submission dishonest and the certificate unsafe. One page ranking in this market sells finished assessments outright, which is a malpractice trigger rather than a service.

faqs.question: Nobody near us teaches the subject combination our daughter has chosen - then what?
faqs.answer: That is the normal situation outside Dubai and Abu Dhabi, not an unusual one. For Extended-tier sciences, Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics or 0417 ICT, the local specialist pool in Fujairah, Umm Al Quwain or Ras Al Khaimah is thin to non-existent. Because every UAE lesson runs over live video, the pool we match from is not limited by your emirate. If we genuinely cannot cover a subject at the tier and standard needed, we say so and decline rather than putting a generalist in front of a specialist paper. You will hear that at the trial stage.

faqs.question: What has the Dubai school-fee freeze got to do with what we spend on tuition?
faqs.answer: It changes the budget arithmetic for one year. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. The largest education line in a Dubai household is therefore flat. Market one-to-one rates in this country run from AED 33 to AED 650 an hour depending on who is teaching, so a frozen fee is the year to fund targeted support in a subject that is slipping rather than waiting for a Year 11 report.

faqs.question: Do we have to pay anything before we meet the tutor?
faqs.answer: No. The first lesson is free, it is taught by the specialist your child would actually work with rather than by a salesperson or a demonstrator, and no payment details are required to book it. The condition is simply that it is one lesson, in one subject, at a time we can both make. After it the tutor sets out what the remaining weeks can realistically cover, component by component. If the honest answer is that the time left cannot reach the grade you are hoping for, you will be told that before any money changes hands.

igcse-home-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Start with the code, the tier and the deadline
igcse-home-tutor-near-me.closingBody: Three pieces of information turn a vague search into a plan: the syllabus code for each subject, the tier on the entry form, and the entry deadline for your centre's series. Your school's exams officer can supply all three in one email, and they decide more about the next twelve months than any tutor's postcode does. Send them to us with the subject that is slipping and we will arrange a free trial lesson with the specialist who teaches that code at that tier. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, from Dubai to Fujairah. If we cannot cover the subject properly, we will tell you so instead of taking the booking.

intro.heading: Pricing an IGCSE tutor is an arithmetic problem before it is a teaching one
paragraphs: A UAE parent searching for IGCSE home tutors is almost never asking whether tutoring exists. They have a report card with eight or nine subjects on it, two or three of them wrong, a quote in their inbox, and no way of telling whether AED 200 an hour is generous or careless. The published market gives them very little help. Of the competitor pages measured for this project in October 2026, three of six publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, a currency no family in Dubai or Abu Dhabi actually transacts in.

So this page starts with the number. Across advertised UAE rates read in October 2026, a university-student or platform tutor working online sits between AED 45 and AED 150 an hour. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between AED 150 and AED 300. A visiting tutor who drives to a villa in Mirdif or Khalifa City sits between AED 180 and AED 500 once travel is absorbed into the fee, with a rate aggregator's Dubai 2026 table putting the common in-home band at AED 180 to AED 350. Named specialists advertise upwards of AED 500. None of those are IB Gram prices; they are what the market publishes, and they are the backdrop any quote you receive has to be read against.

The reason the band is so wide has almost nothing to do with teaching quality and almost everything to do with structure. The IGCSE timetable is wide where the Diploma is deep: a Year 11 student typically carries eight to ten subjects, not six, which means the budget question is not how much per hour but how many of those subjects deserve an hour at all. The tier your child was entered for caps what a grade can reach. The board decides when entries close and therefore when demand for hours spikes. And the UAE adds its own lines: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies run alongside the licensed curriculum in every Dubai private school, which is teaching time already inside the fee you pay.

The value argument for teaching over live video is not that it is cheaper, although it usually is once travel stops being billable. It is that it decouples the tutor from the drive. A family in Al Ain looking for Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478 is not choosing from the people who will cross town for an 8pm Tuesday; they are choosing a specialist in that syllabus and scheduling around Gulf Standard Time. That changes the match before it changes the invoice.

What follows is the whole cost structure, with the sources attached. Where a figure comes from a provider page or a rate table, the page says so and gives the month. Where a figure is not verifiable, the page does not print one: that applies to exam entry fees, which are set by the centre rather than published centrally, and to penalty amounts under the tutoring permit regime, which the ministry has not published.

igcse-home-tutors.programmesIntro: Four stages matter to the cost conversation, because the money behaves differently in each one. Spending in Year 9 buys foundations cheaply. Spending in Year 11 buys exam technique expensively. The stage your child is in should decide the shape of the block you book.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before an IGCSE option form is signed. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October, and the results are the cheapest early-warning system a parent gets. A child whose Checkpoint maths sits below the class median is the child who will be offered the Core tier in Year 10, and that offer is far easier to argue with before it is made than after.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE this stage is where Arabic streams diverge. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabic as a first language and Arabic as an additional language, and prohibits combining the two groups, so a non-Arab child who arrives in Year 8 enters a different Arabic pathway from an Arab classmate at the same desk. Families who sort that out at the start spend nothing on it later.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Eight to ten subjects sat as separate qualifications, several of them tiered into Core and Extended papers. Syllabus codes matter more than subject names once money is involved: Mathematics 0580 and International Mathematics 0607 are different courses with different papers, and a tutor booked for the wrong one is an hour spent in the wrong place. Cambridge runs a June and a November series, plus a March series with its own key dates.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper after the wrong zone timetable was used. Two UAE schools in different zones can sit the same paper on different days. Before buying exam-term hours, get the zone timetable your child's centre actually follows rather than the one a search result offers.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other board a UAE school may enter, graded 9 to 1, with its own codes: 4MA1 for Mathematics, 4PH1 for Physics, 4BI1 for Biology. Some Pearson qualifications allow units to be sat across more than one series, which spreads both the risk and the spending rather than loading everything onto one fortnight. Papers are not interchangeable with Cambridge papers, and nor is the past-paper practice.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson offers International GCSE in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so a UAE family planning a winter resit should work from the live PDF on the Pearson site rather than last year's dates.

programmes.name: What the IGCSE grades buy next
programmes.description: IGCSE grades are entry tickets, and that is the honest case for spending on them. Sixth-form maths and the sciences assume Extended-tier content, so a Core pass can close a door that costs far more to reopen later. This is the stage where the Ministry of Education equivalency file also starts to matter, because the British track asks for A Level or AS Level results on top of the IGCSE count.
programmes.countryNote: For the British track, reporting in July 2026 set out one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3. Verify the current wording on moe.gov.ae before planning around it, and treat any provider offering to arrange equivalency for a fee with scepticism.

igcse-home-tutors.subjectsIntro: Ten subjects where UAE families most often buy IGCSE hours, each with the syllabus code and a note on what the money is actually being spent on. The pattern worth noticing: the cheapest grade moves come from marking discipline, the dearest from content that was never learned in Year 10.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The highest-volume request in the UAE and the one where paid hours repay fastest, because most lost marks are procedural rather than conceptual: method marks forfeited by missing working, bounds and rounding, and the algebraic manipulation questions late in Paper 4. An hour spent marking a past paper against the published scheme usually finds more marks than an hour of re-teaching.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (Cambridge 0607)
subjects.description: Not 0580 with a different cover. It carries a graphics-calculator requirement and an investigation paper, and a tutor who prepares a student for 0580 Paper 4 has prepared them for the wrong assessment. Confirm the code on your child's statement of entry before booking a block, because this is the single most common wasted-hours mistake in UAE maths tutoring.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity, moments and the practical component are where the grade is decided. Cambridge offers an alternative-to-practical written paper, which is examinable technique rather than laboratory skill: reading a scale, identifying a control variable, explaining an anomalous point. That makes it genuinely teachable over video, and it is usually the cheapest marks on the paper.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry carry the arithmetic, organic chemistry carries the memory load, and qualitative analysis carries the practical marks. A student who can balance an equation but cannot convert between mass, moles and concentration is losing marks in a narrow, diagnosable band, which is the sort of problem a short paid block fixes well.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The most volume-dependent of the three sciences and the one where tutoring is most often bought too late. Marks go on command-term discipline rather than knowledge: describe against explain, the difference between a trend and a reason, and the structured long-answer questions where a correct idea written in the wrong register earns nothing.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500, Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response reward a mark-scheme-aware structure that very few students arrive with. The value here is unusual: a handful of hours on how the criteria are applied often moves a grade further than a term of general reading, because the student already has the vocabulary and is losing marks on shape.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Widely taken across the UAE, and the subject where tier choice has the clearest consequence for a Ministry of Education equivalency count. The reading comprehension and summary tasks are heavily technique-driven, so sessions are best spent on timed extraction and paraphrase rather than on conversation practice the school already provides.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the data-response paper decide the grade. Students lose marks drawing an unlabelled axis or an unshifted curve, then lose more by evaluating without ever reaching a judgement. Both failures are correctable in a short block, which makes Economics one of the better-value late additions to a revision plan.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: The case-study paper punishes generic answers. A candidate who can define cash flow but cannot apply it to the named firm in the stimulus will sit in the middle of the grade range all year. Paid hours here are about application discipline, and progress is visible on a marked paper within two or three sessions.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Thin on the ground in the UAE in-home market, and a clear illustration of why a visiting tutor is a narrower pool than an online one. Pseudocode conventions, trace tables and the practical problem-solving paper need a specialist in this syllabus, not a general IT teacher, and families outside Dubai often cannot find one within driving distance at any price.

igcse-home-tutors.regionsTitle: What the same IGCSE hour costs in each emirate
igcse-home-tutors.regionsIntro: Geography changes a tutoring bill in the UAE in two ways: travel time that a visiting tutor has to price in, and the depth of the local teaching pool. Both get worse the further you are from Dubai. Neither affects a lesson taught over live video.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The deepest pool and the tightest market. KHDA oversees 227 private schools serving 387,441 students in 2024-25, with 37% on a UK curriculum, so Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE tutors are easier to find here than anywhere else. A cross-city evening journey is still an hour of someone's time that lands inside an in-home fee.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK licenses and accredits private schools in the emirate, and its professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school. Practically, that removes the convenient option many families assume exists, and in Khalifa City or Al Reef the remaining visiting pool is small enough to carry a premium.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, and far enough from both coasts that specialist subjects simply do not have a local in-home market. Families here routinely find Chemistry 0620 or Computer Science 0478 unavailable at any travel rate, which is the clearest case in the country for teaching over video rather than by car.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Many families work in Dubai and live here, so a 4pm session is unrealistic on a weekday; a 7.30pm online slot after the commute is the one that survives a term.

regions.name: Ajman and Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Private schools in both emirates are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than a local authority. The in-home IGCSE market is thin to the point of absence for sciences and computer science, and competitor pages across this whole SERP mention neither emirate at all, which tells you how much local supply there is.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in RAK and, like SPEA, approves fees and curricula. The driving distance from Dubai means a visiting specialist would price two hours of travel into a one-hour lesson. Online scheduling removes that line from the quote entirely.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education territory on the east coast, and the furthest a UAE family can be from a dense tutoring market. For a tiered subject where the Extended papers need a subject specialist, the realistic choice here is a live video lesson or nothing, and the rate should reflect teaching rather than mileage.

schoolClusters.note: The largest concentration of Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE candidates in the country, and the reason Dubai has the deepest subject-specialist pool. Students we support attend schools across this cluster. Rates quoted to families here tend to sit in the middle of the advertised band, because supply is real and comparison is easy.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain cluster
schoolClusters.note: Schools under ADEK oversight, where IGCSE candidates sit alongside a large British-curriculum cohort. Families here report a narrower visiting-tutor market than Dubai, especially for Extended-tier sciences, and ADEK's ethics rules close off the option of paying a child's own classroom teacher for evening lessons.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the Northern Emirates cluster
schoolClusters.note: Schools under SPEA, the RAK Department of Knowledge and the federal Ministry of Education. The IGCSE cohort is substantial but geographically spread, so the local in-home market cannot staff every syllabus. This is where online delivery stops being a preference and becomes the only way to reach a 0478 or 0607 specialist.

modes.description: The cheapest way to find out whether tuition is the right purchase at all. Four sessions on one subject, built around a past paper marked against the published scheme, which produces a list of where marks are actually going. Families who do this first often buy fewer hours overall, because two of the three subjects they were worried about turn out not to need paid help.

Booked by the term rather than by the month, a weekly slot holds the same tutor and the same hour, which matters more to a Year 11 timetable than the per-hour rate does.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges for IGCSE support, and what sits inside the number
paragraphs: An IGCSE tutor in the UAE is advertised between roughly AED 45 and AED 650 an hour, and the single number a family needs is which part of that range applies to them. Read in October 2026: platform and university-student tutors advertise from AED 45 to AED 150 online; a qualified subject tutor advertises AED 150 to AED 300 online; a visiting tutor who absorbs travel into the fee advertises AED 180 to AED 500, with a Dubai rate aggregator putting the common in-home band at AED 180 to AED 350. Named specialists publish rates above AED 500.

What separates those tiers is not effort. It is three things a parent can check. Whether the tutor teaches the exact syllabus code on the statement of entry, or the subject in general. Whether the hour is a 60-minute hour or a 45-minute school period, which changes the real rate by a third without changing the headline. And whether travel is inside the fee, because a visiting arrangement is buying a journey as well as a lesson, and the journey is the least educational thing on the invoice.

One figure that should never appear anywhere in a quote is a permit cost. The UAE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. A provider adding a licensing or registration line to a first invoice is charging you for something that costs them nothing. The same goes for exam entry fees, which are set and billed by the exam centre rather than by any tutor.

Ask which syllabus code the tutor teaches: 0580 and 0607 are not interchangeable
Ask whether travel, materials or administration appear as separate lines
Refuse any permit, licensing or registration fee: the MoHRE permit is free

sections.heading: Nine subjects, one budget: the triage that comes before the first invoice
paragraphs: This is the structural difference between IGCSE and the Diploma, and it is the part no competitor page addresses. A Diploma student has six subjects, so a worried parent can plausibly consider tutoring all of the weak ones. A Year 11 IGCSE student carries eight to ten separate qualifications. At market rates, buying a weekly hour in four of them runs past AED 3,000 a month before anyone has looked at whether four tutors were needed.

The triage that works starts from the mark, not the mood. For each subject, write down where the grade sits, then write down what is holding it there. There are only a few real answers. Content never learned, which is expensive and slow. Technique and mark-scheme register, which is cheap and fast. Volume of practice, which costs nothing but time. Or a tier or code mismatch, which no amount of tutoring fixes because the problem is on the entry form.

Done honestly, the list almost always collapses. Two subjects are losing marks to technique and will move inside a month. One has a genuine content hole from Year 10 and needs a proper block. The rest need past papers and a quiet room. That is a plan with one or two paid subjects in it rather than four, and it is why the diagnostic block is the first thing worth buying: it converts a vague worry about nine subjects into a short written list of where marks are actually going.

sections.heading: The grade you are moving from decides what the hour is worth
paragraphs: Tutoring is priced by the hour and valued by the move, and those two things are not proportional. Moving a student from a 4 to a 6 is usually a matter of recovering marks they are already close to earning: method marks, command-term register, diagram labels, the arithmetic in a multi-step question. Those are dense, teachable and visible fast. Moving a student from a 7 to a 9 means competing for the marks that discriminate at the top of the paper, which are fewer, harder and far less responsive to a weekly hour.

That has a direct consequence for how a family should spend. If the budget covers one subject, put it where the gap between current and achievable is widest and the cause is technique. If the budget covers two, do not spread them across a strong subject and a weak one out of fairness; the strong subject will move least per dirham. And if a provider is quoting a premium rate on the grounds that your child is near the top of the range, ask what specifically it buys, because scarcity of top-end specialists is a real cost and a reputation premium is not.

The honest limit on all of this is that nobody can promise a grade. No tutor controls grade boundaries, the question paper, or what happens in the hall. What a tutor can be held to is evidence: that marks are moving on marked papers, by question, over weeks you can count. Any quote that leans on a promised outcome rather than a described method should be read carefully, and any provider offering a grade guarantee is selling something it cannot deliver.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tier decision, priced
paragraphs: Tiered Cambridge IGCSE syllabuses offer two routes through the same subject, and the route decides the grade range available before a single lesson is bought. The Core papers award a restricted upper range; the Extended papers reach the top grades. Check the tier for each subject on the syllabus page at cambridgeinternational.org and on your child's statement of entry, because the two sometimes disagree and the statement is the one that counts.

Priced, the decision cuts both ways. An Extended entry carries more content and usually more hours, so it is the more expensive route to support. But a Core entry that was accepted passively is the most expensive thing on this page, because the cost of it arrives two years later when a sixth-form maths or science course assumes Extended content the student never met. Reopening that door means a resit series, a second set of entry fees and a term of catch-up.

The practical point is timing. Tier is fixed by the entry, and entries close long before the papers: Cambridge final entries for the March 2027 series were due on 27 November 2026, against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. A tier conversation in Year 10, backed by Checkpoint results and a marked past paper, is free. The same conversation after the entry deadline is not a conversation at all. If you are going to spend one unpaid hour on your child's IGCSEs this year, spend it reading the statement of entry.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: the same subject, two spending calendars
paragraphs: A UAE family rarely chooses the board; the school has. But knowing which one you are in changes when money should be spent, because the two run different clocks. Cambridge International examines IGCSE in a June and a November series, with a March series carrying its own key dates, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version. Pearson examines International GCSE in May/June and November, and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series.

The dated example is worth having in front of you. For the Cambridge March 2027 series: final entries 27 November 2026, exam period 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results released on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. The spending implication is blunt. The decision that mattered most - subjects, tier, whether to enter at all - had to be made in November, ten weeks before the first paper and nearly six months before results.

Pearson's calendar creates a different option. Its November series gives a second window inside the same academic year, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which means a resit can be marked and in hand before a sixth-form application closes. For some qualifications, units can be sat across more than one series, which spreads both the exam risk and the tutoring spend instead of concentrating everything into one fortnight in June. Check the live timetable PDF on the board's own site before you plan a term around any of it.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor and an online hour are not the same purchase
paragraphs: This page is about IGCSE home tutors because that is the phrase UAE parents type, and it deserves a straight answer. A visiting arrangement in the Emirates is advertised at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel absorbed, and monthly in-home packages run at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. What a family gets for that is a lesson plus a journey, delivered by whoever is willing to make the journey.

IB Gram does not operate that way in the UAE. Lessons here are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time; visiting tutors are a service offered only in India. That is a limit stated plainly rather than hidden behind a booking form, and the argument for it is about the pool rather than the price. A family in Al Ain who needs Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478 is not choosing between specialists when they hire locally - they are choosing among the people within driving distance, which in several emirates is nobody at all.

There are real things an in-home arrangement does better. A younger child who cannot yet manage a screen session alone, a household with unreliable connectivity, a student whose focus holds better with someone physically present: those are genuine reasons, and a family weighing them should weigh them honestly. For an exam-year IGCSE candidate working on marked papers and syllabus-specific technique, though, the trade is usually the other way, and the table sets out exactly what each format is buying.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE tutoring money gets wasted in the UAE
paragraphs: Waste in this market is rarely fraud. It is usually a family paying a fair rate for the wrong thing. The commonest version is paying to re-teach content the school is teaching anyway, in a subject where the student is losing marks on register rather than knowledge. The second commonest is paying for a subject that needed past papers and a quiet evening, while the subject with the real content hole goes untutored because it felt less urgent.

Then there are the charges that should not be there at all. The MoHRE private tuition work permit is free of charge for two years, so no permit or licensing line belongs on an invoice. Boards' past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are copyright material that a provider should be linking you to on the official site, not selling as a resource pack. Nobody should be charging a fee to arrange Ministry of Education equivalency, which is a process families complete through the official channel themselves.

The last category is the most expensive and the quietest: paying for weeks that are not teaching weeks. A month containing Eid, a school mock fortnight or a half-term break does not contain four usable sessions, and a package bought by the month absorbs that difference silently. Pay by the term with the teaching weeks counted, or by the session, and the arithmetic stays yours. Ask for the teaching-week count in writing before a package is agreed; a provider who will not give you one is telling you something.
