sections.heading: Five subjects at grade 3 or E: what the equivalency file changes about the budget
paragraphs: The Ministry of Education equivalency file is where IGCSE spending decisions and UAE university access meet, and almost no competitor page mentions it. On the British track, reporting in July 2026 set out that students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, alongside one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that changes a budget is what is excluded. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects. A family buying weekly Arabic tuition in the belief that it strengthens the equivalency count is spending in a place the count does not look, and the same money moved to a tiered science or to Mathematics 0580 would be working on a subject that does count. One page currently ranking in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five.

Two cautions belong with that. The first is that this is a regulatory process that changes, and it should be verified on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate before any plan is built on it; this page describes it and points you there rather than performing it. The second is that no amount of tutoring is required for equivalency, and any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a government procedure. There is no published IB points threshold we can verify, so this page prints none.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and paying for weeks that are not teaching weeks
paragraphs: The UAE academic year does not deliver four identical teaching weeks a month, and a tutoring budget built as though it does leaks money. Ramadan shortens the school day. Eid removes a week. Mock fortnights fill the evenings a student would otherwise revise in. A June Cambridge series or a late-October Pearson series sits at a fixed distance from all of that, and the revision has to fit around it rather than the other way round.

Handled well, this is a scheduling question rather than a cost increase. During Ramadan, sessions move to post-Iftar slots, which for many families produce better concentration than a 5pm session on a shortened school day ever did. Across Eid, the sensible move is to pause rather than compress, then resume with the same tutor in the same slot. In a mock fortnight, the single most valuable hour is spent marking the mock paper that has just come back, because it is the most recent evidence anyone has.

The practical rule is to count teaching weeks before agreeing a block, and to put the count in writing. A twelve-week term containing Eid and a mock fortnight is not twelve sessions. A family that books ten and keeps two in reserve for the week a paper comes back marked will spend less and get more than a family that bought twelve and lost three to the calendar. This is also the honest answer to whether rates rise before a series: demand firms up, so the slot is worth booking early.

sections.heading: What a tutor may not sell you, at any price
paragraphs: Some of what is for sale in this market should not be bought. There are providers advertising finished coursework and completed assessed pieces to IGCSE and Diploma students in the Gulf, priced in the thousands of dirhams. What a family is buying there is a malpractice risk attached to their child's name, and the exposure sits with the candidate, not the seller. A board that identifies work which is not the student's own can withdraw a grade and, in the IB's case, a whole certificate.

The line a legitimate tutor works inside is clear enough to put in writing. A tutor may teach the content, explain what a criterion is asking for, model the technique on a different question, and give feedback on a draft the student produced. A tutor may not supply text that ends up in a portfolio, may not hand over a finished piece, and may not sit alongside a controlled assessment. Where a school's deadline is on Friday, the answer is feedback on Wednesday on what the student has written, not a replacement.

Two related claims belong in the same bin. A provider describing its tutors as approved by a regulator or a board is describing something that does not exist for individual tutors: KHDA's educational services permit is issued to training institutes with premises, and the MoHRE permit is a work authorisation, not a quality mark. And a tutor described as an examiner should be able to evidence it, because examiner status is often used to imply access to marking standards and boundaries that no individual can offer.

sections.heading: Six paid hours in: what you should be able to see
paragraphs: The weakest part of most tutoring arrangements is that nobody agreed what success would look like. Six hours is enough to answer the question if the evidence was specified in advance. What a parent should have after six sessions is not a feeling that things are better. It is a marked past paper with the marks attributed by question, a comparison against an earlier paper of the same type, and a short written list of what is still losing marks.

Three signals say the money is working. Marks are recovering in the band the diagnostic identified, not in general. The student can say what a command term is asking for and show the difference between a describe answer and an explain answer on their own script. And the tutor's notes are specific enough that you could hand them to a different teacher and they would know where to start. If all three are present after six hours, extend the block. If none are, change something before buying twelve more.

The reverse is worth saying too. If a subject was triaged in and turns out not to need paid hours, stop paying for it. Dropping a subject from the plan after four weeks is a sign the triage worked, not that the money was wasted. The point of starting with one diagnostic block in one subject, rather than four weekly slots across four, is that it keeps every decision reversible while the evidence is still cheap to collect.

process.title: Say which codes, not which subjects
process.description: Send the statement of entry or the last report with the syllabus codes on it: 0580 or 0607, 0620 or 4CH1, Core or Extended. A code tells us which specialist to look for and which past papers to mark. A subject name tells us almost nothing, and is how families end up paying for the wrong assessment.

process.title: Triage before you buy
process.description: We go through the timetable subject by subject and separate content gaps from technique losses from subjects that only need practice. The output is a short list of which one or two subjects repay paid hours this term, which is usually fewer than the family arrived expecting.

process.title: A trial lesson on the real material
process.description: One lesson with the matched tutor, using your child's own marked work rather than a generic assessment, before any block is confirmed. It exists so you can judge the match on evidence. If the fit is wrong, we match again rather than asking you to make it work.

process.title: Book the block in teaching weeks
process.description: Sessions are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school day, the commute and Ramadan timings, and the block is counted in teaching weeks rather than calendar months so Eid and mock fortnights do not quietly absorb sessions you have paid for.

process.title: Review on marked papers at six hours
process.description: At the six-hour mark we look at a marked paper against an earlier one of the same type, with the marks attributed by question. That conversation ends in one of three decisions: extend the block, change the focus, or stop paying for this subject because it no longer needs the hours.

whyPoints.title: The rates are on the page, with sources
whyPoints.description: Three of six competitor pages measured in October 2026 publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars. Every AED band here carries where it came from and the month it was read, so a quote you receive can be compared against something rather than taken on trust.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the syllabus code
whyPoints.description: Mathematics 0580 and International Mathematics 0607 are different courses with different papers, and Cambridge and Pearson sciences are not interchangeable. Tutors are matched to the code on the statement of entry, which removes the single most common source of wasted IGCSE tutoring hours.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. Visiting tutors are a service IB Gram offers only in India. You know which product you are buying before you book, rather than discovering the delivery model after a deposit has moved.

whyPoints.title: Reach beyond the driving radius
whyPoints.description: A family in Fujairah, Umm Al Quwain or Al Ain choosing an in-home tutor is choosing from whoever will travel. Teaching over video replaces that constraint with a subject constraint, which is how an Extended-tier Chemistry or a 0478 Computer Science specialist becomes reachable at all.

whyPoints.title: Fewer paid subjects, chosen deliberately
whyPoints.description: A Year 11 timetable carries eight to ten qualifications, and tutoring all the weak ones is how a budget disappears. Triage puts the hours where the gap is widest and the cause is fixable, and takes subjects off the plan when the evidence says they do not need paying for.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line in writing
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, explain criteria, model technique and give feedback on work the student has produced. Nobody supplies text for a portfolio or hands over a finished piece. That is a boundary worth stating plainly in a market where completed assessed work is openly advertised.

faqs.question: We have been quoted AED 180 and AED 450 for the same IGCSE subject. Which quote is right?
faqs.answer: Both can be legitimate, because they are usually selling different things. Read in October 2026, the UAE market advertises AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online and AED 180 to AED 500 for a visiting tutor with travel inside the fee. Ask three questions before deciding: is the rate per 60 minutes or per 45-minute period, which syllabus code does the tutor actually teach, and is travel being billed. A higher figure is only better value if it buys a specialist in the exact code on your child's statement of entry.

faqs.question: My son takes nine IGCSE subjects. How many should we actually pay for tuition in?
faqs.answer: Usually one or two at a time, not four. A Diploma student has six subjects, so tutoring every weak one is at least arithmetically possible. A nine-subject Year 11 timetable is not: weekly hours in four subjects at market rates passes AED 3,000 a month. Triage each subject by what is holding the grade there. Content gaps need a block. Command-term register needs a handful of hours. Volume of practice needs time, not money. Most families find two subjects genuinely need paid support and the rest need past papers and a quiet evening.

faqs.question: Does a grade 4 to grade 6 move cost the same as a grade 7 to grade 9 move?
faqs.answer: No, and the difference is large. A 4 to a 6 is mostly about recovering marks the student is already close to earning: method marks, diagram labels, answering describe when the question says describe. Those are dense on the paper and respond quickly. A 7 to a 9 competes for the discriminating marks at the top, which are few and much less responsive to a weekly hour. If one subject is funded, put the money where the gap is widest and the cause is technique, not where the child is already strong.

faqs.question: Is the quoted IGCSE rate per 60-minute hour or per school period?
faqs.answer: Always ask, in writing, because a 45-minute period billed as an hour raises the real rate by about a third without changing the headline figure. Market comparisons across the UAE are published per hour, so a per-period quote is not comparable to them until you convert it. The same applies to any package: ask how long a session is, how many sessions the month contains, and how many of those weeks are actually teaching weeks once Eid, half-term and the mock fortnight are taken out.

faqs.question: Should we pay for Arabic tuition to strengthen the Ministry of Education equivalency file?
faqs.answer: Not for that reason. Reporting in July 2026 on the UAE equivalency requirements stated that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects the file counts. If Arabic needs support for its own sake, that is a separate decision, and the mandatory stream is in any case taught and assessed inside your school fee under KHDA's requirements. Money moved from Arabic to Mathematics 0580 or a tiered science is working on a subject the count actually looks at. Verify the current rules on moe.gov.ae before planning around them.

faqs.question: Our daughter is on the Core tier in Maths. Is paying for Extended-level tuition wasted money?
faqs.answer: It is misaimed while the entry stands, because the Core papers award a restricted upper grade range however well she is taught. The useful spend is on the tier conversation itself: bring a marked past paper to the school before the centre's final entry deadline and ask what evidence would support an Extended entry. Cambridge final entries for the March 2027 series were due on 27 November 2026, against papers in February, so this is a Year 10 and early Year 11 decision. Once the entry closes, tutoring should target the papers she is actually sitting.

faqs.question: How much is the IGCSE exam entry itself, and who sets that figure?
faqs.answer: Entry fees are set and billed by the exam centre rather than published as a single national figure, so any page quoting you one number is guessing. A school normally bills entries with term fees. A private candidate pays the centre's own published candidate fee, which varies by centre and by subject. Ask your child's exams officer for the per-subject figure in writing before deciding how many subjects to enter, and treat it as a separate budget line from tutoring. No tutor should be charging an entry fee on your behalf.

faqs.question: Is small-group IGCSE tuition genuinely better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It can be, on one condition: the students are on the same board, the same syllabus code and the same tier, and are losing marks in roughly the same place. Two Extended 0580 candidates both forfeiting method marks will learn well together. A Core candidate and an Extended candidate in the same hour means one of them is in the wrong lesson. Watch the pricing too: a group rate should be per student and visibly below the one-to-one rate, and a group session priced at the individual rate is simply a higher margin.

faqs.question: Does the hourly rate for IGCSE support rise as the exam series gets closer?
faqs.answer: Demand firms up, and so do slots. In the eight to twelve weeks before a series, the evenings a Year 11 student can use are contested, and the specialists in scarce codes fill up first. The practical answer is not to hunt a discount in February but to reserve the slot in autumn, when the same tutor and the same hour are available and the cheapest teaching weeks of the whole course are still ahead. A family that books the slot early is buying availability as much as a rate.

faqs.question: Should a provider charge us for IGCSE past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No. Board syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are copyright material belonging to Cambridge and Pearson, and a provider should be pointing you to the official site rather than selling a resource pack. What you are legitimately paying for is the teaching around that material: a paper marked against the published scheme with the losses attributed by question. If a resource charge appears on an invoice, ask what it covers and where the material came from.

faqs.question: The private tuition permit is free, so why does a permitted tutor charge more?
faqs.answer: Because the permit is a legal authorisation, not a quality mark. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. So a rate difference reflects subject expertise and experience, never permit cost, and no permit or licensing line belongs on your invoice.

faqs.question: We have eight weeks before the first paper. What is a sensible amount to spend now?
faqs.answer: Enough for one subject, properly, rather than a little for three. Eight weeks supports a weekly session plus a full past paper in the subject where marks are most recoverable, which is usually the one losing method marks or command-term register rather than the one with a content hole from Year 10. Spend the first session on a marked paper so the remaining seven have a target. Spreading the same budget across three subjects in eight weeks generally produces three sets of notes and no measurable change on any paper.

faqs.question: Does a Pearson Edexcel entry spread the cost more evenly than Cambridge?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth checking against the specification. Pearson examines International GCSE in May/June and November each year, and some qualifications allow units to be sat across more than one series rather than all at once, which spreads the exam risk and the tutoring spend. Cambridge runs June and November series plus a March series, each as a complete set of papers, so support tends to concentrate into one block. Neither is better; they just ask for money at different times. Your school has usually already chosen the board.

faqs.question: If we pay for a term and the match turns out to be wrong, what happens?
faqs.answer: That is a question to settle before any money moves, in writing. Ask what happens to unused sessions, whether a rematch costs anything, and how many sessions' notice a change needs. The trial lesson exists so the match is tested on your child's own marked work first, which is cheaper than finding out in week five. Treat any provider that will not put the rematch terms in writing as a risk, and be cautious of outcome-linked refund offers, since no tutor controls grade boundaries or the paper itself.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to our address anywhere in the Emirates?
faqs.answer: No. For families in the UAE, IGCSE teaching is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school day, the commute and Ramadan timings. Visiting tutors are a service IB Gram offers only in India. The reason is the size of the pool: outside Dubai, the in-home market cannot staff syllabuses such as Computer Science 0478 or International Mathematics 0607 at any travel rate, while a video lesson is matched on the code rather than on the postcode.

faqs.question: How do we tell after a month whether the tutoring is worth the money?
faqs.answer: Agree the evidence before the first paid hour. After about six sessions you should have a past paper marked against the published scheme with the marks attributed by question, a comparison against an earlier paper of the same type, and a written list of what is still losing marks. Your child should also be able to show, on their own script, the difference between a describe answer and an explain answer. If those are present, extend the block. If none are, change the focus or the tutor before buying another twelve hours.

igcse-home-tutors.closingHeading: Start with the arithmetic, then book one subject
igcse-home-tutors.closingBody: The useful next step is not a bigger budget. It is a shorter list. Send the statement of entry or the last report with the syllabus codes on it, and we will go through the timetable subject by subject and say which one or two genuinely repay paid hours this term and which need past papers and a quiet evening. A trial lesson on your child's own marked work comes before any block is confirmed, so the match is judged on evidence rather than on a profile. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, anywhere in the Emirates.

intro.heading: The system your child's IGCSE sits inside, before anyone talks about tuition
paragraphs: IGCSE online tuition in the UAE means a timetabled one-to-one lesson over live video with a tutor who teaches your child's exact specification: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 rather than 'maths', Pearson 4PH1 rather than 'physics'. IB Gram delivers it that way in every emirate. No tutor is sent to a UAE address; home visiting is a service we run only in India. What a UAE family gets instead is the pick of specialists for one narrow paper, available at five o'clock in Ras Al Khaimah as readily as in Jumeirah, with the whole evening's driving taken out of the arrangement.

The part nobody explains is that your child's school answers to a different authority depending on which emirate it stands in. Dubai's private schools sit with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as 'responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate'. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its own Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Five bodies, one country, and barely any competitor page in this market names all five.

Scale makes that map matter. Dubai's media office put the emirate's private sector at 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with 37% of pupils on a UK curriculum and 7% on the International Baccalaureate. Seven further private schools open for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three IB, adding 16,846 places, after enrolment rose 6% during 2025-26. A UK-curriculum cohort that size produces a deep market for some papers and a very thin one for others: plenty of maths help available, and almost nobody who has taught Computer Science 0478 to a Year 11 class under timed conditions.

Then there are the subjects your child takes whether or not the curriculum asked for them. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's published requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. They occupy real timetable minutes, they are assessed by the school, and they sit beside nine IGCSEs in the same Year 11 week. An honest tuition plan therefore starts by looking at what is already in the week, not at what could be added to it.

So this page is built in that order. Who holds which decision. Which authority your child's school reports to, and what you are entitled to look up about it. Which school-held records set the ceiling on what tuition can achieve. What the market charges and who published each figure. How live one-to-one online compares with a visiting tutor across one real school night. Then Ministry of Education equivalency, data protection for a minor on a video call, the tutor permit, and the line a tutor does not cross with assessed work.

igcse-online-tuition.programmesIntro: IGCSE is the middle of three stages a UAE family passes through, and the stage either side changes what tuition should be doing. Nothing further down this page makes much sense until you know which stage your child is actually in. Below: what feeds into IGCSE, what IGCSE itself asks for, and what the grades are used for at sixteen.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary, the years before IGCSE
programmes.description: Years 7 to 9 are taught to the school's own scheme of work rather than to a board specification, which is why parents rarely see a syllabus code at this stage. Cambridge offers Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and many UAE schools use them as a sorting instrument for Year 10 sets. This is where the tier decision is quietly made: a Year 9 maths set placed on the lower band is the set from which Core entries are later drawn.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE this stage also fixes the Arabic stream. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. A child placed in the wrong stream in Year 7 tends to carry that placement all the way into Year 10.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two boards dominate UAE British-curriculum schools. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and a March series available in some regions. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE papers are available in May/June and November each year, with modular assessment in several subjects so units can be banked across sittings. Cambridge tiers many subjects as IGCSE Core and Extended; both 9-1 and A*-G scales can appear on the same certificate.
programmes.countryNote: For a UAE family the board is not your choice, because the school makes the entry. What is your choice is finding out which board before you buy a single hour, since the papers, the practical arrangement and the deadlines all differ between them. Ask the exams officer for three things: the board, the syllabus code and the series. Those three facts are what turns a well-qualified tutor into a useful one.

programmes.name: A Level, the IB Diploma or a BTEC route
programmes.description: At sixteen the IGCSE grades stop being a school matter and become an entry condition. UAE schools offer A Level, the IB Diploma Programme, and in a few cases BTEC routes. A Level mathematics and the sciences normally expect an Extended-tier grade behind them, and IB Higher Level courses assume the same depth. The grade profile also becomes the first half of a Ministry of Education equivalency file, which is why a weak fifth subject matters more than a brilliant first one.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the equivalency rule bites. Gulf Today, reporting the Ministry's clarification of July 2026, states that British-track students must pass 'five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3', and that Arabic and Islamic education 'are not included among the five required subjects'. Five, not six. At least one ranking competitor publishes six, which is the kind of error that costs a family a term of planning.

igcse-online-tuition.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects UAE families ask for most, with the syllabus codes a tutor should be able to quote back at you without looking them up. A code is the cheapest verification available: anyone who has really taught 0625 knows which paper carries the practical questions. Tiers are given where the subject is tiered.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Two written papers at each tier, non-calculator and calculator. Extended carries algebra, functions, trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles and the harder probability work that Core leaves out. Most lost marks sit in method shown badly rather than method not known, which is why marked scripts matter more than fresh questions.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606 and Pearson Further Pure 4PM1
subjects.description: The bridge course for a child heading to A Level Mathematics or IB Higher Level. Calculus, series, logarithms and vectors appear here a year earlier than most pupils expect. Schools often enter strong sets for it late, which leaves a short run-in and makes a paper-by-paper block the sensible purchase.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and Pearson 4PH1
subjects.description: Electricity and the electromagnetism topics are where UAE cohorts most often stall, because they reward algebraic fluency rather than recall. Cambridge offers a written alternative to practical in place of the laboratory paper at some centres, and whether your child sits it changes the revision order completely.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 and Pearson 4CH1
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic chemistry account for most of the Extended-tier gap. The calculation questions are worth more than their length suggests and are routinely abandoned mid-working. Six timed questions with live annotation does more here than another pass through the textbook.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 and Pearson 4BI1
subjects.description: A content-heavy subject in which marks go missing on command terms: describe, explain and suggest each want a different answer shape. Transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance generate most of the Extended-only material. Vocabulary precision is the thing a weekly slot can genuinely fix.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language 0510 and 0511
subjects.description: The two codes differ only in how speaking is reported, and schools pick one for the whole cohort. Reading comprehension and the summary task carry disproportionate weight. Many UAE pupils speak fluently and still lose reading marks, which is a different problem from the one parents assume.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500 and Pearson 4EA1
subjects.description: Directed writing and the composition task reward structure over vocabulary. Pearson's route includes coursework in some specifications and Cambridge offers both coursework and examined options, so the first question is always which variant the school entered.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 and Pearson 4EC1
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the whole subject at this level. Students who can describe a market failure in prose and cannot draw it lose the same marks every paper. Data-response technique transfers directly to A Level, which makes it a good subject to tutor early rather than late.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: The hardest subject in the UAE to staff. Paper 1 is theory, Paper 2 is algorithms and pseudocode, and a tutor who codes professionally is not automatically a tutor who can teach the board's pseudocode conventions. Coverage here is the clearest case for looking beyond the pool within driving distance.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language 0508 and Arabic as a Foreign Language 0544
subjects.description: Two genuinely different courses that parents routinely conflate. KHDA requires Arab and non-Arab groups to be taught separately, and the language of instruction differs between them. Matching a first-language tutor to an additional-language pupil wastes the hour, so the stream is checked before the match.

igcse-online-tuition.regionsIntro: Delivery is identical in all seven emirates because it runs over video. The school system around your child is not identical. What changes by emirate is the authority holding the school file, the term calendar the lessons work around, and how thin the local pool of IGCSE specialists becomes once you get specific about a paper.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The deepest UK-curriculum market in the country: 227 private schools, 17 curricula, 37% of pupils on a UK curriculum in 2024-25. KHDA publishes inspection reports and the mandatory-subject guidelines, so there is more public information about a Dubai school than about any other in the Gulf.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools here, and its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff restrict teachers from paid private tutoring of pupils at their own school. That rule, press-reported in 2026, is the reason a parent should not ask for their child's own teacher privately.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, with a smaller British-curriculum cohort than the capital's coastal schools. Evening sessions here are the clearest argument for online delivery: the specialist pool for an individual IGCSE paper locally is small, and a video slot removes the question of who is willing to drive out.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Curriculum approval, not just inspection, sits with SPEA, so term dates and assessment timing can differ from Dubai's in ways that matter to a revision block.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority. Fewer schools, a shorter list of IGCSE subject options, and families who often commute into Sharjah or Dubai for school. A 5pm online slot is usually the first realistic start time on a weekday here.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The emirate's own Department of Knowledge regulates private education and holds the same fee and curriculum approval powers as SPEA. RAK returns essentially no mentions across the competitor pages we studied, which means families here are routinely told to look at Dubai agencies instead of being served.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education supervision, an east-coast location, and a drive to Dubai that makes any visiting-tutor arrangement unrealistic for a weekly commitment. Online IGCSE tuition is not the compromise option in Fujairah; it is the only version of specialist one-to-one support that exists at a sensible price.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: The smallest of the seven, also under Ministry of Education supervision for private schools. Pupils frequently sit IGCSEs at centres in neighbouring emirates, which makes confirming the centre, the series and the exam timetable zone with the school a genuinely necessary step rather than a formality.

igcse-online-tuition.regionsTitle: What changes by emirate, and what does not

schoolClusters.note: The schools below between them enter large IGCSE cohorts each year with both Cambridge and Pearson specifications in use, sometimes in different subjects within the same school. That is the single most common surprise for parents arriving from the UK, and the reason the entry record is worth asking for in writing.

ADEK-supervised schools with British-curriculum pathways through Years 10 and 11. The capital's assessment calendars tend to be published earlier in the term than Dubai's, which makes it easier to place revision blocks between internal deadlines rather than on top of them.

Smaller cohorts, longer commutes and fewer subject options per school. Families here most often come to us for a paper nobody nearby teaches, and the conversation starts with whether the school is entering that subject at all this series.

igcse-online-tuition.modesIntro: Three ways an IGCSE plan is normally bought in the UAE. All three are one-to-one and all three run over live video; what differs is how the hours are spread and what the tutor is being asked to carry. Which one fits usually depends on how far your child is from the next entry deadline rather than on budget.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one across the school year
modes.description: One fixed slot a week per subject, running from September. The tutor follows the school's own scheme of work and assessment calendar, which means the lesson is usually about next week's class rather than about the exam. This is the version that changes a tier decision, because it produces a term of evidence before the entry form closes.

This is the right purchase when the entry is already in and the plan has to be counted backwards from a fixed date.

sections.heading: Who holds which decision about your child's IGCSE
paragraphs: Four parties touch an IGCSE. The regulator licenses the school, the school makes the entry and sets the tier, the board writes and marks the paper, and the tutor teaches. Online IGCSE tuition changes exactly one of those four. Knowing which one saves a great deal of money and almost all of the frustration.

Parents arriving from the UK are often surprised that the board is not a family decision. The school holds the centre number, submits the entry and chooses the specification, sometimes differing by subject inside the same school. The tier follows the same route: a head of department enters a pupil for Core or Extended on a form with a deadline, and that form is what the board acts on. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series put final entries on 27 November 2026 against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, which is the clearest illustration available of how far ahead of the paper the decision actually sits.

What tuition controls is narrower and more useful than most marketing admits: what is practised, in what order, with what feedback, between now and the paper. That is the entire territory. It cannot move a deadline, re-tier an entry after submission or influence a mark. It can produce the evidence a department wants before the form closes, and it can change what a student does with ninety minutes of a Paper 2 they have already sat badly once. The table below separates the two so you can stop paying for the wrong thing.

sections.heading: Five authorities, and which of them reaches a private online lesson
paragraphs: Five bodies regulate private schools in the UAE and none of them regulates the lesson in your living room. The authority that does reach the tutor is a sixth: the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, through the private tuition work permit. Separating the two is the single most useful thing a parent can understand before paying for anything.

The school side of the map is public and worth using. u.ae states that ADEK 'supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools' in Abu Dhabi, that KHDA is 'responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education' in Dubai, that the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge each regulate private education in their emirate, and that the Ministry of Education 'plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in the emirates of Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah'. Sharjah's and RAK's authorities also approve fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so in those emirates the regulator shapes the assessment calendar directly.

The tutor side is narrower and more concrete. A permit attaches to the person teaching, not to the premises, and there is no emirate-level approval for an individual giving private lessons over video. That also means nobody can honestly describe a tutor as regulator-approved. A separate KHDA Educational Services Permit exists for training institutes with premises in Dubai, which is a different animal entirely: initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram runs no UAE premises and claims no such permit.

sections.heading: The school-held records that set the ceiling on what tuition can achieve
paragraphs: Six documents decide whether an hour of online IGCSE tuition is spent well. Your child's school holds five of them and the regulator publishes the sixth. Collecting them takes two emails and costs nothing, and a tutor who starts without them is guessing for the first month at your expense.

The most valuable is the marked mock script, not the mock grade. A grade tells you a child is on a 5; the script tells you the marks went on method not shown in Paper 2 question 14, on command terms misread in the structured questions, and on two topics never attempted. Schools release grades automatically and scripts only on request, so ask specifically for the paper back. The second most valuable is three lines from the exams officer: board, syllabus code, series. Without those, a tutor is teaching a subject rather than a specification, which is the difference between an interesting lesson and a higher mark.

The regulator's own report is the one record parents never think to read. A KHDA inspection report, or the equivalent for your emirate, is published free and contains phase-level and subject-level findings rather than a single band. A school rated Good overall can have a weaker secondary science phase, and that detail is more useful to you than the headline. Read the phase your child is in. Finally, ask which class group your child is registered in for Arabic and Islamic Education, because the stream determines which syllabus and which language of instruction apply, and therefore which tutor is the right match rather than merely a qualified one.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in the same Year 11 week
paragraphs: Three Ministry subjects run alongside your child's IGCSEs whatever the licensed curriculum says, and they are the reason a Year 11 week is fuller than the IGCSE timetable implies. KHDA states that Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum licensed, with requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year.

The rules are unusually specific, and they govern how these subjects can be tutored at all. KHDA requires separate classes by group: 'For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs. Combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction.' Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab pupils; and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies to non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Two further details change how a tuition plan is built. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. And for these subjects, 'the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the MoE, is strictly prohibited', so tutoring here stays on the set content rather than enriching around it. In practice that means Arabic support is sequenced in short, frequent slots rather than long weekend blocks, and it means being honest with a Year 11 family that in an exam term these subjects are rarely where the marginal hour belongs.

sections.heading: What IGCSE online tuition costs across the UAE market
paragraphs: IGCSE tuition rates in AED across the UAE run from roughly AED 45 an hour for a university-student tutor online to AED 650 for a premium named provider, with qualified subject specialists clustering between AED 150 and AED 450. Every figure in the table below is a market rate published by the provider named beside it, read in October 2026. None of them is an IB Gram price list.

The spread is not a quality scale, and reading it as one costs parents money in both directions. What actually sits behind the number is the tutor's subject depth, whether planning and marking happen between lessons, whether travel is priced in, and how close the entry deadline is when you book. The same specialist hour costs the same in September and in April; what changes is how many of them you need, which is the real reason an exam-term plan looks expensive. Bestimate's Dubai estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Put it next to the rest of the education bill and the proportion becomes clearer. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are therefore flat this year while tutoring demand is not, which is exactly the market in which unsourced pricing flourishes. Three of the six ranking competitors we studied publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. Ask any provider for the rate, what the hour includes, and what it excludes, in writing, before the first session.

sections.heading: Live one-to-one online against a visiting tutor, counted across one school night
paragraphs: A visiting tutor and a live one-to-one online tutor are not the same product at two prices. They differ in who you can reach, when the lesson can start, what survives it, and what happens when something goes wrong on a Tuesday. IB Gram delivers one-to-one over live video in the UAE and does not send anyone to a UAE address, so this comparison is made on the merits rather than quietly avoided.

Count a real school night. The school run ends somewhere between three and four. A visiting tutor has their own commute across the emirate before the lesson can start, which pushes a Jumeirah or Khalifa City session later and makes a weekday slot in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain close to impossible. The same hour online starts when the laptop opens. The market rate for a visiting hour sits above the online one by roughly AED 30 to 200 depending on the tier, and that gap is travel, not teaching.

The pool is the bigger difference. In-home means whoever will drive to your community; online means any specialist with a free slot. For Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 that distinction barely matters, because help is everywhere. For Computer Science 0478, Further Pure 4PM1 or first-language Arabic it decides whether the subject is coverable at all. The honest cost of online is that a tutor cannot read a room, so the format has to earn it back: a shared screen, live annotation on the student's own script, and the marked paper still sitting in the shared folder next week.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: what the grade profile has to satisfy
paragraphs: A UAE secondary certificate has to be made equivalent by the Ministry of Education before it is used for a local university application, and the rule for British-track students is specific enough to plan around. Gulf Today, reporting the Ministry's clarification in July 2026, states that students must pass 'five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3', plus 'one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E' or 'two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade'.

Two details inside that rule change how families spend tuition money. The first is the number: five subjects, not six. At least one competitor ranking for these queries publishes six, and a family planning around the wrong count either buys an unnecessary subject or drops a necessary one. The second is the exclusion: Arabic and Islamic education 'are not included among the five required subjects'. Both still have to be taken, because KHDA requires them of every Dubai private school pupil, but neither counts towards the five. A child with brilliant Arabic and four passable IGCSEs does not have a complete file.

Note what is not stated. The same clarification sets English and mathematics requirements for the American track, a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and at least 450 in SAT Mathematics, and it gives no IB points threshold at all. So no IB equivalency figure appears on this page, and you should treat any site that publishes one without a moe.gov.ae citation with caution. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring platform performs or guarantees: verify your own case on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate, and treat the fifth-subject arithmetic as the part a tuition plan can genuinely protect.

sections.heading: Safeguarding, recording and a minor's data in an online lesson
paragraphs: An online lesson creates a record that an in-home lesson does not: a video call, a shared folder, a marked script, a message thread and a billing history, all about a child. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection is the reason to be explicit about that rather than vague, and no competitor page we studied addresses it at all.

What a family should expect to be told, before the first session, is short. Which platform the lesson runs on. Whether the session is recorded, by whom, where the recording sits and for how long. Who besides the tutor can open the shared folder. What is collected at sign-up and why: a name, a year group, a board and a syllabus code are necessary to make a match, and a photograph, a school name and a set of grades usually are not. How to ask for all of it to be deleted, and how long that takes. If a provider cannot answer those in writing, that is information about the provider.

The format also hands you something a visiting arrangement does not. A parent can sit in the same room without sitting in the lesson, or review a recording afterwards at a time that suits them, which is a different kind of oversight from being told the session went well. Keep the session in a shared family space rather than a bedroom, keep the camera on at both ends, and keep contact on the platform rather than drifting into a private messaging thread. That last habit matters most in exam term, when a tutor and a student are messaging about a deadline at nine in the evening.

sections.heading: The tutor permit, the ethics rule, and the four questions to ask first
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated, not informal. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, u.ae states that it 'is granted free of charge for two years', and MoHRE's own service page, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Eligibility is broader than parents expect. u.ae lists teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE 'will be subject to fines and penalties' outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure appears here and you should distrust any page that quotes one. A separate restriction matters in the capital: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school, and the permit's own code of conduct points the same way. Asking for your child's own teacher privately is asking them to breach that.

So four questions, before any money moves. Which board and syllabus code have you taught, and for how many series? Do you hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit, and may we see it? Who marks the work between lessons, and what do we receive in writing? And what exactly happens if the match does not work after two sessions? A provider claiming any regulator's approval has already answered a different question badly: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE or board accreditation, operates no UAE premises, and says so on every page rather than in a footnote.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the school deadline is tonight
paragraphs: There is a line in IGCSE coursework, portfolio and practical work that a tutor does not cross, and the week before a school deadline is when families are most tempted to ask. The rule is simple to state: the student's work has to be the student's own, and a tutor teaches, questions, reviews and gives feedback on it. A tutor never writes a sentence of it.

In practice the honest version is more useful than the dishonest one anyway. A tutor can teach the skill the task assesses, read a draft and say which paragraph does not answer the question, mark a practical write-up against the published criteria, model the method on a different dataset, and run the timed conditions the real paper will impose. A tutor cannot supply text, restructure a piece into its final shape, provide completed work to copy from, or sit beside a student editing until the thing is finished. Boards and schools treat that as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever took the money.

This matters commercially as well as ethically, because the alternative is openly on sale in this market. One site ranking for these queries advertises finished Internal Assessments at a fixed price; that is an academic-integrity breach, and buying it puts a child's entry at risk for the sake of one deadline. Reproducing board material is the other common trap: we reference and link official syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes on cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com rather than hosting copies, because distributing them is a copyright problem regardless of how convenient it would be. Ask any provider where the line sits. The answer tells you what you are buying.

process.title: Send three facts, not a shortlist
process.description: Board, syllabus code, series. One email to your school's exams officer produces all three, and they determine everything that follows: which specification is taught, which papers are practised and how many weeks remain. Families who start here get matched faster than families who start with a subject name and a budget.

process.title: A diagnostic against a real paper
process.description: The first session is a timed section of an actual past paper for the right board and tier, marked live on a shared screen. It usually disagrees with the school report, and that disagreement is the useful part. It produces a topic order based on where marks went missing rather than on where the textbook happens to begin.

process.title: Match to a specification, not a subject
process.description: We match on the code your child sits and on the evening hours your family can actually keep on Gulf Standard Time. If nobody in the pool has taught that specification, you are told so before you pay, along with what is available instead. A disclosed gap is cheaper for everyone than a hopeful match.

process.title: A written plan counted backwards
process.description: Sessions are sequenced from the entry deadline and the paper date, not from today. The plan names which paper each block targets, where the school's internal deadlines and mock weeks fall, and how the schedule shifts for Ramadan and Eid. It is written down so it can be argued with.

process.title: Review against marks every half-term
process.description: Progress is read off school assessment marks and timed-paper scores, not off how the sessions felt. Half-termly the plan either continues, changes topic order, or stops. Where a subject cannot realistically be recovered before this series, we say so and discuss the November route instead of selling more hours.

whyPoints.title: The syllabus code goes in writing
whyPoints.description: Before the first paid session you receive the board, the code and the tier your tutor is teaching to. It sounds administrative and it is the single biggest predictor of whether the hours convert. A tutor teaching 'physics' rather than 0625 or 4PH1 is teaching a subject your child is not being examined in.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted with the source attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is a market rate published by the provider named beside it and read in October 2026. We would rather show you the whole range, including the cheaper end, than publish a number with no provenance. Three of the six ranking competitors we studied publish no price at all.

whyPoints.title: The regulator named, never claimed
whyPoints.description: We explain what KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE and the Ministry of Education each do, because a parent needs to know. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from any of them and runs no UAE premises. Anyone selling you regulator-approved tutors is selling something that does not exist for private online lessons.

whyPoints.title: Coursework reviewed, never written
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the skill the task assesses, reads a draft and says what does not answer the question, and marks against published criteria. No text is supplied and no piece is taken to completion. In a market where finished Internal Assessments are openly advertised, this boundary is worth stating rather than assuming.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed before you pay
whyPoints.description: For some specifications, Computer Science 0478 and first-language Arabic among them, the pool is genuinely thin. You are told that before any money moves, with the realistic alternative named. A gap you know about is a scheduling problem; a gap you discover in week three is a refund argument nobody wanted.

faqs.question: Does IGCSE online tuition in the UAE work the same way in Fujairah as it does in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The lesson does, because it runs over live video and the same specialist pool is reachable from every emirate. What differs is everything around it. A Fujairah school is supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than KHDA, its term dates can differ from Dubai's, and the local pool of IGCSE subject specialists willing to drive to the east coast is effectively empty. That last point is why online delivery is not a compromise there: it is the only version of weekly one-to-one specialist support available at a sensible rate. We confirm your school's board, series and assessment calendar first, whichever emirate it sits in.

faqs.question: Which of the five UAE education authorities has any say over a private online lesson?
faqs.answer: None of them, directly. KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge and the federal Ministry of Education regulate private schools and, in Dubai's case, training institutes with premises. A one-to-one lesson over video between a tutor and a family is not a school. The authority that does reach the tutor is MoHRE, through the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. That distinction is why nobody can honestly advertise regulator-approved private tutors, and why you should treat the phrase as a warning sign rather than a credential.

faqs.question: My son's school will not tell me his syllabus code. Who do I ask, and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer rather than the subject teacher or the front desk; the exams officer holds the centre entry record and the answer is three lines long. It matters because Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 assess different papers in a different order, and the practical arrangement differs too. A tutor given the code teaches the specification your child is examined in. A tutor given only the subject name teaches physics in general, which is interesting and does not reliably move a grade. If the school is slow, the code usually appears on a mock paper's front cover.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor see my child's school report or inspection file?
faqs.answer: Only what you choose to share. The school report, the marked mock script, the assessment calendar and the entry record are all held by the school and released to you, not to us. We ask for them because they shorten the guessing period: a marked script tells a tutor where marks actually went in Paper 2, which a grade cannot. The inspection report is different, because it is public. KHDA and the other emirate authorities publish theirs free, and the phase-level findings for your child's year group are more useful to you than the overall band.

faqs.question: If the lesson happens over video, whose rules govern the tutor?
faqs.answer: The permit rules, not the school ones. u.ae states that the MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years, and that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit will be subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so be sceptical of any page quoting an amount. Separately, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of pupils at their own school. That restriction follows the teacher onto a video call, so asking for your child's own teacher privately is asking them to breach it.

faqs.question: What is recorded during an online lesson, and who can see it afterwards?
faqs.answer: Ask before you book, and expect a written answer. A reasonable provider tells you which platform is used, whether sessions are recorded, where any recording is stored, how long it is kept and who besides the tutor can open the shared folder. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection is the reason this is a real question rather than a nicety, particularly when the data concerns a minor. A name, year group, board and syllabus code are what a match actually needs. A photograph, a school name and a full set of grades usually are not, and you can decline them.

faqs.question: Can we get online tuition for Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies as well?
faqs.answer: Yes, with two conditions that come from the rules themselves. First, the stream decides the tutor: KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with different language of instruction for each group, so a first-language tutor is wrong for an additional-language pupil. Second, the content is set. KHDA states that using different or additional content without prior MoE permission is strictly prohibited, so support stays on the prescribed material. In an exam term we will usually tell you this is not where the marginal hour belongs.

faqs.question: Why is my daughter taught Arabic in a different class from her Arab classmates?
faqs.answer: Because the two courses are genuinely different and KHDA requires them to be taught apart. Its mandatory-subject guidelines state that for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for the first-language group; non-Arab pupils are taught in the school's licensed-curriculum language for Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies. It is a curriculum rule, not a judgement about your daughter's ability.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE grades does the UAE Ministry of Education count towards equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five, on the British track. Gulf Today, reporting the Ministry's clarification in July 2026, states that students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One ranking competitor publishes six, which is wrong and expensive to plan around. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae, because no tutoring platform performs or guarantees equivalency.

faqs.question: Does an online tutor replace what my child's school is supposed to be doing?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider who implies otherwise is selling you the wrong thing. The school holds the entry, sets the tier, teaches the specification and runs the internal assessment calendar. Tuition works on a narrower territory: what is practised, in what order, with what feedback, between now and the paper. The most useful tutoring sits alongside the school's own scheme of work rather than running a parallel course. If the school is the problem, the inspection report for that subject phase and a conversation with the head of department will do more than buying extra hours.

faqs.question: We move from Ajman to Dubai in Year 10. What does the new school get to decide?
faqs.answer: More than parents expect. The new school holds its own centre number and makes its own entries, so it decides the board, the specification, the tier and the series your child sits, and it may use a different board from the old one in the same subject. It also places your child in the Arabic and Islamic Education stream and moves the school file from Ministry of Education supervision to KHDA. Ask for the entry record in writing within the first fortnight, then compare specifications. The gap between two boards in the same subject is usually a handful of topics, not a year.

faqs.question: What does an hour of online IGCSE support cost in the UAE, and who publishes those figures?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 run from about AED 45 an hour at the budget online end, where EdFlik lists from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, through AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor, where Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150, to AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists, with Bestimate's Dubai table and TutorChase's AED 270 in that band. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Those are the market's numbers, attributed, not an IB Gram price list. Ask what the hour includes and excludes in writing.

faqs.question: Is a screen a problem for the IGCSE science practical component?
faqs.answer: Less than you would think, because of how the component is actually assessed. Many UAE centres enter candidates for the written alternative-to-practical paper, which tests experimental method, apparatus, variables, tables, graphs and sources of error on paper rather than at a bench. That is well suited to a shared screen: the method is planned, the graph is drawn and annotated live, and the mark scheme's expectations are applied to the student's own answer. Where a centre enters the laboratory paper instead, the school runs the practical work and tuition supports the recording and analysis around it. Confirm which paper your child sits first.

faqs.question: My child has nine subjects and two are failing. Where should the money go first?
faqs.answer: Into whichever two subjects the equivalency file and the post-16 plan actually need, which is not always the two with the worst marks. Five IGCSE passes at grade 3 or E carry the Ministry of Education file, Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, so a borderline fifth subject matters more than a sixth strong one. After that, look at which subject the next stage requires: A Level Mathematics and the sciences expect Extended-tier grades behind them. One marked mock script per subject usually settles the argument in an hour, and it is free to obtain.

faqs.question: Nobody in the pool has taught my child's syllabus. What happens then?
faqs.answer: You are told before you pay, which is the part most of this market avoids. Some specifications are genuinely thin on the ground, Computer Science 0478, Further Pure 4PM1 and first-language Arabic among them. In that case we say what is available instead, whether that is a closely related specification taught by a specialist who will read your board's papers first, a shorter diagnostic block rather than a weekly commitment, or nothing at all this series. A disclosed gap is a scheduling problem you can plan around. An undisclosed one becomes a refund argument in week three.

faqs.question: The page is about online tuition, so does anyone visit the house?
faqs.answer: No. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, and nobody attends a UAE address. Home visiting is a service IB Gram runs only in India. We target the home-tutor phrasing because it is what parents type into Google, and we would rather explain the format honestly than let you discover it after booking. What you gain is the pick of specialists for one narrow paper rather than whoever lives within a twenty-minute drive, plus rescheduling that costs minutes instead of a forfeited session.

igcse-online-tuition.closingHeading: Start with three facts, not with a shortlist
igcse-online-tuition.closingBody: Email your school's exams officer and ask for the board, the syllabus code and the series your child is entered for. Ask the subject teacher for the marked mock script rather than the grade. Then look up your school's inspection report on the regulator's own site and read the phase your child is in, not the headline band. With those in hand, a conversation about online IGCSE tuition takes fifteen minutes instead of three weeks, because the only remaining question is which specialist has the right evening free. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, and the first one is a timed past paper rather than a sales call.

intro.heading: The system an IGCSE family in the UAE is already working inside
paragraphs: Searching for an IGCSE online tutor in the UAE usually starts with a mark on a report. It should start one step earlier, with the paperwork. Your child's school is the exam centre. It chooses the board, enters the candidate, sets the tier, submits coursework and practical marks, and issues forecast grades. A tutor hired from outside that building changes none of those things. What an outside tutor can change is how well your child answers the papers the school has already committed them to, and that is a narrower and far more honest promise than most of this market makes.

The second thing worth knowing is that there is no single UAE schools authority. Five separate bodies sit above private schools here. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah's private education authority regulates private education in that emirate, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Which of those names appears on your child's school file changes what you can look up, who approves the fees, and who publishes the inspection report you should read before buying a single hour. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so the emirate reaches further into the classroom than a parent in Dubai might assume. None of the five, however, inspects private tuition. That is a separate permit, issued to a person rather than to a provider, and it is the part of the picture most tutoring pages skip.

Then there is the Ministry layer that sits on top of every licensed curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of which international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and the federal rule behind that is simple: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Those subjects occupy real hours in a Year 10 and Year 11 week, they are taught from content the Ministry sets, and they are excluded from the five subjects the equivalency route counts.

This page is written around that context rather than around a sales pitch. It covers who owns which decision in an IGCSE year, what the private tuition permit actually says, where the syllabus code lives, how practical science is assessed when the teaching happens on a screen, what the Ministry of Education equivalency file asks of an IGCSE student, what IGCSE tuition rates in AED look like across this market, and where an hour realistically fits in a UAE school week. Lessons from IB Gram are delivered online, one to one, over live video. No tutor is sent to a UAE address.
bullets: The school enters the candidate and owns the tier; a tutor works to that entry
Five authorities regulate UAE private schools; none of them inspects private tuition
A paid private tutor needs a MoHRE work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023
